# PART I — THE SKILLS (WEB-SKILLS.md, ⟦S0001⟧–⟦S1504⟧)
## ⟦S0001⟧ frontend-design — Anthropic skills
- **What it is:** A design-direction playbook for building new UI or reshaping existing UI so it has a distinctive, intentional visual identity instead of reading as a templated default. It is guidance for the designer/builder, not a component or an effect.
- **How it looks:** There is no fixed look — the output is a page whose palette, typography and layout are visibly chosen for its specific subject: the hero opens with the most characteristic thing in the subject's world (a headline, an image, an animation, a live demo or an interactive moment, whichever fits), type is set on a deliberate scale with intentional weights/widths/spacing, and structural devices (borders, dividers, numbering, labels) only appear where they encode real information. Line lengths stay under 80 characters; serif body text gets slightly more line-height than sans-serif. It explicitly does NOT look like the known AI-default clusters: (1) warm cream background near #F4F1EA with high-contrast serif display and terracotta/warm-clay accent near #D97757; (2) near-black background with one acid-green or vermilion accent; (3) broadsheet layout with hairline rules, zero border-radius, dense newspaper columns; (4) the SaaS-card kit — identical rounded cards, one border-radius everywhere, the same soft grey shadow rgba(0,0,0,.1) under each, gradient washes as decoration; (5) template chrome — tracked-out ALL-CAPS eyebrow above every heading, meta strings joined with middle dots ('A · B · C'), 'WORD — fragment' labels with a spaced em dash, tinted near-black #0B0B0B / #111 standing in for black, monospace for small data labels, '→' appended to links/buttons.
- **Frame by frame:** No prescribed animation. The skill's motion rule: use non-user-triggered motion sparingly and deliberately, only to draw attention — one single orchestrated moment (one page-load sequence or one reveal) lands better than scattered effects; fade-and-slide-up entrances on every section and hover transitions on every card are called out as the generic default to avoid. Motion that answers a person's action (opening, expanding, confirming) is welcome when it shows what changed.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Two-pass process. Pass 1 — a compact token plan before any code: Color = 4–6 named hex values forming the core base palette; Type = the typefaces and their roles (one family or two; if two, clearly distinct); Layout = one-sentence prose concepts plus ASCII wireframes, with explicit alignment guidance; Principles = what makes this page unique. Then review the plan against the brief and revise anything that reads like the generic default for any similar page, stating what changed and why; only then build. Type scale follows The Elements of Typographic Style default guidance. Avoid as headline treatments: accenting a single word/phrase in italic/bold/another colour, all-caps labels, unnecessary typographic labels above content. Numbered markers (01/02/03) only when the content really is a sequence (stepped process, timeline). Quality floor while building: responsive down to mobile, visible keyboard focus, reduced motion respected, accessible, harmonious palette; beware CSS selector specificity cancelling (e.g. .section vs .cta padding/margin conflicts). Boldness budget: spend it in one place — one memorable element, everything around it quiet — and remove one decoration before finishing ("take a look in the mirror and remove one accessory"). Copy rules: write from the end user's perspective, name things by what users understand, active voice, a CTA says exactly what happens ("Save changes", not "Submit"), the same action name through the whole flow (button "Publish" → toast "Published"), errors explain what went wrong and how to fix it without apologising, empty states invite action, sentence case, plain verbs, no filler.
- **Reference / source:** Anthropic skills collection (frontend-design). Named inside the text: The Elements of Typographic Style (type-scale guidance). No websites named.
- **Best for:** The starting point of ANY build — setting the art direction, token system and layout concept for a whole page before code, and as an anti-slop checklist when auditing a finished page (hero, all sections, navigation, forms, footer). Trade-fit note: especially valuable for trade sites, where the subject's own materials and vernacular (timber, shingles, brick, vans, yard signage) should drive palette/type instead of agency defaults.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0001⟧

## ⟦S0002⟧ web-artifacts-builder — Anthropic skills
- **What it is:** A build pipeline for elaborate, multi-component claude.ai HTML artifacts that need state management, routing or a component library: it scaffolds a React project, you develop in it, then everything is bundled into one self-contained HTML file. Explicitly not for simple single-file HTML/JSX artifacts.
- **How it looks:** The visitor-facing result is whatever app is built with the stack — the skill itself prescribes only an anti-slop style rule for the output: avoid excessive centered layouts, purple gradients, uniform rounded corners, and the Inter font. Components come from 40+ pre-installed shadcn/ui components (Radix UI based), themed through the shadcn/ui theming system.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion prescribed. The "sequence" is the build workflow, in order: 1) run scripts/init-artifact.sh <project-name> and cd into the project; 2) develop by editing the generated files; 3) run scripts/bundle-artifact.sh, which installs the bundling dependencies, creates the .parcelrc config, builds with Parcel (no source maps) and inlines all JS/CSS/assets into a single bundle.html via html-inline; 4) share bundle.html in the conversation as the artifact; 5) optionally test afterwards (Playwright/Puppeteer) — testing upfront is discouraged because it adds latency before the user sees the artifact.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Stack: React 18 + TypeScript + Vite + Parcel (bundling) + Tailwind CSS 3.4.1 + shadcn/ui. Init script delivers: React + TypeScript via Vite; Tailwind CSS 3.4.1 with shadcn/ui theming; path aliases (@/) configured; 40+ shadcn/ui components pre-installed; all Radix UI dependencies included; Parcel configured via .parcelrc (including parcel-resolver-tspaths for path aliases); Node 18+ compatibility with automatic Vite-version pinning. Bundler dependencies installed at bundle time: parcel, @parcel/config-default, parcel-resolver-tspaths, html-inline. Requirement: the project must have an index.html in its root directory.
- **Reference / source:** Anthropic skills collection (web-artifacts-builder). Named reference: shadcn/ui components documentation — https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components.
- **Best for:** Complex interactive artifacts/dashboards with state and routing — not a section-level design technique, and not the route for a single-file trade homepage (a plain single HTML file is the better fit there). Useful background when a build genuinely needs a React component library.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0002⟧

## ⟦S0003⟧ theme-factory — Anthropic skills
- **What it is:** A theme toolkit: 10 pre-set, named colour-and-font themes that can be applied consistently to an artifact (slides, docs, reports, HTML landing pages), plus a method to generate a new theme on the fly when none of the 10 fit.
- **How it looks:** Each theme restyles the whole artifact with one cohesive palette (4 named hex colours) and one header/body font pairing, held consistently across every page/slide. The 10 looks: Ocean Depths — deep navy #1a2332 base, teal #2d8b8b accent, seafoam #a8dadc secondary, cream #f1faee text/light; professional, calming maritime. Sunset Boulevard — burnt orange #e76f51 primary, coral #f4a261 secondary, warm sand #e9c46a highlights/backgrounds, deep purple #264653 dark contrast/text; warm, golden-hour energy. Forest Canopy — forest green #2d4a2b primary, sage #7d8471 accent, olive #a4ac86 light accent, ivory #faf9f6 background/text; grounded earth tones. Modern Minimalist — charcoal #36454f primary dark, slate gray #708090 accents, light gray #d3d3d3 backgrounds/dividers, white #ffffff; clean grayscale. Golden Hour — mustard yellow #f4a900 bold primary, terracotta #c1666b secondary, warm beige #d4b896 neutral backgrounds, chocolate brown #4a403a dark text/anchors; rich autumnal warmth. Arctic Frost — ice blue #d4e4f7 light backgrounds/highlights, steel blue #4a6fa5 primary accent, silver #c0c0c0 metallic accents, crisp white #fafafa backgrounds/text; cool, precise. Desert Rose — dusty rose #d4a5a5 soft primary, clay #b87d6d accent, sand #e8d5c4 warm neutral backgrounds, deep burgundy #5d2e46 dark contrast; soft, sophisticated. Tech Innovation — electric blue #0066ff primary, neon cyan #00ffff highlights, dark gray #1e1e1e deep backgrounds, white #ffffff text; bold high-contrast tech. Botanical Garden — fern green #4a7c59 rich green, marigold #f9a620 floral accent, terracotta #b7472a earthy tone, cream #f5f3ed soft neutral backgrounds; fresh, organic. Midnight Galaxy — deep purple #2b1e3e dark base, cosmic blue #4a4e8f mid-tone, lavender #a490c2 soft accent, silver #e6e6fa light highlights/text; dramatic cosmic.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. Application sequence: 1) show theme-showcase.pdf unmodified so the user sees all 10 themes; 2) ask which theme to apply; 3) wait for explicit selection; 4) read the chosen theme file from the themes/ directory and apply its colours and fonts consistently throughout, checking contrast and readability. Custom-theme route: from a basic description, generate a new theme in the same format with a descriptive name, show it for review/verification, then apply the same way.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Font pairings (headers / body): Ocean Depths — DejaVu Sans Bold / DejaVu Sans. Sunset Boulevard — DejaVu Serif Bold / DejaVu Sans. Forest Canopy — FreeSerif Bold / FreeSans. Modern Minimalist — DejaVu Sans Bold / DejaVu Sans. Golden Hour — FreeSans Bold / FreeSans. Arctic Frost — DejaVu Sans Bold / DejaVu Sans. Desert Rose — FreeSans Bold / FreeSans. Tech Innovation — DejaVu Sans Bold / DejaVu Sans. Botanical Garden — DejaVu Serif Bold / DejaVu Sans. Midnight Galaxy — FreeSans Bold / FreeSans. Each theme is a file in themes/ carrying palette hex codes, the font pairing and a "best used for" note (e.g. Ocean Depths: corporate/financial/consulting trust decks; Tech Innovation: startups, software launches, AI/ML; Botanical Garden: garden centres, food, natural products; Desert Rose: fashion, beauty, interiors, boutiques).
- **Reference / source:** Anthropic skills collection (theme-factory); theme definitions live in its themes/ directory and are visualised in theme-showcase.pdf. No external websites named.
- **Best for:** Fast, coherent restyling of decks, docs, reports and simple landing pages; as a palette shortlist when a build needs a named starting palette (e.g. Forest Canopy / Golden Hour tones for outdoor trades). Trade-fit note: the palettes are presentation-grade starting points — a trade homepage still needs its own subject-driven direction per ⟦S0001⟧ rather than a preset applied as-is.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0003⟧

## ⟦S0004⟧ canvas-design — Anthropic skills
- **What it is:** A two-step method for creating static visual art (posters, art pieces, single-page designs) as .png / .pdf: first write a design philosophy — an aesthetic movement in a .md file — then express that philosophy on a canvas. Output is only .md, .pdf and .png files; original designs only, never copying existing artists' work.
- **How it looks:** A single, highly visual, design-forward page that is 90% visual design and 10% essential text: form, space, colour, composition, images, graphics, shapes and patterns carry the meaning; text appears as a minimal visual accent — sparse, clinical labels and systematic reference markers, thin fonts mostly, nothing falling off the page, nothing overlapping, everything contained with proper margins and breathing room. The scientific-observation register is the house style: dense accumulation of marks, repeated elements or layered patterns that build meaning through patient repetition, like a diagram from an imaginary discipline documenting an ephemeral subject. The philosophy examples show the range of looks: "Concrete Poetry" — massive colour blocks, sculptural typography (huge single words, tiny labels), Brutalist spatial divisions, Polish-poster energy; "Chromatic Language" — geometric colour zones as the information system, small sans-serif labels, Albers-style colour interaction; "Analog Meditation" — paper grain, ink bleeds, vast negative space, Japanese photobook feel, whispered type; "Organic Systems" — rounded forms, natural clustering, modular growth, key labels floating in space; "Geometric Silence" — grid precision, bold photography or stark graphics, dramatic negative space, Swiss formalism with Brutalist material honesty.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion; the deliverable is a still canvas. The work sequence: 1) create the philosophy .md (name the movement in 1–2 words; articulate it in 4–6 substantial paragraphs covering space/form, colour/material, scale/rhythm, composition/balance, visual hierarchy, mentioning each aspect once, repeatedly stressing master-level craftsmanship); 2) deduce the subtle reference — the niche conceptual thread from the request, woven invisibly into form/colour/composition so those who know feel it and others just see a masterful composition (a jazz musician quoting another song); 3) create the canvas (single page unless more are requested; use fonts from the ./canvas-fonts directory, downloading others as needed, with typography treated as part of the art); 4) final refinement pass — polish and crisp what exists rather than adding graphics or new shapes. Multi-page option: extra pages are distinct twists on the same philosophy, bundled in the same .pdf or as multiple .pngs, like a coffee-table book.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Ratios and counts prescribed: philosophy 4–6 paragraphs; movement name 1–2 words; canvas content 90% visual / 10% essential text. Hard execution rules: text always minimal and integrated as a visual element (scale follows context — a punk poster may use larger, aggressive type; most of the time the font should be thin); all elements contained within canvas boundaries with proper margins; no overlaps; flawless spacing. Craftsmanship framing must be repeated in the philosophy ("meticulously crafted", "painstaking attention", "master-level execution") because the second pass interprets it literally.
- **Reference / source:** Anthropic skills collection (canvas-design). Movements/aesthetics referenced as examples inside the text: Polish poster design, Le Corbusier, Josef Albers' colour interaction, Japanese photobooks, Swiss formalism, Brutalism. No URLs named.
- **Best for:** Posters, cover art, brand art pieces, social/hero artwork and any one-page visual artifact — for trade builds, a route to an original art-directed graphic (e.g. a poster-style hero backdrop or a print-style testimonial card) rather than a web section technique. Not for interactive sections, forms or navigation.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0004⟧

## ⟦S0005⟧ webapp-testing — Anthropic skills
- **What it is:** A testing toolkit for local web applications using Playwright: verify frontend functionality, debug UI behaviour, capture browser screenshots and view browser logs. It is a QA method, not a design technique — nothing here is visitor-facing.
- **How it looks:** No visitor-facing design. What you "see" is the tester's evidence: full-page screenshots of the rendered app (page.screenshot(path='/tmp/inspect.png', full_page=True)), the rendered DOM via page.content(), and element lists such as page.locator('button').all() — used to identify selectors before acting.
- **Frame by frame:** The prescribed sequence ("reconnaissance-then-action"): 1) navigate to the app; 2) wait for page.wait_for_load_state('networkidle') so JS has executed — inspecting the DOM before networkidle on a dynamic app is the named common pitfall; 3) take a screenshot and/or inspect the DOM; 4) identify selectors from the rendered state (text=, role=, CSS selectors or IDs); 5) execute actions with those selectors (plus page.wait_for_selector() / page.wait_for_timeout() waits where needed); 6) always close the browser. Approach decision tree: if the HTML is static, read the file directly to identify selectors (fall back to the dynamic route if that fails); if dynamic and the server is not running, use scripts/with_server.py (run it with --help first) to manage the server lifecycle; if the server is already running, go straight to reconnaissance-then-action.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Native Python Playwright scripts using sync_playwright(); Chromium always launched headless (p.chromium.launch(headless=True)). Helper script scripts/with_server.py manages one or multiple servers — single: python scripts/with_server.py --server "npm run dev" --port 5173 -- python your_automation.py; multiple: repeat --server/--port pairs (example: backend on port 3000, frontend on port 5173). Automation scripts contain only Playwright logic; servers are managed automatically. Rules: run bundled scripts with --help first and treat them as black boxes — do not read their source until running one fails and a customised solution is absolutely necessary (they are large and pollute context); use descriptive selectors; add appropriate waits.
- **Reference / source:** Anthropic skills collection (webapp-testing). Bundled reference files: examples/element_discovery.py (discovering buttons, links, inputs), examples/static_html_automation.py (file:// URLs for local HTML), examples/console_logging.py (capturing console logs). No external websites named.
- **Best for:** The QA loop of any build — screenshot capture (desktop/mobile), interaction checks and console-log inspection of a finished homepage before it is shown for approval; the reconnaissance-then-action pattern suits verifying switchers, forms and animations in local preview files. Not a design source.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0005⟧
## ⟦S0006⟧ impeccable — standalone flagship design-system skill at the head of WEB-SKILLS.md (a whole design operating system, not a single technique; ~5,200 lines with 37 reference files)
- **What it is:** A complete frontend design system that runs a build like an award-winning design director: it loads durable project context (PRODUCT.md for product truth, DESIGN.md for the visual system, per-surface briefs), classifies the surface into one of four visitor modes, picks or builds a committed "visual world," enforces a craft floor of measurable checks and absolute bans, and finishes with an independent review. It ships as one skill with a self-contained `impeccable` CLI (context loader, deterministic design detector, live browser variant mode, comp/build gates) plus 25 sub-commands. Most important commands/modes:
  - **Modes (the visitor's success defines the surface):** *Persuade* — landing/marketing/pricing; the visitor decides and acts, design is the product, full commitment allowed. *Operate* — app UI, dashboards, settings; scanability and familiar affordances outrank expression, the world lends only type, palette, density and one signature move. *Read* — docs/articles; the world owns the frame (masthead, rail, ground, openers), the reading column stays calm. *Experience* — portfolios/galleries; the artifact leads from the first viewport and the interface recedes.
  - **Build:** `init` (capture product truth in PRODUCT.md), `shape` (plan UX/UI, confirmed brief, no code), `document` (generate DESIGN.md from existing code), `extract` (pull repeated patterns into tokens/components), plus the new-work flow: seven candidate visual systems from the audience's own world → a dice-roll `concept-seed` assigns a direction and deals catalog challengers → a ~150-word six-block direction contract (THESIS / OWN-WORLD / STORY / FIRST VIEWPORT / FORM / FINISH) → comp-led build (image comps → measured spec → generated raster "plates" → gated hero → sections → motion → responsive) or code-led build.
  - **Evaluate:** `critique` (two isolated assessments — design review + detector/browser evidence — synthesized into Nielsen heuristic scores, persona red flags, P0–P3 priority issues), `audit` (technical scan: accessibility, performance, theming, responsive, implementation integrity, each scored 0–4).
  - **Refine:** `polish` (final pass, refinement never concealed redesign), `bolder` (amplify one named section using the system's own strongest moves), `quieter` (reduce intensity without going generic), `distill` (strip to essence), `harden` (errors, i18n, edge cases), `onboard` (first-run flows and empty states).
  - **Enhance:** `animate` (purposeful motion under a written motion thesis), `colorize`, `typeset`, `layout`, `delight`, `overdrive` (push past conventional limits — View Transitions morphs, scroll-driven animation, WebGL/WebGPU, springs — only after proposing 2–3 directions and getting the user's pick).
  - **Fix:** `clarify` (UX copy), `adapt` (rethink, not rescale, for other devices/contexts), `optimize` (measured performance fixes).
  - **Iterate:** `live` (pick elements in the browser, get hot-swapped variants, accept one and it is baked into source), `generate [n] [action] [element]` (one-shot variant generation, count defaults to 3, capped at 8). Plus `hooks` (auto-detector after UI edits) and `doctor` (repairs drift between project artifacts).
- **How it looks:** The output is a finished page where every atom — nav, buttons, inputs, links, selection colour, caret, scrollbar, focus rings — is rebuilt in one committed world's vocabulary, so the page reads as one specific product and could not be swapped for a competitor's. Composition is led by one dominant move (the world's material carries the ground and major surfaces), with a steady vertical rhythm, tight grouping inside sections and generous separation between them, more space above a heading than below it. Type has obvious scale and weight steps; colour commits at page scale (whole regions owned by a colour, not accents scattered on neutral). It visibly refuses the template tells: no eyebrow/kicker label above a heading (an absolute ban — the heading carries its own weight), no rows of same-size icon-plus-heading-plus-text cards, no big-number/small-label hero-metric template, no gradient text, no glass/blur decoration, no hard offset block shadows outside a genuinely neobrutalist world, no section numbers (01/02/03), no system display face (Impact, Arial Black) standing in for a sourced, self-hosted display face, no emoji or Unicode glyphs standing in for a drawn icon system.
- **Frame by frame:** This is a system, so its motion grammar applies wherever it builds: (1) On load, content is visible in its default state — nothing hides behind JavaScript or an entrance animation; the page gets ONE rehearsed focal sequence (500–800 ms authored entrance, exponential ease-out) rather than the same fade-and-rise repeated on every section. (2) Routine interaction: a control acknowledges input in 100–150 ms; a state change settles in 150–300 ms; a layout, overlay or view transition takes 300–500 ms; exits always run faster than entrances. (3) Scroll: motion is tied to scroll only when the scroll relationship itself carries the meaning (shared-element/FLIP continuity, a mask or clip-path reveal, a bounded blur/shadow shift), with a static fallback; sibling stagger is allowed only when a list appears as a list, with total delay capped. (4) In `live` mode the visitor sees the picked element hot-swap between up to 8 full replacement variants in the real page, cycles them with the floating bar's arrows, tunes coarse knobs (sliders/segments/toggles driving CSS variables), and on Accept the chosen variant is baked into the real stylesheet and the page reloads clean with no overlay. (5) Every animation ships a `prefers-reduced-motion` path: spatial movement is removed or gentled while opacity, colour and state feedback that carry meaning stay legible; nonessential loops stop when offscreen or hidden.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Easing: natural deceleration `cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)` for confident arrivals; bounce/elastic forbidden by reflex. Duration table: 100–150 ms immediate feedback · 150–300 ms routine state change · 300–500 ms layout/overlay/view transition · 500–800 ms authored focal entrance; Operate surfaces run 150–250 ms with no page-load choreography. Prefer transform/opacity, FLIP and view transitions; blur, backdrop-filter, clip-path, mask, shadow and colour are in the palette when bounded and smooth; never casually animate width/height/top/left/margins; `will-change` only during a known animation. Craft floor numbers: body and placeholder text contrast ≥ 4.5:1, large text and controls/icons/focus ≥ 3:1; body measure 65–75ch (Read surfaces ~60–75ch, body near 16px); display type max 6rem; tracking floor −0.04em; headings `text-wrap: balance`, body `text-wrap: pretty`; shadows must carry offset + soft blur. Responsive: touch targets 44×44px minimum (WCAG AA floor 24×24 CSS px with the spacing rule); mobile body text 16px minimum (iOS force-zooms inputs below that); content-driven breakpoints, typically 640 / 768 / 1024px; detect input with `(pointer: fine/coarse)` and `(hover: hover/none)`, never screen size alone; safe areas via `env(safe-area-inset-*)` + `viewport-fit=cover`; email adaptation 600px max, single column, inline CSS. Colour: build roles not swatches; prefer OKLCH for new palettes; tonal ramps are 8 steps, lightness ~15%→95%, chroma reduced near white and black; colour strategies named before colours are picked — Restrained (tinted neutrals + one accent), Committed (one saturated colour carries 30–60% of the surface), Full palette (3–4 named roles), Drenched (the surface IS the colour); dark-vs-light is decided by one written sentence of physical use-scene, never by category. `quieter` specifics: saturation down to 70–85%, motion distances cut to 10–20px from 40px, ease-out-quart, never gray text on a coloured ground (use a darker shade of that colour). Operate specifics: fixed rem type scale with a tight 1.125–1.2 ratio, every component ships all states (default, hover, focus, active, disabled, loading, error), skeleton loaders not spinners. Scoring systems: `audit` = 5 dimensions × 0–4 = /20 (18–20 Excellent, 14–17 Good, 10–13 Acceptable, 6–9 Poor, 0–5 Critical); `critique` = Nielsen's 10 heuristics × 0–4 = /40 (36–40 Excellent, 28–35 Good, 20–27 Acceptable, 12–19 Poor, 0–11 Critical), renormalized when heuristics are n/a (e.g. 24/32); cognitive-load checklist of 8 items with the working-memory rule — no more than 4 options visible at any decision point. `harden` budgets: allow 30–40% text expansion for translation (German runs ~30% longer than English), use logical CSS properties for RTL, `Intl.DateTimeFormat`/`Intl.NumberFormat` for locale dates/numbers/digits. `optimize` targets: LCP < 2.5s, INP < 200ms, CLS < 0.1, 60fps = 16ms per frame, image compression 80–85% quality, debounce 300ms / throttle 100ms reference values. Build pipeline numbers: comp prompts run 150–300 words; raster plates must be at least 1.5× their region's size with real alpha checked on light and dark grounds, and every shipped raster carries an embedded provenance prompt/origin; the hero gate passes at 72% overall similarity to the approved comp with hard vetoes (missing region, SVG illustration past icon size ~64px, clipped plate, invented ink) at any score; inspection is capped at two batched screenshot rounds; a finish reviewer returns exactly one of four dispositions — recapture, rebuild, fix, ship. Live-mode parameters: 0–4 coarse knobs per variant, budgeted by composition size (leaf/tiny 0; small ≤1; medium target 2; large target 2–3, up to 4); signature knobs include `color-amount` (range 0–1, step 0.05, default 0.5, authored as `var(--p-color-amount, 0.5)`), `density` (0.6–1.4, step 0.05, default 1), and type `scale` (0.85–1.3, step 0.05, default 1); the live helper serves from `http://localhost:8400`.
- **Reference / source:** The Impeccable skill itself — its reference files cite its own GitHub repo (github.com/pbakaus/impeccable, linked for framework-fixture expected outputs) and its docs at impeccable.style/docs. Systems it explicitly builds on: the official DESIGN.md format spec from google-labs-code/design.md (YAML token frontmatter — only `colors`, `typography`, `rounded`, `spacing`, `components` groups allowed, component sub-tokens limited to 8 props — plus up to eight canonical markdown sections and a `.impeccable/design.json` sidecar); Nielsen's 10 usability heuristics and Cowan's working-memory research (Miller's Law revised, ≤4 items) in the critique reference; line-break guidance paraphrased from Matthew Butterick's *Practical Typography*; live-mode tooling named inside references includes Tippy.js/Popper.js, Intro.js, Shepherd.js, React Joyride (onboarding), Three.js/OGL/regl, deck.gl, TanStack Virtual, motion (formerly Framer Motion) and GSAP (overdrive), and Chrome DevTools/Lighthouse/WebPageTest (optimize).
- **Best for:** Governing a whole build rather than supplying one effect — this is the entry to deep-read FIRST for any new homepage, then use its pieces per section. Specifically: choosing a genuinely different visual world and composition for a hero / first viewport (new-work + the Persuade mode rules: the opening must make the offer intelligible and desirable, expose the real working action a category visitor came to take — e.g. a roofer's quote call in working form, not a decorative link — and the world may carry the page but every part must still work as a page: nav reads as links, the primary action is unmistakable, the next section starts as a section); generating three truly different versions of one element (`live` / `generate`: three variants on three DIFFERENT primary axes — hierarchy, layout topology, typographic system, colour strategy, density, structural decomposition — inside one identity lock, or three different aesthetic families in departure mode); motion direction for any section (`animate`'s motion thesis and material palette; `overdrive` when a section earns a morph, spring, scroll-driven or WebGL moment); typography and colour systems (`typeset`, `colorize`); responsive rework (`adapt`); production hardening of forms and CTAs (`harden`, `clarify`); and final QA of any finished section or page (`critique` for design judgment, `audit` for measurable defects, `polish` as the last pass, the craft-floor ban list as the checklist). Trade-fit note: for trade/service homepages it runs in Persuade mode — bold, committed worlds are explicitly permitted, but invented claims are not: prices, customers, benchmarks and testimonials must be real or labelled synthetic, while demonstration material may be authored at full fidelity.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0006⟧
## ⟦S0007⟧ ui-ux-pro-max — UI/UX Pro Max (uupm.cc) — skills
- **What it is:** A searchable design-intelligence skill: a Python script (`scripts/search.py`, Python 3, no dependencies) queries bundled CSV databases of styles, product palettes, font pairings, UX rules, icons, chart types, motion presets and stack guidelines, and can generate a complete design system for a product in one pass.
- **How it looks:** Not a visual in itself — what a builder gets out of it is a coherent page: one named style applied consistently, a full palette filling every slot (primary / secondary / accent / background / card / border / destructive), a matched heading + body font pairing, and spacing density matched to the product type.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion of its own. It selects motion instead: the `--motion` dial (1–10) attaches a GSAP preset tier (Subtle / Standard / Complex) from motion.csv ⟦S0019⟧ to the generated design system.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Modes: `--design-system` (aggregates products, styles, colors, landing, typography + ui-reasoning; `--persist` writes `design-system/<slug>/MASTER.md` plus `pages/` overrides), `--domain <x>`, `--stack <x>`. Dials `--variance / --motion / --density`, each 1–10; density spacing scales: low 24–96px, mid 16–64px, high 8–32px. Rule priority 1→10 with hard numbers: accessibility first (contrast 4.5:1, focus rings 2–4px), touch (44×44pt iOS / 48×48dp Android / web 24×24 CSS px, 8px gaps, tap feedback within 100ms), performance (CLS < 0.1, ~16ms/frame), layout (breakpoints 375 / 768 / 1024 / 1440, line length 35–60 chars mobile, 60–75 desktop, z-index scale 0 / 10 / 20 / 40 / 100 / 1000, min-h-dvh), typography (base 16px, line-height 1.5–1.75, 65–75 chars), animation (transform/opacity only, stagger 30–50ms per item, exit ≈60–70% of enter duration, press scale 0.95–1.05, 1–2 animated elements per view), forms (validate on blur, toasts auto-dismiss 3–5s, input height ≥44px), navigation (bottom nav ≤5 items, sidebar ≥1024px), charts (data vs background ≥3:1, labels ≥4.5:1). Bundled data: 79 styles (50 active), 192 product palettes + reasoning profiles, 74 font pairings, 119 UX guidelines, 105 icons, 17 GSAP presets, 25 chart types, 22 stacks.
- **Reference / source:** UI/UX Pro Max collection (uupm.cc). Embedded references: `references/quick-reference.md` (the full 119-rule set) and `references/pro-rules.md` (app pre-delivery checklist: SVG icons only, icon-md 24pt, stroke 1.5px or 2px consistent, 4/8dp rhythm, section spacing tiers 16/24/32/48, test at 375px + landscape + reduced motion + Dynamic Type).
- **Best for:** The starting point of any build — picking the style, palette, fonts and rule set for a whole site before sections are designed. It is the generator/search layer behind the lookup tables ⟦S0014⟧–⟦S0025⟧.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0007⟧

## ⟦S0008⟧ design — UI/UX Pro Max (uupm.cc) — skills
- **What it is:** The umbrella/routing skill of the design family: it bundles the sibling skills brand ⟦S0011⟧, design-system ⟦S0009⟧ and ui-styling ⟦S0010⟧, and adds built-in generators for logos, corporate identity (CIP), icons, banners, slides and social photos, mostly via AI image models.
- **How it looks:** What it produces: logos always delivered on a white background; full CIP stationery sets (business card 3.5×2in / 85×55mm and the rest of a 50+ deliverable list); icon sets drawn on a 24×24 viewBox grid; social images at exact platform sizes with all text kept inside the central 80% safe zone.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. It produces still brand assets and routes page-design work to its sibling skills.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Logo: 55+ styles, 30 palettes, 25 industry guides; models Gemini Nano Banana (default), Atlas Cloud, MuAPI. CIP: 50+ deliverables, 20 styles/industries; flash model `gemini-2.5-flash-image`, pro model `gemini-3-pro-image` for 4K text; business-card stock 300–400gsm; style hexes include Corporate Minimal navy #0F172A, Modern Tech #6366F1 / #0EA5E9 / #10B981, Luxury Premium #1C1917 / #D4AF37, Warm Organic #8B4513 / #228B22, Bold Dynamic #DC2626 / #F97316. Icon: 15 styles (outlined 2px stroke, thin 1–1.5px, bold 3px, etc.), viewBox 0 0 24 24, currentColor, sizes 16 / 24 / 32 / 48; Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview outputs SVG text. Banner and Slides sub-skills duplicate the references indexed at ⟦S0012⟧ and ⟦S0013⟧. Social Photos: HTML → screenshot via Chrome headless / Playwright / Puppeteer, 3–5s render delay, Puppeteer deviceScaleFactor 2; sizes IG post 1080×1080, story 1080×1920, carousel 1080×1350, FB 1200×630, X 1200×675, LinkedIn 1200×627, YouTube thumbnail 1280×720, Pinterest 1000×1500; type minimums at 1080px width: headline 48px, subhead 32px, body 24px, caption 18px, CTA 28px.
- **Reference / source:** UI/UX Pro Max family. Its logo style guide names real marks as examples (Google, Coca-Cola, FedEx wordmarks; IBM, HBO, NASA lettermarks; Apple, Twitter, Target pictorial marks; Starbucks, Harley-Davidson emblems), and its colour-psychology table gives hexes (Navy #003366, Royal #0055A4, Sky #0EA5E9, Crimson #DC2626, Forest #228B22, Gold #D4AF37) plus named palettes (Tech Professional #6366F1 / #8B5CF6 / #06B6D4; Luxury #1C1917 / #D4AF37 / #FFFFFF).
- **Best for:** Brand assets around a build — logo, icon set, social/OG images, print identity. Not a page-design skill itself; page work routes to ⟦S0009⟧ / ⟦S0010⟧ / ⟦S0011⟧.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0008⟧

## ⟦S0009⟧ design-system — UI/UX Pro Max (uupm.cc) — skills
- **What it is:** A design-token architecture skill: three token layers (primitive → semantic → component) in W3C DTCG-aligned JSON, with generate/validate scripts, plus a slide design system driven by eight decision CSVs.
- **How it looks:** The same components everywhere on a site: buttons in three fixed heights (32 / 40 / 48px), cards built from 24px padding blocks, one radius scale and one shadow scale across every section, and a dark mode that restyles the whole page by swapping semantic tokens only — no component changes.
- **Frame by frame:** Mostly static; state changes run at fixed speeds — colour/background 150ms ease-in-out, transform 200ms ease-out, opacity 150ms ease, shadow 200ms ease-out. State priority: disabled > loading > active > focus > hover > default.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Scripts `generate-tokens.cjs` / `validate-tokens.cjs`. Primitives: gray 50 #F9FAFB – 950 #030712; blue 50 #EFF6FF – 900 #1E3A8A; spacing on a 4px base (`--space-0-5` 2px … `--space-24` 96px); font sizes xs 12px, sm 14px, base 16px, lg 18px, xl 20px, 2xl 24px, 3xl 30px, 4xl 36px, 5xl 48px; leading none 1 – loose 2; weights 400/500/600/700; tracking −0.05em – 0.05em; radius sm 2px, default 4px, md 6px, lg 8px, xl 12px, 2xl 16px, 3xl 24px, full 9999px; durations 75/100/150/200/300/500/700/1000ms (fast 150, normal 200, slow 300); z-index 0–50 plus dropdown 1000, sticky 1100, modal 1200, popover 1300, tooltip 1400. Components: input heights 32/40/48px with focus ring at primary/20%; card padding header 24px 24px 0, content 24px, footer 0 24px 24px, gap 16px; badge heights 20/24/28px; dialog max-widths sm 384px, default 512px, lg 640px, xl 768px, full 100%−32px, overlay rgb(0 0 0 / 0.5); table cell padding 12px 16px, row heights 40/48/56px. Focus ring 2px width + 2px offset; disabled opacity 0.5. Tailwind integration uses space-separated HSL variables (e.g. `--primary: 217 91% 60%`), radius lg = var(--radius), md = −2px, sm = −4px. Slides: 8 decision CSVs (strategies, layouts, layout-logic, typography, color-logic, backgrounds, copy, charts) searched by BM25 via search-slides.py with `--context --position --prev-emotion`; Duarte Sparkline pattern breaks at 1/3 and 2/3; slides must import design-tokens.css and use var() exclusively; Chart.js for charts.
- **Reference / source:** UI/UX Pro Max family; the W3C Design Tokens Community Group (DTCG) format is named as the token standard. No external sites named.
- **Best for:** The foundation layer of any build — set tokens first so hero, proof/reviews, work/gallery, process and CTA sections all share one spacing, type, colour and motion scale.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0009⟧

## ⟦S0010⟧ ui-styling — UI/UX Pro Max (uupm.cc) — skills
- **What it is:** A component-styling skill built on shadcn/ui (Radix primitives, components copied into the codebase) and Tailwind utility CSS, with an added canvas/poster visual-design method in its references.
- **How it looks:** Clean utility-built interfaces — consistent buttons, menus and dialogs with visible focus rings, light and dark themes that swap entirely through CSS variables — plus, from the canvas layer, poster-like compositions: massive colour blocks, sculptural type, roughly 90% visual / 10% text.
- **Frame by frame:** Interaction motion comes from the Radix components and Tailwind transitions; the skill prescribes a reduced-motion override that cuts animation/transition durations to 0.01ms, and a theme toggle where the sun/moon icons rotate and scale as the theme flips.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Installed via `npx shadcn@latest init/add`; scripts shadcn_add.py and tailwind_config_gen.py (refuses to overwrite an existing config without --force). References: (1) canvas-design-system — write a 4–6 paragraph design philosophy first, then express it visually; palette limited to 2–5 colours in oklch (example: primary oklch(0.55 0.22 264), accent oklch(0.75 0.18 45)); thin fonts 200–300 preferred; named movements Concrete Poetry, Chromatic Language, Analog Meditation, Organic Systems, Geometric Silence. (2) shadcn-accessibility — Radix focus trap / Esc / return-focus in dialogs; contrast AA 4.5:1 normal / 3:1 large, AAA 7:1 / 4.5:1; focus-visible ring-2 + ring-offset-2; 200% zoom check; `motion-reduce:transition-none`. (3) shadcn-components — full catalog with variant sets (Button: default/destructive/outline/secondary/ghost/link; sizes default/sm/lg/icon); Date Picker = Popover + Calendar composition. (4) shadcn-theming — HSL CSS variables for light and dark (light `--background: 0 0% 100%`, `--foreground: 222.2 84% 4.9%`, `--primary: 222.2 47.4% 11.2%`, `--radius: 0.5rem`); next-themes provider (attribute="class", defaultTheme="system"); base colours Slate/Gray/Zinc/Neutral/Stone; styles Default vs New York. (5) tailwind-customization — Tailwind v4 `@theme` (oklch brand scale, named spacing `--spacing-navbar: 4.5rem`, custom breakpoints `--breakpoint-3xl: 120rem`, `--breakpoint-tablet: 48rem`, `--shadow-glow: 0 0 20px rgba(139,92,246,0.3)`), `@utility glass` (background rgba(255,255,255,0.1), blur(10px), 1px border rgba(255,255,255,0.2)). (6) tailwind-responsive — breakpoints sm 640 / md 768 / lg 1024 / xl 1280 / 2xl 1536, mobile-first, container queries @sm–@2xl, test widths 320/640/768/1024/1280, touch targets min 44×44px. (7) tailwind-utilities — spacing scale 0–24 (96px), text-xs 12px – 5xl 48px, 11-shade colour scales 50–950, radius up to full 9999px, arbitrary values like `grid-cols-[1fr_500px_2fr]`.
- **Reference / source:** UI/UX Pro Max family; named resources ui.shadcn.com, tailwindcss.com, radix-ui.com, tailwindui.com, headlessui.com, v0.dev; the canvas reference cites Josef Albers (colour zones as information) and Swiss formalism.
- **Best for:** Building the actual components of any section — navigation, forms, dialogs, cards — with accessible behaviour baked in; the canvas layer suits bold hero/poster sections.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0010⟧

## ⟦S0011⟧ brand — UI/UX Pro Max (uupm.cc) — skills
- **What it is:** A brand-identity system skill: colours, logo rules, typography, voice and messaging frameworks, and an asset registry, all kept in one source-of-truth file (`docs/brand-guidelines.md`) and synced into design tokens.
- **How it looks:** One consistent brand on every surface: the logo never stretched, rotated, shadowed or recoloured, used at set sizes (header 120–200px wide, footer 100–150px, favicon 32×32, apple touch icon 180×180); colour used in fixed proportions — primary 60–70%, secondary 20–30%, accent 5–10%.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. Identity rules, sizing rules and copy frameworks, not animation.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Scripts: `sync-brand-to-tokens.cjs` (writes `assets/design-tokens.json` + `.css`; stops if it detects an existing token source, `--force` only for managed outputs), inject-brand-context.cjs, validate-asset.cjs, extract-colors.cjs (k-means dominant colours → nearest brand colours → compliance %). Colour system: 1–2 primary, 2–3 secondary, 3–5 neutrals; semantics Success #22C55E / Warning #F59E0B / Error #EF4444 / Info #3B82F6; off-brand tolerance max 20%; contrast AA 4.5:1 / 3:1, AAA 7:1 / 4.5:1; never pure black #000 for text. Logo: clear space = height of the logo mark; minimum sizes digital full logo 120px wide, icon 24px (32px in UI), print full 35mm, icon 10mm; social icons LinkedIn 300×300, X 400×400, Facebook 180×180, Instagram 320×320. Typography: base 16px, scale ratio 1.25 (Major Third) — Display 3.815rem/61px w700 lh1.1, H1 49px, H2 39px, H3 31px, H4 25px, H5 20px, Body Large 18px lh1.6, Body 16px lh1.5, Small 14px, Caption 12px; mobile (<768px) H1 32px / H2 24px / H3 20px; headings lh 1.1–1.3, long-form 1.6–1.75; tracking display −0.02em, all-caps 0.05em; max line length 65–75 chars. Starter defaults: Primary Blue #2563EB, Secondary Purple #8B5CF6, Accent Green #10B981, neutrals #FFFFFF / #F9FAFB / #111827 / #6B7280 / #E5E7EB, Inter + JetBrains Mono; spacing 4/8/16/24/32/48px; radius buttons 8px, cards 12px, inputs 8px, modals 16px, pills 9999px. Update presets with hexes: ocean-professional #3B82F6 / #F59E0B / #10B981; electric-creative #FF6B6B / #9B5DE5 / #00F5D4; forest-calm #059669 / #92400E / #FBBF24; midnight-purple #7C3AED / #EC4899 / #06B6D4; sunset-warm #F97316 / #DC2626 / #FACC15. Voice: four spectrums (Formal↔Casual, Simple↔Complex, Serious↔Playful, Reserved↔Expressive), 3–5 traits written as "X, not Y"; prohibited terms include Revolutionary, Best-in-class, Seamless, Synergy, Leverage. Messaging framework Mission→Vision→Value Prop→Positioning→Key Messages→Proof Points, with 10s/30s/60s elevator pitches. Assets: `.assets/manifest.json` registry; naming `{type}_{campaign}_{description}_{YYYYMMDD}_{variant}.{ext}`.
- **Reference / source:** UI/UX Pro Max family; tools named: Coolors, WebAIM Contrast Checker, Color Hunt.
- **Best for:** Locking a client's brand (or a portfolio site's consistent house brand) before page design; logo usage rules for navigation and footer; voice rules governing all copy, including CTA and form text.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0011⟧

## ⟦S0012⟧ banner-design — UI/UX Pro Max (uupm.cc) — skills
- **What it is:** A banner workflow skill: gather requirements → research (bundled reference plus optional 3–5 browser references) → build each option in HTML/CSS at the exact platform size → export PNG (or deliver HTML with export marked pending) → present options side by side and iterate. Default quantity: 3 options.
- **How it looks:** A banner laid out in three zones — top: logo / value prop; middle: main message + visual; bottom: a single CTA button at bottom-right, minimum 44px tall, with an action verb. Critical content sits in the central 70–80%; nothing important within 50–100px of an edge.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. The deliverable is a still image or HTML banner (one of its 22 art styles, Motion-Ready/Kinetic, is a look, not playback).
- **Mechanism & key values:** Sizes — FB cover 820×312 (mobile 640×360, event 1920×1080), X header 1500×500 (ad 800×418), LinkedIn company 1128×191, personal 1584×396, YouTube 2560×1440 with safe area 1546×423, IG story 1080×1920, post 1080×1080, Pinterest 1000×1500; Google Display: Medium Rectangle 300×250 (highest CTR), Leaderboard 728×90, Wide Skyscraper 160×600, Half Page 300×600, Large Rectangle 336×280, Mobile 320×50, Large Mobile 320×100, Billboard 970×250; web hero 1920×600–1080, section 1200×400, blog header 1200×628, email header 600×200; print roll-up 850×2000mm, step-and-repeat 8×8ft, vinyl 6×3ft, trade show 33×78in. 22 art-direction styles: Minimalist, Bold Typography, Gradient/Color Wash, Photo-Based, Illustrated, Geometric, Retro/Vintage, Glassmorphism, 3D/Sculptural, Neon/Cyberpunk, Duotone, Editorial, Collage, Retro Futurism, Expressive/Anti-Design, Digi-Cute/Kawaii, Tactile, Data/Infographic, Dark Mode/Moody, Flat, Nature/Organic, Motion-Ready/Kinetic. Rules: max 2 typefaces, body ≥16px, headline ≥32px, contrast ≥4.5:1, max 7 words per line and 3 lines for ads; ad text <20% of image (Meta); social covers 60/40 image-to-text; print 300 DPI (150 large format), CMYK, 3–5mm bleed, 70pt+ headlines at 3–5m viewing distance, 1pt per foot rule. Generated visuals must contain no text or letters. File naming `assets/banners/{campaign}/{style}-{width}x{height}.png`, optional YYMMDD prefix.
- **Reference / source:** UI/UX Pro Max family; platform size specifications as listed above. No external sites named.
- **Best for:** Graphics around a site — social covers, ad creatives, email headers, hero-adjacent banners — not page sections themselves.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0012⟧

## ⟦S0013⟧ slides — UI/UX Pro Max (uupm.cc) — skills
- **What it is:** A standalone HTML slide-deck skill: full-viewport 16:9 decks with keyboard/click navigation, 25 layouts, 15 deck strategies and 25 copywriting formulas. Its four references substantially duplicate the slides material inside ⟦S0008⟧ design.
- **How it looks:** A dark deck (default background #0D0D0D), one slide filling the screen, a large gradient headline — `clamp(32px, 6vw, 80px)`, 135deg gradient text — Space Grotesk headings with Inter body, a 3px progress bar along the top, and 40px circular navigation buttons near the bottom.
- **Frame by frame:** Click / ArrowRight / Space → the current slide fades out (opacity 0, visibility hidden), the next fades in (transition: opacity 0.4s), and the progress bar width animates over 0.3s. Content entrances: fadeUp 0.6s ease-out from translateY(30px); scaleIn 0.5s from scale(0.9); number count-up 1s; staggered children fadeUp 0.5s with delays 0.1 / 0.2 / 0.3 / 0.4s.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Desktop letterboxed to 16:9 (`max-width: calc(100vh * 16 / 9)`); slides absolutely stacked, content centred in `.slide-content` with gap 16px; slide padding 60px (32px/24px at ≤768px, 24px/16px at ≤480px); nav buttons 40px circles (32px mobile) at bottom 30px; keyboard ArrowRight/Space/ArrowLeft, click advances. Charts via Chart.js 4.4.1 CDN (example line chart: tension 0.4, borderWidth 3, fill at 10% alpha). 25 layouts, 14 detailed with animation mapping (Feature Grid 3-col gap 24px → 2-col ≤768px → 1-col ≤480px; Metrics 4-col gap 16px; split 1fr 1fr gap 48px → 24px; Big Number with animate-count; popular-plan highlight scale 1.05; logo rows in grayscale). 15 strategies with slide counts and emotion arcs (YC Seed 10–12, Guy Kawasaki 10, Series A 12–15, Product Demo 5–8, Sales Pitch 7–10, QBR 10–15, Conference 15–25, Workshop 20–40, Webinar 20–30); Duarte Sparkline alternation with breaks at 1/3 and 2/3. 25 copywriting formulas (PAS, AIDA, FAB, Cost of Inaction, Before-After-Bridge among those detailed) mapped to slide types and emotions.
- **Reference / source:** UI/UX Pro Max family (references duplicated from ⟦S0008⟧); names Nancy Duarte's Sparkline method and Guy Kawasaki's 10-slide pattern; Chart.js.
- **Best for:** Pitch decks and presentation pages — not homepage sections, though its Big Number / metrics treatments and grayscale logo rows transfer directly to proof sections.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0013⟧

## ⟦S0014⟧ app-interface.csv — UI/UX Pro Max — lookup databases
- **What it is:** A lookup table of 32 native-app interface rules (iOS / Android / React Native); each row is one issue with a description, a Do, a Don't, good and bad code examples, and a severity.
- **How it looks:** What the table lets a builder produce: app screens with 44pt (iOS) / 48dp (Android) touch targets and ≥8dp spacing between them, bottom tab bars of 3–5 items, a loading indicator on any operation over 300ms, inline validation on blur or submit (never per keystroke), and base text at 14–16pt that scales with Dynamic Type / fontScale.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. (The motion values the table prescribes are in the Mechanism field.)
- **Mechanism & key values:** Columns: No, Category, Issue, Keywords, Platform (iOS/Android/React Native), Description, Do, Don't, Code Example Good, Code Example Bad, Severity. Key values: micro-interactions 150–300ms, ease-out on enter / ease-in on exit (good example: 200ms Easing.out(Easing.quad); bad: 800ms linear); back navigation = goBack preserving state; safe-area insets respected; semantic tokens (not hardcoded colours) for dark mode; any drag interaction needs a named Move up / Move down button alternative; authentication must allow password managers, passkeys and paste. Note the platform split: web targets are judged separately at 24×24 CSS px (WCAG 2.5.8), not by the 44pt/48dp native numbers.
- **Reference / source:** UI/UX Pro Max — lookup databases. None named beyond the platform conventions the numbers come from.
- **Best for:** Native app screens, not trade websites — but its touch-target, validation-timing and loading rules transfer to mobile web forms and tap targets.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0014⟧

## ⟦S0015⟧ charts.csv — UI/UX Pro Max — lookup databases
- **What it is:** A lookup table of 25 chart types: for each data type, the best chart, secondary options, when to use and not use it, data-volume thresholds, colour guidance, accessibility risk and fallback, and the library to build it with.
- **How it looks:** What the table lets a builder produce: the right chart for the data at the right size — a trend line in #0080FF under a 20%-opacity fill, a waterfall with green increases #4CAF50 and red decreases #F44336, a funnel of 3–8 stages — always with a visible data-table fallback and a keyboard path, never colour alone.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. (Interactivity level is a data column, not an animation spec.)
- **Mechanism & key values:** Columns: No, Data Type, Keywords, Best Chart Type, Secondary Options, When to Use, When NOT to Use, Data Volume Threshold, Color Guidance, Accessibility Grade (deprecated), Accessibility Risk, Accessibility Notes, A11y Fallback, Library Recommendation, Interactive Level. Thresholds and colours: Trend/Line — <1000 points SVG, ≥1000 Canvas + downsampling, >10000 aggregate; Bar — <20 categories vertical, 20–50 horizontal, >50 paginated table, sorted descending; Pie/Donut — max 6 slices, largest at 12 o'clock, risk high; Scatter — <500 SVG, 500–5000 Canvas at 0.6–0.8 opacity, >5000 hexbin; Heatmap — up to 10,000 cells, calendar 365 cells in SVG; Choropleth — <1000 regions SVG, ≥1000 Canvas/WebGL (Deck.gl); Forecast — actual solid #0080FF, forecast dashed #FF9500, band 15% opacity, history 30–90 days, horizon ≤30% of axis; Anomaly — normal #0080FF, marker #FF0000, alert band #FFF3CD; Treemap — <200 SVG, 200–1000 Canvas, white separators 2–3px, risk high; Sankey — <50 flows SVG, flow opacity 0.4–0.6; Waterfall — 4–12 bars, start #2196F3, end #0D47A1, dashed running-total line; Radar — max 2–3 datasets, 5–8 axes, fill 20–30%; Candlestick — bullish #26A69A, bearish #EF5350, volume at 40% opacity, max 500 candles visible; Network — ≤100 nodes SVG, 101–500 Canvas, >500 clustering, edges #90A4AE at 60%, highlight #F59E0B, risk high; Box plot — fill #BBDEFB, border #1976D2, median #D32F2F; Bullet — ranges #FFCDD2 / #FFF9C4 / #C8E6C9, bar #1976D2, black 3px target marker; Waffle — 10×10 grid, 2–3px cell gaps, max 3–5 categories; Sunburst — each level 15–20% lighter; 3D — Deck.gl up to 1M points, Three.js LOD beyond 50,000, opacity 0.4, mandatory 2D fallback, risk high; Streaming — buffer last 60–300s, pulse #00FF00 on dark / #0080FF on light; Word cloud — 50–5000 terms, positive #22C55E / negative #EF4444 / neutral #94A3B8, risk high; Process map — <30 nodes SVG, 30–100 Canvas, >100 filter to top 80% of cases, happy path #10B981 thick, deviations #F59E0B thin, bottleneck #EF4444. Gauge/Bullet rows require text-labelled zones (red→yellow→green never by colour alone). Libraries named: Chart.js, Recharts, D3.js, ApexCharts, Plotly, Lightweight Charts.
- **Reference / source:** UI/UX Pro Max — lookup databases; chart libraries as listed above.
- **Best for:** Any data display — stats/proof sections (review counts, jobs completed, response times) and dashboards. Rarely the centrepiece of a trade homepage, but it decides how any numbers on one are drawn.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0015⟧

## ⟦S0016⟧ colors.csv — UI/UX Pro Max — lookup databases
- **What it is:** A lookup table of 192 complete colour palettes, one per product type; each row fills every semantic slot — primary, secondary, accent, background, foreground, card, muted, border, destructive, ring, plus the on-colour for each — with hex values.
- **How it looks:** What the table lets a builder produce: a whole site's colour system from a single pick — e.g. Home Services (Plumber/Electrician): blues #1E40AF / #3B82F6 with urgent-orange accent #EA580C ("Professional blue + urgent orange"); Construction/Architecture: industrial greys #64748B / #94A3B8 with safety-orange accent #EA580C; Luxury: near-black #1C1917 with gold accent #A16207.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Columns: No, Product Type, Primary, On Primary, Secondary, On Secondary, Accent, On Accent, Background, Foreground, Card, Card Foreground, Muted, Muted Foreground, Border, Destructive, On Destructive, Ring, Notes. Examples: SaaS (General) — primary #2563EB, secondary #3B82F6, accent #EA580C, background #F8FAFC, foreground #1E293B, border #E2E8F0, destructive #DC2626 ("Trust blue + orange CTA contrast"); Financial Dashboard — dark background #020617, card #0E1223, accent #22C55E; Real Estate — #0F766E with accent #0369A1. Many Notes record contrast fixes of the form "[Accent adjusted from #F97316]" — the table's accents were pre-adjusted for contrast. The 192 rows span SaaS, dashboards, health, trades, apps and games, ending with niche platforms (rows 162–192: wiki, auction, LMS, telemedicine, ticketing, and similar).
- **Reference / source:** UI/UX Pro Max — lookup databases. None named.
- **Best for:** Palette selection for a whole site or a single section; the construction and home-services rows are the direct fit for roofer / HVAC / remodel sites.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0016⟧

## ⟦S0017⟧ icons.csv — UI/UX Pro Max — lookup databases
- **What it is:** A lookup table of 105 icon rows: 100 individual Phosphor icons with import code and usage rules, 4 per-style icon-system configurations, and 1 icon-selection guideline.
- **How it looks:** What the table lets a builder produce: one consistent outline icon set used at size 20, weight "regular" — house for home, phone for call, map-pin for service areas, star for reviews, shield for guarantees — each icon either decorative beside visible text or carrying its own text alternative.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. (One row, circle-notch, is the loading spinner and is used with animate-spin.)
- **Mechanism & key values:** Columns: No, Category, Icon Name, Keywords, Library, Import Code, Usage, Best For, Style, Semantic Role, Allowed Contexts. Rows 1–100: Phosphor icons, all Outline style, imported from `@phosphor-icons/react` (e.g. `import { List } from '@phosphor-icons/react'`), used at `size={20} weight="regular"`. Categories: Navigation, Action, Status, Communication, User, Media, Commerce, Data, Files, Layout, Social, Device, Security, Location, Time, Development. Every row repeats the context rule: decorative beside visible text → aria-hidden="true"; meaningful without text → text alternative; inside a control → accessible name + state (aria-pressed / aria-expanded). Rows 101–104 are style configs (phosphor-react-native): Bold Typography (icons paired with JetBrains Mono labels, accent #FF3D00, 20px controls / 32px feature anchors, standalone icons only for standard nav), Cyberpunk (accent #00FF88, wrapper shadowOpacity 0.6 / shadowRadius 8, borderRadius 0), Academia (weight "thin", brass #C9A962, circular 1px brass border), Web3 Bitcoin (orange #F7931A, circular BlurView intensity 20, 1px border, shadowOpacity 0.4 / radius 8). Row 105 guideline: prefer the most semantically precise Phosphor icon even outside this subset; Heroicons only as a consistent fallback; one visual family per surface.
- **Reference / source:** UI/UX Pro Max — lookup databases; Phosphor Icons library; Heroicons named as the fallback family.
- **Best for:** Iconography on any section — navigation, service lists, feature grids, contact/CTA blocks, footer.

## ⟦S0018⟧ landing.csv — UI/UX Pro Max — lookup databases
- **What it is:** A lookup table of 34 landing-page patterns; each row gives the pattern's section order, where the primary CTA sits, its colour strategy, the effects to use, and its conversion rules.
- **How it looks:** What the table lets a builder produce: a whole page skeleton — e.g. Hero + Testimonials + CTA with the testimonial band on #F5F5F5 and quotes in italic #666; a Bento Grid Showcase with cards on #F5F5F7; a Before-After Transformation with a comparison slider, the before image muted/grey and the after vibrant.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion as a table. Each pattern's Recommended Effects column names its motion (hero parallax, card hover lift, CTA glow, scroll-triggered storytelling chapters), and every effect carries a reduced-motion condition: parallax disabled, carousels paused (and stopped on focus/hover), and a final readable state presented instead.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Columns: No, Pattern Name, Keywords, Section Order, Primary CTA Placement, Color Strategy, Recommended Effects, Conversion Optimization, Pattern ID, Aliases. Notable values: Hero + Features + CTA — feature cards #FAFAFA, hero parallax, card hover lift, CTA glow; Product Demo + Features — feature icon colour #0080FF, text #222; Funnel 3-Step — step colours 1 red (problem), 2 orange (process), 3 green (solution) plus a progress-bar fill; Comparison Table + CTA — own product highlighted #FFFACD light yellow or green; Lead Magnet + Form — input border #CCCCCC; Pricing Page + CTA — Free grey, Starter blue, Pro green/gold, Enterprise dark, monthly/yearly toggle animation, FAQ accordion; Video-First Hero — autoplay muted, parallax, fade-in, with pause control + poster under reduced motion; Scroll-Triggered Storytelling — ScrollTrigger, parallax layers, chapter transitions; Waitlist/Coming Soon — countdown allowed only if current, verified and dated (no fabricated scarcity); App Store Style — star ratings in gold, device frames, screenshot carousel with keyboard controls; Immersive/Interactive Experience — WebGL/3D with mandatory skip + keyboard + non-3D fallback; Before-After Transformation — slider must also have arrow buttons + keyboard steps so drag is never required; Horizontal Scroll Journey — progress bar #000000, keep a normal vertical path, disable scroll-jacking under reduced motion; Bento Grid Showcase — card background #F5F5F7 or glass, hover scale 1.02, tilt and staggered reveal suppressed under reduced motion; Interactive 3D Configurator — named buttons/keyboard control plus a 2D/spec fallback; Trust & Authority + Conversion — navy/grey, stat counters, logo carousel that pauses. Cross-cutting rules: CTA label ≥4.5:1 against the button fill (7:1 only for an explicit AAA target); social-proof counts only when current, verified and dated.
- **Reference / source:** UI/UX Pro Max — lookup databases. None named.
- **Best for:** Choosing the page-level structure of a homepage (hero → proof → work → process → CTA order) before section-level design; the Trust & Authority + Conversion and Hero + Testimonials + CTA patterns are the direct trade fit.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0018⟧

## ⟦S0019⟧ motion.csv — UI/UX Pro Max — lookup databases
- **What it is:** The motion-data table: 17 ready-to-paste GSAP animation presets across 7 categories (hover, scroll reveal, stagger, page transition, parallax, loading, carousel/auto-rotation), each at a Subtle, Standard or Complex intensity tier.
- **How it looks:** What a visitor sees when these are applied: cards that lift 4px and grow 2% with a soft shadow under the pointer; sections whose children rise 24px and fade in one after another as they scroll into view; a pinned headline scrubbing through the scroll while its background layer drifts up 20%; shimmering skeleton blocks while content loads; a carousel that advances every 5 seconds and stops the moment it is hovered or focused.
- **Frame by frame:** Per preset — Hover: pointer enters → the tween plays → a reverse tween plays on leave. Scroll Reveal: the element crosses the ScrollTrigger start line → children play in with stagger → fully visible end state (subtle tier uses toggleActions 'play none none reverse'). Stagger/SplitText: the headline enters → characters rise from rotateX −40 one by one → the settled line. Page Transition: click → overlay wipe or fade out → navigate → wipe/fade in. Parallax: continuous with scroll, scrubbed. Loading: a looping shimmer or dot bounce until content mounts, then the loop is killed. Carousel: auto-advance every 5000ms → stops on focusin, pointerenter, offscreen (IntersectionObserver), hidden tab, and reduced motion, where the active slide renders as the final state.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Columns: No, Category, Intensity Tier, Keywords, Trigger, Duration, Easing, GSAP Snippet, Framework Notes, Do, Don't, Performance Notes. The 17 presets: (1) Hover Subtle — 150–200ms, power1.out, `y: -1, opacity: 0.9, duration: 0.15`, displacement under 2px, transform/opacity only. (2) Hover Standard — 200–300ms, power2.out, `y: -4, scale: 1.02, boxShadow: '0 12px 24px rgba(0,0,0,0.12)', duration: 0.25`, use gsap.quickTo, always attach the reverse tween. (3) Hover Complex (magnetic) — hover + mousemove, 300–500ms, elastic.out(1, 0.4), pull clamped to ×0.3 of offset from centre, max 1–2 focal elements, named handler + removeEventListener cleanup. (4) Scroll Reveal Subtle — viewport enter, 300–400ms, power1.out, from `opacity: 0, y: 12, duration: 0.35`, start 'top 90%', y offset 8–16px. (5) Scroll Reveal Standard — 400–600ms, power2.out, children from `y: 24, duration: 0.5, stagger: 0.08`, start 'top 85%', don't stagger more than ~8 children. (6) Scroll Reveal Complex (pin/scrub) — scrub 1, pin true, start 'top top', end '+=150%', headline from y 40, background layer to yPercent −20, max 1–2 pinned sections per page. (7) Stagger Subtle — 250–350ms, power1.out, from `y: 8, duration: 0.3, stagger: 0.03` (per-item delay 0.02–0.04s for lists >10). (8) Stagger Standard — 300–450ms, back.out(1.4), from `opacity: 0, scale: 0.92, y: 16, duration: 0.4, stagger: { each: 0.06, from: 'start', grid: 'auto' }` (from 'center' suits bento grids). (9) Stagger Complex (SplitText) — 400–700ms, expo.out, chars from `opacity: 0, y: 20, rotateX: -40, duration: 0.6, stagger: 0.015`, headlines under ~8 words only, split.revert() on cleanup. (10) Page Transition Subtle — route change, 200–300ms, power1.inOut, fade out 0.2s → navigate → fade in 0.2s; exit capped ~250ms and faster than the entrance. (11) Page Transition Standard (overlay wipe) — 400–600ms, power2.inOut, overlay yPercent 0 over 0.4s → navigate → yPercent −100 over 0.4s after delay 0.1; overlay mounted at layout root. (12) Page Transition Complex (Flip) — 500–800ms, expo.inOut, Flip.from duration 0.6, absolute true, zIndex 100; one element pair per navigation. (13) Parallax Subtle — scrub, linear, background layer yPercent 10 (keep delta 5–15), decorative layers only, never text. (14) Parallax Standard — layers at (i+1) × −8 yPercent, scrub 0.5, 3–4 layers max, clip with overflow hidden. (15) Loading Skeleton Subtle — loop 1200–1600ms, sine.inOut, backgroundPosition '200% 0', duration 1.4, repeat −1; kill on mount/unmount, pause offscreen/hidden. (16) Loading Standard — loop 800–1200ms, power1.inOut, loader dots y −8, duration 0.4, stagger each 0.15 yoyo; cap loop under ~1.5s; no elaborate loader for waits under 300ms. (17) Carousel/Auto-Rotation Standard — setInterval 5000ms, one cancellable timer, prev/next + play/pause controls required. Every preset: respect prefers-reduced-motion via gsap.matchMedia and render the final state immediately.
- **Reference / source:** UI/UX Pro Max — lookup databases; GSAP with ScrollTrigger (plus SplitText and Flip plugins) named throughout.
- **Best for:** The motion layer of every section — hero entrances, proof/gallery staggers, a pinned process story, CTA hover states. Pick one intensity tier per site and stay consistent.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0019⟧

## ⟦S0021⟧ react-performance.csv — UI/UX Pro Max — lookup databases
- **What it is:** A lookup table of 44 React / Next.js performance rules; each row is one issue with a description, a Do, a Don't, good and bad code examples, and a severity.
- **How it looks:** Nothing a visitor sees directly — what the table produces is speed: pages that don't flicker before hydration, long lists that stay smooth (content-visibility with a reserved size), and heavy panels that load only when hovered, focused or opened.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. (A code-rules table.)
- **Mechanism & key values:** Columns: No, Category, Issue, Keywords, Platform (React/Next.js), Description, Do, Don't, Code Example Good, Code Example Bad, Severity. Rules by category — Async Waterfall: defer await into branches, Promise.all for independent calls, better-all for partial dependencies, start promises early in API routes, Suspense boundaries. Bundle Size: import directly, not barrel files (good: `lucide-react/dist/esm/icons/check`); next/dynamic lazy loading; defer analytics until after hydration; conditional dynamic imports; preload on hover/focus. Server: React.cache deduplication; LRU cache max 1000 entries, ttl 5×60×1000; minimise RSC serialization (pass only used fields); parallel fetching via component composition; Next.js after() for post-response logging. Client: SWR dedup; shared global listeners via useSWRSubscription. Rerender: defer state reads to callbacks; memo() extraction; primitive effect deps ([user.id], not [user]); derived booleans; functional setState; lazy useState initializer; startTransition. Rendering: animate a wrapper div around an SVG, not the SVG itself; `content-visibility: auto` with `contain-intrinsic-size: 0 80px`; hoist static JSX; inline pre-hydration script to avoid flicker; ternary instead of && for conditional render; the Activity component to preserve toggled state. JS Performance: batch DOM CSS writes via class/cssText; Map index lookups O(1); cache property access, function results and localStorage reads; combine filter/map into one loop; length check before expensive compares; hoist RegExp to module scope; loop min/max in O(n) instead of sorting; Set/Map membership; toSorted() for immutable sorts. Advanced: useEffectEvent for non-reactive values in effects; latest-value refs synced after commit, never mutated during render.
- **Reference / source:** UI/UX Pro Max — lookup databases; the React, Next.js and SWR APIs named inside the rules themselves.
- **Best for:** Performance hardening of React builds — background infrastructure under any section. Not applicable to single-file HTML previews.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0021⟧

## ⟦S0022⟧ styles.csv — UI/UX Pro Max — lookup databases
- **What it is:** The style catalogue: rows numbered to 89, each a named visual style (General, Landing Page, BI/Analytics, Mobile, or Platform/System) with its colours, effects, best-for and do-not-use-for, performance cost, accessibility risk, an implementation checklist, and ready design-system variables.
- **How it looks:** What the table lets a builder produce: a named style applied with real numbers — e.g. Bento Box Grid: 4-column grid, 200px auto-rows, 16px gaps, 24px radius, page background #F5F5F7, cards scaling to 1.02 on hover; Neubrutalism: 3px solid black borders, hard shadows 4px 4px 0 #000, colours #FFEB3B / #FF5252 / #2196F3; Glassmorphism: blur 10–20px over rgba(255,255,255,0.15) with a 1px border of rgba(255,255,255,0.2).
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion as a table. Each row's Effects & Animation column specifies that style's own motion (e.g. Motion-Driven: 300–400ms transitions, 3–5 parallax layers; Kinetic Typography: 1s duration, 0.05s letter delay, 100ms typing).
- **Mechanism & key values:** Roughly 30 columns, including Primary Colors, Secondary Colors, Effects & Animation, Best For, Do Not Use For, Light Mode ✓, Dark Mode ✓, Performance (cost|drivers), Accessibility (risk|requires), Mobile-Friendly, Conversion-Focused, Framework Compatibility, Era/Origin, Complexity, AI Prompt Keywords, CSS/Technical Keywords, Implementation Checklist, Design System Variables, Style ID, Aliases, Status, Parent Style ID, Replacement Domain / Replacement ID, Preferred Mode. Sample values: Minimalism & Swiss Style — 12–16 column grid, 2rem spacing, radius 0, no shadow (1950s Swiss); Neumorphism — radius 12–16px, dual shadows −5px −5px 15px / 5px 5px 15px, press 150ms, accessibility risk high; Brutalism — radius 0, transitions none/0s, weight 700+, pure primaries #FF0000 / #0000FF / #FFFF00; Dark Mode (OLED) — #000000 / #121212, contrast 7:1+; Accessible & Ethical — contrast 7:1+, type 16px+, focus ring 3–4px, targets 44×44px; Claymorphism — radius 16–24px, borders 3–4px, bounce cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56); Aurora UI — gradient loops 8–12s, background-size 200% 200%; Flat Design — no shadows or gradients, 4–6 solid colours, radius 0–4px, transitions 150–200ms; Exaggerated Minimalism — type clamp(3rem, 10vw, 12rem), weight 900, tracking −0.05em, spacing 8rem+; Parallax Storytelling — layer speeds background 0.3 / mid 0.6 / foreground 1, 100vh sections, 600ms transitions, perspective 1px; Data-Dense Dashboard — 12-col grid, gap 8px, padding 12px, font 12–14px, table row 36px, sidebar 240px, header 56px; Interactive Cursor Design — cursor 20px, hover scale 1.5, magnetic distance 100px, trail length 10. Lifecycle data matters: the Landing Page rows 20–27 are all marked deprecated, each pointing to a landing.csv replacement (e.g. Hero-Centric Design: min-height 100vh, headline clamp(2rem, 5vw, 4rem), CTA padding 1rem 2rem, hover scale 1.05 → landing pattern hero-centric-design); BI/Analytics rows 29–37 are supplemental children of Data-Dense Dashboard (Heat Map: cool #0080FF → hot #FF0000, cell 24px; Executive Dashboard: KPI font 48px, 4–6 KPIs; Real-Time Monitoring: pulse 2s infinite, update interval 5s); Mobile rows 69–85 carry full React Native specs (Bauhaus mobile: hard shadow 4px 4px 0 #121212, 2px black borders, Outfit 900 uppercase headlines, mechanical press with instant 0ms transitions; Kinetic Brutalism mobile: acid yellow #DFE104, infinite 5s linear marquee, hero parallax scale 1.0→1.3); Platform rows 86–89 cover Fluent 2, Shopify Polaris, Adobe Spectrum and Spectrum 2.
- **Reference / source:** UI/UX Pro Max — lookup databases; the Era/Origin column names real movements and systems (1950s Swiss design, 1919 Bauhaus, Apple Liquid Glass 2025, Google Material Design 3, Microsoft Fluent 2, Shopify Polaris, Adobe Spectrum).
- **Best for:** Choosing — and then faithfully executing — the visual style of a whole site or one section variant. The Do Not Use For column is the trade-fit filter: several styles explicitly exclude trust-critical or conservative contexts.
