## ⟦S0049⟧ Web Interface Guidelines — full rule set (command.md) — PART 04 — Vercel
- **What it is:** The live rule file that the web-design-guidelines skill fetches before every review: roughly 120 concrete UI rules grouped into Accessibility, Focus States, Forms, Animation, Typography, Content Handling, Images, Performance, Navigation & State, Touch & Interaction, Safe Areas & Layout, Dark Mode & Theming, Locale & i18n, Hydration Safety, Hover & Interactive States, and Content & Copy — plus a flag-list of anti-patterns and a fixed terse output format (grouped by file, `file:line`, "✓ pass" for clean files).
- **How it looks:** Applied to a page, the visitor sees: a visible focus ring that appears for keyboard navigation but not on mouse click (`:focus-visible`); form errors sitting inline beside the field that caused them, with focus moved to the first error on submit; headings wrapped evenly with no widows (`text-wrap: balance`); number columns aligned in tabular figures; images holding their exact space before they load, so the page never jumps (explicit `width`/`height`); input placeholders ending with "…" and showing an example pattern; loading text written as "Loading…", "Saving…".
- **Frame by frame:** Motion rules only: animations animate `transform`/`opacity` only (compositor-friendly), never `transition: all` — properties are listed explicitly; `transform-origin` set correctly; SVG transforms go on a `<g>` wrapper with `transform-box: fill-box; transform-origin: center`; animations must be interruptible — they respond to user input mid-animation; autoplay motion running more than 5 seconds alongside other content needs pause, stop or hide controls; `prefers-reduced-motion` gets a reduced variant or disables motion entirely, including muted decorative loops.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Accessibility: `aria-label` on icon-only buttons; `<label>` or `aria-label` on every form control; `aria-live="polite"` for async updates (toasts, validation); semantic HTML before ARIA; hierarchical h1–h6 plus a skip link; `scroll-margin-top` on heading anchors; decorative icons `aria-hidden="true"`. Focus: never `outline: none` without a focus replacement; `:focus-within` for compound controls; sticky headers/footers must not cover the focused element. Forms: correct `type` (`email`, `tel`, `url`, `number`) and `inputmode`; `autocomplete` and meaningful `name` on inputs; never block paste; `spellCheck={false}` on emails, codes, usernames; checkbox/radio label and control share one hit target; submit stays enabled until the request starts, spinner during it; warn before navigating away with unsaved changes. Images: below-fold `loading="lazy"`; above-fold critical images `priority` / `fetchpriority="high"`. Performance: virtualize lists over 50 items (`virtua` or `content-visibility: auto`); no layout reads (`getBoundingClientRect`, `offsetHeight`…) in render; batch DOM reads/writes; `<link rel="preconnect">` for CDN domains; critical fonts preloaded with `font-display: swap`; prefer `<video autoplay muted loop playsinline>` over animated GIFs. Navigation & State: filters, tabs, pagination and expanded panels reflected in URL query params; real `<a>`/`<Link>` so Cmd/Ctrl+click and middle-click work; destructive actions need a confirmation modal or undo window, never immediate. Touch: `touch-action: manipulation`; intentional `-webkit-tap-highlight-color`; `overscroll-behavior: contain` in modals/drawers/sheets; page-level `overscroll-behavior: none` on `<html>` only inside `@media (pointer: fine)`; during drag, disable text selection and set `inert` on dragged elements; gestures need tap/click and keyboard alternatives. Safe areas: `env(safe-area-inset-*)` on full-bleed layouts; flex/grid over JS measurement. Dark mode: `color-scheme: dark` on `<html>`; `<meta name="theme-color">` matching the page background; explicit background/color on native `<select>`. Locale: `Intl.DateTimeFormat` and `Intl.NumberFormat`, never hardcoded formats; language from `Accept-Language`/`navigator.languages`, not IP; `translate="no"` on brand names and code tokens. Typography: curly quotes, "…" not "...", non-breaking spaces in values like `10 MB`, `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` for comparisons. Copy: active voice, Title Case for headings/buttons, numerals for counts ("8 deployments"), specific button labels ("Save API Key", not "Continue"), error messages that include the fix, second person. Anti-patterns flagged on sight: `user-scalable=no`, paste blocking, `transition: all`, bare `outline-none`, `<div onClick>` navigation, images without dimensions, unvirtualized large `.map()` lists, unlabeled inputs, hardcoded date formats, unjustified `autoFocus`, animated GIFs where compressed video fits.
- **Reference / source:** Vercel's Web Interface Guidelines (PART 04 — Vercel) — this file is the stored copy of the live `command.md` rule file the web-design-guidelines skill fetches before every review.
- **Best for:** The pre-ship review checklist for any page or section — especially quote/estimate forms (Forms + Focus rules), hero and gallery images (Images + Performance rules), navigation and tabs (Navigation & State rules), and any animated section (Animation rules). One of the few entries in this range that directly governs what a visitor sees and feels on trade sites.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0049⟧

## ⟦S0050⟧ baseline-ui — PART 05 — UI Skills — ibelick
- **What it is:** An opinionated "deslop" constraint set for AI-generated UI, invoked as `/baseline-ui` (apply to all UI work in the conversation) or `/baseline-ui <file>` (review mode: output violations quoting the exact line/snippet, one short sentence on why it matters, and a concrete code-level fix). Rules are stated as MUST / SHOULD / NEVER across Stack, Components, Interaction, Animation, Typography, Layout, Performance and Design.
- **How it looks:** A cleaned-up, restrained interface: one accent colour per view; flat surfaces — no gradients at all unless explicitly requested, never purple or multicolor gradients, no glow effects as primary affordances; shadows from Tailwind's default scale; headings balanced across lines (`text-balance`), body text set `text-pretty`; data in tabular numbers; square elements sized with a single `size-*` class; empty states showing one clear next action; loading shown as structural skeletons; destructive actions sitting behind a confirmation dialog; errors appearing next to the control that caused them.
- **Frame by frame:** Motion is deliberately minimal and only present when explicitly requested in the first place: entrance and micro-animations use `tw-animate-css` or `motion/react`; entrance easing is `ease-out`; interaction feedback never exceeds 200ms; only compositor properties animate — `transform` and `opacity` — never layout properties (`width`, `height`, `top`, `left`, `margin`, `padding`), and paint properties (`background`, `color`) only for small local UI like text and icons; no custom easing curves unless explicitly requested; looping animations pause when off-screen; `prefers-reduced-motion` respected; large images and full-screen surfaces should not be animated.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Stack: Tailwind CSS defaults (custom values only if already present or explicitly requested); `motion/react` (formerly framer-motion) when JavaScript animation is required; `tw-animate-css` for entrance and micro-animations; `cn` utility (clsx + tailwind-merge) for class logic. Components: accessible primitives for anything with keyboard or focus behaviour (Base UI preferred for new primitives, React Aria, Radix); use the project's existing primitives first; never mix primitive systems within the same interaction surface; `aria-label` on icon-only buttons; never rebuild keyboard or focus behaviour by hand unless explicitly requested. Interaction: AlertDialog for destructive or irreversible actions; `h-dvh` never `h-screen`; respect `safe-area-inset` for fixed elements; never block paste in inputs/textareas. Typography: `tabular-nums` for data; `truncate` or `line-clamp` for dense UI; never modify letter-spacing (`tracking-*`) unless explicitly requested. Layout: a fixed z-index scale, no arbitrary `z-*` values. Performance: never animate large `blur()` or `backdrop-filter` surfaces; never apply `will-change` outside an active animation; never use `useEffect` for anything expressible as render logic. Design: use existing theme or Tailwind colour tokens before introducing new ones.
- **Reference / source:** ibelick (PART 05 — UI Skills — ibelick). Named inside: Tailwind CSS, motion/react, tw-animate-css, Base UI (base-ui.com), React Aria, Radix, clsx, tailwind-merge.
- **Best for:** A fast polish/cleanup pass over any built page before delivery, and as guardrails while generating forms, cards and dashboards. Note the tension: its restraint rules (no animation unless requested, no gradients, one accent) suit product UI; on award-style immersive trade-site builds they should be applied selectively, not wholesale.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0050⟧

## ⟦S0051⟧ component-canvas — PART 05 — UI Skills — ibelick
- **What it is:** A build procedure for a full-screen interactive canvas that displays a project's existing UI components and all their variants for side-by-side exploration, with pan and zoom. The canvas wraps components and never changes them: no edits to component source, exports, styles, hooks or behaviour, and components must not import or depend on canvas code.
- **How it looks:** The viewport is filled with a plain background — no background dots, decorative cards, page menus, instruction banners or selection tools. Components sit inside wide groups; every group has the same padding and corner radius and a thin dashed border in an existing muted colour at roughly 25% opacity, with the group's plain title in muted text placed 8px above the border. Inside a group, equal-width example slots fill each row with generous horizontal and vertical gaps, components shown at their real size, spread out without being enlarged. In a comparison, everything is held constant except the one prop under test — e.g. every button in a size comparison reads "Continue" with `variant="default"` and only `size` changes slot to slot. Fit-all and reset icon buttons with accessible names stay reachable even when the view is lost; a light/dark toggle appears only if the project already supports themes.
- **Frame by frame:** The camera moves, the components do not: drag on empty canvas space pans; mouse wheel and trackpad pinch zoom around the cursor; touch pans and pinches; gesture transforms are applied at most once per animation frame; keyboard camera navigation moves the view, and keyboard focus outside the visible area is revealed by camera movement; native page scrolling never moves the canvas. Inside the previews, clicks, typing, text selection, button/switch activation, focus and nested scrolling all keep working natively, and portal content (modals, menus) stays in its native root at screen-space size, correctly positioned and clickable at several zoom levels.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Build order: 1) minimal canvas route with one group and one component, confirm it works; 2) remaining groups with sample data; 3) variant comparisons, then advanced gestures and persistence, one feature at a time. Variants: show every supported named variant and useful state in scope, read from the components' public APIs (styles, text/icon sizes, orientation, placement, alignment, modality, collapse modes); never invent variants or generate every prop combination — list omissions and why; test hover, focus and pressed states through real pointer and keyboard input, not added classes; keep each component's own state styling (disabled opacity, checked colour). Safety: previews mount only with test data, mock services or existing callback props blocking live calls and real writes — never production credentials or data; if safe isolation is unavailable, omit the example and say why. Camera: handle pointer-count changes, cancellation, lost capture, window blur and hidden tabs; release captures and clean up listeners/observers/timers/animation frames on teardown; validate camera values and keep them in bounds; groups cannot be dragged and fitting never rearranges groups. Persistence: save only the camera, in a versioned format under a storage key per project/workspace; handle malformed/oversized data and quota errors; reset restores the camera only, never preview state or drafts. Reporting: every build/review ends with the headings Changed / Checks run / Not working or not tested / Decisions made — and a check counts as passing only if it was actually run.
- **Reference / source:** ibelick (PART 05 — UI Skills — ibelick). No external sites named.
- **Best for:** Internal design-system QA — comparing button, card and form variants side by side before committing to one (the same job as comparing the 1·2·3 versions of a section during a build review). A builder's tool, not a visitor-facing page pattern.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0051⟧

## ⟦S0052⟧ create-canvas — PART 05 — UI Skills — ibelick
- **What it is:** A build procedure for a freeform exploration canvas: a workspace where anything — components, layouts, content — is placed as named, movable live previews and iterated through conversation. A typed registry in the source files is the single source of truth: each entry defines a stable ID, a unique readable name, the component, safe test data, initial position and dimensions.
- **How it looks:** A quiet, full-viewport workspace: plain background, subtle preview boundaries, minimal fixed controls — pan, zoom, zoom-in/out buttons, fit-all, reset-camera and one global theme selector. Every item is shown at its intended dimensions, never stretched into oversized frames. Above each preview sits its readable name as plain text (e.g. "Pricing card · compact") — not button-styled, with a visible move handle beside it. Clicking, pressing Enter/Space on, or touching the name copies that exact name (never an ID, code or URL) and shows a brief "Copied" announcement only after success; the name stays visible during the feedback. No decorative cards, banners or background patterns anywhere.
- **Frame by frame:** One finger or the mouse drags an item by its handle, with pointer movement converted to canvas coordinates at the current zoom. Dragging empty space pans; Ctrl/Meta+wheel and trackpad pinch zoom with the canvas point under the pointer held fixed; Space + primary-button drag and middle-button drag pan anywhere, including over previews — and after such a pan, the control under the pointer does not activate, no label is copied and no link is followed. Two-finger trackpad pan works over empty space and previews; a nested scroll area scrolls itself first when it can scroll in the gesture direction, otherwise the canvas pans. Camera transforms are written at most once per animation frame, kept outside component-wide React state so camera movement never re-renders the previews. Moving items, copying names, changing theme or moving the camera never remounts a preview or erases its input.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Registry discipline: adding an item must not require changes to camera or gesture code; membership, names, dimensions and implementations live in source only — browser storage must never create or hide items, and stored strings are never evaluated as code. "Try another version" preserves the original and gives the variation a new ID, unique name and independent state; "change this version" updates in place; removal removes only that registry entry. Comparison discipline: one feature changes at a time with data, content, dimensions and global theme held constant. Layout saving: only the camera, the supported theme preference, and positions keyed by stable registry ID are saved — a small versioned document under a project- and canvas-specific key; saves happen after gestures or on a bounded debounce, never on every pointer event; stale IDs are ignored, new entries always shown; malformed data, unavailable storage and quota errors fall back safely. Gesture separation: canvas shortcuts apply to the shell only and never steal keys from preview controls; Space-to-pan is not armed while an interactive control has focus; modal portals stay outside canvas gesture handling; `overscroll-behavior-x: none` is applied to the viewport while the route is active (blocking Chrome horizontal history swipes) and prior document styles are restored on teardown; no `pushState` history traps or patched browser APIs. Performance: finite, bounded camera coordinates and zoom; cached measured bounds; no per-frame measurement of every preview; virtualization/memoization only with profiling evidence. Testing honesty: profile a representative populated canvas before claiming smooth performance and record preview count, browser, device and measurements; a test counts as passed only if run. Omit unless requested: resizing, width presets, comparison arrangements, drawing, connectors, catalogs, property editors, multi-selection, snapping, undo/redo.
- **Reference / source:** ibelick (PART 05 — UI Skills — ibelick). No external sites named.
- **Best for:** Design exploration sessions — laying out several section or layout alternatives side by side at real size and iterating on them by name in conversation ("change this version", "try another version"). A builder's workspace tool, not a visitor-facing pattern.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0052⟧

## ⟦S0053⟧ create-design-md — UI Skills registry
- **What it is:** Creates or updates a `DESIGN.md` file that documents one product's or website's design language — its color, type, spacing, shape and component rules — either from a source repository or reconstructed from a public URL. It records the design system that governs a site, not every value that happens to exist in it.
- **How it looks:** The output is a document, not a screen. It opens with YAML frontmatter holding flat token mappings (e.g. `typography.display` with `fontFamily`, `fontSize: 64px`, `lineHeight: 64px`, `fontWeight: 510`; `rounded.base: 0.625rem` when the source has a single `--radius`), then Markdown sections in a fixed order: Overview, then only the supported ones of Colors, Themes, Typography, Layout, Elevation & Depth, Shapes, Components, Do's and Don'ts. Every prose sentence must change an implementation choice; there are no token inventories or component lists in the prose.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Two modes (repository mode writes at the repo root; URL mode samples up to three same-origin pages at desktop and mobile widths and works from computed styles and loaded CSS). Evidence pipeline: `role → value → source → scope → recurrence → confidence`, with a three-proof gate for URL claims (observation, basis, consequence). Token names must match `^[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9-]*$`. Validated with `npx @google/design.md spec`, `lint` and `export`; export targets are `css-tailwind` (Tailwind v4), `json-tailwind` (v3) and `dtcg` otherwise, with expected output families `--color-*`, `--font-*`, `--text-*`, `--radius-*`, `--spacing-*`.
- **Reference / source:** UI Skills collection; built on Google's DESIGN.md format and the `@google/design.md` CLI.
- **Best for:** Up-front documentation for any build — writing the design-system brief a build session works from, or reverse-documenting an existing site (e.g. a client's current site) before a redesign. Not a visual section technique.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0053⟧

## ⟦S0054⟧ fixing-accessibility — UI Skills registry
- **What it is:** An audit-and-fix rulebook for HTML accessibility: accessible names, keyboard access, focus and dialogs, semantics, forms and errors, live-region announcements, contrast and states, media and motion. Applied to a file, it reports violations with the exact snippet, why it matters, and a minimal code-level fix.
- **How it looks:** What the visitor experiences after fixes: every icon-only button has a spoken name (the close button's SVG is `aria-hidden`, the button carries `aria-label="Close"`); a visible focus ring follows Tab order through menus and dialogs; a dialog traps focus while open and returns focus to the button that opened it on close; a form error appears as text tied to its field (`aria-describedby` + `aria-invalid="true"`), not just a red border; disabled states never rely on color alone.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion of its own; it governs focus behaviour and requires non-essential motion to respect `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Nine rule categories in priority order (accessible names and keyboard access are critical). Hard rules copied from the source: no `tabindex` greater than 0; Escape must close dialogs/overlays; modals trap focus and set initial focus inside; lists use `ul`/`ol` with `li`; heading levels never skip; expandable controls use `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`; critical form errors use `aria-live`; decorative icons are `aria-hidden`; prefer native elements (`<button>`, `<a>`, `<input>`) over role-based hacks, and prefer minimal targeted fixes over rewrites.
- **Reference / source:** UI Skills collection; WCAG-oriented practice, no single site named.
- **Best for:** The accessibility QA pass on any interactive surface — quote forms, navigation, galleries, dialogs and CTA sections on trade sites (roofing, siding, remodeling, HVAC alike).
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0054⟧

## ⟦S0055⟧ fixing-metadata — UI Skills registry
- **What it is:** An audit-and-fix rulebook for page `<head>` metadata: titles, descriptions, canonical URLs, robots, Open Graph and Twitter cards, favicons and manifest, JSON-LD structured data, and locale/hreflang alternates.
- **How it looks:** Nothing changes on the page itself. What a visitor sees is the result elsewhere: the page's title and plain-text description as the search-result snippet, and the social share card — Open Graph title, description and an absolute-URL image at a stable aspect ratio — when the link is pasted into a message or feed. Title, description, canonical and `og:url` all agree with each other.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Eight priority categories, correctness/duplication and tool boundaries rated critical. Defaults copied from the source: `twitter:card` is `summary_large_image` by default; `og:type` is usually `website` or `article`; staging/preview pages should be `noindex` by default; JSON-LD only when it maps to real rendered content — never invent ratings, reviews or prices; metadata defined in one place per page, deterministic, with safe defaults for every page; social cards verified on a real URL, not localhost.
- **Reference / source:** UI Skills collection. No external site named.
- **Best for:** Every page's head — homepage and inner pages of any trade site, and especially shareable preview pages whose links get sent to clients.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0055⟧

## ⟦S0056⟧ fixing-motion-performance — UI Skills registry
- **What it is:** An audit-and-fix rulebook for animation performance: it finds layout thrashing, scroll-driven jank, oversized blur and wrong-property animation, and replaces each with the cheapest rendering path that keeps the same visual.
- **How it looks:** The same animations, minus the stutter. A panel that used to resize (animating `width`) now slides by `transform`, so surrounding content no longer reflows frame by frame; a scroll reveal is tied to the scroll position itself via a view timeline instead of a JavaScript scroll listener, so it tracks the scrollbar exactly; a FLIP list change measures positions once, jumps, then glides from the old spot to the new one via transform.
- **Frame by frame:** Scroll-linked reveal (the skill's own fix pattern): user scrolls → the element's `fade-in` animation advances in direct proportion to its travel through the viewport (`animation-timeline: view()`) → fully visible when scrolled into place, with no scroll-event code running. FLIP: read start rect → apply the end state → read end rect → invert with a transform offset → play the transform to zero over `0.3s` → element settles in its real layout position.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Rendering tiers — composite (`transform`, `opacity`) is cheapest, then paint (color, borders, gradients, masks, filters), then layout (size, position, flex/grid). Never-patterns: no interleaved layout reads/writes in one frame, no animation driven from `scrollTop`/`scrollY`/scroll events, no `requestAnimationFrame` loop without a stop condition. Animated blur stays small (`<=8px`), short and one-time, never continuous or on large surfaces. `will-change` used temporarily and surgically. Fixes shown verbatim: `transition: width 0.3s` → `transition: transform 0.3s`; JS scroll fade → `.reveal { animation: fade-in linear; animation-timeline: view(); }`.
- **Reference / source:** UI Skills collection. No external site named.
- **Best for:** Performance QA on any animated section — pinned scroll stories, parallax heroes, marquees and reveal-heavy pages — before delivery, especially for mid-range phones.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0056⟧

## ⟦S0057⟧ improve-ui — UI Skills registry
- **What it is:** A strictly read-only audit of one existing product surface against its own design evidence (its `DESIGN.md`, tokens, primitives and variants). It proves or discards UI problems, reports at most three findings, and — only for changes the user selects — writes self-contained implementation plans under `design-plans/` for another agent to execute.
- **How it looks:** No screen change; the deliverable is a report plus plan files. The report states the audited surface's design language (sources, documented decisions, governing owners, explicit exceptions), then a findings table — Problem, Evidence, Proposed change, Scope, Confidence — ordered by confidence, user impact, reach and correction cost, ending with one "Improve first" recommendation. Each plan file carries an evidence chain, the exact reusable token/component to use, ordered changes per path, and validation steps.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** A candidate finding survives only with all three proofs: Contract (a binding design decision or a direct contradiction in user-facing presentation), Runtime (the cited owner/value provably reaches the surface through imports, props, CSS inheritance or rendering), Correction (one change the evidence fully determines). Findings are capped at three. Functional behaviour, accessibility/semantics (unless requested), metadata and performance findings are out of scope. Never modifies product source; no installs, formatters or commits.
- **Reference / source:** UI Skills collection; plan format in its bundled `improve-ui/references/plan-template.md`.
- **Best for:** Auditing a built homepage or preview before a redesign round — checking a finished section against the site's own tokens and rules and producing the fix list, on any trade.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0057⟧

Route by topic, then stack, then specificity; prefer specific and framework-specific skills over broad ones.

## ⟦S0059⟧ emil-design-eng — UI Skills — Emil Kowalski (animation & design engineering)
- **What it is:** Emil Kowalski's design-engineering philosophy as a working rulebook: how to decide whether something should animate, which easing and duration to use, how to build pressable, origin-aware components, springs, gestures, clip-path tricks and staggers — plus a mandatory Before/After table format for reviewing UI code.
- **How it looks:** Interfaces where every small motion feels physical. A popover grows out of the button that opened it instead of appearing from its own centre; a button visibly depresses the instant it is pressed (label and icon shrinking together); a drawer occupies the full height hidden below the screen edge and slides up when summoned; toasts rise from the bottom and can be flicked away; a row of cards appears as a cascade, each one fading and rising a few pixels in turn rather than all at once; a hold-to-delete button fills with colour left-to-right while held and snaps empty the moment it is released.
- **Frame by frame:** Popover entry: click the trigger → the panel starts at `scale(0.95)` with `opacity: 0`, anchored at the trigger's position (`transform-origin: var(--transform-origin)`) → it expands to full size and full opacity over ~200ms on a strong ease-out → settled, flush under its trigger. Button press: pointer down → button scales to `0.97` over `160ms` ease-out → release returns it. Stagger entrance: items begin at `opacity: 0`, `translateY(8px)` → each animates `300ms` ease-out to rest, item 2 delayed 50ms, item 3 100ms, item 4 150ms → a left-to-right/top-to-bottom cascade finishes. Hold-to-confirm: press and hold → a clipped colour overlay wipes across the button over 2s linear → release early and it snaps back in 200ms ease-out. Drag dismissal: drag a drawer/toast → it follows the pointer 1:1 with damping past its boundary → release with velocity above ~0.11 (distance ÷ elapsed time) and it flies off the way it entered; below that it springs back.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Custom curves: `--ease-out: cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1)`, `--ease-in-out: cubic-bezier(0.77, 0, 0.175, 1)`, `--ease-drawer: cubic-bezier(0.32, 0.72, 0, 1)`; `ease-in` is banned on UI. Durations: button press feedback 100–160ms; tooltips and small popovers 125–200ms; dropdowns/selects 150–250ms; modals/drawers 200–500ms; all UI under 300ms. Frequency gate: 100+ uses/day = no animation ever (keyboard actions never animate); tens/day = remove or drastically reduce; occasional = standard; rare/first-time = delight allowed. Entrances start at `scale(0.9–0.97)` + `opacity: 0`, never `scale(0)`. Springs: Apple-style `{ type: "spring", duration: 0.5, bounce: 0.2 }` or physics `{ mass: 1, stiffness: 100, damping: 10 }`, bounce kept 0.1–0.3. clip-path inset recipes: reveal `inset(0 100% 0 0)` → `inset(0 0 0 0)`; scroll image reveal from `inset(0 0 100% 0)` with `useInView { once: true, margin: "-100px" }`; comparison slider by dragging the right inset. Crossfade masking blur `blur(2px)` at `opacity: 0.7` over 200ms (blur always under 20px). Stagger delays 30–80ms between items. Only `transform` and `opacity` animate; set `transform` directly on the element, never via an inherited CSS variable; in Framer Motion use the full `transform` string, not `x`/`y` props. Hover motion gated behind `@media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)`; reduced motion keeps opacity/color, drops movement.
- **Reference / source:** Emil Kowalski's design-engineering philosophy (emilkowal.ski); his Sonner toast library (13M+ weekly npm downloads) and Vaul drawer are the worked examples; curve-finding resources named: easing.dev and easings.co; Paul Graham quoted on unseen details.
- **Best for:** The motion-and-polish standard for every interactive element on any section — buttons and CTA press states, dropdowns and menus in navigation, toasts after a quote-form submit, drawers, staggered card grids in work/gallery and proof sections, hold-to-confirm on destructive actions. Applies to all trades.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0059⟧

## ⟦S0060⟧ animate — UI Skills — Emil Kowalski (animation & design engineering)
- **What it is:** The construction counterpart to ⟦S0059⟧: given a request for motion, it runs a fixed seven-step build sequence — should it animate, what purpose, which tool, which properties, which curve/duration or spring, interruption and exit, reduced-motion and pointer gating — and writes the implementation. Ships with a recipe file covering twelve common components.
- **How it looks:** The same physical interface world as ⟦S0059⟧, delivered as finished code: dropdowns that scale out of their trigger, a modal that fades and settles at centre screen over a fading backdrop, a bottom drawer parked at `translateY(100%)` that slides up on the iOS drawer curve, an accordion that grows open smoothly instead of snapping, a tab bar whose active colours sweep across as one clipped layer instead of each label fading separately, and marketing images that wipe upward into view as you scroll to them.
- **Frame by frame:** Scroll reveal (recipe, verbatim values): the element sits clipped to nothing (`clip-path: inset(0 0 100% 0)`) → when it enters the viewport (IntersectionObserver, or Motion `useInView` with `{ once: true, margin: "-100px" }`) the clip animates to `inset(0 0 0 0)` over `600ms` on the strong ease-in-out → the image stands fully revealed, and it never replays on later scroll-bys. Drawer: closed state `translateY(100%)` (hidden by its own height, whatever the content) → opens to `translateY(0)` over `500ms` with `cubic-bezier(0.32, 0.72, 0, 1)`. Modal: from `opacity: 0; scale(0.96)` with `transform-origin: center` → full size and opacity over `250ms` ease-out, backdrop fading in alongside at the same 250ms. Toast entry: `@starting-style` starts it at `opacity: 0; translateY(100%)` → it rises into place over `400ms` with plain `ease` (deliberately slightly slower and more elegant, Sonner-style). Tab indicator: a duplicated tab list styled as the active state is clipped to just the active tab → on tab change the clip window slides over `250ms` ease-in-out → text and background colours arrive together, perfectly in sync.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Same curve tokens and duration table as ⟦S0059⟧ (`--ease-out: cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1)`; `--ease-in-out: cubic-bezier(0.77, 0, 0.175, 1)`; `--ease-drawer: cubic-bezier(0.32, 0.72, 0, 1)`; UI under 300ms; springs `{ duration: 0.5, bounce: 0.2 }` or `{ mass: 1, stiffness: 100, damping: 10 }`, bounce 0.1–0.3). Tool ladder, cheapest first: CSS transition → CSS `@starting-style` → CSS animation (off the main thread) → WAAPI `element.animate()` → Motion (motion.dev) for springs/layout/exit/gesture. Accordion recipe: `height` + `opacity` transition at `200ms` ease-out (height is tolerated only here). Hold-to-confirm and drag-to-dismiss recipes reuse the 2s-linear / 200ms-ease-out asymmetry and the velocity > ~0.11 dismissal rule. A "Never Ship" checklist blocks `transition: all`, `scale(0)` entrances, `ease-in` on UI, keyframes on rapidly-triggered elements, layout-property animation and ungated hover.
- **Reference / source:** Emil Kowalski's animation philosophy; recipes file `animate/RECIPES.md` bundled with the skill; Sonner and Vaul behaviour as reference implementations; curves from easing.dev / easings.co when a new one is needed.
- **Best for:** Actually building the motion for a section — hero entrances, dropdown navigation, modal/drawer patterns, scroll reveals in work/process sections, tabbed service switchers, accordions in FAQ — with values that pass review the first time. All trades.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0060⟧

## ⟦S0061⟧ animation-vocabulary — UI Skills — Emil Kowalski (animation & design engineering)
- **What it is:** A reverse-lookup glossary of roughly eighty animation terms in eleven groups. The user describes an effect loosely ("the bouncy thing when a popover opens", "the iOS rubber-band scroll") and it returns the exact term with the glossary's verbatim definition, plus close alternates where two terms compete.
- **How it looks:** A naming tool, so "how it looks" is the effects it names, in its own words: **Pop in** — an element appears with a slight overshoot, like it bounces into place; **Origin-aware animation** — a popover grows from the button that opened it instead of from its own centre; **Rubber-banding** — resistance and snap-back when you drag past a boundary; **Parallax** — background and foreground move at different speeds while scrolling; **Morph** — one shape smoothly turns into another, e.g. Dynamic Island; **Shared element transition** — a thumbnail travels and transforms into a card; **Line drawing** — an SVG path draws itself in like an invisible pen tracing it; **Skeleton / Shimmer** — a placeholder with a moving sheen while content loads; **Number ticker** — digits rolling or counting up to a value; **Marquee** — content scrolling continuously in a loop; **Float** — a gentle continuous up-and-down drift; **Before / after slider** — a draggable divider wiping between two overlaid images.
- **Frame by frame:** Signature effects as defined: a **Stagger** fires several items one after another with a small delay between each, building a cascade; a **Scroll reveal** fades or slides elements into place as they enter the viewport; a **Crossfade** fades one element out as another fades in, in the same spot; a **Typewriter** adds text one character at a time as if being typed; an **Alternate (yoyo)** loop plays forward then reverses each iteration instead of jumping back to the start. The glossary itself prescribes no durations — it names and distinguishes, and its definitions are to be quoted verbatim, not paraphrased.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Groups: Entrances & Exits; Sequencing & Timing (keyframes, interpolation/tween, fill mode, stepped animation); Movement & Transforms (translate, scale, rotate, skew, 3D tilt/flip, perspective, transform origin); Transitions Between States (crossfade, continuity transition, morph, layout animation, direction-aware transition); Scroll (scroll-driven animation, parallax, page/view transitions); Feedback & Interaction (press/tap feedback, hold to confirm, drag to reorder, swipe to dismiss, shake/wiggle, ripple); Easing (ease-out is "the default for most UI", ease-in "usually avoided", linear reserved for spinners and marquees); Springs (stiffness/tension, damping, mass, bounce, perceptual duration, velocity, interruptible animation); Looping & Ambient; Polish & Effects (blur, clip-path, mask, text morph, tabular numbers); Performance (60fps baseline, jank, dropped frames, compositing, will-change, layout thrashing); Principles (purposeful animation, anticipation, follow-through, squash & stretch, perceived performance, frequency of use, spatial consistency, reduced motion).
- **Reference / source:** Emil Kowalski's animation philosophy; the glossary mirrors the animations.dev project's `/vocabulary` page.
- **Best for:** The briefing stage of any build — turning "make the heading do that thing where…" into the exact term (stagger, line drawing, parallax, morph) to specify in a section plan or a prompt, for any section and any trade.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0061⟧

## ⟦S0062⟧ animation-performance — UI Skills — Emil Kowalski (animation & design engineering)
- **What it is:** A diagnostic skill for motion that drops frames: it matches a symptom (stutter, jank during navigation, lag that grows with list size) to its cause in the layout/paint/composite pipeline and prescribes the cheapest fix. It judges only whether each frame finishes in time — easing and duration choices belong to ⟦S0060⟧.
- **How it looks:** The difference is visible smoothness. Broken: a tab indicator that hitches mid-slide exactly while the next page loads; a drawer drag that gets laggier the more items the drawer holds; a shadow that shimmers because it repaints every frame. Fixed: the same motions holding a steady 60fps (or 120fps) because they run on `transform`/`opacity` off the main thread — the Vercel dashboard case in the source, where a Framer Motion shared-layout tab animation dropped frames during page loads until it was moved to a CSS animation.
- **Frame by frame:** The budget the skill enforces: at 60fps the browser has 16.7ms per frame; at 120Hz it has 8ms; a single layout recalculation on a complex page can take over 100ms — a dozen missed frames in one step. A main-thread (`requestAnimationFrame`) animation whose callback misses that window shows a visible hitch; the same animation as a CSS transition/keyframe or WAAPI continues compositing on the GPU while JavaScript is busy, so no frame is dropped.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Property cost tiers — composite-only: `transform`, `opacity` (plus `filter`, `clip-path`, `background-color` in current Chrome/Firefox); paint+composite: `box-shadow`, `border-radius`, `color`; layout+paint+composite: `width`, `height`, `padding`, `margin`, `top`, `left`, `border-width`. Swap-down table: grow/shrink → `scale()`; move → `translate()`; `display`/`visibility` swaps → `opacity`; animated `box-shadow` → `filter: drop-shadow()`. Driver table: JS + rAF (GSAP, motion/react components) always main thread; WAAPI and CSS can be hardware-accelerated. Framer Motion `x`/`y`/`scale` shorthands run via CSS variables and are not accelerated — use the full `transform` string; in React write to `ref.current.style`, never `setState` per frame. Inherited CSS variables recalc styles for every descendant per frame (Vaul's drag degraded past ~20 drawer items). Animated `blur()` stays under 20px. `will-change: transform` only after seeing a 1px start/end shift or measured dropped frames, on the animating element only. Diagnosis order: animated properties → jank coinciding with page load/fetch → per-frame React re-renders → content-growth degradation → animated CSS variables → blur over 20px → `will-change` last.
- **Reference / source:** Emil Kowalski's design-engineering philosophy; worked examples from Sonner, Vaul and the Vercel dashboard.
- **Best for:** The performance gate on motion-heavy sections — parallax and pinned heroes, marquees, drag interactions, big galleries — and for any animation that must stay smooth on a mid-range phone. All trades.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0062⟧

## ⟦S0063⟧ review-animations — UI Skills — Emil Kowalski (animation & design engineering)
- **What it is:** A review skill that measures animation code in a diff against ten non-negotiable craft standards and returns a mandatory Before/After findings table plus a tiered verdict ending in Block or Approve. It defaults to flagging; approval is earned. It reviews motion only — it does not write features or fix code.
- **How it looks:** No screen output; the deliverable is the review itself. Part 1 is a single markdown table (Before | After | Why), one row per issue — e.g. `transition: all 300ms` → `transition: transform 200ms ease-out`; `transform: scale(0)` → `transform: scale(0.95); opacity: 0`; `ease-in` on a dropdown → `ease-out` + custom curve; `transform-origin: center` on a popover → `var(--transform-origin)`. Part 2 groups commentary into six impact tiers (feel-breaking regressions; missed simplifications; performance; interruptibility & timing; origin, physicality & cohesion; accessibility) and closes with an explicit Block/Approve decision.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion; it judges other motion against the standards in its bundled `review-animations/STANDARDS.md`.
- **Mechanism & key values:** The standards file carries the exact values findings must cite: the frequency table (100+/day = no animation ever; tens/day = remove or drastically reduce; occasional = standard; rare/first-time = delight allowed); easing decision order (enter/exit `ease-out`, on-screen movement `ease-in-out`, hover/color `ease`, constant motion `linear`) with curves `cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1)`, `cubic-bezier(0.77, 0, 0.175, 1)`, `cubic-bezier(0.32, 0.72, 0, 1)`; durations (press 100–160ms, tooltips/popovers 125–200ms, dropdowns 150–250ms, modals/drawers 200–500ms, UI under 300ms); never `scale(0)` — start `scale(0.9–0.97)` + `opacity: 0`; press feedback `scale(0.97)`, transition `transform 160ms ease-out`; springs `{ duration: 0.5, bounce: 0.2 }` or `{ mass: 1, stiffness: 100, damping: 10 }`, bounce 0.1–0.3; drag dismissal velocity > ~0.11; stagger 30–80ms; crossfade mask `blur(2px)`; reduced-motion and `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` gating snippets. Remedial hierarchy: delete → reduce → fix easing → fix origin/physicality → make interruptible → move to GPU → asymmetric timing → polish → accessibility & cohesion. Block triggers include `scale(0)`/`ease-in` on UI, animation on keyboard/high-frequency actions, and non-GPU animation with an easy GPU fix.
- **Reference / source:** Emil Kowalski's animation philosophy (animations.dev), with the review method adapted from aggressive code-quality review.
- **Best for:** The QA gate on any built animation before it ships — reviewing a finished hero, navigation, gallery or form interaction against the craft bar. All trades, all sections.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0063⟧

## ⟦S0064⟧ improve-animations — UI Skills — Emil Kowalski (animation & design engineering)
- **What it is:** A codebase-wide motion audit that produces prioritized, self-contained implementation plans for other agents to execute. Strictly read-only on source: it recons a repo's motion surface, audits eight categories, vets every finding at its file:line, then writes one plan per selected finding into `plans/` with exact values inlined.
- **How it looks:** The deliverable is a findings table (Severity | Category | Location | Finding | Fix summary, ordered by leverage) plus plan files and a `plans/README.md` with execution order and statuses. Each plan states the problem with the current code quoted verbatim, the exact target code (curves, durations, spring configs spelled out), the repo conventions to follow with an exemplar, ordered steps, hard boundaries, and a verification section including a feel check (slow motion, frame-by-frame, real device). Two to four "missed opportunities" are listed separately from corrective findings.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion; it plans motion fixes using the values in its bundled `improve-animations/AUDIT.md`.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Eight audit categories: purpose & frequency; easing & duration; physicality & origin; interruptibility; performance; accessibility; cohesion & tokens; missed opportunities. Effort levels: quick (high-traffic components, 0–1 subagents, ~5 HIGH findings), standard (all interactive UI, ≤4 subagents), deep (whole repo incl. marketing, ≤8 subagents). Severity: HIGH = feel-breaking (wrong easing on UI, animation on keyboard/high-frequency actions, dropped frames, `scale(0)`); MEDIUM = wrong origin, non-interruptible dynamic UI, missing reduced-motion; LOW = polish. Target values are the shared Kowalski set: curves `cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1)` / `(0.77, 0, 0.175, 1)` / `(0.32, 0.72, 0, 1)`; UI under 300ms with the standard per-element duration table; `scale(0.9–0.97)` entrances; `scale(0.97)` press feedback at 160ms; velocity > ~0.11 drag dismissal; blur under 20px; stagger 30–80ms. Invocation variants include bare, `quick`/`deep`, a category focus, `plan <description>`, `execute <plan>` and `reconcile`.
- **Reference / source:** Emil Kowalski's design-engineering philosophy (emilkowal.ski); workflow adapted from senior-advisor codebase auditing.
- **Best for:** Auditing a whole finished site — e.g. a completed trade homepage — and generating the ordered fix-plan set for its motion, rather than reviewing a single change.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0064⟧

## ⟦S0065⟧ find-animation-opportunities — UI Skills — Emil Kowalski (animation & design engineering)
- **What it is:** A read-only search skill that sweeps an interface for moments that do not animate but should, runs every candidate through a four-question gate, and reports at most 5–7 surviving suggestions with exact motion recipes — plus a mandatory list of candidates it deliberately rejected, and why.
- **How it looks:** The output is a table (Location | Today | Purpose | Frequency | Suggested motion) describing changes like: a toast that today appears instantly would instead rise in from `translateY(100%)` via `@starting-style` over `400ms ease` and exit by the same edge; a button with no press feedback gains `:active { transform: scale(0.97) }` at `160ms ease-out`; a grid that pops in all at once gains a 30–80ms stagger. The rejected list shows the restraint — e.g. a command palette's open/close rejected as keyboard-initiated, 100+/day; an animated chart line rejected because users read that data.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion of its own; every suggestion it emits specifies its motion frame by frame with exact values (see the toast and stagger examples above).
- **Mechanism & key values:** The Gate, in order: 1) Frequency — 100+/day reject outright (keyboard-initiated actions are a disqualifier), tens/day near-imperceptible only, occasional eligible, rare/first-time is where the delight budget lives; 2) Purpose — must be named as Feedback, Spatial consistency, State indication, Preventing a jarring change, Explanation (marketing/onboarding only), or Delight (rare tier only); 3) Speed — must fit the standard budgets (press 100–160ms; tooltips/popovers 125–200ms; dropdowns 150–250ms; modals/drawers 200–500ms; UI under 300ms); 4) Function — no decorative motion on data the user reads or acts on. Hunt list: feedback gaps (missing `:active`, plain-click destructive confirms → hold-to-confirm clip fill, 2s linear press / 200ms ease-out release), teleporting state (conditional renders, snapping accordions, un-bridged list add/remove), missing spatial story (panels unconnected to triggers, asymmetric toast exits), group entrances, gesture seams (springs `{ duration: 0.5, bounce: 0.2 }`, velocity > ~0.11, rubber-banding), and the delight budget (first-run, empty states, success). Shared curves: `cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1)`, `(0.77, 0, 0.175, 1)`, `(0.32, 0.72, 0, 1)`; entrances from `scale(0.95–0.97)` + `opacity: 0`, never `scale(0)`; `transform`/`opacity` only; reduced-motion and hover gating included in every suggestion.
- **Reference / source:** Emil Kowalski's philosophy, specifically his essay "You Don't Need Animations" (emilkowal.ski/ui/you-dont-need-animations); Raycast's unanimated command palette is the cited exemplar.
- **Best for:** The pre-build or pre-polish sweep of a page plan — deciding which sections and interactions earn motion (hero entrance, proof-section counters, CTA feedback) and which stay still. All trades.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0065⟧

## ⟦S0066⟧ break-ui — UI Skills — Emil Kowalski (animation & design engineering)
- **What it is:** An adversarial stress test: it maps every value a component renders, builds one realistic worst-case dataset (very long names, unbreakable emails, missing optional fields, counts of 0, 1 and 1,284, empty and 1,000-item lists, non-Latin text, emoji), renders demo and worst-case data behind a dev-only toggle, and reports everything that broke with the fix for each.
- **How it looks:** The component shown twice, flipped by a plain segmented control fixed at bottom-centre of the viewport — grey track, white pill on the active segment, system font, labelled "Demo data / Worst case" (extra segments for Empty / One / 1,000 rows). In the worst-case view the visitor sees the failure signatures directly: an avatar squished into a 28×56 pill beside a three-line name; a 63-character email (`bartholomew.fitzgerald@northwind-industries-holdings.example.com`) pushing the row's menu off-screen; a badge wrapped onto two lines; "1 members"; a broken-image icon where an avatar 404'd; Vietnamese diacritics clipped by a tight line-height. Checks run at the component's real container width, then 320px and the widest layout, at 200% zoom, and in dark mode and RTL where supported.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — switching datasets is instant, with deliberately no animation on the content; the toggle itself is chrome, not part of the design under test.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Worst-case values come from its bundled `break-ui/CATALOG.md` and must be plausible or schema-backed, never random strings. Signature fixes copied from the source: squished flex children → `flex-shrink: 0`; text overflow in flex/grid → `min-width: 0` (`minmax(0, 1fr)` in grid); unbreakable strings → `overflow-wrap: anywhere`; badges → `white-space: nowrap; flex-shrink: 0`; pluralization → `Intl.PluralRules`; numbers → `Intl.NumberFormat` with the user's locale and `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`; initials from grapheme clusters via `Intl.Segmenter`, first + last word; long previews → `line-clamp: 2`; middle-truncation for file names/emails that differ at the end; never truncate numbers, amounts or dates. Data enters through the same boundary as demo data (fixture/mock/props), never by editing markup. Severity scale: Broken / Ugly / Fragile. Output: a what-broke table, a decisions-for-you list, and a what-held-up list.
- **Reference / source:** Emil Kowalski's design-engineering philosophy; the catalog values are the skill's own curated set (example.com/.test domains only, so fixtures never point at real inboxes).
- **Best for:** Hardening data-dense sections before delivery — review and testimonial lists, team/staff grids, service-area lists, pricing tables, project galleries with long titles — on any trade site.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0066⟧

## ⟦S0067⟧ prototype — UI Skills — Emil Kowalski (animation & design engineering)
- **What it is:** Builds several genuinely different versions of one described UI piece — default 3, maximum 5, each diverging on a named axis (layout, density, personality, motion, interaction model) — rendered one at a time, full size, in realistic context behind a fixed visual picker, so the user can flip through them live and promote the winner into the codebase.
- **How it looks:** The work itself fills the screen one variant at a time, surrounded by realistic context (a toast appears over a real page, a card among sibling cards). The only constant is the picker: a floating dark-glass pill at bottom-centre — near-black translucent background (`rgba(10, 10, 10, 0.82)`), backdrop blur 12px with saturation 1.4, fully rounded (999px radius), 13px system font, one labelled button per variant ("Quiet", "Editorial", "Playful" — never "Option A/B/C"), a hairline divider, and a ↻ replay button when a variant has motion worth re-triggering. The active button's text is white (inactive rgba white 0.55), and a soft white highlight pill (rgba white 0.12) sits behind the active label. If a variant occupies bottom-centre (a toast stack, a bottom sheet), the picker moves to the top via `data-position="top"` — the one allowed modification.
- **Frame by frame:** Pressing a number key, arrow key or picker item → the highlight pill slides to the newly active label over 250ms on `cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1)` (transform and width), while the variant on stage swaps instantly with no transition — flipping is a 100+/session action, so the swap itself never animates → the new variant re-mounts, so its own entrance animation replays from the start. Pressing R re-mounts the current variant to replay its motion without switching. On first load the highlight takes its position without animating (a `data-ready` flag is added after first paint). Selection persists across reload in the URL (`?v=2`).
- **Mechanism & key values:** Picker spec (from bundled `prototype/PICKER.md`, to be copied verbatim — never restyled with project tokens): pill padding 4px, item height 28px, item padding 0 12px, divider 1px × 16px, z-index 2147483647, bottom offset 24px; item colour transition `color 150ms ease-out`; `:active` press `scale(0.97)`; focus ring 2px `rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.4)` at 2px offset; highlight slide 250ms on the strong ease-out, disabled under `prefers-reduced-motion`. Keys: `1–N` and `←`/`→` switch, `R` replays; key events ignored while typing in inputs or with modifiers held. Every variant must fully work with realistic content (no lorem ipsum, no dead buttons) and individually meet the Kowalski craft bar (ease-out entrances, sub-300ms UI motion, correct transform-origin, transform/opacity only, reduced-motion handled). In a project it lives on an isolated route (`/prototypes/<slug>`); standalone, in one self-contained HTML file. On selection, the winner is integrated and the prototype surface deleted.
- **Reference / source:** Emil Kowalski's design-engineering philosophy and craft bar; picker markup/CSS/JS specified verbatim in the bundled `prototype/PICKER.md`.
- **Best for:** Exactly the multi-version workflow — building the 3 wholly-different versions of a hero, proof, work or CTA section behind a 1·2·3 switcher so the owner flips and picks. All trades, all sections.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0067⟧

## ⟦S0068⟧ pick-ui-library — UI Skills — Emil Kowalski (animation & design engineering)
- **What it is:** A curated, opinionated lookup: name a frontend task and it returns the one library to use for it, from Emil Kowalski's list — no menu of alternatives unless the task is genuinely uncovered. It runs only when explicitly invoked.
- **How it looks:** A reference table rather than a visual; what the visitor ends up seeing is the chosen library's component on screen — Sonner's stacked toasts, cmdk's ⌘K command palette, NumberFlow's digits rolling as a price or stat changes, Cobe's rotating 3D globe, Virtuoso's endlessly scrolling long list, base-ui's accessible dropdown that grows from its trigger. The skill's visual guidance: reach for the motion library only when springs, layout animations, exit animations or gesture-driven values are needed — a simple hover or fade is plain CSS.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion of its own; it selects the tools (including the motion tool) that other skills then use.
- **Mechanism & key values:** The picks, copied from the source: unstyled accessible primitives (dialogs, popovers, menus, selects) → base-ui; command menus → cmdk; toasts → Sonner; OTP inputs → input-otp; control panels → Leva (dialkit alternative); general animation → motion (motion.dev / Framer Motion); animating numbers → NumberFlow; animated text → torph; 3D globes → Cobe; dynamic OG images → Satori; syntax highlighting → shiki; real-time/streaming charts → Liveline; general charts → recharts; drag and drop → dnd kit; virtualization → Virtuoso; state → zustand; conditional classNames → clsx; variant-driven Tailwind styling → cva; dark mode without flash → next-themes. Workflow: identify the task (not the library the user named), check `package.json` first and keep an already-installed listed library, recommend one library with a one-sentence reason, and flag when leaving the curated list.
- **Reference / source:** Emil Kowalski's curated list; each library linked at its own site (base-ui.com, cmdk.paco.me, sonner.emilkowal.ski, motion.dev, virtuoso.dev, dndkit.com, recharts.org, etc.).
- **Best for:** Component decisions inside any build — toast system for quote-form feedback, virtualization for a long service-area or review list, NumberFlow for animated stat counters in proof sections, Satori for social share images. All trades.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0068⟧

## ⟦S0069⟧ ask-sonner — UI Skills — Emil Kowalski (animation & design engineering)
- **What it is:** The complete working guide to Sonner, the React toast library: install and mount the Toaster, choose the right `toast()` call for each job, promise/loading flows, updating, dismissing and persisting toasts, the styling escalation ladder, theming and icons, positioning and multiple toasters, plus a symptom-by-symptom troubleshooting table and the full API reference.
- **How it looks:** A stack of small toast cards anchored to a screen corner — bottom-right by default — at most 3 visible at once, the rest tucked behind; hovering spreads the stack out with a 14px gap so each card can be read; a typed toast carries its icon (success, error, info, warning, or a spinner for loading); an action button and an optional cancel button sit inside the card; cards sit 32px from the screen edges on desktop and 16px on screens under 600px. With `richColors` the success and error cards take on their green/red colouring (the default look is grey); `invert` flips a toast dark in light mode or vice versa.
- **Frame by frame:** Trigger: code calls `toast('Title')` → the card enters the stack (Sonner's own enter motion; newcomers push the stack, which expands on hover and collapses back when the pointer leaves) → the card lives for its `duration` — 4000ms by default, forever with `duration: Infinity` → it leaves by auto-close (firing `onAutoClose`), by the close button or a swipe (firing `onDismiss`); swipe direction follows the toaster's position unless `swipeDirections` overrides it. Loading flow: `toast.loading('Uploading…')` shows the spinner card → calling `toast.success('Uploaded', { id })` with the same id converts that same card in place to the success state instead of stacking a second toast.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Setup is exactly two pieces: one `<Toaster />` mounted once near the root, and `toast()` called from client code only. `<Toaster />` defaults from the bundled API file: `theme: 'light'` (does not track the OS — pass `'system'` or a resolved theme), `position: 'bottom-right'`, `visibleToasts: 3`, `gap: 14`, `offset: '32px'`, `mobileOffset: '16px'` under 600px, `hotkey: ⌥/alt + T`, `closeButton: false`, `expand: false`, `richColors: false`. `toast()` defaults: `duration: 4000`, `dismissible: true`. Call family: plain, `.success/.error/.info/.warning`, `.loading`, `.promise(promise, { loading, success, error })`, action/cancel objects, `toast(<jsx />)`, headless `toast.custom((t) => …)`, `toast.dismiss(id?)`, `toast.getActiveToasts()`, `useSonner()`. Styling ladder: defaults + `richColors`/`invert` → `toastOptions.style` → `classNames` per part (needs `!important` against Sonner's injected styles) → fully headless. Multiple toasters need an `id` each and `toasterId` per call or every toaster renders every toast. Duplicate toasts mean two Toasters mounted or a StrictMode double-fired effect.
- **Reference / source:** Sonner by Emil Kowalski (sonner.emilkowal.ski); full prop tables in the bundled `ask-sonner/API.md`.
- **Best for:** Notification feedback on any interactive flow — quote-request and contact-form submissions, saved settings, error surfacing — in React/Next builds for any trade.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0069⟧

## ⟦S0070⟧ better-accessibility — UI Skills — Jakub Krehel (better-* series)
- **What it is:** A WCAG 2.2 review-and-fix skill covering semantics and ARIA, keyboard and focus behaviour, accessible names, forms, live-region announcements, motion and zoom. Every finding cites the WCAG criterion it breaks (Level A/AA by number) and the fix is written in the project's own styling system. Ships with five reference files: focus-and-keyboard, forms, hit-areas, motion-and-zoom, screen-readers, semantics-and-aria.
- **How it looks:** What the visitor gets: a "Skip to content" link that appears at the top-left (16px in from the corner) on the first Tab press; a visible focus ring — ideally the browser's own, offset 2px — travelling in DOM order through nav, buttons and form fields, never hidden behind the sticky header; checkboxes whose label text is part of the same click target as the box, with no dead zone; an inline error sentence appearing directly under a failed field, tied to it for screen readers; a dialog that opens with focus inside it and hands focus back to its trigger button on close; status messages announced politely without focus ever jumping to a toast; decorative icons invisible to assistive tech while every icon-only button speaks its name.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion of its own. Its motion rules: wrap animation in `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)` so motion is opt-in; under reduced motion, slides and scales are replaced by opacity cross-fades and parallax and autoplay are removed entirely; anything moving, blinking or auto-updating for more than 5 seconds must show a visible pause control (WCAG 2.2.2), and a timed toast gets at least 5 seconds and pauses while hovered or focused.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Contrast thresholds it applies: text 4.5:1 (1.4.3 AA), large text — at least 24px, or 18.67px bold — 3:1, UI component boundaries/states and meaningful graphics 3:1 (1.4.11); a custom focus ring must reach 3:1 against every adjacent colour it crosses, and a 2px solid perimeter with a 3:1 change is the 2.4.13 AAA target. Hit areas: WCAG 2.5.8 AA baseline is 24×24 CSS px (with exceptions — under the spacing exception 20px targets pass with a 4px gap); aim for 44×44px on touch and 40×40px on desktop; WCAG AAA is 44×44, Apple HIG 44pt, Material 48dp; expand a small control's hit area with a pseudo-element on its wrapper (a 20px checkbox given a 44px hit area), never on the `<input>` itself; decorative overlays get `pointer-events: none`. Keyboard: only `tabindex="0"` and `"-1"` are allowed, never positive; composite widgets use roving tabindex (active item 0, others −1, arrow keys move); comboboxes use `aria-activedescendant`; prefer native `<dialog>.showModal()` for trapping, else `inert` + `role="dialog"` + `aria-modal="true"`. Announcements: `aria-describedby` for field errors, `role="status"` (polite) for non-urgent updates, `role="alert"` for urgent untied errors only; a repeated polite region must exist empty in the DOM before its text updates. Forms: validate on submit (never disable submit to gate validity), `aria-invalid="true"` + `aria-describedby` on failing fields, focus the first invalid field, valid `autocomplete` tokens (1.3.5) and the right `type`/`inputmode` per field (OTP: `type="text" inputmode="numeric"`). Zoom: content survives 200% text resize (1.4.4) and reflows at 320px width with no horizontal scrolling (1.4.10); never `maximum-scale=1` or `user-scalable=no`. Alt text by purpose: decorative `alt=""`, informative = the meaning, functional = the action. Escalation (HIGH on sight): missing accessible name, missing focus indicator, pointer path with no keyboard path, motion ignoring reduced motion, loss at 320px or 200%, meaning carried by color alone.
- **Reference / source:** Jakub Krehel's UI Skills (better-* series); standards cited are WCAG 2.2 and the ARIA Authoring Practices (APG) patterns.
- **Best for:** The deep accessibility pass on any finished build — quote forms, navigation and menus, galleries, dialogs and CTA sections — across all trades; pairs with ⟦S0054⟧, which is the quicker checklist version.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0070⟧

## ⟦S0071⟧ better-colors — UI Skills — Jakub Krehel (better-* series)
- **What it is:** Builds and audits colour systems: generates hue-locked ramps, maps every step to a role, names primitives and semantic tokens, converts between notations, handles gamut (sRGB vs Display P3), and measures rendered contrast pairs — reporting the measured value and the missed threshold when a pair fails, and leaving the colours alone unless asked.
- **How it looks:** What the visitor sees is the finished palette at work: page background, card surfaces, borders and text all drawn from one neutral ramp that carries 80–90% of the interface, one accent hue reserved for interactive elements and the single filled primary action in each view (a filled button reads as primary across the room; accent-coloured text on a neutral button reads as a link), and status colours that never collide with the accent. Gradients keep their colour through the middle — interpolated `in oklab` by default so brightness stays even, or `in oklch` when a two-hue gradient would otherwise go grey in the centre — and dark mode is a re-derived palette (accent a step or two less vivid, dark-end steps spread wider), not the light ramp reversed.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** System shape: one neutral ramp, one accent ramp, and only the status ramps the product renders (danger, warning, success, info). Step-to-role mapping: page background = Tailwind `50` / Radix `1`; component background `100`/`3`; hover `200`/`4`; subtle border `200`/`6`; border/focus ring `300`/`7`; solid fill `600`/`9` (600 because white text on most `500` hues fails 4.5:1 — white on the example `#3b82f6` measures 3.68:1, so that brand colour sits at `500` and fills use `600`); solid hover `700`/`10`; low-contrast text `700`/`11`; high-contrast text `900`/`12`. Ramp construction in OKLCH: hue constant end to end, vividness peaking mid-ramp; light-end steps (`50`–`200`) spaced about 0.04–0.05 of OKLCH `L`, mid-ramp 0.07–0.10; adjacent steps closer than 0.03 L means drop a step; both ends stop short of pure black and white. Neutral tint toward the accent: chroma 0.005–0.02 at the accent's hue. Status hues at least 15° of OKLCH hue from the accent; anything within 15° counts as the same colour. Near-duplicate colours (within 0.02 OKLab ΔE) are collapsed to one. Token tiers: primitives named by hue and step (`--blue-600`), semantics named by role (`--color-text-secondary`, `--color-accent-solid`) — components reference only the semantic tier; never `--color-primary` beside `--color-text-primary` (the brand token is `accent`). Contrast reporting: WCAG 2 — text 4.5:1 AA / 7:1 AAA, large text 3:1 / 4.5:1, UI components 3:1; APCA — body text Lc 75 (preferred 90), labels/headlines Lc 60, large text (≥36px regular or 24px bold) Lc 45, solid icons/UI Lc 30, dividers Lc 15; polarity crossover near 56% OKLCH lightness (at `oklch(65% 0 0)`, black measures 6.49:1 and white 3.23:1). Fixes change lightness first, holding hue. Gamut: at OKLCH `L` 0.65, P3 gains about 0.07 chroma for green but only about 0.015 for blue; declare the sRGB value first, then the vivid value inside `@media (color-gamut: p3)`. Increased contrast: each appearance's variant widens the lightness gap to its background by at least 0.15 L, aiming for Lc 90 on body text. Gradients: `shorter hue` is the default polar direction; banding on large low-contrast gradients is fixed by widening contrast, shrinking the area or adding noise. Tools named for the maths: culori, colorjs.io, chroma.js.
- **Reference / source:** Jakub Krehel's UI Skills (better-* series); conventions referenced are Tailwind's 50–950 scales and Radix's role-defined 1–12 scales; contrast standards WCAG 2 and APCA.
- **Best for:** Building the brand palette and token layer for any site — a roofer's or remodeler's colours turned into a full light/dark token system — auditing an existing palette for failing pairs, and setting up gradient heroes that stay vivid. All trades.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0071⟧

## ⟦S0072⟧ better-interface — UI Skills — Jakub Krehel (better-* series)
- **What it is:** The orchestrator review: it takes one screen, flow or whole interface and runs it through all six domain skills — accessibility, layout, writing, typography, colour, UI polish — then consolidates everything into a single ranked report with one verdict, instead of six separate findings lists.
- **How it looks:** The deliverable is one report document (format in its bundled `better-interface/review-format.md`): a scope-and-coverage header naming the exact scope, stack and conventions inspected, with a coverage table (Domain | Evidence inspected | Result — `Clear`, a findings count, or `Not reviewed` with the reason); then one findings table ordered by severity then reach (Severity | Domain | Location | Before | After | Why) capped at 15 findings, one row per root cause with every location it appears in; a verification section listing each check run and its result, with unrun checks marked `Not verified`; and a closing verdict — `Block` while any HIGH finding remains, `Approve` otherwise, naming every domain that was not reviewed.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Domain review order is fixed: `better-accessibility` → `better-layout` → `better-writing` → `better-typography` → `better-colors` → `better-ui`, each loaded as the source of truth for its domain (an unavailable skill means that domain is marked `Not reviewed`, never reconstructed from memory). Severity: HIGH blocks a task, misleads, hides content or creates systemic failure; MEDIUM harms comprehension, efficiency, adaptability or consistency; LOW is isolated polish. Escalation triggers are HIGH on sight once the owning skill confirms them — including: a control with no accessible name; no visible focus indicator; pointer-only path; motion ignoring `prefers-reduced-motion`; content clipped or unreachable at 320px or 200% zoom; a rendered contrast pair failing its required ratio; meaning carried by colour alone; a destructive action with no confirmation or undo; truncated content with no route to the full value; an error naming no recovery; a semantic colour used against its meaning; a state change carried by motion alone. Fix preference order: 1) Delete, 2) use the platform/native element, 3) reuse an existing token/step/curve, 4) correct the value, 5) add something new. Every finding cites `path/to/file:line` and shows the current implementation; change-scoped requests (a branch, PR or uncommitted work) are handed to the user-invoked `interface-review` skill rather than resolved here.
- **Reference / source:** Jakub Krehel's UI Skills (better-* series); it owns no domain rules itself — all rules live in the six `better-*` skills it routes to.
- **Best for:** The final whole-page QA gate on a finished homepage or preview before delivery — one ranked fix list across accessibility, layout, copy, type, colour and polish. All trades, all sections.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0072⟧
## ⟦S0073⟧ better-layout — Part 07 — UI Skills — Jakub Krehel (the better-* family)
- **What it is:** A layout audit-and-fix skill: it sets grouping, alignment, reading order and responsive structure, then stress-tests the result by resizing, translating (long-string locales) and mirroring it for RTL. It owns no visual styling — radius/shadows/motion belong to better-ui, text metrics to better-typography.
- **How it looks:** Pages where grouping is carried by space, not lines: tight gaps inside a group (e.g. 8px between fields) and at least double that between groups (16–24px+), so sections read as units without divider lines. Everything sits on a small set of shared alignment edges with one indent step per nesting level (~16px). Controls always look like controls (background shape, border, underline or a toolbar zone), never like the static text beside them. One primary action per view; secondary actions go behind a menu past 3. Backgrounds and photos bleed to the viewport edges while text and buttons stay inside the margins and safe areas; content scrolls under sticky chrome without anchor targets hiding beneath the header. Collapsed or off-screen content always shows a cue — the next card peeks 16–32px past the scroll edge, or a disclosure control names what is hidden ("Show 12 more results").
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion of its own. Its dynamic rules are structural: as the viewport narrows, the expanded layout holds until the content itself stops fitting, then collapses (container queries preferred over device-preset breakpoints); in RTL the whole arrangement mirrors via logical properties while digit order inside numbers never reverses.
- **Mechanism & key values:** CSS logical properties (`margin-inline-start`, `padding-inline-end`, `inset-inline-start`, `text-align: start`, `float: inline-start`) for anything that mirrors, with `[dir="rtl"]` overrides for `translateX`/`background-position`. Group gap ≥2× within-group gap (8px in → 16px+ between). Clearance: 12px between adjacent bordered/filled controls, 24px between visible glyphs of borderless controls, 24px+ between unrelated control groups. Full-width buttons inset ~16px inline on mobile; peek cue 16–32px (card width = 100% + gap − peek, scroll-snap). `scroll-padding-block-start` = sticky header height. Overflow fixes: `minmax(0, 1fr)` tracks, `min-width: 0` on flex children, `100%` not `100vw`, `100dvh` not `100vh`, `min-height` instead of fixed heights on text boxes, `@container` instead of `@media` inside reusable components. Severity: clipping/overlap at 320px or 200% zoom is always HIGH. Findings reported as Severity/Location/Before/After/Why tables; verdict Block or Approve.
- **Reference / source:** UI Skills — Jakub Krehel's better-* family; sibling skills better-ui, better-typography, better-writing, better-colors, better-accessibility, better-interface. Deep references inside the skill: grouping-and-alignment.md, spacing-and-adaptivity.md. No external sites named.
- **Best for:** Every section of every build — the structural pass behind hero, proof/reviews, work/gallery, process, towns and CTA layouts; especially card rows that must hint at more content, sticky headers, and any layout that must survive 320px and 200% zoom. Core QA tool for trade homepages.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0073⟧

## ⟦S0074⟧ better-typography — Part 07 — UI Skills — Jakub Krehel (the better-* family)
- **What it is:** A typography audit-and-fix skill covering the full rendering of text: type scale, font loading and synthesis, line-height, letter-spacing, measure, wrapping, truncation, tabular numbers, punctuation and bidi behaviour.
- **How it looks:** Clean, deliberate text: rarely more than three typefaces, hierarchy carried by size and weight rather than extra fonts; a serif headline over a sans body reads intentional, two near-identical sans-serifs read as a mistake. Headings sit tight (line-height 1.1 display, 1.2–1.3 headings), body copy breathes at 1.5–1.6, and no line of long-form text runs past roughly 60–75 characters. Prices, timers and review counts never wobble because their digits are tabular. Headlines wrap evenly (balanced), paragraphs never strand a single word on the last line, and rendered copy uses curly quotes, en/em dashes and the real ellipsis character instead of keyboard stand-ins.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. It notes the one exception: of an underline, only its colour animates reliably (200ms ease-out colour transition in the reference recipe); any other underline animation needs a separate element and belongs to better-ui.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Exact findings when missed: unitless line-height; weight 400+ below 18px (weights 100–300 only at 28px+); measure 60–75ch (≈560–680px at 16px body; Tailwind max-w-xl 576px / max-w-2xl 672px / max-w-prose 65ch fit); inputs at 16px on iOS (either `text-base sm:text-sm`, or keep 16px and render smaller via transform scale — 13px = scale 0.8125 with width/line-height divided by the same factor). Letter-spacing: −0.01em to −0.02em on headings ≥24px, 0.05em on uppercase labels ≤14px, 0 on body. Starting role scale: Display 2.25rem/1.1/600, Title 1.5rem/1.2/600, Heading 1.125rem/1.3/600, Body 1rem/1.5/400, Caption 0.8125rem/1.4/400; anything wrapping to 3+ lines needs line-height ≥1.4. Use properties over raw tags (`font-weight: 650`, `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`, never `font-variation-settings: "wght"` or `font-feature-settings: "tnum"`); leave `font-optical-sizing: auto`; underlines `text-underline-position: from-font` + `text-decoration-thickness: from-font`; font smoothing once on the root; `text-wrap: balance` for headings only (Chromium ignores past six lines), `text-wrap: pretty` on paragraphs; `text-box: trim-both cap alphabetic` to trim button/badge text boxes (Chromium 133+, Safari 18.2+). Sizes in rem; body starts at 16px, UI text 14px, captions 13px, rarely below 12px. Reference files: choosing-fonts.md, css-cheat-sheet.md, details-and-accessibility.md, spacing-and-sizing.md, variable-fonts-and-opentype.md, wrapping-and-punctuation.md.
- **Reference / source:** UI Skills — Jakub Krehel's better-* family. No external sites named; font facts given in-source (e.g. Inter's variable file exposes only wght and opsz; Inter ss01 = open digits, cv11 = single-story a).
