- **Best for:** All type everywhere — hero headlines, review text, stat figures (tabular numbers), form inputs on mobile, long service-area copy. A mandatory QA pass before any trade homepage ships.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0074⟧

## ⟦S0075⟧ better-ui — Part 07 — UI Skills — Jakub Krehel (the better-* family)
- **What it is:** The visual-polish skill of the better-* family: exact values for border radius, optical alignment, shadows, image outlines, icon states and interface motion. It applies once the underlying interaction is sound — a polish finding never outranks a broken interaction.
- **How it looks:** Nested surfaces look machined rather than stacked: a card's outer corner radius equals the inner element's radius plus the padding between them, so the two curves run concentric. Depth comes from soft layered shadows, not borders — a 1px translucent ring plus two faint drop layers — while real borders survive only on dividers, table cells, selected states and inputs. Photos carry a hairline outline in pure black at 10% (white at 10% on dark) inset 1px inside the image edge, so gallery images sit crisply on any background. Icons match the weight of the text beside them and flip from outline to filled only when active. Buttons feel physical: they shrink slightly when pressed. Entrances are staged in semantic chunks — title, then description, then actions — each fading in with a whisper of blur and a short rise; exits are quicker and smaller than entrances.
- **Frame by frame:** Press: button scales to 0.96 over 150ms ease-out (never when disabled). Staged entrance (infrequent moments only): chunks stagger 100ms apart, each going opacity 0→1, blur 4px→0, translateY 12px→0 over 300ms ease-out; a short display headline may split into words staggered 80ms apart. Exit: opacity 1→0, blur 0→4px, fixed translateY −12px over 150ms ease-out — never the full container height; full slide-out only where the destination means something (a drawer closing). Icon swap on an infrequent state change (play→pause, copy→copied): the old icon scales 1→0.25 while fading and blurring to 4px as the new one runs the same values in reverse — Motion spring `{type:"spring", duration:0.3, bounce:0}` (bounce is always 0) or a 300ms cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1) CSS cross-fade with both icons kept in the DOM. High-frequency moments (keystrokes, row hovers, tab switches) get instant feedback or ≤150ms on opacity/background only. Theme switch: all transitions are suppressed for one frame so colours don't smear. Under reduced motion, movement/scale/blur are replaced by an opacity cross-fade.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Concentric radius: outerRadius = innerRadius + padding + borderWidth; past 24px padding (or deliberately asymmetric padding) treat layers as separate surfaces. Optical nudges: 2px less padding on a button's icon side; play triangle shifted translateX(2px) toward its point. Shadow recipes — light: `0 0 0 1px oklch(0 0 0/0.06), 0 1px 2px -1px oklch(0 0 0/0.06), 0 2px 4px 0 oklch(0 0 0/0.04)` (hover: 0.08/0.08/0.06); dark: single ring `0 0 0 1px oklch(1 0 0/0.08)` (hover 0.13); always keep `border: 1px solid transparent` under a shadow ring for forced-colors mode. Image outline: `outline: 1px solid oklch(0 0 0/0.1)`, `outline-offset: -1px` (dark: oklch(1 0 0/0.1)); never a tinted palette colour. Icon stroke tracks adjacent text weight: 1.5px at weight 400 (14–16px), 2px at 500–600, 2.5px at 700 — rendered pixels, so use absoluteStrokeWidth or non-scaling-stroke; inline icons sized 1em–1.25em; one library per surface; `currentColor` only. Transitions over keyframes for anything interactive; name exact properties, never `transition: all`; `will-change` only after observed first-frame stutter, naming the property, transforms/opacity/filter only; hover styles behind `@media (hover: hover)`; `overscroll-behavior: contain` on scrollable overlays; `initial={false}` on AnimatePresence state swaps (never around an intentional entrance). Reference files: animations.md, enter-exit.md, icon-transitions.md, icons.md, performance.md, surfaces.md.
- **Reference / source:** UI Skills — Jakub Krehel's better-* family. No external sites named.
- **Best for:** The final polish pass on every section — gallery/work cards (concentric radius, image outlines), CTA buttons (press scale), hero staged entrances, icon state swaps in process/steps, and motion QA across the whole homepage.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0075⟧

## ⟦S0076⟧ better-writing — Part 07 — UI Skills — Jakub Krehel (the better-* family)
- **What it is:** A copy skill for interface text: it inventories a product's existing strings first, then writes and reviews labels, errors, empty states, confirmations and status copy so the words match the product's voice and always tell the reader what to do next.
- **How it looks:** Nothing moves; what the visitor sees is text that reads plainly and consistently. Buttons start with a verb and name the object ("Send", "Save draft", "Delete project" — never "OK!" or "Yes"). Links describe their destination ("Read the billing docs", never "Click here"; every "Learn more" is suffixed, e.g. "Learn more about exports"). Errors sit beside the field that failed and read as instructions with no blame and no exclamation marks: "Choose a password with at least 8 characters", "Unable to save. Check your connection and try again." Empty states orient and point forward — a heading ("No projects yet"), one line of explanation, one clear action button — instead of a bare "No results." Destructive confirmations are answerable from the title alone ("Delete 'Q3 report'?") with buttons "Delete report" / "Cancel". One capitalisation policy per element type, everywhere.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. (Status copy pairs an in-progress string with its resolution — "Saving changes…" resolves to "Changes saved" — but the animation itself belongs to other skills.)
- **Mechanism & key values:** Workflow: inventory first — search the translation call (`t(`, `i18n.`, `<FormattedMessage`, `$t(`) and locale files, list the noun per object and verb per action, note case per element type; new copy must use the inventoried terms. Tone flexes with stakes: warm/light for success, onboarding and empty states; neutral/minimal for routine actions; calm, plain, zero playfulness for errors and destructive confirmations; serious and explicit for data loss and security. Address the reader as "you"; avoid "we" in errors; possessives sparingly ("Favorites" beats "Your favorites"). Build strings whole — one ICU MessageFormat message with plural categories (`=0`/`one`/`other`, translators add `few`/`many`), never fragments concatenated around a variable or `n === 1 ? "" : "s"`; format numbers, dates and lists through `Intl` (NumberFormat, DateTimeFormat, RelativeTimeFormat, ListFormat). Toggles are labelled for the ON state ("Send read receipts"). Undo beats confirmation for reversible frequent actions ("Project archived. Undo"); confirm irreversible ones, and for an account/workspace/repository require typing the object's name to enable the button. Placeholders show a realistic example in the accepted format (`name@example.com`, `DD/MM/YYYY`), never an instruction. Reference file: patterns.md (destructive-flow templates, status-copy table, plural/Intl recipes).
- **Reference / source:** UI Skills — Jakub Krehel's better-* family. No external sites named.
- **Best for:** All homepage copy QA — hero and CTA labels, quote-form errors and placeholders, empty states, confirmation dialogs; and for trade sites specifically, keeping one noun/verb set ("quote", "book", "call") consistent from hero to footer.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0076⟧

## ⟦S0077⟧ break — Part 07 — UI Skills — Jakub Krehel
- **What it is:** A stress-test skill: it renders ONE chosen component on a temporary harness page under every worst-case scenario that can actually reach it in production, so the breaks are seen side by side rather than predicted. It observes and reports; it owns no design rules and fixes nothing unasked.
- **How it looks:** A plain single-column page inside the real app (real layout, fonts, global styles and providers), the untouched production component repeated once per scenario with a short text label above each instance. After one look, each visible break is marked with a one-line note under that scenario's label, so the page itself reads as the report — e.g. a card fed one unbreakable 60-character string with its text visibly escaping the right edge.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. The "playback" is a single page load and one skim top to bottom; widths are fixed containers on the page, never a resized viewport, and environment modes (dark mode, zoom, reduced motion) are named in the report for the viewer to toggle live rather than simulated.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Scenario axes from scenarios.md, each kept only when its cue matches the component: Content length (empty string; one word; typical; several sentences; one unbreakable string such as a long URL or "Donaudampfschiffahrtsgesellschaft"), Content shape (emoji alone and mixed; RTL text; mixed-direction text; diacritics and tall scripts; numbers in aligning columns), Quantity (zero items; one item; realistic count; 10× realistic), Container (always applies: a 320px container; squeezed by a flex/grid sibling; a very wide container), State (loading, error, disabled — only states that arrive as props), Environment (modes the project supports). Hard rules: import the real component, never a rebuilt lookalike; the page is client code ("use client" in Next) or fixture data silently vanishes; the harness never imports production state; a predicted failure is not a finding — findings are only what visibly broke, each routed to its owner skill (better-typography for wrap/truncation, better-layout for room, better-writing for empty states, better-accessibility for states, better-colors for dark mode). Report table: Scenario / Observed / Owner. The page stays up after reporting and is deleted only on the user's word.
- **Reference / source:** UI Skills — Jakub Krehel; sibling of variant, state-machine and interface-review in the same family. Deep reference: scenarios.md. No external sites named.
- **Best for:** Pre-ship hardening of the components a trade homepage depends on — review cards fed very long or emoji/RTL text, gallery grids at zero/one/10× items, quote forms in a 320px container, price/stat blocks with long German-length strings.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0077⟧

## ⟦S0078⟧ build-design — Part 07 — UI Skills — Jakub Krehel
- **What it is:** A design-to-code fidelity skill: it builds UI from a Figma file (or, weakly, a design image) so the result matches the design, using only the project's existing tokens and components, then compares the build against the design element by element before calling it done.
- **How it looks:** The finished screen is the design itself, not an interpretation: the same spacing, sizes, radii, colours, type and component variants the file specifies. Where a design value lands between tokens, the nearest existing token is used and reported as rounded — the screen may differ from the file by that rounding, and anything more visible is escalated as a question rather than silently absorbed.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion of its own. It builds only the states the file actually draws (hover, empty, error as drawn); a state the design does not draw is left to the existing component's default and listed as missing.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Five steps: (1) Read the design at its source — a Figma link means the official Figma MCP (`get_design_context` per frame, requesting the screenshot in the same call; `get_variable_defs` for variables; `get_metadata` to find frames in large files; node-id `1-2` in the URL is `1:2` for the tools; on branch URLs pass the branch key as the file key). Trust order: variable names over raw values, Code Connect over name matching, auto layout gaps/padding over absolute positions, downloaded assets over expiring Figma URLs. From a screenshot there are no values — sizes are ratios to the capture and the assumed scale must be stated. (2) Map onto the project: bound variable → same-named token; raw value equal to a token → that token; no token → nearest token, reported as rounded; component instance → the project's component; no equivalent → plain markup in place, listed as a deviation. Never add a token, variant or arbitrary value to hit a number; stop and ask when rounding would visibly change the design — more than 2px on spacing or size, or a colour landing on a different step. (3) Build only what the design shows; leave everything around it untouched. (4) Compare at each frame's width beside the design screenshot, property by property ("Gap is 12px, design is 16px" is a finding; "feels tight" is not). (5) Report as Element / Design / Built / Status, plus Unwired, Missing states and Domain conflicts lists. Deep reference: figma.md.
- **Reference / source:** UI Skills — Jakub Krehel; tool names are the official Figma MCP server's. Domain conflicts route to the better-* owners (contrast/focus better-accessibility, type better-typography, spacing better-layout, palette better-colors, copy better-writing, surfaces/icons/motion better-ui).
- **Best for:** Building any section from an approved design file without drift — most relevant when a trade homepage section exists as a Figma design and must land in code exactly; also the discipline for screenshot-based rebuilds (state the scale, treat every measurement as an estimate).
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0078⟧

## ⟦S0079⟧ explain-interface — Part 07 — UI Skills — Jakub Krehel
- **What it is:** A reverse-engineering skill that explains how a website, a visual effect or an animation was built, from a live URL or a screenshot. It explains rather than judges: it finds the layer stack behind an effect and gives the recipe in words — deliberately never a copy-paste code rebuild.
- **How it looks:** The deliverable is a written explanation, but its subject is exactly what a visitor sees: e.g. a soft glow behind a hero resolved into its real stack in paint order — an element oversized past its container so no edge lands inside the viewport, a low-alpha multi-stop gradient, a large `filter: blur()`, and a `backdrop-filter` layer frosting whatever sits beneath. Every value in the explanation is tagged measured (read off the page), derived (computed from measurements) or inferred (intent, never stated as fact).
- **Frame by frame:** For animated effects it reads the live animation rather than guessing: `document.getAnimations()` returns each animation's target, duration, delay (where a stagger shows), easing and per-keyframe opacity/transform/filter — e.g. a fade whose keyframes run opacity 0 → 0.85 at 20% → 1 over 1500ms is explained as 85% of the fade landing in the first 300ms and the last 15% taking the remaining 1200ms, so the layer arrives at once and never reads as finished. A page at rest returns nothing (the reveal already finished or never started), so the method is to reload or scroll the target into view and read during the reveal.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Layer search by property signature across every element and both pseudo-elements (::before/::after carry effects more often than elements do), over backgroundImage, filter, backdropFilter, mixBlendMode, maskImage, boxShadow, opacity — after filtering idle values (`blur(0px)`, `opacity: 1`, `transform: none`) that animation libraries leave behind. A stop list at fractional offsets (9.99%, 19.07%, …) is one generated easing gradient, not twelve stops — name the technique. `elementsFromPoint(x, y)` gives the paint stack at one pixel, front to back. Browser route via chrome-devtools-mcp (`evaluate_script`, `resize_page`, `take_screenshot`, `list_network_requests`, `performance_start_trace`) or Playwright's page.evaluate; never kill a browser you did not start. No-browser route: fetch raw HTML and linked CSS with curl (never a markdown-converting fetch), grep utility classes, inline styles, :root tokens, @media breakpoints, @font-face and @keyframes; stack fingerprints from the HTML (`__NEXT_DATA__`/`/_next/static` = Next.js, `__NUXT__`, `astro-island`, `data-radix-`, `bg-linear-to` = Tailwind v4). Whole-system reads: stack first, tokens second (walk recursing into @layer/@media/@supports), type scale from leaf text nodes, spacing rhythm (group gap vs within-group gap against better-layout's 2× yardstick), radii/shadows, transition table, breakpoints (Tailwind v3 defaults 640/768/1024/1280/1536px; v4 40/48/64/80/96rem), fonts and theming; then re-read at 375px, with the theme toggled, and tabbed to the first control. From a screenshot it is a reconstruction: colours and contrast are exact from pixels, sizes are ratios only (never report px; if body copy is identifiable, assume 16px and say so), typeface by category and tells (single/double-storey a and g, aperture, x-height) never by name. Reference files: find-the-effect.md, from-an-image.md, no-browser.md, read-the-system.md.
- **Reference / source:** UI Skills — Jakub Krehel. Tools named: chrome-devtools-mcp, Playwright. No reference sites named.
- **Best for:** The bank's core research move — taking an award-winning reference site's hero, scroll effect or gradient apart layer by layer so its mechanism (not a lookalike) can be adapted into a section version; also stack/token reconnaissance before any redesign.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0079⟧

## ⟦S0080⟧ interface-review — Part 07 — UI Skills — Jakub Krehel
- **What it is:** A change-scoped review skill: it reviews a branch, pull request or uncommitted change for the interface problems that change introduced or regressed, across accessibility, layout, writing, typography, colour and UI. It owns scope, classification and the report; severity, the cap and the verdict belong to better-interface, to which it hands over.
- **How it looks:** The output is a document, not a screen: a scope block (target, base ref and head ref with SHAs, committed and uncommitted counts, files in scope after exclusions, excluded paths, surfaces expanded), a coverage table, then a findings table where every row carries a Status — Introduced, Regression or Pre-existing — beside Severity, Domain, Location (file:line), Before, After and Why. At most three pre-existing findings are shown as a courtesy, plainly marked as not this change's responsibility.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. Its sequence is procedural: resolve scope → expand changed files to the surfaces they render in → read the removed side of every hunk → classify → check the change against its stated intent → hand to better-interface.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Scope resolution order with no target: (1) HEAD ahead of `git merge-base origin/<default-branch> HEAD` — review that range plus uncommitted changes, counts stated separately; (2) dirty working tree — review uncommitted changes; (3) neither — never fall back to HEAD~1..HEAD uninvited; state the facts and offer the open PR, the last commit (named by SHA and subject), a named target, or a whole-repo audit via better-interface. Diff a branch with three dots (merge base); honour the dots the user wrote in an explicit range. Pair `git diff HEAD` with `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard` or new files silently drop out of scope. PRs: fetch the head in place (`git fetch origin "pull/<n>/head:refs/remotes/pr/<n>"`), diff against the PR's own base from `gh pr view --json baseRefName,baseRefOid`, read files with `git show <head-ref>:path`, cite against the head ref. Read-only rule: `git fetch` only — never `gh pr checkout`, `git checkout`, `git switch` or `git stash`; render other targets in an isolated worktree. Blast radius: expand one hop to direct importers/callers by default, a second hop only for tokens, theme values and shared primitives; at most 5 consumers total, ordered route/layout entry points first, then importer count, then proximity; state how many were not expanded. Removed-signal routing table: removed aria-*/role/alt/label/focus outline/tabindex → better-accessibility; prefers-contrast → better-colors; logical properties swapped for left/right → better-layout; lang/dir and text-wrap/line-clamp/tabular-nums → better-typography; a deleted or shortened user-facing string → better-writing — with equivalent replacements (aria-labelledby for aria-label, a box-shadow ring for outline, a token of the same value for a literal, a string moved into the translation catalogue) clearing the signal first. Intent check hunts the incomplete change: a variant applied to some states but not hover/focus/active/disabled/loading/selected, a new string with no translation-catalogue entry, a new component with no empty/loading/error/disabled/narrow state. Exclusions: lockfiles (every suffix — `*.lock` misses package-lock.json and pnpm-lock.yaml), snapshots/fixtures, generated output, vendored code, binaries — except a font file (better-typography) and a component image (better-ui/better-accessibility) stay in scope. Shallow clone: deepen 50, retry, deepen 200, then declare unresolvable; mid-rebase/merge trees are detected via `git rev-parse --git-path` and stopped, not reviewed. Reference files: removed-signals.md, scope-resolution.md.
- **Reference / source:** UI Skills — Jakub Krehel; hands off to better-interface for severity/cap/verdict. No external sites named.
- **Best for:** Reviewing any build round's diff before it ships — catching a removed focus ring, a dropped aria-label or a token swap that broke contrast in exactly the sections a Claude build just touched; regression-checking section-version rebuilds.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0080⟧

## ⟦S0081⟧ state-machine — Part 07 — UI Skills — Jakub Krehel
- **What it is:** A workbench skill: it renders ONE component on a throwaway page in every state the code can actually reach — loading, empty, error, plan tiers, permissions — each fed mock data at the data boundary, with a switcher to flip between them while you work on the visuals state by state.
- **How it looks:** One instance of the real component, at its production width, inside the real app's layout and fonts, with a deliberately foreign-looking control beside it: a dark neutral panel (rgb(20 20 20 / 0.92), system font stack, 14px radius, thin inset white ring at 10%) listing the states grouped under headings (Data, Account, or narrower product words like Connection or Access), the active state lit white on a 14% white fill. On a narrow page the list collapses to a dark pill-shaped select above the component. The switcher never uses the project's tokens, so it never becomes part of what is being judged.
- **Frame by frame:** Switching is instant and keeps the scroll position — the component swaps state with no animation; the only transition anywhere is the switcher's own active label easing colour and font-weight over 200ms ease-out. Loading and pending states hold still indefinitely (kept pending until the switcher moves, never resolved after a timeout). Arrow keys step through every state in list order across groups; H hides and shows the switcher for screenshots.
- **Mechanism & key values:** States are the branches the component already has — read from the component and its data hooks: Data (loading, empty, error, one item, typical set, set long enough to scroll/paginate, partial resolution, stale refetching), Account (plan tier, role, owner vs member), Feature (flags, trials, limits, locked). A state the code cannot reach is not rendered; a designed-but-uncoded state is listed as missing. Combine kinds only where the code branches on the combination (member-empty), never as a cross product. Data is fed where the component receives it — props first, then the app's own seam (seeded query cache, mock provider, request mocks) — never by editing the component or threading fixtures five levels deep. Fixtures must be product-shaped: real names, timestamps, amounts, realistic counts. The switcher sets a `__state` search param (double underscore keeps it clear of app params) so every state is a link; active button carries `aria-pressed="true"` and scrolls into view; key handling ignores modifiers, already-prevented events and events from inputs/textareas/selects/contenteditable. Layout: container query on the page — list beside the component when list (208px) + gap (24px) + production width fits (the reference CSS uses a 644px component, breakpoint 876px); the list is sticky, scrolls inside itself, list and select are both always rendered with the query showing one. Page, fixtures and switcher live in one folder (e.g. /states/audit-log) so removal is one delete, only on the user's word. Reference file: switcher.md (full HTML/CSS spec).
- **Reference / source:** UI Skills — Jakub Krehel; siblings break, variant, interface-review. No external sites named.
- **Best for:** Working through the states of trade-site components one at a time — a quote form (idle/submitting/success/error), a reviews block (zero reviews vs hundreds), a gallery (one project vs many) — and re-checking every state after each visual change.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0081⟧

## ⟦S0082⟧ variant — Part 07 — UI Skills — Jakub Krehel
- **What it is:** A variant-exploration skill: it builds three versions of one described piece of UI that differ on purpose — different answers to the same brief, not different tints — hosts them behind a picker in the real page, and hands the choice to the user with the tradeoffs stated. It produces candidates and never ranks them.
- **How it looks:** The real page, with real chrome, real neighbours and realistic data, showing one full-size variant at a time beside a dark, deliberately unbranded picker panel (same switcher design as state-machine: near-black translucent surface, system font, grouped list, active item lit). Each variant occupies a different position on one named axis — e.g. a Density group holding Quiet and Dense — so flipping feels like comparing genuinely different designs: one airy with oversized type and few items, one compact with tight spacing and smaller type steps, one colour-led where the filled accent moves.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — variants swap instantly via the `?__variant=quiet` URL param; the picker behaves exactly like the state-machine switcher (arrow keys step across groups, H hides it, the active label eases colour/font-weight over 200ms ease-out, scroll position kept). No entrance animation is prescribed for the variants themselves; their own motion follows the project's language.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Axes, each owned by a better-* skill: Structure and Density (better-layout — grouping, order, column count, what collapses; spacing scale, how much fits), Emphasis (better-colors — where filled colour goes, what recedes), Type (better-typography — scale steps, weight contrast, measure), Voice (better-writing — labels, tone, amount of copy). Pick ONE primary axis, give each variant a different position on it; secondary choices follow from the axis (a dense variant may take a smaller type step — coherence, not a second axis). Default three variants, five only when asked; names state the direction (Quiet, Editorial, Dense — never Option A). Every variant must first clear the better-interface floor, which is not an axis and never trades against one: accessible name and visible focus on every control; keyboard reaches everything a pointer does; reduced-motion respected; nothing clips or becomes unreachable at 320px or 200% zoom; contrast passes; no meaning on colour alone and no state change on motion alone; destructive actions confirmed/undoable; truncated content reachable in full; nothing hidden past a scroll edge without a cue; every error names a recovery; no semantic colour used against its meaning. Build into the real page (or one self-contained HTML file where no page can host it), one variant at a time at full size — thumbnails distort the spacing being judged. Present a Variant / Axis position / Right when / Costs table, never marking a favourite. On a choice: promote that variant properly, delete the others, the picker and the imports, and search for the variant names and `__variant` param so no harness survives. Reference file: picker.md (full switcher spec, container-query breakpoint = 232px + production width).
- **Reference / source:** UI Skills — Jakub Krehel; axis owners are the better-* family, floor from better-interface. No external sites named.
- **Best for:** The exact discipline behind the builds' 1·2·3 section switchers: three genuinely different heroes (or proof/work/process sections) on one declared axis each, judged in place at real widths — and a warning system against versions that differ only in accent colour.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0082⟧

## ⟦S0083⟧ 12-principles-of-animation — Part 08 — UI Skills — Raphael Salaja
- **What it is:** An audit skill that reviews animation code against Disney's 12 principles of animation adapted for web interfaces, and reports violations as file:line findings with a severity summary. Despite the name, the shipped rule set concentrates on four categories: timing, easing, physics and staging.
- **How it looks:** It produces no visuals itself; the interfaces it polices look like this: motion that is quick and uniform (every user-initiated animation done within 300ms, similar elements sharing identical durations), entrances that arrive fast and settle gently, exits that build momentum before leaving, buttons that squash almost imperceptibly when pressed, and scenes with a single clear focal point — a modal's background dimmed so the eye goes to the dialog, tooltips layered above everything else.
- **Frame by frame:** Per its rules: an entrance starts fast and decelerates into place (ease-out); an exit starts slow and accelerates away (ease-in); a pressed button scales down within the subtle deformation band and springs back with a slight overshoot only where a spring (not an easing curve) drives it; a list entrance cascades item by item with no more than 50ms between items. Linear timing appears only where a progress bar's fill tracks real elapsed time.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Rule IDs with exact thresholds — Timing: `timing-under-300ms` (user-initiated animations ≤300ms), `timing-consistent` (identical timing for similar elements), `timing-no-entrance-context-menu` (context menus animate exit only, never entrance). Easing: `easing-entrance-ease-out`, `easing-exit-ease-in`, `easing-no-linear-motion` (linear only for progress indicators), `easing-natural-decay` (exponential ramps for decay — `exponentialRampToValueAtTime(0.001, …)`, never linear, never a 0 target). Physics: `physics-active-state` (interactive elements need an :active scale transform), `physics-subtle-deformation` (squash/stretch held to 0.95–1.05; whileTap scale 0.98 passes, 0.8 fails), `physics-spring-for-overshoot` (springs for overshoot-and-settle; example stiffness 500, damping 30), `physics-no-excessive-stagger` (stagger delay ≤50ms per item; 0.03 passes, 0.15 fails). Staging: `staging-one-focal-point`, `staging-dim-background` (modal overlay dimmed, e.g. `background: var(--black-a6)`), `staging-z-index-hierarchy` (e.g. tooltip z-index 50). Output: `file:line - [rule-id] description` lines, then a Rule/Count/Severity table.
- **Reference / source:** UI Skills — Raphael Salaja. References named in the skill: "The Illusion of Life: Disney Animation" (Thomas & Johnston) and Apple WWDC23 "Animate with Springs".
- **Best for:** Motion QA on any built section — a fast rule-based pass over hero entrances, card staggers, button presses and modal staging before a version is judged; pairs with S0089 (spring vs easing choice).
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0083⟧

## ⟦S0084⟧ generating-sounds-with-ai — Part 08 — UI Skills — Raphael Salaja
- **What it is:** An audit skill for procedural UI sound: it reviews Web Audio API code that synthesises sounds (no audio files) against best practices for context management, envelopes, sound design and parameter ranges, outputting file:line findings.
- **How it looks:** Nothing on screen — its subject is what the visitor hears: a click that sounds like a click (a tiny filtered noise burst, crisp and present, not a sine-wave "beep"), and a confirmation that sounds tonal and reassuring (a short oscillator tone whose pitch sweeps upward, 400Hz rising to 600Hz in 40ms) instead of a flat static beep. Sounds die away naturally and exponentially, never chopping off or fading in a straight line.
- **Frame by frame:** A passing click, in time: a noise buffer of 8ms (clicks must be 5–15ms) whose samples decay as exp(−i/50) → passed through a bandpass filter at 4000Hz with Q 3 (allowed 3000–6000Hz, Q 2–5) → gain set first with setValueAtTime (example 0.3, never above 1.0) then ramped exponentially down to 0.001, not 0 → nodes disconnected in onended. A passing confirmation: oscillator frequency set at 400Hz, then exponentialRampToValueAtTime(600, t + 0.04).
- **Mechanism & key values:** Context: one shared AudioContext (lazy singleton), resumed if `state === "suspended"` before playing, nodes disconnected and cleaned up after playback. Envelopes: exponential ramps for decay; exponential targets never 0 (use 0.001); always setValueAtTime before a ramp to avoid glitches. Design: filtered noise for percussion, oscillators with pitch movement for tonal sounds, bandpass filter to give percussion its character. Parameters: click duration 5–15ms (100ms fails), bandpass 3000–6000Hz (500Hz fails as muffled), gain ≤1.0 (start ~0.3), Q 2–5 (15 fails as harsh). Parameter-translation table maps user words to changes: "too harsh" → lower filter frequency, reduce Q; "too muffled" → higher filter frequency; "cuts off abruptly" → exponential decay; "softer" → lower gain, triangle wave. Output: `file:line - [rule-id] description` plus a Rule/Count/Severity table.
- **Reference / source:** UI Skills — Raphael Salaja. Reference named: Web Audio API on MDN.
- **Best for:** Only where a site deliberately uses synthesised UI sound (rare on trade homepages) — e.g. checking a form-submit confirmation chirp or an interactive configurator's clicks. Mostly a specialist audit tool; mark SITUATIONAL for trades.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0084⟧

## ⟦S0085⟧ mastering-animate-presence — Part 08 — UI Skills — Raphael Salaja
- **What it is:** An audit skill for Motion (Framer Motion) AnimatePresence code: it checks exit animations, presence hooks, mode selection and nested exits, and reports violations as file:line findings.
- **How it looks:** It produces no visuals itself; correctly built interfaces under its rules look like this: a modal or card that, when removed, leaves the way it came in — fading and sliding back to the exact offset it entered from instead of vanishing or shrinking to nothing; a list whose items exit without the remaining items jumping, because the exiting item is popped out of the layout flow; a swapped view where the total changeover stays snappy instead of two full animations running back to back.
- **Frame by frame:** Correct exit: element enters from opacity 0, y 20 → opacity 1, y 0; on removal it returns along the same path → opacity 0, y 20 (exit mirrors initial; an unrelated exit such as scale to 0 fails). In mode "wait", the exit runs fully before the enter starts, so a 0.3s pair totals ~600ms and fails — durations must be halved (~0.15s each, ~300ms total) to stay acceptable. In popLayout mode, the exiting element leaves the layout flow the moment its exit starts, so siblings reflow immediately while it fades in place.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Exit rules: `exit-requires-wrapper` (every conditional motion element wrapped in AnimatePresence), `exit-prop-required`, `exit-key-required` (unique keys from item.id, never the array index), `exit-matches-initial` (exit mirrors initial). Presence hooks: `presence-hook-in-child` (useIsPresent called in a child of AnimatePresence, never the parent), `presence-safe-to-remove` (with usePresence, always call safeToRemove after async cleanup resolves), `presence-disable-interactions` (disable controls while isPresent is false, e.g. `disabled={!isPresent}`). Mode rules: `mode-wait-doubles-duration` (halve durations under mode="wait"), `mode-sync-layout-conflict` (sync mode makes exiting and entering elements compete for space — position exiting elements absolutely or change mode), `mode-pop-layout-for-lists` (popLayout for list reordering). Nested rules: `nested-propagate-required` (propagate on nested AnimatePresence or children vanish instantly when the parent exits), `nested-consistent-timing` (coordinate parent/child exit durations — parent 0.2s with child 0.15s passes; parent 0.1s with child 0.5s fails). Output: `file:line - [rule-id] description` plus a Rule/Count/Severity table.
- **Reference / source:** UI Skills — Raphael Salaja. References named: Motion's AnimatePresence documentation (motion.dev) and MDN's @starting-style page.
- **Best for:** React/Motion builds with modals, toasts, tab swaps and animated lists. Limited direct use in the single-file vanilla-HTML trade builds (no AnimatePresence there), but its principles — exit mirrors entrance, halve durations on sequential swaps, pop exiting items out of flow — transfer to any exit animation QA.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0085⟧

## ⟦S0086⟧ morphing-icons — Part 08 — UI Skills — Raphael Salaja
- **What it is:** A build skill (not an audit) for icon components where any icon morphs into any other through real SVG shape transformation — the lines themselves travel and rotate into the new glyph instead of one icon fading out and another fading in.
- **How it looks:** A menu icon's three horizontal bars glide and rotate until they form a close cross; an arrow's shaft and two head strokes swing as one rigid shape from pointing right to pointing down; a check mark's two strokes stretch into a plus. Unused structure never pops: extra lines shrink into the centre point and fade out as the morph begins, and grow back out when an icon needs them again. Endpoints stay soft because every line cap is round.
- **Frame by frame:** Trigger: the icon state changes (click/hover/state swap). Step 1: each of the three SVG lines begins interpolating its endpoints (x1, y1, x2, y2) and opacity toward the target icon's three lines over 0.4s with exponential ease-out [0.19, 1, 0.22, 1]; lines the target doesn't need collapse to zero-length points at the centre (7, 7) while fading to opacity 0. Step 2: if both icons belong to the same rotation group, the whole group also rotates on a spring toward the target rotation (0° → 90° → 180° → −90° for the arrow family); if the groups differ, rotation jumps instantly with no animation. End state: the exact target glyph, resting. Under prefers-reduced-motion the whole morph becomes an instant swap (transition duration 0).
- **Mechanism & key values:** Hard architecture: every icon is exactly 3 lines on one shared 14×14 viewBox (centre 7); unused lines use the collapsed constant `{x1:7, y1:7, x2:7, y2:7, opacity:0}` — never null or omission. Icon definition: `lines: [IconLine, IconLine, IconLine]`, optional `rotation`, optional `group`. Rotational variants must share the same base lines and group (arrow lines: shaft {2,7}→{12,7}, head {7.5,2.5}→{12,7} and {7.5,11.5}→{12,7}; plus/cross share one line set at rotation 0/45 in group "plus-cross"). One- and two-line icons (minus, check, chevrons) pad with collapsed lines; dot icons (more, grip) are zero-length lines at visible positions ({3,7}, {7,7}, {11,7}). Rotation runs through Motion's useSpring with transformOrigin "center"; non-grouped rotation uses `rotation.jump()`, grouped uses `rotation.set()`. `strokeLinecap="round"` on every line; SVG carries `aria-hidden="true"`. Recommended transition: `ease: [0.19, 1, 0.22, 1], duration: 0.4`. Also ships audit output: `file:line - [rule-id] description` plus a Rule/Count/Severity table.
- **Reference / source:** UI Skills — Raphael Salaja. References named: Benji's "Morphing icons with Claude" experiments (benji.org/morphing-icons-with-claude), Motion useSpring docs, MDN SVG line element.
- **Best for:** Icon state swaps in navigation and CTAs — menu→close in a mobile nav, play→pause, plus→cross expanders in process/FAQ rows — anywhere a trade homepage swaps one glyph for another and a crossfade (S0075) feels cheap; for true shape-morph moments in heroes and section switchers.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0086⟧

## ⟦S0087⟧ pseudo-elements — Part 08 — UI Skills — Raphael Salaja
- **What it is:** An audit skill for CSS pseudo-elements and the View Transitions API: it reviews ::before/::after usage, native pseudo-element styling (::backdrop, ::placeholder, ::selection) and page-transition wiring, outputting file:line findings.
- **How it looks:** It produces no visuals itself; interfaces built to its rules show: decorative layers (background washes, overlays) that exist without extra wrapper divs cluttering the markup; small links and icon buttons that are easier to hit than they look, because an invisible pseudo-element extends the clickable area past the visible glyph; dialogs resting on a dimmed, softly blurred backdrop that the browser itself paints; and page changes where a card's image grows into the hero image of the next view instead of the whole page cross-fading.
- **Frame by frame:** A passing view transition: before the change, the source image alone carries a unique view-transition-name (e.g. "card"); the DOM updates inside `document.startViewTransition(...)` while the name hands over to the target image and is cleared from the source; the browser then animates the shared element between its two positions/sizes — with custom styling such as `::view-transition-group(card)` at animation-duration 300ms and cubic-bezier(0.215, 0.61, 0.355, 1) — instead of the default crossfade; afterwards no element keeps a stale name, so the next transition can't conflict. A passing dialog open: the dialog appears over a ::backdrop painted with a translucent black (var(--black-a6)) plus backdrop-filter blur(4px).
- **Mechanism & key values:** Before/After rules: `pseudo-content-required` (::before/::after need `content` to render at all), `pseudo-over-dom-node` (decorative layers as pseudo-elements, not extra DOM nodes), `pseudo-position-relative-parent` (absolute pseudo needs a positioned parent), `pseudo-z-index-layering` (parent `z-index: 1`, pseudo layer at `z-index: -1` so it never covers the text), `pseudo-hit-target-expansion` (negative insets on a pseudo, example `inset: -8px -12px`, instead of wrapper markup). View Transitions rules: `transition-name-required`, `transition-name-unique` (one name per page during a transition — assign per element, e.g. `card-${id}`, never a class-wide name on many cards), `transition-name-cleanup` (clear the name from the source inside the transition callback), `transition-over-js-library` (prefer the native View Transitions API over a JS library's shared-element layoutId), `transition-style-pseudo-elements` (style ::view-transition-group and friends rather than accepting the default crossfade; example 300ms, cubic-bezier(0.215, 0.61, 0.355, 1)). Native styling rules: `native-backdrop-styling` (dialog::backdrop, example background var(--black-a6) + blur(4px); no hand-rolled overlay div), `native-placeholder-styling` (::placeholder with opacity 1, not a fake span), `native-selection-styling` (::selection, e.g. background var(--blue-a5), color var(--gray-12)). Output: `file:line - [rule-id] description` plus a Rule/Count/Severity table.
- **Reference / source:** UI Skills — Raphael Salaja. References named: MDN Pseudo-elements reference and MDN View Transitions API.
- **Best for:** Page/section transition polish and CSS hygiene on any build — shared-element image transitions from a work/gallery grid into a case view, dialog and lightbox backdrops, hit-area fixes on small nav and footer links, branded text selection. The view-transition rules are the reference for gallery→detail morphs on portfolio-style trade pages.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0087⟧

## ⟦S0088⟧ sounds-on-the-web — Part 08 — UI Skills — Raphael Salaja
- **What it is:** An audit skill for audio feedback in interfaces: it reviews where sound is used, whether it is accessible, and how it is implemented, and reports violations as file:line findings.
- **How it looks:** Nothing visual of its own — its rule is that sound never carries information alone: every audio cue is paired with a visible change (a success state on the button, a confirmation panel, an error toast), so the interface reads identically with the sound off. Where sound is used at all it is quiet by default and user-controlled: an explicit sound toggle in settings, an independent volume control, and restraint — most interactions (typing, hovering, scrolling, navigating) stay silent.
- **Frame by frame:** No motion; the temporal rules are about when a sound fires: a short click (~50ms) at the moment an instant action completes; a success sound at the moment a payment or form submission resolves, alongside the visual confirmation; an error sound at the moment an error that can't be overlooked appears, alongside its toast. A long sound (e.g. a 2-second whoosh) on an instant action fails — duration must match the action's own duration.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Accessibility: `a11y-visual-equivalent` (visual equivalent for every cue), `a11y-toggle-setting` (explicit disable toggle wired into the sound provider), `a11y-reduced-motion-check` (prefers-reduced-motion treated as a proxy for sound sensitivity — don't play), `a11y-volume-control` (volume from user preference, not hard-coded 1). Appropriateness: `appropriate-no-high-frequency` (no sound on typing or keyboard navigation), `appropriate-confirmations-only` (payments, uploads, form submissions are the yes cases), `appropriate-errors-warnings`, `appropriate-no-decorative` (no hover sounds), `appropriate-no-punishing` (gentle alert, never a loud buzzer). Implementation: `impl-preload-audio` (construct and .load() all sounds at app init, not on first play), `impl-default-subtle` (default volume 0.3; 1.0 fails), `impl-reset-current-time` (set currentTime = 0 before replay so rapid retriggering works). Weight matching: `weight-match-action` (soft click for a toggle; success chime for a purchase; a triumphant fanfare on a minor action fails), `weight-duration-matches-action` (50ms click for a click; a progress-length sound for an upload). Appropriateness matrix in the skill scores payment success, form submission, error state and notification as Yes; significant button click as Maybe; typing, hover, scroll and navigation as No. Output: `file:line - [rule-id] description` plus a Rule/Count/Severity table.
- **Reference / source:** UI Skills — Raphael Salaja. References named: Web Audio API documentation (MDN) and MDN's prefers-reduced-motion page.
- **Best for:** Only if a build deliberately adds sound feedback — e.g. a subtle confirmation on quote-form submission. For standard trade homepages the honest application is its restraint rules: no hover/typing/scroll sounds, and any sound paired with a visual equivalent. SITUATIONAL for trades.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0088⟧

## ⟦S0089⟧ to-spring-or-not-to-spring — Part 08 — UI Skills — Raphael Salaja
- **What it is:** An audit skill for timing-function selection: it reviews animation code and decides, per interaction, whether the motion should run on a spring, an easing curve, linear timing, or no animation at all — and reports wrong choices as file:line findings.
- **How it looks:** It produces no visuals itself; interfaces that follow it feel like this: a dragged panel that, when flicked, flies and settles with the flick's own energy — a hard flick travels faster than a gentle one — while a toast announcing a saved change simply arrives on a clean, predictable fade-slide with no bounce or restlessness; a progress bar whose fill honestly tracks elapsed time; menus and keyboard navigation that respond instantly with no animation at all.
- **Frame by frame:** A passing drag release: the element leaves the pointer with the pointer's velocity fed into a spring (stiffness 500, damping 30), overshoots at most slightly, and settles — interrupting it mid-flight retargets smoothly because the spring preserves velocity. A passing modal entrance: 200ms ease-out (arrive fast, settle gently). Its exit: 150ms ease-in (build momentum, then gone). A passing page transition: 250ms ease-in-out. A context menu: no entrance frame at all — it is simply there; only its exit animates.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Decision framework — ask "is this motion reacting to the user, or is the system speaking?": user-driven (drag, flick, gesture) → spring (survives interruption, preserves velocity); system-driven (state change, feedback) → easing (clear start/end); time representation (progress, loading) → linear (1:1 with time); high-frequency (typing, fast toggles) → none. Spring rules: `spring-for-gestures`, `spring-for-interruptible`, `spring-preserves-velocity` (pass the gesture's velocity into the spring), `spring-params-balanced` (stiffness 500 / damping 30 passes; stiffness 1000 / damping 5 fails as excessive oscillation). Easing rules: `easing-for-state-change` (a spring on a toast fails as restless), `easing-entrance-ease-out`, `easing-exit-ease-in`, `easing-transition-ease-in-out`, `easing-linear-only-progress`. Durations: `duration-press-hover` 120–180ms (150ms example), `duration-small-state` 180–260ms (200ms example), `duration-max-300ms` (user-initiated animations never exceed 300ms), `duration-shorten-before-curve` (if motion feels slow, shorten the duration before sharpening the curve — 400ms with a sharp bezier fails, 200ms ease-out passes). No-animation rules: `none-high-frequency`, `none-keyboard-navigation` (CSS :focus-visible only), `none-context-menu-entrance`. Quick reference in the skill: drag release = spring 500/30; button press = 150ms ease; modal enter 200ms ease-out; modal exit 150ms ease-in; page transition 250ms ease-in-out; progress = linear; typing feedback = 0ms none. Output: `file:line - [rule-id] description` plus a Rule/Count/Severity table.
- **Reference / source:** UI Skills — Raphael Salaja. References named: Apple WWDC23 "Animate with Springs", Freya Holmér's "The Beauty of Bézier Curves" (YouTube), and the Motion library (motion.dev).
- **Best for:** Choosing the timing engine for every animated moment in a build — draggable/scroll-driven hero elements and drawers (springs), section entrances and CTA feedback (easing), progress and loading (linear), menus (none). The decision table behind all motion QA; pairs with S0083.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0089⟧

## ⟦S0090⟧ improve-react — Part 09 — UI Skills — other featured authors (millionco, shadcn, 0xdesign, Dammyjay93, bencium, addyosmani, wshobson, taste-skill)
- **What it is:** A read-only React audit-and-planning skill: it surveys a whole React codebase as a senior engineer, using React Doctor's scan as machine-verified evidence, then produces a prioritised findings table and fully self-contained implementation plans that other agents (including cheaper models) execute later. It never edits source — plans are the product.
- **How it looks:** No visitor-facing visuals; the deliverables are documents in a `plans/` folder (or `react-plans/` if plans/ is taken): a findings table ordered by leverage (# / Severity / Category / Location / Rule / Finding / Fix summary), 2–4 separately listed "missed opportunities", one plan file per selected finding (NNN-short-slug.md, stamped with the short commit SHA), and a plans/README.md giving execution order, dependencies and status.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. Its sequence: Phase 1 Recon (one read-only React Doctor JSON scan, stack identification, a leverage map of hot vs cold paths) → Phase 2 Audit in parallel across five categories → Phase 3 Vet every finding at its file:line, prioritise, confirm selection with the user → Phase 4 Write the self-contained plans.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Run `npx react-doctor@latest --json --json-out react-doctor-report.json` read-only; never `--fix`, installs, commits or formatters. Five audit categories (AUDIT.md): Bugs & correctness (no-array-index-as-key, no-random-key, jsx-key, exhaustive-deps, no-self-updating-effect, no-set-state-in-render, no-uncontrolled-input, rendering-conditional-render), Performance (jsx-no-constructed-context-values, jsx-no-new-object/array/function-as-prop, no-inline-prop-on-memo-component, rerender-dependencies, no-layout-property-animation, no-transition-all), Accessibility (alt-text, control-has-associated-label, click-events-have-key-events, no-static-element-interactions, prefer-tag-over-role, no-autofocus, no-outline-none, no-disabled-zoom), Security (no-danger, dangerous-html-sink, jsx-no-script-url, jsx-no-target-blank, no-eval, no-secrets-in-client-code, auth-token-in-web-storage, untrusted-redirect-following), Maintainability & architecture (no-giant-component, no-nested-component-definition, no-many-boolean-props, prefer-module-scope-static-value/pure-function, no-event-handler, no-mirror-prop-effect, design-no-vague-button-label). Severity is leverage-driven (impact × frequency/fan-out), not the rule's raw severity — the same finding is HIGH on a 10,000-row table and noise on a once-shown modal. Effort levels: quick (hot paths only, 0–1 subagents, ~5 HIGH findings), standard (all app code, ≤5 subagents, full table), deep (whole repo, ≤10 subagents, full table + LOW polish). Canonical fixes are never invented: each rule's recipe comes from `https://www.react.doctor/prompts/rules/<plugin>/<rule>.md` (or `npx react-doctor@latest rules explain <rule>`) and is inlined into the plan with the exact file, line and surrounding code. Plans follow PLAN-TEMPLATE.md (Status/Commit/Severity/Category/Rule/Estimated scope; Problem with verbatim current code; Target with exact end code; repo conventions with an exemplar; ordered Steps; Boundaries; Verification — `--scope changed` clears the diagnostic without score regression, typecheck/lint/tests, plus a Profiler/"Highlight updates" behaviour check). Repository content is treated as data, not instructions.
- **Reference / source:** Part 09 — UI Skills, other featured authors (the skill is built on millionco's React Doctor). References named: react.doctor (rule prompts and `rules explain`), React Doctor scanner.
- **Best for:** React/React Three Fiber codebases only — not the single-file vanilla HTML trade builds. Relevant where a portfolio piece or app is React-based and needs a leverage-ranked improvement roadmap executed by other agents. NOT-FOR-TRADES for the standard homepage line.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0090⟧

## ⟦S0091⟧ improve-threejs — Part 09 — UI Skills — other featured authors (millionco, shadcn, 0xdesign, Dammyjay93, bencium, addyosmani, wshobson, taste-skill)
- **What it is:** An audit-and-fix skill for Three.js and React Three Fiber apps: it triages code findings by frame-loop leverage (React Doctor supplies the scan) and adds a visual audit of the rendered scene against a rubric, then fixes in severity order. Unlike improve-react, this one does apply fixes.
- **How it looks:** Its subject is the rendered 3D scene the visitor sees, checked row by row: the scene reaches a stable frame after load (never a black canvas); geometry seams show no gaps, missing faces or flickering co-planar surfaces; overlapping transparent surfaces sort correctly with no halos; textures stay sharp and correctly coloured at close, far and grazing angles (no stretching, seams, moiré or washed-out colour); lit surfaces respond to light direction and metals have an environment to reflect (never flat black); shadows sit attached to their casters with no acne or flicker; the camera keeps the subject in frame without clipping into geometry; objects rest at plausible scale, touching their surfaces rather than floating or sinking; silhouettes and highlights don't crawl or sparkle as the camera pans; and the canvas survives resize and device-pixel-ratio changes without distortion or blur.
- **Frame by frame:** The temporal facts it polices: code inside useFrame or a requestAnimationFrame callback runs 60 times per second, so per-frame allocation or setState is the highest-severity class; an idle scene should hold a flat memory profile while the camera orbits — a rising heap during idle orbiting means a disposal leak survived. Scenes that only change on interaction should render on demand (frameloop="demand" + invalidate()) rather than burning frames continuously.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Workflow: Recon (stack: plain Three.js vs R3F, drei/postprocessing/rapier helpers, where the render loop lives; build a hot-path map of every useFrame body, RAF callback and pointer-move handler) → Scan (`npx react-doctor@latest --verbose`, read-only; re-run with `--scope changed` after fixes and confirm the score did not drop) → Triage: HIGH = allocation inside useFrame (new Vector3()/Color()/arrays per frame — hoist a scratch object and mutate in place), setState inside useFrame (mutate refs instead), missing dispose() on imperatively created geometries/materials/textures/render targets, object reconstruction in render (unmemoised geometry/material, identity-changing inline args); MEDIUM = unstable scene-graph props, missing instancing for hundreds of identical meshes (use Instances/InstancedMesh), frameloop="always" on interaction-only scenes, asset loading outside useLoader/useTexture/useGLTF; LOW = scanner findings on non-canvas UI, missing Preload, oversized textures. Visual-rubric causes: washed-out/dark colour → renderer.outputColorSpace and texture.colorSpace must be SRGBColorSpace (data textures must NOT be sRGB); z-fighting → polygonOffset or a nudge, near plane too small for scene scale; shadow acne/floating shadows → tune shadow.bias and shadow.normalBias, shrink the shadow camera frustum; blurry/stretched canvas → sync renderer size to CSS size, setPixelRatio, camera.updateProjectionMatrix() on resize; black metals → metalness 1 with no scene.environment; transparency glitches → depthWrite:false, manual renderOrder, split large transparent meshes; shimmer/crawl → texture anisotropy, antialiasing, thicker thin geometry. Hand-checks the scanner always misses: dispose() coverage, allocations/setState in the loop, canvas/window listener and ResizeObserver cleanup, raycasting against the full scene per pointer move, global shadows/postprocessing where only part of the scene needs them, colour-space configuration. Canonical rule fixes come from `https://www.react.doctor/prompts/rules/<plugin>/<rule>.md`, never improvised.
- **Reference / source:** Part 09 — UI Skills, other featured authors (built on millionco's React Doctor). References named: react.doctor rule prompts.
- **Best for:** Any build that ships a real 3D/WebGL moment — a rotating roof/house model, a materials configurator, an immersive hero — where frame-loop performance and rendered correctness decide whether the 3D earns its place; the visual rubric doubles as the QA checklist for screenshots of 3D sections. SITUATIONAL for trades (only the 3D builds).
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0091⟧

## ⟦S0092⟧ improve — Part 09 — UI Skills — other featured authors (millionco, shadcn, 0xdesign, Dammyjay93, bencium, addyosmani, wshobson, taste-skill)
- **What it is:** The general-purpose senior-advisor skill (the parent pattern of improve-react): it surveys any codebase, finds the highest-value improvement opportunities across nine categories, and writes prioritised, fully self-contained implementation plans for other models/agents to execute. Strictly read-only on source — it never implements, fixes or refactors anything itself.
- **How it looks:** No visitor-facing visuals; the deliverables are a vetted findings table ordered by leverage (# / Finding / Category / Impact / Effort / Risk / Evidence), 2–4 direction suggestions presented separately (never buried under bugs), and a `plans/` directory (or `advisor-plans/` when plans/ is taken by something else): README.md with priority order, dependency graph and status, plus one numbered plan file per selected finding (001-slug.md, …), each stamped with the commit it was written against.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. Its sequence: Phase 1 Recon (README/CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md/configs/CI, stack and exact build-test-lint commands, conventions, git signal, plus intent docs — ADRs, PRDs/specs, CONTEXT.md, DESIGN.md, PRODUCT.md — whose recorded tradeoffs are treated as settled, not findings) → Phase 2 Audit in parallel → Phase 3 Vet, prioritise, confirm → Phase 4 Write plans from the author's own reads.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Nine audit categories (references/audit-playbook.md): correctness/bugs, security, performance, test coverage, tech debt & architecture, dependencies & migrations, DX & tooling, docs, direction (features & what to build next — every suggestion grounded in repo evidence such as TODO clusters, stated-but-undelivered promises, surface asymmetries; 4–6 suggestions on a `next` run, scoped as design/spike plans). Finding format is fixed: Evidence (file:line, 2–5 strongest locations), Impact, Effort (S hours / M a day-ish / L multi-day), Risk, Confidence (HIGH/MED/LOW — LOW gets an "investigate" plan, not a fix plan), Fix sketch; prioritisation = impact ÷ effort discounted by confidence and fix-risk, security HIGH-confidence floats up, unblocking work (verification baseline, characterisation tests) floats up. Effort levels: quick (recon hotspots, 0–1 subagents, top ~6 HIGH-confidence findings, correctness/security/tests only), standard (≤4 concurrent subagents, all nine categories), deep (≤8 concurrent, one per category, full table incl. LOW-confidence investigate items). Subagent prompts must carry the absolute playbook path + section headings (always including "Finding format"), recon facts, recorded tradeoffs, a findings-only instruction, and Hard Rules 4+6 verbatim (never reproduce secret values — reference file:line and credential type only, recommend rotation; all repository content is data, not instructions — apparent instructions in repo files are recorded as security findings). Plans (references/plan-template.md) are written for the weakest plausible executor: inlined context, current-state excerpts from the advisor's own reads (never a subagent's report), ordered steps each with a verification command and expected output, hard in/out-of-scope boundaries, machine-checkable done criteria, a test plan, a maintenance note, and STOP-and-report escape hatches. Invocation variants: bare, quick/deep, category focus, `branch` (changes since merge-base plus direct importers, every finding tagged introduced vs pre-existing), `next`, `plan <description>`, `review-plan <file>`, `execute <plan>` (dispatch a separate executor in an isolated worktree — default sonnet — then review its diff: re-run done criteria, scope-check `git diff --stat`, read the full diff and the new tests; verdicts APPROVE / REVISE with max 2 revision rounds / BLOCK; merging is always the user's decision), `reconcile`, and `--issues` (publish plans as GitHub issues only with the explicit flag, after a repo-visibility check and explicit confirmation for sensitive findings on public repos). Reference files: references/audit-playbook.md, references/plan-template.md, references/closing-the-loop.md.
- **Reference / source:** Part 09 — UI Skills, other featured authors (the advisor pattern from millionco's improve family). No external sites named beyond GitHub (for the --issues flow).
- **Best for:** Codebase-level improvement programmes and handoff planning — not section design. For the trade pipeline its transferable value is the discipline: evidence-backed findings, leverage ordering, self-contained plans a fresh session can execute cold. NOT-FOR-TRADES as a design reference; process reference only.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0092⟧
## ⟦S0093⟧ design-lab — Part 09 — UI Skills — other featured authors
- **What it is:** A design-exploration workflow, not a style: it interviews the user, auto-detects the project's framework/styling/design tokens, then generates five meaningfully different variants of a component or page inside a temporary "design lab" route so they can be compared side by side with the same data. The user comments by clicking elements in an in-browser feedback overlay (or answers in the terminal), the skill synthesises a hybrid variant if wanted, shows a final preview, then deletes every temporary file and writes an implementation plan (`DESIGN_PLAN.md`) plus a persistent `DESIGN_MEMORY.md`. Visual styles are never predefined — they are inferred from the project's own Tailwind config, CSS variables, UI-library theme and existing components.
- **How it looks:** The deliverable the user sees is a lab page: a header carrying the design-brief summary, then a grid of five rendered variants labelled A–E, each with a short "why this exists" note and its key differences called out; variants sit in a 2–3 column grid on desktop and a horizontal scroll or tabs on a phone, all fed by one shared fixtures file so the comparison is fair. All five variants wear the project's own visual language (its colours, type, radius, shadows), pushed along five different axes: A restructures information hierarchy (Gestalt grouping, one primary action), B swaps the layout model (card vs list vs table vs split-pane), C changes density against the brief, D changes the interaction model (modal vs inline vs panel vs drawer, all states built), E pushes the stated brand direction expressively. The bundled DESIGN_PRINCIPLES reference defines the house look the variants are judged against: a type scale of Display 32–48px / H1 24–32px / H2 20–24px / H3 16–18px / Body 14–16px / Caption 12–13px, an 8px spacing grid (4/8/12/16/24/32/48/64+px), a neutral foundation (background #FFFFFF, surface #FAFAFA, border #E5E5E5, text #171717 / #737373 / #A3A3A3, dark surfaces #000000/#111111/#333333), a radius scale (0 tables, 4px buttons/inputs, 8px cards/modals, 12px feature cards, 9999px avatars/pills) and four shadow levels from `0 1px 2px rgba(0,0,0,0.05)` to `0 20px 25px rgba(0,0,0,0.15)`.
- **Frame by frame:** The lab itself is a sequence: preflight detection → five-step interview → brief summary → lab page generated → user clicks "Add Feedback" (bottom-right), clicks any element, types a comment, submits → comments are parsed per variant and applied → either the winning variant is refined, or a new hybrid Variant F replaces the lab with F prominent and the 1–2 closest originals kept for comparison → final preview route, with a before/after toggle or split view for redesigns → confirm → all temp files deleted, plan and memory written. Motion inside the variants follows the principles file: a card under a fine pointer lifts on hover (translateY −2px plus a shadow step up, gated behind `@media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)`); a pressed button scales to 0.97; entrances fade in while sliding up 8–16px, or scale from 0.95 with a fade (never from 0), children staggered 30–50ms apart; exits run 20–30% faster than entrances; loading feedback is staged by wait time — under 100ms nothing, 100–300ms a subtle opacity/skeleton change, 300ms–1s a spinner or progress bar, over 1s skeleton screens, over 10s background processing with a notification; icons swap by crossfade (old scales to 0.5 with 7px blur out, new scales up from 0.5 with blur clearing, 0.15s); drag interactions track the pointer instantly with `jump()` during the drag and spring to their snap point with `set()` on release.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Eight phases (0 preflight → 8 finalize) driven by lock-file/config detection (`pnpm-lock.yaml`, `next.config.*`, `tailwind.config.*`, `@mui/material`, etc.) and a JSON design brief at `.claude-design/design-brief.json`; variants live in `.claude-design/lab/variants/` with a mandatory `data-variant="A–E"` attribute per container and a self-contained `FeedbackOverlay.tsx` copied into the route directory itself (relative import, so it never breaks); optional env config `DESIGN_AUTO_IMPLEMENT`, `DESIGN_KEEP_LAB`, `DESIGN_MEMORY_PATH`. Prescribed motion numbers: micro-interactions 100–150ms, tooltips/dropdowns 150–250ms, modals/drawers 200–300ms, page transitions 300–400ms, UI transitions generally 150–300ms with ease-out entrances and ease-in exits; easing tokens `--ease-out-quad: cubic-bezier(0.25, 0.46, 0.45, 0.94)`, `-cubic: (0.215, 0.61, 0.355, 1)`, `-quart: (0.165, 0.84, 0.44, 1)`, `-quint: (0.23, 1, 0.32, 1)`, `--ease-in-out-cubic: cubic-bezier(0.645, 0.045, 0.355, 1)`; springs tuned per interaction, never shared (typical stiffness 200–400, damping 20–40, mass 0.5–2; exit springs at double stiffness); rubber-band elasticity 0.55; iOS momentum projection deceleration 0.998; drag-vs-click threshold 5px; hit areas expanded with an `inset: -12px` pseudo-element; accessibility floors: contrast 4.5:1 text / 3:1 UI, touch targets 44×44px min, focus ring 2px with offset, body measure 60–75 characters, line height 1.4–1.6; tables virtualised past 50 rows; blur of 1–2px on layers that cross during transitions.
- **Reference / source:** Part 09 collection; the skill text identifies the generator as the "Design Variations plugin". Its DESIGN_PRINCIPLES.md reference curates Jakob Nielsen's 10 heuristics, Don Norman's principles, Dan Saffer's microinteractions, and patterns credited inline to Stripe, Linear, Vercel, Airbnb, Apple, Material, Notion and iA; its "study these systems" list names linear.app, stripe.com, vercel.com, airbnb.com, notion.so, slack.com, bloomberg.com, figma.com, github.com, apple.com and framer.com.
- **Best for:** Deciding a section's design before committing — generating genuinely different directions for a hero, pricing block, form or whole page and letting a human pick and annotate, exactly the discipline a 1·2·3 version switcher needs (five axes here; the same axis discipline applies to three). Its principles file doubles as a standing rulebook for forms (label above, validate on blur, focus first error), cards, tables (right-aligned tabular numbers, min row 40–48px), navigation sizing (2–5 items tabs, 5–10 side nav) and motion values on any build. It is a process skill: it produces no look of its own, and it targets app UI in a live codebase rather than a single self-contained homepage file.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0093⟧

## ⟦S0094⟧ interface-design — Part 09 — UI Skills — other featured authors
- **What it is:** A craft discipline for product interfaces — dashboards, admin panels, SaaS apps, tools, settings and data screens — whose whole job is stopping the model from shipping the generic template its training defaults to. It forces an intent brief first (the actual human, the verb they must accomplish, the feeling in concrete words), then a product-domain exploration that produces five-plus domain concepts, a colour world taken from the product's physical world, one signature element only this product could have, and three named defaults to reject — before any layout, colour or type is chosen. Explicitly not for landing pages, marketing sites or brand-only work.
- **How it looks:** Quiet, layered product UI where hierarchy is unmistakable and nothing shouts. One focal point wins each view through size, weight, contrast or surrounding space while everything else is deliberately demoted: its worked metric reads REVENUE in 11px/500 muted tracked caps, the figure $48,200 at 28px/600 in primary ink with tabular numbers, and a ↑12% delta at 12px/500 in the success colour — against the flat default of two identical grey 14px lines in identical boxes. Surfaces stack in whisper steps (dark-mode base, then +7%, +9%, +12% lightness per level); the sidebar wears the same background as the canvas with only a subtle border; inputs sit slightly darker than their surroundings so they read as inset; borders are low-opacity rgba (about rgba(255,255,255,0.06–0.12) on dark) that disappear until you look for them. Colour runs roughly 60/30/10 — dominant neutral surface, secondary tone, about 10% one accent — and token names evoke the product's world (`--ink`, `--parchment`) instead of `--gray-700`. Type hierarchy is built from a ratio scale (about 1.25 from a 14px base gives 11/14/16/18/22/28/44+) and from weight-plus-opacity tiers at a single size, not from size alone.
- **Frame by frame:** Mostly a still interface; movement is small and functional. Press a button → it scales to 0.97 (never below 0.95) for the duration of the press → releases back. Open a popover or dropdown → it grows out of its trigger point (transform-origin set to the trigger, modals excepted — they stay centred) starting at scale 0.95 with opacity 0 → settles at full size; menus and drawers follow the same grow-from-source pattern. A list or group entering → its items arrive staggered 30–80ms apart → all visible. Any exit → the same path reversed, faster and subtler than the entrance. Actions repeated 100+ times a day (keyboard shortcuts, command palette) get no animation at all — the state simply changes.
- **Mechanism & key values:** A mandatory checkpoint stated before writing any component — Intent / Hierarchy / Palette / Depth / Surfaces / Typography / Spacing, each with a WHY, or the work is defaulting. Controls are built native HTML first, then a battle-tested headless primitive (Radix UI, React Aria, Ark, Headless UI, Vaul, cmdk are named), hand-rolled only as a last resort with the full keyboard/focus/ARIA contract; styling goes system → component → semantic token → utility, never hardcoded hex or repeated utility strings. Numbers: durations under 300ms for UI (button press 100–160ms, tooltips/popovers 125–200ms, dropdowns 150–250ms, modals/drawers 200–500ms); easing `cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1)` for entering/interactive, `cubic-bezier(0.77, 0, 0.175, 1)` for on-screen movement, ease-in banned; only transform and opacity animate; spacing on a 4px or 8px base with symmetric padding; four text levels (primary/secondary/tertiary/muted); ONE depth strategy committed per product (borders-only, subtle shadows, layered shadows, or surface shifts); light-mode lift shadow stack `0 0 0 1px rgba(0,0,0,.06), 0 1px 2px -1px rgba(0,0,0,.06), 0 2px 4px rgba(0,0,0,.04)`, collapsing on dark to a single `0 0 0 1px rgba(255,255,255,.08)` ring; image outlines 1px inset rgba(0,0,0,0.1); concentric radius rule outer = inner + padding; hit areas 44×44px (40 minimum). Work is verified with four tests — swap (change the typeface/layout: if nothing feels different you defaulted), squint, signature (point to five elements carrying the signature), token (read the CSS variables aloud) — and decisions are saved to `.interface-design/system.md`; ships two commands, `/interface-design:design-review` and `/interface-design:design-deslop`.
- **Reference / source:** Part 09 collection. No external origin is named in the text; its stated craft benchmarks are the product teams of Linear, Vercel, Stripe and Apple.
- **Best for:** Dashboards, admin panels, settings pages, data tables and tool screens — anywhere a trades business's software-like surface appears: a quote configurator, a booking or job-management view, an internal CRM-style panel, or the app fragments embedded in a product page. Not a homepage-section skill: it refuses marketing pages by design, so for trade homepages it governs the functional fragments (calculators, forms, account views) rather than the hero, proof or gallery sections.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0094⟧

## ⟦S0095⟧ design-taste-frontend — Part 09 — UI Skills — other featured authors (tasteskill v2)
- **What it is:** A complete anti-template system for building pages (and, in a parallel run, app screens) whose core claim is that a model left to invent a look picks the category average — centred headline, little label above it, icon cards, soft gradient — so the design decisions are dealt, not improvised. A script (`scripts/draw.mjs`) deals three of twenty researched directions distilled from a study of 247 real sites; the builder picks the one that can carry an idea found in the subject's own inventory (its name, street, materials, numbers, rituals, printed artefacts), writes the page's argument and full copy deck first, builds the page still, then must pass machine gates (`lint.mjs`, and `inspect.mjs` measuring the real page in a browser at 1440/768/390px) and up to three screenshot-critique rounds scored like an Awwwards juror, before a choreographed motion layer is added last. Ships 11 reference files (copy, type, colour, layout, imagery, motion, scenes, critique, tells, research, app-screens), a scroll-scene stage library, and an asset search over open image collections.
- **How it looks:** A finished page has one dominant thing per screen and reads as posters in sequence. Very large type does the talking (display tracking −0.02 to −0.05em, leading 0.85–1.05; on the studied top sites the largest type medians 8.4vw against 5.0vw on weak ones) beside small quiet text, with almost nothing in between — five sizes maximum. The frame is tight and exact: one pair of equal outer margins (16–32px) at every width, everything aligned to two or three left anchor lines, sections 120–240px apart on desktop, each section a different composition from its neighbours. Colour is flat and rationed: one ground holding 70–90% of the page, one ink, one accent under 5% appearing on the action and at most one other thing; whole sections can flip to a full colour field, meeting edge to edge with a hard line. Pictures are real and large — at least four, usually six to twelve, roughly a third of the scrolled page is picture, media square-cornered (94% of the October 2026 study) in one or two crop ratios. Absent by rule: eyebrows/kickers, pill badges, gradients, shadows on resting elements, glass, monospace labels, 01/02/03 numbering, hairline rules, icon-topped card rows, styled accent words. Navigation is a plain bar (wordmark, three to five links, one action) or none; the footer is a designed close, most often the name returned at full width. App screens (the parallel run) look different on purpose: a noun title at about 24px, KPI values as bare type (median 24–26px, no tiles, no icons, no sparklines), colour only on data at about 3% of pixels, 1px rules instead of shadows, one grotesk throughout.
- **Frame by frame:** On load, everything is already painted and a sequence of at most four elements settles inside 1.2 seconds: the headline's lines rise from behind their own baselines (translateY(105%) → 0, 800–900ms on the expo-out curve, staggered 90–110ms per line) → the supporting sentence and the one primary button rise 12px while fading in (delays around 420–480ms) → the hero picture opens downward as its clip-path inset goes from `inset(0 0 100% 0)` to full over about 1,000–1,150ms while the image inside settles from scale 1.08–1.12 to rest.
