## ⟦S0181⟧ gsap-core — PART 11 — GSAP official skills
- **What it is:** The official GSAP core-engine skill: single tweens (gsap.to / from / fromTo / set), eases, staggers, defaults, transforms, and gsap.matchMedia() for responsive and reduced-motion animation. This is the base layer under nearly every animated section in the bank.
- **How it looks:** Whatever the tween targets: elements sliding, scaling, rotating, fading on a web page — entrances that rise and fade in, cards that stagger across, SVG shapes rotating around a shared point. Fades use autoAlpha, so a fully faded element also becomes invisible and non-clickable.
- **Frame by frame:** A gsap.from() entrance: at creation the element is immediately placed at the start values (e.g. opacity 0, y offset) so there is no flash of the final state → over the duration (default 0.5s) it eases toward its natural end state with the chosen ease ("power1.out" default; "back.out(1.7)" overshoots then settles; "elastic.out(1, 0.3)" wobbles into place) → with stagger, each sibling starts its own run offset by the stagger interval (e.g. 0.1s, or { amount: 0.3, from: "center" }) → end state is the element's natural layout, optionally with inline styles cleared via clearProps.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Methods: gsap.to (to given values), gsap.from (from given values to current), gsap.fromTo (explicit both ends), gsap.set (immediate). Vars: duration (default 0.5s), delay, ease (built-ins none/power1–4/back/bounce/circ/elastic/expo/sine, each .in/.out/.inOut; CustomEase for cubic-bezier or SVG-path curves), stagger (number or { each, amount, from: "start"|"center"|"end"|"edges"|"random" }), overwrite (false / true / "auto"), repeat (-1 = infinite), yoyo, immediateRender (default true for from/fromTo — set false on later competing from() tweens). Transform aliases applied in fixed order (translation → scale → rotationX/Y → skew → rotation): x/y/z px, xPercent/yPercent, scale/scaleX/scaleY, rotation (deg), rotationX/rotationY, skewX/skewY, transformOrigin; relative values "+=20" / "-=30"; directional rotation suffixes "_short", "_cw", "_ccw"; SVG svgOrigin in global coords (never combine with transformOrigin). CSS vars animatable ("--hue": 180). gsap.defaults() sets project-wide duration/ease. gsap.matchMedia() (GSAP 3.11+): mm.add("(min-width: 800px)", fn) or a conditions object { isDesktop, isMobile, reduceMotion: "(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)" }; unmatched contexts auto-revert; with reduceMotion use duration: 0. CamelCase property names throughout. Do not animate width/height/top/left when a transform alias does the job.
- **Reference / source:** Official GSAP skill (gsap.com), PART 11; docs links inside: gsap.com/docs/v3/GSAP/gsap.matchMedia/, gsap.com/resources/getting-started/Staggers. Skill notes GSAP powers Webflow Interactions.
- **Best for:** The engine for everything — hero entrances, staggered proof/reviews cards, gallery motion, call/CTA emphasis, SVG drawing/morph bases. Framework-agnostic, works in the single-file HTML builds.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0181⟧

## ⟦S0182⟧ gsap-frameworks — PART 11 — GSAP official skills
- **What it is:** Official GSAP skill for Vue, Nuxt, Svelte/SvelteKit and other lifecycle frameworks: create animations after mount, scope selectors to the component, and clean up on unmount. (React has its own skill, ⟦S0185⟧.)
- **How it looks:** No look of its own — it governs how GSAP animations behave inside components: they start once the component's DOM exists, only affect that component's subtree, and vanish cleanly (inline styles reverted) when the component unmounts.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. Lifecycle sequence instead: component mounts → onMounted/onMount creates tweens and ScrollTriggers inside gsap.context(callback, scopeElement) → component unmounts → ctx.revert() kills all of them and reverts inline styles.
- **Mechanism & key values:** gsap.context(() => {...}, containerRef) scopes selector text to the root; Vue 3 Composition API and <script setup> patterns with onMounted/onUnmounted; Svelte onMount returning () => ctx.revert(), with bind:this for the container; Svelte 5 same principle. Nuxt 4: a useGSAP() composable that registers ScrollTrigger once and lazy-loads any of the 26 listed plugins (SplitText, MorphSVG, Flip, Draggable, etc.) via dynamic import to cut bundle size. ScrollTriggers created inside the context are reverted with it; call ScrollTrigger.refresh() after layout changes (after nextTick/tick or async content load). Never create tweens in setup/top-level code before the DOM exists; never use unscoped global selectors in components; register plugins once at app level, not per render.
- **Reference / source:** Official GSAP skill (gsap.com), PART 11; ships runnable examples/ folders (vue/, nuxt/) as referenced in the skill.
- **Best for:** Framework builds (Vue/Nuxt/Svelte sites and componentised previews). For the single-file vanilla HTML homepages, ⟦S0181⟧/⟦S0186⟧/⟦S0187⟧ are the operative skills; this one governs any component-based work.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0182⟧

## ⟦S0183⟧ gsap-performance — PART 11 — GSAP official skills
- **What it is:** Official GSAP skill for animation performance: keeping GSAP at a smooth 60fps by animating compositor-only properties, batching, and reducing simultaneous work.
- **How it looks:** No look of its own — its result is motion that never stutters: scroll-driven sections and mouse followers that stay fluid on low-end phones.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. It constrains how other skills' motion is implemented.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Animate transform (x, y, scale, rotation, rotationX/Y, skewX/Y) and opacity only; avoid width/height/top/left/margin/padding (layout thrash). Add CSS will-change: transform only on elements that actually animate (never blanket will-change/force3D). Batch DOM reads before writes. Use stagger instead of many hand-delayed tweens; virtualize long lists or animate only visible items; reuse timelines instead of creating them per frame. For frequently updated properties (mouse followers) use gsap.quickTo() — the skill's example: gsap.quickTo("#id", "x", { duration: 0.4, ease: "power3" }). ScrollTrigger: pin only what's needed (pin promotes the element); scrub with a small value (e.g. scrub: 1) can reduce scroll work; call ScrollTrigger.refresh() only when layout actually changes, debounced — not on every resize. Pause/kill off-screen or inactive animations.
- **Reference / source:** Official GSAP skill (gsap.com), PART 11. No external sites named beyond GSAP docs context.
- **Best for:** The performance gate for every animated homepage version — pinned stories, parallax and WebGL-adjacent sections on trade pages must pass these rules to stay smooth on visitors' phones.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0183⟧

## ⟦S0184⟧ gsap-plugins — PART 11 — GSAP official skills
- **What it is:** Official GSAP skill for the whole plugin suite: registration, ScrollTo, ScrollSmoother, Flip, Draggable + Inertia, Observer, SplitText, ScrambleText, DrawSVG, MorphSVG, MotionPath, easing plugins (CustomEase, EasePack, CustomWiggle, CustomBounce), Physics2D/PhysicsProps, GSDevTools, PixiPlugin. Key licensing fact recorded in the skill: since Webflow's acquisition of GSAP every plugin is free including commercial use — no Club GSAP, license key, auth token or private registry; install everything from the public gsap npm package.
- **How it looks:** Per plugin: text splitting into letters that ripple in (SplitText); SVG line art that draws itself stroke by stroke (DrawSVG); one shape melting into another (MorphSVG); an element travelling along a curved path (MotionPath); cards flinging with momentum (Draggable + Inertia); a grid that reshuffles with every item gliding to its new slot (Flip); text that scrambles through random glyphs before resolving (ScrambleText); smooth momentum page scroll (ScrollSmoother).
- **Frame by frame:** SplitText chars (skill's example): SplitText.create(".heading", { type: "words, chars" }) → each char starts at opacity 0, y 20 → chars animate in with stagger 0.03 over duration 0.4 → line-split variant: lines start y 100, opacity 0 → stagger 0.05, duration 0.5; with mask: "lines", each line is wrapped in an overflow-clip mask so it reveals upward out of its mask. DrawSVG: the stroke's visible segment grows from "0% 0%" to "0% 100%" (or any segment, e.g. "20% 80%") over the tween. Flip: Flip.getState(".item") captures positions → DOM changes instantly → Flip.from(state, { duration: 0.5, ease: "power2.inOut" }) glides every element from its old box to its new box. ScrollTo: window scroll animates over duration 1 to a y position or element (offsetY 50 in the example). Physics2D example: a ball launches with velocity 250 at angle 80 under gravity 500 and arcs for 2s.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Register every used plugin once with gsap.registerPlugin() before first use. ScrollToPlugin scrollTo: { y | x (number or "max"), element, offsetX, offsetY }. ScrollSmoother requires #smooth-wrapper > #smooth-content DOM and ScrollTrigger. Flip.from vars: absolute (default false), nested, scale (default true), simple, duration, ease. Draggable: type "x"|"y"|"x,y"|"rotation"|"scroll", bounds, inertia (needs InertiaPlugin), edgeResistance 0–1, callbacks onDragStart/onDrag/onDragEnd/onThrowUpdate/onThrowComplete; InertiaPlugin.track(target, "x") then inertia: { x: "auto" } glides to a stop. Observer: target, onUp/onDown/onLeft/onRight, tolerance default 10, type "touch,pointer" default. SplitText.create vars: type (default "chars,words,lines" — split only what's needed), charsClass/wordsClass/linesClass (append "++" for incremented classes), aria "auto"|"hidden"|"none" (auto adds aria-label + aria-hidden), autoSplit with onSplit(self) returning the animation for re-split sync, mask "lines"|"words"|"chars", tag default "div", deepSlice default true, ignore selector, smartWrap, wordDelimiter, propIndex (adds --word/--char CSS vars), reduceWhiteSpace default true; revert() restores markup; split after fonts load; font-kerning: none avoids char-spacing shift; no SVG <text> support. ScrambleText: { text, chars: "01", revealDelay: 0.5 } over duration 1. DrawSVG works on path/line/polyline/polygon/rect/ellipse, needs a visible stroke; getLength()/getPosition() utilities. MorphSVG: morphSVG { shape (required), type "linear" (default) | "rotational", map "size"|"position"|"complexity", shapeIndex (number or per-segment array; "log" to discover; findShapeIndex utility), smooth (v3.14+: number | "auto" | { points, redraw, persist }), curveMode, origin default "50% 50%", precision default 2, precompile }; MorphSVGPlugin.convertToPath() converts primitives. MotionPath: { path, align, alignOrigin default [0.5, 0.5], autoRotate, curviness 0–2 }; MotionPathHelper for visual tuning. EasePack adds SlowMo, RoughEase, ExpoScaleEase. GSDevTools: development only, never ship. PixiPlugin animates PixiJS display objects via a pixi: {} vars object.
- **Reference / source:** Official GSAP skill (gsap.com), PART 11; doc links inside: gsap.com/docs/v3/Plugins/ (and per-plugin pages for Flip, SplitText, DrawSVG, MorphSVG), gsap.com/blog/webflow-GSAP/ for the licensing change.
- **Best for:** The special-effects shelf for homepage versions — SplitText for hero headline reveals, DrawSVG for a roofline/truss line drawing itself, MorphSVG for icon/state morphs, MotionPath for a van/leaf travelling a route in a towns section, Flip for filterable work galleries, Draggable for before/after sliders. This is the highest-value plugin reference in the bank.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0184⟧

## ⟦S0185⟧ gsap-react — PART 11 — GSAP official skills
- **What it is:** Official GSAP skill for React/Next.js: the useGSAP() hook from @gsap/react, scoped refs, contextSafe callbacks, and guaranteed cleanup on unmount.
- **How it looks:** No look of its own — it makes React-component animations start after render, stay inside their component, and clean up without leaks or warnings when the component unmounts.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. Lifecycle: component renders → useGSAP(callback, { scope }) runs the GSAP setup → animations play → unmount triggers automatic revert of all animations and ScrollTriggers created in the context.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Install gsap + @gsap/react; gsap.registerPlugin(useGSAP) before any use. useGSAP(() => {...}, { scope: containerRef, dependencies: [...], revertOnUpdate: true }) — scope limits selector text to the component root; revertOnUpdate reverts and re-runs cleanup whenever dependencies change. Callbacks created after the hook runs (event handlers) must be wrapped in the returned contextSafe() or they escape cleanup. Without the hook: gsap.context(() => {...}, ref) inside useEffect with return () => ctx.revert() — mandatory. Use refs for targets, not bare global selectors. SSR: never execute gsap/ScrollTrigger during server render; client-only via useGSAP/useEffect or dynamic import.
- **Reference / source:** Official GSAP skill (gsap.com), PART 11; gsap.com/resources/React linked inside.
- **Best for:** React/Next.js builds and componentised previews. Not applicable to the vanilla single-file HTML homepages (use ⟦S0181⟧/⟦S0186⟧/⟦S0187⟧ there), but governs any React artifact work.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0185⟧

## ⟦S0186⟧ gsap-scrolltrigger — PART 11 — GSAP official skills
- **What it is:** Official GSAP skill for ScrollTrigger: scroll-linked animation — triggers, scrub, pinning, snapping, batching, and fake horizontal scroll. The single most important skill for scroll-driven homepage sections.
- **How it looks:** Sections that animate as you scroll: a panel pins to the screen while its contents transform, a bar slides sideways as the page moves down, rows of cards fade up in a wave as they enter, progress tied exactly to scroll position so scrolling backwards reverses the scene.
- **Frame by frame:** Basic scrub scene (skill's example): the trigger's top reaches viewport center (start: "top center") → as the user scrolls toward end: "bottom center", the tween (x to 500) advances in direct proportion to scroll (scrub: true), or trails behind by the scrub value in seconds (scrub: 1 = the playhead takes 1s to catch up) → scrolling back reverses it frame-for-frame. Pinned story: section top hits viewport top (start: "top top") → the section pins and stays while 1000px of scrolling (end: "+=1000") drives its inner timeline with scrub 1 → at the end it unpins and the page continues. Batch reveal: each card crossing start: "top 80%" is collected into a batch → the batch animates opacity 0→1, y 100→0 with stagger 0.15.
- **Mechanism & key values:** gsap.registerPlugin(ScrollTrigger) once. start/end format "triggerPosition viewportPosition" ("top top", "center center", "bottom 80%"), numeric px, relative "+=300" / "+=100%", "max", functions, and clamp() wrapping (v3.12+); defaults: start "top bottom" ("top top" when pin: true), end "bottom top"; endTrigger for a different end element. toggleActions: four slots onEnter/onLeave/onEnterBack/onLeaveBack, each play|pause|resume|reset|restart|complete|reverse|none, default "play none none none" — never combine scrub and toggleActions (scrub wins). pin: true pins the trigger (animate children, not the pinned element); pinSpacing default true (spacer prevents layout collapse), or false/"margin". snap: number increments (0.25), array, "labels", or { snapTo, duration: 0.3, delay: 0.1, ease: "power1.inOut" }. toggleClass, once, id (ScrollTrigger.getById), refreshPriority (lower refreshes first; create triggers top-to-bottom or set priorities). Callbacks onEnter/onLeave/onEnterBack/onLeaveBack/onUpdate/onToggle/onRefresh/onScrubComplete receive the instance (progress, direction, isActive, getVelocity()). ScrollTrigger.create() for standalone triggers. ScrollTrigger.batch(targets, vars): interval default ~one requestAnimationFrame, batchMax (number or responsive function); batched callbacks receive (targets, scrollTriggers); don't pass trigger/scrub/snap/toggleActions to batch. scrollerProxy() integrates third-party smooth scrollers — the scroller MUST call ScrollTrigger.update on its updates; pinType "fixed" if pins jitter, "transform" if they don't stick. Horizontal containerAnimation pattern: pin the panel, tween the inner wrapper's x/xPercent with ease: "none" (mandatory — any other ease breaks the 1:1 scroll mapping), inner triggers use containerAnimation: scrollTween with starts like "left center"; pinning/snapping unavailable on containerAnimation triggers. ScrollTrigger.refresh() recalculates after DOM/font/image changes; auto-called on resize, debounced 200ms. markers: true is development-only. ScrollTrigger goes on the timeline or top-level tween, never on a child tween inside a timeline.
- **Reference / source:** Official GSAP skill (gsap.com), PART 11; gsap.com/docs/v3/Plugins/ScrollTrigger/ and the batch() docs linked inside.
- **Best for:** The backbone of award-style trade homepages — pinned process stories (survey → strip → rebuild), parallax heroes, horizontal work galleries, scrubbed before/after reveals, staggered proof cards. Pair with ⟦S0183⟧ performance rules and respect reduced-motion via ⟦S0181⟧ matchMedia.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0186⟧

## ⟦S0187⟧ gsap-timeline — PART 11 — GSAP official skills
- **What it is:** Official GSAP skill for timelines: gsap.timeline(), the position parameter, labels, nesting and playback control — sequencing many tweens into one choreographed, controllable animation.
- **How it looks:** Multi-step scenes instead of isolated effects: a headline slides in, then its underline draws, then three cards cascade, then a badge pops — all timed against each other, and the whole sequence can be played, paused, reversed or scrubbed as one unit (including by scroll, via ⟦S0186⟧).
- **Frame by frame:** Default timeline: tween A runs to completion → tween B starts → tween C follows, appended end to end. With the position parameter the choreography overlaps: a tween placed at "<" starts together with the previous one, "<0.2" starts 0.2s after the previous start, "-=0.2" begins 0.2s before the previous end, "+=0.5" waits half a second after it; labels ("intro", "outro") mark chapters the playhead can jump to.
- **Mechanism & key values:** gsap.timeline({ defaults: { duration: 0.5, ease: "power2.out" }, paused, repeat, yoyo, onComplete/onStart/onUpdate }) — defaults are inherited by every child tween. Position parameter (third argument): absolute seconds (0, 1), relative strings ("+=0.5", "-=0.2"), labels ("labelName", "labelName+=0.3"), "<" (start of recently added), ">" (end of recently added, the default), "<0.2". Labels: tl.addLabel("intro", 0), tl.play("outro"), tl.tweenFromTo("intro", "outro") (returns a tween of the playhead itself, no ease). Nesting: master.add(childTimeline, position). Playback: play(), pause(), reverse(), restart(), time(2), progress(0.5), kill() (kills children by default). Timeline duration is derived from its children, not set directly. ScrollTrigger attaches to the timeline (or a top-level tween), never to tweens inside it, and ScrollTriggered animations must not be nested inside a parent timeline. Prefer timelines over chaining with delay.
- **Reference / source:** Official GSAP skill (gsap.com), PART 11. No external sites named beyond GSAP docs context.
- **Best for:** Choreographing every multi-element section — hero entrance sequences, process-step stories, pinned scroll narratives (as the timeline ScrollTrigger scrubs), and coordinated proof/gallery reveals.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0187⟧
## ⟦S0188⟧ gsap-utils — Official GSAP skills
- **What it is:** The official reference for `gsap.utils` — GSAP's pure helper functions for clamping, range-mapping, normalizing, interpolating, randomizing, snapping, wrapping and distributing values inside animations. It produces no visual design of its own; it is the maths layer that scroll-driven and randomized motion is built from.
- **How it looks:** Nothing on screen by itself. In use it shows up as motion that stays inside set bounds, scroll progress converted proportionally into rotation or travel, elements scattered to random positions, values landing exactly on grid steps, or a property (scale, opacity) spread across a row of elements so the middle ones differ from the edges.
- **Frame by frame:** No motion of its own. Typical wiring: scroll or pointer moves → `normalize` turns the raw position into 0–1 → `mapRange` converts that into the target range (e.g. 0–360deg) → `clamp`/`snap` keep the result inside limits or on steps → the tween applies it each frame.
- **Mechanism & key values:** `clamp(min,max,value)`, `mapRange(inMin,inMax,outMin,outMax,value)`, `normalize(min,max,value)`, `interpolate(start,end,progress)` (numbers, colours, objects), `random(min,max,snapIncrement,returnFunction)` plus the tween-var string forms `"random(-100, 100, 5)"` / `"random([red, blue, green])"`, `snap(snapTo,value)` (multiple or array of allowed values), `shuffle`, `distribute({base, amount|each, from: "start"|"center"|"edges"|"random"|"end"|[ratios], grid:[rows,cols]|"auto", axis, ease})`, `getUnit`, `unitize`, `splitColor(color, returnHSL)` → [r,g,b(,a)] or [h,s,l], `selector(scope)`, `toArray(value, scope)`, `pipe(...)` (left-to-right composition), `wrap(min,max,value)` (inclusive min, exclusive max — for infinite scroll/cyclic values), `wrapYoyo` (bounces at the ends). Key behaviour: omit the value argument and most utils return a reusable function; `random` is the exception — pass `true` as the last argument. `mapRange`/`normalize` work on numbers only, not units.
- **Reference / source:** Official GSAP skill; docs at gsap.com/docs/v3/GSAP/UtilityMethods and gsap.com/docs/v3/HelperFunctions. Pairs with gsap-core, gsap-timeline, gsap-scrolltrigger.
- **Best for:** The plumbing behind scroll-scrubbed sections, parallax mapping, randomized/staggered reveals, grid-snapped motion and centre-out distributions — not a design source in itself.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0188⟧

## ⟦S0189⟧ make-interfaces-feel-better — MCP Market (ECC + Antigravity)
- **What it is:** A polish checklist of small design-engineering details — concentric radii, optical alignment, shadow/border use, text wrapping, image outlines, motion defaults, hit areas — that compound into an interface that feels finished rather than flat or jumpy.
- **How it looks:** Nested rounded surfaces whose corners agree (outer radius = inner radius + padding), icons that look centred rather than geometrically centred, images with a hairline neutral inset outline so their edges don't blur into the page, headings that wrap evenly instead of leaving a widow word, and numbers (prices, counters) whose digits don't shift width as they change.
- **Frame by frame:** Interaction states only: a control is pressed → it scales to `scale(0.96)` for tactile feedback → releases back. An element enters → opacity + small translateY (+ optional blur) ease in; exits → shorter and quieter, usually 150ms. An icon swaps → old and new cross-fade with opacity, scale and blur instead of an instant toggle.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Concentric radius rule `outer = inner + padding` (large padding = treat as separate surfaces). `text-wrap: balance` on headings/short titles, `text-wrap: pretty` on short-to-medium body text (neither on long prose/code). `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` for counters, timers, prices, tables. Root font smoothing `-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased`. Image outline `1px solid rgba(0,0,0,0.1)`, `outline-offset: -1px` (white 0.1 alpha in dark mode; never brand-tinted). Hit areas at least 40×40px, ideally 44×44px, expandable by pseudo-element without overlapping neighbours. CSS transitions for state changes (they retarget mid-motion); keyframes reserved for staged one-shots/loaders. Never `transition: all` — list properties (example given: transform, background-color, box-shadow at 150ms ease-out). `will-change` only for first-frame stutter on transform/opacity/filter; never `will-change: all`. Review output format: before/after table per principle.
- **Reference / source:** MCP Market ECC/Antigravity collection; salvaged from stale community PR #1659 by `linus707`.
- **Best for:** Final polish pass on every section — cards, buttons, forms, navigation, galleries — and as a QA checklist before a build is called done.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0189⟧

## ⟦S0190⟧ frontend-design-direction — MCP Market (ECC + Antigravity)
- **What it is:** A direction-setting and evidence-gated workflow skill: before coding, fix purpose, audience, tone, one memorable detail and constraints, then build from a checkable "evidence contract" covering every content state, and pass a rendered finish gate before calling UI work done.
- **How it looks:** No single look — it produces interfaces whose first viewport immediately shows the actual product/workflow (not a marketing hero hiding it), with a palette that spans more than one hue family, contextual type sizes instead of reflexive oversized hero text, and stable grids/toolbars/counters that don't shift when labels or hover states change. Explicitly bans the generated look: purple gradients, decorative blobs, oversized cards, vague hero copy, stock-like atmospheric media, cards inside cards.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion of its own. Its motion rule: use sparingly and deliberately; high-signal transitions that clarify state over decorative animation.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Five direction decisions (Purpose / Audience / Tone — utilitarian, editorial, playful, industrial, refined, technical, maximal, minimal, dense, calm / Memorable detail / Constraints). Evidence contract records product surface, user's job, primary action, hierarchy, target viewports, and the reference observation behind each important choice. Six content states each need a trigger, visible feedback and safe next action recorded: Loading (stable structure, progress, cancellation), Empty (explain + next action), Error (specific failure + recovery path), Partial (show available, mark unavailable), Success (confirm + next action/undo), Permission (explain boundary + safe request/return); "not applicable" needs a recorded reason — untested access is not a reason. Rendered finish gate: inspect the actual render at the contract's viewports (a mobile capture cannot cover a desktop target), check keyboard nav, visible focus, labels, contrast, reduced motion, touch targets, and exercise each content state including partial data. Evidence is a local JSON record (`contract`, `targetViewports`, `accessibility`, `responsive`, `contentStates`, `renderedEvidence` with non-symlink artifact files) validated by the bundled `check-evidence.js`; the checker rejects incomplete/failed/untested records. Optional UIZZE MCP research (`find_ui_references`, `find_ui_materials`, 800,000+ real web/iOS screens) only with consent and only sanitized aggregate needs sent.
- **Reference / source:** MCP Market ECC/Antigravity collection; salvaged from stale community PR #1659 by `linus707`; state/evidence contribution from UIZZE's anti-ui-slop workflow (github.com/uizze/uizze) via PR #2814. ECC deliberately does not rebundle Anthropic's canonical `frontend-design` skill (install from anthropics/skills).
- **Best for:** Process discipline behind whole builds — direction briefs, state coverage on forms/CTAs, and the rendered-QA gate for any section before it is presented.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0190⟧

## ⟦S0191⟧ frontend-patterns — MCP Market (ECC + Antigravity)
- **What it is:** A React/Next.js pattern library: component composition, compound components, render props, custom hooks, Context+Reducer state, memoization, code splitting, virtualization, controlled forms, error boundaries, Framer Motion animation patterns, and keyboard/focus accessibility patterns.
- **How it looks:** Standard app UI built cleanly — tab bars where the active tab is highlighted and switches panels, lists that animate in item by item, modals that fade in over a dimmed overlay, dropdowns you can drive entirely from the keyboard, long lists that scroll smoothly because only the visible rows exist in the DOM.
- **Frame by frame:** Framer Motion list pattern: each item starts at opacity 0, y +20 → animates to opacity 1, y 0 → on removal exits to opacity 0, y −20, all at duration 0.3s under `AnimatePresence`. Modal pattern: overlay fades opacity 0→1; the panel enters from opacity 0, scale 0.9, y 20 → opacity 1, scale 1, y 0; exit mirrors it. Dropdown: ArrowDown/ArrowUp move the active option (clamped at both ends), Enter selects and closes, Escape closes. Modal focus: on open, focus is saved and moved into the dialog; on close it returns to the element that opened it.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Composition over inheritance; compound components via Context; render props `(data, loading, error)`. Hooks: `useToggle`, `useQuery` (fetcher/options kept in refs so `refetch` stays referentially stable — without this, an infinite fetch loop), `useDebounce` (example delay 500ms). Performance: `useMemo` (copy before sort — `sort` mutates), `useCallback`, `React.memo`; lazy loading via `React.lazy` + `Suspense` with skeleton fallbacks. Virtualization with `@tanstack/react-virtual`: `estimateSize: 100`px rows, `overscan: 5`, container example height 600px. Forms: controlled inputs with per-field error strings (example rules: name required, max 200 characters). Animation values: list/modal transitions duration 0.3; enter y 20, exit y −20; modal scale 0.9.
- **Reference / source:** MCP Market ECC/Antigravity collection. Names Framer Motion and @tanstack/react-virtual; no external reference sites named.
- **Best for:** React/Next.js app builds rather than single-file trade homepages — but its modal, tab, dropdown and focus-management patterns transfer directly to quote-form modals and interactive widgets.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0191⟧

## ⟦S0192⟧ frontend-a11y — MCP Market (ECC + Antigravity)
- **What it is:** Accessibility patterns for React and Next.js components: label/error wiring for forms, semantic HTML, correct ARIA use, keyboard navigation, focus management, image/icon labelling and reduced-motion support — the issues most commonly flagged in code review.
- **How it looks:** A form where every field has a real visible label, required fields show an asterisk that screen readers don't read out as text, and errors appear as text linked to the exact field they belong to — the same clean form a sighted visitor sees, with nothing visual added or removed.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. Its one motion rule is subtractive: when the OS `prefers-reduced-motion` setting is on, transitions are removed entirely (worked example: card transition becomes `'none'` instead of `transform 300ms ease`).
- **Mechanism & key values:** Label pairing via `htmlFor`/`id`. Required fields: native `required` + `aria-required="true"`, asterisk wrapped in `aria-hidden="true"`. Errors: `aria-describedby` pointing at the error element's id, `aria-invalid`, error span with `role="alert"`. `aria-label` when no visible label exists (icon buttons); `aria-labelledby` when a visible label exists; `aria-describedby` for supplementary warnings. `aria-live`: `polite` for status, `assertive` only for urgent errors, with `aria-atomic="true"`. Accordion pattern: `aria-expanded` + `aria-controls` + `hidden`. Dropdown keyboard map: ArrowDown/ArrowUp clamp the active index, Enter/Space select, Escape closes, wrapper `role="combobox"`, `aria-haspopup="listbox"`. Modal: save `document.activeElement`, focus the dialog (`role="dialog"`, `aria-modal="true"`, `tabIndex={-1}`), Escape closes, restore focus on close; full Tab/Shift+Tab trapping delegated to the `focus-trap-react` library. Decorative images: `alt=""` + `aria-hidden="true"`. Anti-patterns named: click handlers on bare div/span, aria-label on a role-less div, placeholder-as-label, positive `tabIndex`, `aria-hidden` on focusable elements. Reduced motion via a `useReducedMotion` hook on `matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)')`.
- **Reference / source:** MCP Market ECC/Antigravity collection; names focus-trap-react (github.com/focus-trap/focus-trap-react).
- **Best for:** Quote forms, call/CTA widgets, accordions/FAQs, tabs and any interactive control on a trade homepage — the compliance layer, not a visual source.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0192⟧

## ⟦S0193⟧ accessibility — MCP Market (ECC + Antigravity)
- **What it is:** A WCAG 2.2 Level AA design/implement/audit skill spanning Web, iOS and Android: semantic roles and labels, platform traits/hints, focus management, contrast, target size and screen-reader support, organized around the POUR principles (Perceivable, Operable, Understandable, Robust).
- **How it looks:** The same interface, operable by everyone: text that stays readable against its background, tap targets big enough to hit reliably, a clearly visible focus outline as you tab through, forms that explain errors in words and suggest the correction instead of just turning a border red.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Contrast 4.5:1 for normal text, 3:1 for large text and UI components. Content must reflow up to 400% zoom without loss of function. Minimum target size 24×24 CSS px on web (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8), 44×44pt native. Visible focus indicator per SC 2.4.11. Single-pointer alternatives for dragging movements. Error suggestions per SC 3.3.3; Redundant Entry per SC 3.3.7 (never ask for the same data twice). Modals must contain focus and release it via Escape or a close button (SC 2.1.2). Five-step method: identify the component's role → perceivable attributes → operable controls → understandable logic → robust Name/Role/Value. Cross-platform mapping table: primary label = `aria-label`/`<label>` (Web), `.accessibilityLabel()` (iOS), `contentDescription` (Android); live updates = `aria-live="polite"`, `.accessibilityLiveRegion(.polite)`, Compose `liveRegion = LiveRegionMode.Polite`. Anti-patterns: div-buttons, colour-only meaning, uncontained modal focus, "Image of…" alt text.
- **Reference / source:** MCP Market ECC/Antigravity collection; references WCAG 2.2 (w3.org/TR/WCAG22), WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices, Apple Accessibility Programming Guide and HIG, Android Accessibility Developer Guide.
- **Best for:** The accessibility audit layer across any build — especially forms, navigation, modals and galleries; also the source for target-size and contrast numbers used in QA.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0193⟧

## ⟦S0194⟧ design-system — MCP Market (ECC + Antigravity)
- **What it is:** A three-mode skill that generates a design system from an existing codebase, audits a UI's visual consistency across 10 scored dimensions, and detects generic AI-generated design patterns ("AI slop").
- **How it looks:** Its generate mode outputs `DESIGN.md` + `design-tokens.json` + a self-contained interactive `design-preview.html` showing the extracted colours, type, spacing, radii and shadows as one coherent system. The slop mode names the look it hunts: gratuitous gradients everywhere, purple-to-blue defaults, purposeless glass-morphism cards, rounded corners on things that shouldn't be rounded, excessive scroll animations, and the generic centred-text-hero-over-stock-gradient.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. (Animation is one of its audit dimensions: "purposeful or gratuitous?")
- **Mechanism & key values:** Generate workflow: scan CSS/Tailwind/styled-components → extract colours, typography, spacing, border-radius, shadows, breakpoints → research 3 competitor sites (browser MCP) → propose token set as JSON + CSS custom properties → DESIGN.md rationale → HTML preview. Audit scores 0–10 on each of 10 dimensions: colour consistency, typography hierarchy, spacing rhythm (consistent 4px/8px/16px scale vs arbitrary), component consistency, responsive behaviour, dark-mode completeness, animation, accessibility (contrast, focus states, touch targets), information density, polish (hover states, transitions, loading and empty states) — each with specific examples and a fix at exact file:line. Invocation examples: `/design-system generate --style minimal --palette earth-tones`, `/design-system audit --url … --pages / /pricing /docs`, `/design-system slop-check`.
- **Reference / source:** MCP Market ECC/Antigravity collection. No external sites named beyond the competitor-research step.
- **Best for:** Pre-redesign audits of a client's existing site, token extraction so a rebuild stays consistent, and a slop check on any draft design before it goes further.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0194⟧

## ⟦S0195⟧ motion-foundations — MCP Market (ECC + Antigravity)
- **What it is:** The foundation layer of a three-skill motion system for React/Next.js (motion/react): shared motion tokens, five named spring presets, a `shouldAnimate()` gate, reduced-motion handling and SSR-safe initial states that the pattern and advanced skills inherit.
- **How it looks:** Motion with one consistent personality across a whole site — buttons, cards and modals all easing on the same curves and timings instead of each component inventing its own; on a reduced-motion or low-end device the same interface simply appears, with at most a short opacity fade.
- **Frame by frame:** Governed by the token timings: a tooltip or badge change is near-instant (0.08s); a button press or icon swap is quick (0.18s); a modal opening or card expanding takes 0.35s; a hero entrance 0.6s; a deliberate storytelling move 1.0s. Under `prefers-reduced-motion`, transforms are disabled entirely and only opacity fades of ≤0.2s remain.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Duration tokens: instant 0.08, fast 0.18, normal 0.35, slow 0.6, crawl 1.0 (seconds). Easing tokens: smooth [0.22, 1, 0.36, 1], sharp [0.4, 0, 0.2, 1], bounce [0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1], linear [0, 0, 1, 1]. Distance tokens: xs 4, sm 8, md 16, lg 24, xl 48 (px). Scale tokens: subtle 0.98, press 0.95, pop 1.04. Springs: snappy {stiffness 300, damping 30} (default UI), gentle {120, 14} (cards/modals), bouncy {400, 10} (playful moments), instant {600, 35} (tooltips/popovers/dropdowns), release {200, 20, restDelta 0.001} (drag release). Hard rules: import only from `motion/react`, never `framer-motion`; `initial` must match server-rendered output (mount guard pattern) or hydration breaks; never animate width/height/top/left/margin/padding — transform and opacity only; all durations/easings/springs come from the token maps, never inline; `"use client"` on every motion file; never read `window`/`navigator` at module level. Device gate: low-end = `navigator.hardwareConcurrency <= 4` → non-essential animation off, durations collapse to instant. Accessibility priority order: reduced-motion > low-end device > design preference. Motion must do at least one of: guide attention, communicate state, preserve spatial continuity — otherwise it is removed.
- **Reference / source:** MCP Market ECC/Antigravity collection; built on the `motion` package (motion/react). Foundation for ⟦S0196⟧ motion-patterns and ⟦S0197⟧ motion-advanced.
- **Best for:** Setting up the motion system before any animated build in React — the values layer only; the visible patterns live in S0196/S0197.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0195⟧

## ⟦S0196⟧ motion-patterns — MCP Market (ECC + Antigravity)
- **What it is:** Copy-paste production animation patterns for React/Next.js built on the S0195 tokens and springs: buttons, stagger lists, modals, toast stacks, page transitions, scroll reveals, a scroll progress bar, expanding cards, shared-element crossfades and accordions — each with correct enter AND exit behaviour.
- **How it looks:** A list whose items rise and fade in one after another; a modal panel that scales up softly from slightly small over a fading dark overlay; toast notifications sliding in from the right edge and sliding back out; a thin progress bar growing across the very top of the page as you scroll; a card that expands in place to reveal its body text while its heading stays put; a thumbnail photo that grows into the full-size photo on the next view.
- **Frame by frame:** Stagger list: container waits 0.1s (delayChildren), then items appear one by one every 0.08s — each from opacity 0, y +16px → opacity 1, y 0 on the gentle spring. Modal: overlay fades 0→1; panel enters from opacity 0, scale 0.95, y +8px → full size, on the gentle spring; exit mirrors it. Toast: enters from opacity 0, x +48px, scale 0.98 → settles at x 0; exits back to x +48px fading out, with layout animating the remaining toasts up. Page transition (App Router, `mode="wait"`): old page fades and rises −8px out completely, then the new page fades in from y +8px, over 0.35s on the smooth curve. Scroll reveal: as the element scrolls into view (viewport margin −80px, once only) it goes from opacity 0, y +24px → visible over 0.6s. Scroll progress: a fixed 4px-high bar, origin left, scaleX tied directly to scroll progress. Accordion: content scales Y 0→1 with opacity, transform-origin top, 0.35s.
- **Mechanism & key values:** All values imported from S0195 (duration normal 0.35, slow 0.6, fast 0.18; distances sm 8 / md 16 / lg 24 / xl 48; scale press 0.95, pop 1.04; springs snappy/gentle). Rules: `AnimatePresence` + stable `key` + `exit` prop or exits silently never fire; stagger interval must stay between 0.05s and 0.10s (worked example 0.08, delayChildren 0.1); page transitions use `mode="wait"`, stacks use `mode="sync"`, reflow lists `mode="popLayout"`; never use `layout` on subtrees over ~5 children — explicit transforms instead; `layout="position"` on text inside expanding containers to stop reflow animating; modals must ship focus trap, Escape close, scroll lock, `role="dialog"`, `aria-modal="true"`; scroll reveals use `viewport={{ once: true }}`; shared elements via matching `layoutId` (e.g. "hero-image") across source and destination.
- **Reference / source:** MCP Market ECC/Antigravity collection; motion/react. Consumes ⟦S0195⟧; extended by ⟦S0197⟧.
- **Best for:** Standard interactive furniture on any section — review/gallery lists entering, CTA modals, notification toasts, FAQ accordions, expanding service cards, page-to-page continuity.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0196⟧

## ⟦S0197⟧ motion-advanced — MCP Market (ECC + Antigravity)
- **What it is:** The advanced tier of the motion system: drag and drag-to-dismiss, swipe and long-press gestures, reorderable lists, word/character text animation, number counters, SVG path drawing and progress rings, custom hooks (scroll reveal, cursor follower), imperative `useAnimate` sequences, and loaders (spinner, shimmer, pulse).
- **How it looks:** A card you can grab and throw inside invisible bounds, lifting slightly with a soft shadow while held; a bottom sheet you drag down and flick away, fading as it goes; a headline whose words rise into place one after another; a stat number counting up from zero; an SVG line that draws itself across the screen; a ring that fills to show progress; a soft dot of colour trailing the visitor's cursor with springy lag; skeleton blocks with a band of light sweeping across them while content loads.
- **Frame by frame:** Drag-to-dismiss sheet: visitor drags down → sheet follows the finger 1:1 while its opacity maps drag distance 0–200px onto 1→0 → on release past 120px offset OR 500 velocity it closes, otherwise the release spring (stiffness 200, damping 20) settles it back. Swipe: drag is constrained to snap back (constraints 0/0) → on end, offset beyond 50px or velocity beyond 300 fires the swipe action. Word reveal: words start opacity 0, y +12px → rise in sequence, staggered 0.05s apart, on the gentle spring. Counter: on mount, a 1.0s smooth-eased count from 0 to the target written straight into the DOM node. SVG draw: `pathLength` animates 0→1 over 0.6s with opacity fading in alongside. Progress ring (r=40, circumference ≈ 251.3): stroke-dashoffset tweens over 0.35s as progress changes, ring rotated −90° so it starts at the top. Shimmer: a translucent white gradient band sweeps x −100%→100% on a 1.0s linear infinite loop, paused when the tab is hidden. Pulse dot: scale 1→1.4→1 with opacity 1→0.6→1 over 1.0s, infinite, also visibility-paused. Cursor follower: a 24px dot chases the pointer through a gentle spring (120/14), so it lags and settles rather than sticking to the cursor.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Drag: `dragConstraints` bounds, `dragElastic 0.1`, whileDrag scale 1.04 + shadow `0 16px 40px rgba(0,0,0,0.2)`, `dragTransition` = release spring. Thresholds must be explicit and combine offset + velocity (sheet: offset.y > 120 || velocity.y > 500; swipe: OFFSET_THRESHOLD 50, VELOCITY_THRESHOLD 300). Long press default 600ms. `useMotionValue` + `useTransform` for render-free derived values (e.g. x ∈ [−200, 200] → opacity [0, 1, 0]). `useAnimate` sequences are imperative and interrupt-safe (a new call cancels the running one); the scope ref must be mounted first. All tokens/springs from S0195 (durations: fast 0.18, normal 0.35, slow 0.6, crawl 1.0; stagger for text 0.05). Rules: test drag on real touch devices; infinite animations must pause on `document.visibilityState === "hidden"`; motion values via `useMotionValue`, never `new MotionValue` in render; every window listener gets cleanup; SVG morphs need equal path-command counts or they snap instead of interpolating. useSpring (continuous, pointer-tracked) vs spring transition (discrete state changes) decision table included.
- **Reference / source:** MCP Market ECC/Antigravity collection; motion/react. Requires ⟦S0195⟧; standard patterns are in ⟦S0196⟧.
- **Best for:** Interactive heroes and galleries — draggable before/after-style cards, swipeable review rows, counting stat strips (reviews, years, jobs), self-drawing SVG diagrams and route/process lines, custom cursor followers on portfolio-grade pages.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0197⟧

## ⟦S0198⟧ react-patterns — MCP Market (ECC + Antigravity)
- **What it is:** Idiomatic React 18/19 patterns: pure renders, hooks discipline, a state-location decision tree, Server/Client Component boundaries, Suspense + error boundaries, React 19 form actions, data-fetching choices, composition recipes and performance rules.
- **How it looks:** No visual design of its own — it governs how React UIs are structured underneath. Its visible fingerprints are interfaces that reveal progressively (skeletons close to the data, content streaming in section by section rather than one blocked page) and forms that show a pending state on the button ("Adding...") while the action runs.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion prescribed.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Core rules: render is a pure function of props and state (derive during render, never store derived state via useEffect); effects live in handlers/effects only; compose, don't inherit. Hooks: top-level only, clean up every subscription, functional updaters, default to NO memoization until a profiler proves otherwise, extract a hook only when the same sequence appears in 2+ components. State decision tree: one component → useState; parent + descendants → lift to nearest common ancestor; distant low-frequency (theme/auth/locale) → Context; high-frequency shared → external store (Zustand/Jotai/Redux Toolkit); server-derived → TanStack Query/SWR/RSC fetch. RSC boundaries: server→client passes serializable props or children; never import a Server Component into a Client Component file. Suspense boundaries sit close to the data, not at the route root. Forms: React 19 `useActionState` + server actions preferred; controlled inputs when the value drives other UI; a form library past trivial complexity. Data fetching: RSC `await fetch()` per-request, TanStack Query for client cache/mutations, SWR for lightweight cache, SSE/WebSockets for realtime; avoid useEffect+fetch for app data. Performance: `React.memo` only when re-renders are frequent, props usually equal, and render measurably expensive; split contexts per concern; virtualize lists once visible items exceed ~50 non-trivial rows; stable keys from database ids, never array index. Accessibility-first composition: semantic HTML before roles, keyboard-reachable interactives, labelled inputs, focus managed on route change and modal open/close, axe in component tests. Worked extras: `useDebounce` default 300ms; `useOptimistic` for instant list updates.
- **Reference / source:** MCP Market ECC/Antigravity collection; cross-links rules/react/, react-performance, frontend-patterns and accessibility skills, plus react-reviewer / react-build-resolver agents.
- **Best for:** React app architecture and review — background discipline for any React build, not a visual or motion source.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0198⟧

## ⟦S0199⟧ react-performance — MCP Market (ECC + Antigravity)
- **What it is:** A 70+ rule performance catalogue for React/Next.js in 8 priority categories — eliminating waterfalls, bundle size, server-side, client fetching, re-render, rendering, JS micro-performance, advanced — adapted from Vercel Engineering's React Best Practices.
- **How it looks:** Nothing visual by itself; its results are felt as speed: pages that paint their shell immediately and stream slower sections into reserved skeleton space instead of blocking on the slowest query, and lists of hundreds of rows that scroll without rendering cost for the off-screen rows.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. (One rendering rule touches animation: animate a wrapper div around an SVG, not the SVG itself, because wrapper transforms are GPU-accelerated while SVG transforms trigger paint.)
- **Mechanism & key values:** Priority order: 1 CRITICAL waterfalls (`async-`) — check cheap sync conditions before awaiting, defer awaits into the branch that uses them, `Promise.all` for independent work, start-early/await-late for partial dependencies, Suspense close to data, split sibling awaits into child Server Components so they run in parallel. 2 CRITICAL bundle (`bundle-`) — direct imports over barrels (barrel files cost 200–800ms of first-load JS in many real apps), statically analyzable import paths, dynamic imports for heavy components, third-party scripts after hydration (`next/script` strategy afterInteractive/lazyOnload), preload on hover/focus. 3 HIGH server (`server-`) — authenticate AND authorize inside every Server Action; `React.cache()` for per-request dedupe; LRU/`unstable_cache` for cross-request data; hoist static I/O to module scope; no mutable module-level state in SSR; minimize serialized props; Next.js `after()` for post-response work. 4 MEDIUM-HIGH client (`client-`) — SWR/TanStack Query dedupe; one shared global listener instead of per-component listeners; `{ passive: true }` on scroll listeners; versioned, minimal localStorage. 5 MEDIUM re-render (`rerender-`) — read store state inside callbacks instead of subscribing; hoist non-primitive defaults (a shared EMPTY array constant); primitive effect deps; subscribe to derived booleans; functional setState; lazy state initializers; startTransition/useDeferredValue; never define components inside components. 6 MEDIUM rendering (`rendering-`) — `content-visibility: auto` with `contain-intrinsic-size: auto 80px` for long lists; hoist static JSX; trim SVG coordinate precision to ~2 decimals; inline-script hydration no-flicker for theme/locale; narrow `suppressHydrationWarning` on leaf nodes only; React 19 `<Activity>` for show/hide; ternary over `&&` (a 0 renders as text); react-dom preload/preconnect hints. 7 LOW-MEDIUM JS (`js-`) — Map/Set O(1) lookups, single-pass filter+map, loop for min/max instead of sort, hoisted RegExp, requestIdleCallback. 8 LOW advanced (`advanced-`) — useEffectEvent values stay out of deps, handler refs/useLatest for stable callbacks, module-scope init-once guards. Tooling: Next.js 13.5+ optimizePackageImports, React Compiler (demotes manual memo rules to review-only), Turbopack, Bundle Analyzer. Web Vitals map: LCP ← waterfalls/bundle/hints; INP ← re-render/rendering/JS; CLS ← rendering; TBT ← bundle/JS/third-party.
- **Reference / source:** Adapted from Vercel Labs `react-best-practices` (MIT, v1.0.0, January 2026) — github.com/vercel-labs/agent-skills/tree/main/skills/react-best-practices.
- **Best for:** Performance review of any React/Next.js build — page-load waterfalls and bundle weight are its highest-value checks; the single-file HTML builds in this bank borrow its content-visibility and wrapper-animation rules only.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0199⟧

## ⟦S0200⟧ frontend-slides — MCP Market (ECC + Antigravity)
- **What it is:** A system for creating zero-dependency, animation-rich HTML presentations (or converting PPT/PPTX into them): style is discovered through visual preview slides rather than abstract questions, and every slide must fit exactly one viewport with no internal scrolling.
- **How it looks:** A deck of full-screen slides — atmospheric backgrounds (layered radial-gradient mesh, SVG noise grain, faint 50px grid lines), strong type hierarchy, abstract shapes and geometry rather than illustrations. Twelve named presets with exact fonts and palettes: Bold Signal (Archivo Black + Space Grotesk; charcoal, hot orange focal card, white text; oversized section numbers), Electric Studio (Manrope; black/white/cobalt; two-panel split), Creative Voltage (Syne + Space Mono; electric blue, neon yellow, deep navy; halftone), Dark Botanical (Cormorant + IBM Plex Sans; near-black, ivory, blush, gold, terracotta; blurred abstract circles, fine rules), Notebook Tabs (Bodoni Moda + DM Sans; cream paper on charcoal, pastel side tabs), Pastel Geometry (Plus Jakarta Sans; pale blue field, cream card, pink/mint/lavender; vertical pills), Split Pastel (Outfit; peach + lavender split, mint badges), Vintage Editorial (Fraunces + Work Sans; cream/charcoal/dusty; bordered callouts, serif headlines), Neon Cyber (Clash Display + Satoshi; midnight navy, cyan, magenta; glow, particles, grids), Terminal Green (JetBrains Mono; GitHub dark + terminal green; scan lines), Swiss Modern (Archivo + Nunito; white/black/signal red; visible grids, asymmetry), Paper & Ink (Cormorant Garamond + Source Serif 4; warm cream, charcoal, crimson; pull quotes, drop caps).
- **Frame by frame:** Scroll or arrow-key nav snaps slide to slide (`scroll-snap-type: y mandatory`); as a slide enters the viewport, an Intersection Observer adds `.visible` and its content reveals: default fade + slide-up (opacity 0, translateY 30px → in place over 0.6s on cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)), with scale-in (0.9→1), slide-from-left (−50px) and blur-in (blur 10px→0 over 0.8s) variants; staggered children follow at 0.1s / 0.2s / 0.3s / 0.4s delays; a progress bar and nav dots track position; a 3D tilt effect is available on cards (mousemove → rotateY ±10deg / rotateX ∓10deg inside a 1000px perspective, resetting on mouse leave). Feeling map: dramatic = slow 1–1.5s fades and 0.9→1 scale-ins with parallax; professional = subtle 200–300ms transitions; editorial = staggered text/image interplay.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Hard gate: every `.slide` is `height: 100vh; height: 100dvh; overflow: hidden`; all type/spacing via `clamp()` — title clamp(1.5rem, 5vw, 4rem), h2 clamp(1.25rem, 3.5vw, 2.5rem), body clamp(0.75rem, 1.5vw, 1.125rem), slide padding clamp(1rem, 4vw, 4rem); short-height breakpoints at 700px, 600px, 500px shrink tokens and hide nav dots/hints; cards capped at min(90vw, 1000px) × min(80vh, 700px); images max-height min(50vh, 400px), object-fit contain. Density limits: title slide 1 heading + 1 subtitle; content 1 heading + 4–6 bullets or 2 paragraphs; feature grid max 6 cards; code max 8–10 lines; quote 1 + attribution; image slide under 60vh. Overflow is solved by splitting slides, never by shrinking below readable sizes. Style discovery: generate 3 single-slide preview files in `.ecc-design/slide-previews/` (self-contained, ~100 lines each) for the user to pick/mix. Controller class covers keyboard (arrows, space, page up/down), wheel, touch/swipe, progress, nav dots. Optional inline editing: JS hover with a 400ms grace timeout (CSS `~` sibling approach explicitly banned — pointer-events breaks the hover chain), E key toggle, and `exportFile()` must strip contenteditable/edit classes before capturing outerHTML. CSS gotcha: never `-clamp(...)`/`-min(...)` — browsers silently ignore them; use `calc(-1 * clamp(...))`. PPT conversion via python-pptx. Fonts from Google Fonts/Fontshare, never system fonts; reduced-motion block collapses animation durations to 0.01ms / transitions 0.2s. Validation sizes include 1920×1080, 1280×720, 768×1024, 375×667, 667×375.
- **Reference / source:** MCP Market ECC/Antigravity collection; inspired by the visual exploration approach of zarazhangrui (@zarazhangrui). Bundled references: STYLE_PRESETS.md, animation-patterns.md, html-template.md.
- **Best for:** Talk, pitch and workshop decks — not homepage sections; its reveal choreography, preset discipline and viewport-fit rules transfer to full-screen section design.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0200⟧

## ⟦S0201⟧ nextjs-turbopack — MCP Market (ECC + Antigravity)
- **What it is:** Short guidance skill for Next.js 16+: Turbopack as the default dev bundler, its file-system caching, when to fall back to webpack, and the middleware.ts → proxy.ts filename change.
- **How it looks:** Static — no visual output; it governs tooling behaviour (dev startup and hot-reload speed) only.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** From Next.js 16, `next dev` runs Turbopack unless disabled (`--webpack` / `--no-turbopack` depending on version). Turbopack is an incremental Rust bundler with file-system caching (typically under `.next`); restarts reuse previous work and are cited as 5–14× faster on large projects. Next.js 16.1+ adds an experimental Bundle Analyzer. Production `next build` may use either bundler depending on version — check the docs for the release in hand. Filename rule: Next.js 16+ uses `proxy.ts` at project root for middleware; pre-16 uses `middleware.ts`; the change is tied to the Next.js version, not the bundler — never flag `proxy.ts` as misnamed in a Next 16 project, and never suggest renaming it (that breaks middleware execution).
- **Reference / source:** MCP Market ECC/Antigravity collection; Next.js proxy docs (nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/proxy).
- **Best for:** Next.js dev-environment decisions and code review only — no design or motion content.

## ⟦S0202⟧ vue-patterns — MCP Market (ECC + Antigravity)
- **What it is:** A Vue 3 Composition API pattern guide: feature-first project structure, SFC discipline, composables, Pinia setup stores, Vue Router, template and performance patterns, testing, Nuxt specifics and the Vue 3.5+ APIs.
- **How it looks:** No visual design of its own — standard Vue/Nuxt app structure underneath ordinary component UI. Nothing on screen is prescribed.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** SFC order fixed: script (imports → props/emits/slots → composables → state → computed → methods → watchers → lifecycle), template, scoped style. Naming: PascalCase.vue components, useCamelCase.ts composables, kebab-case route folders. Composables: `use` prefix, return reactive values only, accept MaybeRef/toValue inputs, clean up in onUnmounted/onCleanup, no module-scope side effects; they fully replace mixins. State choice table: ref/reactive local → props+emits parent-child → provide/inject for theme/config → Pinia (setup-store syntax preferred) for global state → server-state composable for API data. Router: lazy route components, `beforeEach` guards reading meta (e.g. requiresAuth), route params consumed via computed + watch. Performance: v-memo for rarely-changing list items, v-once for static-forever content, shallowRef/shallowReactive for wholesale-replaced data, v-show over v-if for frequent toggles, `<KeepAlive :max="10">`, lazy routes, Suspense. Vue 3.5+: reactive props destructure (destructured props stay reactive but must be watched via getter), `useTemplateRef()` replaces name-matched refs (supports dynamic ids), `onWatcherCleanup()` called synchronously inside watchers, `useId()` for SSR-stable ids, `<Teleport defer>`, defineAsyncComponent `hydrate` strategies (e.g. hydrateOnVisible). Nuxt: auto-imports, `useAsyncData` with a unique cache key, `useFetch` with key/query dedupe, server routes via defineEventHandler with validated params, runtimeConfig split server-only vs public. Anti-patterns named: destructuring defineProps pre-3.5, v-if+v-for on one element, index keys, prop mutation, unsanitized v-html, Options API in new code. Testing stack: Vitest + Vue Test Utils + @pinia/testing + Playwright.
- **Reference / source:** MCP Market ECC/Antigravity collection. No external sites named.
- **Best for:** Vue/Nuxt project work and review only — background architecture, nothing visual for the trade builds.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0202⟧

## ⟦S0203⟧ nuxt4-patterns — MCP Market (ECC + Antigravity)
- **What it is:** Nuxt 4 patterns for hydration safety, route-level rendering rules, lazy loading/hydration and SSR-safe data fetching — aimed at apps whose server HTML and client render keep disagreeing.
- **How it looks:** No visual design of its own. Its visible outcome is negative space: pages that don't flicker, jump or re-render differently a moment after they load, and below-the-fold interactive blocks that wake up only when scrolled into view.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion prescribed. (Lazy hydration is the nearest behaviour: a component renders as static server HTML, then becomes interactive when it becomes visible or the browser idles.)
- **Mechanism & key values:** Hydration safety: first render must be deterministic — no `Date.now()`, `Math.random()`, browser APIs or storage reads in SSR template state; browser-only logic goes behind `onMounted()`, `import.meta.client`, `ClientOnly` or a `.client.vue` file; use Nuxt's `useRoute()`, never vue-router's, and never drive SSR markup from `route.fullPath` (fragments are client-only); `ssr: false` is an escape hatch, not a default fix. Data: `await useFetch()` for SSR-safe reads (payload forwards server data, no second fetch on hydration); `useAsyncData()` for custom fetchers/keys/composed sources — stable key required, handler side-effect free; `$fetch()` only for user-triggered writes; `lazy: true` / useLazyFetch / useLazyAsyncData for non-blocking data with explicit `status === 'pending'` UI; `server: false` only when data isn't needed for SEO/first paint; trim payloads with `pick`. Route rules per group in nuxt.config (example: `/` prerender, `/products/**` swr 3600, `/blog/**` isr, `/admin/**` ssr false, `/api/**` cache maxAge 60×60=3600). Lazy: Nuxt code-splits by route already; `Lazy` prefix + `v-if` so chunks load only when needed; lazy hydration via `hydrate-on-visible` or defineLazyHydrationComponent with visibility/idle strategies (passing new props to a lazily hydrated component hydrates it immediately); NuxtLink for prefetching.
- **Reference / source:** MCP Market ECC/Antigravity collection. No external sites named.
- **Best for:** Nuxt 4 builds and hydration debugging only — no visual or motion content.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0203⟧

## ⟦S0204⟧ scroll-experience — MCP Market (ECC + Antigravity)
- **What it is:** A scroll-experience architect skill for immersive scroll-driven sites — parallax storytelling, scroll-scrubbed animation, pinned/sticky sections and horizontal-scroll panels — in the manner of NY Times interactives, Apple product pages and award sites. Ships with a detailed guide covering the stack, story structure, performance, mobile and accessibility failure modes.
- **How it looks:** A page that behaves like a film the visitor plays with their thumb: a full-viewport hook visual; as you scroll, background layers drift slower than the content, a section pins to the screen while panels slide sideways through it, text reveals beat by beat (fade, typewriter, word-by-word highlight), and a five-beat story arc runs Hook (full viewport) → Context → Journey (parallax) → Climax (dramatic reveal) → Resolution (CTA).
- **Frame by frame:** Parallax: scroll begins → background layer translates at 0.2× speed, midground 0.5×, foreground/content 1.0×, floating elements 1.2× (worked GSAP values: background y −20%, foreground y −50%, both scrubbed to scroll). Pinned horizontal section: the section pins at the top → continued scrolling drives the panel row sideways by xPercent −100 × (panels − 1) with scrub 1 → the section unpins when the row's full width has passed (end = += container width). CSS-native reveal: an element entering the viewport runs a keyframed reveal (opacity 0, translateY 50px → settled) bound to `animation-timeline: view()` across range entry 0% → cover 40%. Sticky fallback: a 300vh container with a position-sticky 100vh element gives the same pin without JS.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Stack choices: GSAP ScrollTrigger (complex; setup: trigger, start 'top center', end 'bottom center', scrub true), Framer Motion useScroll/useTransform (React; example maps progress 0–1 to y 0→−200), Locomotive Scroll (smooth + parallax), Lenis (smooth only), CSS scroll-timeline (simple/native). Pin pattern: `pin: true`, start 'top top', end '+=1000' for a 1000px pin. Performance: animate transform and opacity only (filter and clip-path allowed but paint cost must be profiled; width/height/top/left/margin/padding/font-size banned); rAF-throttle raw scroll handlers (GSAP handles it internally); init/destroy heavy animations on ScrollTrigger enter/leave; debug with ScrollTrigger markers. Mobile: parallax glitches on iOS momentum scroll — reduce movement (example: y −50 mobile vs −200 desktop), prefer viewport width < 768px detection, `translate3d(0,0,0)` + backface-visibility hidden, `-webkit-overflow-scrolling: touch`, or CSS scroll-timeline where supported; consider disabling on low-end. Accessibility: full `prefers-reduced-motion` reset (animations none, transitions 0.01ms, scroll-behavior auto) and JS gating on matchMedia; never hide content behind animation; content readable with no JS; skip links and keyboard focus must survive pinned/horizontal sections; key message and CTA visible without scrolling (content-first: Level 1 content, Level 2 styling, Level 3 scroll enhancement). Validation checks flag: no reduced-motion support (HIGH), unthrottled scroll events, animating layout properties, missing will-change, scroll hijacking.
- **Reference / source:** MCP Market ECC/Antigravity collection. Reference points named in the skill: NY Times interactives, Apple product pages; delegates 3D to ⟦S0205⟧ 3d-web-experience.
- **Best for:** Process/how-it-works storytelling, pinned before-after or step walkthroughs, town/area journeys and any cinematic homepage section — the core scroll grammar for immersive trade builds, with its mobile and reduced-motion caveats carried along.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0204⟧

## ⟦S0205⟧ 3d-web-experience — MCP Market (ECC + Antigravity)
- **What it is:** A 3D web architect skill covering Three.js, React Three Fiber, Spline and WebGL: stack selection, the model pipeline (formats, compression, loading), scroll-driven 3D, performance budgets and fallback strategy.
- **How it looks:** A real 3D object living in the page: a product model you can orbit with zoom disabled so the page still scrolls, a loading percentage counting up in the middle of the canvas while the model arrives, and — on scroll — the model rotating a full turn or the camera gliding through the scene as the visitor moves down the page.
- **Frame by frame:** Scroll-driven 3D (R3F ScrollControls, pages=3): as the visitor scrolls three pages of depth, the model's rotation.y tracks scroll offset × 2π — one full revolution across the scroll. GSAP variant: scroll progress scrubs the camera to z 5, y 2 through the pinned section. Loading: Suspense fallback shows useProgress as a live percentage (0% → 100%) centred over the canvas, then the model swaps in. Orbit: drag rotates the model under OrbitControls (enableZoom false in the baseline example so scroll isn't captured).
- **Mechanism & key values:** Stack decision: Spline for a quick/designer-led element, React Three Fiber for React apps needing control, vanilla Three.js for maximum control/performance, Babylon.js for games/heavy 3D. Model pipeline: model → set a triangle/draw-call budget on real target devices → bake textures/combine materials → export GLB → compress with gltf-transform (Draco + WebP textures) → measure transfer size, decode time, memory and frame time against budget. Illustrative starting budgets (explicitly not guarantees): desktop 60fps / 500K triangles, mobile 30–60fps / 100K, low-end 30fps / 50K. Formats: GLB/GLTF standard, USDZ for Apple AR, FBX large, OBJ medium. Performance levers: Instances/Instance for repeated objects, LOD, lazy-loaded models, few lights (worked lights block: ambient 0.5 + one directional), conservative DPR — `dpr={[1, 1.5]}` (validation flags high mobile DPR; fix is limit DPR to 1 on mobile). Fallbacks are mandatory: Canvas `fallback` for GL-init failure, an error boundary for context/asset crashes, product info and purchase controls kept in accessible DOM outside the canvas. Validation checks: no loading indicator (HIGH), no WebGL fallback, uncompressed models, OrbitControls capturing scroll, high mobile DPR. Skill states its own limits plainly: the Spline scene URL in examples is a placeholder, not a working scene.
- **Reference / source:** MCP Market ECC/Antigravity collection; R3F Canvas/fallback docs (r3f.docs.pmnd.rs/api/canvas), glTF Transform CLI (gltf-transform.dev/cli).
- **Best for:** A single 3D hero moment or product/work visualiser where depth genuinely earns its weight — with the budget and fallback discipline applied; heavy for most trade pages, use sparingly.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0205⟧

## ⟦S0206⟧ premium-3d-website — MCP Market (ECC + Antigravity)
- **What it is:** Guidelines for premium/award-tier 3D websites: custom GLSL shaders, post-processing (bloom, depth of field, vignette), physics-based interaction, preloaders and device optimization on Three.js / R3F / Spline.
- **How it looks:** A WebGL scene with a filmic finish: a glowing orange object whose brightness blooms into the surrounding darkness, the background falling out of focus (depth of field with a soft bokeh blur), corners darkened by a vignette; elsewhere, a surface that ripples like liquid — its skin pulsing brighter and darker in waves as time passes.
- **Frame by frame:** The wavy shader material displaces the mesh continuously: each vertex's z rises and falls with sin(x × 5 + time) × 0.1 plus cos(y × 5 + time) × 0.1, while the fragment colour pulses at 0.5 + 0.5 × sin(time + uv.x × 10) — a slow breathing shimmer across the surface, driven by a render loop updating the uTime uniform. (The material alone does nothing: it needs a subdivided mesh and a loop feeding it time.)
- **Mechanism & key values:** Render setup: pixel ratio capped at a maximum of 2 (`dpr={[1, 2]}`; pitfall fix: `renderer.setPixelRatio(Math.min(devicePixelRatio, 2))`), `powerPreference: "high-performance"`, antialiasing chosen deliberately (worked example: antialias false at the renderer with an EffectComposer). Post-processing via @react-three/postprocessing EffectComposer with `disableNormalPass`: DepthOfField (focusDistance 0, focalLength 0.02, bokehScale 2, height 480), Bloom (luminanceThreshold 0.3, luminanceSmoothing 0.9, height 300), Vignette (offset 0.1, darkness 1.1); keep pass counts low and combine fragment shaders to minimize draw calls. Worked material: emissive orange at emissiveIntensity 2.0 feeding the bloom. Physics: Cannon.js or Rapier (or procedural springs) for hover/drag/click reactions. Assets: Draco/Meshopt compression mandatory, THREE.LoadingManager + an interactive preloader (the named fix for long loads and white screens). Bake AO/lighting/shadows into textures instead of dynamic lights; InstancedMesh for repeated meshes; no real-time shadow maps (e.g. DirectionalLightShadow) on mobile/low-end. Safety notes in the skill: only trusted HTTPS CDNs for externally loaded models, no unpinned packages; DPR 2 and compression are starting choices, not guarantees — profile low-end devices, pause offscreen rendering, dispose GPU resources.
- **Reference / source:** MCP Market ECC/Antigravity collection; builds on ⟦S0205⟧ 3d-web-experience and ⟦S0204⟧ scroll-experience.
- **Best for:** A flagship hero moment on a portfolio-grade build where one polished WebGL scene carries the page — bloom/DOF/vignette finish and shader surfaces; overkill and risky for ordinary trade sections.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0206⟧

## ⟦S0207⟧ spline-3d-integration — MCP Market (ECC + Antigravity)
- **What it is:** The integration handbook for embedding interactive Spline.design scenes into web projects — per-stack embed paths (vanilla, React, Next.js, Vue, iframe), the runtime control API, a performance/mobile guide, and a common-problems guide of production gotchas.
- **How it looks:** A designer-built 3D scene (objects, materials, physics, hover/click events authored in the Spline editor) running inside the page — as a full-page background behind the content, or an inline interactive object that reacts to the cursor — with a static background or image standing in while it loads or on devices that can't run it.
- **Frame by frame:** No motion values of its own — the scenes' animation is authored inside Spline. The integration behaviour it prescribes: page renders with a fallback background instantly → scene loads (preloaded via `<link rel="preload">`, or lazy via Intersection Observer when scrolled near) → fallback fades/hides and the live scene takes over; if the scene hasn't loaded in 8000ms, a timeout swaps the fallback back in permanently.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Stack map: vanilla → `<spline-viewer>` web component or `@splinetool/runtime`; React/Vite → `@splinetool/react-spline`; Next.js → `@splinetool/react-spline/next` (or dynamic import with `ssr: false` on hydration errors); Vue → `@splinetool/vue-spline`; no-code → public-URL iframe. Scene URL form: `https://prod.spline.design/<id>/scene.splinecode` — a snapshot that does NOT auto-update; editor changes need Generate Draft / Promote to Production. Play Settings before copying the URL: Hide Background on (custom/dark sites), Hide Spline Logo on (paid plan), Geometry Quality = Performance, disable Page Scroll / Zoom / Pan unless needed. Runtime API: `findObjectByName`/`findObjectById`, `emitEvent`/`emitEventReverse`, addEventListener for mouseDown/mouseUp/mouseHover/mousePress/keyDown/keyUp/start/scroll — and ALL rotation values are radians (90° = Math.PI/2). Size gates: under ~3MB fine, 3–10MB optimize, over 10MB serious problem, over 20MB do not embed live — export video; lights under 3, Matcap materials to fake reflections, max 1–2 embeds per page (never more than 3). Mobile: skip below 768px width or `hardwareConcurrency <= 2`, or serve an MP4 recording instead; preload + Intersection Observer loading; reserve space with explicit height + `contain: strict` to stop CLS jumps. Critical gotchas: Spline injects `overflow: hidden` on body (fix: `body { overflow: auto !important }` or disable Page Scroll); white box = background not hidden; canvas swallows clicks (fix: pointer-events none on a decorative wrapper, or z-index + pointer-events all on the overlay); intermittent CDN failures → 8000ms timeout fallback or self-host the .splinecode (with CORS/rights review); CORS errors → self-host.
- **Reference / source:** MCP Market ECC/Antigravity collection; Spline.design and its packages (@splinetool/viewer, runtime, react-spline, vue-spline). Skill's own strict rules: use only when requested and useful; never hide required Spline branding with CSS; pin reviewed CDN dependencies; allowlist scene origins.
- **Best for:** One designer-authored interactive 3D accent (hero object, product visual) where a scene already exists in Spline — with the mobile-skip and fallback rules treated as part of the design, not afterthoughts.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0207⟧

## ⟦S0208⟧ animejs-animation — MCP Market (ECC + Antigravity)
- **What it is:** A working guide to the Anime.js animation engine for complex, high-performance web animation — timelines, staggering and precise control over DOM, CSS properties and SVG paths, aimed at awards-calibre interactive sites.
- **How it looks:** Orchestrated multi-stage entrances rather than single tweens: a hero's lines of text rising and fading in one after another with a springy settle, followed by the hero image scaling up from slightly small as it fades in — the second movement starting before the first has finished, so the whole entrance reads as one continuous gesture.
- **Frame by frame:** The worked timeline (Anime.js v3 API): the timeline opens with easing `spring(1, 80, 10, 0)` and duration 1000ms → hero text elements animate translateY 50→0 and opacity 0→1, each delayed by `anime.stagger(100)` so they cascade 100ms apart → at offset "-=800" (800ms before the text finishes) the hero image joins, scaling 0.9→1 while fading 0→1 → all elements settle together at the timeline's end.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Workflow: identify targets → define properties and easing (advanced easings — custom cubicBezier, spring, elastic — explicitly instead of linear/ease-in-out) → orchestrate with `anime.timeline()`, mastering relative offsets ('-=200') vs absolute positioning for overlapping motion → implement. `anime.stagger()` is to be used extensively for organic rhythm across grids, text and data visualisations. Performance: monitor main-thread usage; `will-change: transform, opacity` where appropriate (the skill itself cautions it is a temporary hint, not a guarantee, and not to leave it on every element). Version discipline is a named limitation: the examples are v3 (`anime.timeline()`); v4 uses imported `createTimeline()` with a different signature — never mix. Reduced motion: provide a static final state, no scroll hijacking, dispose animations on component unmount.
- **Reference / source:** MCP Market ECC/Antigravity collection; Anime.js (animejs.com, timeline docs at animejs.com/documentation/timeline/).
- **Best for:** Hero entrances, staggered grid/text reveals and SVG path drawing/morphing sequences on single-file builds where GSAP isn't the chosen engine.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0208⟧
