## ⟦S0210⟧ pro-motion — MCP Market (ECC + Antigravity)
- **What it is:** A complete method for making motion-graphics launch/brand/promo films audio-first: plan the campaign and its music before any picture, analyse the locked track's beat grid, then render the film in code (deterministic canvas frames to MP4) cut exactly to the music. Distilled from a real project that took ~10 rounds of rejections ("PPT", "ugly material", "text floating on top") before the method fixed it.
- **How it looks:** A short vertical film (default master 9:16) where one protagonist — a brand dot, shape or mascot — performs through every scene and finally becomes part of the logo: features act themselves out on musical hits (a punch lands as an impact, dots breathe on hi-hats, an outline draws itself, a sticker peels), brand colours slam in as full-screen blocks at the biggest hits, text is written on by the protagonist or rides a path instead of sitting in caption boxes, and scene changes are morphs, match cuts, shard/scan/push wipes or metaball convergences — never plain content swaps inside a fixed frame.
- **Frame by frame:** Not a fixed sequence — each film is built from a shot map (time · music event · picture · transition in · words) written after music analysis. Timing grammar: every major move lands on an analysed onset; secondary moves on 8ths/16ths computed as `grid0 + k × 60/BPM/4`. Frame-rate language is a style choice: 60fps smooth for product films, 24fps with objects stepped on twos (`Math.floor(t*12)/12`) for hand-made animation, 12fps line boil for doodle layers — the checklist runs two rates at once (hand-drawn lines boil at 12fps while camera/objects stay 60fps). Rendering: `render(t)` must be pure and deterministic (seeded rand/hash, no Math.random, no state between frames) because frames render in parallel tabs — ~30s per 20s of film at 60fps with 6 parallel tabs, versus ~5 min single-tab. Verification: a contact sheet at chosen seconds plus an audio-length check on the final MP4 (an ffmpeg `-shortest` mux once silently truncated audio at ~13s — mux with `-map 0:v -map 1:a -t <dur>` instead).
- **Mechanism & key values:** Audio-first rails: hits by 3–5s, no soft intro; final peak IS the logo moment with tail 2–3s; bars on round seconds (120 BPM → 2s bars) so 6s/15s/full cut-downs splice; one curveball/beat switch; silence of ½–1 beat before the two biggest hits; sonic logo 2–5 notes, ≤3s, must work alone. Campaign step: pick a mechanism type A–G (physical binding, spatial impossibility, shared moment, co-creation, product-fact gamification, hijacked channel, imitable meme) and design the sound that IS the mechanism — the case bank cites Coca-Cola Friendly Twist, Hyundai's coquí lock-beep (Cannes 2026 Audio GP), Mercado Livre's 104m stadium Field Barcode, Spotify Wrapped, Budweiser One Second Ads. Music analysis pipeline: ffmpeg to mono 22050Hz wav → analyze_music.py → tempo/grid/onsets/RMS + spectrogram; loudness loudnorm I=-14 LUFS social, −23/−24 broadcast. Direction step: 3 clearly different style frames rendered and shown before any film is built — if a direction can be named by one familiar label ("pop art", "flat", "Y2K") it is not new enough. Languages via `?lang=` (EN master + local cuts swapping only key lines); bundled OFL handwriting fonts per language (Patrick Hand EN/VI, Yomogi JA, Gaegu KO, ZCOOL KuaiLe ZH). Toolchain: Node 18+, Python 3 (numpy/scipy/matplotlib), Chrome; subject cutouts need macOS 14+. IMPORTANT availability note from the skill itself: this catalog entry bundles only documentation, the audio-plan template, references and LICENSE — the runtime template (film.html/film.js/motion-lib.js, fonts) and scripts live at the pinned upstream commit (github.com/jack-reson8/pro-motion @ 50db395), and fetching/executing them requires user consent and inspection first.
- **Reference / source:** MCP Market ECC/Antigravity collection; upstream jack-reson8/pro-motion (pinned commit 50db3957004a086c24575897c0b97a2a975624a1). References named: System1/Effie sonic-fluency finding (sonic devices 2.3× the brand fluency of a visual logo across 1,250+ campaigns), Spotify Wrapped and Figma Config opener technique sheets (60fps.design), React Bits effect library, Persona 5 / Promare / Mind Game / Spider-Verse as stylized-film reference pools.
- **Best for:** Launch films, brand films and social promos — video work, not homepage sections; its reference-research discipline (technique sheets + contact-sheet frame pulls) is the transferable part for design work.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0210⟧
## ⟦S0211⟧ ui-motion — PART 12 — MCP Market — website / animation / scroll / 3D / UI / UX skills (ECC + Antigravity)
- **What it is:** A motion applier for StyleSeed React projects: it gives every component one consistent motion "personality" by spreading a pre-calibrated recipe (a seed × a context) onto a framer-motion element, instead of hand-writing transition values in each component.
- **How it looks:** The page itself doesn't change shape — what changes is how things move. Buttons give slightly when pressed, dialogs glide in smoothly instead of popping, dropdowns snap open instantly, list items cascade in one after another, a live dot throbs like a heartbeat, a toggle flips over in 3D like a card. One personality runs through the whole product: bouncy and playful (Spring), smooth and elegant (Silk), instant and precise (Snap), gentle and drifting (Float), or rhythmic and punchy (Pulse).
- **Frame by frame:** Trigger depends on context. *Entrance:* element mounts → seed's entrance recipe plays (e.g. Silk fades/slides content in smoothly; Spring arrives with slight overshoot) → settles still. *Hover:* pointer enters → subtle seed-styled lift/scale → pointer leaves → returns. *Press:* pointer down → button scales/gives under the finger → release → springs back. *Exit:* element removed inside AnimatePresence → seed exit plays in reverse character → unmounts. Named moves: `toggle-flip` rotates a card on the Y axis to show its other face; `toggle-curtain` wipes a panel open top-to-bottom with a clip-path; `reveal-blur` starts at blur(12px) and focus-pulls to sharp; `reveal-rise` climbs masked text up into view; `pop-in` springs a badge/checkmark in from 0 with overshoot; `press-squish` squashes with a skew on tap; `tap-ripple` radiates a ripple from the tap point; `wiggle` shakes horizontally for errors; `shimmer` sweeps light across a skeleton; `stagger-cascade` fades children up in sequence.
- **Mechanism & key values:** framer-motion only (`motion.X` JSX + `AnimatePresence`); recipes are spread (`{...spring.press}`), never inlined — the exact stiffness/damping values live in the project's `engine/motion` library, which this catalog copy does not bundle. Exactly 5 seeds: Spring, Silk, Snap, Float, Pulse. Brand defaults: "Toss"/"Arc" style → Spring; Stripe/Notion style → Silk; Linear/Raycast/Vercel style → Snap; vague "natural/real app" → Silk. Contexts: entrance, exit, hover, press, layout (FLIP). Use-case map: CTA press = spring·press; modal/sheet enter = silk·entrance (never bounce serious content); dropdown/popover = snap·entrance; toast = spring·entrance; feed items = stagger-cascade; marketing card hover = tilt-3d; dashboard card hover = snap·hover; like button = like-burst; live dot = pulse-beat; loading = shimmer; success = pop-in; toggle/tab = toggle-flip; route change = silk·entrance; numbers/prices/balances = NO animation. Anti-rules: one seed per product; never delay the payload (prices, balances, search results appear instantly). Reduced motion: `usePrefersReducedMotion` + `REDUCED_TRANSITION` override for long-running surfaces.
- **Reference / source:** PART 12 — MCP Market (ECC + Antigravity). Internal to the StyleSeed project (`engine/motion/index.ts`, `engine/motion/library.ts`, DESIGN-LANGUAGE.md Rule 59 bans scroll-linked/parallax animation in that system). No external site named beyond framer-motion's docs.
- **Best for:** Micro-interaction layer of any section — CTA buttons (call section), toggles and the 1·2·3 version switcher (toggle-flip/toggle-slide), toasts, feed/gallery entrances, live-status dots. Not for scroll-linked timelines or parallax heroes (explicitly out of scope). Trade fit: Silk or Snap keep a roofer's site calm and trustworthy; Pulse/Float suit marketing moments only.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0211⟧

## ⟦S0213⟧ design-taste-frontend — PART 12 — MCP Market — website / animation / scroll / 3D / UI / UX skills (ECC + Antigravity)
- **What it is:** A senior-designer rulebook for React/Next.js/Tailwind builds, driven by three dials — DESIGN_VARIANCE 8 (asymmetric), MOTION_INTENSITY 6 (fluid), VISUAL_DENSITY 4 (airy) — plus a large arsenal of named premium patterns and a strict list of banned AI tells.
- **How it looks:** Asymmetric, left-leaning layouts inside a max-w-[1400px] container: split-screen or offset heroes instead of centered ones, bento grids with mixed tile sizes, zig-zag feature rows, a neutral Zinc/Slate base with exactly ONE desaturated accent (Emerald, Electric Blue or Deep Rose), no purple/blue "Lila" glow anywhere, big tight-tracked headlines in Geist/Outfit/Cabinet Grotesk/Satoshi (Inter banned), body text capped at 65ch, cards used only where elevation means something, titles sitting below bento tiles like gallery labels. Surfaces: background #f9fafb, pure-white tiles with a 1px border-slate-200/50, rounded-[2.5rem] corners and a wide soft diffusion shadow (0 20px 40px -15px rgba(0,0,0,0.05)), p-8/p-10 inside.
- **Frame by frame:** Load → lists/grids never appear at once: children waterfall in with staggerChildren or CSS `animation-delay: calc(var(--index) * 100ms)`. Interactive elements move on spring physics (`type: "spring", stiffness: 100, damping: 20`), no linear easing; shared elements glide between states via Framer Motion `layout`/`layoutId`. Buttons at MOTION_INTENSITY > 5 pull magnetically toward the cursor (via useMotionValue/useTransform, never React state). Press → tactile `-translate-y-[1px]` or `scale-[0.98]`. Scroll (advanced tier) → GSAP ScrollTrigger/Three.js only in isolated full-page scrolltelling components, never mixed with Framer Motion in the same tree. Named moves in its arsenal include: curtain reveal (hero parts in the middle on scroll), sticky scroll stack (cards stick and stack over each other), horizontal scroll hijack (vertical scroll pans a gallery sideways), zoom parallax, text-mask reveal (giant type as a window onto video), kinetic marquee (bands reverse/speed up on scroll), coverflow and dome galleries, hover image trails, text scramble, circular text paths.
- **Mechanism & key values:** React/Next.js RSC + Tailwind (v3/v4 lock checked in package.json); headlines `text-4xl md:text-6xl tracking-tighter leading-none`; body `text-base text-gray-600 leading-relaxed max-w-[65ch]`; accent saturation < 80%; heroes must use `min-h-[100svh]`/`100dvh`, never h-screen; CSS Grid always, never flex percentage math; asymmetric layouts collapse to single column (w-full, px-4, py-8) below 768px; density 8–10 = no cards, 1px dividers, font-mono for all numbers; forms: label above input, error below, gap-2; grain/noise only on fixed pointer-events-none pseudo-elements; animate transform/opacity only. Banned: Inter, pure black #000000, gradient text on big headers, custom cursors, 3-equal-card rows, emojis, "Elevate/Seamless/Unleash/Next-Gen" copy, generic names (Acme/Nexus/SmartFlow), Unsplash links (use picsum.photos/seed/…).
- **Reference / source:** PART 12 — MCP Market (ECC + Antigravity). Names real products as style anchors (Vercel, Dribbble, Apple Control Center for bento, Pinterest masonry, Mac OS Dock magnification) and libraries GSAP/Three.js/Framer Motion; no single reference site URL.
- **Best for:** Whole-page art direction for a homepage — hero (asymmetric split standard), bento work/gallery sections, feature zig-zags, navigation (dock/magnetic/gooey/dynamic-island ideas). Its dials are a fast way to brief "how different, how much motion, how dense" per section version. Trade fit: strong — variance 8 gives three genuinely different version directions; keep density low and motion mid for homeowner trust.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0213⟧

## ⟦S0214⟧ high-end-visual-design — PART 12 — MCP Market — website / animation / scroll / 3D / UI / UX skills (ECC + Antigravity)
- **What it is:** An agency-tier visual system ("Vanguard_UI_Architect") built on a variance engine — pick one vibe archetype + one layout archetype per build — and on nested "double-bezel" component construction, floating-pill navigation and fluid spring-feeling motion with custom cubic-beziers.
- **How it looks:** Deep, soft, expensive. Three vibes: *Ethereal Glass* — OLED black #050505, faint glowing mesh-gradient orbs behind vantablack cards with heavy backdrop-blur-2xl and white/10 hairlines; *Editorial Luxury* — warm cream #FDFBF7, sage/espresso tones, huge variable-serif headings, a whisper of film grain (opacity 0.03) like paper; *Soft Structuralism* — white/silver-grey, massive grotesk type, components floating on very diffused ambient shadows. Layouts: an asymmetrical bento of mixed-size tiles, a Z-axis cascade of slightly overlapping cards rotated -2deg/3deg, or an editorial split (massive type left half, scrollable image pills right). Every major card looks like machined hardware: a tinted outer shell (p-1.5–p-2, rounded-[2rem], hairline ring) holding an inner core with its own background, an inset top highlight and a smaller concentric radius. Buttons are full pills (px-6 py-3); an arrow never sits naked — it lives inside its own 32px circular chip flush to the button's right edge. Tiny pill eyebrow badges (10px, uppercase, tracking 0.2em) precede headings. Sections breathe: py-24 to py-40.
- **Frame by frame:** Page load/scroll → each element enters with a heavy fade-up: starts translate-y-16 + blur-md + opacity-0, resolves to translate-y-0 blur-0 opacity-100 over 800ms+, staggered. Nav → a floating glass pill sits detached (mt-6, w-max, rounded-full); hamburger click → its 2–3 lines rotate/translate into a perfect X (rotate-45 / -rotate-45) → a full-screen glass overlay (backdrop-blur-3xl, bg-black/80 or bg-white/80) expands → links fade-and-rise one by one from translate-y-12 opacity-0 with delay-100/150/200 staggers. Button hover → whole button presses to active:scale-[0.98]; the inner icon chip slides diagonally (translate-x-1, -translate-y-[1px]) and scales to 105, creating internal tension. All transitions use custom curves (e.g. duration-700 ease-[cubic-bezier(0.32,0.72,0,1)]); linear and ease-in-out are banned.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Tailwind classes throughout; double-bezel math: outer rounded-[2rem], padding p-1.5/p-2, inner radius calc(2rem - 0.375rem), inner highlight shadow-[inset_0_1px_1px_rgba(255,255,255,0.15)]; scroll reveals via IntersectionObserver or Framer Motion whileInView (never window scroll listeners); animate transform/opacity only; backdrop-blur only on fixed/sticky elements; grain only on fixed pointer-events-none overlays. Banned: fonts Inter/Roboto/Arial/Open Sans/Helvetica (use Geist, Clash Display, PP Editorial New, Plus Jakarta Sans — subject to licensing), thick Lucide/FontAwesome/Material icons (Phosphor Light, Remix Line instead), 1px solid gray borders, harsh shadows (shadow-md, rgba(0,0,0,0.3)), edge-to-edge sticky navbars, symmetrical 3-column grids. Mobile: every asymmetric layout collapses below 768px to w-full px-4 py-8, rotations/overlaps removed; min-h-[100dvh], never h-screen.
- **Reference / source:** PART 12 — MCP Market (ECC + Antigravity). Style anchors named in text: Apple-esque / Linear-tier design language; no reference site URL recorded.
- **Best for:** Premium heroes and full homepage art direction; the double-bezel is a distinctive treatment for work/gallery cards, review cards and quote-form panels; the fluid island nav suits any section version wanting a "product" feel. Trade fit: Editorial Luxury maps naturally onto a roofer's cream/espresso palette; keep blur off scrolling content for phone performance.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0214⟧

## ⟦S0215⟧ industrial-brutalist-ui — PART 12 — MCP Market — website / animation / scroll / 3D / UI / UX skills (ECC + Antigravity)
- **What it is:** A severe industrial design system fusing 1960s Swiss print identity with military CRT-terminal telemetry: rigid blueprint grids, monolithic uppercase typography, one hazard-red accent, and simulated analog degradation (halftone, dithering, scanlines). Pick ONE archetype per project and never mix them.
- **How it looks:** *Swiss Industrial Print (light):* matte newsprint background #F4F4F0 or #EAE8E3, carbon-ink text #050505–#111111, and a single aviation red #E61919/#FF2A2A used for thick dividing lines, strike-throughs and vital data. Enormous uppercase headlines — clamp(4rem, 10vw, 15rem), tracking crushed to -0.03em…-0.06em, line-height 0.85–0.95 — bleed off the viewport edge like machinery-manual covers, while tiny monospace metadata (10–14px, uppercase, tracking 0.05em–0.1em) clusters in dense tabular blocks. Zones are boxed by visible 1px–2px solid borders and full-width rules; corners are exactly 90 degrees everywhere (border-radius is banned). ASCII framing decorates data: `[ DELIVERY SYSTEMS ]`, `>>>`, `///`, crosshair `+` marks at grid intersections, barcode-like line runs, ®/©/™ symbols used as geometric ornaments. *Tactical Telemetry (dark):* near-black #0A0A0A/#121212 (never pure black), white-phosphor #EAEAEA text, the same red accent, and terminal green #4AF626 allowed on ONE element only (a single status readout). Images and big serif words (Playfair Display/EB Garamond) appear rarely, degraded by halftone dots or 1-bit dithering so they look printed, not digital.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion system. The skill prescribes no animation, transitions or scroll behaviour; its "effects" are fixed textures: a repeating-linear-gradient CRT scanline layer, a low-opacity SVG noise grain over the whole page, and halftone overlays (mix-blend-mode: multiply + SVG radial dot pattern). Any movement would have to come from another skill, and reduced-motion/readability testing of the CRT layers is explicitly required.
- **Mechanism & key values:** CSS Grid with `display: grid; gap: 1px` over contrasting parent/child backgrounds to draw razor hairlines without borders; fluid macro type via clamp() only; semantic tags `<data>`, `<samp>`, `<kbd>`, `<output>`, `<dl>`. Fonts: macro — Neue Haas Grotesk Black, Inter Extra Bold/Black, Archivo Black, Roboto Flex Heavy, Monument Extended; micro — JetBrains Mono, IBM Plex Mono, Space Mono, VT323, Courier Prime. Scanline recipe: repeating-linear-gradient(0deg, transparent, transparent 2px, rgba(0,0,0,0.1) 2px, rgba(0,0,0,0.1) 4px). Gradients for colour, soft shadows and translucency are prohibited (the scanline/noise textures are the only overlays). Honesty rule in the text: simulated telemetry must be marked as demo data — never invent live readings.
- **Reference / source:** PART 12 — MCP Market (ECC + Antigravity). Design ancestry named in text: mid-century Swiss typographic/corporate identity systems, heavy-machinery blueprints, aerospace/military HUD terminals. No site URL recorded.
- **Best for:** A deliberately raw version direction — hero or towns/areas sections styled as spec sheets, process sections as technical manuals, data-dense proof blocks. NOT-FOR-TRADES as a whole-page default for most home-service brands (severity can read cold to homeowners), but strong as one contrasting version or for a workshop/fleet/industrial audience. Accessibility caution: tiny uppercase labels and CRT layers must be tested for contrast and readability.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0215⟧

## ⟦S0216⟧ minimalist-ui — PART 12 — MCP Market — website / animation / scroll / 3D / UI / UX skills (ECC + Antigravity)
- **What it is:** "Premium Utilitarian Minimalism" — a Notion/Linear-like editorial system: warm monochrome surfaces, hairline borders instead of shadows, serif display type against a clean sans, flat bento grids, and motion so quiet it should feel invisible.
- **How it looks:** A document-like page on pure white #FFFFFF or warm bone #F7F6F3/#FBFBFA. Everything is divided by 1px solid #EAEAEA hairlines; cards are flat white #FFFFFF/#F9F9F8 with crisp 8–12px corners and generous 24–40px padding — no drop shadows at all. Body text is off-black #111111/#2F3437 at line-height 1.6; secondary text muted gray #787774. Serif hero headings (Lyon Text, Newsreader, Playfair Display, Instrument Serif) with tight tracking (-0.02em…-0.04em) and 1.1 line-height sit over a geometric sans body (SF Pro Display, Geist Sans, Helvetica Neue, Switzer) and mono details (Geist Mono, SF Mono, JetBrains Mono). Colour appears only as washed-out pastel tags — pale red #FDEBEC with #9F2F2D text, pale blue #E1F3FE/#1F6C9F, pale green #EDF3EC/#346538, pale yellow #FBF3DB/#956400 — in small pill badges (text-xs, uppercase, 0.05em tracking). Primary buttons are solid #111111 with white text and a slight 4–6px radius. FAQ rows have no boxes at all — just a bottom hairline and a sharp +/− toggle. Illustrations are monochrome continuous-line ink sketches with one pastel shape; photos are desaturated, warm, with a 0.04-opacity grain.
- **Frame by frame:** Scroll → each block fades in gently: translateY(12px) + opacity 0 resolving over 600ms with cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), fired by IntersectionObserver; grids cascade with `animation-delay: calc(var(--index) * 80ms)`. Hover on a card → an almost-imperceptible shadow fades in (0 2px 8px rgba(0,0,0,0.04)) over 200ms. Press → scale(0.98). Optional hero ambience → one radial warm light blob drifting on a fixed layer over 20s+ at opacity 0.02–0.04. A no-motion path for prefers-reduced-motion is mandatory, and content must remain visible if observers fail.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Sections spaced py-24/py-32; text measure max-w-4xl/max-w-5xl; animate transform/opacity only; will-change sparingly. Icons: Phosphor (Bold/Fill) or Radix UI icons at one standardized stroke — Lucide/Feather/Heroicons banned. Banned: Inter/Roboto/Open Sans, Tailwind shadow-md/lg/xl, primary-coloured section backgrounds, gradients/neon/glassmorphism, rounded-full on large containers/buttons, emojis, cliché copy ("Elevate", "Seamless", "Unleash", "Next-Gen", "Delve"). Keyboard-shortcut chips are drawn as physical keys (`<kbd>`, 1px #EAEAEA border, 4px radius, #F7F6F3 fill); software mock-ups get faux-macOS chrome (white bar, three light-gray circles).
- **Reference / source:** PART 12 — MCP Market (ECC + Antigravity). Named style anchors: Notion, Linear and editorial workspace products; placeholder photos via picsum.photos/seed/{context}/1200/800.

## ⟦S0217⟧ redesign-existing-projects — PART 12 — MCP Market — website / animation / scroll / 3D / UI / UX skills (ECC + Antigravity)
- **What it is:** An audit-and-upgrade playbook for existing websites: scan the codebase, diagnose against a long checklist of generic-AI patterns, then apply targeted premium fixes with the existing stack — explicitly no rewrites, no framework migrations.
- **How it looks:** It produces no look of its own; it transforms a flat, generic page into the upgraded version of itself: a characterful font pairing instead of Inter-everywhere, heavier tightened headlines, one desaturated accent on a consistent warm-or-cool gray family, tinted shadows, sections with real depth (background imagery, ambient gradients, grain) instead of text on bare flat colour, asymmetric layouts instead of three equal card columns, and finished states everywhere — skeleton loaders matching the layout, composed empty states, inline form errors, visible focus rings, an active-nav style.
- **Frame by frame:** The upgrades it mandates, as interactions: hover on any interactive element → background shift, slight scale or translate (never an instant jump — all interactive transitions run 200–300ms); press → scale(0.98) or translateY(1px) physical feedback; page load/lists → staggered entry (Y-translation + opacity cascade, never everything at once); scroll → optional reveals through expanding masks, wipes or draw-on SVG paths, parallax card stacks that stick and pile over each other, split-screen halves sliding in opposite directions, headline text that animates variable-font weight, and outlined type that fills with colour as it enters; anchor clicks glide (scroll-behavior: smooth). All of it gated on reduced-motion, keyboard/touch and anchor behaviour staying intact.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Fix priority order: 1) font swap, 2) colour palette cleanup (one accent, saturation < 80%, no purple/blue AI gradients, pure #000000 → #0a0a0a/#121212), 3) hover/active states, 4) layout & spacing (CSS Grid not flex-math, container 1200–1440px, min-height: 100dvh not 100vh, double the whitespace, card CTAs pinned to a shared bottom line), 5) replace generic components (3-card testimonial carousel → masonry wall/single rotating quote; accordion FAQ → side-by-side list or progressive disclosure; pill badges → square/flags/text; avatar circles → squircles), 6) loading/empty/error states, 7) typography polish (65ch body measure, tabular-nums for data, text-wrap: balance for orphans, sentence case). Surface upgrades: true glass = backdrop blur + 1px inner border + inner shadow; spotlight borders that light under the cursor; fixed pointer-events-none grain overlays; hue-tinted shadows. Icons: Phosphor/Heroicons/custom over Lucide/Feather defaults, one stroke width. Placeholders: picsum.photos/seed/{name}/1920/1080.
- **Reference / source:** PART 12 — MCP Market (ECC + Antigravity). No external site named; techniques reference common patterns (variable fonts, text-mask video reveals) without URLs.
- **Best for:** The improvement pass on an already-built homepage or client preview — exactly the "second QA pass" situation: run its audit lists section by section (hero, proof, work, forms, footer) and apply fixes in its priority order. Trade fit: built for this — it preserves real business facts and working behaviour while removing the generic look; its content rules also ban invented testimonials/metrics.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0217⟧

## ⟦S0218⟧ stitch-design-taste — PART 12 — MCP Market — website / animation / scroll / 3D / UI / UX skills (ECC + Antigravity)
- **What it is:** A generator of `DESIGN.md` design-system documents for Google Stitch: it translates the anti-slop taste rulebook (same dial family as ⟦S0213⟧) into Stitch's semantic, natural-language format — descriptive colour names + exact hex, typography specs, component behaviours, layout and motion intent — so Stitch generates premium, non-generic screens from it.

Canvas White #F9FAFB ground, Pure Surface #FFFFFF cards with a Whisper Border (rgba(226,232,240,0.5)) and a Diffused Shadow (0 20px 40px -15px rgba(0,0,0,0.05)), Charcoal Ink #18181B text, Steel Secondary #71717A body, Muted Slate #94A3B8 metadata — and exactly ONE accent picked per project (Emerald Signal #10B981, Electric Blue #3B82F6, Deep Rose #E11D48, or Amber Warmth #F59E0B). Display type (Geist/Satoshi/Cabinet Grotesk/Outfit) at clamp(2.25rem, 5vw, 3.75rem), tracking -0.025em, weight-driven hierarchy; body leading 1.65 at 65ch; cards rounded a generous 2.5rem with 2rem–2.5rem padding. Forms: label above, error below (Deep Rose), 0.5rem stack gap, 2px-offset accent focus ring. Bans mirror ⟦S0213⟧: Inter, generic serifs (Fraunces/Gambarino/Editorial New/Instrument Serif allowed for editorial), pure black, neon glows, >80% saturation, gradient header text, overlapping elements, 3-equal-card rows, centred heroes at high variance, emojis, cliché copy, generic names.

## ⟦S0220⟧ anti-slop-design — PART 12 — MCP Market — website / animation / scroll / 3D / UI / UX skills (ECC + Antigravity)
- **What it is:** An autonomous "Principal Design Technologist" system for curing vibe-coded UI: a 12-pattern banned matrix with mandatory replacements, four complete token archetypes, an 8-state interaction standard, a 5-phase execution loop, and a 7-axis quality gate (every axis must score ≥4/5 before delivery).
- **How it looks:** Depends on the archetype chosen — all four share hairline borders, zero glow, zero emojis, tabular numbers: **A. Quiet Luxury SaaS** (dark, default for B2B): canvas #09090b, surface #121215, elevated #18181c, borders rgba(255,255,255,0.08) (hover 0.16), cobalt accent #1d4ed8, text #f4f4f5/#a1a1aa/#71717a, radii 6/10/14px. **B. Technical Dense Terminal**: canvas #0c0d0e, surfaces #141618/#1a1d20, borders #24282c, emerald accent #10b981 + amber alert #f59e0b, JetBrains Mono, radii 2/4px. **C. Editorial & Refined** (light): canvas #faf8f5, white surfaces, borders #e8e4df, near-black accent #1a1a1a, Playfair Display display + Newsreader body, radii 0/2px. **D. Warm Tactile** (light consumer): canvas #f4f4f0, borders #e2e1db, warm ochre accent #d97706, radii 8/16/24px. Layouts anchor to proven scaffolds: app shell (240px sidebar or 64px icon rail + header + main at max-w-7xl px-6 py-8), dashboard (one sticky page-level control bar + single-row 4-KPI grid + 70/30 split analysis + paginated table), landing (crisp nav with 1 CTA → 44px-headline hero with 1 primary button + 1 secondary link → social proof strip → 3-tier benefit bento → product preview → pricing matrix → low-friction footer). One primary action per section, max 3 secondary (the "1-to-3" rule); one brand mark, one primary CTA, one global filter bar per viewport.
- **Frame by frame:** Governed by its Emil Kowalski decision matrix. High-frequency actions (100+ times/day: shortcuts, command menus, row selection) → 0ms, never animated. Standard interactions (tooltips, dropdowns, popovers) → 120–180ms. Modals/drawers → 200–250ms. All UI easing is punchy ease-out `cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1)`; ease-in is banned as laggy. Popovers/dropdowns scale out of their trigger point (transform-origin at the trigger corner), not screen centre. Press → tactile scale(0.97) with a 60ms ease-out transform transition; the standard button transitions background-color 140ms ease-out / transform 80ms ease-out, hover brightens 1.08, focus-visible draws a 2px ring at 2px offset. Every interactive primitive must render all 8 states: default, hover, focus-visible, active/press, disabled, loading/spinner, error, success. Under prefers-reduced-motion, transitions and the press-scale switch off.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Spacing on a strict 4/8pt rhythm: 4 (hairline), 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64px; minimum 16px internal card padding. Nested-radius formula: radius_inner = max(0, radius_outer − padding). Type scale: H1 2.25–3rem weight 700; H2 1.5–1.875rem 600; H3 1.125–1.25rem 600; body 0.875–1rem 400; meta 0.75–0.8125rem 500; headings tracking-tight/-0.02em, body leading 1.6, measure 65–75ch (max-w-prose), max 2 font families, tabular-nums on all metrics. Banned matrix replacements include: purple radial "AI dark mode" blobs → monochrome surfaces + 1px hairlines; 3 identical glowing cards → asymmetric bento/split panels/workflow rows; emojis as icons → single-weight SVG (Phosphor/Lucide/Heroicons, unified 1.5px/2px strokes); fabricated vanity stats → real telemetry or delete; tracked-out uppercase eyebrow labels → sentence case or omit; per-card filters → one page-level control bar; giant decorative maps/3D blobs → compact bar comparisons and sparklines. Visual-DNA ingestion extracts 5 foundation tokens (canvas, elevated surface, accent, text hierarchy, hairline border) from any reference screenshot.
- **Reference / source:** PART 12 — MCP Market (ECC + Antigravity). Cites "Google AI Studio Evolution" for its 8 cures and Emil Kowalski's animation principles for the motion matrix; no site URLs recorded.
- **Best for:** De-slopping and QA-gating any built page — run the 12-pattern scan and the 7-axis gate over a homepage before delivery; Archetype C (Editorial) and D (Warm Tactile) token sets are directly usable as trade-site palettes, and its landing scaffold is a clean conversion structure. Trade fit: strong as a discipline layer over a chosen design direction, not as the direction itself.

## ⟦S0221⟧ anti-ui-slop — PART 12 — MCP Market — website / animation / scroll / 3D / UI / UX skills (ECC + Antigravity)
- **What it is:** A short workflow discipline for coding agents: work from the product's own brief, existing components and design system first; write a small design contract for big changes; cover every required state; and finish by rendering and inspecting the result. Optional evidence comes from UIZZE's library of 800,000+ real web/iOS screens.

The visible outcome it aims for: screens that reuse the product's existing components, semantic tokens, typography and spacing (no new visual language invented mid-task), with product-specific labels and real data instead of invented metrics, testimonials or placeholder workflows, and with loading, empty, error, success, disabled and permission states all present.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. No animation, transition or interaction values are given anywhere in the skill.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Four steps: (1) identify the screen's real job, primary user/action, required content and states; (2) reuse repo components/tokens before adding abstractions; (3) for new/major work, write a design contract (hierarchy, workflow shape, allowed components, required states, responsive behaviour, acceptance criteria); (4) render once, inspect, fix observable breakage (clipping, overlap, distorted media, inert controls, missing states). UIZZE evidence is optional and question-driven: the authenticated MCP exposes exactly two tools, `find_ui_references` and `find_ui_materials`; a no-result search means continue silently from repo evidence. Install: `npx skills add https://uizze.com --skill anti-ui-slop` (free skill works without account/token).
- **Reference / source:** PART 12 — MCP Market (ECC + Antigravity). External: UIZZE, https://uizze.com (screen/material library). References are evidence to transfer decisions from — copying another product's branding, text, imagery or exact layout is explicitly forbidden.
- **Best for:** Process glue on any build or redesign task — pairs with a design-direction skill (it supplies none) to keep execution honest and state-complete. Trade fit: process only; useful as the "inspect the rendered result before calling it done" rule on preview QA.

## ⟦S0222⟧ antigravity-design-expert — PART 12 — MCP Market — website / animation / scroll / 3D / UI / UX skills (ECC + Antigravity)
- **What it is:** A compact persona skill for "Antigravity" interfaces — weightless, spatial, glassy UIs built with GSAP ScrollTrigger and CSS 3D transforms (or React Three Fiber): floating cards, isometric-tilted grids, translucent glass panels, parallax depth.
- **How it looks:** Elements hover above deep backgrounds on layered, soft, diffused shadows (example: box-shadow 0 20px 40px rgba(0,0,0,0.05)); panels are frosted glass (backdrop-filter: blur(12px), semi-transparent borders); dashboards and card grids can snap into an isometric tilt — transform: rotateX(60deg) rotateZ(-45deg) — so the whole grid reads as a 3D slab floating in space, with foreground elements popping toward the viewer via CSS perspective layering.
- **Frame by frame:** Scroll → GSAP ScrollTrigger floats elements up into view from the Y axis with a slight rotation as they arrive; background layers drift slower than foreground (parallax), deepening the 3D illusion. Grid load → cards stagger in one by one at 0.1s intervals, dropping like dominoes rather than appearing together. All animation is disabled under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, and focus/active/validation feedback must stay immediately visible — only decorative change animates.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Stack: React/Next.js, Tailwind + custom CSS for 3D transforms, GSAP + ScrollTrigger, R3F or CSS 3D (rotateX/rotateY/perspective). Performance rules: apply `will-change: transform` only around measured animations and remove it afterwards; never continuously animate expensive properties like box-shadow or filter. Modular reusable components required. The skill gives few hard numbers — shadow, blur and isometric values above are its only concrete parameters.
- **Reference / source:** PART 12 — MCP Market (ECC + Antigravity). Named tools: GSAP/ScrollTrigger (GreenSock), React Three Fiber. No reference site URL recorded.
- **Best for:** One immersive version direction — a hero or work/gallery section with floating glass cards and scroll-floated entrances, or a 3D-tilted project grid. Trade fit: situational — the weightless/glass look can read tech-startup for a roofer; best kept to a single section version, with real photography carrying trust. Mind the skill's own warning: heavy continuous effects cost performance.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0222⟧

## ⟦S0223⟧ frontend-design — PART 12 — MCP Market — website / animation / scroll / 3D / UI / UX skills (ECC + Antigravity)
- **What it is:** A design-direction process skill (AAS-maintained edition): before code, name one dominant aesthetic direction, define purpose/tone/differentiation anchor, score the direction with the DFII index, then deliver direction summary + design-system snapshot + working code + a verification report.
- **How it looks:** Deliberately unspecified — the look must follow the chosen thesis (brutalist/raw, editorial/magazine, luxury/refined, retro-futurist, industrial/utilitarian, organic, playful, maximalist — blend at most two). Its constants: typography does structural work (1 expressive display font + 1 restrained body font); an uneven, committed colour story — one dominant tone, one accent, one neutral system, all as CSS variables (evenly-balanced palettes are out); composition that breaks the grid on purpose (asymmetry, overlap, negative space or controlled density); texture from noise/grain, gradient meshes, layered translucency, custom dividers, shadows with intent. The test it sets: with the logo removed, a screenshot should still be recognisable by its differentiation anchor.
- **Frame by frame:** Motion is a philosophy here, not a spec: purposeful, sparse, high-impact — prefer ONE strong entrance sequence and a few meaningful hover states; decorative micro-motion spam is banned. No durations, easings or distances are prescribed anywhere in the text.
- **Mechanism & key values:** DFII = (Aesthetic Impact + Context Fit + Implementation Feasibility + Performance Safety) − Consistency Risk, each dimension 1–5, arithmetic range −1 to +19; bands: 12–19 excellent, 8–11 strong (proceed with discipline), 4–7 risky (reduce scope/effects), ≤3 weak (rethink direction). The text itself flags DFII as a subjective discussion aid, not a validated score or release gate. Implementation standards: semantic HTML, accessible by default (contrast/focus/keyboard), CSS-first animation with Framer Motion only when justified, complexity must match ambition (maximalist design → complex code; minimalist → extremely precise spacing/type). Existing brand/design-system conventions outrank novelty.
- **Reference / source:** PART 12 — MCP Market (ECC + Antigravity). Bundled Apache-2.0-licensed skill, modified by AAS maintainers on 2026-09-05. No external site named; cross-references sibling skills (page-cro, copywriting, marketing-psychology, branding, ab-test-setup).
- **Best for:** The first 30 minutes of any new page or deliberate visual refresh: choosing and stress-testing the ONE design idea per section version before building (pairs directly with the reference-first method — score the adapted reference, not an invention). Trade fit: process layer; its verification section (primary action, responsive widths, keyboard/focus, contrast, loading/error states) is a good delivery checklist.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0223⟧

## ⟦S0225⟧ landing-page-generator — PART 12 — MCP Market — website / animation / scroll / 3D / UI / UX skills (ECC + Antigravity)
- **What it is:** A generator of complete Next.js/React + Tailwind landing pages from a product brief: five hero variants, features, pricing, FAQ with schema, testimonials, CTA and footer, with copy written in a chosen framework (PAS, AIDA, BAB — plus 4Ps in its references) and four ready Tailwind style sets.
- **How it looks:** Its representative hero (centered gradient, Dark SaaS): a full-screen near-black section, a 600px violet blur orb glowing behind centred content, a small pill badge ("Now in public beta" with a dot), a two-line text-5xl→md:text-7xl bold headline whose second line is a violet-to-pink gradient text span, a max-w-2xl text-xl gray-400 subhead, two buttons (violet primary, outlined ghost), and micro-copy underneath ("No credit card required · 14-day free trial"). The four style sets: **Dark SaaS** (bg-gray-950, violet-500 accent, bg-gray-900 cards, violet-600 CTA); **Clean Minimal** (white, blue-600 accent, bg-gray-50 rounded-2xl cards); **Bold Startup** (white, orange-500, shadow-xl rounded-3xl cards, font-black tracking-tight headings); **Enterprise** (slate-50, slate-700 accent, white cards, slate-900 CTA). Below the hero: alternating feature rows, a 3-column pricing grid where the highlighted plan wears border-2 border-violet-500 + ring-4 ring-violet-500/20, testimonial grid or single big quote, FAQ accordion in a max-w-3xl column, CTA banner, footer.
- **Frame by frame:** Essentially a static scaffold — the skill prescribes no entrance/scroll animation system. Its only built-in interactions: the FAQ accordion expands/collapses (shadcn Accordion, single collapsible) with FAQPage JSON-LD injected for search; the pricing annual/monthly toggle swaps prices; buttons take Tailwind hover colour shifts (e.g. hover:bg-violet-500). Everything else is layout and copy. Any motion must come from another skill.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Workflow: gather inputs (trigger format) → optional brand-voice analysis maps tone to style+framework → generate sections in order Hero → Features → Pricing → FAQ → Testimonials → CTA → Footer → SEO checklist → output TSX. Performance targets: LCP < 1s, CLS < 0.1, INP < 200ms, TTFB < 200ms, JS bundle < 100KB. SEO numbers: title 50–60 chars, meta description 150–160 chars, OG image 1200×630, one H1 with the primary keyword, alt text ≤125 chars, breakpoints 480/768/1024/1200px, mobile load < 3s, content depth 500+ words at reading grade 6–8. Conversion reference values: headlines under 10 words; logo bar of 5–7 logos directly under the hero; testimonials 2–3 in a row (carousel beyond); pricing anchored on the highlighted middle/high plan with 9-ending prices; tap targets ≥44×44px, CTAs in the bottom 40% thumb zone on mobile, sticky CTA bar on scroll; A/B test priority: headline → CTA text/colour → hero media → social-proof placement → form fields. Copy guardrail in the text: its framework examples use fictional numbers — publish only substantiated metrics and authorised testimonials.
- **Reference / source:** PART 12 — MCP Market (ECC + Antigravity). Bundled reference files: references/conversion-patterns.md, references/frameworks.md, references/landing-page-patterns.md, references/seo-checklist.md. No external site URL recorded.
- **Best for:** Page structure and copy frameworks for conversion pages — the section order, hero-variant menu (centered/split/gradient/video-bg/minimal), pricing and FAQ patterns, and the above-the-fold checklist (value prop, audience, CTA, one trust signal, all inside 5 seconds) transfer directly to a trade homepage's call/CTA and pricing-band sections. Trade fit: structure YES, styling NO — its violet-gradient SaaS look is exactly the generic direction the design-method rule rejects; take the skeleton and the PAS/BAB copy shapes, dress them from bank references.

## ⟦S0226⟧ page-cro — PART 12 — MCP Market — website / animation / scroll / 3D / UI / UX skills (ECC + Antigravity)
- **What it is:** A diagnostic framework for analysing one page's conversion performance: it establishes the page's single goal and traffic context, audits six constraint categories in impact order, and outputs prioritised fixes where every recommendation maps to a category, a constraint and a measurable hypothesis.
- **How it looks:** No visual design of its own — its deliverable is a written report with a fixed shape: Conversion Readiness Summary (baseline, evidence gaps, key limiting factors) → Quick Wins → High-Impact Improvements → Testable Hypotheses → 2–3 copy alternatives each for headlines, subheadlines and CTAs with rationale. Applied to a page, the changes it typically drives: a headline that answers what/who/why-this in one glance, one primary CTA visible above the fold and repeated at decision points with secondary actions visibly demoted, proof placed next to CTAs, objections answered by FAQ/guarantee/comparison, and friction (form fields, slow load, unclear next steps) removed.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. The skill contains no animation, transition or interaction specifications.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Diagnostic order: 1) Value proposition & headline clarity, 2) CTA strategy & hierarchy (exactly one primary goal; secondary goals explicitly demoted), 3) Visual hierarchy & scannability, 4) Trust & social proof (specificity rule: numbers > adjectives; relevance to audience; placement near CTAs), 5) Objection handling by page type (price/value, fit, time-to-value, complexity, risk), 6) Friction & UX barriers. Page-type guidance: homepage = positioning + audience routing; landing = message match + single CTA; pricing = clarity + risk reduction; feature = benefit framing + proof; blog = contextual CTAs. Experiment guardrails: resolve low traffic, unclear value prop or ambiguous goal before testing; each hypothesis must state the change, expected behavioural impact and primary success metric. The text explicitly forbids inventing conversion lifts or a calibrated readiness score.
- **Reference / source:** PART 12 — MCP Market (ECC + Antigravity). Cross-references sibling skills (signup-flow-cro, form-cro, popup-cro, copywriting, ab-test-setup); no external site named.
- **Best for:** Auditing a finished homepage or preview before it ships — a structured pass over the hero promise, the call/CTA hierarchy and proof placement, and for writing the 2–3 headline alternatives a client chooses between. Trade fit: directly applicable to trade homepages (single goal = call/quote request); it is an analysis tool, not a design source.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0226⟧

## ⟦S0227⟧ tailwind-design-system — PART 12 — MCP Market — website / animation / scroll / 3D / UI / UX skills (ECC + Antigravity)
- **What it is:** A build playbook for production design systems in Tailwind: a three-level token hierarchy (brand → semantic → component), CVA variant components, compound components, forms, responsive grids, animation utilities and class-based dark mode — the shadcn/ui architecture written out as reusable code patterns. (Its playbook uses the Tailwind v3 config model; the text itself warns v4 setup differs and not to mix them.)
- **How it looks:** The classic clean shadcn look: white (or near-black-blue in dark mode) surfaces, soft gray borders, small 6–8px-radius controls, medium-weight 14px button labels, cards with 24px padding whose titles are 24px semibold tight-tracked headings over 14px muted descriptions, inputs 40px tall with a 2px focus ring offset by 2px. Colour is entirely semantic — primary/muted/accent/destructive — driven by HSL CSS variables, so light and dark themes are the same components with swapped values (light: background 0 0% 100%, foreground 222.2 84% 4.9%, primary 222.2 47.4% 11.2%; dark: background 222.2 84% 4.9%, foreground 210 40% 98%, muted-foreground 215 20.2% 65.1%, destructive 0 62.8% 30.6%).
- **Frame by frame:** Motion comes from tailwindcss-animate utilities wired to Radix data-states. Dialog open → overlay fades in while content fades + zooms from 95% + slides from top-48%/left-50% offset, 200ms; close → the same in reverse (fade-out, zoom-out-95), 200ms. Dropdown → fade + slide-in-from-top, 150ms in, 150ms out. Generic entrances (fade/slide/zoom) run 300ms. Theme toggle → the Sun icon rotates 0→-90deg while scaling 100→0 as the Moon rotates 90→0 and scales 0→100, one continuous cross-morph on `transition-all`. All dialog animations carry motion-reduce:animate-none fallbacks.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Token math: --radius 0.5rem base; lg = var(--radius), md = calc(var(--radius) − 2px), sm = calc(var(--radius) − 4px). Button sizes: sm h-9 px-3, default h-10 px-4 py-2, lg h-11 px-8, icon h-10 w-10; variants default/destructive/outline/secondary/ghost/link. Card: p-6 blocks, header space-y-1.5, content/footer p-6 pt-0. Input: h-10 w-full px-3 py-2 text-sm, error state swaps border/ring to destructive with an aria-describedby-linked role="alert" message. Grid variants: cols 1–6 stepping at sm/lg (e.g. 4 = 1 → sm:2 → lg:4), gaps gap-2/4/6/8. Container: mx-auto px-4 sm:px-6 lg:px-8, sizes max-w-screen-sm → max-w-screen-2xl (xl default). Utilities: cn() = clsx + tailwind-merge; focus ring = ring-2 ring-ring ring-offset-2. Dark mode via .dark class + localStorage-backed ThemeProvider (the text notes the SSR flash risk and points at a prepaint strategy instead).
- **Reference / source:** PART 12 — MCP Market (ECC + Antigravity). Named sources: Tailwind CSS docs (tailwindcss.com/docs), CVA (cva.style/docs), shadcn/ui (ui.shadcn.com), Radix Primitives (radix-ui.com/primitives). Bundled reference: resources/implementation-playbook.md.
- **Best for:** The component substrate under a design — buttons, cards, forms (quote-request forms especially), grids, dialogs — when a build is React/Tailwind. It standardises sizes and states but supplies a deliberately neutral look: a trade homepage still needs its art direction from design entries. Trade fit: engineering scaffolding only; its illustrative colour pairs are not contrast-certified (the text says measure both themes).
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0227⟧

## ⟦S0228⟧ tailwind-patterns — PART 12 — MCP Market — website / animation / scroll / 3D / UI / UX skills (ECC + Antigravity)
- **What it is:** A compact reference card for Tailwind CSS v4: CSS-first configuration with the `@theme` directive, native container queries, OKLCH colour tokens, breakpoints, dark mode, layout/type/animation pattern tables, and anti-patterns.
- **How it looks:** No page design of its own — it defines the plumbing values a v4 build runs on: semantic tokens declared in CSS (example: --color-primary: oklch(0.7 0.15 250); --color-surface: oklch(0.98 0 0); --color-surface-dark: oklch(0.15 0 0)), spacing tokens (--spacing-xs 0.25rem → --spacing-lg 2rem), and font tokens (sans Inter/system-ui, mono JetBrains Mono, display Outfit/Poppins in its example stack).
- **Frame by frame:** Only generic transition patterns are specified: transition-all duration-200, transition-colors duration-150, ease-out/ease-in-out, hover:scale-105 with transition-transform; built-in keyframe utilities animate-spin (continuous rotation), animate-ping (attention pulse), animate-pulse (opacity pulse), animate-bounce. No sequenced or scroll-linked motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** v4 vs v3: CSS `@theme` replaces tailwind.config.js; Oxide engine; native nesting; all tokens exposed as CSS variables; `@apply` discouraged. Breakpoints: sm 640px, md 768px, lg 1024px, xl 1280px, 2xl 1536px, mobile-first. Container queries: `@container` on the parent, `@sm:`/`@md:`/`@lg:` on children, named containers `@container/card` — use breakpoints for page layout, container queries for reusable components. Dark mode in v4 defaults to the media query; class strategy needs `@custom-variant dark (&:where(.dark, .dark *));`. Type scale: text-xs 0.75rem, text-sm 0.875rem, text-base 1rem, text-lg 1.125rem, text-xl 1.25rem+. Layout patterns: auto-fit grid `grid-cols-[repeat(auto-fit,minmax(250px,1fr))]`, asymmetric bento `grid-cols-3 grid-rows-2` with spans (explicitly preferred over symmetric 3-column grids), sidebar `grid-cols-[auto_1fr]`. Colour architecture: primitive → semantic → component layers, OKLCH preferred for perceptual uniformity. Anti-patterns: arbitrary values everywhere, !important, inline styles, duplicated long class lists, mixing v3 config with v4, heavy @apply.
- **Reference / source:** PART 12 — MCP Market (ECC + Antigravity). Subject: Tailwind CSS v4 (2025). No external URL recorded in the text.
- **Best for:** Setup and consistency checks on any Tailwind v4 build — token declaration, container-query behaviour for cards that must adapt to their column (work/gallery tiles, review cards), and the breakpoint table every version's responsive collapse follows. Trade fit: plumbing only; pairs with ⟦S0227⟧ (v3-style playbook) as its v4 counterpart — use one, not both.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0228⟧

## ⟦S0229⟧ radix-ui-design-system — PART 12 — MCP Market — website / animation / scroll / 3D / UI / UX skills (ECC + Antigravity)
- **What it is:** A guide to building a design system on Radix UI's unstyled, accessibility-first React primitives: Radix supplies behaviour (focus trapping, keyboard navigation, ARIA, portals), you supply all appearance — via CSS variables, Tailwind + CVA, or (legacy) Stitches. Includes a full detailed guide with patterns for Dialog, Dropdown, Tabs, Tooltip, Popover, Select, a cmdk command palette, and form integration.
- **How it looks:** Entirely up to the styling you write — the skill's own examples produce familiar production UI: a ⌘K command palette centred over a 50%-black overlay; an icon-button dropdown with separators and a red Delete item; dialogs with title, description and close control; tab bars; select dropdowns with check indicators. The point for a designer: any look (including the bank's trade looks) can be skinned onto behaviour that already handles the hard parts correctly.
- **Frame by frame:** Behaviour sequences, step by step: Dialog — trigger click → portal mounts outside the DOM hierarchy → overlay appears → content appears → focus is trapped inside → Escape or close-click dismisses → focus returns to the trigger. With its Framer Motion pattern (forceMount + AnimatePresence): overlay fades opacity 0→1 while content fades 0→1 and scales 0.95→1 on open; on close both reverse (opacity→0, scale→0.95) before unmount. Dropdown — open → arrow keys move through items with type-ahead search and wrap behaviour → Enter selects → Escape closes. Tooltip — after the provider's delay (example: delayDuration 200ms) the bubble with its arrow appears on the chosen side. No durations are specified for the motion pattern in the text.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Universal anatomy: Root / Trigger / Portal / Content (+ Title & Description, both required for dialog accessibility). Key props: `asChild` (render as your own element, avoiding nested-button/link errors), `defaultValue` vs controlled `value`/`onValueChange`, `open`/`onOpenChange`, `side`/`align` positioning. Theming example variables: --color-primary 220 90% 56%, --color-surface 0 0% 100%, dark surface 222 47% 11%, --radius-base 0.5rem, --shadow-lg 0 10px 15px -3px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.1). Stitches size example: dialog widths 300/500/700px. CVA button variants/sizes mirror ⟦S0227⟧ (h-9/h-10/h-11). Accessibility checklist values: contrast WCAG AA 4.5:1 text / 3:1 UI, full keyboard support (Tab, arrows, Enter, Esc), aria-invalid + aria-describedby on errors, aria-busy on loading. Install per primitive: npm install @radix-ui/react-{dialog,dropdown-menu,…}; React 16.8+ required. Performance: lazy-load heavy primitives, memoise item renderers, share Tooltip.Provider timing context.
- **Reference / source:** PART 12 — MCP Market (ECC + Antigravity). Named sources: Radix UI docs (radix-ui.com/primitives), Radix Colors, Radix Icons, shadcn/ui (ui.shadcn.com, built on Radix), CVA docs (cva.style/docs), Radix Discord. Bundled reference: references/detailed-guide.md.
- **Best for:** Interactive components whose behaviour must be bulletproof — quote-form dialogs, dropdown navigation, tabbed service sections, tooltips, accordions — underneath any visual direction from the bank. Trade fit: engineering layer only; especially valuable where a version switcher or form must stay keyboard- and screen-reader-correct.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0229⟧

## ⟦S0231⟧ web-performance-optimization — PART 12 — MCP Market (ECC + Antigravity)
- **What it is:** A measure-first playbook for speeding up a site: audit Core Web Vitals and bundle size, then fix LCP, INP, CLS, images and caching in that order, then re-measure.
- **How it looks:** Nothing visitor-facing of its own — its "output" is the same page arriving fast and stable: the hero image paints immediately in the correct box (no reflow), taps respond at once, and below-fold pictures fade in only as you scroll to them. Worked examples show a before/after report table (LCP 4.2s → 1.8s, CLS 0.25 → 0.05, Lighthouse 62 → 94) and a grey shimmer skeleton block that holds space where slow content will land.
- **Frame by frame:** One motion prescribed: the skeleton placeholder — a 200%-wide grey gradient (90deg, #f0f0f0 25% / #e0e0e0 50% / #f0f0f0 75%) sweeping left on a 1.5s infinite loop until real content replaces it. Everything else is about removing motion the user never asked for: layout jumping as unsized images load.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Gate numbers: LCP < 2.5s, INP ≤ 200ms, CLS < 0.1, TTFB < 600ms; field metrics judged at the 75th percentile (lab scores alone don't certify INP). Hero image compressed < 200KB, served as AVIF (quality 70) / WebP (quality 80) / progressive JPEG via `<picture>` with `fetchpriority="high"` + preload; responsive srcset at 400/800/1200w, sizes `(max-width: 768px) 100vw, 50vw`; below-fold images `loading="lazy"`, hero `loading="eager"`; every image carries width/height or `aspect-ratio` (example 1200×600, 4/3). JS bundle target < 200KB gzipped; main-thread tasks under 50ms chunks; code splitting + lazy imports, analytics deferred to window `load`; worked swap moment.js 67KB → date-fns 12KB, whole lodash 72KB → per-function 5KB. Tools named: Lighthouse, WebPageTest, PageSpeed Insights, webpack-bundle-analyzer, sharp.
- **Reference / source:** PART 12 MCP Market skill; its own resource list names web.dev/performance, web.dev/vitals, Lighthouse docs, MDN Performance, Next.js performance docs.
- **Best for:** The final performance pass on any build — heaviest single-file pages (our immersive homepages) most of all: hero LCP discipline, image format/size budgets, and the skeleton-reserve rule for slow sections. Process/QA skill, not a design reference.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0231⟧

## ⟦S0232⟧ frontend-lighthouse — PART 12 — MCP Market (ECC + Antigravity)
- **What it is:** A portable CI gate: one `lighthouserc.cjs` holding every performance budget, run against the production build on every pull request, blocking merges that break Core Web Vitals budgets or category floors.
- **How it looks:** No visitor-facing output. What a team sees is a red or green CI check on the PR and an uploaded Lighthouse HTML/JSON report artifact — including on failure (`if: always()`), so a red gate is debuggable.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. The "sequence" is collect → assert → upload: Lighthouse runs 3 times against the locally served production build and asserts on the median run.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Budgets as named constants: LCP ≤ 2500ms, CLS ≤ 0.1, TBT ≤ 200ms (chosen lab proxy — there is no lab INP audit; field INP ≤ 200ms is monitored separately). Category floors, all `error` severity with `aggregationMethod: "median"`: performance ≥ 0.9, SEO ≥ 0.95, accessibility ≥ 0.95, best-practices ≥ 0.9. `numberOfRuns: 3` minimum (odd, raise to 5 for flake); server on fixed port 3100, `startServerReadyTimeout: 120000`; `onlyCategories` lists exactly the four gated categories; mobile (Moto G4 / slow 4G) emulation is the default gate, desktop optional via `LHCI_FORM_FACTOR=desktop`. Install `@lhci/cli` as dev dependency; script `lhci autorun --config=./lighthouserc.cjs`. Per-framework start commands table (Next.js `pnpm start`, Astro node entry or `npx serve dist`, SvelteKit `node build`, Vite `vite preview`).
- **Reference / source:** PART 12 MCP Market skill; follows the Anthropic SKILL.md format, published from `skills/frontend-lighthouse/SKILL.md`; pairs with frontend-seo and frontend-architecture skills from the same family.
- **Best for:** Process/QA — bolting a non-negotiable speed floor onto a build pipeline so a heavy hero or 3D section can't silently regress LCP/CLS after it was approved. Not a design entry.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0232⟧

## ⟦S0233⟧ ui-visual-validator — PART 12 — MCP Market (ECC + Antigravity)
- **What it is:** A skeptical visual-QA persona: verify from observed pixels (plus DOM/keyboard evidence where screenshots can't reach) that a UI change actually achieved its goal — default assumption is that it did NOT until proven otherwise.
- **How it looks:** Produces a written verdict, not a design: reports open with "From the visual evidence, I observe…", state achieved / partially achieved / not achieved, give visual measurements, an accessibility assessment, edge cases, and specific remediation steps.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion of its own. It does prescribe frame-by-frame animation analysis and layout-shift (CLS) detection as validation techniques applied to other people's motion, plus reduced-motion and high-contrast-mode checks.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Eight-step process: objective description first → goal verification → measurement validation (rotation/position/size) → reverse validation (actively hunt failure evidence) → critical assessment → accessibility evaluation → cross-platform consistency → edge cases. A 13-item mandatory checklist (describe actual content, don't infer from code, confirm contrast ratios, focus indicators, breakpoints, loading/error states, token compliance…). Tools named: Chromatic, Percy, Applitools, BackstopJS, Playwright visual comparisons, Cypress, Jest Image Snapshot, Storybook. Hard evidence limits stated in the skill: a screenshot cannot prove alt text, accessible names, keyboard order, focus trapping or full WCAG compliance; pixel estimates are not precise CSS measurements; contrast must be measured from rendered colours.
- **Reference / source:** PART 12 MCP Market skill. No external site named.
- **Best for:** The audit loop on our builds — an independent judge for section screenshots (desktop + 375px mobile) that refuses "looks different" as proof of "looks correct". QA skill; pairs naturally with the frame-by-frame section review habit.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0233⟧

## ⟦S0234⟧ design-system — PART 12 — MCP Market (ECC + Antigravity)
- **What it is:** The mechanical invariants layer for frontend builds: token architecture, type hierarchy, first-viewport loading order, font-loading without visible pop, graceful loading states, stable chrome, and motion timing — used alongside the direction/aesthetic skills.
- **How it looks:** A page whose first screen paints complete and correct: hero text and image present at first paint (never an empty hero box), titles never flash in a fallback font then jump, headers/toolbars hold one constant height while status text changes, and slow sections sit in styled placeholders that match the final layout instead of blank boxes and partial reflows.
- **Frame by frame:** Load sequence, in order: (1) only the above-the-fold set is prioritized — hero text, hero image/video, brand mark — everything else waits; (2) decorative display text may be held at `opacity: 0` under a `fonts-pending` class, then on `document.fonts.ready` it fades in over ~0.5s, with a hard ~2.5s safety reveal so a failed font never hides text forever; (3) annotation labels start at opacity 0 and fade up over ~0.35s once JS positions them; (4) canvas/WebGL and 3D viewers sit at opacity 0 until the first real frame renders, then fade in; (5) below-fold images lazy-load into reserved aspect-ratio boxes. Scrollytelling motion: as the reader scrolls, each text step crossing the viewport mid-line activates and the pinned graphic tweens between states over 300–700ms (colour/width/opacity), inactive steps dimmed to opacity .3.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Tokens in five families only (foreground, background, border, brand, semantic) — no hardcoded hex. Fonts self-hosted WOFF2, preloaded for first-viewport weights; never a render-blocking third-party font stylesheet. Type: headlines heavier + tighter tracking; data in monospace with `tabular-nums` — and an explicit ban on mono for decorative eyebrow/spec microtext. Motion defaults for restrained UIs: micro-interactions ~150ms, larger transitions 200–250ms, ease-out; one orchestrated moment (staggered load with animation-delay) over scattered micro-interactions. Scrollytelling mechanics: IntersectionObserver `rootMargin: '-48% 0px -48% 0px'`, threshold 0; steps ~85vh tall; graphic `sticky top-0 h-screen`; graphic is a pure function of the active step. Nested radii: child ≤ parent, ideal `child_radius = max(0, parent_radius − gap)`. Contrast: APCA for perceptual decisions, WCAG 2 ratios (4.5 / 3:1) as the compliance gate. Its bundled motion-choreography reference adds: duration table (toggle 100–200ms, route slide 150–250ms, reveal 200–400ms, shared-element morph 300–500ms); navigation honesty rule — hierarchical/ordered = directional slide, lateral/tab = fade, never a slide between peers; motion blur `filter: blur(3px)` near the 30% mark of a morph; loader anti-flicker show-delay ~150–300ms and minimum visible ~300–500ms; animate transform/opacity only, never `transition: all`.
- **Reference / source:** PART 12 MCP Market skill. Its motion reference is adapted from Vercel's Web Interface Guidelines (vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines @ 4e799d4) and the React View Transitions skill (vercel-labs/agent-skills @ f8a72b9); contrast guidance points to apcacontrast.com; sibling skills design-spatial and design-thinking are referenced but not bundled.
- **Best for:** Every build's foundation pass — token discipline, hero load order, font behaviour, and the scrollytelling pattern for process/how-it-works sections (a pinned graphic with scrolling steps suits a "how a job runs" narrative directly). Also the graceful-loading rules for any 3D/WebGL hero.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0234⟧

## ⟦S0235⟧ design-md — PART 12 — MCP Market (ECC + Antigravity)
- **What it is:** A documentation skill: pull a Google Stitch project's screens and theme via the Stitch MCP server, analyse the HTML/screenshot, and synthesize a `DESIGN.md` — a descriptive "source of truth" file used to prompt Stitch for new screens in the same design language.
- **How it looks:** The deliverable is a five-section Markdown document: (1) Visual Theme & Atmosphere in evocative words ("Airy", "Dense", "Utilitarian"), (2) Color Palette & Roles — each colour with a descriptive name plus exact hex plus functional role (e.g. "Deep Muted Teal-Navy (#294056) — used for primary actions"), (3) Typography Rules, (4) Component Stylings — buttons/cards/inputs described physically (rounded-full = "Pill-shaped", rounded-lg = "Subtly rounded corners", rounded-none = "Sharp, squared-off edges"; shadows as "Flat" / "Whisper-soft diffused" / "Heavy, high-contrast"), (5) Layout Principles.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. Workflow order: discover Stitch MCP namespace → list projects/screens → get_screen metadata (screenshot + HTML download URLs, width/height/deviceType) → download assets → get_project designTheme → extract identity, atmosphere, palette, geometry, depth → write DESIGN.md.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Precision rule: descriptive name + hex in parentheses + role, never colour names alone; exact pixel values in parentheses after natural-language descriptions. Structure is fixed (the five sections above). Project ID taken from the `name` field (e.g. `projects/13534454087919359824`). Limitation recorded in the skill itself: screenshots show tokens, not the designer's intent — observed values must be separated from inferred WHY, and an existing DESIGN.md is merged, not overwritten.
- **Reference / source:** PART 12 MCP Market skill; built around Google's Stitch and its Effective Prompting Guide at stitch.withgoogle.com/docs/learn/prompting/.
- **Best for:** Process — capturing an existing design language into a promptable document. Marginal for our single-file trade builds (no Stitch in the pipeline); the transferable value is the discipline of writing palette/type/shape descriptions a generator can follow exactly.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0235⟧

## ⟦S0236⟧ ui-a11y — PART 12 — MCP Market, StyleSeed family
- **What it is:** A static accessibility audit-and-fix pass for a component or page, run against WCAG 2.2 AA across the four principles (Perceivable, Operable, Understandable, Robust), assuming the StyleSeed token conventions (`data-slot`, semantic tokens).
- **How it looks:** No visual output of its own; its effect on screen is the corrected page: muted text dark enough to read (the skill's own worked check: `text-muted-foreground` #717182 on white #FFFFFF = 4.6:1, passes), visible focus rings on keyboard tab, and motion that freezes for reduced-motion users.
- **Frame by frame:** The only motion it prescribes is a kill-switch: under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, all animation and transition durations are forced to 0.01ms. Everything else is static audit criteria.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Contrast: text 4.5:1 normal, 3:1 large/bold; non-text UI/graphics 3:1. Token minimums table: `--foreground` 7:1+, `--muted-foreground` 4.5:1+, `--brand` 4.5:1+, `--destructive` 4.5:1+, `--success` 3:1+ (large/icons only), `--warning` 4.5:1+. Pointer targets: WCAG 2.2 AA SC 2.5.8 floor is 24×24 CSS px (or a spacing exception) — the skill is explicit that 44×44 (`min-h-11 min-w-11`) is the preferred usability target, not an AA pass/fail line. Focus style: `focus-visible:ring-2 ring-ring ring-offset-2`. Output format: issues by severity (Critical/Major/Minor), auto-fixes applied directly, manual-review flags. Not for runtime/screen-reader testing — static code audit only.
- **Reference / source:** StyleSeed family (the /ss-* command set); links the W3C WCAG 2.2 target-size understanding pages.
- **Best for:** QA pass on any finished section — forms and CTA areas especially (labels, error association via `aria-describedby`, focus visibility), and the contrast check on muted/secondary text over tinted backgrounds.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0236⟧

## ⟦S0237⟧ ui-component — PART 12 — MCP Market, StyleSeed family
- **What it is:** A component generator that produces one new UI component exactly to StyleSeed conventions: semantic tokens, CVA variants, `data-slot`, and a fixed typography/spacing system.
- **How it looks:** Components that sit invisibly inside the StyleSeed look: cards and controls coloured only from tokens (`bg-card`, `text-foreground`, `text-brand`, `text-muted-foreground`, `border-border`), shadows from `--shadow-card` / `--shadow-elevated` variables, radii from the rounded-md / rounded-lg / rounded-2xl steps, and text set on its four-step scale — display 36–48px tight, headings 18–24px, body 14–17px, uppercase captions 10–13px.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion of its own; transitions are delegated to tokens (`duration-[var(--duration-fast)]`, `ease-[var(--ease-default)]`) and must respect `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Rules: `function` declarations, `cn()` for all className merging, `React.ComponentProps<>` typing, `className` override always supported, named exports only, primitives to `src/components/ui/`, composed patterns to `src/components/patterns/`. Spacing in multiples of 6px (`p-1.5`, `p-3`, `p-6`); `size-*` instead of `w-* h-*`; logical `ms-/me-` instead of `ml-/mr-`. Type tracking: display `leading-none tracking-[-0.02em]`, heading `leading-snug tracking-[-0.01em]`, caption uppercase `tracking-[0.05em]`. Touch targets minimum 44×44px. StyleSeed-project-only: the referenced CLAUDE.md/theme.css/button.tsx are not bundled in the bank.
- **Reference / source:** StyleSeed (bitjaru/styleseed conventions, via the /ss-* family). No external site named.
- **Best for:** Process reference for component discipline — token-only colour and the 6px spacing rhythm are portable habits; the generator itself only runs inside a real StyleSeed project. Low direct value for single-file HTML builds.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0237⟧

## ⟦S0238⟧ ui-lint — PART 12 — MCP Market, StyleSeed family
- **What it is:** A seconds-fast, grep-based lint that flags common design-system violations in a file and prints each with its fix — detection only; it never applies the refactor.
- **How it looks:** A console-style report: 🔴 FAIL / 🟡 WARN lines with file:line and the correction (e.g. `Hardcoded hex: text-[#3C3C3C] → use text-text-primary`, `Raw px: p-[24px] → use p-6`), ending in a 🟢 PASS or a totals line "X errors, Y warnings".
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Eight checks, each a literal grep: (1) hex colours in classNames outside theme/token files, (2) raw pixel Tailwind values `p-[24px]`/`gap-[12px]`, (3) old `w-4 h-4` pairs → `size-4`, (4) physical `ml-/mr-/pl-/pr-` → logical `ms-/me-/ps-/pe-`, (5) forbidden pure black (`text-black`, `#000000`), (6) components missing `data-slot`, (7) ambiguous arbitrary font-size values (with the Tailwind v4 nuance that `--text-*` tokens are legitimate), (8) template-literal className without `cn()`. The skill itself warns the rules are project-dependent (pure black, `data-slot`, `cn()` are StyleSeed choices, not universal violations) and every match must be eyeballed in context.
- **Reference / source:** StyleSeed family; links the official Tailwind font-size docs.
- **Best for:** QA — a pre-delivery sweep pattern. The habit transfers (grep for hardcoded hex / raw px before calling a file done) even though the exact rules are StyleSeed's.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0238⟧

## ⟦S0239⟧ ui-page — PART 12 — MCP Market, StyleSeed family
- **What it is:** A mobile-first page scaffolder: assembles a new screen from StyleSeed's PageShell / TopBar / BottomNav patterns and then runs a mandatory Golden Rules verification before presenting it.
- **How it looks:** A phone-width page (max 430px) on the app background: top bar with logo/title and actions, content sections stacked with 24px rhythm, every piece of content sitting inside cards (`bg-card rounded-2xl p-6`, card shadow token), generous bottom padding (pb-24) so nothing hides behind the bottom navigation bar.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion specified.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Layout numbers: container `max-w-[430px]`, section padding `px-6`, vertical rhythm `space-y-6`, bottom clearance `pb-24`, safe-area insets via `env(safe-area-inset-*)`. Golden Rules checklist: all content in cards; only `--brand` as accent; zero hardcoded hex; section types alternate (no two identical in a row); numbers at ~2:1 ratio with their units; spacing in 6px multiples; `mx-6` for single cards vs `px-6` for grids/carousels; touch targets ≥ 44px. Mobile-only — explicitly not for desktop screens.
- **Reference / source:** StyleSeed family (/ss-page). No external site named.
- **Best for:** Process reference — the "alternate section types, one accent, everything carded, verify before presenting" checklist is a usable QA shape for mobile page composition generally; the scaffold itself needs a StyleSeed project.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0239⟧

## ⟦S0240⟧ ui-pattern — PART 12 — MCP Market, StyleSeed family
- **What it is:** A generator for composed UI patterns — card sections, grids, lists, form sections, tables, action sheets — assembled from existing StyleSeed primitives rather than new code.
- **How it looks:** A catalogue of 14 named pattern shapes with fixed geometry: card-section (titled card inset by mx-6), grid-2col (`grid grid-cols-2 gap-4 px-6`), scroll-horizontal (a row of cards sliding sideways, scrollbar hidden), list-section, form-section, stat-grid; data patterns data-table, detail-card (key–value), chart-card (Recharts wrapper), ranking-list; interactive patterns action-sheet (bottom sheet of action buttons), filter-bar, search-header. Section titles sit at 18px bold above their cards; lists breathe at `space-y-3`, grids at `gap-4`.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion specified; the only movement implied is the horizontal card row's native scroll.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Cards: `bg-card rounded-2xl p-6 shadow-[var(--shadow-card)]`; section wrapper `mx-6`; title `text-foreground font-bold text-[18px] mb-4`; all colour from semantic tokens; output must be a reusable component with props. Compose-only rule: never recreate primitives from `components/ui/`.
- **Reference / source:** StyleSeed family (/ss-pattern). No external site named.
- **Best for:** A naming/geometry reference for section building blocks — the horizontal scrolling card row and stat-grid shapes map onto work/gallery and proof sections; generation itself is StyleSeed-bound.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0240⟧

## ⟦S0241⟧ ui-review — PART 12 — MCP Market, StyleSeed family
- **What it is:** A full UI code review against an eight-part checklist — tokens, component conventions, accessibility, mobile, performance, typography, spacing, and "coherence" — returning Pass / Needs Improvement / Fail with file:line issues and concrete fixes.
- **How it looks:** No visual output; a review document: a verdict line, then violations each pinned to a line, then the exact code change for each.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion of its own; it checks that other people's motion uses tokens (`duration-[var(--duration-fast)]`) and respects `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Typography scale: 14 steps, 10–48px, fonts Pretendard/Inter; weights 400/500/600/700; display 36–48px `leading-none tracking-[-0.02em]`, headings 18–24px `leading-snug tracking-[-0.01em]`, body 14–17px, captions 10–13px uppercase `tracking-[0.05em]`; `line-height: 1.5` on display/heading text is a violation. Spacing: multiples of 6px only (p-5=20px and gap-3.5=14px are named violations). Text floor 12px. Contrast WCAG AA 4.5:1 text / 3:1 large; 44×44px targets as the design goal (with the WCAG 2.2 AA 24×24 floor noted). The distinctive part is §8 Coherence — "one choice per axis": one radius personality (sharp 0–4px OR soft 8–12px OR pill) across every card/button/input/modal; one accent colour; no emoji as UI icons; status colour = severity only (a normal state is neutral grey); one shadow language and light direction; one icon family/stroke; nested radius `inner = outer − padding`; one control-height set (e.g. 40px); errors never by colour alone. The skill states plainly this mixed-parts problem is the biggest reason UI reads as AI-generated.
- **Reference / source:** StyleSeed family (/ss-review); coherence rules cite the project's VISUAL-CRAFT.md §C0 (not bundled).
- **Best for:** QA — the coherence checklist is the most portable part of the whole StyleSeed run: a one-accent / one-radius / one-shadow audit is a sharp final pass for any homepage before delivery.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0241⟧

## ⟦S0242⟧ ui-score — PART 12 — MCP Market, StyleSeed family
