- **Mechanism & key values:** Eight checkpoint areas with fixed criterion sets: keyboard & focus (2.1.1, 2.1.2, 2.4.3, 2.4.7, 2.4.11 — always driven), structure & semantics (1.3.1, 1.3.2, 2.4.1, 2.4.6 — from the snapshot), names/roles/states (4.1.2, 2.5.3, 4.1.3), visual adaptation (1.4.1 use of colour, 1.4.4, 1.4.10 reflow, 1.4.12, 1.3.4, 2.3.3, 1.4.11 non-text contrast), forms & errors (3.3.1–3.3.3, 1.3.5, 3.3.7, 3.3.8), media & timing (1.2.x, 2.2.1, 2.2.2), pointer & target (2.5.1, 2.5.7, 2.5.8), content & navigation (3.1.1/2, 2.4.4, 3.2.3/4, 3.2.6). Evidence budgets are hard caps: ● gets full proof gathered once; ◐ gets at most one selector, one screenshot, an opinion and a confirmation request; ○ gets zero driving — just the ability, AT and flow named. "Not exercised" is a legitimate reported outcome (undetermined), never silently dropped and never a pass. Requires a browser MCP (chrome-devtools recommended, or playwright/puppeteer); without one, only static checks run and the rest become ○ handoffs. Detailed per-checkpoint procedure lives in the skill's references/checkpoints.md; --deep drives every triggered area through it.
- **Reference / source:** github.com/AccessLint/claude-marketplace (plugins/accesslint/skills/accessibility-inspect/SKILL.md); shared rules in the plugin's shared/methodology.md; widget contracts from the WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices (APG).
- **Best for:** Operability QA on interactive sections — the 1·2·3 version switcher, menus, galleries, quote forms — anywhere "lint-clean" is not the same as usable by keyboard or screen reader. The contrast in its catalog name is covered inside the visual-adaptation area (1.4.1, 1.4.11) plus the engine's flat-background contrast checks in ⟦S0271⟧.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0273⟧

## ⟦S0274⟧ AccessLint/link-purpose — PART 13 — UI Skills, rest of the ui-skills.com catalog
- **What it is:** A second bundling of the same AccessLint **accessibility-inspect** skill body as ⟦S0273⟧ (and ⟦S0276⟧), catalogued under the name link-purpose with topics accessibility / testing / interaction. The skill it contains is the manual inspection tier: drive a live page through the interaction and judgment checks a rule engine cannot decide, grade findings by evidence basis (● verified / ◐ flagged / ○ human-required) and severity, and close every criterion in a ledger as verified, flagged, not exercised or N/A. It locates and assesses; it does not fix.
- **How it looks:** The same report shape as ⟦S0273⟧: a compact ledger of success-criterion numbers by bucket at the top, then verified findings with selector and reproduction, flagged findings with capped evidence and an opinion, and human-required handoffs. Under this entry's name, the relevant slice is the content & navigation checkpoint area, where link purpose (SC 2.4.4) and page language (3.1.1/2) are read from the initial snapshot, while cross-page consistency (3.2.3/4, 3.2.6) is explicitly not exercised here — it belongs to the whole-site audit, ⟦S0272⟧.
- **Frame by frame:** As ⟦S0273⟧: one snapshot after the wait gate, one batched keyboard walk (focus each tabbable in order, recording :focus outline/box-shadow, bounding box and overlay coverage per stop), real key events only at suspect widgets, scoped re-reads after state changes, resize passes for reflow/zoom.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Identical to ⟦S0273⟧ — the same eight checkpoint areas and criterion sets (keyboard & focus 2.1.1, 2.1.2, 2.4.3, 2.4.7, 2.4.11; visual adaptation including 1.4.1 and 1.4.11; forms 3.3.1–3.3.3 et al.), the same evidence budgets (◐ capped at one selector + one screenshot; ○ zero driving), the same dedup rule (the scan engine owns statically detectable criteria; inspect never re-checks them), and the same browser-MCP prerequisite. Read ⟦S0273⟧'s entry for the full detail; this entry exists so the catalog name is accounted for in the coverage ledger.
- **Reference / source:** github.com/AccessLint/claude-marketplace (plugins/accesslint/skills/accessibility-inspect/SKILL.md) — the same source file as ⟦S0273⟧ and ⟦S0276⟧; shared rules in the plugin's shared/methodology.md.
- **Best for:** The same jobs as ⟦S0273⟧ — keyboard, focus, screen-reader-tree, reflow and form-error checks on one page. For a build session, treat the three catalog names (contrast-checker, link-purpose, use-of-color) as one tool: accessibility-inspect.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0274⟧ (same skill body as ⟦S0273⟧)

## ⟦S0275⟧ AccessLint/refactor — PART 13 — UI Skills, rest of the ui-skills.com catalog
- **What it is:** The bundled source is the AccessLint **accessibility-fix** skill: remediation only. It repairs WCAG 2.2 violations in a baseline → apply → verify loop, taking either a findings worklist (from ⟦S0271⟧, ⟦S0273⟧ or ⟦S0272⟧) or a target (URL, files, directory) that it audits first for its own baseline. It only fixes; finding is the other skills' job.
- **How it looks:** The changes land in the page's source files — a missing alt attribute, label or accessible name added at the exact line a Source: pointer names — and each cycle reports: the flow used, violations by impact, what was applied (file and rule), what was deferred as TODOs and why, and the before/after counts. Judgment calls are never filled in silently: a violation marked contextual or visual gets a TODO carrying its rule ID, and content (alt text, labels, link text) is never invented.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. The loop itself is the sequence: baseline audit in compact format recording rule ID + selector per violation; apply fixes grouped per file (mechanical fixes exactly as given in each finding's Fix: field); re-run the same audit and diff against the baseline — every targeted violation gone and no new ones, or the run reports the failure and stops rather than iterating silently.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Two flows: audit_live for URLs (attaches to a debuggable Chrome; for authenticated pages the user starts a headed Chrome and signs in first) and audit_html for raw HTML/JSX strings and files. Source: lines come from React DevTools fibers and exist only in live-DOM audits against React dev builds — the first path listed is the JSX literal, the rest are enclosing components; without one, fixes are located by grepping stable hooks (data-testid, id, aria-label), then visible text, then tree position. Scope discipline: confirm before editing files outside the obvious target, or before more than about 10 mechanical fixes. `explain_rule` resolves rule questions. A violation with no Fix: directive is left as a TODO, never guessed.
- **Reference / source:** github.com/AccessLint/claude-marketplace (plugins/accesslint/skills/accessibility-fix/SKILL.md, catalogued here as "refactor"); shared conventions in the plugin's shared/methodology.md.
- **Best for:** Clearing the worklist a scan or inspection produced on a built page — the remediation pass between ⟦S0271⟧/⟦S0273⟧ finding problems and ⟦S0270⟧ proving none regressed.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0275⟧

- **What it is:** A third bundling of the same AccessLint **accessibility-inspect** skill body as ⟦S0273⟧ and ⟦S0274⟧, catalogued under the name use-of-color with topics accessibility / color / testing. The skill it contains is the manual inspection tier: drive a live page through the checks a rule engine cannot decide — keyboard and focus, accessibility-tree names/roles/states, reflow and zoom, reduced motion, form errors, target size — grading each finding by evidence basis and severity and closing every criterion in a ledger. It locates and assesses; it does not fix.
- **How it looks:** The same report shape as ⟦S0273⟧: ledger first (bare SC numbers per bucket), then verified, flagged and human-required findings. Under this entry's name, the relevant slice is the visual-adaptation checkpoint area, whose first criterion is SC 1.4.1 Use of Color — whether colour is the sole carrier of meaning. The source works an explicit example of its grading subtlety: a missing programmatic status in the a11y tree is a ●-grade 1.3.1 fact sitting inside a ◐ finding, while the conclusion that colour alone carries the meaning (1.4.1) stays ◐, because citing the machine-checkable half never upgrades the interpretive half.
- **Frame by frame:** As ⟦S0273⟧: one snapshot after the wait gate, one batched keyboard walk recording per-stop :focus styles, bounding boxes and overlay coverage, real key presses only at suspect widgets, scoped re-reads after state changes, one resize each for reflow and zoom; motion checks only when the page has motion.

Read ⟦S0273⟧'s entry for the full detail; this entry exists so the catalog name is accounted for in the coverage ledger.

## ⟦S0277⟧ addyosmani/accessibility — PART 13 — UI Skills, rest of the ui-skills.com catalog
- **What it is:** A self-contained WCAG 2.2 guideline and audit skill organised by the POUR principles (Perceivable, Operable, Understandable, Robust): concrete code patterns for each criterion family, an evidence-led audit workflow (live Lighthouse audit → localise the failing component → inspect the accessibility tree → exercise the flow by keyboard → fix and re-run), and manual/automated testing checklists.
- **How it looks:** What following it produces on a page: images with real alt text (decorative ones emptied with alt="" and role="presentation"); icon buttons carrying an aria-label or a visually-hidden text name (the hidden class is a 1×1 px clipped, nowrap span); video with caption and description tracks and audio with a transcript tucked into a details element; a skip link before the navigation; navigation marked with aria-label and aria-current="page"; form fields with programmatically associated labels, errors announced via role="alert" with aria-invalid set, and the first error focused on submit; login that allows paste and offers passkey or email-link alternatives instead of a memory test.
- **Frame by frame:** Motion enters through one rule: under `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)`, all animations and transitions collapse to 0.01 ms duration and a single iteration, and scroll-behavior returns to auto — motion effectively freezes rather than merely slowing. Everything else in the skill is static markup and style.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Contrast (1.4.3 AA / 1.4.6 AAA): normal text 4.5:1 / 7:1; large text (≥18 px, or ≥14 px bold) 3:1 / 4.5:1; UI components and graphics 3:1; focus indicators need 3:1 against their background (1.4.11) — the given pattern is a 2 px solid currentColor outline with 2 px offset on :focus-visible, or a brand box-shadow of 0 0 0 3px rgba(0, 95, 204, 0.5). Focus-not-obscured (2.4.11): scroll-margin-top 80 px and scroll-margin-bottom 60 px so focused elements clear sticky bars (2.4.12 AAA: no part hidden). Target size (2.5.8): minimum 24×24 CSS px, with 44×44 recommended. New-in-2.2 criteria covered: 2.4.11, 2.5.7 (dragging needs a single-pointer alternative), 2.5.8, 3.2.6 (help in the same relative order on every page), 3.3.7 (never re-ask for information already given), 3.3.8 (accessible authentication). Timing example: a session-expiry warning 2 minutes (120,000 ms) ahead with extend/log-out actions. Testing: Lighthouse with --only-categories=accessibility or axe CLI for automation (a score of 100 is explicitly not conformance), plus manual passes — full keyboard tab-through, a screen reader (VoiceOver/NVDA/TalkBack), 200% zoom, Windows High Contrast, reduced motion.
- **Reference / source:** github.com/addyosmani/web-quality-skills (skills/accessibility/SKILL.md); bundled references WCAG.md and A11Y-PATTERNS.md (modal focus trap, skip link, form labels, error handling, ARIA tabs, live regions, screen-reader commands); external references named: WCAG 2.2 Quick Reference (w3.org), WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices, Deque axe rules.
- **Best for:** The build-time standard every section is written against — focus states on the version switcher and menus, labels and error handling on quote forms, contrast of text over hero photography, alt text on work galleries. Broader and more code-oriented than the AccessLint suite (⟦S0270⟧–⟦S0276⟧), which is the run-time checking machinery.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0277⟧

## ⟦S0278⟧ addyosmani/api-and-interface-design — PART 13 — UI Skills, rest of the ui-skills.com catalog
- **What it is:** A design doctrine for stable public interfaces — REST and GraphQL endpoints, module boundaries, component props — built on contract-first design, one consistent error shape, validation only at system boundaries, additive change over breaking change, and idempotency that is actually honoured rather than merely accepted.
- **How it looks:** No visitor-facing surface. Its visible product is predictable machine-readable shape: a list endpoint returning `{ data: [...], pagination: { page, pageSize, totalItems, totalPages } }` (the example pages 142 items at 20 per page into 8 pages), and every error on every endpoint wearing the identical envelope `{ error: { code, message, details? } }` — a machine-readable code such as "VALIDATION_ERROR" beside a human-readable message.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Status-code map: 400 invalid data, 401 unauthenticated, 403 unauthorised, 404 not found, 409 conflict, 422 semantically invalid, 500 server error (internals never exposed). Naming: plural-noun endpoints with no verbs, camelCase query params and response fields, is/has/can boolean prefixes, UPPER_SNAKE enum values. Pagination from day one (page / pageSize / sortBy / sortOrder). Idempotency, the skill's deepest section: the key must derive from the intent, never the attempt — client-supplied, or built from an immutable identifier (`charge:v1:${orderId}`); a fresh randomUUID, a timestamp, or `${userId}:${amount}` are all called out as broken. Claiming must be atomic — an INSERT against a unique constraint, never a check-then-act SELECT-then-INSERT race. The same key arriving with a different payload hash fails loudly with 422 instead of replaying the first response. An in-flight duplicate gets a deliberate answer: 409 Conflict, a bounded wait, or 202 plus a status URL. Every call has three outcomes — success, failure, and unknown — so intent is recorded before calling out. Retention is set from the longest retry chain, not disk cost (a 24-hour key TTL behind a 7-day dead-letter queue is named as a duplicate waiting to happen). Framing laws: Hyrum's Law (every observable behaviour becomes a de facto contract) and the One-Version Rule (extend rather than fork). Closes with rationalization/red-flag tables and a 13-point verification checklist.
- **Reference / source:** github.com/addyosmani/agent-skills (skills/api-and-interface-design/SKILL.md); it cross-points to a deprecation-and-migration skill for safe removal, which is not part of this entry.
- **Best for:** Backend and contract work behind a site — the form-submission endpoint, a configurator's pricing API, any integration a build depends on. Not a design or motion reference; situational for page builds, essential when the page talks to a server that must not double-charge or double-book.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0278⟧
## ⟦S0279⟧ addyosmani/best-practices — PART 13 — UI Skills — rest of the ui-skills.com catalog
- **What it is:** An audit-and-fix skill for modern web best practices — security, browser compatibility and code quality — based on the Lighthouse Best Practices audits. It produces no design of its own; it hardens a page that already exists.
- **How it looks:** Nothing visual is prescribed. The page it leaves behind is a valid HTML5 page: `<!DOCTYPE html>`, charset as the first element in `<head>`, a responsive viewport meta tag, semantic elements (`header`, `nav`, `main`, `article`) instead of nested divs, images kept at their true aspect ratio (a 4:3 photo declared 300×225, or `object-fit: cover`), a clean console, and permission prompts (e.g. geolocation) that appear only after a user action with an explanation, never on page load.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Evidence-led workflow: run a live Lighthouse Best Practices audit (Chrome DevTools MCP `lighthouse_audit`, navigation mode, or snapshot mode to preserve state), inspect console/network failures, fix, re-run; never treat a high score as proof of security. Security: HTTPS with no mixed content; HSTS only after every subdomain supports HTTPS; strict CSP as defence in depth, preferring nonces/hashes, tested report-only before enforcing; SRI on pinned third-party code; sanitize untrusted HTML; production source maps hidden (`devtool: 'hidden-source-map'`, Vite `sourcemap: 'hidden'`) with `sourcesContent` stripped. Compatibility: feature detection (`'IntersectionObserver' in window`, CSS `@supports`) over user-agent sniffing; polyfills bundled at build time (Babel/SWC + core-js, or `@vitejs/plugin-legacy`), never loaded from an uncontrolled third-party CDN (the skill names the mid-2024 polyfill.io supply-chain compromise). Banned deprecated APIs: `document.write`, synchronous XHR, Application Cache (use Service Workers). Touch/wheel listeners passive (`{ passive: true }`) unless `preventDefault` is needed; event delegation over per-element handlers; listener cleanup via `removeEventListener` or `AbortController` signals. Permissions-Policy meta to restrict geolocation/camera/microphone.
- **Reference / source:** https://github.com/addyosmani/web-quality-skills (best-practices skill). Tools it names: `npm audit`, SecurityHeaders.com, W3C Validator, Mozilla Observatory, Lighthouse CLI. References named: MDN Web Security, OWASP Top 10.
- **Best for:** A pre-launch hardening pass over any finished page — every section benefits, but it supplies no layout, look or animation. Trade fit: good final QA gate for single-file trade homepages.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0279⟧

## ⟦S0280⟧ addyosmani/core-web-vitals — PART 13 — UI Skills — rest of the ui-skills.com catalog
- **What it is:** A diagnosis-and-fix skill for the three Core Web Vitals — LCP (loading), INP (interactivity), CLS (visual stability) — using field data to prioritise and browser traces to find causes.
- **How it looks:** The visitor sees the largest hero element (usually the hero image, video or big headline block) painted fast, taps and clicks answered without a lag, and a page that never jumps as fonts, images or injected content arrive — every image carries real width/height or an aspect-ratio so its space is reserved before it loads.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion is prescribed; the skill's whole aim is removing unwanted motion (layout shift) and delay from load and interaction.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Thresholds, judged at the 75th percentile of visits: LCP good ≤ 2.5s, needs work 2.5–4s, poor > 4s; INP good ≤ 200ms, needs work 200–500ms, poor > 500ms; CLS good ≤ 0.1, needs work 0.1–0.25, poor > 0.25. LCP fixes: TTFB < 800ms; LCP resource discoverable in the initial HTML as a real `<img>` with `fetchpriority="high"` (preload added only when a trace shows late discovery); critical CSS inlined (< 14KB) with the rest deferred; `font-display: swap` so fonts don't block text; LCP element server-rendered, not fetched by client JS. Speculation Rules API prerendering for likely next pages, with Chrome eagerness triggers: conservative = pointer/touch down; moderate = 200ms hover on desktop (viewport heuristics on mobile); eager = 10ms hover desktop / 50ms after the anchor enters the viewport on mobile (Chrome 143+); immediate = as soon as rules are observed — each prerender costs roughly a full page load, and load-time side effects must be gated on `prerenderingchange`. INP is diagnosed as input delay + processing time + presentation delay separately. Measurement sources ranked: browser performance trace, CrUX/Search Console p75, Lighthouse CLI/PageSpeed Insights, first-party RUM (prefer the `web-vitals` library); a `PerformanceObserver` snippet is given to identify the LCP element in-session. Framework quick fixes included for Next.js (`next/image` priority), React (preload + `useTransition`), Vue/Nuxt (`NuxtImg` preload, aspect-ratio CSS).
- **Reference / source:** https://github.com/addyosmani/web-quality-skills (core-web-vitals skill). References named: web.dev articles on LCP, INP and CLS; Chrome's prerender/eagerness documentation.
- **Best for:** The hero above all (it is almost always the LCP element), plus a whole-page performance gate. Trade fit: directly applicable to image-heavy trade homepages — big job photos must be prioritised, correctly sized and dimensioned.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0280⟧

## ⟦S0281⟧ addyosmani/performance — PART 13 — UI Skills — rest of the ui-skills.com catalog
- **What it is:** A general web performance optimisation skill: loading speed, runtime responsiveness and resource delivery, driven by a measure-first workflow (field baseline, trace, fix only the measured bottleneck, re-measure).
- **How it looks:** A page that arrives light and paints early: hero image in AVIF/WebP at the sizes the layout actually uses, text visible immediately in a fallback font then swapping to the webfont, below-fold images loading lazily as they near the viewport, embedded videos shown as a static thumbnail facade with a play button until clicked, and long lists that render only their visible rows.
- **Frame by frame:** One motion pattern is described: a View Transitions navigation — trigger: the user navigates → the browser snapshots the current view → the DOM swaps underneath → the snapshot cross-fades (or a custom animation runs) to the new state as a single GPU-composited step, with no double render and no CLS contribution; elements given the same `view-transition-name` (e.g. a product thumbnail and its hero) morph between the two states. Everything else is static delivery rules.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Starting budgets for a typical content/commerce page: total page weight < 1.5 MB; JavaScript compressed < 300 KB; CSS compressed < 100 KB; above-fold images < 500 KB; fonts < 100 KB; third-party < 200 KB. Server: TTFB < 800ms; Brotli preferred (15–20% smaller than gzip); HTTP/2 or HTTP/3; optional HTTP 103 Early Hints for measured document latency (Cloudflare reported a 20–30% LCP improvement in an artificial image-heavy test — flagged in the skill as a vendor case study, not an expected saving). Images: AVIF for photos (92%+ browser support), WebP fallback (97%+), PNG for transparency, SVG for icons/logos; full `<picture>` srcset pattern (400w/800w/1200w, `sizes="(max-width: 600px) 100vw, 50vw"`); LCP image `fetchpriority="high"`, `loading="eager"`, `decoding="sync"`; below-fold `loading="lazy"`, `decoding="async"`. Fonts: `font-display: swap` (or `optional`), `unicode-range` subsetting (e.g. U+0000-00FF Latin), variable fonts (one file, weight 100–900). Caching: hashed static assets `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`; unhashed `max-age=86400, stale-while-revalidate=604800`; HTML `no-cache, must-revalidate`; API `private, max-age=0`. Runtime: batch DOM reads before writes to avoid layout thrash; debounce scroll/resize (100ms example); `requestAnimationFrame` instead of `setInterval(animate, 16)`; virtualise lists over 100 items with `content-visibility: auto` + `contain-intrinsic-size`. JavaScript: `defer`/`async`/module scripts, route- and component-based code splitting, per-function imports for tree shaking. Third parties: async, delayed until interaction, or loaded via IntersectionObserver when their container approaches; facade pattern for embeds. View Transitions: same-document via `document.startViewTransition()` (Baseline 2026), cross-document via `@view-transition { navigation: auto; }` (Chromium-stable, progressive enhancement elsewhere).
- **Reference / source:** https://github.com/addyosmani/web-quality-skills (performance skill, with its MEASUREMENT.md and RUM.md references). References named: Chrome View Transitions and Speculation Rules documentation, MDN's HTTP 103 example, the Cloudflare Early Hints study.
- **Best for:** Whole-page delivery discipline — heaviest payoff in the hero (image priority, font swap) and in galleries/work sections (lazy loading, facades, virtualisation). Trade fit: the budget table is a practical weight ceiling for media-rich trade homepages.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0281⟧

## ⟦S0282⟧ addyosmani/seo — PART 13 — UI Skills — rest of the ui-skills.com catalog
- **What it is:** A technical and on-page SEO skill based on Lighthouse SEO audits and Google Search guidelines: crawlability, metadata, structured data, mobile and international SEO, plus AI-crawler discoverability.
- **How it looks:** Almost nothing on the page itself changes visually — the results appear in search listings (a descriptive title link and a compelling snippet) and in how completely the site can be crawled. On-page traces a visitor can see: one clear descriptive main heading with a logical heading hierarchy, descriptive link text instead of "click here", breadcrumb navigation, descriptive image filenames and alt text, and mobile pages with a true responsive viewport, body text at 16px with 1.5 line-height, and tap targets at least 48×48px.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** robots.txt must not block rendering resources; meta robots variants (`index, follow`, `noindex`, `max-snippet:150, max-image-preview:large`); self-referencing canonical URLs. XML sitemap: maximum 50,000 URLs or 50MB per sitemap file, sitemap index beyond that, canonical indexable URLs only, honest `lastmod`. URLs: hyphens not underscores, lowercase, short (< 75 characters), keywords natural, HTTPS always. Title tags: 50–60 characters and meta descriptions roughly 150–160 characters are linting proxies only, not pass/fail limits — Google truncates by rendered width and may rewrite title links or pick a different snippet. Structured data: JSON-LD, most specific applicable type, describing visible accurate content only (Organization, Article, Product, FAQ and Breadcrumb examples live in the skill's STRUCTURED-DATA.md reference). Security headers named as trust signals: HSTS `max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`. International: hreflang alternates including `x-default`, `lang` attribute (e.g. `en`, `es-MX`). Agentic browsing kept strictly separate from ranking: Lighthouse checks the accessibility tree, optional `llms.txt` (an experimental proposal, never a ranking factor) and WebMCP registrations; crawler controls are per-product — `OAI-SearchBot` (ChatGPT search), `PerplexityBot`, `Claude-SearchBot`/`Claude-User`, `Google-Extended` (Gemini training/grounding only, no effect on Search), with training crawlers `GPTBot`/`ClaudeBot` distinct from search/fetch crawlers. Audit cadence checklist: critical (HTTPS, robots, no stray noindex, unique titles, descriptive primary heading), high (descriptions, sitemap, canonicals, mobile, Core Web Vitals), medium (structured data, internal linking, alt text, URLs, breadcrumbs).
- **Reference / source:** https://github.com/addyosmani/web-quality-skills (seo skill). References named: Google Search Central, Schema.org, Google's title-link guidance; crawler documentation from OpenAI, Perplexity, Anthropic and Google; tools: Google Search Console, PageSpeed Insights, Rich Results Test, Screaming Frog, Lighthouse.
- **Best for:** The head/metadata layer of every page and the discoverability of towns/areas and service pages; heading and link-text discipline inside hero, work and process copy. Trade fit: local trade sites live on search — the sitemap, canonical and structured-data rules apply directly.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0282⟧

## ⟦S0283⟧ addyosmani/web-quality-audit — PART 13 — UI Skills — rest of the ui-skills.com catalog
- **What it is:** The umbrella audit skill: one evidence-led review covering Performance, Accessibility, SEO, Best Practices and Agentic Browsing, combining live browser evidence with source inspection and refusing to treat an aggregate score as proof of quality.

- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Targets restated: LCP < 2.5s, INP < 200ms, CLS < 0.1; colour contrast minimum 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text (WCAG AA); mobile tap targets ≥ 48px. Tool routing: performance via browser trace + focused insights (Chrome DevTools MCP `performance_start_trace` → `performance_analyze_insight`), explicitly NOT via `lighthouse_audit` (which excludes performance; navigation mode reloads, snapshot mode preserves state); real-user data from CrUX values in trace summaries; accessibility/SEO/best-practices/agentic browsing via live Lighthouse audit with CLI fallbacks; semantics via accessibility-tree snapshots; a bundled `scripts/analyze.sh` static smoke test. Note carried in the skill: Lighthouse 13+ Performance uses shared Performance Insights — follow current insight names, never resurrect removed audit IDs. Severity ladder: Critical (security vulnerabilities, complete failures — fix immediately), High (Core Web Vitals failures, major accessibility barriers — fix before launch), Medium (performance opportunities, SEO improvements — fix within sprint), Low (minor optimisations — when convenient). Cadence: deploy gate (vitals passing, no accessibility or console errors, HTTPS, meta tags), weekly (Search Console, vitals trends, dependencies, screen-reader test), monthly deep dive (full Lighthouse, profiling, accessibility with real users, keyword review).

- **Best for:** The final QA gate on a finished homepage build — one pass that checks the hero's load, every section's accessibility, and the page's metadata together. Trade fit: a repeatable sign-off checklist for client preview pages.

## ⟦S0284⟧ AminBlg/simple-english — PART 13 — UI Skills — rest of the ui-skills.com catalog
- **What it is:** A plain-English writing skill drawn from ASD-STE100, the controlled language aerospace uses for maintenance manuals: write prose a smart reader outside the field understands on one read. It has two registers — the document being written/rewritten, and the chat reply.
- **How it looks:** On the page: short single-topic paragraphs of plain sentences — condition first, then the command ("If the build fails, read the log."); numbered steps with one instruction each; warnings that state the command or condition first and the risk second ("Do not run this against production. The command deletes rows."); no bold lead-ins, no emoji, no decorative formatting; lists only for three or more parallel items, each starting with a capital and holding one instruction. The skill's worked example turns a jargon-dense connection-timeout paragraph into a headed, numbered two-step procedure.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Document rules: procedural text in the imperative, maximum 20 words per sentence, one instruction per sentence; descriptive text in simple tenses, maximum 25 words per sentence, one topic per paragraph, at most six sentences per paragraph. Modals restricted to can, will, must — never should/would/may/might/could (a required "should" becomes "must", an optional one is deleted). No present perfect, no "-ing" verb after a comma, no contractions, no semicolons, no em-dashes; articles and "that" kept; active voice with the actor named. One word, one meaning across the whole document (`make sure that` for check/verify/confirm/validate/ensure; `configuration` for config/settings/options); noun chains over three words broken with a preposition. Terms defined at first use in under ten words; facts and dependencies (host, flag, prior step) named before the step that needs them. Filler banned outright: simply, seamlessly, robust, powerful, comprehensive, leverage, crucial, "in order to", "it is worth noting". Reply register: prose only — no headers, bullets, bold or tables; first sentence gives the answer; concept terms defined in a few words at first use ("idempotent (safe to run twice)"). Modes: Plain (default) and Strict (user names STE/ASD-STE100/compliance → read the strict-vocabulary reference; no tool guarantees compliance). CHECK mode reports each violation as rule number quoted from the 53-rule Issue 9 catalog + offending text + compliant rewrite, never a rule number from memory. The skill states its own limit: these rules are for facts and instructions, not marketing copy, because they delete persuasion.
- **Reference / source:** https://github.com/AminBlg/SimpleEnglish (simple-english skill). Source standard: ASD-STE100 (free download at asd-ste100.org), Issue 9 rule catalog; bundled references: rule-catalog.md, strict-vocabulary.md, word-swaps.md, use-cases.md.
- **Best for:** A clarity pass over instructional copy — form help text, error messages, process/how-it-works steps, FAQ answers. Trade fit: good for the plain-spoken parts of a trade site (what happens next, what a quote visit involves); by its own admission it must not be applied to persuasive hero or sales copy.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0284⟧

Package versions checked with `fast-npm-meta` instead of `npm view`. TypeScript config: target/module ESNext, moduleResolution bundler, strict, esModuleInterop, skipLibCheck, resolveJsonModule, isolatedModules, noEmit. Knip catches unused files/exports/dependencies — fix by deleting, not by allowlisting. Every project exposes one `ci` script chaining lint && typecheck && knip && test; run `nr lint --fix` then `nr ci` before every commit and never commit on a failing gate. Git hooks: simple-git-hooks + nano-staged, pre-commit runs the full ci gate; `prepare` also installs agent skills via skills-npm. Testing with Vitest: `foo.ts` → `foo.test.ts` beside it, `describe`/`it` API, `toMatchSnapshot` / `toMatchFileSnapshot`. pnpm catalogs for versions, named prod / inlined / dev / frontend, never the default catalog. Publishing: npm Trusted Publishing (OIDC) over NPM_TOKEN secrets, `bumpp`-driven `nr release` from `v*` tags.

## ⟦S0286⟧ antfu/antfu-design — PART 13 — UI Skills — rest of the ui-skills.com catalog
- **What it is:** A usage skill for `@antfu/design`, Anthony Fu's shared design layer for devtools-style Vue 3 apps: a composable UnoCSS preset, a semantic token vocabulary, token-driven Vue primitives, and a colour-contrast accessibility check.
- **How it looks:** Dense, quiet devtools UI that survives light/dark switching without a single hard-coded colour: surfaces and text come from semantic classes (`bg-base`, `color-base`, `color-muted`, `border-base`, `op-fade`); counts, sizes, durations and dates render in tabular monospace via display components; statuses and tags are badges coloured by hash or palette; file paths truncate with dimmed directories; severity (fresh→stale, fast→slow, small→large) reads as a colour-scale ramp rather than ad-hoc red/green.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. The skill text prescribes no durations or easings; overlay components (modal, drawer, tooltip, dropdown) are named, but their motion values live in the package, not in the skill body.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Three standing rules: (1) own the tokens, not the colours — never hard-code a hex or raw Tailwind colour in app UI; (2) light/dark parity is automatic if tokens are used, and the standing contrast scan (`@antfu/design/a11y`) catches the worst violations; (3) no slop — technical values in `font-mono tabular-nums`, an em-dash ban in UI copy, one obvious affordance over three competing ones. Rule 4: reuse package components before building new ones, and persist that instruction into the consuming project's AGENTS.md. Components are prefixed by category — Display*, Form*, Overlay*, Layout*, Action*, Feedback* — and chosen by job: a count/size/duration/date → DisplayNumber / DisplayBytes / DisplayDuration / DisplayDate; a status or tag → DisplayBadge or DisplayLabel; a path → DisplayFilePath; an overlay → OverlayModal / OverlayDrawer (reka-ui), a popover → OverlayTooltip / OverlayDropdown; a severity → the `color-scale-*` ramp via a `colorize` prop. The package ships no dark toggle: dark mode is the app's own, components that vary take a `colorScheme: 'light' | 'dark'` prop; a toggle is composed from ActionIconButton + VueUse `useDark`. Setup is a single preset (`presetAnthonyDesign`) that bundles no base preset, icons, fonts or reset — the app adds those.
- **Reference / source:** https://github.com/antfu/design (antfu-design skill). Built on UnoCSS and reka-ui; bundled references: core-setup.md, core-tokens.md, core-components.md, recipes.md, best-practices.md, features-data-presentation.md, advanced-patterns.md, storybook.md.
- **Best for:** Devtools and admin interfaces, not marketing pages. Transferable discipline for trade builds: semantic token roles with automatic dark parity, tabular mono for numbers (prices, ratings, counts in proof sections), and severity-as-ramp instead of traffic-light colours.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0286⟧

## ⟦S0296⟧ anthropics/pdf — PART 13 — UI Skills — rest of the ui-skills.com catalog
- **What it is:** A complete PDF processing skill from Anthropic: read and extract text/tables, merge, split, rotate, watermark, create, encrypt/decrypt, extract images, OCR scanned PDFs, and fill PDF forms — via Python libraries and command-line tools, with JavaScript libraries in its reference file.
- **How it looks:** The output is PDF documents, not web pages: generated pages on a letter-size canvas with drawn text and rules (reportlab), multi-page reports assembled from title/body paragraphs with spacers and page breaks (Platypus), tables exported to Excel, watermark pages merged over every page of a document, and form PDFs returned filled — either through real form fields or through text annotations placed at measured coordinates on the page image.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Tool choice per task is tabulated in the skill: merge/split with pypdf (`writer.add_page(page)`), text with pdfplumber (`page.extract_text()`), tables with pdfplumber (`page.extract_tables()`, convertible to pandas DataFrames and Excel), creation with reportlab, CLI merge with qpdf, OCR with pytesseract after pdf2image conversion. Concrete values in the text: page rotation in 90° steps (`page.rotate(90)`, qpdf `--rotate=+90:1`); qpdf page ranges (`--pages . 1-5 --`, `--split-pages=3` for groups of three), linearize for web streaming, 256-bit encryption with print/modify permission flags; pdftotext flags `-layout`, `-f 1 -l 5`, and `-bbox-layout` for coordinate XML (named the fastest plain-text route); pdfplumber debugging via `page.to_image(resolution=150)` and custom table settings (snap_tolerance 3, intersection_tolerance 15); pypdfium2 rendering at scale 2.0 for pages, 1.5 in batch loops, 3.0 for figure extraction, JPEG quality 90; performance guidance to chunk large PDFs 10 pages at a time and prefer `pdfimages` over rendering for image extraction. Hard rule stated: never use Unicode subscript/superscript characters in reportlab PDFs (built-in fonts lack the glyphs and they render as solid black boxes) — use `<sub>`/`<super>` markup in Paragraphs instead. Form filling is a strict ordered workflow in its forms.md reference: run `check_fillable_fields` first; for fillable forms extract field info (field_id, page, rect in PDF coordinates with y=0 at the bottom, type, checkbox checked/unchecked values, radio/choice options), convert pages to PNGs, write `field_values.json`, run the fill script and fix any validation errors; for non-fillable forms extract structure (labels, lines, checkboxes, row boundaries) and use those PDF coordinates, falling back to visual estimation with ImageMagick zoom crops (`magick <page> -crop WxH+X+Y +repage`), always validating with `check_bounding_boxes.py` before filling and re-rendering the output to verify placement. Licences noted: pypdf BSD, pdfplumber MIT, pypdfium2 Apache/BSD, reportlab BSD, poppler-utils GPL-2, qpdf Apache, pdf-lib MIT, pdfjs-dist Apache.
- **Reference / source:** https://github.com/anthropics/skills (pdf skill, with its forms.md and reference.md). Libraries named: pypdf, pdfplumber, reportlab, pypdfium2, pytesseract, pdf2image, poppler-utils (pdftotext, pdftoppm, pdfimages), qpdf, pdftk, pdf-lib, pdfjs-dist (rendered at viewport scale 1.5 in its example).

## ⟦S0297⟧ arifszn/slide-wright — PART 13 — UI Skills — rest of the ui-skills.com catalog
- **What it is:** A presentation builder: it turns a topic, rough notes or an outline into a boardroom-grade slide deck delivered as a single self-contained HTML file that runs in any browser, and it edits decks afterwards (add, remove or revise slides).
- **How it looks:** A full-screen slide deck with a theme invented for that one deck — its colours live in `:root` variables and its fonts in a `<link>` — slides that read like a strategy/product team's work, each content slide carrying a chosen visual exhibit rather than walls of bullets. The build always starts as a two-slide preview in the proposed theme so the look can be judged before the full deck exists.
- **Frame by frame:** Navigation is step-by-step: the viewer presses arrow keys or space, or swipes, and the deck advances one slide at a time; **F** toggles fullscreen, **Esc**/**O** opens the slide overview grid, **S** opens the speaker view with notes. The skill body prescribes no transition durations or easings — animation recipes live in its motion-recipes.md reference, read only when the user asks for animation.
- **Mechanism & key values:** The defining rule: propose the look before building — generate a theme, build a two-slide preview, stop for the user's approval, and only then build the rest; one proposal at a time, never a menu; a rejected direction is thrown out for a clearly different one; every theme is invented for the deck in front of it, with no library of presets. Decks render with reveal.js loaded from a CDN (an internal implementation detail — the library name appears only inside the generated link/script tags and is never mentioned to the user). Editing path: if an existing HTML deck is built on reveal.js, keep its theme and edit in place, skipping the proposal gate; after editing, run `node <skill-dir>/scripts/check-deck.mjs <deck.html>` and fix every line it prints; a non-reveal.js HTML deck is outside the edit path and is declined rather than rewritten. Handoff: state where the deck lives, the theme name and the slide count, explain the driving keys, and offer PDF export (add `?print-pdf` to the URL and print), PowerPoint export with editable text, revision, re-theme, or deployment to a live URL (Surge, Vercel or Netlify — the user picks the host). Reference files are read as reached, not all at once: new-deck.md (the four steps and the approval gate), design-aesthetics.md, theme-generation.md, deck-template.md, exhibits.md, code-slides.md, motion-recipes.md, media.md, export-pdf.md, export-pptx.md, deploy.md.
- **Reference / source:** https://github.com/arifszn/slide-wright (slide-wright skill). Engine named (internally): reveal.js via CDN. Deploy hosts named: Surge, Vercel, Netlify.
- **Best for:** Pitch decks, talk decks and presentation versions of a proposal — the closest cousin in this range to a homepage job is a sales deck for a trade firm. Trade fit: the propose-two-slides-then-build gate is the same proof-first discipline used for homepage sections.

## ⟦S0298⟧ arla6ka/build-design-system — PART 13 — UI Skills — rest of the ui-skills.com catalog
- **What it is:** An eight-step process skill for building a design system out of the UI an app already ships: inventory the existing surfaces, cluster their raw values into named tokens, rebuild the component families, add automated checks, and prove the system on one pilot flow before any wider migration.
- **How it looks:** The app itself does not change visually — that is the point. Every surface is photographed before and after at the narrowest and widest supported widths (390 and 1280 by default) and the pixel diff must read 0% at tolerance 0 for every surface a token swap touched. The only sanctioned visible difference is a decided one (a merge inside tolerance, or an added semantic such as a name, a role or `aria-current`); anything else is a defect.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion values are prescribed in the skill body; motion presets live in its references/tokens.md. The one behaviour rule with a visible state sequence: a saving button keeps its idle label, a spinner appears inside the same box, and `aria-busy` is set — the label never swaps to "Saving...".
- **Mechanism & key values:** Steps: (1) Frame — write the complaint in the person's words, the first visible change that answers it, and the pilot flow; record unanswered questions as `default (unanswered)` and proceed; keep all run notes under `.design-system/`, excluded from commits via `.git/info/exclude`. (2) Inventory and baselines — count raw values in occurrences (`#fff`, `text-gray-500`, `p-[13px]`) with `scripts/check-system.mjs --no-allowlist --no-self-test --json`; capture every surface in every state at both widths with `scripts/capture.mjs`, which refuses to start without a `--writes` list (or `--no-backend`) and proves each app write is blocked before the browser opens; delete what nothing uses in its own commit. (3) Tokens — cluster raw values by role and name by purpose; colour merges inside delta E OK 2 and spacing merges inside 2px are decisions, past tolerance each cluster opens one gate whose default is the merge; border width, weight and easing have no tolerance. (4) Components — build the most-used family end to end first; the text primitive and small-text primitive ship in wave 1 beside Button; every canonical component gets a registry row, a doc, and captured disabled/required/error/long-text states shown to the person before fan-out. (5) Checks — a rule counts only once it has been seen failing: plant one violation, watch the check exit 1 naming the rule, delete the plant; the allowlist and ratchet only shrink; a ban ships with its check rule in the same change. (6) Pilot — move the pilot flow with a codemod read hunk by hunk, recapture with the identical command changing only `--kind after`, pixdiff the two folders, walk the flow by keyboard and force its error and loading states. (7) Readiness — five audits must hold or carry a recorded exemption: slot and prop parity, behaviour contracts (a "what fires when" table per interactive primitive, each row a test), tone parity (every pressable/row primitive crossed with every status tone plus muted), pinned strings (every legacy test query has a default name on the new primitive), and hardest screens (one hardest call site per family rendered in the showcase with a screenshot). (8) Handoff — rerun the counts, report coverage in numbers with the producing command named, unanswered defaults first; offer the migration with its size, never start it. Never list: no push/publish/deploy unasked, no committing on the starting branch, no stash or dirty-checkout branch switch (use a worktree), no deleting anything another package or a public API exports, no silent skipped steps, and never call your own work "verified" (mark self-checks `self-verified`).
- **Reference / source:** https://github.com/arla6ka/skills (build-design-system skill). Sibling skills named: token-mapping, component-docs, migrate-design-system, ui-review. Tooling named: Playwright + Chromium, the skill's own capture.mjs / capture-guard.mjs / pixdiff.mjs / check-system.mjs / oklch.mjs scripts.
- **Best for:** Extracting a token/component system from an existing app without changing how it looks. Trade fit: process discipline only — its baseline-capture and zero-diff proof method transfers to redesign QA, but it builds no homepage sections.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0298⟧

## ⟦S0299⟧ arla6ka/component-docs — PART 13 — UI Skills — rest of the ui-skills.com catalog
- **What it is:** A documentation skill that writes one component's doc entry strictly from its code, stories and real call sites — variants, props, states, tokens and usage rules, with every gap marked instead of filled.
- **How it looks:** A single Markdown entry under `docs/system/<name>.md` (with a draft comment on line 1): nine fixed headings in the order given by its doc-format reference, followed by Sources, Conflicts, Guessed at, and Gates sections. A section with nothing sourced reads `Not applicable: <reason>` rather than being padded; a behaviour that looks like a bug is documented as it is, with a `Defect:` line to the owner naming what goes wrong for the user and the smallest fix.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Seven steps: paste the nine headings in empty; find the component and record code, props type, styles and stories each as a Sources line; find two real uses by call-site search or from the ask; trace which source gave each example, variant, prop, state and token, logging every disagreement under Conflicts with the quoted rule that settles it (or "no rule, not chosen"); fill sections copying token names and example code character for character; write Usage rules last; fill Guessed at with one line per judgement call. Each usage rule is formatted `rule/<component>-<slug>` with a condition, an action, a reason, its evidence (two call sites, a measurement with its path, a named principle, or the person's words) and a `Don't:` line with real code that breaks it — a rule that cannot be broken with a snippet is cut. Stop table: no code → stop (nothing sources the variants); no variant list in the props type or stories → stop (a guessed list documents a different component); no use, real or planned → stop (invented uses read like real ones and get copied first). A props type with no variant prop is not a stop: Variants reads "None". One real use, planned uses and a deprecated predecessor are marked as such. Compound components (Tabs with Tab) are one entry; a part also used alone gets a `### Parts` subsection. Counts in the reply come from `grep -o` on the saved file. The skill does not judge the design, publishes nothing, and never edits the code, stories or spec being documented.
- **Reference / source:** https://github.com/arla6ka/skills (component-docs skill, with its references/doc-format.md holding the nine headings and a worked example). Sibling named: build-design-system.
- **Best for:** Documenting individual components inside a design-system effort. Trade fit: none for homepage design; a documentation discipline reference only.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0299⟧

## ⟦S0300⟧ arla6ka/design-system-boss — PART 13 — UI Skills — rest of the ui-skills.com catalog
- **What it is:** A router skill for vague whole-app design-system asks: it reads the app, matches exactly one playbook from its trigger table, copies that playbook's steps word for word into `.design-system/state.md`, and runs them — coordinating the sibling skills rather than doing their work itself.
- **How it looks:** No visual output. Its artefacts are run files: `.design-system/state.md` (the playbook steps, with any dropped step kept in the list as `skipped (<reason>)`), `roles.md`, an append-only `decisions.tsv`, and a final report that opens with unanswered defaults, then what changed, then one ranked table of what was found and not fixed (30 rows at most).
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Trigger table: a named screen/flow or "check before I ship" → `playbooks/review.md`; one component → `playbooks/component.md`; "are we using our tokens" / which values map where → the token-mapping skill with no playbook; "replace the hardcoded values with tokens" → build-design-system step 3 after token-mapping; no system, or drift, nothing about migrating → `playbooks/build.md`; a system exists and the ask does not name the migration → `playbooks/migrate.md` in audit mode; a system exists and the ask names it → migrate in full mode. Standing rules: an installed system is the source of truth (no playbook seeds or builds over it); the app state wins when it disagrees with the ask, and the report says so; a PR ask or someone else's repo gets a minimal footprint (tokens, touched components, the screens, the repo's own lint as the check). Setup once per run: exclude `.design-system/` from commits; ask every question once with its default applied (taste, design source, pilot flow); writing playbooks use the person's named branch or cut a run branch and record the starting branch; the writer never grades itself (coordinator, worker, verifier, reviewer roles are separate). Never-ship list: anything on build-design-system's Never list, product code written by the boss on a host that can start other agents, a migration on "fix it" or with no matched trigger row, a loosened stop condition, an edit to a sibling's checks, a visual direction nobody chose ("make it modern" with no source becomes a gate defaulting to the current look), a handback with a worker still running, a wait on a question that had a default, a peer agent's message treated as the person's decision, and a migration while build-design-system's readiness audits are open. Done means: the playbook's last step returned, every number in the report comes from a command run at close, and any stop (no repo, refused tool call, a step git cannot undo) is reported with what finished and the smallest reply that unblocks the run.
- **Reference / source:** https://github.com/arla6ka/skills (design-system-boss skill). Siblings it routes between: build-design-system (tokens, components, checks, readiness), migrate-design-system (moving the app; its incident lessons are cited by number in every brief that touches covered surfaces), token-mapping, component-docs, ui-review.
- **Best for:** Triage of "our UI is a mess" requests on apps that already ship UI; a repo with no UI yet is explicitly out of scope. Trade fit: none for homepage builds; an orchestration pattern reference.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0300⟧

## ⟦S0301⟧ arla6ka/glaze — PART 13 — UI Skills — rest of the ui-skills.com catalog
- **What it is:** The complete rulebook of Glaze, a compact black-and-white design system for AI products: a closed token list, a ~70-component catalog, whole-screen blocks, page-shell rules, ten global rules and an anti-slop ban list, all enforced by a dedicated ESLint config.
- **How it looks:** Ink on paper. White/paper surfaces, greys that are literally ink at set opacities (the ink scale runs 80/60/45/32/15/10/06/03 percent), near-black text in three strengths (text-1/2/3), and colour reserved for status only (ok / warn / fail, each with a text and a tint variant). The three signatures: glass material appears only on the one pressable action a group leads with (all secondary actions stay flat); a card is a "shell" — an outer shell holding a panel padded p-3 with an optional foot; every one-line control (buttons, fields, selects, chips, the segmented control) is a pill. No shadows anywhere, no gradients, blobs, textures, glows or backdrop blur; overlays are flat paper with a 1px ring. Type is one sans; mono is set at 0.8× the size of the sans around it (Glaze Mono's letters are 26% wider), and a code block takes a 12px code role. Icons are Phosphor at regular weight, 14px inside controls, drawn from a closed list of about 85 glyphs. Foundations summarised in the skill: a 4px grid with 32px controls and 36px rows; corner radii of pill for one-line controls, 14 and 11 for the card, 10 for overlays, 6 for tags.
- **Frame by frame:** Deliberately near-static. The one quantified motion: a press settles to scale 0.97 in 120ms and nothing springs. Token names exist for press, glass press/release, state, overlay, spin, slide and sweep durations plus wait/stale timings, but their numeric values live in the token files, not the skill body. Explicitly banned motion: no blinking cursor, shimmer sweep or word-by-word fade on streamed answers, and no fade/slide scroll reveals — content is simply present.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Scope rule: all styles and tokens apply only inside an element with the `glaze` class, with `GlazePortalProvider` inside it so menus, dialogs, popovers and toasts (which render at the end of `<body>`) keep the tokens; dark mode is `data-theme="dark"` on the glaze element or an ancestor and does not follow `prefers-color-scheme` by itself. Priority order when rules conflict: accessibility/keyboard behaviour > tokens by role, never raw values > existing components/recipes, never rebuilt > the three signatures > compact spacing and type. Global rules with numbers: at most one primary (glass) button per card, footer, dialog or action group; a 2px ink `:focus-visible` ring on every control, never `outline: none`, with fields showing focus by darkening their line; sentence case with verb-plus-object action labels ("Run eval", not "OK"); no emoji, no em dash. Page shell: root `<div className="glaze min-h-dvh bg-page text-text-1">`; card footer is meta first with `me-auto`, then small flat secondaries, then at most one primary; one `type-title` h1 per page; a phone moment is a component at `w-full max-w-sm` sized to its content. Token families are a closed list — surfaces, ink, text, lines, status, glass (20 tokens readable only through classes/components), flat (4), switch, small-glaze, type roles, a space scale (0.5–10), control sizes, radii, motion, layers (raised/sticky/overlay), layout widths (overlay-sm/overlay/overlay-lg, popover, toast, menu, tooltip, measure) and scrollbar; referencing a token by raw value is a lint error. The component catalog runs Actions (Button, Toolbar, Copy button, Button group), Inputs (Field, Input, Textarea, Chip, Date picker, Number input, OTP input), Selection (Checkbox, Radio group, Switch, Slider, Segmented control, Select, Combobox), Display (Kbd, Card, Panel, Badge, Avatar, Item, Data list, Truncate, Relative time), Feedback (Status, Skeleton, Progress, Empty state, Alert, Toast), Overlays (Dialog, Sheet, Popover, Tooltip, Dropdown menu, Command), Navigation (Tabs, Breadcrumb, Steps, Pagination), Layout (Collapsible), Data (Filter bar, Table, Data grid, Bulk action bar, Timeline), Code (Code block, JSON view, Log viewer), Media/charts (Attachment, Chart) and AI (Prompt input, Send button, Mention, Message, Conversation, Response, Reasoning, Tool call, Activity, Follow-ups, Action receipt, Autonomy rule) — plus 11 installable blocks (Today, Voice capture, Note recap, Booking approval, Assistant limits, Conversation insights, Cited answer, Agent plan, Agent procedure, Simulations, Experiment), each fetched from design.how before use and installed via `npx shadcn@latest add https://design.how/r/glaze/<name>.json`. Review loop: run the lint (`npx eslint -c glaze.eslint.config.mjs .`), render at 390 and 1280 wide, check the global rules and anti-slop list, fix the worst defect, check again. ## ⟦S0302⟧ arla6ka/lime — PART 13 — UI Skills — rest of the ui-skills.com catalog
- **What it is:** The complete rulebook of Lime, a design system for consumer apps: a white page, warm-grey surfaces and near-black text with exactly one acid-lime accent reserved for the main action — plus money-specific UX rules (assistant payments need approval first and a receipt with Undo after), a closed token list, a ~55-component catalog, blocks and an anti-slop list.
- **How it looks:** Bright and quiet: a white page (`bg-page`), warm-grey cards and surfaces in three steps (surface / surface-2 / surface-3) plus a raised tone, near-black text in three strengths (fg / fg-2 / fg-3), hairlines (line, line-strong), and a single glowing lime primary button per view — every other action solid ink, secondary, outline or ghost. Lime never fills a page, card or section, and text on lime is the dark `--on-accent`, never white. Glow is rationed to primary and destructive buttons, the balance chip and one featured card. Amounts always render through the Amount component or `formatAmount` — sign, currency and tabular figures intact. Headings are real headings in sentence case; icons are one Carbon set, drawn in the text colour.
- **Frame by frame:** Static by rule — content never fades, slides or scales in on scroll, streamed text arrives as it is with no blinking cursor or shimmer, and no animation loops except the spinner. Motion tokens exist (durations instant/fast/base/slow/spin, ease-out and ease-in, scale-enter and scale-press) but their numeric values live in the token files, not the skill body; dialogs, sheets and alert dialogs stay mounted and controlled (`open` + `onOpenChange`) so their exit motion and focus return work.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Scope: tokens apply only inside the `lime` class with `LimePortalProvider` inside it; dark mode is `data-theme="dark"` on the lime element or an ancestor, never automatic from `prefers-color-scheme`. Priority order: accessibility/keyboard > tokens by role, never raw values > existing components, never rebuilt > spacing/radius/type scales > polish. Page shell numbers: a one-task flow (send, pay) sits in `main` at `max-w-md px-4 pt-4 pb-8` (sm: px-6 pt-8); home/activity/settings use the same main at `max-w-2xl`; a wide table at `max-w-5xl`; the sticky header is `h-14` and gains a `border-b border-line` only once content scrolls under it; the page title is one h1 at `text-xl leading-tight font-semibold tracking-tight` (sm: text-2xl); sections are `flex flex-col gap-8` apart, each led by an h2 at `text-lg font-semibold` with inner `gap-3`; forms stack fields at `gap-4` within `max-w-md`, submit last at `size="lg"` and full width on a phone; a phone flow's main action sticks to the bottom (`sticky bottom-0 bg-page pt-3 pb-4`) with the safe-area inset under a home bar. Global rules with teeth: one lime primary per view; every input wrapped in a Field with a label above it (a placeholder is never a label); every control keyboard-operable with a 2px olive `:focus-visible` ring, never `outline: none`; section names are real h2s, never a small grey label above content; sentence case, verb-plus-object labels, no emoji, no em dash, no title case. Money rules: the assistant shows an ApprovalRequest before moving money and an ActionReceipt with Undo after; a person paying gets a review step, then "Payment done" with Undo. Coverage gaps are specified as stand-ins, not inventions: bottom navigation is a fixed `bg-page` nav with `border-t border-line`, 3–5 links each an Icon at 20px over a text-xs label, at least 56px tall, the current one marked `aria-current="page"` in fg and the rest fg-3; the date picker is a native `type="date"` input in a Field; charts stop at the Insight sparkline or figures in a List. Anti-slop bans include: no eyebrow labels or "01" numbers above titles, no rows of equal stat cards (show one Balance, a List, or a sentence), cards only around one actionable thing and never nested, no icon tiles, no coloured side rails (a chosen row takes `--accent-wash`), no decoration or extra glow, sentences a person must read never set in text-xs or fg-3, peer amounts at one size and weight, no capitals or letter-spacing, no hype words (instant, secure, effortless, seamless, invented urgency), no emoji, believable example data only (real-looking names, amounts with cents, dates near today — never Lorem ipsum, John Doe or $1,234.56), and never flatten a screen to grey — keep the one glowing action. Reject list: no blue, no second brand hue, no gradient behind content, no coloured shadows, no second icon set, no weight 700, no `transition: all`. Components span Actions (Button with Spinner, Copy button), Inputs (Input, Textarea, Field, Select, Combobox, Dropzone, Keypad), Selection (Checkbox, Radio, Switch, Slider, Segmented, Chip), Display (Badge, Avatar, Card, Table, List, Progress, Amount, Bill schedule, Balance), Feedback (Status, Empty, Skeleton, Error state, Toast), Overlays (Dialog, Alert dialog, Sheet, Popover, Dropdown menu, Tooltip), Navigation (Tabs, Toolbar), Layout (Accordion, Separator, Scroll area) and Assistant (Chat input, Message, Tool call, Follow ups, Approval request, Action receipt, Autonomy rule, Receipt match, Insight); five blocks install whole screens (Home screen, Assistant approval, Assistant alert, Settings rules, Split request) via `npx shadcn@latest add https://design.how/r/lime/<name>.json`. Review loop: lint with `lime.eslint.config.mjs`, render at 390 and 1280, check global rules and anti-slop, fix the worst defect, check again.
- **Reference / source:** https://github.com/arla6ka/skills (systems/lime skill). System home named throughout: design.how — component pages at design.how/systems/lime/components/<name>.md, foundations at design.how/systems/lime/foundations/*.md, registry installs at design.how/r/lime/. Icon set named: Carbon.
- **Best for:** Consumer app interfaces, especially money flows. Trade fit: not a homepage system, but two disciplines transfer — exactly one loud action per view (the call/CTA rule) and approval-then-receipt-with-undo as the pattern for any quote or booking confirmation flow.
