## ⟦S0303⟧ arla6ka/migrate-design-system — PART 13 — UI Skills — rest of the ui-skills.com catalog
- **What it is:** A process skill for moving an app that already ships UI onto an existing design system: audit first, baseline every surface, migrate a pilot by hand, turn the pilot into a codemod, fan out surface by surface with independent verification, then delete the legacy code.
- **How it looks:** The migration's promise is that nothing looks different except announced fixes: every surface, state, width and theme is captured before the first edit (with fixture data and a frozen clock, plus a no-change control capture) and recaptured at the final commit, and parity is judged from those captures. A baseline that itself looks wrong is kept as captured and becomes a gate — the default is to keep it and fix the bug it shows as a listed intended change.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Two modes: audit mode is the default and writes only under `.design-system/` (excluded from commits), cuts no branch, commits nothing, and ends with the inventory, the plan and an offer of the full run with its size; full mode starts only when the ask names the migration or the person accepts the offer with a budget (`Go, <budget>`) — "clean it up" and "fix it" are not clearance. Nine steps: (1) Roles — coordinator, worker, verifier, reviewer recorded in `.design-system/roles.md` (the writer never grades itself; the verifier is a different agent, on another model family where the host has one); decisions logged as append-only rows (`time, phase, decision, why, evidence pointer, result`) where evidence is a sha, a path or a command, never prose, and a wrong call gets a superseding row, never an edit. (2) Readiness — build-design-system's five audits must pass; every open backlog row is checked against the code first because rows go stale; no fan-out while a text or control primitive is missing, a gap is open, or the system's own check is red. (3) Inventory — `legacy.mjs --init-config` pointed at the real legacy and system modules, then `--inventory`, which exits 2 while a placeholder remains or no file was scanned; in full mode the script and config are copied into the repo's `scripts/` and the baseline recorded in its own commit. (4) Baselines — the capture tool refuses to start without `--writes <file>`, and with it until every listed write is seen blocked. (5) Shared layer first — one agent alone lands layout and providers; then the pilot surface is migrated by hand with a verifier, the codemod is written from that hand work, its output diffed against the hand work, and it is run twice — the second run must change nothing — before any fan-out. (6) Fan out — a rolling window, one surface per worker, each brief carrying a MAY EDIT list; a retry goes to a fresh worker with the brief, every later directive and the prior verdict. (7) Land — one commit per verified surface through `land.mjs`; a surface whose diff touches write lines lands with `--bodies-check`. (8) Delete legacy — a module with zero callers goes in one change with its adapter and allowlist rows, and the ratchet bans its path; a module another package or a public API exports stops the delete and becomes a gate. (9) Close — recapture everything at the final commit (only verdicts at that commit count), a read-only reviewer audits the diff's comments and the decisions log, and the correction pass runs. Done when `legacy.mjs --zero` exits 0 at the final commit, every remaining raw/palette row is a listed exception, every surface holds a `verified` verdict at that commit, and the system's check exits 0. Worker brief format is fixed: SURFACE (id, name, sha), MAY EDIT paths, KEEP behaviours, LESSONS numbers from its incident-backed lessons file, STANDING preferences word for word, BANS (git push, `sed -i`, `pkill`, `git add -A`, git stash, merge or checkout in the shared tree, `git reset --hard`), SCRATCH under `.design-system/tmp/<worker id>/`, and a RETURN verdict file written before the final message. Verification matches risk: a visual-only change gets unit tests, typecheck, the system check and one before/after capture pair; a write surface gets every width and theme plus request-body equality. A bug in a primitive's contract is fixed in the primitive with every caller found — patching one caller leaves the rest broken, and "legacy did it too" never keeps a data bug. A missing primitive parks the surface as `blocked-on <gap>` with the file restored to HEAD.
- **Reference / source:** https://github.com/arla6ka/skills (migrate-design-system skill). Siblings named: build-design-system (readiness audits, capture.mjs, pixdiff.mjs, capture-guard.mjs, glossary and taste references), token-mapping, component-docs; its own references: lessons.md (eight incident-backed lessons, cited by number), parity.md, running-many-agents.md, correct.md.
- **Best for:** Planned rollouts of an existing system across a whole app, and adoption audits. Trade fit: none for homepage design; its baseline/parity method is a QA pattern for redesigns.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0303⟧

## ⟦S0304⟧ arla6ka/quartz — PART 13 — UI Skills — rest of the ui-skills.com catalog
- **What it is:** The complete rulebook of Quartz, a design system for AI support products and agent consoles: a black-and-white chassis where five muted kind hues name categories as words, amber and red are reserved for trouble, and status is always written out — backed by a closed token list, a ~70-component catalog, whole-screen blocks and an anti-slop list of some 26 bans.
- **How it looks:** Flat ink-and-paper console UI: white working cards on grey fields, containers separated by grey fields rather than stacked hairlines, no shadows on anything flat (only overlays get a shadow), no gradients, glass, pills on labels, or side bars. A thing's kind is a tinted word — a `<Badge kind="agent"/>` — never a coloured region, header or icon tile. Status reads as a word (idle, queued, running, waiting, ok, warn, fail) with colour only on warn and fail. Type is one sans in a full role scale (display sizes down through heading, body, label, tag and stat roles); mono appears only on things a person copies — code, commands, paths, IDs, keys, hashes — while numbers take a data utility. Corners run from square marks through 6px controls to 10px frames; spacing steps are 4px. Pages sit in a sidebar shell: a sidebar the width of the `--sidebar` token (a sheet under 768px), a sticky top bar holding the sidebar trigger and a breadcrumb — the h1 never lives in the top bar, it sits in the page header with its status in the description. Icons are Font Awesome Free Classic Solid from a closed list of about 140 glyphs, used only for actions found by shape.
- **Frame by frame:** Near-static by rule: no pulse, ping, bounce, glow, sweep, shimmer text or decorative motion; a running status is a single small turning arc, and only the running tool row in a turn shows it. Motion tokens exist (press/fast/base/slow/spin/run/slide durations, a press scale, skeleton step/delay/hold timings, and toast reading-time tokens scaled by base + per-character + action with min/max clamps) but their numeric values live in the token files, not the skill body. Skeletons hold the shape of loading content in steps; a toast stays for a reading time computed from its length, then leaves.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Scope: the `quartz` class goes on `<body>` once in the root layout with `QuartzPortalProvider` inside it (a wrapper div is explicitly wrong, because the class carries every token and the font); dark mode is `data-theme="dark"` or a `dark` class on the quartz element or any ancestor, never automatic from `prefers-color-scheme`. Priority order: accessibility/keyboard > tokens, never raw values > existing components, never rebuilt > layout and spacing scale > polish (motion, radius, details). Global rules with teeth: a kind is named with `<Badge kind/>` or `data-kind` and hue never fills a region; amber/red only for warn and fail; props are named by the question they answer (status, orientation, layout, placement; variant only for a Button and a menu item's intent); every control keyboard-operable with a visible focus ring and an accessible name (icon buttons take an `aria-label`); sentence case with verb-plus-object labels ("Create key", not "Submit"); stop and say so when a component or token is missing — never invent one. Agent-safety rule: before a destructive or irreversible action the agent stops at a ToolCall awaiting permission with Deny and Allow; typed confirmation is saved for deleting for good a thing that holds others, such as a project. AI turns are built inside Conversation from AgentTurn, ToolCallList, Response and ConversationTail, with PromptQueue above PromptInput, so a turn never shows two spinners or two status phrases. Page shell measurements: list pages (runs, keys, agents) sit in a container of `max-w-(--container)` with `gap-6` and `py-6`; a docked detail Sheet (`modal={false}`, `stackBelow="3xl"`) takes the full width under the list in a narrow container; a full-height chat/run view pins its composer in a `max-w-3xl` column with the conversation flexing above it. Token families are closed: ink and paper (6 tokens via classes only), category hues (30 via classes only), reserved warn/fail hues with named mark/field/wash/line/text tokens, type families/weights/roles, a space scale (0.5–30), layout tokens (container, sidebar, topbar, gutters, control sizes, overlay widths, row heights, label column, measure), radii (0 / inner / soft / frame / full), line tokens, motion tokens, layers (raised/above/cover/drop/overlay), code colours, surfaces, text, borders, elevation, an accent slot, button (18 via classes only) and chart tokens. Components span Actions (Button with pressed and pending states that keep the label, Button group with split menu, Copy button), Inputs (Input with text/password/secret/copy/search/number/OTP variants, Textarea, Field + Form, Date picker, Combobox), Selection (Checkbox, Radio group, Switch, Slider, Select, Segmented control for two to five views), Display (Badge, Chip, Status, Stat, Avatar, Kbd, Relative time — shown as "3m ago" with the exact time on hover and focus, Truncate, Item, Card, Panel, Data list), Feedback (Alert, Toast, Empty state, Skeleton, Progress as bar/ring/steps/meter), Overlays (Dialog with alert and typed-confirm variants, Sheet, Popover, Tooltip, Dropdown menu, Command), Navigation (Tabs including closable/reorderable document tabs, Breadcrumb, Pagination), Layout (Collapsible), Data (Table with sort/selection/virtualisation, Filter bar, Timeline, Data grid with spreadsheet cell editing and paste), Code (Code block, JSON view, Log viewer) and Media/AI (Attachment, Chart with frame states/legend/tooltip/data table built in, Message, Conversation that stays pinned to the bottom until the person scrolls, Response, Reasoning — open while it streams, folded when done, Tool call, Activity, Prompt input with mentions, slash commands and voice). Seven blocks install whole screens (Workspace home, Agent session, Tool approval, API keys, Prompt release, Run trace, Live activity) via `npx shadcn@latest add https://design.how/r/quartz/<name>.json`. Coverage gaps specify stand-ins: attachments ride above the message bubble in an AttachmentGroup, a failed run's retry is a small secondary button naming the run ("Rerun refund-eval"), and durations are formatted in milliseconds except Reasoning, which takes seconds. Anti-slop bans include: no capitals or tracked-out text, no em dash for a pause or an empty value (write None), no middle-dot fact joining, no eyebrow labels, no side rails, no three-equal-icon-card stat rows (compose one stats strip, a table or a sentence), no fully-rounded labels, no box-in-box, no centred empty states (top-left, with the query in a code tag), no tinted alert blocks, no red-filled destructive buttons (fail edge and fail text instead), no ink-filled headers/tiles/second buttons, no hue wallpaper, no icon tiles, no status dots, no outline rings on filled badges, no empty-state art, no terminal cosplay, no arrow-suffixed "Learn more" links, no filler words (seamless, robust, effortless, leverage).
- **Reference / source:** https://github.com/arla6ka/skills (systems/quartz skill). System home named throughout: design.how — component pages at design.how/systems/quartz/components/<name>.md, foundations at design.how/systems/quartz/foundations/*.md (colour, typography, space, radius, borders and lines, elevation, motion, iconography, grid, anti-slop), registry installs at design.how/r/quartz/. Icon set named: Font Awesome Free, Classic Solid.
- **Best for:** Agent consoles, support tools and operations dashboards. Trade fit: not a customer-facing homepage system, but its disciplines transfer — status always as a word (a "Booked / On the way / Done" job tracker), one ink-filled primary action per view, and the Deny/Allow stop before any irreversible action.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0304⟧
## ⟦S0305⟧ arla6ka/token-mapping — Part 13 — UI Skills, rest of the ui-skills.com catalog (arla6ka)
- **What it is:** A read-only audit that reports how every hardcoded style value on a page, file or diff (raw hex, px, shadows) maps onto the project's existing design-token list. It never edits anything; actually replacing the values is the sibling build-design-system skill's job.
- **How it looks:** It produces no visitor-facing design. Its output is a report: a Summary, a Mapping table (each raw value with its file, line, property and job, landed on a token), then Do not use, Ambiguous, Gaps, For a person to decide, and Source sections, ending with a `Coverage:` line stating what was scanned and what was not.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Six steps: find the real token list (token files, theme entries, `:root` custom properties — a framework default theme or a public system like Geist never stands in for the team's list; if the read fails, stop, never fill a list from memory); find the values (what the caller named, else the branch diff, else the product code); resolve every alias to its final value in each mode and record disagreements; normalise both sides with code (lengths to px, colours to OKLCH compared by delta E OK), never by eye; classify each row once per mode, purpose first then value — Exact (job covers it, values match), Semantic (job covers it, value inside tolerance, difference stated in numbers), Ambiguous (two or more tokens fit, all named), Gap (no token's job covers it, or the only fit is out of tolerance — a gap never gets a new name). Hard rules: a value match before purpose is wrong (`#6b7280` is text, so it maps to text tokens, not `color.border.default`, which goes in Do not use); a semantic token beats the primitive it aliases; a palette class like `text-gray-500` names a value and no job, so it gets its own row counted apart. Gap threshold: when gaps are over 30% of rows and number 12 or more, lead with `Status: not actionable (gap threshold)`. Counts always carry their unit (occurrences, lines or mapping rows); anything inferred is marked inferred. Done means every row has a job, class and reason, and `git status` is unchanged.
- **Reference / source:** arla6ka skills collection — https://github.com/arla6ka/skills/blob/main/skills/token-mapping/SKILL.md ; its classification, normalising and tolerance rules live in its own references/mapping-rules.md.
- **Best for:** The token-compliance pass behind any section build — checking a finished hero, proof or form section is actually built from the site's tokens before it ships, and planning a token migration. It is an audit instrument, not a design generator.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0305⟧

## ⟦S0306⟧ arla6ka/ui-review — Part 13 — UI Skills, rest of the ui-skills.com catalog (arla6ka)
- **What it is:** A critique skill for a screen, flow, prototype or running build — accessibility included — that ranks what is actually broken and ends in a ship / no-ship verdict. The render is the evidence; descriptions, DOM text or source code only support it. Not for token compliance (that is ⟦S0305⟧).
- **How it looks:** It produces no visitor-facing design. Its output is a verdict document whose first line answers the ask in plain words, followed by a ship line such as `Ready to ship: no. Enter in Email cancels the invite (blocking 1, should-fix 2, 3 questions for a person).`, then a review record, findings sorted into blocking / should-fix / note / dismissed buckets, edge cases not shown, decisions for a person, and a closing `Coverage:` line. Run standalone, the report is saved to `.ui-review/<date>-<flow>.md` with its captures beside it.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion of its own. It measures motion and responsiveness instead of prescribing them: press feedback is probed with the Event Timing API (a `PerformanceObserver` on `event` entries, each `duration` must be under 100 ms), and a responsiveness finding from a screenshot alone is invalid — it needs that measured probe.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Nine steps: scope (what the caller names, else the branch's changed screens, else the five top routes); run the project's own lint and record command + exit code; capture each screen at the app's narrowest and widest widths (390 and 1280 by default), one fresh navigation per width, in the states that matter, plus the accessibility tree and the project's accessibility scanner; fix each screen's purpose in one line (marked assumed when not given); probe the traps on a local build only — keyboard path, focus after close, loading and error states, a throttled tab, reduced motion, a touch width — each with a measured result or a reason it did not run, never clicking anything that writes shared data; walk the 13 criteria (in references/criteria.md; an installed design system's own rules count as agreed criteria and come first) at each width; sort findings — with a panel, every reviewer gets the same prompt with no persona, and a finding raised independently by two reviewers is the strongest signal; walk the edge cases; write the verdict last. Finding standard: every finding carries a criterion, a findable location (element by role and name with its capture, e.g. `button 'Save changes' (settings-1280.png)`), the width, and evidence — "Label sits 24 px from its own field and 8 px from the next one (criterion 4, settings-390.png)", never "the spacing feels tight". Verdict logic: any blocking finding = `no`; an inferred blocking = `no, pending <the check>`; should-fix alone = `yes, with fixes`; notes only = `yes`. Contrast, target-size and keyboard problems are always ranked; a fix is written as a check that fails on the current build.
- **Reference / source:** arla6ka skills collection — https://github.com/arla6ka/skills/blob/main/skills/ui-review/SKILL.md ; severity, the 13 criteria and edge cases in its references/criteria.md; captures can be made by the sibling build-design-system's scripts/capture.mjs behind a write-blocking guard.
- **Best for:** The pre-ship QA gate for any homepage — hero, proof, work, form and CTA sections checked at phone and desktop widths with accessibility, keyboard and jank evidence before Asiful sees screenshots. A judging instrument; pair it with a design skill for the fixes.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0306⟧

## ⟦S0307⟧ ayghri/i-have-adhd — Part 13 — UI Skills, rest of the ui-skills.com catalog (ayghri)
- **What it is:** An output-shaping mode for a reader with ADHD: responses are structured so an ADHD brain can act on them — action first, numbered steps, state restated every turn, no tangents, concrete time estimates, visible wins. Invoked with /i-have-adhd and stays on until the reader says "stop adhd mode" or "normal mode".
- **How it looks:** Text output only, no visual design. A response opens with the doable action itself (a command, path or snippet first, prose after if at all), multi-step work appears as a short numbered list of bounded single actions, and the reply ends with one concrete next action the reader can do in under two minutes. No preamble, no recap, no closing pleasantries; visible lists are capped at 5 items per group, most relevant first.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Ten rules: (1) lead with the next action; (2) number multi-step tasks, one bounded action per step, no step containing "and then" twice, fewest steps that still work; (3) end with one concrete next action; (4) suppress tangents — a second issue is offered afterwards as a separate question; (5) restate state every turn ("Step 3 of 5 done: schema updated. Next: backfill…"), using a task/plan tool for multi-step work when the harness has one; (6) specific time estimates in concrete units ("About 15 minutes if tests already cover this. An afternoon if not."), never "some work"; (7) make completed work visible in concrete terms; (8) matter-of-fact error tone — cause and fix, never "Uh oh"; (9) cap visible lists at 5 per group (presentation only — never limits analysis, search or retained information); (10) no preamble, recap or closers — forbidden openers include "Great question", "Let me…", "Sure!". Driven by five stated facts about ADHD reading: small working memory, knowing ≠ doing, starting is the hardest step, vague time estimates register as uniform, dopamine is scarce so buried wins do not register. Overrides: full explanations when asked to "explain / walk me through" (headers added, still no preamble/closer); confirm before destructive actions; after three "still broken" turns, stop iterating, name the possibly-wrong assumption and ask one diagnostic question; genuine ambiguity gets one short clarifying question; "what are my options" gets 2–4 ranked options, recommendation first. Pre-send check: delete the announcing first sentence, the "anything else?" last sentence, sidebars, information-free hedges and idioms; the first and last lines alone must tell the reader what to do next and what just happened.
- **Reference / source:** ayghri — https://github.com/ayghri/i-have-adhd/blob/main/skills/i-have-adhd/SKILL.md . No external design references named.
- **Best for:** Shaping status reports, build handovers and approval asks to this user — not a page-design skill. Its shape (action first, numbered steps, one next action, state restated) is the format for presenting section approvals and follow-up decisions in chat.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0307⟧

## ⟦S0308⟧ blader/humanizer — Part 13 — UI Skills, rest of the ui-skills.com catalog (blader)
- **What it is:** A rewriting skill that removes AI-writing patterns so text reads like its writer, not a chatbot. It keeps everything the text says and invents nothing: mark the tells, draft the rewrite, read it aloud and check no fact was added or dropped, then write the final version stating each point naturally.
- **How it looks:** The output is prose, not page design: the same content with uneven, specific, human rhythm — varied sentence lengths, plain verbs (is / are / has), sentence-case headings without emoji or arrow decoration, no decorative bold, no bold-label-colon list items, and no chatbot wrapper ("Great question!", "I hope this helps", "let me know"). Three return modes: pasted text (draft + remaining patterns + final rewrite), file mode (only the final text written to the file, prose only — code blocks, commands, paths, YAML, data and link targets untouched), embedded mode (final text only, for PRs, commits, documents).
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** 26 numbered patterns in six groups, strongest first; §1–§5 justify an edit on one sighting, patterns marked *weak alone* need company. A. Staging: §1 Not X but Y (and split-sentence and clipped-tail forms), §2 one-line closers and dramatic fragments, §3 deep-sounding sayings ("the real question is", "at its core"), §4 staged run-ups ("Let's dive in", "Here's the thing"), §5 arguing with no one. B. Rhythm by rule: §6 forced triads, §7 repeated sentence openings, §8 dashes as universal connector — the final rewrite must contain no em or en dashes unless the writer's sample uses them, then match the sample's rate (dashes inside code, paths and URLs are left alone), §9 stacked qualifiers, §10 hyphenated pairs kept only before a noun, §11 passive voice / missing subjects. C. Inflation: §12 an overused-AI-word watch list (delve, crucial, pivotal, robust figurative, tapestry, underscore…), §13 inflated significance and stock "challenges / outlook" sections and send-offs, §14 vague association verbs, §15 shallow -ing riders, §16 sales language, §17 borrowed authority (unnamed experts, prestige-outlet lists), §18 avoiding is/are/has. D. Formatting: §19 bold as decoration, §20 decorative headings, §21 curly quotes (*weak alone*). E. Leftovers, removed outright: §22 chatbot residue, §23 knowledge-limit disclaimers and gap-filling guesses, §24 heading repeated in the first sentence, §25 writing about the document instead of its subject. F. Wrong reader: §26 re-explaining what the reader already knows — lead with the decision, keep only the reasoning that could change agreement. Voice rule: a user-supplied writing sample overrides the patterns (including the dash rule); without one, voice follows the text kind — opinion writing keeps opinions, humour and asides, reference/technical/legal stays neutral and plain. Guardrails: never act inside quotations, titles or proper names; text written before 30 November 2022 is not AI-written; keep specific unusual details, mixed feelings, era-bound references and genuine asides — they carry the writer's voice.
- **Reference / source:** blader — https://github.com/blader/humanizer/blob/main/SKILL.md . The patterns are drawn from Wikipedia's "Signs of AI writing" (WikiProject AI Cleanup), named in the skill's Source section.
- **Best for:** All visitor-facing copy on a trade homepage — hero headlines, proof/review text, section body copy, CTA lines — and for emails and proposals: the pass that stops copy reading as generated while keeping every fact intact. Especially §1, §2, §6, §8 and §19, named as the tells that most often survive a first rewrite.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0308⟧

## ⟦S0309⟧ CaliCastle/chalk-logic — Part 13 — UI Skills, rest of the ui-skills.com catalog (CaliCastle)
- **What it is:** An image-generation recipe system that turns one idea into one quiet, wordless chalkboard illustration: a single white-chalk proposition drawn on an even green schoolroom board. It renders the image when generation and inspection are available, otherwise returns the compiled prompt and recipe (status PROMPT_ONLY).
- **How it looks:** A flat, dry, desaturated green board filling the frame edge to edge with microscopic matte grain, and one compact chalk motif in warm-white mineral chalk — pressure variation, slightly broken stroke edges, occasional double strokes, tiny chalk deposits. Roughly 65%–75% of the board stays empty (76%–86% for a single sparse sequence or observational vignette), with generous outer margins. Three restrained contrast levels: faint construction/context marks, readable structure, very few brighter contacts. No text, letters, numerals, equations, pseudo-writing, signatures, logos or watermarks by default; if the user requires text, only their exact wording as one short phrase or up to three micro-labels, six words total. The proposition must read at thumbnail size and reward full-size inspection.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — a still illustration; the "motion" is the reading path the eye follows through the composition (first encounter → what changes or relates → where attention ends), carried by one named semantic carrier: spacing, density, scale, repetition, pressure or object arrangement.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Six composition families, exactly one primary: Directional progression (left-to-right/diagonal sequence), Open cycle (three to five unequal stages around a large central void, one incomplete loop), Source to branches (one compact source, three to five asymmetrical non-crossing trajectories), Axial observation (one object separated into an exact part count along one shared axis), Environmental flow (one boundary/field, one continuous causal route), Quiet vignette (one compact off-centre constellation in a vast field). Formats: 16:9 default landscape, 1:1 for an open cycle or compact accumulation, 4:5 for a branching study / exploded object / poster, ~2.2:1 only for a long transformation; exact user dimensions honoured natively. Eight-step workflow: lock the brief (concept, explanation, emotional temperature, format, text policy, execution mode); distill the reading path; anchor quality on one or two entries from references/example-index.md with a recorded anchor delta (three preserved identity traits per anchor, one target topology, exactly two independent target axes, each target observably different from every anchor source value); declare a 14-axis recipe; compile a four-paragraph image prompt containing only pixel information; generate one candidate; inspect at full and thumbnail size against all 21 gates and repair in a fixed precedence order (format → text policy → proposition → family → reading path → causal order → semantic carrier → exact counts → recognition cues → topology/anchor targets → preserved traits → quiet space → placement → thumbnail clarity → material detail → coherent strokes → even board → mineral hand → contrast hierarchy → mood → authored restraint), maximum two repair passes via references/repair-playbook.md; deliver with status DONE, DONE_WITH_CONCERNS (remaining failed gates listed) or PROMPT_ONLY. In image-free conversations all image work routes through one fresh isolated worker returning text findings and file paths only.
- **Reference / source:** CaliCastle skills — https://github.com/CaliCastle/skills/blob/main/skills/chalk-logic/SKILL.md ; its own references/example-index.md (quality anchors) and references/repair-playbook.md.
- **Best for:** Editorial illustration, not page structure: a process or "how it works" visual with a hand-drawn, non-diagram feel — e.g. a chalk-style explainer image inside a process section or blog post. The wordless, sparse discipline also suits a quiet hero illustration where photography would be too literal. Not a layout or web-motion skill.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0309⟧

## ⟦S0310⟧ CaliCastle/signal-geometry — Part 13 — UI Skills, rest of the ui-skills.com catalog (CaliCastle)
- **What it is:** An image-generation recipe system that translates one idea into one precise spatial behaviour — orbit, convergence, divergence, compression, deflection, propagation, oscillation, filtering, enclosure or release — rendered as a sparse geometric system on clean matte paper. Renders by default when generation + inspection exist, otherwise returns the compiled prompt and recipe.
- **How it looks:** A full-frame flat matte paper surface (clean neutral off-white stock in light mode, charcoal-dyed stock in dark mode — the two are equal modes) with fine irregular grain and faint fibres visible up close, no borders, mockup depth, edge shadows, stains or vintage distress. On it, a precise mark system — hairlines, arcs, dots, nodes, particles, restrained hatching, grids or wireframe meshes — in a three-step contrast hierarchy (faint scaffold, readable structure, very few bright anchors). Roughly 70%–95% of the canvas stays quiet background with only 2%–8% line/dot/hatch/mesh coverage. Grayscale by default; colour, when it carries meaning, is one pin-sized coral, orange-red or cobalt accent covering under ~0.2% of the canvas. No text by default (same gate as ⟦S0309⟧: exact user wording only, one short phrase or up to three micro-labels, six words total). Crisp, orthographic, calm, analytical editorial finish that reads at thumbnail size.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — a still poster/illustration; movement exists only as the implied transformation (the one active verb) the geometry depicts, never as animation.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Five grammar families, one primary plus at most one subordinate mark language: Orbital field (circles, arcs, radial ticks, loops, spherical meshes), Flow transformation (streamlines, particles, arrows, gates, obstacles), Signal strip (waveforms, lanes, bars, repeated measures, faint grids), Topology map (nodes, edges, frames, sparse modules), Layered field (ruled planes, hatching, contours, wireframe surfaces). Formats: 16:9 default illustration, 4:5 poster (recomposed vertically, never a crop), ~2.2:1 only on explicit ultrawide request, exact user dimensions honoured. Eight-step workflow: lock the brief (concept, emotional temperature, format, polarity, text policy, execution mode); distill the spatial proposition to one transformation verb + one family in a single internal visual sentence; lock quality anchors from references/example-index.md — one or two entries, each with an anchor delta of three invariants to preserve and three axes to change (format, topology, composition, viewpoint, polarity, motion, scaffold, accent); declare a 9-axis recipe (format, polarity, family, transformation, geometry — radial / bilateral / directional / paired / distributed / vertically staged, scaffold — open field / faint grid / framed region / baseline, anchor, accent, text); compile a four-paragraph prompt (canvas + material + quiet target; proposition + family + transformation + geometry + focal placement; mark vocabulary + three-tier contrast + accent + text policy; flat finish + rejection constraints); generate one candidate; inspect full-size and thumbnail against the critical gates and repair once, tightening only the relevant prompt fields via references/repair-playbook.md; deliver image + exact final prompt + recipe + status (DONE / DONE_WITH_CONCERNS / PROMPT_ONLY). Hard rejects: anything resolving into a dashboard, infographic, product screen, sci-fi HUD, colourful data visualisation, generic gradient blob, photographic scene, character illustration, collage, aged zine, glossy 3D render, or a recognisable copy of a reference composition.
- **Reference / source:** CaliCastle skills — https://github.com/CaliCastle/skills/blob/main/skills/signal-geometry/SKILL.md ; its own references/example-index.md and references/repair-playbook.md as quality anchors and repair source.
- **Best for:** Sparse editorial posters and abstract section artwork — a services or process backdrop, an areas/towns visual system, or a poster-style graphic where a precise geometric event carries the idea. Pairs naturally with restrained, type-led heroes. Not a photo treatment, layout system or motion skill.
