## ⟦S0340⟧ diip3sh/feel — UI Skills (ui-skills.com catalog)
- **What it is:** Builds UI interactions whose motion comes from a physical model — mass, stiffness, damping and force fields (magnets, friction, walls) — instead of durations and easing curves. A feel described in words ("a toggle that feels heavy", "a drawer with a magnetic snap", "a knob with heavy detents") is converted to numbers by Feel.words(); the skill ships a runtime, a test rig that plots position/velocity/force against the model's prediction, four example components, and exports of the same spring to Framer Motion, react-spring, SwiftUI, Compose and CSS linear().
- **How it looks:** The bundled demo page (index.html) shows four components, each inside its rig: a heavy toggle whose thumb lags and lands with a thump, a magnetic drawer coasting between stops, a card you throw that flies to the nearest corner and lifts with speed, a knob turning through detents that click it into place. Around each, the rig draws the position/velocity/force plots (orange measured line over a dashed predicted ghost), word chips, dials and a numeric readout.
- **Frame by frame:** Continuous physics — there is no timeline → on drag, the pointer becomes a "hand spring" pulling the body, so a heavy body visibly lags the finger and a light one doesn't → on release the body keeps its real velocity and coasts; where it stops is decided from the projected coast (x + v·m/c) or by simulating forward, never from a millisecond threshold → a spring body overshoots by its damping ratio (worked example: frequency 1.35 Hz, ζ 0.74 → about 3% overshoot, "the thump of something landing"; mass 3 lags a fast drag by a few px and coasts 80px per 1000px/s) and any overshoot past a travel end is caught by a wall, never drawn through it → magnets pull a thrown body into the nearest well; detents click a knob into stops → grabbing mid-flight takes over from the exact current position and velocity with no jump → with prefers-reduced-motion the body jumps straight to rest.
- **Mechanism & key values:** The one rule: every motion from the model — no transition durations, no cubic-bezier, no timers that move things; scripts/audit.mjs fails a build containing any. Models: spring-to-a-target for discrete states (toggle, press, expand); a field (magnets/friction/walls) for thrown things (sheets, carousels, pickers); Feel.Body2D for two-direction throws (points/corners measured in a straight line); a Body with unit "°" for knobs (detents as magnets, period: 360 for endless wheels). Drag velocity zeroes if stale by 60 ms. Feel.handoff bakes each free motion by simulating at 240 Hz and simplifying to CSS keyframes within 0.2px of the true path (animated custom properties must be registered with @property); runtime/feel.js is 15 kB gzipped; all bodies share one requestAnimationFrame loop that stops when everything settles. Limits (v0.2): a body holds a position or an angle, not both; the CSS linear() export replays only a step from rest; fields export to Framer Motion only as an inertia approximation; points-in-a-plane and detented knobs have no Framer equivalent. Sizing guide: one interaction 20–45 minutes, a gesture system 1–3 hours, a full motion system half a day or more (don't start it — propose the 3 interactions that matter most).
- **Reference / source:** diip3sh/feel on GitHub (github.com/diip3sh/feel); the rig's own controls follow Fluid Functionalism (fluidfunctionalism.com).
- **Best for:** Toggles, sliders, drawers, bottom sheets, carousels, drag-and-throw cards and detented controls anywhere feel is the quality bar — the physics alternative to easing-curve microinteraction in navigation, forms and interactive sections.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0340⟧

## ⟦S0341⟧ diip3sh/playthru — UI Skills (ui-skills.com catalog)
- **What it is:** Adds a scripted, looping product demo to a website using the playthru library (about 5 kB, no dependencies, no stylesheet): a fake cursor glides over the site's real UI, clicks real elements, types into real inputs and zooms a camera in on what matters — with no video file.
- **How it looks:** Inside a fixed-height stage box (example height: 520px) sits the app's actual interface. A drawn cursor glides between targets and clicks — real pointerdown/mousedown/pointerup/mouseup/click events fire, so the app's own handlers do the work (a modal opens, a row is added) — types with human timing and a drawn caret in single-line inputs, and the camera pushes in on the part being worked on, then pulls back out to show the result. When a real visitor hovers the stage, the demo freezes and the fake cursor hides so they can try the UI themselves.
- **Frame by frame:** The chained script runs in order and loops → click a control → zoom in on the working area → type the text → click through the flow → zoomOut to show the result → a reset step restores the starting state → the loop restarts from the top. It starts automatically the first time the stage is 30% in view. With prefers-reduced-motion the cursor jumps instead of gliding, the camera stays still and loops cut without fades; on small screens, if a zoom target can't fit at 1.3×, the camera stays out.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Steps: move, click, type, key, zoom, zoomOut, wait, run, reset, chained on playthru("#stage"); options loop, autoplay and pauseOnHover all default to true; every timing is fixed by the library — there is no speed, easing or duration option. The fake cursor cannot trigger :hover and never moves real focus, so styles are mirrored onto [data-playthru-hover] and [data-playthru-focus] attributes. Events are untrusted, links and submit buttons don't navigate, and the demo pauses while a menu outside the stage is open (detected via aria-expanded or :popover-open); it cannot target elements inside iframes, canvas or WebGL. A good demo is 4–8 steps telling one story, and a reset that undoes everything is mandatory. Setup: npm i playthru, or the CDN module https://esm.sh/playthru in plain HTML; React via the Playthru component or usePlaythru hook ("use client" required in Next.js App Router).
- **Reference / source:** diip3sh/playthru on GitHub (repo spelled "playthrou"); docs at playthrou.diip3sh.xyz.
- **Best for:** Hero sections and "how it works" — a self-playing demo of a real interface instead of a video or screenshot carousel. For trades, it fits a booking/quote-form walkthrough staged on a working copy of the form.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0341⟧

## ⟦S0342⟧ edenspiekermann/apply-design-system — UI Skills (ui-skills.com catalog)
- **What it is:** A Figma workflow that reconnects an existing screen to a published design system, section by section: capture the current state, back the screen up, inventory its sections, build a component map from the library, classify each section as already-connected, exact-swap, compose-from-primitives or blocked, then swap or rebuild one section at a time with screenshot validation after each.
- **How it looks:** No page output — the result is the same Figma screen with local wrappers replaced by real library instances: header summary blocks typically composed from avatar, badge, button and metric primitives; alerts and metrics swapped one-to-one; bottom nav bars rebuilt as custom containers over nav-item primitives. The closing report lists Swapped / Composed / Already connected / Blocked, with node names, component keys and whether each final node is local or library-backed.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Reads via Figma MCP (get_metadata and get_screenshot preferred; get_design_context optional), writes via a figma-use-style helper. The backup duplicate is placed to the right of the original, named e.g. "Backup - Start", in its own call before any destructive edit. Component discovery prefers, in order: existing screens already using the system, direct inspection of the library file, then search_design_system as fallback only (results may include unrelated team/community libraries). Variants are chosen by matching the original's semantic and visual cues — fills, strokes, effects, corner radius, typography, primary vs secondary treatment — never blindly the default variant; exact component keys over names. One section per script, never a whole-screen rewrite. In non-auto-layout parents, preserve x, y, width and height explicitly and warn that swaps can drift. Import failures are hard blockers: stop, check for the key elsewhere in the file, try the component key instead of the component-set key, otherwise mark the section blocked and report why. If an audit produces only one narrow finding, this skill hands off to ⟦S0344⟧ instead.
- **Reference / source:** edenspiekermann/Skills on GitHub (github.com/edenspiekermann/Skills); Figma MCP / figma-use.
- **Best for:** Design-system migration work inside Figma. A process reference only — no visitor-facing pattern for trade pages.

## ⟦S0343⟧ edenspiekermann/audit-design-system — UI Skills (ui-skills.com catalog)
- **What it is:** A read-only Figma audit for design-system integration drift: shared primitives recreated as ad-hoc frames, repeated siblings that should collapse into one component, hard-coded values sitting beside tokenised peers, custom-built global patterns, and variant drift inside a nominal component. Every finding is anchored to a specific node and backed by structural evidence, not screenshot taste.
- **How it looks:** A report, not a page. The markdown form: a header (file and node reviewed, overall verdict ✅ Passes / ⚠️ Needs Work / ❌ Significant Issues, confidence percentage), a 2–3 sentence summary, a findings table with priority icons (🔴 priority 3, 🟠 2, 🟡 1, ⚪ 0), a details section per finding (what's wrong, why it matters, likely replacement, affected node IDs) and prioritised recommendations. The JSON form is a fixed schema: findings[] with title (≤80 chars, imperative), body, confidence_score, priority and code_location set to /figma/<fileKey>/nodes/<nodeId> with line_range 1–1; overall_correctness is "patch is correct" only when there are no findings.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Evidence pulled with Figma MCP reads: get_design_context for the exact node, get_screenshot, get_variable_defs, get_code_connect_map, get_metadata for large or board-like scopes, and search_design_system only after a likely non-systemised primitive is identified (a candidate is included only when the match is credible from structure and naming). Keep findings to the highest-signal issues — usually 0–6; omissions are preferred over weak findings. Priority: 3 = severe library- or navigation-level, 2 = important reusable primitive or tokenisation, 1 = moderate drift, 0 = nit. Confidence: 0.9–1.0 direct structural evidence, 0.7–0.89 strong inference from repetition and nearby token use, 0.5–0.69 plausible but incomplete — prefer omitting. Every finding must answer what concrete Figma evidence shows the drift and why it matters for propagation, consistency, theming or maintenance. Output format by environment: raw JSON for Codex Desktop and machine-consumed surfaces, markdown for chat-style CLIs. Handoff routing: one narrow finding → ⟦S0344⟧; a broader screen-wide pass → ⟦S0342⟧.
- **Reference / source:** edenspiekermann/Skills on GitHub; Figma MCP.
- **Best for:** QA of Figma screens before a build. A process reference only — no visitor-facing pattern.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0343⟧

## ⟦S0344⟧ edenspiekermann/fix-design-system-finding — UI Skills (ui-skills.com catalog)
- **What it is:** Fixes one specific design-system finding in Figma — one offending node or local cluster at a time, with minimal read scope and minimal write scope — after ⟦S0343⟧ has identified the issue. The review result is the scope contract; the skill never silently widens into a cleanup pass.
- **How it looks:** The same screen with only the targeted area changed: an ad-hoc frame replaced by the correct library instance, raw values bound to variables, or an instance moved to the right variant. The closing report stays tied to the single finding: Finding fixed (what changed, on which node), Validation (how the original complaint was confirmed resolved), and Blocked or Follow-up only when the fix could not be completed.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** The target is extracted from the finding's code_location (/figma/<fileKey>/nodes/<nodeId>); without a specific node, the skill stops and asks for one. When the replacement choice is ambiguous, a local compatibility check runs before any backup or write and must return safe-to-apply — blocked or needs-human-choice stop the run. Evidence reads are the smallest useful set: get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_variable_defs (token findings), get_code_connect_map, search_design_system only if the primitive still isn't located. Exactly one remediation mode is chosen: swap-instance, compose-from-primitives, bind-tokens, align-variant, or blocked — preferring the smallest change that satisfies the finding. The backup duplicates only the offending node or smallest enclosing section ("Backup - Fix finding 1") in its own call. Prefer swapComponent() to preserve position and valid overrides; rebuild beside the original when visual comparison is needed. Validation screenshots the changed node or its immediate section only — expanding to the full screen only when a global pattern such as navigation was touched. Never claim the whole screen is "on system" after one fix.
- **Reference / source:** edenspiekermann/Skills on GitHub; Figma MCP / figma-use.
- **Best for:** Targeted Figma fixes following an ⟦S0343⟧ audit. A process reference only.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0344⟧

## ⟦S0345⟧ Egonex-AI/understand — UI Skills (ui-skills.com catalog)
- **What it is:** A seven-phase pipeline that analyses a codebase and writes an interactive knowledge graph — knowledge-graph.json in the project's data directory (.ua/, or the legacy .understand-anything/ when it already exists) — powering a dashboard for exploring the project's architecture, components and relationships. It supports full builds, deterministic incremental updates on new commits, and an optional full LLM graph review.
- **How it looks:** The graph itself is data: nodes (files, functions, classes, modules, concepts, configs, documents, services, tables, endpoints, pipelines, schemas, resources) joined by typed edges, grouped into architectural layers, with a guided tour of ordered steps — "Project Overview" pointing at the README, "Application Entry Point" pointing at the boot files — that a separate dashboard skill renders as an explorable map. In the terminal it appears as phase banners ("[Phase N/7] …") with per-batch progress lines during analysis.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. This is a batch pipeline; the only step-through "playback" is the dashboard's tour, which belongs to the separate dashboard skill, not this one.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Phase 0 pre-flight: resolve the project root (a git worktree redirects output to the main repo root; plugin build needs Node ≥ 22 and pnpm ≥ 10); options --full, --auto-update / --no-auto-update, --review, --language <ISO 639-1 code or friendly name>, --exclude <glob patterns>. Phase 0.5: generate or confirm the .understandignore file — a user-confirmation gate. Phase 1: scan via the project-scanner subagent (over 100 files triggers a scoping warning). Phase 1.5: semantic batches via compute-batches.mjs. Phase 2: file-analyzer subagents, up to 5 concurrent, each writing one output file per batch index (batch-<i>.json or batch-<i>-part-<k>.json — any other naming is silently dropped by the merge); merge-batch-graphs.py normalises IDs, dedupes, drops dangling edges and runs a two-pass tested_by linker. Phase 3: assemble review (full runs only). Phase 4: architecture layers, each requiring id, name, description, nodeIds. Phase 5: guided tour steps (order, title, description, nodeIds). Phase 6: validation — an inline deterministic Node validator by default, or the graph-reviewer subagent with --review. Phase 7: save — the structural-fingerprint baseline must be written before meta.json or every later commit classifies as fully structural; intermediates are moved to a .trash-<timestamp> folder (purged after 7 days) while scan-result.json is preserved for cheap incrementals. Schema: 13 node types with ID conventions (file:<path>, function:<path>:<name>, class:<path>:<name>, module:<name>, concept:<name>…); 26 edge types with weights — contains 1.0, inherits/implements 0.9, calls/exports/defines_schema 0.8, imports/deploys/migrates 0.7, depends_on/configures/triggers 0.6, tested_by/documents/provisions/serves/routes 0.5. Incremental updates pass a strict symbol-loss gate (source identity = file path + symbol kind + owner + name) with exactly one repair retry; deterministic deletion confirmation exists only for JavaScript/JSX, TypeScript/TSX, Ruby, Python, Go, Rust and C++ — other languages' missing symbols stay "unknown" and block publication.
- **Reference / source:** Egonex-AI/Understand-Anything on GitHub (github.com/Egonex-AI/Understand-Anything, understand-anything-plugin).
- **Best for:** Codebase onboarding and architecture documentation tooling. Not a visitor-facing design source; its layered graph plus guided-tour shape is at most a structural reference for organising a complex explanation.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0345⟧
# Bank Index chunk — skills S0346–S0370

All 25 skills in this range sit in **Part 13 — UI Skills, rest of the ui-skills.com catalog** of WEB-SKILLS.md. Most are agent workflow/tooling skills rather than visual-design skills; where a skill produces no on-screen page design, "How it looks" describes the artifact the user actually ends up seeing.

Family note: S0346–S0353 are all commands of one plugin, Egonex-AI's **Understand-Anything**, and share a large block of identical text (the knowledge-graph structure reference, the "read efficiently" rules, and the git-freshness check). They are distinct commands, not the same skill renamed — but the shared graph reference is written out in full only under S0346; the other entries point back to it instead of repeating it.

## ⟦S0346⟧ Egonex-AI/understand-chat — Part 13, UI Skills (rest of ui-skills.com catalog)
- **What it is:** A chat command for the Understand-Anything plugin: it answers questions about a codebase by searching a pre-built knowledge graph (`.ua/knowledge-graph.json`) instead of reading source files wholesale.
- **How it looks:** No page design. The user sees a text answer in chat that names specific files, functions and relationships from the graph, and says which architectural layer is relevant and why.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. (Workflow: resolve the data dir → check graph freshness against git → grep the graph for the question's keywords → pull the 1-hop edges around matching nodes → answer from that subgraph only.)
- **Mechanism & key values:** Grep-first reading of one JSON graph. Node types: code (file, function, class, module, concept), non-code (config, document, service, table, endpoint, pipeline, schema, resource), domain/knowledge (domain, flow, step, article, entity, topic, claim, source); IDs are type-prefixed (`file:path`, `function:path:name`). Edge types include imports, contains, calls, depends_on, configures, documents, deploys, triggers, contains_flow, flow_step, related, cites. Freshness check compares the graph's stored `gitCommitHash` against `git rev-parse HEAD` plus staged/unstaged/untracked diffs, scoped with the `-- .` pathspec so sibling monorepo changes don't count as stale; a hash mismatch with an empty project diff is NOT stale.
- **Reference / source:** Egonex-AI/Understand-Anything plugin on GitHub (github.com/Egonex-AI/Understand-Anything). Companion command to ⟦S0345⟧ understand, which builds the graph this one reads.
- **Best for:** Developer tooling only — codebase Q&A during builds. No use in visitor-facing sections; trade fit is indirect (faster orientation inside a large site codebase).
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0346⟧

Without the `?token=` parameter the page shows an "Access Token Required" gate instead of the graph. The dashboard auto-opens in the default browser.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion prescribed. (Launch sequence: resolve project + data dir → verify `knowledge-graph.json` exists → find the dashboard package → try the prebuilt viewer first → fall back to pnpm install/build + Vite dev server → capture the token URL from server output.)
- **Mechanism & key values:** Fast path runs a version-pinned, self-contained viewer tarball from the plugin's GitHub release via `npx` (no install, no build). Fallback: `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, build `@understand-anything/core`, then `GRAPH_DIR=<project> npx vite --host 127.0.0.1`. Default port 5173, next free port if taken. Plugin root is resolved from 8 candidate paths (CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT, ~/.understand-anything-plugin, skill-symlink-relative paths, and codex/opencode/pi/home clone roots).
- **Reference / source:** Egonex-AI/Understand-Anything plugin on GitHub; viewer releases at github.com/Egonex-AI/Understand-Anything/releases.

## ⟦S0352⟧ Egonex-AI/understand-knowledge — Part 13, UI Skills (rest of ui-skills.com catalog)
- **What it is:** Analyses a Karpathy-pattern LLM wiki (raw sources + LLM-written markdown with wikilinks + a schema file) and generates an interactive knowledge graph with entity extraction, implicit relationships and topic clustering. ## ⟦S0354⟧ ehmo/slopbeth — Part 13, UI Skills (rest of ui-skills.com catalog)
- **What it is:** A prose-editing skill that removes AI-writing tells from drafts, edits and reviews while preserving the author's meaning, voice and density — with an evidence-bound rule: vague source copy stays vague (claims become proof gaps or questions), never polished into invented specifics.
- **How it looks:** No page design. Output is the revised text first, in the author's own register — plain sentences, no title-case hype headings, no decorative bold, no em dashes or emojis unless the author's sample uses them — plus, only when useful, a compact note on material changes; for reviews, exact bad spans marked with label + reason alongside preserved spans.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. (8-step workflow: classify the task → separate the brief from the artifact (instructions about the writing are never printed in the output) → lock facts/entities/numbers/dates/quotes → set the evidence boundary → diagnose tell clusters, not isolated words → rewrite using Orwell's six rules as defaults → validate with bundled lint scripts when files exist → output text first.)
- **Mechanism & key values:** Bundled scripts: `deslop_lint.py`, `orwell_lint.py` (exposes `passive_ratio` as a first-class metric), `preservation_check.py`, `density_report.py`, plus corpus-only scorers. Five load-on-demand references (slop taxonomy, voice & preservation, density/unsummarizability, writing system, evaluation). Hard rules include: never claim text is undetectable; no invented owners/dates/metrics in support, policy, incident or product copy; over-editing strong human text is a failure; check cadence (repeated sentence lengths/openers) on medium/long rewrites. Shipped BENCHMARKS.md reference: v2 corpus of 88 output cases / 264 judge rows; on the 25-case real competitor-agent panel Slopbeth averages 112.10 vs best peer 112.55 — parity within the 2.0-point gate, 0 missing required facts, 0 forbidden-output hits (an earlier 0.92 win-rate claim was withdrawn as a scoring artifact).
- **Reference / source:** ehmo/slopkit on GitHub; Orwell's "Politics and the English Language" (1946) six rules; benchmarked against stop-slop, humanizer, skill-deslop, anti-ai-slop-writing.
- **Best for:** Copy quality on any section — hero lines, benefits, testimonials, FAQ — anywhere AI-sounding filler would cheapen a trade site. Pairs with the simpler ⟦S0358⟧ anti-slop for a light pass; this is the heavy, benchmarked version.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0354⟧

## ⟦S0355⟧ ehmo/slopgent — Part 13, UI Skills (rest of ui-skills.com catalog)
- **What it is:** The companion to ⟦S0354⟧ slopbeth, applied to the agent's own chat replies instead of a shipped document: replies must be honest about what actually ran, action-first, and plain-language, without dropping load-bearing caveats. Stays active until the user says "stop slopgent".
- **How it looks:** Chat messages that lead with the action, command or path ("Changed `verifyToken` at `auth.ts:42`. Not run yet. Next: `npm test -- auth.spec.ts`"), separate what changed from what is verified, number multi-step work one bounded action per step, and restate state across turns. No apology theatre, no invented confidence, no fixed clipped cadence.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. Three fixes in priority order: 1) Honesty (never trade a true caveat for a cleaner line; never report a tool as run when it wasn't), 2) Structure (action first, one concrete next step for anything left open), 3) Plain language (drop jargon, keep exact commands/paths/numbers/error codes). Time estimates must be in agent units — turns and tool calls, with wall-clock as a range pinned to the one driving variable — never human calendar time.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Can be made permanent via `node scripts/slopgent-memory.js enable` (writes a marked, idempotent block into ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, ~/.codex/AGENTS.md or ~/.gemini/GEMINI.md). Evidence state: on a 16-case comms corpus, deterministic lint scores slopgent 99.1 vs i-have-adhd 88.7, "bro" 77.1, unshaped baseline 62.3; a blinded 3-judge panel scores it 4.96/5 with 40 of 48 best-picks; against dedicated honesty systems it ties at 5.00 on honesty and wins overall by 0.28, below its own pre-registered 0.30 margin gate — the skill states this honestly. Drop the shaping for explainers, before destructive actions, after three "still broken" turns, or on real ambiguity.
- **Reference / source:** ehmo/slopkit on GitHub; structure rules adapted from i-have-adhd by Ayoub G. (MIT), plain-language rules from the "bro" skill by Dillon Mulroy.
- **Best for:** Agent communication discipline during builds — status reports and completion claims the owner can trust. Not a design skill and never applied to the user's own text (that is ⟦S0354⟧).
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0355⟧

## ⟦S0356⟧ elayadesign/landing-page-design — Part 13, UI Skills (rest of ui-skills.com catalog)
- **What it is:** A complete landing-page system in two halves: Part A decides strategy, structure and conversion copy; Part B is a non-negotiable visual system (type, spacing, radius, hero, icons, motion) that every value must resolve through instead of being invented.
- **How it looks:** A single-offer page: hero with headline + subheadline (both capped at 680px wide, lines broken at meaningful points), one primary CTA and one proof signal above the fold; benefits, 3-step how-it-works, proof, FAQ and final CTA below. Flat backgrounds only (dark mode restricted to #000000, #181818, #1F1F1F, #272727, #313131, #131209); the one gradient allowed is on the hero heading text — left-to-right #FFFFFF→#9B9B9B on dark, #000000→#666666 on light. One typeface (Geist, Manrope, Geist Mono or Poppins; Inter/Roboto/Arial/Open Sans/Helvetica banned), no italics, no weight above bold. A mandatory standalone "tagline reveal" section sits in the mid-page argument: 2+ lines of big type starting muted and colouring in word by word on scroll.
- **Frame by frame:** Motion is restrained and specified: base curve cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1); layout/position changes 500ms, hover colour/opacity 300ms (never under 200ms); only transform and opacity animate. Scroll reveals: sections rise 32px (Spacing-400) and fade 0→1 over 600–800ms, triggered by IntersectionObserver, played once only. Floating nav: compact bar floats off the top edge, translucent with backdrop blur; menu open/close icon morphs between states; mobile menu is a full-height blurred panel whose links arrive staggered — each rises 24px (Spacing-300) while fading in, 60ms apart, whole sequence capped at 400ms. Tagline reveal: each word transitions individually from ~25–35% opacity to full colour as it crosses a trigger line, in reading order, on the base curve. `prefers-reduced-motion` replaces movement with a plain opacity change.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Type sizes snap to the Tailwind scale (text-xs 12/16 → text-9xl 128/1), snapping DOWN to the closest step with its paired line height; buttons text-base or text-sm, semibold; `text-wrap: balance` on headings, `pretty` on body; no hyphens inside copy. Spacing tokens only: 0, 2, 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 40, 48, 64, 80, 96px; main buttons padded 8px vertical / 12px horizontal. Nested radius rule: when the gap between nested shapes is under 32px, inner radius = outer radius − gap, applied only if the result is over 2. Card borders all the way around or none; no background gradients. Icons only from Phosphor, Solar or Iconamoon (Material Icons/Symbols banned). Four layout types (A classic hero, B long-form story, C minimal conversion, D comparison); sections built one at a time in the order hero → benefits → how-it-works → proof → FAQ → final CTA. Full state set required (hover, active scale(0.98)/translateY(1px), focus ring, skeleton loading, composed empty, inline error). Copy rules: benefit-first, CTA = verb + what they get (never "Learn more"/"Submit"), at least one risk reversal; banned filler words include "revolutionize", "supercharge", "cutting edge", "effortless", "world class".
- **Reference / source:** elayadesign/ai-design-skills on GitHub; partly adapted from taste-skill by Leon Lin (MIT). Companion skill named for existing sites: redesign-existing-projects (github.com/elayadesign/redesign-skill).
- **Best for:** Whole landing pages and every section type — hero, benefits, process (how-it-works), proof/reviews, FAQ, final CTA. High trade fit as a discipline layer (specific numbers, proof beside claims, one primary action = phone call), though its font bans and no-hyphen copy rule must be weighed against a trades brand's existing identity.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0356⟧

## ⟦S0357⟧ elithrar/animated-sprites — Part 13, UI Skills (rest of ui-skills.com catalog)
- **What it is:** Creates, repairs and reviews custom characters for 2D animation — animated sprite sheets and custom Codex/ChatGPT pets — keeping character identity consistent and motion readable at real display size and timing.
- **How it looks:** A sprite atlas: a grid of animation cells, one row per state (idle, working, running…), same character, same scale and anchors across every cell, transparent background, poses staged so the silhouette reads at small size. Previews must play at the target's actual timing — never slowed down to hide a pacing defect.
- **Frame by frame:** Motion is choreographed per state: key poses and silhouettes approved first, then in-betweens planned with anticipation, arcs, spacing, easing and follow-through where they clarify the action; secondary motion stays subordinate. Intentional jump lift and gait bounce must survive assembly (poses are registered to a shared scale, never independently fitted into their cells). Every loop seam and state transition is checked in the perceptual gate.
- **Mechanism & key values:** The target's own contract governs: required states and their meanings, frame order/counts, canvas and cell geometry, anchors, transparency, timing, repeat/trigger behaviour. Two separate acceptance gates: 1) structural — the encoded output validated against the contract (required/unused cells, boundaries, alpha, file constraints); 2) perceptual motion — consistency, anatomy, attachment, state meaning, amplitude, cadence, contact, loop seams at actual timing and scale; neither gate substitutes for the other. Three bundled references: art-direction-and-generation.md, motion-review.md, repair-and-delivery.md. Technical state IDs are not user meanings (a state called `running` can mean active work, not foot-running).
- **Reference / source:** elithrar/dotfiles on GitHub (.agents/skills). For Codex/ChatGPT pets it defers to the product-specific creation/update skill for the current sprite contract.
- **Best for:** Mascot/pet artwork and small character loops — e.g. a trade mascot in a loading state or empty state. Not a page-section design system; situational for trades sites.

## ⟦S0360⟧ elithrar/web-perf — Part 13, UI Skills (rest of ui-skills.com catalog)
- **What it is:** A performance-investigation workflow: diagnose page-load and interaction problems from browser traces, network evidence and source code — for site-speed, Lighthouse, Core Web Vitals or layout-shift complaints.
- **How it looks:** No page design. Output is a findings report: the measured symptom, its supported cause, the concrete fix or recommendation, and the verification limit — with a metric table when several measurements help comparison.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. (Workflow: identify page + symptom + device conditions → pick the evidence path → diagnose from trace to request/element/source → validate fixes under equivalent conditions → report, separating measured values, tool estimates and unmeasured hypotheses.)
- **Mechanism & key values:** Chrome DevTools traces preferred (via its bundled references/devtools.md); falls back to existing traces/Lighthouse artifacts or source inspection and states what could not be measured. Discipline rules: record page/build, viewport, device/emulation, throttling, cache state and interactions (a reload alone does not establish cold cache); keep mobile and desktop observations separate; field CWV is never conflated with lab data; a load-only trace does not establish INP and TBT is a lab diagnostic, not an INP substitute; confirm ownership/use before recommending removal of third-party resources; never promise additive savings from overlapping insights; a performance request does not expand into an accessibility or whole-codebase audit.
- **Reference / source:** elithrar/dotfiles on GitHub (.agents/skills).

## ⟦S0361⟧ enesozturk/dimensional-drawing — Part 13, UI Skills (rest of ui-skills.com catalog)
- **What it is:** Produces an Apple-style monochrome dimensional drawing of a UI component or physical product: one dense engineering sheet — title block, notes, dimensioned views, exploded layer stack and variable tables — delivered as a single self-contained HTML file.
- **How it looks:** Black line on white paper, greys only, no colour anywhere (light theme forced, every colour explicit). Top: an HTML title block framed like the drawing (1.2px black frame, radius 16, 0.8px cell rules, 9.5px caps labels in Arimo/Helvetica) with DWG NO./REV/SHEETS/UNITS/SCALE/SOURCE cells, general notes and a row of 6–7 key variables. Below, the SVG sheet (viewBox 0 0 1700×1060): notes boxed top-left, the plan view top-centre at ~1:1 with chain dimensions and dashed detail circles, a hatched shadow-envelope diagram under the notes, an exploded axonometric layer stack bottom-left, nested-corner and radius details along the bottom, and variable tables down the right column. UI is drawn as architecture, never content: slot boxes labelled `TITLE SLOT · FLEX`, `CONTENT SLOT · FILL`, lead boxes with an X — no real copy, no text-width dimensions.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion in the sheet itself. (Its companion ⟦S0362⟧ animates the finished sheet into a film.)
- **Mechanism & key values:** Every dimension is a variable code, never a raw number: S# spacing, H#/Z#/I# heights/sizes/icon, B border, W width, R# radius, Y/BL/SP shadow, E# envelope, T1 touch min, V1 viewport margin, MH max height. Derived values are formulas with results (`H1 = 2·S1 + H3 = 64`, `R2 = R1 − B − S6`, `MH = 100vh − 2·V1`); anything not in the source is marked `[TBD]` and drawn as a proportional schematic. Inline-JS SVG kit: begin() creates per-sheet defs (arrow marker, 45° hatch); helpers dimH/dimV/callout/rad/nb/detailRef/table/notes. Line weights: object outline 1.6px, dim lines 0.7px, extension lines 0.55px (3px off the feature, 5px overshoot), 7px filled arrows; dim text 11px with a white paint-order stroke knockout, slot labels 9px caps letter-spaced, view titles 12px caps. Slots dashed 4 3; hug elements light grey fill. Exploded projection matrix (.94s, .17s, −.34s, .47s). Components are measured from real source via Playwright (getBoundingClientRect + getComputedStyle) and grep instance counts. Physical products: third-angle top/front/right views + hatched section A–A, mm units, published specs only, conflicts flagged CONFLICT. Pre-publish checks: every code on the drawing exists in a table, every formula closes, no brand text, no non-grey hex. Worked examples ship beside the skill: examples/dialog-sheet.html and examples/card-sheet.html.
- **Reference / source:** enesozturk/dimensional-drawing on GitHub; modelled on Apple's accessory dimensional drawings (developer.apple.com/accessories/dimensional-drawings).
- **Best for:** Spec/anatomy presentations of a component or product — a striking "engineering drawing" section or deliverable for a product-like offer (e.g. a door/window system anatomy). Niche for trade homepages; strong as a proof-of-craft artifact.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0361⟧

## ⟦S0362⟧ enesozturk/dimensional-drawing-motion — Part 13, UI Skills (rest of ui-skills.com catalog)
- **What it is:** Turns a finished ⟦S0361⟧ dimensional-drawing sheet into a ~10-second Apple-style motion film: the sheet draws itself line by line while a camera moves over it, layers lift into the exploded view, and the full sheet resolves. Same monochrome, slots-not-content, unbranded rules as the drawing.
- **How it looks:** A 1920×1080, 60fps film on a white background, ink #111: it opens in extreme close-up on the plan's header corner as strokes draw themselves, pulls back to reveal the whole plan, slides left as the layer stack explodes upward, then pulls out to the complete sheet and holds with a barely-moving final push. Arimo/Helvetica caps lettering throughout; no colour, no music or voice unless asked.
- **Frame by frame:** Scene time is scaled `t = t / 0.85` (runs ~15% faster on screen). Beat 1 (0–2.3s): camera at ~4.4× zoom on the plan's top-left; the outer border draws from the top-left corner, then lead circle, X-box, title slot, header divider, then header dims (S1, Z1, S5, H1); tiny drift z 4.4→4.2. Beat 2 (2.3–4.2s): log-zoom pull-back to ~1.7× while the rest of the plan draws — trail control, body well, content slots, footer actions, centre lines, chained dims, radius callouts, boxed notes, detail circles, view title. Beat 3 (4.2–7.2s): camera eases left; container → body → slots morph from the flat plan matrix to the axonometric matrix and rise to their z — strokes first, fills fading in after (from a+0.55 to a+1.25) so no white fill flashes over the drawing; static bottom layers (viewport, scrim, shadow) draw in beneath; leaders and layer labels follow. Beat 4 (7.2–9.2s): zoom out to 1.0; sheet border draws, then notes, tables and detail views each appear in a 0.3–0.5s burst. Beat 5 (9.2s–end): hold with a very slow push, z 0.998→0.988. Total ~11s; keep films 8–15s.
- **Mechanism & key values:** The scene is a pure function of time — `render(t)` sets every property from t alone — so a headless renderer (Playwright + ffmpeg via adapters/headless/render.mjs) can jump to any frame; primary target is the claude.ai Motion artifact type (adapter bundled as a reference file). One SVG (viewBox 0 0 1900×1060) and one camera: wrapper transform from keys DW_CAM = [{t, cx, cy, z}] interpolated ease-in-out with log zoom (exp(lerp(log z0, log z1, p))). Registration: `at(start, stagger, dur)` gives every subsequently drawn element a window [start + i·stagger, +dur], ordered outline → structure → slots → dims → labels. Drawn elements: pathLength=1, strokeDasharray 1 2, dashoffset 1→0 ease-in-out, fill fades over the last 45%. Faded elements (text, dashed slots, centrelines, hatches): opacity ease-out. Morph groups lerp matrix flat=[k,0,0,k,PX,PY] → iso=[.94s,.17s,−.34s,.47s,TX,TY] minus z·v on ty, with `--u = 1/√|det M|` keeping stroke widths constant; values quantised to 1/400 and skipped when unchanged. Style rules: ease-in-out for camera and strokes, ease-out for fades, no bounce, no overshoot. Check frames at 0, 1.2, 2.4, 3.3, 4.6, 5, 5.9, 6.6, 8, 10, 11s. Start from templates/scene-dialog.js + templates/base.css — adapt, never start blank. (Remotion needs a company licence above 3 people; other libraries untested.)
- **Reference / source:** enesozturk/dimensional-drawing on GitHub; companion to ⟦S0361⟧.
- **Best for:** An animated spec-sheet film — a hero-adjacent motion piece or social/proof asset showing a product's anatomy drawing itself. Niche but distinctive for a product-configurator-style trade offer.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0362⟧

## ⟦S0363⟧ ericzakariasson/scandinavian-design — Part 13, UI Skills (rest of ui-skills.com catalog)
- **What it is:** A full Scandinavian design system for restyling interfaces: neutral black-and-white foundation, restrained sans-serif type, generous spacing, clear page chapters and minimal decoration — with an unusually deep set of judgement rules for when restraint helps and when it would damage meaning, identity or density.
- **How it looks:** Calm, quiet, left-aligned pages on a white canvas: pure black primary ink, hierarchy built from alpha-black rungs rather than grey colours, hairline borders at 10% black, product imagery carrying all the expression while the chrome stays silent. Long pages read as a sequence of distinct spacious chapters (alternating white and ~4% black fills), one dominant media anchor per chapter, monochrome third-party logo rows, and short direct copy. No serif display type, no all-caps, no emoji icons, no decorative gradients or premium shadows.
- **Frame by frame:** Motion is deliberately minimal: ordinary UI motion under 300ms; ease-out for entrances/exits, ease-in-out for movement already on screen, ease for colour/hover; transform and opacity only; entrances never from scale(0) — subtle scale(0.95–0.98) with opacity; press feedback scale(0.97) for ~100–160ms when used; hover motion gated behind `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)`; `prefers-reduced-motion` keeps colour/opacity feedback and removes movement. Stopping perpetual decorative motion must also clear the driven transform/opacity so the element returns to rest instead of freezing mid-marquee.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Colour defaults: canvas/surface #FFFFFF, primary ink #000000, secondary rgb(0 0 0/64%), tertiary rgb(0 0 0/44%), border 10%, strong border 18%, hover fill 5%, pressed 9%, scrim 44% — set with alpha colours, never the opacity property; no tinted neutrals (correct a cast at ~8+ points of channel spread, leave under 5). Metadata rung may need lifting to ~56% where real reading sits at 40–50%. Dark canvas inverts with different numbers: canvas ~#0A0A0A, secondary white 56%, tertiary 36% (≈46% reaches 4.66:1 on #0A0A0A; use 50% above #1A1A1A), borders white 10–12%, hover 9%, pressed 14%, focus ring ≥2px. Type: one sans (preserve the product's own well-made face first; web default Inter Variable; Scto Grotesk A if licensed); body 16–18px/400/1.5–1.6, labels 500, headings 500–600 (avoid 700–900 — and check which weights the family actually ships before restating), large headings line-height 1.05–1.15 with slight negative tracking, prose measure 55–68 characters, 3–4 text styles per screen (up to 6 on dense operational screens). Structure: 8px rhythm with 4px adjustments, 24px mobile / 40–64px desktop margins, chapter transitions 96–144px desktop / 64–96px mobile, heading belongs to what follows when the gap above is ~3× the gap below, radii restrained at 6–12px, ~3% alternating row fill beats hairlines on long lists. Four invocation modes (Apply default; Review edits nothing; Prototype builds 3 named directions — Quiet/Editorial/Utilitarian — behind an instant switcher; Deep covers full flow). Remediation order is fixed: flow/hierarchy → layout → remove ornament → spacing/density → typography → tokens → controls/states → motion last. Brand marks and signature datum colours (a rating's gold) keep their colour; third-party logos and payment marks go monochrome; merchandising flashes are neutralised. Verification is scripted: scripts/lines.js, tints.js, density.js, bands.js (playwright-core + local Chrome), plus recon/snap/probe/run-eval from the bundled websites.md reference, which covers the CSS-override fallback mode for sites without source access.
- **Reference / source:** ericzakariasson/scandinavian-design on GitHub; bundled reference file websites.md (deep read inside ⟦S0363⟧).
- **Best for:** A whole-site calm/monochrome direction and as a restraint discipline for any section — navigation, footer, proof bands, product/commerce pages (its commerce rules: media dominant left, name/price/options/availability/buy kept together, prices at one size and weight). Trade fit: strong for premium-minimal positioning; risky where a trade brand's warmth and colour ARE the identity — the skill itself says identity wins over the rules.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0363⟧

## ⟦S0364⟧ figma/figma-code-connect — Part 13, UI Skills (rest of ui-skills.com catalog)
- **What it is:** Creates and maintains Figma Code Connect template files (`.figma.ts`) that map published Figma components to real code snippets, so a design in Figma shows the actual code component it corresponds to.
- **How it looks:** No page design — the deliverable is a code file sitting beside the component source: a header comment with the Figma URL, source path and component name, then a default export whose `example` is a `figma.code` tagged-template snippet (e.g. a `<Button variant="primary" size="lg">` with live values pulled from the Figma instance).
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. (6 steps: parse the Figma URL into fileKey + nodeId (hyphens→colons) → `get_code_connect_suggestions` to find unmapped published components → `get_context_for_code_connect` for property definitions → locate and confirm the matching code component by prop interface → write the template → validate by reading it back.)
- **Mechanism & key values:** Parserless format only: `.figma.ts` + `figma.code\`...\`` — never `.figma.tsx` / `figma.connect()` (that output is rejected). Property mapping: TEXT→getString, BOOLEAN→getBoolean (with optional true/false mapping), VARIANT→getEnum (mapping MUST list every value or unmapped values silently return undefined), INSTANCE_SWAP→getInstanceSwap, SLOT→getSlot (only for true SLOT properties); descendants via findInstance/findText/findConnectedInstance(s)/findLayers, with SelectorOptions {path, traverseInstances}. Interpolation: strings in quotes, instance results in braces, slot sections interpolated directly, booleans as conditionals. Pitfalls: never string-concatenate template results (ResultSection[] becomes [object Object]); no hasCodeConnect() guards; always check `type === 'INSTANCE'` before executeTemplate() (failures return a truthy ErrorHandle). Prerequisites: Figma MCP connected, components published to a team library, Organization/Enterprise plan, `@figma/code-connect/figma-types` in tsconfig types.
- **Reference / source:** figma/mcp-server-guide on GitHub; references api.md and advanced-patterns.md named.
- **Best for:** Design-system infrastructure — keeping Figma and code components in sync during a build. No visitor-facing section use.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0364⟧

## ⟦S0365⟧ figma/figma-code-workflows — Part 13, UI Skills (rest of ui-skills.com catalog)
- **What it is:** A routing workflow for importing local HTML or project files INTO Figma — choosing between editable Design frames, a runnable Code Layer, or standalone Code (Make) — and repairing imported previews.
- **How it looks:** Inside Figma: either editable Design layers replicating the page, or a runnable Code Layer/standalone Code file whose live preview runs the actual app. The user sees progress reports at the main stages (preparing/validating, uploading, import complete) and finishes with the returned file/layer link.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. (Flow: identify the intended output — if unclear, ask "Editable design layers or a code layer?" and stop → branch by input/output table → follow `send_code_to_figma`'s returned nextStep instructions exactly for preparation, archive, upload and recovery → report only established outcomes.)
- **Mechanism & key values:** Routing rules: running app + Design layers → load figma-generate-design (⟦S0368⟧) and call generate_figma_design; static HTML + Design layers → html_to_figma; runnable output → send_code_to_figma from this skill. Before choosing a Design Code Layer, call `whoami` — only allowed when `whoami.code_layers_enabled` is true. Destination heuristic when nothing is specified: fewer than 10 screens (or unknown) → Code Layer; 10+ screens → standalone; never ask the user to count screens. Explicit links/requests override the heuristic. Only triggers when the user explicitly names a Figma output or supplies a Figma file key/link as destination — generic "make a code project" requests must be clarified first.
- **Reference / source:** figma/mcp-server-guide on GitHub.

## ⟦S0367⟧ figma/figma-design-to-code — Part 13, UI Skills (rest of ui-skills.com catalog)
- **What it is:** The mandatory prerequisite skill before calling the Figma MCP `get_design_context` tool: the rules for implementing a Figma design as production code faithfully — visual target, asset handling, component reuse.
- **How it looks:** The deliverable is running code that visually matches the Figma design's screenshot (which must be requested with the first get_design_context call and used as the target — never shipped as an implementation asset). Static assets appear in the exact positions the design uses them; absolute positioning from the tool output is translated into the project's native layout; interactive parts are implemented as interactive code.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion of its own; any animation in the design is implemented per the design's data (motion-specific work belongs to figma-implement-motion, outside this range). (Flow: call get_design_context with `figma-design-to-code` in skillNames (prefixed `resource:` if loaded via MCP resource) → if the response is flagged sparse, correlate child node IDs with the screenshot and batch-request the visible children for high-fidelity data → inspect project paths and installed design libraries → implement reusing matching components/tokens and Code Connect mappings → verify every asset and the rendered geometry.)
- **Mechanism & key values:** Hard rules: implement exclusively from high-fidelity get_design_context responses; reuse or compose existing code components instead of raw markup/inline styles/hardcoded values; apply Code Connect at its mapped nodes and reuse the connected component unless it cannot express the design; never omit, edit, redraw or substitute a visible static asset (API/prop/data imagery stays dynamic); never override an SVG's root width/height; all assets must end up as local files — no temporary Figma asset URLs left in code; verify only the requested screen/component and note (don't alter) out-of-scope mismatches; a single substituted or misproportioned asset is a FAIL.
- **Reference / source:** figma/mcp-server-guide on GitHub.
- **Best for:** Implementing any designed section — hero, proof, gallery, forms — from a Figma file into a real build. Core process skill for design-to-code handoffs on trade sites.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0367⟧

## ⟦S0368⟧ figma/figma-generate-design — Part 13, UI Skills (rest of ui-skills.com catalog)
- **What it is:** Builds or updates full screens and multi-section views inside Figma FROM code or a description, assembling them from the file's published design system — component instances, variables and styles — instead of primitives with hardcoded values. The reverse direction of ⟦S0367⟧.
- **How it looks:** An editable Figma view (page, modal, dialog, drawer, sidebar, panel, form, dashboard) built inside one wrapper frame: auto-layout sections populated with real component instances, fills and spacing bound to variables, text and effect styles applied. A flattened screenshot of the UI inside the deliverable is a hard failure — the output must be editable layers; screenshots serve only as reference.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. (Workflow: 1 understand the deliverable — sections, components, the product's real font family (never default to Inter), and whether it contains images → 2 collect component keys (Code Connect files first, then library search, then an existing-screen inventory), variables and styles → 3 create the wrapper frame first (never build sections as page children and reparent — appendChild across calls silently fails) → 4 customise covered sections and build missing ones in retry-safe phases → 5 validate with ONE full-view screenshot, assert the font family explicitly, transfer images → 6 update path for existing views.)
- **Mechanism & key values:** Wrapper widths by container: full page 1440, modal/dialog 640, drawer/sidebar 360, panel 400 (adapt to the source's real dimensions); wrapper placed at maxX + 200 in clear space. For web apps, a parallel `generate_figma_design` capture into the same fileKey is run alongside and later deleted — MANDATORY when the view contains discrete content images (photos, avatars, logos, icons), because the Plugin API cannot fetch external image URLs; images transfer by copying `imageHash` fills. Component discovery order: Code Connect files (`*.figma.ts/.js/.tsx`, Kotlin `@FigmaConnect`, Swift `FigmaConnect`) → `get_libraries` (org libraries paginate 20 per page; community kits first page only) → `search_design_system` with ONE intent per query (no OR-packing) scoped by includeLibraryKeys → existing-screen inventory in a single read-only pass. Variables: never conclude "no variables exist" from `getLocalVariableCollectionsAsync()` returning empty — library variables are invisible to it; always also search. Text overrides via setProperties() with the discovered property keys (e.g. `"Text#2104:5"`), including checking source-code default prop values. Icons: import the codebase SVG via `figma.createNodeFromSvg` (string must include viewBox AND explicit width/height) and resize to the slot (16/20/24px typical) — never reconstruct icons from rotated primitives; currentColor imports as black and must be recoloured or variable-bound after import. Repeated elements must be componentised on the first pass (createComponent once, place instances). Set `layoutSizingHorizontal = "FILL"` only AFTER appending a section to the wrapper. Must be loaded together with figma-use (⟦S0375⟧, outside this range); `figma-generate-design` goes in the skillNames parameter of every use_figma call.
- **Reference / source:** figma/mcp-server-guide on GitHub; loads figma-use references (component-patterns, variable-patterns, text/effect-style patterns, gotchas) and its own references (discover-product-font.md, componentization.md).
- **Best for:** Recreating a built page inside Figma for client review, or generating design views from a codebase. Process tool — the deliverable lives in Figma, not on the live site.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0368⟧

## ⟦S0369⟧ figma/figma-generate-diagram — Part 13, UI Skills (rest of ui-skills.com catalog)
- **What it is:** The mandatory prerequisite before every `generate_diagram` tool call: routes a diagram request to the right type, applies universal Mermaid constraints, and produces an editable FigJam diagram from Mermaid syntax.
- **How it looks:** A clean editable diagram on a FigJam board (figma.com/board/…): flowchart boxes and arrows, sequence-diagram actors and messages, ERD tables with cardinality, state machines, or a Gantt timeline — in FigJam's default styling. Rendered Gantt charts have NO colours (styling is stripped in preprocessing) and sequence diagrams show no Mermaid notes (silently stripped); both need the hybrid use_figma pass if the user wants them.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. (Flow: 1 check the tool supports the type → 2 route to the type's reference file → 3 apply universal constraints → 4 gather real context before writing Mermaid (source code, documents, existing FigJam, other tools, or 1–2 focused user questions) → 5 decide whether the hybrid workflow is warranted → 6 call generate_diagram → 7 return the link; iterate by reusing the same fileKey.)
- **Mechanism & key values:** Supported types: flowchart, sequenceDiagram, stateDiagram/stateDiagram-v2, gantt, erDiagram. Unsupported — refuse rather than call: pie chart, mindmap, venn, class diagram, journey, timeline, quadrant, C4, git graph, requirement diagram. Universal constraints: no emojis (the tool rejects them), no `\n` escapes and no HTML in labels, never use `end`/`subgraph`/`graph` as node IDs, node IDs in camelCase with no spaces (underscores can break edge routing), quote labels containing special characters (`A["Process (main)"]`). Software-infrastructure flowcharts route to the architecture reference, not the flowchart one. Hybrid workflow (references/workflow.md) composes generate_diagram with use_figma for sticky annotations and per-node colour; extensions must use FigJam-only APIs — `figma.createPage()` throws in FigJam; organise with sections. Tool parameters: name + mermaidSyntax required; userIntent, fileKey optional; useArchitectureLayoutCode only for architecture diagrams. Never call create_new_file first — the tool creates its own file; every call without a fileKey makes a new draft FigJam, so pass the existing fileKey when iterating. After 2 failed attempts at the same diagram, stop regenerating and ask what's wrong.
- **Reference / source:** figma/mcp-server-guide on GitHub; per-type references (architecture, flowchart, sequence, erd, state, gantt) and workflow.md named.
- **Best for:** Diagrams as content — a process/how-it-works flow drawn as a real diagram, or internal architecture/pipeline visuals. On a trade homepage the flowchart type maps naturally to a process section; the deliverable is a FigJam board, not web code.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0369⟧

## ⟦S0370⟧ figma/figma-generate-library — Part 13, UI Skills (rest of ui-skills.com catalog)
- **What it is:** Builds or updates a professional-grade design system inside Figma from a codebase — variables/tokens, component libraries with proper variant sets and variable bindings, theming modes, foundation documentation, or code↔Figma reconciliation. Teaches WHAT to build in WHAT ORDER; the companion figma-use skill (⟦S0375⟧, outside this range) teaches the Plugin API calls, and both must be loaded together.
- **How it looks:** In Figma: organised variable collections (primitives → semantic aliases), text/effect styles, component pages with variant grids laid out properly, and review frames showing component states as instances in one compact frame. Scope is locked before any mutation — tokens only, a single component/family, a full library, or a reconciliation — and the deliverable never silently grows beyond it.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. (Scoped paths: tokens → create collections/modes/aliases/scopes/code syntax + styles, validate, stop. Single component → reuse compatible foundations, create only missing tokens, build variants/properties/bindings, validate. Full library → discovery + gap analysis → foundations → file structure (cover, getting-started, foundations, component, utility pages) → components in dependency order → integration/QA incl. Code Connect. Reconciliation → inventory, diff against code, update only affected assets in place.)
- **Mechanism & key values:** Token architecture by count: <50 tokens = single collection, 2 modes (Light/Dark); 50–200 = standard (Primitives 1 mode + Color semantic Light/Dark + Spacing + Typography); 200+ = advanced (multiple semantic collections, 4–8 modes). Every variable gets scopes (never ALL_SCOPES: fills FRAME_FILL/SHAPE_FILL, text TEXT_FILL, border STROKE_COLOR, spacing GAP, radii CORNER_RADIUS, primitives hidden []) and code syntax (WEB uses the var() wrapper: `var(--color-bg-primary)`; Android/iOS no wrapper). Semantic variables alias primitives — never duplicate raw values. Components: INSTANCE_SWAP for icons, never a variant per icon; cap variant matrices at Size × Style × State ≤ 30 combinations or split into sub-components; variants must be manually grid-positioned after combineAsVariants (they stack at 0,0). Execution rules: use_figma calls strictly sequential, never parallel; setCurrentPageAsync at most once per script; colours 0–1 range; fonts loaded before any text write; never use figma.notify() (it throws); never guess node IDs. State lives in a ledger file at /tmp/design-system-state-{RUN_ID}.json, re-read every turn, with an idempotency check (query by name + ledger ID) before every create and a resume protocol that rescans the file by name. Naming: slash-separated variables (color/bg/primary, spacing/xs–2xl, radius/none–full), primitives blue/50→blue/900, variants named `Property=Value, Property=Value`. Decision forks: when code ≠ Figma or a library match is close-but-not-exact, surface both with provenance and ask — don't silently default. Bundled helper scripts: inspectFileStructure, createVariableCollection, createSemanticTokens, createComponentWithVariants, bindVariablesToComponent, createDocumentationPage, validateCreation, cleanupOrphans.
- **Reference / source:** figma/mcp-server-guide on GitHub; references discovery-phase.md, token-creation.md, documentation-creation.md, component-creation.md, code-connect-setup.md, naming-conventions.md, error-recovery.md.
- **Best for:** Design-system foundations behind a build — the token/component layer a multi-page trade site design would live in. Infrastructure, not a section design.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0370⟧
## ⟦S0371⟧ figma/figma-generative-plugins — Part 13 — UI Skills, rest of the ui-skills.com catalog
- **What it is:** A mandatory-prerequisite workflow skill for authoring reusable generative Figma plugins through the Figma MCP server (`create_generative_plugin` / `update_generative_plugin`). It governs how a plugin is scaffolded, read, rewritten and shipped — it is design tooling, not a page design.
- **How it looks:** Nothing on a web page. The visible artefact lives inside the Figma Design editor: a plugin panel with functional UI for its core workflow — configurable inputs, one clear primary action, and status or validation feedback — plus whatever the plugin draws on the canvas (the starter scaffold draws squares; the authored plugin replaces that with the requested behaviour).
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. The sequence is a workflow, not an animation: create the scaffold once → read every scaffold source file → replace `code.ts` (and `ui.html` when the UI changes) with the complete authored plugin → update with a specific commit message.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Preflight rules: plugins run in the Figma Design editor only; every plugin must ship functional UI even with no inputs; never embed API keys, OAuth tokens or signed URLs in plugin source. `update_generative_plugin` can replace `code.ts` and `ui.html` but cannot replace `manifest.json` or create new files; `figma.showUI(__html__, ...)` stays in `code.ts`. On a build error: smallest correction, retry once, then surface the error. Completion reports a try-it URL of the form `https://www.figma.com/file/new?try-tool-resource-content-id=<id>&try-tool-resource-type=gen_tool&type=design&mode=design`.
- **Reference / source:** figma/mcp-server-guide (GitHub), the official Figma MCP server guide skills.
- **Best for:** Building Figma plugins as internal design tooling. No homepage-section use and no trade fit — it produces no visitor-facing design.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0371⟧

## ⟦S0372⟧ figma/figma-implement-motion — Part 13 — UI Skills, rest of the ui-skills.com catalog
- **What it is:** A production pipeline skill that translates animations authored in Figma into runnable application code — motion.dev snippets for React, CSS `@keyframes` for vanilla targets, or values adapted into the codebase's existing motion library. It moves motion that already exists in a Figma file into code without re-inventing it.
- **How it looks:** Whatever the Figma design itself animates, reproduced faithfully in the browser: the same elements moving with the designer's exact keyframe values, easings, timings and transform origins — staggered text-group reveals, coordinated multi-node timelines that loop or boomerang, SVG paths that draw themselves. Nothing has a "house look"; fidelity to the source design is the whole point.
- **Frame by frame:** Driven entirely by the source design's data: `get_motion_context` returns each animated node's tracks; text animations start each group at `startMs + orderPosition × staggerStepMs` and play for `groupDurationMs`; nodes sharing one timeline are driven from a single `timelineCohorts` entry (`durationMs`, `loopMode: 'once' | 'loop' | 'boomerang'`). Trigger, steps and end state are whatever the Figma author keyframed — the skill forbids fabricating motion for nodes that have none.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Two tools linked by node id: `get_design_context` = structure of record (layout, assets, `data-node-id`, split-node markers `data-motion-keys` / `data-motion-wrapper-for` / `data-motion-transform-template`); `get_motion_context` = source of truth for values, with `recursive: true` capped at 500 nodes. Pre-generated `codeSnippets` are used verbatim — never regenerated from fallback `keyframeBindings` (that loses custom beziers, spring approximations, overshoot). Interleaved-transform rule, with the skill's worked numbers: a `rotate` snippet of [45, 125, 125] over a `rotate-45` static base must animate the offset [0, 80, 80], or the base rotation applies twice. `transformOrigin` is per element, including nested scalers. Motion.dev imports from `motion/react`; exact id match beats `fallbackNodeId`; animated groups lose `display: contents` for a real positioned wrapper. Hard rules: any added motion softens or disables under `prefers-reduced-motion`; validate one animation end-to-end before batching; repeated motion is factored into one parameterized component/variants object, never pasted per element; expiring asset URLs are downloaded locally, never referenced.
- **Reference / source:** figma/mcp-server-guide (GitHub); motion.dev; SwiftUI targets receive the CSS snippet format (no SwiftUI snippets are emitted).
- **Best for:** Implementing motion for any section (hero, proof, work, process…) when the motion was first designed in Figma. Trade fit is indirect: it is a fidelity pipeline, not a design source — it invents no mechanisms of its own.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0372⟧

## ⟦S0373⟧ figma/figma-shaders — Part 13 — UI Skills, rest of the ui-skills.com catalog
- **What it is:** A mandatory-prerequisite workflow skill for authoring shaders in Figma through the MCP server (`create_shader` / `update_shader`). Shaders come in two kinds: `effect` (samples and transforms the rendered layer beneath it) and `fill` (generates pixels with no input raster). The kind can never be silently switched during an update.
- **How it looks:** Inside Figma: an effect shader reads as post-processing over a layer — blur, distortion, glow, colour grading, pixelation, halftone. A fill shader reads as a generated surface — gradients, patterns, noise, textures, procedural backgrounds. Controls for values a user is likely to tune per layer are exposed; implementation details stay hardcoded.
- **Frame by frame:** Static unless authored otherwise. A shader becomes animated only when its source reads time-related frame inputs, and mouse-reactive only when it reads `frame.mousePosition`; the authoring rules require `metadata.isAnimated: true` / `metadata.usesMouse: true` to match the source exactly. Prefer `frame.time` — an absolute millisecond clock (seconds = `Number(frame.time) * 0.001`) — so skipped frames do not change the result. If the tool reports animation or mouse input unavailable, that is a terminal capability gate: author a static shader whose properties can be keyframed in Motion mode instead.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Workflow mirrors the plugin skill: resolve `planKey` → `create_shader` once (scaffold only) → `get_shader` and read every source (or `includeSource: true`) → author the complete replacement `main.ts` → `update_shader` with the same `kind`, `files: [{ path: "main.ts", content }]` and a specific commit message. Numeric ranges stay bounded with visually useful defaults. Try-it URL uses `try-tool-resource-type` = `gen_effect` or `gen_fill` by kind.
- **Reference / source:** figma/mcp-server-guide (GitHub), Figma MCP server guide; authoring detail lives in its `references/authoring.md` (module shape, WebGPU lifecycle, parameter schemas, WGSL failure checklist).
- **Best for:** Designing shader-based backgrounds, textures and layer effects inside Figma — a design-stage tool. No direct homepage-section use; relevant only if a build's visual effects are first prototyped as Figma shaders.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0373⟧

## ⟦S0374⟧ figma/figma-spec — Part 13 — UI Skills, rest of the ui-skills.com catalog
- **What it is:** The required skill for creating, reading, editing, reviewing or commenting on Figma specs — GitHub-Flavored Markdown documents stored under a `SPEC_BLOCK` node, either standalone or embedded in a Design or FigJam file. It covers PRDs, briefs and RFCs written inside Figma.
- **How it looks:** A rendered Markdown document on the Figma canvas: an H1 title block kept first (never removed, nothing inserted before it), bold table header rows, underline written as `<ins>` (including combined forms like `<ins>**bold and underlined**</ins>` — `<u>` only works in HTML imports), images embedded as GFM image syntax (base64 data URLs are decoded and uploaded; remote URLs are fetched server-side, disallowed hosts rejected), and comment threads anchored to exact spans of text, marked inline as `[comment:<uuid>]…[/comment:<uuid>]` pairs.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. It is a document format, not an animation system.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Gate first: always call `whoami` and confirm the owning plan has `specs_enabled: true`; never infer the plan from the file key. Discovery: resolve a URL `node-id` and require `type === "SPEC_BLOCK"` plus `specBlockType === "DOCUMENT"`, else search pages with `findAllWithCriteria({ types: ['SPEC_BLOCK'] })`, loading other pages one at a time. Content calls: `getContent` (body field is `markdown`, supports `offset`/`maxLines` paging), destructive `setContent` only for an empty first draft or explicit whole-document replacement, and multiplayer-safe surgical `editContent` as the default — each `oldText` must match exactly once or the edit fails with no changes. Markdown is passed as plain strings, never base64 (base64 is only for image data URLs). Comments: `anchorText` must appear exactly once in the rendered spec, disambiguated by a longer `contextText`; thread reads/replies take the root comment UUID, never a reply UUID. Comment markers overlapping an edit must be preserved exactly or the thread detaches. Shared specs use portable links (GitHub permalinks), never local paths or localhost.
- **Reference / source:** figma/mcp-server-guide (GitHub), Figma MCP server guide.
- **Best for:** Specs, briefs and PRDs kept inside Figma. No homepage-section use and no trade fit — documentation tooling only.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0374⟧

## ⟦S0375⟧ figma/figma-use — Part 13 — UI Skills, rest of the ui-skills.com catalog
- **What it is:** The foundational Plugin API skill for the `use_figma` MCP tool — mandatory before every `use_figma` call. It is the operating contract for executing JavaScript in a Figma file: creating and editing nodes, variables/tokens, components and variants, auto-layout, fills, and programmatic file inspection. The editor companions in this range (⟦S0376⟧ FigJam, ⟦S0377⟧ motion, ⟦S0378⟧ Slides) and the workflow skills (⟦S0379⟧, ⟦S0380⟧, ⟦S0382⟧) all build on this one skill; they are separate skills, not duplicates of it.
- **How it looks:** Whatever design gets built on the Figma canvas — frames, components, token sets — following the target file's own existing conventions, which the skill requires inspecting first. Its one self-described visual device: sections under construction carry `node.placeholder = true`, a shimmer overlay marking work in progress, which must always be removed when the section is finished.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion prescribed. The "sequence" is the incremental build workflow: inspect the file → create tokens/variables → create components → compose layouts from instances → one composition screenshot → one post-fix screenshot if needed → stop.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Plain JavaScript with top-level `await`; the `return` value is the only output channel (JSON-serialized; `console.log` is invisible, `figma.notify()` throws). Colours are 0–1 range; a paint's `color` is `{r, g, b}` only, opacity at paint level; fills/strokes are read-only arrays (clone, modify, reassign); `setBoundVariableForPaint` returns a new paint that must be captured. Text edits follow one recipe — load the node's current fonts (`getStyledTextSegments(['fontName'])`, verify style names via `listAvailableFontsAsync`, never guess "SemiBold" vs "Semi Bold") → await → mutate → return IDs; `lineHeight`/`letterSpacing` take `{unit, value}`. Pages: `await figma.setCurrentPageAsync(page)`, at most one switch per call, page context resets to the first page every call, multi-page work fans out as parallel calls in one message. Sizing: `layoutSizingHorizontal/Vertical` take FIXED/HUG/FILL (HUG only on an auto-layout frame or its TEXT child; FILL only on a non-absolute child of an auto-layout frame); frame-level `primaryAxisSizingMode`/`counterAxisSizingMode` take FIXED/AUTO — the two enums must not be crossed; `resize()` resets sizing modes to FIXED so it runs before sizing is set; wrapping text needs `textAutoResize = 'HEIGHT'` plus an explicit fixed width. Related children go in `figma.createAutoLayout()`, not absolute x/y frames. Efficient APIs: `node.query()` CSS-like selectors, `node.set(props)` batch updates (`layoutMode` always applies first), `node.screenshot()` (default 0.5x, auto-capped so the largest dimension ≤ 1024px; explicit scale bypasses the cap). New top-level nodes must be positioned away from (0,0). Every write returns all created/mutated node IDs; variables always get explicit `scopes` (default ALL_SCOPES pollutes every picker). Editor modes gate node types: design files block Sticky/Connector/Slide etc.; `figma.createPage()` exists only in Design files.
- **Reference / source:** figma/mcp-server-guide (GitHub), Figma MCP server guide; its reference docs (gotchas, common-patterns, plugin-api-standalone.d.ts) are the API source of truth.
- **Best for:** Any programmatic Figma build or edit — the base layer under the other Figma skills. No direct homepage-section use; it builds designs in Figma rather than supplying web design patterns.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0375⟧

## ⟦S0376⟧ figma/figma-use-figjam — Part 13 — UI Skills, rest of the ui-skills.com catalog
- **What it is:** The FigJam companion to ⟦S0375⟧ figma-use: FigJam-specific rules for running `use_figma` in a whiteboard file (`figma.com/board/...`) — sections, stickies, connectors, shapes with text, tables, code blocks and labels. A separate editor skill, not a duplicate of figma-use; figma-use still carries the foundational Plugin API rules.
- **How it looks:** A FigJam board: coloured sections organising the canvas, sticky notes, connector lines with arrows and labels wiring a diagram, shapes with embedded text, tables and small numbered/lettered label markers. Text defaults differ by node — sticky and shape sublayers default to Inter Medium; a connector's text is invalid until its font is set — so fonts are always loaded from `node.text.fontName`, never hardcoded.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. Boards are static artefacts; the skill's sequences are inspection and build order (inspect with `get_figjam` first, batch-load deferred tool schemas in one `ToolSearch` call, load only the reference docs the task needs — in a single parallel batch when several are needed).
- **Mechanism & key values:** `get_figjam` is the inspection tool — it returns the full node tree as XML with the IDs later calls need. `get_metadata` does not work on FigJam files (design-mode only, fails immediately); `get_screenshot` requires a valid nodeId. `figma.createPage()` throws in FigJam — a FigJam file has one implicit page, organised with sections instead. Images enter a FigJam file only via `upload_assets` (single-use upload URLs; pass `nodeIds` to attach uploads as fills to existing nodes, omit to drop them on the board as new layers). Text mutations follow the same load-font → await → mutate → return-IDs recipe as Design files.
- **Reference / source:** figma/mcp-server-guide (GitHub), Figma MCP server guide; reference docs cover board planning, sections, stickies, connectors, tables, labels and the canonical FigJam colour palettes.
- **Best for:** Workshop, planning and diagram boards in FigJam — the execution layer under ⟦S0379⟧ generate-project-plan. No homepage-section use and no trade fit.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0376⟧

## ⟦S0377⟧ figma/figma-use-motion — Part 13 — UI Skills, rest of the ui-skills.com catalog
- **What it is:** The motion companion to ⟦S0375⟧ figma-use: animating Figma nodes from `use_figma` — manual keyframes, animation styles, reusable local custom animation styles, text animation, easing and timeline duration. Load it alongside figma-use for any task that adds, edits or inspects animation on a node; static design work uses figma-use alone.
- **How it looks:** Inside Figma's Motion mode: layers that translate, rotate, scale, fade and blur along a timeline; fill and stroke colours that shift over time; text that reveals character by character (typewriter) or staggers by word, line or paragraph via the native `TextStagger` preset, whose Position, Rotation, Scale, Opacity and Blur sub-styles are configurable. What a screenshot shows is only the timeline's resting state — motion itself is verified by rendering video and sampling frames.
- **Frame by frame:** Keyframes on public transform fields (`TRANSLATION_X`, `TRANSLATION_Y`, `ROTATION`, `SCALE_X`, `SCALE_Y`, `SCALE_XY`) plus opacity, blur and colour tracks, played over the containing top-level frame's timeline, whose duration is read/written in seconds (`node.timelines`, `node.setTimelineDuration(id, seconds)` — extend it, never shorten unless asked). Easing is set with the public object shape `{ type: 'EASE_OUT', easingFunctionCubicBezier?, easingFunctionSpring? }` — ease-in-out is exactly `EASE_IN_AND_OUT` (or `EASE_IN_AND_OUT_BACK`); `HOLD` easing holds a value then cuts. For text: a `TextStagger`'s `duration` is the total stagger span, not per-character time, and it is applied to the existing text node with characters, formatting and wrapping preserved.
