## ⟦S0399⟧ iart-ai/60fps-animation — Part 13 — UI Skills — rest of the ui-skills.com catalog
- **What it is:** A performance discipline for web animation: eliminate jank by animating only compositor properties (`transform`, `opacity`) and converting every layout/paint animation into an equivalent cheap one.
- **How it looks:** The same motion the designer intended — a card sliding 200px and doubling in width, a shadow deepening on hover, a panel opening to full content height, cards reordering in a grid — but running at a locked 60/120fps with no stutter, no per-frame layout bands in DevTools, and no stretched text (FLIP keeps content crisp where a raw `scaleX` would distort it).
- **Frame by frame:** Trigger (hover / state change / layout change) → the browser skips layout and paint entirely and the compositor interpolates `transform`/`opacity` on the GPU → element lands exactly on its real final layout (FLIP) or final visual state. For height: the grid track animates 0fr → 1fr and content is revealed by overflow clipping rather than a measured height tween.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Property mapping table (width/height → scale or FLIP; top/left/margin → translate; box-shadow → opacity of a `::after` holding a pre-painted shadow, e.g. `0 12px 28px rgba(0,0,0,0.35)` fading in over 300ms; background-position → translate on a child layer; filter blur → cross-fade). FLIP via WAAPI: measure First/Last rects, invert with `translate(dx,dy) scale(sx,sy)`, animate to `none` over 300ms with `cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)`. Height-to-auto: `interpolate-size: allow-keywords` (Chrome 129+) or the grid `0fr→1fr` fallback with `overflow: hidden; min-height: 0`. Batch all layout reads before writes to avoid thrashing. `will-change: transform` just-in-time only, removed when idle. Verification bar: DevTools Performance shows no Layout/Paint per frame; deliverable is one self-contained HTML with a `?t=N` freeze harness.
- **Reference / source:** iart-ai web-animation-skills on GitHub. No specific sites named.
- **Best for:** Every animated section — it is the performance gate for heroes, galleries, accordions (forms/FAQ), card grids (work/gallery, services). Trade fit: essential on trades sites, which are image-heavy and often viewed on mid-range phones.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0399⟧

## ⟦S0400⟧ iart-ai/accessible-animation — Part 13 — UI Skills — rest of the ui-skills.com catalog
- **What it is:** The reduced-motion companion to ⟦S0399⟧ in the same iart-ai family: honor `prefers-reduced-motion` by tiering motion (remove / soften / keep) instead of switching all animation off.
- **How it looks:** For a reduced-motion visitor, the same page with the dangerous motion gone: no parallax layers sliding, no zooming hero, no spinning or auto-playing carousel; a card that normally slides in over 600ms instead cross-fades in 150ms; focus rings, color transitions and loading spinners still animate normally so nothing teleports and state stays readable.
- **Frame by frame:** Trigger (OS setting on, or toggled live mid-session) → Tier-1 motion (parallax, large slides/zooms, 3D spin, marquees, smooth-scroll hijack, pinned scroll scenes) is removed outright → Tier-2 motion is replaced by an opacity fade ≤200ms → Tier-3 motion (fades, color, focus rings, spinners) plays unchanged → end state identical to the full-motion page, just arrived at without displacement.
- **Mechanism & key values:** CSS global safety net uses `0.01ms` durations (never `0s`, so `transitionend`/`animationend` still fire) plus `animation-iteration-count: 1` and `scroll-behavior: auto`; positive form `(prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)` opts elaborate motion in. JS side: `matchMedia` helper + `change` listener; GSAP via `gsap.matchMedia()` conditions; Lenis is not instantiated at all when reduced; React `useReducedMotion` hook (SSR default `false`, sync in `useEffect`; Framer example cuts duration 0.5s → 0.15s and drops the `y: 40` offset). WCAG anchors: 2.3.3 (AAA), technique C39, and 2.2.2 — any auto-playing motion over 5 seconds needs a pause control regardless of the media query. Verification: screenshot both paths mid-animation (Playwright `--reduced-motion=reduce` + a `?reduce=1` harness flag).
- **Reference / source:** iart-ai web-animation-skills on GitHub; WCAG 2.3.3 / 2.2.2 / C39 named.
- **Best for:** A mandatory layer over every animated section (hero, work/gallery, process, testimonials) — pair it with whichever motion skill builds the effect. Trade fit: high — trades audiences skew older and include vestibular-sensitive users.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0400⟧

## ⟦S0401⟧ iart-ai/ascii-animation — Part 13 — UI Skills — rest of the ui-skills.com catalog
- **What it is:** Renders motion entirely out of text characters — generative character fields, image/video converted live to ASCII, a Three.js scene post-processed into ASCII, or terminal/CLI intros and loaders.
- **How it looks:** A block of monospace characters whose density forms a moving picture: a plasma field rippling through ` .:-=+*#%@`, a photo or video playing as shifting letters (bright areas dense with `@%#`, dark areas blank), or a rotating 3D scene drawn in green-on-black characters. Character cells are taller than wide, so images are sampled with roughly half as many rows as columns to avoid vertical stretch.
- **Frame by frame:** Trigger (page load / rAF loop) → each frame samples the source (sine-field math, an offscreen canvas of the image/video, or the WebGL render) → every pixel's luminance (0.2126R + 0.7152G + 0.0722B) picks a character from the brightness ramp → the full grid is rewritten as one string (or per-cell `fillText`) → next frame the values shift and the picture moves. Terminal variant: cursor hidden, frame printed at home position, throttled to 12–24fps for a retro feel.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Ramps: short 10-level ` .:-=+*#%@`; Paul Bourke's standard 70-level ramp for photo fidelity. Aspect correction: `rows = Math.round(cols * (imgH/imgW) * 0.5)`. `<pre>` + `textContent` is fine to ~120×60 chars at 30fps; canvas `fillText` for per-character color or 60fps. Three.js route: `AsciiEffect` from three/addons renders the scene as ASCII (render through the effect, not the renderer). Terminal: ANSI `\x1b[H` home per frame (cheaper than clear), `\x1b[?25l` hide cursor, truecolor via `\x1b[38;2;R;G;Bm`. Deliverable: one HTML file, injectable time + fixed seed, `?t=N` renders exactly one deterministic frame.
- **Reference / source:** iart-ai web-animation-skills on GitHub; Paul Bourke's 70-level ramp; Three.js AsciiEffect.
- **Best for:** Retro/hacker or terminal-themed moments — a loader, an intro, an easter-egg background. Trade fit: weak for trades homepages (reads techy, not trustworthy); at most a novelty preloader. Flag as SITUATIONAL.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0401⟧

## ⟦S0402⟧ iart-ai/glassmorphism — Part 13 — UI Skills — rest of the ui-skills.com catalog
- **What it is:** Frosted and "liquid" glass UI: translucent panels that blur whatever sits behind them, rimmed with a bright edge of light, plus an SVG-refraction variant where the background visibly bends through the panel.
- **How it looks:** A card, nav bar or modal floating over a photo or busy gradient: the backdrop shows through as soft color, the panel fill is a faint white wash, the top edge catches a bright highlight line while the bottom is shaded, and a layered shadow lifts it off the page. On hover the frost deepens, the highlight brightens and the panel rises slightly. The liquid-glass hero version slowly churns, bending the backdrop like a thick lens with a specular sweep crossing it.
- **Frame by frame:** Entrance → panel starts clear (`backdrop-filter: blur(0)`, opacity 0, 16px low) and resolves into frost as it rises into place. Hover → blur 16px → 24px, saturate 160% → 180%, fill alpha rises, panel translates up 4px, shadow grows. Liquid variant (continuous) → an animated turbulence field displaces the panel's pixels in slow waves on a 12–20s cycle while a skewed white gradient sweeps the surface.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Four required ingredients: frost = `backdrop-filter: blur(16px) saturate(160%)` (with `-webkit-` prefix), translucency = background alpha 0.08–0.18, edge = 1px border `rgba(255,255,255,0.25)` plus a masked `::before` lit-corner ring, depth = `0 8px 32px rgba(0,0,0,0.25)` + `inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,0.35)` + `inset 0 -1px 0 rgba(0,0,0,0.12)`. Frost tiers: light chrome blur 8–12px / alpha 0.08–0.14; heavy modal/login blur 24–40px / alpha 0.10–0.18. Anti-banding grain: `feTurbulence` noise `::after` at opacity ≤ 0.06. Hover transition 0.4s, transform easing `cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1)`; animating blur radius is the expensive path — keep deltas small. Liquid refraction: `feDisplacementMap` scale 8–14 subtle / 20–30 pronounced / >40 molten, `baseFrequency` 0.008–0.012, one hero element only. Fallbacks are mandatory: `prefers-reduced-transparency` → solid panel (`#1a1a2e`), `@supports not (backdrop-filter)` → near-opaque fill, text contrast ≥ 4.5:1 against the brightest backdrop region.
- **Reference / source:** iart-ai web-animation-skills on GitHub; Apple's "liquid glass" style named as the reference look.
- **Best for:** Navigation bars and CTA/call panels floating over hero photography, modals, login/quote-form panels. Trade fit: works over real job-site photos; keep counts low (each glass element re-blurs its backdrop — a dozen tanks scroll FPS).
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0402⟧

## ⟦S0403⟧ iart-ai/gsap-web — Part 13 — UI Skills — rest of the ui-skills.com catalog
- **What it is:** The GSAP workhorse skill: timelines, ScrollTrigger pinning/scrubbing, SplitText reveals, Flip layout transitions, and correct Lenis/Locomotive smooth-scroll wiring. All GSAP plugins are free since 3.12, including commercial use.
- **How it looks:** Sequenced hero entrances (headline lines rising out of clipped masks, sub-copy and CTA following with overlap), sections that pin to the viewport while their content animates across 2,000px of scroll, horizontal-scroll galleries, parallax panels, and elements that glide between grid and list layouts without a jump.
- **Frame by frame:** Hero: timeline plays — title rises from `yPercent: 100` inside an overflow-hidden line mask → sub-copy fades/rises 0.3s before the title finishes → CTA scales from 0.9 as the previous tween starts. Scroll sections: trigger top hits viewport top → section pins → scroll progress scrubs the tween (with `scrub: 1` the animation catches up over 1s) → at `end: "+=2000"` the pin releases and the page continues. Layout change: Flip records positions → DOM changes instantly → elements animate the visual difference over 0.6s with 0.05 stagger.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Timeline defaults example: `power3.out`, 0.6s; position params `"-=0.3"` overlap, `"<"` align to previous start. ScrollTrigger: `start: "top top"`, `scrub: true` exact or a number for smoothing lag, `ease: "none"` for scrubbed tweens, `toggleActions: "play pause resume reverse"`. Lenis sync (the critical recipe): `lenis.on("scroll", ScrollTrigger.update)` + drive Lenis from `gsap.ticker` with time × 1000 (seconds → ms) + `gsap.ticker.lagSmoothing(0)`; never a second rAF loop, never `scrollerProxy` under Lenis (required under Locomotive). SplitText line reveal: `yPercent: 100`, stagger 0.08, 0.7s, `power4.out`, split only after `document.fonts.ready`. Easings: `power2/3.out` entrances, `power2.inOut` on-screen moves, `back.out(1.7)` pops, `elastic.out(1, 0.3)` sparingly. Performance: transform/opacity only, `ScrollTrigger.batch()` for repeated reveals, `gsap.context()`/`ctx.revert()` cleanup in SPAs, `prefers-reduced-motion` gate (skip Lenis, native scroll).
- **Reference / source:** iart-ai web-animation-skills on GitHub; GSAP (GreenSock) and its ScrollTrigger / SplitText / Flip / MotionPath / MorphSVG plugins; Lenis and Locomotive Scroll.
- **Best for:** Hero entrances, pinned process/how-it-works sections, horizontal work galleries, parallax proof sections — the core scroll-storytelling engine for a homepage. Trade fit: excellent; this is the main mechanism family behind scroll-driven trades sections.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0403⟧

## ⟦S0404⟧ iart-ai/lottie-animation — Part 13 — UI Skills — rest of the ui-skills.com catalog
- **What it is:** Integrates After Effects animation exported as Lottie (`.json` or zipped `.lottie`) into web/mobile, with playback, segment, scroll-drive and runtime-recoloring control via the dotLottie runtime.
- **How it looks:** Crisp resolution-independent vector animation playing in a canvas: a looping illustrated scene in a hero or empty state, an animated icon that plays a "loading" loop then a "checked" segment, a vector illustration whose frames advance as the visitor scrolls through its section, or the same animation recolored instantly for a dark theme without a re-export.
- **Frame by frame:** Trigger options: autoplay loop plays continuously; hover/click (via lottie-interactivity modes scroll / hover / click / play / cursor) starts the mapped frame range; scroll → autoplay off, scroll progress 0–1 through the section is mapped to `setFrame(p * (totalFrames − 1))` so the illustration scrubs with the page; state sequences play one segment, fire `complete`, then switch to the idle segment loop.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Prefer `.lottie` over `.json` (60–80% smaller, can bundle images + themes); runtime `@lottiefiles/dotlottie-web` (canvas + WASM) over legacy lottie-web except for SVG-renderer `.json` needs. Controls: `play/pause/stop`, `setSpeed(1.5)`, `setMode("forward"|"reverse"|"bounce"|"reverse-bounce")`, `setFrame(42)`, `setSegment(30, 90)`; events `load` (totalFrames available), `complete`, `frame`. Theming: embedded dotLottie themes via `setTheme("dark")`, or brittle manual JSON walk patching `layers[].shapes[]` `c.k` RGBA arrays. Mobile parity: lottie-ios, lottie-android, lottie-react-native with the same segment/progress concepts. Optimization: lazy-load offscreen players, pause offscreen via IntersectionObserver, file size tracks keyframe/path complexity not duration. Reduced motion: never autoplay a loop — static frame or a play control.
- **Reference / source:** iart-ai web-animation-skills on GitHub; LottieFiles dotLottie, Bodymovin / After Effects export.
- **Best for:** Animated icons and spot illustrations (process steps, empty states, success moments), a lightweight hero illustration where video is too heavy. Trade fit: good for icon-level motion (phone, calendar, checkmark) if artwork exists; it needs an AE-authored asset, so it cannot be improvised from photos.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0404⟧

## ⟦S0405⟧ iart-ai/micro-interaction — Part 13 — UI Skills — rest of the ui-skills.com catalog
- **What it is:** Small functional UI motion — hover/press/focus feedback, toggles, toasts, drawers, modals, list add/remove/reorder and shared-element transitions — built with Framer Motion (motion/react) or pure modern CSS. The direct ancestor of the transitions.dev recipes in ⟦S0409⟧ (same icon-swap numbers: scale 0.25, blur), but library-based rather than copy-paste CSS.
- **How it looks:** A button that dips to scale 0.96 the instant it is pressed and springs back; a toast that rises 8px while fading in, then leaves faster than it arrived; a card that "magic moves" — the same element visibly glides and resizes into its expanded state instead of cutting; list items that slide aside to make room when one is removed instead of jumping.
- **Frame by frame:** Press → scale 0.96 immediately under the finger/cursor → release → spring back. Enter → opacity 0 + 8px offset → ease-out into place (slower) → exit → same path reversed but faster (ease-in). Layout change → element's old and new positions are bridged by a transform spring so it travels continuously. Loading → success → error morphs within the one mounted element (spinner becomes checkmark) rather than swapping components.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Duration band 100–250ms for micro-interactions; anything over ~400ms feels laggy as click feedback. Transform/opacity only. Springs: `stiffness: 400, damping: 30` snappy default; `damping: 12` for visible bounce; layout springs `stiffness: 500, damping: 40`. Easings: entrance `cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)`, overshoot `cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1)`, standard move `cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1)`. Exit animations require `AnimatePresence` with stable keys; `mode="popLayout"` for toasts/lists so exiting items don't hold space. Shared elements: matching `layoutId` on both elements. CSS-only path: `@starting-style` for enter-from values + `transition-behavior: allow-discrete` to animate to/from `display: none`. Gotcha: plain `layout` distorts border-radius/text mid-flight — counter-scale children or use `layout="position"`. State freeze harness: `?state=idle|hover|open`.
- **Reference / source:** iart-ai web-animation-skills on GitHub; Framer Motion / motion/react.
- **Best for:** Forms (submit feedback, toggles), call/CTA buttons, FAQ accordions, mobile navigation drawers, toast confirmations after a quote request. Trade fit: high — this is the polish layer on every interactive element of a trades homepage.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0405⟧

## ⟦S0406⟧ iart-ai/page-transition-animation — Part 13 — UI Skills — rest of the ui-skills.com catalog
- **What it is:** Page/route transition animation for Next.js App Router — and specifically the fix for Framer Motion `AnimatePresence` exit animations silently never firing on navigation. Two solutions: a pathname-keyed AnimatePresence with a FrozenRouter, or the native View Transitions API.
- **How it looks:** Navigating fades/slides the old page out (opacity to 0, −12px up) and the new page in (+12px rise to rest) as one continuous move, with the outgoing page still showing its own content while it leaves — instead of the default instant cut or a flash of the new page's content inside the old page's exit.
- **Frame by frame:** Click a link → router begins navigation → the outgoing page (frozen on its old route context) plays its exit: opacity 1 → 0, y 0 → −12px over 0.3s → with `mode="wait"` the exit fully completes → the new page mounts and enters: opacity 0 → 1, y 12 → 0 → end state is the new page at rest. View Transitions variant: the browser snapshots old and new DOM and cross-fades the snapshots (0.25s fade each way in the example CSS).
- **Mechanism & key values:** Solution A: `template.tsx` (remounts per navigation — `layout.tsx` persists and must not be used), `AnimatePresence mode="wait" initial={false}`, child keyed `key={pathname}`, and FrozenRouter snapshotting `LayoutRouterContext` in a `useRef` so the exiting tree renders its own content; transition 0.3s with ease `[0.22, 1, 0.36, 1]`; keep durations ~0.2–0.4s so `mode="wait"` doesn't feel laggy. Solution B: `@view-transition { navigation: auto; }` or `document.startViewTransition(() => router.push(href))` guarded by a feature check, or the `next-view-transitions` library with its own `Link`. Shared elements via `view-transition-name`. Caveats: `LayoutRouterContext` is a Next internal whose import path can change on upgrade; every file needs `'use client'`; reduced motion drops the slide to a short crossfade.
- **Reference / source:** iart-ai web-animation-skills on GitHub; Next.js App Router, Framer Motion, the View Transitions API, next-view-transitions.
- **Best for:** Multi-page sites (inner service/town pages) where moving between pages should feel app-like. Trade fit: limited for single-file homepage previews (no router), directly relevant when a build grows real inner pages; the crossfade pattern itself ports to any view swap.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0406⟧

## ⟦S0407⟧ iart-ai/svg-animation — Part 13 — UI Skills — rest of the ui-skills.com catalog
- **What it is:** SVG motion techniques: stroke draw-on, path morphing, motion along a path, and animated gradients/filters — via CSS, SMIL, or GSAP.
- **How it looks:** A line, signature, logo or map outline drawing itself onto the screen stroke by stroke; a hamburger icon melting into a close X (or play into pause); a dot or rocket travelling along a curved route, rotating to follow its direction; a sheen of light sweeping repeatedly across a gradient logo.
- **Frame by frame:** Draw-on: the path starts fully hidden (dash offset equal to its length) → on trigger the offset animates to 0 over e.g. 1.4s so the stroke appears to be drawn in the path's point order → end state is the complete outline; multiple paths stagger with delays. Morph: start shape's points interpolate to the end shape's points over 0.8s `power2.inOut`. Motion path: the element travels the track over its duration (4s loop in the example), auto-rotating to the tangent. Sheen: a white gradient band translates −1 → 1 across the shape every 2s, indefinitely.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Draw-on core: `stroke-dasharray: var(--len); stroke-dashoffset: var(--len)` → animate offset to 0; length from `path.getTotalLength()`, or the no-JS trick `pathLength="1"` with dasharray/offset of 1. Morphing needs identical command structure for naive interpolation; GSAP MorphSVG (free since 3.12) or Flubber (`maxSegmentLength: 2`) handle mismatched point counts. Motion: GSAP MotionPath (`align`, `autoRotate: true`, `alignOrigin: [0.5, 0.5]`), SMIL `<animateMotion>` with `<mpath>`, or CSS `offset-path: path(…)` animating `offset-distance` to 100%. Filters (displacement scale, blur stdDeviation) are paint-heavy — animate sparingly. Authoring: inline the SVG (an `<img>` SVG can't be reached by page CSS/JS), keep `viewBox`, SVGO with `cleanupIds`/`removeViewBox`/`mergePaths` disabled when internals are animated. SMIL unsupported in IE/old Edge.
- **Reference / source:** iart-ai web-animation-skills on GitHub; GSAP MorphSVG and MotionPath plugins; Flubber.
- **Best for:** Logo/brand marks, route-and-coverage maps in towns/areas sections, process diagrams that draw themselves, animated icon toggles in navigation. Trade fit: strong — a service-area map or a roofline logo drawing on is exactly this technique.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0407⟧

## ⟦S0408⟧ Jakubantalik/refine-live — Part 13 — UI Skills — rest of the ui-skills.com catalog
- **What it is:** A tooling skill that turns a chat agent into the LLM behind the transitions.dev Timeline Inspector's "Refine" button — the in-chat fallback for when no persistent refine agent is wired. It long-polls a local relay and answers three job kinds: small refinements, recipe replacements, page scans, and apply-to-source writes. It carries the full transitions.dev motion-token scale inline.
- **How it looks:** Nothing on a web page. In the developer's inspector panel, each Refine click produces suggestion cards (e.g. "Duration → Snappy (250ms)", from 400ms → to 250ms, with a one-sentence reason) that preview live in the browser when applied; scan jobs turn a flat list of detected transitions into grouped components with open/close phases.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion of its own; it retunes other elements' motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Relay at `http://localhost:7331` (long-poll `GET /jobs/next` blocks ~25s; 204 = no work; `{"stop": true}` ends the loop; idle backoff to ~5s pauses, self-stop after ~10 min idle; relay errors a waiting job after ~120s). Token scale it applies — durations: 40ms stagger, 80ms micro, 150ms quick, 250ms fast, 350ms medium, 400ms slow, 500ms very slow; default easing "Smooth ease out" `cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1)`; on-grid easings left unchanged: ease-out (tooltip), ease-in-out (swaps/reveals), linear (shimmer/spinner), `cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.36, 0.64, 1)` badge pop, `cubic-bezier(0.34, 3.85, 0.64, 1)` avatar return; pre-scales 0.96 modal / 0.97 dropdown open / 0.98 tooltip / 0.99 dropdown close; blur 2px / 3px page slide & text reveal / 8px success check; distances 4px text swap / 6px shake small / 8px badge, page slide, shake large / 12px text reveal / 30px check badge. Replace jobs pick one of 21 named recipes (01-card-resize … 21-accordion — a wider list than ⟦S0409⟧'s 12). Preferred route is the persistent CLI: `npx transitions-refine live` spawns an agent per click with zero idle burn.
- **Reference / source:** Jakubantalik/transitions.dev on GitHub; the transitions.dev Timeline Inspector and its relay.
- **Best for:** Development workflow only — live-tuning transitions in a project that uses ⟦S0409⟧/⟦S0410⟧. No homepage section; its token table is the useful artifact for a builder.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0408⟧

## ⟦S0409⟧ Jakubantalik/transitions-dev — Part 13 — UI Skills — rest of the ui-skills.com catalog
- **What it is:** Twelve production-ready, copy-paste CSS transitions for common UI elements, all namespaced under `t-*` classes and driven by one shared `:root` block of semantic CSS variables. No framework, no dependencies; every snippet ships a `prefers-reduced-motion` guard. This is the recipe library that ⟦S0408⟧'s replace tab and ⟦S0410⟧'s polish tokens both point back to.
- **How it looks:** A notification dot slides diagonally onto a bell icon and pops with a spring; digits of a price pop in one by one with a slight blur, the last two staggered; a dropdown grows out of its trigger's corner; a modal scales up from 96% in the centre of the screen; a panel slides up 100px into its card, sharpening from a 2px blur as it arrives; two wizard pages slide past each other 8px with a soft blur; icons cross-fade with a shrink-and-blur; a success checkmark fades in, rotates upright from 80°, bobs down 40px and draws its own stroke; avatars in a row lift like a comb under the cursor and spring back with an overshoot; an invalid input shakes left-right and grows an error message that fades away after 3 seconds.
- **Frame by frame:** Per recipe — Card resize: state class changes width/height → both tween 300ms on the smooth ease-out → rest at new size. Number pop-in: digits start 8px below, transparent, 2px blurred → spring `cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.45, 0.64, 1)` over 500ms into place, decimal digits delayed 70ms and 140ms. Badge: wrapper slides from offset (−8.2px, 12.4px) over 260ms while the dot scales 0 → 1 with blur over 500ms on the pop ease; close reverses in 180ms. Text swap: old text exits up 8px + blur + fade (200ms) → content swaps → new text jumps below and animates back to rest. Dropdown: from scale 0.97 at the trigger-origin corner, opacity 0 → open 250ms to scale 1; close dips only to 0.99 over 150ms. Modal: scale 0.96 → 1, 250ms open / 150ms close. Panel: translateY(100px) + blur 2px → 0 over 400ms open / 350ms close. Page slide: outgoing page shifts 8px its own way + 3px blur + fade, incoming mirrors in, 200ms. Icon swap: outgoing icon scales to 0.25 + 2px blur + fade while incoming reverses, 200ms ease-in-out. Success check: fade 550ms + rotate 80°→0 550ms + blur 10px→0 500ms + bob 40px→0 450ms on a bouncy ease, SVG path draws over 550ms after an 80ms delay. Avatar hover: hovered item lifts −4px and scales 1.05, neighbours lift by −4px × 0.45^distance, 320ms; on mouseleave everything returns on the strong bounce `cubic-bezier(0.34, 3.85, 0.64, 1)`. Error shake: 280ms total in four legs (80/80/60/60ms) — +6px, −6px, +4px overshoot, rest — border turns error-coloured, message fades in, holds 3000ms, fades back over 280ms.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Universal `:root` install (copy once) with per-recipe variables — e.g. `--resize-dur: 300ms`, `--digit-stagger: 70ms`, `--badge-pop-ease: cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.36, 0.64, 1)`, `--dropdown-pre-scale: 0.97`, `--modal-scale: 0.96`, `--panel-translate-y: 100px`, `--page-slide-distance: 8px`, `--icon-swap-start-scale: 0.25`, `--check-rotate-from: 80deg`, `--avatar-falloff: 0.45`, `--shake-distance: 6px`, `--revert-hold: 3000ms` — shared master ease `cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1)`. Decision rules match element + verb first and prefer the lower-overhead recipe (dropdown over modal, card resize over panel reveal). Craft details that must survive copying: paste CSS verbatim (no shorthand collapsing, keep `will-change`), reflow trick (`void el.offsetWidth`) to replay animations, `.is-closing` cleanup timeouts so the next open doesn't jump, success-check `stroke-dasharray` must be replaced with the real `path.getTotalLength()` (20 is a placeholder), avatar timing-function is set inline in JS before the variable writes so hover-in and return use different easings. Live demo values live at transitions.dev.
- **Reference / source:** Jakubantalik/transitions.dev on GitHub; live tuned demo at transitions.dev.
- **Best for:** The micro-motion layer of a whole homepage: navigation dropdowns, FAQ/modals, form error + success states (quote forms), price/stat number updates (proof sections), wizard-style steps. Trade fit: excellent — framework-free CSS that drops straight into a single-file HTML build.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0409⟧

## ⟦S0410⟧ Jakubantalik/transitions-polish — Part 13 — UI Skills — rest of the ui-skills.com catalog
- **What it is:** The tuning companion to ⟦S0409⟧: where transitions-dev installs whole transitions, this add-on audits motion that already exists and snaps its five dimensions (duration, distance, scale, blur, easing) to the shared transitions.dev token scale — matching on usage, never on the nearest number. It also feeds the Refine panel's Small-refinement tab used by ⟦S0408⟧.
- **How it looks:** No visual of its own. The felt result: closes that get out of the way faster than opens, hover returns that settle with a soft spring instead of snapping, staggers that finish before they feel late, tooltips that don't fire when a cursor merely passes over.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion of its own; it changes the timing of other elements' motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Doctrine: infer the usage first (modal close, tooltip, badge appear…), then pick the token whose documented usage matches; a 300ms modal close maps to the 150ms quick token because the usage matches, and values with no matching usage are left untouched. Tokens — durations: 40ms stagger offset / 80ms micro / 150ms quick (modal & dropdown close, text swap, tooltip appear) / 250ms fast (opens, tabs, page slide) / 350ms medium (panel & toast close) / 400ms slow (panel open, skeleton reveal) / 500ms very slow (emphasis, badge appear, success check). Easings: smooth-out `cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1)` default; bounce `cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.36, 0.64, 1)`; bounce-strong `cubic-bezier(0.34, 3.85, 0.64, 1)`. Distances 4/6/8/12/30px; scales 0.96/0.97/0.98/0.99 by surface size; blur 2/3/8px. Rules: open/close asymmetry (dropdown & modal 250 → 150ms; panel 400 → 350ms) with named symmetric exceptions (page slide, tabs, accordion, icon swap at 250ms; text swap 150ms); overshoot easings on entrances only, never on a close; hover-in quick (≤250ms), hover-out may be longer and bouncy; stagger totals (offset × count) under ~300ms; intent delay 80ms (tooltips, success-check path); never delay a close or hover-out; trim duration before adding delay. Commands: `transitions review` (scan everything incl. Tailwind arbitrary values and CSS-in-JS, report only, grouped by file) and `transitions polish` (propose, confirm, then write token references or literals, keeping the file's existing unit format).
- **Reference / source:** Jakubantalik/transitions.dev on GitHub; add-on to the transitions-dev skill (⟦S0409⟧), restating its token scale so it can audit standalone.
- **Best for:** A QA/polish pass over any finished build's motion — navigation, modals, forms, galleries. Trade fit: high as a final-pass checklist on trades homepages; pairs with S0409's recipes.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0410⟧

## ⟦S0411⟧ Jakubantalik/transitions-ui-generation — Part 13 — UI Skills — rest of the ui-skills.com catalog
- **What it is:** Makes any UI element appear as if an AI agent is generating it live: a dotted wireframe is drawn from the element's own measured structure, then the real UI is revealed behind a scan line. Five variants (ui, text, small-text, image, auto) and two modes (skeleton, skeleton-texts), one dependency-free runtime for any framework.
- **How it looks:** Grey monochrome dots on the page where a card will be: a dot field ripples out from the centre with matrix-rain columns, construction guides run past the corners, corner handles pop in, a size label counts up to the real pixel size with a build timer; the outline is traced from the top centre in both directions by flowing dots while loose dots fly in and land on it; then every box, text line and icon path is traced in document order, a targeting reticle jumping part to part with a coordinate readout. Finally a scan line sweeps top to bottom and the real, full-colour UI sharpens in behind it as the drawing wipes away. Headline variant: every letter's true glyph outline is traced in flowing dots, then the letters fade in one by one. Image variant: dotted frame, a sketch of the photo's tones, a halftone of its own pixels, a dot matrix in its colours — then the photo.
- **Frame by frame:** Trigger (mount / data arrival / scroll into view / on demand) → dot field + probe sweep → guides, handles, counting size label → outline traced both ways from top centre → parts traced in document order with reticle + readouts → scan-line reveal, real UI fading and sharpening on the smooth ease-out while dots clear → end state: the untouched real element, fully interactive. Text variant timing inside that: each glyph fades in 140ms after its outline finishes, 90ms per glyph, staggered 90ms apart. Total run ≈ duration × 1.09 (ui) or × 1.06 (text/image).
- **Mechanism & key values:** Runtime files `ui-generation.js` + `text-image-generation.js` + two CSS files, no dependencies; `generate(el, options)` returns `{ finished, cancel, element }`; re-calling cancels the previous run. Defaults: ui duration 2400ms (keep 1600–3600), maxParts 60, keys 5 (elements getting their own guides/labels); text/image duration 3000ms (keep 2000–4500), `display` threshold 32px for the auto variant, maxGlyphs 140, fade 90ms, fadeDelay 140ms, fadeStagger 90ms, default sequenceEase `[0.37, -0.02, 0.73, 0.88]`, fadeBy character / word / gradient. Grid stagger for several elements: ~260ms delay per item, texts mode around one element only. Drawing variables: `--gen-dot: 2.1px`, line `#9a9a9a`, strong `#6c6c6c`, Roboto Mono labels; keep the drawing monochrome — colour arrives with the real UI. Internals: glyph outlines via canvas + marching squares, simplified at 0.3px (Ramer-Douglas-Peucker); image sketch = marching squares at six tone levels on a 3px grid, strokes up to 240px; `timeline(el, opts)` exposes `seek(ms)` for video tools. Accessibility: `prefers-reduced-motion` skips the drawing entirely (200ms fade in), overlay is `aria-hidden` and pointer-transparent. Do not use under ~120px or on frequent UI — it is a moment, not a loading state; wire after fonts/images load or the drawing lands in the wrong place.
- **Reference / source:** Jakubantalik/transitions.dev on GitHub (install `npx skills add Jakubantalik/transitions.dev`); demos ship in the skill (demo.html, demo-text.html, demo-editorial.html).
- **Best for:** AI-product landing heroes, launch/demo moments, an AI feature returning a generated card. Trade fit: NOT-FOR-TRADES for a roofer/plumber homepage — the aesthetic says "AI tool", not local tradesman; noted here so it is not picked by mistake.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0411⟧

## ⟦S0412⟧ jakubkrehel/make-interfaces-feel-better — Part 13 — UI Skills — rest of the ui-skills.com catalog
- **What it is:** A 19-principle detail checklist for building or reviewing UI — the small typography, surface, icon and motion decisions that compound into an interface feeling right. Written by Jakub Krehel; note it sits here in Part 13, separate from the Part 07 Jakub Krehel collection. Its icon-animation values (scale 0.25, blur 4px) are the same numbers ⟦S0405⟧ and ⟦S0409⟧ use.
- **How it looks:** Nothing changes category-level; everything gets slightly more correct: nested cards whose corners are concentric instead of pinched, play triangles nudged 2px right so they look centred, images with a hairline neutral outline instead of a dirty tinted edge, numbers that hold still while counting because every digit is the same width, headings whose lines balance evenly, buttons that dip almost imperceptibly when pressed.
- **Frame by frame:** The motion rules: interactive state changes use CSS transitions so they can be interrupted and retarget mid-flight (keyframes reserved for one-shot staged sequences); an infrequent entrance splits into semantic chunks staggered ~100ms apart (title words ~80ms), each rising 12px with opacity and a 4px blur clearing; exits are smaller and shorter than entrances (fixed −12px translateY, 150ms ease-out vs ~300ms enters); contextual icons cross-fade with scale 0.25 → 1, opacity 0 → 1, blur 4px → 0 on a 0.3s spring with bounce exactly 0; buttons scale to exactly 0.96 on press over 150ms ease-out. High-frequency interactions get no custom animation at all — instant feedback or a ≤150ms opacity/color transition.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Concentric radius: `outerRadius = innerRadius + padding` (only when padding ≤ 24px; beyond that treat layers independently). Optical alignment: icon-side padding = text-side padding − 2px; play triangle `margin-left: 2px`. Elevation: layered transparent shadow instead of border — light mode `0 0 0 1px oklch(0 0 0 / 0.06), 0 1px 2px -1px oklch(0 0 0 / 0.06), 0 2px 4px 0 oklch(0 0 0 / 0.04)`; dark mode a single `0 0 0 1px oklch(1 0 0 / 0.08)` ring; structural borders (dividers, inputs, tables) stay borders. Image outline: 1px, `oklch(0 0 0 / 0.1)` light / `oklch(1 0 0 / 0.1)` dark, `outline-offset: -1px`, never a tinted neutral. Type: `text-wrap: balance` on headings (≤6 lines Chromium / ≤10 Firefox), `text-wrap: pretty` as the default for short-medium body text, `-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased` once at root, `tabular-nums` on dynamic numbers. Icons: stroke 1.5px beside 400-weight text, 2px beside 500–600, 2.5px beside 700; one `currentColor` SVG recolored per state, outline default / fill active; flip directional icons in RTL, never logos/checkmarks/playback. Hit areas: 44×44px touch, ≥40×40px dense desktop, extended via pseudo-element, never overlapping. Performance: never `transition: all` (name exact properties), `will-change` only for transform/opacity/filter and only when stutter is observed, never `will-change: all`. Never animate on page load for stateful components: `initial={false}` on AnimatePresence. Review method: replay motion at 10% speed in the Animations panel and walk hover/focus/active/loading/empty; review output is capped (quick mode 5 findings, HIGH/MEDIUM only; full mode 15) with a Block / Needs changes / Approve verdict.
- **Reference / source:** jakubkrehel/make-interfaces-feel-better on GitHub; five bundled reference files (typography.md, surfaces.md, animations.md, icons.md, performance.md). No external sites named.
- **Best for:** The final polish/QA pass over every section — hero type, cards (work/gallery, proof/reviews), forms, buttons/CTAs, icon rows. Trade fit: excellent; these are exactly the details that separate a template-feeling trades site from a crafted one.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0412⟧
## ⟦S0413⟧ jakubkrehel/oklch-skill — Part 13 — UI Skills — rest of the ui-skills.com catalog
- **What it is:** A working method for using the OKLCH colour space in web projects: converting hex/rgb/hsl colours to oklch, generating palette scales, checking and fixing contrast, handling sRGB vs Display P3 gamut, and theming with Tailwind v4. Ships with four reference files (conversion, palette generation, accessibility/contrast, gamut & Tailwind).
- **How it looks:** Nothing renders by itself; what a visitor sees is the result — colour palettes whose steps look evenly spaced in brightness (no step suddenly jumps darker or shifts purple), text that stays readable on its background in both light and dark mode, and on wide-gamut (P3) screens, more vivid accent colours than sRGB-only visitors get.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. (Only state change: a `.dark` class swaps CSS variables to the reversed palette mapping.)
- **Mechanism & key values:** oklch(L C H [/ alpha]); L 0–1 (0 black, 1 white, perceptually uniform), C 0–~0.4, H 0–360°. Format L and C to 3 decimals, drop trailing zeros. Light/dark boundary: L > 0.6 = light background → dark text. Lightness gaps: background L > 0.85 → foreground L < 0.45; background L < 0.25 → foreground L > 0.75. Hue drift: > 10° H spread across palette steps = visible drift (example given: an HSL blue ramp drifts ≈18°, H ≈269 → ≈285). Contrast: APCA recommended — normal text |Lc| ≥ 60 pass, ≥ 75 pass+; large text 45 / 60; UI components 30. WCAG 2: normal text 4.5:1 AA, 7:1 AAA; large text 3:1 AA, 4.5:1 AAA; UI components 3:1. Fix contrast by adjusting L only — chroma has negligible effect. Palette algorithm: scale labels 50–950 (9 steps standard, matching Tailwind); delta = 0.4, minL = max(0.05, baseL − 0.4), maxL = min(0.95, baseL + 0.4); distribute L evenly; each step's C = chroma% × that step's max chroma for its L/H (never the same absolute C across hues). Gamut at L = 0.5 in sRGB: highest max chroma purple (H ≈ 285) C ≈ 0.29; red-orange (H ≈ 0–30) C ≈ 0.20; lowest cyan (H ≈ 195) C ≈ 0.09. P3 covers ~50% more colours than sRGB; serve P3 values inside `@media (color-gamut: p3)` with an sRGB fallback, and hex + `@supports (color: oklch(0 0 0))` for older browsers. Tailwind v4: define scales as `--color-brand-*` oklch values in `@theme`; opacity modifiers compile to slash-alpha oklch. Dark mode: derive by reversing the light palette's L mapping, don't hand-pick. Browser support: Baseline 2023, 96%+ global.
- **Reference / source:** github.com/jakubkrehel/oklch-skill. Interactive explorer named in the skill: oklch.fyi. Colour-science basis: OKLCH / APCA as published standards (no single site design referenced).
- **Best for:** The colour foundation under every section — hero, proof, gallery, CTA, forms, footer. Directly trade-fit: generating a roofer/HVAC/remodeler's brand palette whose steps stay even and whose call-button text passes contrast, plus a derived dark mode, without hue drift.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0413⟧

## ⟦S0414⟧ jakubkrehel/teardown — Part 13 — UI Skills — rest of the ui-skills.com catalog
- **What it is:** A method for producing technical "teardown" illustrations of physical objects — and of formless concepts like display pixels or interface layers — from photos, descriptions, CAD models or ideas: one 3D-ish model is built, then projected into coherent line drawings, packaged as a viewable page with SVG, PNG and PDF downloads. Explicitly an explanatory illustration, not a manufacturing drawing (nothing toleranced).
- **How it looks:** An assembly-print look: dark contour linework on plain paper, open (unfilled or lightly part-tinted) interiors, generous separation between components in an exploded axonometric view, peripheral callouts kept restrained. Concept sheets show an exploded stack of thin plates, one plate per layer, filled so colour tells the layers apart. The bundled viewer shows one drawing with switches: assembled ↔ exploded, and an Annotations switch that labels each visible part with its name and a leader line (no balloons or dimensions unless a separate annotated sheet is composed).
- **Frame by frame:** Page load → the drawing appears in its chosen state (assembled or exploded). Click the view switch → the same model re-projects to the other state (parts separated along their explosion paths, or back together). Toggle Annotations → part names with leader lines appear/disappear. Use the colour panel → a part fills with a tint of its own line colour. Object animation/simulation is out of scope unless requested — otherwise static.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Workflow in 6 steps: (1) read object and reference separately, keep an `evidence.md` classifying every feature group (supplied geometry / photo-visible-estimated / hidden-omitted-or-flagged / fictional-concept); (2) choose the smallest view set that explains the construction (exploded axonometric for fit, parallel pictorial for external shape, aligned orthographic for dimensions, section for internal passages, exploded plate stack for layered concepts); (3) construct ONE model and derive every view from it — bundled geometry helpers by default, CAD projection when booleans are needed; build order: silhouette/volumes → interfaces, cavities, fasteners → functional details → resolve occlusion; (4) ink line roles at paper size; (5) render and inspect the actual deliverable, fix largest failure first; (6) package a standalone page (no build step/server) and test controls + downloaded bytes. Renderer detail from the troubleshooting table: it only rounds vertices that turn less than 35° (give steep-angle circles more segments); smooth turned surfaces showing stripes need `lathe` a `creaseAngle` or `loft`'s `lines` option. Title blocks that can't preserve scale must say NTS. Companion skills named: better-typography (text), better-colors (palette), better-accessibility (embedding), better-layout (surrounding UI).
- **Reference / source:** github.com/jakubkrehel/skills (teardown). Bundled references it defers to: views-and-annotations.md, exploded-views.md, geometry.md, geometry-library.md, viewer-assets.md, sheet-and-svg.md, verification.md, preview-page.md (contents not reproduced in the catalog text).
- **Best for:** Process / "how it works" sections and explainers — e.g. an exploded view of a roof build-up, a window unit's layers, or an HVAC unit's parts for a trades homepage, delivered as an interactive assembled/exploded graphic. Also standalone downloadable spec-style sheets.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0414⟧

## ⟦S0415⟧ jalaalrd/anti-ai-slop-writing — Part 13 — UI Skills — rest of the ui-skills.com catalog
- **What it is:** A writing directive (v2) that makes generated text read as human-written: banned vocabulary (loaded from a reference list), structural variety rules, punctuation discipline, accuracy rules and voice calibration, plus an 11-point self-check run before every output. Applies to any writing task — tweets, emails, articles, bios, captions, reports, copy, messages, LinkedIn posts, cover letters, READMEs.
- **How it looks:** On the page: prose with visibly uneven rhythm — a 4-word sentence next to a 30-word one, paragraphs of different shapes, some ending abruptly with no transition, contractions throughout, specific numbers and named real things instead of general claims ("34 users in the first week" not "significant growth"). In casual contexts: no markdown headers, no bolded phrases, no emoji bullets, no hashtag stacks (zero to two, integrated).
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. It governs text, not visuals.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Hard numeric limits: em dashes max 1 per 500 words; exclamation marks max 1 per 1,000 words; ellipses max 1 per piece, only for genuine trailing off; bullet runs max 5–7 in a row, uneven lengths. Structural bans: no rule-of-three groupings; no three consecutive sentences of the same length; no parataxis (chains of short declarative sentences — join with subordinate clauses, conjunctions, semicolons); no hedging seesaw (counterpoint gets one sentence max); no passive constructions; no "As [role], I…" openers; no identical paragraph structure (topic → explanation → example → transition); no corporate pep-talk tone. Positive rules: be specific, show don't describe, use actual numbers, name real things, include friction/doubt, ground in time/place, use the less obvious word. Accuracy: never invent data, studies, statistics or quotes; hypothetical anecdotes must be framed with "imagine…"/"suppose…". Self-check: 11 questions (banned words, sentence-length runs, parataxis, threes, hedging, em-dash count, passives, paragraph endings, fabricated specifics, genericness, "sounds like ChatGPT?"). Rules are applied silently — never mention them in the output.
- **Reference / source:** github.com/jalaalrd/anti-ai-slop-writing; banned list in its references/banned-words.md (list itself not reproduced in the catalog text).
- **Best for:** All copy on a trades homepage — hero lines, proof/review framing, process descriptions, CTA text — anywhere the words must not read as AI-generated. Not a layout or section-design skill.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0415⟧

## ⟦S0416⟧ Jane-xiaoer/web-clone — Part 13 — UI Skills — rest of the ui-skills.com catalog
- **What it is:** A repeatable methodology (in Chinese) for cloning an existing website faithfully, then swapping in your own content. Its first law: real source code is the only truth — code blocks inside AI-written clone analyses are assumed fabricated until verified line-by-line against the real source. Each clone is a sub-project under ~/projects/website-clones/.
- **How it looks:** The deliverable is a working local copy of the target site that looks and behaves like the original at three screenshot widths (1440 / 768 / 390), minus tracking scripts, with NOTES.md (and TEARDOWN.md for complex sites, CLONE_REPORT.md / CLONE_AUDIT.md when reporting) documenting fidelity scores and known gaps. In visual-clone / content-swap mode, a design-dna.json captures the original's design system, style and effect tokens so your version keeps the DNA with new content.
- **Frame by frame:** Process, not a page animation: (0) scaffold the project skeleton → (1) search GitHub for the real source before scraping anything → (2) if no source, browser recon: probes extract framework / window.THREE / canvas count / smooth-scroll library / fonts / scrollHeight, screenshots at 1440/768/390 → (2.5) grade complexity L1–L6 and pick a mode (faithful / visual / content-swap) before promising anything → (3) pick the build path from a decision table (static → wget mirror; React/Vue/Next content site → rebuild template; SPA → capture API fixtures first; multi-page → route-crawl map, max 25 pages / depth 2; complex interaction → interaction-probe records hover/click/scroll/canvas-drag states; WebGL-heavy → deep reverse-engineering; static-built Astro/Vite/Hugo → full asset mirror) → (4) build in the hub, keeping a read-only index-original.html baseline → (5) cut trackers line-by-line, write notes, verify in a real browser (console clean, screenshots vs original), then re-run recon on the clone and generate an automated comparison + pixel visual-diff → (6) swap in your own text, media and brand colours.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Bundled Node scripts: init-clone.mjs, recon-site.mjs (Playwright), asset-harvest.mjs, network-capture.mjs, mirror-site.mjs (full-scroll real-browser capture of every request incl. runtime-fetched .sog/.buf/.wasm/.riv/fonts), route-crawl.mjs (max-pages 25, max-depth 2), interaction-probe.mjs, sourcemap-hunt.mjs, compare-recon.mjs, visual-diff.mjs (browser-canvas pixel diff + visual score), audit-clone.mjs, dna-scaffold.mjs. Reverse-engineering discipline: every conclusion labelled SOURCE / PARTIAL / GUESS (unlabelled = GUESS); no-compensation rule (never mask timing/coordinate/state errors by tweaking brightness/speed/position/noise); baseline-first gate (replay real draw calls/shaders/uniforms raw and pass frame comparison before restructuring). Worked paradigm from its flagship case: the marbles site refracts the live DOM by computing a displacement map off-screen in WebGL (RG = displacement, B = Fresnel) and feeding it to SVG feDisplacementMap — not ray-marching/SDF as an AI analysis had claimed. Licence gate before cloning: MIT/Apache/BSD/Unlicense = reuse with attribution; no LICENSE = all rights reserved, local study only, no public redeploy; proprietary = read-only learning.
- **Reference / source:** github.com/Jane-xiaoer/claude-skill-web-clone. Flagship case: ~/projects/website-clones/marbles-clone/ (native WebGL + SVG filter + custom physics glass-marble site). References named: marbles-case.md, reverse-engineering.md, effect-extraction.md, assessment.md, deliverables.md, design-dna.md, complex-playbooks.md, static-mirror.md (oryzo.ai, a Lusion L6 gaussian-splatting site, hero pixel diff 5/5).
- **Best for:** Reference-site work behind any section: when a build starts from a proven award site, this is the discipline for extracting its REAL mechanism (the bank's "copy the mechanism, then adapt" method) instead of guessing from screenshots. Not itself a section design.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0416⟧

## ⟦S0417⟧ joe-bell/letterboxd-diary — Part 13 — UI Skills — rest of the ui-skills.com catalog
- **What it is:** Fetches a Letterboxd member's recently watched films from their public diary RSS feed and renders them as a compact markdown list, with first-run username setup. Answers "what did they last watch / watch since a date / last N films" even when Letterboxd isn't named.
- **How it looks:** Plain markdown text output: a single film is one unbulleted line — linked title, year in parentheses, star rating (e.g. `[Casablanca](…) (1942) ★★★★★`), with any review as plain text on the next line; several films are one bullet each, reviews as sub-bullets. No preamble, headers or closing commentary.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. A fetch-and-format pipeline.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Feed: https://letterboxd.com/<username>/rss/, fetched fresh every time. Username resolution order: in-request → saved (LETTERBOXD_USERNAME env var or a "Letterboxd username:" line in host memory files) → ask once; never store it inside the skill file. Retrieval ladder, one attempt per rung, never retry or climb back up: (1) curl -sSf — a 404 means wrong username (curl exits 22 over HTTP/1.1, 56 over HTTP/2; read the message, not the code), a 403/allowlist denial or other failure drops to rung 2; (2) host fetch tool; (3) ask the user to paste the feed URL back as its own message in a fenced block; (4) host browser tool, read the raw XML (a full 50-entry feed is ~43 KB). Never web-search for the feed. Parse per item: letterboxd:filmTitle (never parse the rating out of <title>), filmYear, watchedDate, memberRating (field absent = unrated), rewatch, memberLike, tmdb:movieId. Rating render: one ★ per whole point plus ½ for a half (3.5 → ★★★½). Filter/sort on watchedDate, not pubDate. Coverage: the window is the 50 most recent diary entries by publish date; total <item> count runs 50–100 because lists are mixed in and skipped; fewer than 50 diary entries = complete, exactly 50 = truncated (say so, link letterboxd.com/<username>/films/diary/). Reviews detected by guid prefix letterboxd-review- vs letterboxd-watch-; strip the poster <img> paragraph and spoiler notice. Only two pre-approved calls: curl against letterboxd.com and fetching that domain.
- **Reference / source:** github.com/joe-bell/skills (letterboxd-diary). Behaviour claims are sourced to observations of letterboxd.com RSS feeds and claude.ai / Claude Desktop sessions dated 2026-09-22 recorded in the skill text.
- **Best for:** No homepage-section use — a personal data-retrieval utility (film-diary questions). Included for completeness of the catalog.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0417⟧

## ⟦S0418⟧ kitlangton/effect — Part 13 — UI Skills — rest of the ui-skills.com catalog
- **What it is:** A reference skill for writing TypeScript with the Effect library at v4: current APIs, production defaults, and a branch chooser that routes each task type (schema, services/layers, config, scheduling, caching, streams, HTTP clients, testing) to a dedicated reference file.
- **How it looks:** No visual output — it shapes code. What a reviewer sees: Effect.gen workflows, services defined with Effect.fn("Domain.operation"), Schema-based models with matching interfaces, typed TaggedError failures, and tests using TestClock instead of sleeps.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Reviewed against Effect 4.0.0, upstream commit 6389d9ac64c0f62ccc8b575fb9afc65fc104e814 (github.com/Effect-TS/effect); the project-pinned installed version takes precedence over the skill. Core defaults: Context.Service for services, Layer.effect + Service.of for implementations, Schema.Struct + same-name interface for records, Schema.TaggedError for typed errors, Config (never direct process.env) for runtime config, Schedule for retry/repeat/polling/backoff, Stream for effectful multi-value sources, Cache.make / Effect.cached for keyed TTL caching and dedupe, Effect.request + RequestResolver for batching, HttpClient.retryTransient for HTTP retries, decode unknown input with Schema.decodeUnknownEffect. Boundary rules: thin HTTP handlers, business rules in services, retry only proven-idempotent operations, provider calls outside DB transactions. Do-nots include: no `as any` / unchecked casts, no Schema.Class defaults, no hand-rolled _tag errors, no blind Layer.mergeAll, no arbitrary Effect.sleep in tests.

## ⟦S0419⟧ larashero3-dotcom/lieflat-charts — Part 13 — UI Skills — rest of the ui-skills.com catalog
- **What it is:** A template-driven data-visualisation system (in Chinese) that generates HTML charts, HTML/PDF slide decks (Presentation Mode) and full-page HTML reports (Report Mode) strictly from a built-in gallery of real template implementations — never freehand. Default output is charts; decks and reports only on explicit request. Aims at non-programmers who describe data in plain words.
- **How it looks:** Editorial, magazine-grade charts on cards: paper-grey #F0EFEB and charcoal #1C1C1A only by default (Mono), a 7-step grey ladder where the darkest mark is the most important value, solid fills only — no glow, no gradients, no shadows. Cards have 24px radius, no border, separated by whitespace, each with a four-part structure: a conclusion headline (never the chart-type name), a subtitle carrying legend + time range separated by "·", the chart, and an all-caps letterspaced source line. Two visual families: Lupi (fine 0.5–0.7px hairlines, one dot = one record, for 30s+ close reading) and Glance (chunky 2px+ shapes, pre-aggregated, readable in under 10 seconds). Colour, when used, is one locked system per deliverable: porcelain (single-hue blue steps), palm (low-saturation green/yellow with amber accent) or wire (black/grey + one fluorescent orange hero), or a user-supplied custom palette.
- **Frame by frame:** Trigger: a chart scrolls into the viewport → its entrance animation plays once (default easing quarticOut — fast in, settle, no bounce; elasticOut allowed for wave entrances), with per-element stagger of 8–15 ms per dot or 80–130 ms per bar → end state: the full chart at rest. Click a chart → the reveal replays (a single reveal mechanism, obsReveal, with timer cleanup). With prefers-reduced-motion set → the animation is dropped to the static end state. Interactive big charts (e.g. Threads): hover a line → that whole path lights while others recede; hover a label → its whole bundle lifts; click → the path pins.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Charts must be built from the gallery card's actual structure + render code (found via catalog.md → gallery file → the `<div class="card">` block + the matching `// ════` script block); inventing a lookalike or mixing templates is a fail. Selection order is fixed: Lupi Editorial L1–L19 first, then Lupi Basics F1–F17 (mains L1–L15 / F1–F13; reserves L16–L20 / F14–F17 / G19–G22 need a written reason, except five data shapes that go straight to reserves: OHLC → F17 Candlestick, five-number summary → F15 Tick Box, 3–6 continuous dimensions → L20 Parallel Coordinates, full-year 52×7 → L17 Calendar Heat, composition-over-time → F16 Stream Ribbon), then Glance G3–G22 only if both fail or a dashboard/3-second read is requested; Maps M1–M2 only when the user explicitly asks for a map. Typography: Inter throughout — headline 700, in-chart values 800, axis labels 600; minimum SVG text 6.5px on half-width cards, 5.5px full-width. Bars never use a broken axis; area-encoded values use radius = sqrt(value); demo data must use the deterministic rnd(i,k), never Math.random(). Chart count follows independent conclusions: 1 for a single question, 2–3 for two-three conclusions, 4–6 for an article/case, max 6 per page. Colour rules: lines ×1.8 width and opacity floor 0.85 when coloured; at least 3 colour steps or fall back to grey; contrast ≥ 4.5:1 body text, ≥ 3:1 large text and data shapes; dark cards max 1 per 4-card screen, only for shapes that need a dark ground. Interactive hit targets: a 9px transparent twin line under each visible Threads line. Engines: hand-written SVG (Lupi), Chart.js 4 (G1/G3 only, must mount on <canvas>), ECharts 6 (CDN). Reports pick one of R01–R12 templates (zh/en); decks one of P01–P10, 16:9, complete colour decks are 19 pages. Delivery self-check: 14 items (proportionality, single colour system, label collisions, min type size, deterministic data, reveal behaviour, `node --check` on scripts, card four-piece set, ≥3 audited candidates with rejection reasons, template IDs recorded…).
- **Reference / source:** github.com/larashero3-dotcom/lieflat-charts. Style families named for Giorgia Lupi's editorial data style ("Lupi") and glanceable dashboard charts ("Glance"); the skill states its "Lupi style" means its own gallery's visual grammar, not Lupi's hand-drawn work. Developer credit line recorded in the skill: developed by "躺在废墟里" (attribution requested when publicly distributing outputs).
- **Best for:** Proof sections with real numbers — review counts, project counts, years, coverage stats — as restrained editorial charts instead of generic dashboard widgets; also one-page reports and pitch decks. Trade fit: strong for a "by the numbers" proof band on a trades homepage if kept in Mono/Lupi mode; the no-glow/no-3D/no-broken-axis honesty rules suit trades data.

## ⟦S0420⟧ latent-spaces/brag — Part 13 — UI Skills — rest of the ui-skills.com catalog
- **What it is:** Turns the current project's website/app into a short, polished, shareable launch video. The full version reads the project code, plans and storyboards, then hands a composition brief to Hyperframes (which builds, lints and renders the video), and delivers brag.mp4 + a poster frame + share copy. Optional Kokoro narration via --voice. NOTE: on Claude Opus 5.5 it automatically hands off to brag-slim (⟦S0421⟧), whose complete text is bundled inside this skill as its slim.md reference — see the duplicate note on ⟦S0421⟧.
- **How it looks:** A slick 15–25 second launch video built from the product's real UI, copy, colours and fonts — hook first, then the reveal, 2–3 sharp highlights of the actual product in use, then a punchline/outro. Typography personality, pacing and transitions follow one of 7 tone presets (default playful-clean, polished, yc-parody, deadpan, chaotic, cinematic, app-store). The idle thumbnail everywhere is a deliberately picked best frame, baked in as frame 0.
- **Frame by frame:** Video timeline: Hook (2–3s, planned first — the first 2 seconds decide whether anyone keeps watching) → Reveal (2–4s) → 2–3 highlights (5–12s total) → Punchline/outro (2–4s); scene durations must sum to 15–25s. Readability rule inside every scene: motion is fast-in then HOLD — a short label settles ~0.8s, a sentence holds ~0.3s per word; text is never flashed and removed. Workflow frames: parse invocation → inspect project (gate: answer the 9-question planning rubric) → write brag-plan.md storyboard → Hyperframes composition (gate: `npx hyperframes check` zero errors) → validate, render to brag-output/brag.mp4, pick best poster frame to brag.jpg, bake it as frame 0, write share-copy.txt.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Options: --tone (7 presets or freeform), --format landscape/vertical/square (default landscape), --duration (auto 15–25s), --no-music, --no-sfx, --title, --voice (Kokoro via Hyperframes, single provider, opt-in only). Hyperframes owns composition structure, exact animation timing and render; /brag owns angle, storyboard, tone, format, audio selection and music cue guidance (bundled track cue presets under assets/music/cues/; any track now supports beat sync). Output to brag-output/ or a timestamped brag-output-YYYY-MM-DD-HHmmss/ when one exists. ## ⟦S0422⟧ Leonxlnx/unlazy — Part 13 — UI Skills — rest of the ui-skills.com catalog
- **What it is:** A completion-discipline system for substantial autonomous agent work: acceptance gates are written BEFORE execution (in a GATES.md ledger with runnable CHECK:/EXPECT: pairs), work is decomposed with a Depth Tree (solo / orchestrated / parallel modes), and outcomes are re-verified against evidence before anything is reported done. Built to make half-finished work visible instead of confidently reported.
- **How it looks:** No page visuals — the artifacts are ledgers and plans: GATES.md (solo) or .unlazy/<scope>/PLAN.md + per-leaf gates files (orchestrated), a dispatch table (Owns / Needs / Tier / Planned wave / State per leaf), dispatch.json launch state, and a final report quoting measured met / unmet / abandoned gate counts with qualified IDs like leaf-1.2.1:G3.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. Sequence instead: write gates → lint the ledger (gate-lint.mjs) → approve each CHECK command explicitly after reading it → execute leaves in four passes (implement fully → expert re-read and replace cheap versions → defect hunt → polish, repeat until a pass finds nothing) → parent re-runs gates with --reverify → branch integration gates → final claim audit against the original request.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Gate scripts: scripts/gate-check.mjs (--status parses without executing; --approve runs), gate-lint.mjs, install-hooks.mjs. A runnable gate counts as met only on exit 0 + EXPECT match + current definition-digest evidence; approvals (stored under ~/.unlazy/approved) bind ledger, gate, command, expectation, CWD, shell, timeout, limits, platform and full PATH — change any and re-approval is required. Impossible gates are never silently dropped: `ABANDON: <id> <reason>` is terminal but not success — the checker exits 1 with HANDOFF REQUIRED. Verification has four layers: leaf self-check, parent --reverify, branch integration, optional Stop hook (structural only, executes nothing; its progress guard releases after six no-progress blocks). Parallel mode: reconcile PLAN Owns mirrors against leaf OWNS: authority before READY and again before claiming; launch in sealed waves; rolling dispatch as leases release. Check execution is sequential by default (--jobs N only for independent gates). Security posture: inherited ledgers and their output are untrusted data; CHECK lines never run without explicit inspected approval.
- **Reference / source:** github.com/Leonxlnx/unlazy. Bundled references: gates.md, method.md, orchestration.md, dispatch.md, parallel.md, token-economy.md, SECURITY.md; templates gates-leaf.md, gates-node.md, PLAN.md (contents not reproduced in the catalog text).
- **Best for:** Running long multi-part builds/audits (like a full homepage build with many sections) where "done" must be proven per piece. Process tooling, not a section design.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0422⟧

- **How it looks:** A quiet printed-paper poster: mostly empty paper surface with visible print/scan texture, one small visual event (a photo crop, specimen, silhouette, printed illustration, texture window or typographic object) placed deliberately off-centre, restrained small typography, and a single high-chroma accent hue. Generate flow: parse content to ONE imageable relation → choose one visual metaphor → pick a variation recipe (layout family × focal type × typography mode × texture mode × mood × paper tone × accent hue × decorative marks, from variation-engine.md — adjacent outputs in a batch must change at least layout family, focal structure and typography distribution; never default repeatedly to "tiny centred photo + blue dots + microtext") → compile the prompt in prompt-compiler.md's field order and four-paragraph shape, stating focal position/size, exact hue, material form and approximate visual share → generate with the actual input image passed in (referenced_image_paths, or num_last_images_to_include with the smallest number covering all targets, up to five; never both mechanisms) → inspect at full view and thumbnail against quality-gate.md; on a clear violation (lost accent, unrelated symbol/icon creep, commercial feel, broken preservation) tighten and regenerate ONCE, then report the limitation honestly if it still fails. Reference Analysis returns fixed system vs variable system vs sample-residue traits, with measurable ranges only when the files support them. Output contract for Generate: the image, the final prompt, recipe line, photo role/preservation lines, one short interpretation note.

## ⟦S0425⟧ lucasmarkes/hairline-create — Part 13 — UI Skills — rest of the ui-skills.com catalog
- **What it is:** Creates one Hairline figure: an isometric line drawing built from rounded solids in a single stroke that answers the pointer, shipped as one self-contained HTML file with nothing to install. The agent writes only the figure file; the engine (kernel.js) and page (bench.html) are fixed and must never be edited.
- **How it looks:** A spare isometric line figure on a plain stage — one object (a terrain-like continuous field, or discrete items like a riffle of cards), drawn in silhouette strokes with at most a highlight stroke for emphasis: no colour, no fills, no glow, no labels or letters inside the drawing (names go to the read-out text under the stage). Beneath the stage: a one-sentence "means" line and a slider that drives the figure's one number. A play button runs an "unseen pointer" tour so a stranger sees the figure's story with no hand on the page.
- **Frame by frame:** At rest → the figure sits in a composed rest pose (rule: rest is the thumbnail — never flat, empty or symmetric by laziness). Pointer moves over/near the figure → the figure answers with its gesture: parts move via springs or tweens registered on the stage tick (register(stage, tick) — hand-written timers, requestAnimationFrame loops and CSS animations are banned), with the pointer tested against the rest/target pose, not the currently drawn pose. Drag the slider → the figure's single ranged value moves through its intensity 0 → 0.5 (default) → 1 states, all in one direction. Press play (or open with ?play=1) → the unseen pointer visits the tour's 3–6 viewBox points in order — three stops that each show a different answer, then a leave; a lap is a sentence, not an inventory.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Pipeline: (0, only with an SVG source) read.mjs renders the SVG + a measurement card; source.md fixes object and parts. (1) concepts.md → offer 2–3 one-line concepts (object / pointer gesture / read-out / tour stops); wait for a pick unless the object + gesture arrived chosen (no audience → take the strongest rest pose and say so). (2) Build: read rules.md (ten rules, breaking one = unfinished), read only the API index comment at the top of kernel.js down to `var HL`, read the nearer example (examples/terrain.js for a continuous field, examples/riffle.js for discrete items), then write <name>.js defining mount({stage, svg, read}, value) → {set, destroy} and ending with hairline({name, means, rules, range, tour, mount}). Contracts: name lowercase one word/hyphenated; means ≤ 140 characters; range is the figure's own number read at intensities 0, 0.5, 1 (not 0–1 normalised); tour is 3–6 literal [x, y] viewBox points or null. Assemble with build.mjs → hairline-<name>.html (without Node: paste kernel.js at /*KERNEL*/ and the figure at /*FIGURE*/ in bench.html, changing nothing else). (3) Check: look.mjs builds, validates and shoots eight pictures on one sheet (hairline-<name>-look.png) plus frame/read-out/console checks — fix every failure and rerun until exit 0; without a browser, validate.mjs + the manual look list. (4) Hand over the HTML (artifact if possible) with one line each: metaphor, rules leaned on, tour stops, anything unverified. (5) Adjustments edit only <name>.js and re-run the look. Drawing rules sampled: a box is a prism of two rounded rings (silhouette + one crease), never twelve edges; emphasis = move one stroke from `sil` to `hi`, never colour/fill/glow; one figure, one idea.
- **Reference / source:** github.com/lucasmarkes/hairline (@lucasmarkes/hairline); its six shipped figures are the quality bar, examples/terrain.js and examples/riffle.js are two of them. Bundled: concepts.md, rules.md, source.md, look.md, kernel.js, bench.html, build.mjs, validate.mjs, look.mjs, read.mjs (contents not reproduced in the catalog text beyond the summaries above).
- **Best for:** A small interactive emblem in a hero, an empty state, a loading/404 moment, or beside a CTA — one memorable pointer-reactive line figure (e.g. a little roofline or house figure that reacts as the visitor's cursor passes). Single-purpose garnish, not a section system.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0425⟧
