- **Reference / source:** github.com/millionco/skills (skills/paper-flex) plus its bundled SPEC.md; operates through the Paper MCP tools.
- **Best for:** Design-file hygiene inside Paper before handoff. No direct use on a trade website build.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0463⟧

## ⟦S0464⟧ millionco/paper-to-code-components — Part 13 — UI Skills, rest of the ui-skills.com catalog
- **What it is:** The discipline for turning a Paper design (or Paper-exported JSX) into maintainable React/Next.js code: map the design hierarchy and extract components before writing JSX, so the result is a composed page of named components — never one giant pasted artboard. Companion to ⟦S0463⟧ (restructuring inside Paper) and ⟦S0466⟧ (reconciling the build afterwards).
- **How it looks:** The built page matches the Paper frame pixel-for-pixel (same typefaces, spacing, colours, crops, decorations), while the code underneath reads as composition: a HeroSection, FeatureCard, TestimonialCard, IconButton, each rendered from data. Pick the canonical artboard first — multi-iteration files include simplified handoff frames, and the cleanest one often drops detail (chart error bars, extra states); build the richer encoding and flag the discrepancy.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion prescribed; the code reproduces whatever the design shows.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Component rules: extract any group appearing 2+ times, any semantic region, any control with variants; near-duplicates become variant props/slots, never copy-tweaked JSX; one component per icon (distinct SVG artwork = distinct component — no BrandIcon name="…" switch; shared chrome like a logo frame is the extractable part). Charts are data, not pixels: recover the full data model (a bar with an error bar is 3 values: value + low/high; box-and-whisker up to 5; stacked bar N segments) and read post-transform computed geometry, because transforms make class literals lie (a whisker w-[7px] h-[73px] rotate-90 is really 73px long horizontally); convert via the axis ticks; never invent chart numbers. Tokenise repeated arbitrary values into globals.css without changing rendered values; Tailwind v4 spacing scale takes bare numbers (n × 0.25rem): max-w-[1160px] → max-w-290, gap-[24px] → gap-6, h-[96px] → h-24 — brackets only for off-scale values (w-[17.18px]); keep deliberate one-off deviations un-tokenised. Fonts: port the real files the Paper stack names (the system-ui/sans-serif tail is a fallback, not the design), @font-face per weight/style, font-synthesis: none, one token per typeface role (--font-sans / --font-serif / --font-data / --font-numeric / --font-mono). Keep data-paper-* attributes on useful roots; prefer React Server Components, "use client" only for behaviour; reuse local or canonical shadcn components (search ui.shadcn.com) before custom markup; group files by kind — charts in components/charts/, flat kebab-case files, no barrel index.ts (React Doctor's no-barrel-import). Verify by screenshotting build and canonical frame at the SAME width and reconciling stacking order, measure, type scale and dropped leaf decorations (code-chip backgrounds, hairlines, badges).
- **Reference / source:** github.com/millionco/skills (skills/paper-to-code-components); names ui.shadcn.com as the component reference.
- **Best for:** Design-to-code production workflow when a design arrives from Paper. Not a page section; relevant to any build that starts from a design file.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0464⟧

## ⟦S0465⟧ millionco/react-doctor — Part 13 — UI Skills, rest of the ui-skills.com catalog
- **What it is:** React Doctor: a scanner that audits React codebases for security, performance, correctness and architecture problems (lint, accessibility, bundle size) and reports a 0–100 health score; includes a design-only diagnostics mode and a runtime performance scan.
- **How it looks:** Nothing a site visitor sees — its outputs are terminal/CI reports grouped by rule and file with line numbers, a numeric health score, and, during a runtime scan, an isolated Chrome window where purple outlines flash around components with their names as React renders, while a DevTools trace is recorded.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion prescribed for any page. (The purple-outline flashing exists only inside the diagnostic runtime scan.)
- **Mechanism & key values:** Commands: `npx react-doctor@latest --verbose --scope changed` after React changes (the score must not regress before committing); default full scan for cleanup (fix errors first, then warnings); `npx react-doctor@latest design --verbose` for UI composition/typography/interaction/accessibility/motion rules only; `--scope contextual --base origin/main` reports findings in the functions/elements/files being edited; `--scope lines` restricts to changed lines; `--score` prints only the number. Runtime problems: `npx react-doctor@latest scan <url> --format json` records a trace while the user reproduces the slow interaction; authenticated state via --cdp <remote-debugging-url> (never copy the user's browser profile). Baseline workflow: save a full --json scan, then --baseline base-report.json reports only groups whose finding counts increased (fingerprint + message-similarity + git-adjusted line distance matching; reports must share version, rules and settings). GitLab CI: --warning-exit-code accepts 2–255 (example 123) for non-blocking warnings. The full `/doctor` triage fetches its canonical playbook live from react.doctor/prompts/react-doctor-agent.md, with per-rule fix recipes at react.doctor/prompts/rules/<plugin>/<rule>.md; it edits the working tree directly and never commits or opens PRs. Rule tuning lives in doctor.config.* or package.json#reactDoctor.
- **Reference / source:** github.com/millionco/react-doctor; playbooks and rule prompts hosted at react.doctor.
- **Best for:** Pre-commit QA on React builds — a health gate after any feature work. Process tool; no page use.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0465⟧

## ⟦S0466⟧ millionco/reconcile-paper-sync — Part 13 — UI Skills, rest of the ui-skills.com catalog
- **What it is:** The verification-and-repair phase after a Paper-to-code build (companion to ⟦S0464⟧): using the project's local paper-sync mirror as the canonical oracle, it finds and fixes every way the running app drifted "slightly off" its Paper design — fonts first, then exact values, then a screenshot diff.
- **How it looks:** The running app, screenshotted at the design frame's own width, matches the paper-sync render of that frame: same real typefaces (not system fallbacks), same type scale and line heights, same colours, spacing, stacking order and small decorations (code-chip backgrounds, hairlines, dashed outlines, badges).
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** The oracle: .paper-sync/<fileId>/ holds .canonical/*.tsx (verbatim Paper export per frame, named page-1--frame-<id>-0.tsx with the Paper URL in a header comment), paper.css, public/paper-assets/fonts/*.otf, and a dev server (usually localhost:6006) whose ?preview#<FRAME> route renders one frame alone — trust the live preview for what the user sees, the canonical .tsx for exact numbers (on-disk canonical can lag the server). Fonts first: extract the frame's families with grep over font-['…'] — expect several by role; any family the app renders in Geist/Georgia/system-ui instead of the self-hosted real font is the bug; port missing .otf files, @font-face per weight, one token per typeface. Exact values from canonical classes: text-[15px]/6 means 15px size AND 24px line-height; colours kept as exact display-p3/hex. Screenshot diff without Playwright: chrome-headless-shell --hide-scrollbars --force-device-scale-factor=2 --virtual-time-budget=6000 --window-size=<w>,<h> --screenshot, app (localhost:3000) vs frame at matched width, allowing time for @font-face loading. Every difference is classified: conversion drift (the app dropped/substituted something — fix it) vs version drift (the frame is a newer design than the export the app was built from — flag it; never invent data, e.g. fake error bars, to match). Finish: re-run lint/build and report the comparison.
- **Reference / source:** github.com/millionco/skills (skills/reconcile-paper-sync).
- **Best for:** Final QA on any Paper-derived build before calling it done. Process tool; no page use.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0466⟧

## ⟦S0467⟧ millionco/tailwind-token-consolidation — Part 13 — UI Skills, rest of the ui-skills.com catalog
- **What it is:** A rigorous procedure for shrinking the number of CSS custom properties / Tailwind v4 design tokens in a globals.css — deleting dead tokens and collapsing near-identical ones by script — while the rendered site stays visually identical.
- **How it looks:** Exactly as before: same cards, page background, dropdowns, colours in light and dark. Only the token file changes — realistically 50–60% fewer tokens with named tokens preserved; the skill explicitly refuses to chase ~70% by inlining values into arbitrary-value classes, which just moves the noise into classNames.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion; visual identity before/after is the success criterion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Order of operations is mandatory: (1) parse globals.css into blocks (@theme inline, :root, .dark, scoped blocks) and count tokens; build a usage map from ALL .ts/.tsx/.css/.mdx files (class names and var(--…) refs); (2) compute the LIVE set transitively — used as a class, referenced as var(), or referenced inside another live token's value, iterated to a fixed point; (3) also scan globals.css's own utility classes for var() hard dependencies (strip the token blocks out, collect var() refs in the remainder — those tokens must stay); (4) build a deterministic rename map (old_suffix → new_suffix or DELETE) and apply it by script to CSS and code in one pass, never by hand-editing class names; (5) verify after every pass: typecheck, lint, format, build all green. Two levers in order: dead deletion (zero risk), then value-similar collapse (values within ~5% in BOTH light and dark). The eight named bugs: value precedence (first-write-wins picks the wrong source colour — fix with an explicit CANONICAL_SOURCE override dict); scoped overrides (tokens overridden in blocks like .dashboard-page must stay tokens); intra-globals consumers; category cross-pollination (a suffix can be both a colour and a shadow prefix — only the colour category renames the bare --X); aggressive icon-grey collapse (keep two icon tones, --icon ≈ #696969 and --icon-soft ≈ #b3b3b3); transparent-in-one-mode surfaces (never collapse into an always-opaque token); bg-X collision (Tailwind v4 resolves bg-X against both --color-X and --background-image-X — grep before choosing a target name); always-dark surfaces (dropdown/tooltip text is light in both modes — diff light/dark values before collapsing into a flipping token like --foreground). Block emission uses the three-pass order: canonical entries → CANONICAL_SOURCE overrides → renamed entries only if unset. Done = all four checks pass, token counts reported (rg count of --…: declarations), and the top 3 surfaces read-verified in the resulting :root.
- **Reference / source:** github.com/millionco/skills (skills/tailwind-token-consolidation).
- **Best for:** Design-system maintenance on Tailwind v4 projects. Process tool; pairs with ⟦S0455⟧ (Tailwind practice) but is a separate, narrower operation.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0467⟧

## ⟦S0468⟧ moguzbulbul/blueprint-animation — Part 13 — UI Skills, rest of the ui-skills.com catalog
- **What it is:** A production spec (v1.3.1) for one continuous, never-cutting animation of a single app screen that explains UX decisions step by step: in Redesign mode (Before + After screens) the changed parts rebuild on screen; in Explain mode (one screen) each module is annotated with what it is and why. Built on Claude Design's animations_v3 engine (React/JSX scene files). For case studies and posts.
- **How it looks:** The real UI, reproduced 1:1 from Figma, sits on a canvas with a text band beneath it. Per step: everything except one focus area washes toward white; then a cyan scan line sweeps down and everything above it becomes a blueprint drawing — the whole screen redrawn as cyan-ink wireframes on white, wires carrying their real labels, with dotted alignment guides, dimension lines with small uppercase mono labels (e.g. "CENTERED COLUMN · 760"), and 5px selection handles on the wires that matter. The changed wires then rebuild (or the reasoning marks draw in), the scan line sweeps again to reveal the new (or same) real UI, and a caption line in the band states the problem and the fix.
- **Frame by frame:** Each step runs five phases on local step time t (authored seconds ÷ K, K = 1.4 slow factor). Problem/Focus, t 0 → 0.9: all but the focus rect fades toward white (≈78%); a thin grey outline draws around the focus; the band shows number, name and problem (or "what" in Explain). Blueprint in, t 0.95 → 1.75: the scan line sweeps top → bottom; above it the whole app is blueprint, below it the real old UI. Construct/Annotate, t 1.9 → c1: in Redesign only the changing wires move/resize/merge (static blueprint behind dims 0.7 → 0.3, guides and dimension lines draw); in Explain nothing moves — handles → guides → dimension line → labels draw in, staggered 0.08–0.12s apart. Reveal, t c1 + 0.05 → c1 + 0.85: the scan sweeps again; above it the real new UI (Explain: the same UI), below it blueprint — the old/new swap only ever happens fully covered by the blueprint, never as a visible fade. Hold: the fix (or "why") sentence fades in, then the focus fades out. Final 1s of the piece: the whole app fades out so the loop seam is soft.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Fidelity is rule zero: every value read from the Figma source (frame size, x/y/w/h, fills, strokes, radii, text styles), real fonts loaded, icons exported from Figma as SVG, letter-spacing % → em (−2% = −0.02em); the app renders at the frame's own 1:1 size (a 1440×900 frame gives the default 1600×1200 canvas including margin and text band). Blueprint style: white ground, line colour cyan-ink #0B8FC2, fill #2ACCFF14, guides dotted 2 4, labels 11–12px mono with letter-spacing .06em, no stroked halos. Text rules: no text on a moving wire (wire text fades out when motion starts, q > 0.15, back in when settled, q > 0.85); disappearing wires collapse in place (height → 0); labels live in empty bands only; only one step's notes visible, as [number badge · NAME] [problem] [fix]. Motion hygiene: no value may go 0 → 1 in under ~0.3s unless hidden; layout pushes happen before elements land in the freed space; groups stagger 0.08–0.12s so wires never cross. 3–6 steps, each with a 2–4 word name and one-sentence problem/what (≤ 12 words) and fix/why. Architecture: OM_SCENES scene literal (Before, <steps>, After — or Screen, <modules>, End in Explain), layers stay mounted and hide with visibility, React.memo on all real-UI components with quantised props, moves via transform only, playhead persisted to localStorage at most every 500ms; performance budget: seek loop < 7ms/frame, no playback frame > 34ms. QA: filmstrips at each phase, plus a pixel overlay/diff of the resting UI against the Figma export.
- **Reference / source:** github.com/moguzbulbul/blueprint-animation (skill v1.3.1); engine: Claude Design's animations_v3 starter (copied into the project, not part of the skill); it ships a reference scene, example-scene.jsx (a CRM record page redesigned in 5 steps).
- **Best for:** Case-study and social posts that walk through a design decision — a portfolio piece about a build, not a section of a client homepage. The Explain marks vocabulary (dimension lines for spacing/hit areas, guides for alignment, numbered badges for reading order) is also a good annotation language for design reviews.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0468⟧

## ⟦S0469⟧ mrstev3n/balise-ux-writing — Part 13 — UI Skills, rest of the ui-skills.com catalog
- **What it is:** Balise UX Writing: a context-aware UX-writing skill that reviews, rewrites, creates, harmonises and implements interface copy — buttons, navigation, forms, errors, empty states, onboarding, confirmations, settings, consent, notifications, help — across design files, screenshots, specs, source code, localisation catalogs and rendered apps, without inventing product behaviour or changing facts.
- **How it looks:** Nothing visual of its own: the output is corrected interface text in place (a button that names the real action, an error that offers a recovery path, an empty state that says what happens next) and, for reviews, a findings table (Priority / Location / Current / Proposed / Why).
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Five modes — Review (diagnose only, no edits; the default when intent is ambiguous), Rewrite (smallest change that fixes the diagnosed issue), Generate, Harmonize (one term per object, one verb per recurring action, one progression vocabulary per flow), Implement (approved copy only, applied at the canonical source). Workflow: frame the experience (person, purpose, moment, action, system, proof) → inspect complete context, not isolated strings → inventory copy by role (orientation, action, input, feedback, recovery, assistance, state, decision, data) → diagnose against ten criteria (clarity, action, context, consistency, recovery, trust, inclusion, accessibility, localisation, fit) → act per mode → verify (terminology drift search, tokens/placeholders/plural branches, wrapping/truncation in supported layouts, relevant tests). Severity: Critical (misleads, hides a material consequence, blocks completion/recovery), Important (substantial ambiguity, inconsistency, mistrust), Improvement (clarity/tone polish). High-stakes rules: delete/remove/archive/discard/cancel/leave/revoke/sign out are distinct and must stay distinct; never turn an obligation into a benefit or a pending action into a success; never silently alter consent, privacy, security, payment or legal meaning. Reference files loaded on demand: interface-patterns.md, voice-tone-terminology.md, localization-accessibility.md, source-runtime-workflow.md, research-measurement.md.
- **Reference / source:** github.com/mrstev3n/balise-skills (skills/balise-ux-writing).
- **Best for:** Copy quality on the functional text of any build — quote/contact form labels and errors, CTA wording, confirmation and empty states. A craft layer over sections, not a section.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0469⟧

## ⟦S0470⟧ nolanperk/rad-spacing — Part 13 — UI Skills, rest of the ui-skills.com catalog
- **What it is:** A Figma spacing method built on the Gestalt principle of proximity: spacing grows with nesting depth — outer containers get proportionally more space than inner elements — using the file's library variables in 8px/4px increments. For creating screens, refactoring spacing, and standardising hierarchy.
- **How it looks:** Layouts where grouping is obvious without dividers: labels hug their inputs, fields sit a little further apart, sections further still, and the page frame is the airiest of all — the eye parses the structure from the rhythm of gaps alone.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** The ~40% rule: each parent level gets approximately 1.4× its child level's spacing (equivalently child = parent × 0.6), snapped to the nearest 8px increment — unless the 0.6 result lands closer to a 4px increment, in which case use the 4px value. Work from the innermost level outward, commonly from an 8px base for the tightest grouping. Default variable set when the library has none: spacing/xs 4px, sm 8px, md 12px, lg 16px, xl 24px, 2xl 32px, 3xl 48px (adapt to the file's existing naming). Worked example (settings page): field label↔input gap 8px → fields within a section 12px (8 × 1.4 = 11.2 → 12) → sections 16px (12 × 1.4 = 16.8 → 16) → content-area padding 24px → page padding 32px. Apply with padding on auto-layout frames for containers and gap (itemSpacing) between siblings, bound to the variables. Edge cases: cap deep hierarchies at 48–64px and compress inner levels; floor the innermost level at 4px and recalculate outward; a component reused at different depths takes the spacing of its context, not its definition; remap inconsistent existing designs systematically from the inside out, never value by value.
- **Reference / source:** github.com/nolanperk/rad-spacing (rad-spacing.md); applied through the Figma (use_figma) MCP tool.
- **Best for:** Spacing discipline for any layout — the underlying rhythm transfers directly to web builds (section padding vs card padding vs inner gaps in hero, process, forms and footer stacks).
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0470⟧

## ⟦S0471⟧ nutlope/hallmark — Part 13 — UI Skills, rest of the ui-skills.com catalog
- **What it is:** Hallmark (by Nutlope; "Powered by Together AI"): a design skill for building new websites and pages that look designed, not generated — a non-waivable quality "Floor", a dealt-theme system so consecutive builds don't converge on the same look, one signature idea per screen, and a linted sweep at the end. Never to be used on an existing design unless the user explicitly names Hallmark (e.g. "/hallmark redesign <path>").
- **How it looks:** Pages with a real point of view and very little text: the hero is a headline of seven words or fewer, one short sentence and the primary action — all visible at 1280×800 without scrolling — above large, real imagery or one built-live product moment ("the signature"). No eyebrows, no tracked-capital labels, no purple-to-blue gradients, no cards inside cards, no emoji icons, no invented metrics or testimonials; labels sit in the body face, a step smaller, sentence case. The container is capped and centred, so at 1920px the gutters grow and the measure does not.
- **Frame by frame:** Deliberately near-still: at most one reveal per page, none where the theme keeps still, and content visible by default (and with scripting off). What motion exists animates transform and opacity only — never width, height, top or left, and never `transition: all`. Every animation carries a prefers-reduced-motion fallback.
- **Mechanism & key values:** The Floor (16 rules, none waivable): every colour and font via a token declared at :root; overflow-x: clip on html and body (never hidden, never 100vw); image-bearing grid tracks use minmax(0, 1fr), display heads get overflow-wrap: break-word + min-width: 0; every interactive element has an instantly appearing :focus-visible; no invented metric/testimonial/logo wall/case-study count; ~80 words per screen, ≤450 visible words per page; 6–9 sections including hero and footer (5 on a thin prompt); headline ≤7 words / 50 characters, supporting sentence ≤12 words; pictures at most a third of the page below the hero, never two photo-led sections in a row; the first non-empty CSS line is the Hallmark stamp, then the critique line, then waivers (all within 40 lines). Workflow: pre-flight (read the project; a design.md/DESIGN.md at root locks the system and overrides everything) → ask once (material, audience, use, tone — tone must be an extreme: editorial, brutalist, soft, utilitarian, luxury, playful, technical, austere) → shape from the material inventory and the job's anatomy → direction (a named theme, a custom derivation, or theme.mjs deal — three dealt themes, pick by material) → the draw (theme.mjs draw deals shape, hero posture, nav, footer, compositions to avoid) → one Picks block stating every decision → build hero first and lint it (sloplint.mjs <file> --render --stage hero) before building sections → sweep (sloplint --render until clean, gates review, fresh-context finish review, material ask). Genres assigned silently: atmospheric (AI/generative/dark), modern-minimal (SaaS/B2B/dev), playful, editorial (default). Verbs, only when named: redesign <target> (keep content and wiring), audit <target> (report). Note: its imagery rules ban drawn illustration outright — pages show photographs, product screenshots or the product built live, never model-drawn illustration.
- **Reference / source:** github.com/nutlope/hallmark (skills/hallmark); tooling: scripts/theme.mjs (deal/draw/scaffold/photos/log), scripts/sloplint.mjs, scripts/capture.mjs; "Powered by Together AI".
- **Best for:** Whole new-page builds that must not read as AI-generated — a discipline and art-direction layer over an entire homepage rather than a section technique. Its Floor rules (token discipline, fold rule, word budget, no invented proof) are a useful audit checklist for trade builds.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0471⟧

## ⟦S0472⟧ nvillapiano/cc-figma-component — Part 13 — UI Skills, rest of the ui-skills.com catalog
- **What it is:** A skill that generates complete Figma component sets from JSON "component contracts": it reads a contract, derives component-scoped (Tier 3) tokens at runtime, and builds a fully variable-bound variant matrix in Figma via the Plugin API. Companion to ⟦S0473⟧, which must run first — the Primitives and Semantic variable collections must already exist in the file.
- **How it looks:** A dedicated Figma page per component holding one component set per primary-variant value (e.g. Button/Primary, Button/Secondary, Button/Ghost, Button/Destructive), each set a tidy grid of variants — every Size × State combination, correctly coloured by bound variables, buttons wider than tall — plus a pale-yellow ⚠️ Generation Notes frame underneath documenting every assumption and unresolved gap.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion; the deliverable is a Figma component set, not an animation.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Contract: {CONTRACTS_DIR}/{id}.contract.json with tokens / props / a11y / platforms sections. Tier 3 naming: --ds-{componentId}-{role}-{qualifier}, qualifier taken from the Semantic alias with its scale suffix dropped ("background.primary": "brand.500" → --ds-button-fill-brand; state suffixes append after: --ds-button-fill-brand-hover); role translation: color.background→fill, color.text→text, color.border→border, spacing→spacing, typography→typography, border.radius/width→border, motion→transition. Semantic lookup maps contract values to variable names ("brand.500" → "brand/500"); a missing Semantic variable stops the run. Architecture: primary variant values become separate sets; remaining axes become variant properties in title case. Standard example: Button = 3 sizes × 6 states (Default, Hover, Focus, Active, Disabled, Loading) = 18 variants per set; states always read from the contract's states array (Accordion has 5, no Loading); above 30 variants per set, raise it with the user. The HUG rule: every frame gets layoutSizingHorizontal AND layoutSizingVertical = 'HUG' immediately after creation, on every duplicate, and on the Notes frame — Figma defaults new frames to FIXED 100px height, and omitting the vertical line is the classic portrait-button bug; a post-creation enforceHug sweep walks the subtree. Variant grid after combineAsVariants (which does not auto-layout): COLS = 6 (one column per state), GAP = 40, PADDING = 40, then resize the set to computed content bounds (max right/bottom + padding) — never guessed. Icon placeholders: fixed size (20×20 at md), no fill, visible: false by default, wired to a BOOLEAN iconStart property via componentPropertyReferences (type visible); the TEXT label property binds characters on ALL variants including Loading (never hardcode "Saving"). Binding: Semantic variables only, never Primitives; setExplicitVariableModeForCollection recursively after every binding (ghost-mode prevention); cornerRadius can't take setBoundVariable — bind the four corners individually; letter-spacing can't be bound (set fixed px); rotation values are degrees, never radians; always setSharedPluginData/getSharedPluginData under the component_contracts namespace, never the non-shared pair; eval is blocked in the sandbox (new Function workaround); atob undefined. fullWidth and iconOnly exist as properties but cannot drive layout through the API — documented in the Notes frame (#FFFBEB fill), which also flags focus-ring colour conflicts rather than fixing them (a focus/default equal to a variant fill gets a note suggesting a focus/onBrand token). Workflow: Phase 0 discovery + plan approval → 1 page setup → 2 base component → 3 variant matrix → 4 binding pass → 5 properties → 6 annotations → 7 validation + summary JSON; all working scripts live in scripts/ and are deleted at the end (except in debug mode, which stops after each phase for approval). Config from .component-contracts at project root (FIGMA_ACCESS_TOKEN — never output — FIGMA_FILE_KEY, TOKENS_DIR, CONTRACTS_DIR); every use_figma call passes skillNames: "cc-figma-component".
- **Reference / source:** github.com/nvillapiano/component-contracts-figma (skills/cc-figma-component); requires the figma-use and figma-generate-library skills.
- **Best for:** Design-system production inside Figma — generating contract-true component sets. Infrastructure for design teams; no direct role on a trade website page.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0472⟧

## ⟦S0473⟧ nvillapiano/cc-figma-tokens — Part 13 — UI Skills, rest of the ui-skills.com catalog
- **What it is:** The prerequisite companion to ⟦S0472⟧: it builds or updates the two Figma variable collections — Primitives and Semantic — from component-contracts token files in W3C DTCG format, so components can bind to native Figma variables.
- **How it looks:** Inside Figma's variables panel: two collections, each with a single "Value" mode — Primitives holding raw values in scale-named variables (color/blue/500, space/4, radius/md), Semantic holding role-named aliases (brand/500, surface/default, text/primary, focus/default) that point into Primitives.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Token files: {TOKENS_DIR}/primitive/{color, motion, shape, space, typography}.tokens.json and semantic/semantic.tokens.json; read all files and build the complete in-memory map before any Figma call. Collections created in order (Primitives, then Semantic), one mode ("Value") each. Naming uses / as the group separator, matching the DTCG path. Scopes are role-based — NEVER ALL_SCOPES: background/fill colours → FRAME_FILL, SHAPE_FILL; text colours → TEXT_FILL; border colours → STROKE_COLOR; focus colours → all three; spacing → GAP only (HORIZONTAL_PADDING / VERTICAL_PADDING are not valid VariableScope values); border width → STROKE_WIDTH; radius → CORNER_RADIUS; font size/weight/line-height → FONT_SIZE / FONT_WEIGHT / LINE_HEIGHT; all Primitives get scopes [] (hidden from property panels). WEB code syntax is mandatory on every variable: var(--ds-{path with / → -}), e.g. var(--ds-color-blue-500), var(--ds-brand-500); ANDROID/iOS take no var() wrapper. Batching is the performance rule: ALL variables of a collection in ONE use_figma call (split by category only if a collection exceeds ~80 variables — never one call per variable), no intermediate state files, validate once at the end. Aliases: figma.variables.createVariableAlias; chained aliases are permitted and not flattened (Semantic border/brand → Semantic brand/500 → Primitive color/blue/500), so creation order must create targets before dependents. Updates: add new variables and edit Primitive values (the alias chain follows); never delete variables without explicit confirmation; idempotency check via getLocalVariables() before creating. Phase 3 calls setExplicitVariableModeForCollection on every node to suppress the ghost mode Figma auto-creates. Constraints: letter-spacing cannot be a variable (unitless FLOAT vs em) — Text Styles only; font family needs a STRING variable; always setSharedPluginData (component_contracts namespace), never setPluginData. Config from .component-contracts; every use_figma call passes skillNames: "cc-figma-tokens"; requires figma-use and figma-generate-library.
- **Reference / source:** github.com/nvillapiano/component-contracts-figma (skills/cc-figma-tokens).
- **Best for:** Design-token infrastructure in Figma — run before ⟦S0472⟧. No direct role on a website page.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0473⟧

## ⟦S0474⟧ openai/define-goal — Part 13 — UI Skills, rest of the ui-skills.com catalog
- **What it is:** OpenAI's goal-definition skill: it shapes a fuzzy intention into a concrete, measurable objective — outcome, verification evidence, scope bounds, stop condition — and only then creates it with the goal tool. Definition only; it deliberately does not create planning artifacts, snapshots, ledgers or decision logs.
- **How it looks:** Nothing visual — the output is one concise objective string, of the shape: the concrete thing that will be true, the artifact/system it touches, the exact validator that proves it, and the boundaries.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Workflow: confirm a goal is actually wanted (don't force goal creation on ordinary implementation work) → restate the goal concretely (specific outcome; artifact/system/repo involved; how completion is verified; in scope; out of scope; the stop condition for asking instead of grinding) → quantify where the domain supports it (pass/fail validators: exact tests, CI jobs, commands, acceptance criteria; quality thresholds: latency, error rate, cost, accuracy, coverage, bundle size, uptime; artifact constraints: paths, modules, formats, deadlines, blast radius; evidence counts: reproduced failures, successful reruns, reviewed examples) → repair weak goals (rewrite vague ones when safe; ask ONE concise question when a missing detail changes the outcome; reject pure-activity goals like "make progress" or "keep investigating") → check active goal state with get_goal (continue a matching goal, never duplicate; ask on conflict) → create_goal with a single objective string that carries its own verification evidence, scope bounds, and a token budget only if the user explicitly requested one. Quantification heuristics per domain: bugs = reproduction first, then a failing-then-passing validator; performance = metric + threshold + method + number of runs; research = the decision it must enable + sources in scope + evidence standard; operations = healthy state + monitoring window + failure threshold + rollback/escalation trigger.
- **Reference / source:** github.com/openai/skills (skills/.curated/define-goal).
- **Best for:** Project process — framing work before execution. No role on any page or section.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0474⟧

## ⟦S0475⟧ oso95/scroll-world — Part 13 — UI Skills, rest of the ui-skills.com catalog
- **What it is:** A full production pipeline for a "scroll-world" landing page: the visitor's scroll drives a camera that dives from outside an AI-generated miniature scene into its interior, then flies out and into the next scene, continuously, with no visible cuts — the Apple scroll-through technique. The visuals are pre-rendered AI video (scene stills → dive clips → connector clips); the page itself only scrubs video by scroll position, using a self-contained vanilla-JS scrub engine that drops into any stack.
- **How it looks:** A sequence of miniature worlds — by default soft matte low-poly clay dioramas, isometric, tilt-shift, warm light — presented as scenes the camera flies through. On load, the first scene's still image greets the visitor with pinned copy (eyebrow, headline, one body line, up to 3 tag pills) and a route rail; scrolling sets the camera moving: descending into the scene as its copy peaks, then pulling up and over an aerial hop to the next island (fly-through style), or gliding forward through doorway to doorway (walkthrough style); the final scene holds its copy and CTA. Scenes can float transparent over an atmospheric page background if their backgrounds are knocked out.
- **Frame by frame:** Trigger: scroll (and it plays in reverse on scroll-up). Per section: still poster shows until the clip paints → scroll drives video.currentTime (rAF-smoothed) → the camera dives/glides through the scene — with linger set, it settles mid-scene exactly while the pinned copy peaks, then speeds up toward the seam → a short crossfade at the seam (frame-matched endpoints underneath) → in architecture B, the connector clip pulls up and back out, rises, glides across the miniature world and begins descending into the next scene; in architecture A there is no connector — the next leg simply continues forward from the previous leg's actual last frame → end state per scene: next scene's interior with its copy pinned; the last section holds its CTA.
- **Mechanism & key values:** The seam law (the make-or-break rule): connector endpoints must be the neighbouring clips' ACTUAL rendered frames — start-image = dive_i's last frame (ffmpeg -sseof -0.15), end-image = dive_{i+1}'s first frame (ffmpeg -ss 0) — never the original stills, or every seam pops. Chain shape: N stills → N dive clips → N−1 connectors = 2N−1 clips, all from ONE video model (each renderer has its own grain/motion character). Camera architecture is chosen at interview and never re-decided: A) continuous forward take — legs generated sequentially, each --start-image = previous leg's actual last frame, no --end-image (an end-image forces a pull-back = the #1 stutter cause), wired with connectors: [] and crossfade ~0.08; legs may take expressive mid-leg moves (half-orbit, crane-up, lateral track) provided each leg ends settling into a slow forward drift for its final ~1s and the next begins continuing it; A + locked-iso clause = fixed isometric angle throughout, world slides past (calmest, cheapest re-rolls). B) dive + aerial connector — only for diorama/miniature worlds, because the camera reverses direction at every seam (in grounded/photoreal work that reads as a rewind stutter). Model roster (frame-locking is the entry requirement — a model whose inputs are reference-only can condition but not continue a shot, so it is declined): seedance_2_0 (default; dives --mode std --resolution 1080p --aspect_ratio 16:9 --duration 8; connectors --duration 5); kling3_0 (720p native — no --resolution param; --sound off; legs --duration 10; the sanctioned NSFW-filter fallback); seedance_2_0_mini (720p, the draft/previz tier — run the chain cheap, approve, re-render finals). Stills: gpt_image_2 at 3:2, 2k, quality high, one byte-identical style preamble for all N (cohesion), or Codex image_gen (same model, ChatGPT-billed, 1536×1024) — one source for all stills of a build; optional knockout.py border-connected flood-fill to float scenes. Billing: Monid is the default chain biller (pay-per-clip USD; token price width × height × 24 × seconds / 1024 at $7/1M for 480p/720p, $7.7/1M at 1080p — measured: 1080p 8s dive ≈ $2.99, 5s connector ≈ $1.87, 720p ≈ $1.21/$0.76; an N=6 desktop chain ≈ $27 at 1080p / ~$11 at 720p); Higgsfield credits are the fallback biller (observed on a Plus plan: standard video ≈ 40–55 credits, still ≈ 15). Monid contract: images by public URL only (via its free sfs file system — base64 rejected), ratio passed explicitly (16:9 or 9:16), cost.value read off every run, result URLs expire in ~24–48h. Encoding for scrubbing: blob URLs make clips fully seekable regardless of host range support; native resolution, libx264 crf 20, GOP -g 8 (NOT all-intra — that bloats an 8s clip to ~25MB vs ~8MB), -an, +faststart, unsharp=5:5:0.8:5:5:0.0. Engine pacing: diveScroll 1.3 and connScroll 0.9 viewport-heights per clip by default; per-section scroll overrides dwell; linger 0–1 (keep ≤ 0.6) remaps time so the camera settles mid-scene; theme via --sw-* CSS variables in an @layer sw block. Mobile is a separate opt-in decision asked up front: a native 9:16 portrait chain (~2× spend) encoded 720 wide, -g 4, crf 23, wired as clipMobile/connectorsMobile/stillMobile — the 16:9 centre-crop is a labelled stopgap only, never the default. Phone hardening is always on regardless: seek-coalescing, still-as-poster until first paint, first-touch priming (the iOS blank-video fix), safe-area insets, height-only resizes ignored. Reduced motion: fall back to the stills, no video, no particles. QA: screenshot just before/after every seam and compare composition (a good frame-locked seam can still read ~18–25 dB PSNR from detail shimmer; a real mismatch shows different props/composition), verify video.seekable.end(0) > 0. Known traps: Seedance's NSFW filter false-positives on innocuous interiors (bed/pool/waterfall wording) — re-roll, strip trigger words, or re-render that one clip on kling3_0; Higgsfield gens take 3–8 min each, always detached; never pass --generate-audio on seedance; bash 3.2 on macOS (no associative arrays; array loops belong in #!/bin/bash scripts, never inline zsh).
- **Reference / source:** github.com/oso95/scroll-world; bundled references: prompts.md (intake + every prompt template), pipeline.md (batch scripts), scrub-engine.js, index-template.html, knockout.py. Generation backends: Monid CLI (default) and Higgsfield CLI (stills + fallback chain).
- **Best for:** A flagship campaign-style hero/journey — a firm's whole story told as one flight (e.g. fields → workshop → showroom → delivery). Heavy and expensive (2N−1 AI video generations, sequential for architecture A, plus re-roll headroom), and the imagery is AI-generated rather than the firm's real work — so it suits a brand/campaign piece, not a standard trade homepage where real project photography carries the proof.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0475⟧
## ⟦S0476⟧ petergyang/human-review — Part 13 — UI Skills, rest of the ui-skills.com catalog (petergyang)
- **What it is:** A review-loop tool, not a design: it opens an HTML file, Markdown file, or localhost page in the user's real browser so they can edit text in place and attach comments to selections or whole blocks, then returns everything as one JSON batch for the agent to apply. Used after producing anything the user will read — specs, plans, reports, newsletter drafts, landing pages, slide decks.
- **How it looks:** The page itself, rendered in the browser (Markdown shows rendered, never raw), with its text blocks directly typeable. Author-named regions appear in the user's edit list under their given names when the HTML carries `data-block="Problem body"` on a region or `data-container="Metrics callout"` on a commentable wrapper; otherwise labels are guessed from the DOM. The user selects any rendered text to comment on it, clicks Send, and the page reloads on its own the moment the agent saves fixes — there is no chat reply.
- **Frame by frame:** Not page motion — a workflow sequence. Agent writes/updates the file (or starts the dev server) → runs `npx -y human-review <file-or-localhost-URL>` → user types edits (on plain HTML these autosave to disk as they type; on Markdown/localhost/self-rendering HTML they exist only in the batch) and adds selection/element comments → user hits Send → the blocking `poll` command prints one batch grouped by page: `edits` (label, kind edited/deleted/moved, before, after, after_html) and `comments` (quote plus anchor prefix/suffix) plus an optional `overall_note` → agent applies edits verbatim to the source (never reverts `after`; a `deleted` edit deletes the block; a `moved` edit repositions it after the block starting with `moved_after`, both clipped to 90 characters) → next poll runs with `--ack`, which clears the handled batch and deletes staged assets, so images must be copied out before acking. A poll only reports `timeout` after 12 hours; `closed` ends the loop, `superseded` means a newer poll owns the wait.
- **Mechanism & key values:** CLI via `npx -y human-review` with subcommands open / `poll` / `poll --ack` / `status` (status answers instantly: `{"status":"feedback-waiting"}` plus unsent counts). Edit text is cut at 200k characters (flagged `truncated: true` — read the block from the page, not the batch). Pasted images land in an `assets/` folder beside the reviewed file (or under `staged_assets` for localhost pages) and keep their relative path. `edits_saved: true` means the on-disk file is already newer than the agent's copy — re-read before touching, make targeted changes only. In Claude Code the poll runs with `run_in_background: true`; in other harnesses it must run in the foreground of the active turn.
- **Reference / source:** github.com/petergyang/human-review (src/SKILL.md). No design references or sites named.
- **Best for:** The human-approval step of any deliverable — directly relevant to a screenshot/draft approval workflow for previews, plans and copy sign-off. Trade fit: process tool only; it designs no homepage section, but it is a clean way to collect a client's or owner's exact wording edits on a preview page or proposal.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0476⟧

## ⟦S0477⟧ petergyang/no-ai-slop — Part 13 — UI Skills, rest of the ui-skills.com catalog (petergyang)
- **What it is:** A copy-editing skill with two jobs: edit a draft into sharper, human-sounding writing while preserving the writer's own voice (the default), or detect-only — name each AI-slop pattern found, quote the line, give a short fix, never rewrite, score, or guess authorship. Ships with a bundled self-check file, `eval.md`.
- **How it looks:** Nothing visual changes except the words on the page, but the effect is concrete: headlines and body copy that state facts instead of announcing importance. The skill's own before/afters show the look — "The integration improved efficiency" becomes "The integration cut deploy time from 40 minutes to 4"; "The app serves as a centralized hub for sponsor management" becomes "The app tracks sponsors, drafts, due dates, and approvals in one place"; "The launch marks a pivotal moment for the company" becomes "The launch is the company's first paid product." Output is the full edited draft plus a short "What changed" section.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. It governs text only.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Minimum-effective-edit rule: fix patterns, errors, repetition and unclear passages; leave strong human sentences alone; keep the writer's vocabulary, cadence, bluntness, humor, uncertainty and digressions. Banned outright (28 terms): delve, foster, leverage, utilize, facilitate, empower, streamline, robust, cutting-edge, paradigm shift, game changer, tapestry, realm, beacon, multifaceted, meticulous, intricate, paramount, transformative, elevate, embark, supercharge, harness, ever-evolving, and similar. Often-empty adverbs (just, literally, honestly, simply, actually, truly…) and phrases ("it's worth noting", "at the end of the day", "at its core", "in today's world", "let's dive in"…) are cut when they add nothing. Named patterns to cut: binary contrasts ("not X, it's Y"), throat-clearing openers, faux-insight setups ("the part everyone misses"), colon reveals, trailing -ing superficial analysis, importance puffery ("stands as a testament"), weasel attribution ("experts agree"), fake-strong verbs, synonym cycling, negative listing, dramatic fragmentation, rhetorical setups, fake-profound kickers (delete, never rewrite into a better metaphor), summary-recap endings, formatting slop, and em-dash clusters (none in short copy; 1–2 allowed in long drafts). The portability test: a sentence that could move unchanged to another person/company/product is filler — cut or make it specific. After editing, the draft must pass eval.md's 26 checks (11 editing-principle, 1 word, 9 pattern, 5 final-read) before it is returned.
- **Reference / source:** github.com/petergyang/no-ai-slop (skills/no-ai-slop/SKILL.md + eval.md). No external sites named.
- **Best for:** The copy pass on any section words — hero headlines, proof/reviews framing, process descriptions, CTA lines, follow-up emails — anywhere generic AI phrasing would flatten a real business's voice. Trade fit: strong for trade copy specifically because the whole method is names, numbers and mechanisms over abstraction (years trading, review counts, towns covered, response times).
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0477⟧

## ⟦S0478⟧ PrototyperAI/animate-ui — Part 13 — UI Skills, rest of the ui-skills.com catalog (Prototyper UI library)
- **What it is:** The animation law for the Prototyper UI component library (Tailwind CSS v4 + Base UI): five copy-paste patterns that cover ~95% of component animation, plus easing tokens, duration tiers, scale values, per-component class strings, performance constraints and an accessibility checklist. One of four sibling skills for the same library (with ⟦S0479⟧, ⟦S0480⟧, ⟦S0481⟧) — not a duplicate of them: this one owns motion only, and the others defer to it for animation.
- **How it looks:** Small, fast, physical-feeling interface motion. A popover, menu or tooltip blooms out of its trigger — fading in while scaling from 95% and sliding 0.5rem (8px) in from the side it sits on, growing from the trigger point rather than its own centre. A dialog fades in over a black/10 backdrop with a faint backdrop blur and slightly overshoots — it scales in at 1.02 and settles, and shrinks to 0.98 on the way out. A sheet slides the full width/height of its edge. Buttons squash a touch when pressed. A checkbox's tick literally draws itself on as a pen stroke. A navigation menu's large panels glide sideways over a third of a second. Nothing bounces, nothing spins except a loading spinner, and under reduced-motion settings all of it switches off.
- **Frame by frame:** Canonical overlay (Pattern A — popover/tooltip): click trigger → popup fades opacity 0→1 and zooms 0.95→1 over 150ms with ease-out-fluid, simultaneously sliding 0.5rem from its placement side (e.g. a bottom popup slides in from top-2), transform-origin pinned to the trigger via `--transform-origin` → close reverses it in 100ms with ease-in-quart (fade + zoom back to 0.95). Dialog (Pattern B): backdrop fades in/out over 200ms; content fades and zooms 1.02→1 entering, 1→0.98 exiting, 200ms ease-out-fluid both ways. Sheet (Pattern C): slides 100% edge-to-edge, 300ms in / 200ms out. Press (Pattern D): while pressed, the element scales to 0.97 (standard), 0.98 (menu items, tab triggers) or 0.95 (small controls), always behind `motion-safe:`. Checkbox: on check, background fills first, then the SVG tick draws — stroke-dashoffset animates 66→44 over 200ms linear with a 50ms delay (dasharray 22). Accordion: panel height animates open/closed with 0.2s ease-out keyframes. Switch: track colour shifts over 250ms while the thumb travels over 300ms ease-out-fluid. Navigation menu: content and positioner move over 350ms on cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1), panels slide 13rem (slide-*-52), popup starts at scale 0.90 + opacity 0, chevron rotates 180° over 300ms. Toasts (sonner, library-handled): enter translateY(100%)→0 over 400ms ease; stacked toasts offset by `--lift-amount` × index with 0.05 scale per level. Drawers (vaul, library-handled): 500ms on the same curve as ease-out-fluid, page behind scales and rounds proportionally to drag progress.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Easing tokens (defined in prototyper-tokens.css): ease-smooth cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1) for on-screen state changes; ease-out-fluid cubic-bezier(0.32, 0.72, 0, 1) for entering elements; ease-in-quart cubic-bezier(0.895, 0.03, 0.685, 0.22) for exits; unused reserves ease-out-quad (0.25, 0.46, 0.45, 0.94), ease-out-quart (0.165, 0.84, 0.44, 1), ease-in-quad (0.55, 0.085, 0.68, 0.53), ease-in-out-quad (0.455, 0.03, 0.515, 0.955). Decision rule: entering → ease-out-fluid, exiting → ease-in-quart, staying → ease-smooth, constant motion → linear; never ease-in for UI entrances. Duration tiers: 100ms instant (alert dialog, context menu, hover card, exits), 150ms fast (state transitions, overlay enter), 200ms standard (dialog, sheet exit, accordion, checkbox), 250ms medium (switch track, slider thumb), 300ms smooth (sheet enter, switch thumb, progress), 350ms long (nav menu only); UI stays under 300ms except nav; exits run 20–33% faster than enters; hold-to-confirm ≈2s linear with ~200ms ease-out release. Scale floor: never animate from scale(0) — minimum 0.85 (slider thumb while dragging), 0.90 (nav popup), 0.95 overlays, always paired with opacity. Animate only transform, opacity, clip-path; never `transition-all`, never width/height/padding/margin (accordion keyframe height excepted); `will-change` only while entering/exiting; transitions preferred over keyframes because they retarget mid-flight. Clip-path inset() recipes for reveals/comparison sliders with recommended easing cubic-bezier(0.77, 0, 0.175, 1); blur bridging = filter blur(2px) mid-transition as a last resort. Gesture values: flick-to-dismiss velocity threshold 0.11 (swipe distance ÷ time), pointer capture during drags, 100ms settle delay after scroll-to-top before drawer drag engages. Accessibility is contractual: `motion-reduce:animate-none` / `motion-reduce:transition-none` on everything animated, `motion-safe:` on all press scales, `hover-only:hover:` on hover effects; never animate keyboard-triggered or hundreds-of-times-per-session actions; tab panels switch instantly.
- **Reference / source:** github.com/PrototyperAI/prototyper-ui (apps/docs/skill/animate-ui/SKILL.md). Built on Base UI (base-ui.com) + Tailwind CSS v4; toast/drawer behaviour delegated to the sonner and vaul libraries. Sibling skills ⟦S0479⟧ build-primitive, ⟦S0480⟧ create-component, ⟦S0481⟧ prototyper-ui cover the same library's other layers.
- **Best for:** The motion settings for any interactive component on a page — dropdown navigation, quote-form dialogs and popovers, FAQ accordions, menus, toasts after form submit. The numbers port directly to vanilla CSS/GSAP builds: a trade homepage's nav menu, call/quote modal and FAQ should run on exactly these durations, easings and exit-faster ratios rather than invented ones.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0478⟧

## ⟦S0479⟧ PrototyperAI/build-primitive — Part 13 — UI Skills, rest of the ui-skills.com catalog (Prototyper UI library)
- **What it is:** How to build a primitive-quality interactive component from scratch when Base UI has none — Breadcrumb, Avatar, Badge, Rating, Pagination, Stepper, Tag Input, File Upload, Calendar, Data Table, Tree View, Command Palette and the like. ARIA contracts first, then keyboard navigation, state management, styling hooks, and form integration. Sibling of ⟦S0478⟧/⟦S0480⟧/⟦S0481⟧ in the same library — this one is the from-scratch path; ⟦S0480⟧ is the wrap-an-existing-primitive path.
- **How it looks:** The components themselves are plain, correct-looking UI — a row of stars for a rating, a strip of page numbers, a text field that grows chips — but the skill's real output is behaviour a visitor can feel: stars fill ahead of the pointer as it hovers and stay keyboard-adjustable; a tag field swallows typed entries into removable pills; only one item in a toolbar/pagination strip is ever in the tab order, arrow keys walk the rest. Visually it follows the library's tokens: semantic colours only (no raw hex, no `dark:` classes), `data-slot` on every element, icons normalised to size-4, hover effects gated to hover-capable devices, press feedback at `motion-safe:active:scale-[0.97]`, 150ms ease-smooth state transitions everywhere.
- **Frame by frame:** Rating (the worked interactive example): Tab lands on the slider as one stop → ArrowRight/ArrowUp steps the value up, ArrowLeft/ArrowDown down, Home = 0, End = max → hovering star i previews fill up to i (hovered value overrides committed value; stars scale to 110% on hover-capable devices) → click commits → mouse-leave clears the preview; colour change runs 150ms ease-smooth; disabled/readOnly ignore all input. Tag Input: type text → Enter commits a chip (trimmed, duplicates and maxTags rejected, input clears) → Backspace in an empty field deletes the last chip → clicking a chip's × removes it; every value is mirrored into hidden inputs so a real form submit carries it. Composite widgets (roving tabindex): Tab focuses only the active item → arrows move focus and swap tabindex 0/−1 between items, wrapping if loop is on → Home/End jump to first/last. Combobox pattern (active descendant): focus never leaves the input; arrows move a highlight in the list, Enter selects, Escape closes. Scratch-built overlays use an animated-presence cycle: open → mount, double requestAnimationFrame, then fade/scale in (opacity 0 + scale 0.95 → full, 150ms ease-out-fluid); close → reverse and unmount only on transitionend (or onAnimationEnd for the keyframe variant, 150ms in / 100ms out).
- **Mechanism & key values:** Four templates chosen by a decision gate (presentational / interactive / form control / composite), and a prior check for headless state machines before hand-building: react-aria (calendar/date), @tanstack/react-table (data table), cmdk (command palette), embla-carousel-react (carousel), react-resizable-panels, @tanstack/react-virtual, @dnd-kit/core. Core hooks given in full: `useControllableState` (value / defaultValue / on{Value}Change convention), `useRovingFocus` (orientation, loop default true, selector `[data-roving-item]`), `useTypeahead` (500ms buffer timeout, prefix match), `useFocusTrap` (selector list a[href], button/input/select/textarea not disabled, [tabindex] not −1; Tab wraps first↔last), `useFocusRestoration`, `useClickOutside` (pointerdown, not click), `useEscapeKey` (stopPropagation so parent overlays stay open), `useAnimatedPresence`, `useMergedRef`. ARIA: a full role-selection tree (slider/meter/progressbar, listbox/radiogroup/combobox, toolbar/tablist, tree/grid, dialog/alertdialog/tooltip, alert/status/log) plus the state-attribute table (aria-expanded/selected/checked/pressed/current/valuenow/min/max/valuetext/live/modal) and naming rules (never put the role name in the label — "Close", not "Close button"). Grid keyboard map: arrows cell-to-cell, Home/End row ends, Ctrl+Home/End grid corners, PageUp/PageDown page/month jumps, clamped. Data-attribute law: booleans are present-or-`undefined`, never the string "false"; dynamic values also exposed as CSS variables (--{component}-value, --available-height, --anchor-width, --transform-origin). Form pattern: one hidden input per value under the same `name`, a visually-hidden required input for validation, and compatibility with a wrapping `<Field>` (id hookup, `data-invalid` error ring).
- **Reference / source:** github.com/PrototyperAI/prototyper-ui (apps/docs/skill/build-primitive/SKILL.md). Anchored to the WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices patterns (w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/) and Base UI primitives (base-ui.com/react/components/{name}); defers animation to ⟦S0478⟧ and component creation to ⟦S0480⟧.
- **Best for:** Building the interactive pieces a trade homepage needs that no library hands you finished — a star-rating display tied to real review counts, photo-gallery pagination, multi-select service pickers in a quote form, steppers — at full keyboard/screen-reader quality. Also the accessibility backbone reference for forms and navigation on any build.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0479⟧

## ⟦S0480⟧ PrototyperAI/create-component — Part 13 — UI Skills, rest of the ui-skills.com catalog (Prototyper UI library)
- **What it is:** The end-to-end production line for adding a component to the Prototyper UI library by wrapping a Base UI primitive: four copy-paste templates, decision trees, props/styling/context conventions, then registry registration, examples, and an MDX docs page. Sibling of ⟦S0478⟧ (animation), ⟦S0479⟧ (from-scratch primitives), ⟦S0481⟧ (usage guide) — the workflow skill of the set, not a duplicate.
- **How it looks:** The components it produces are the library's standard look: a button is a 36px-high (h-9) rounded-md text-sm control with 16px horizontal padding and 16px icons, in semantic token colours (bg-primary, bg-surface, border-border) with tiered shadows (shadow-surface / shadow-field / shadow-overlay — never shadow-lg). A popup is a min-width 8rem rounded-lg panel on bg-overlay with shadow-overlay, sitting 4px from its trigger (sideOffset default 4, align center). A dialog is a centred max-w-lg rounded-xl panel with 24px padding over a black/10 backdrop with extra-small backdrop blur. Dark mode needs no extra classes — token values swap under a `.dark` class on <html>.
- **Frame by frame:** Motion is inherited wholesale from ⟦S0478⟧ and the templates embed its exact strings: Template C popups enter at 150ms ease-out-fluid (fade + zoom from 0.95 + 0.5rem directional slide, origin at the trigger) and exit at 100ms ease-in-quart; Template D dialog content runs 200ms ease-out-fluid with the 1.02 overshoot zoom-in / 0.98 zoom-out; state changes on controls run the standard `transition-[color,background-color,border-color,box-shadow,opacity] duration-150 ease-smooth`, always paired with `motion-reduce:` fallbacks. No other motion is prescribed here.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Template A simple (Button, Toggle — CVA variants + sizes: default h-9 px-4, sm h-8 px-3 text-xs, lg h-10 px-6), Template B compound visual (Switch, Slider, Meter, Progress — Root + Track/Indicator sub-components, optional React context only when sub-components share state, context always created with a safe default), Template C positioned overlay (Portal → Positioner `isolate z-50` → Popup; positioning props side/align/sideOffset/alignOffset live on Positioner, styling on Popup), Template D dialog (Backdrop + centred Popup + Header/Footer/Title/Description/Close wrappers). Hard conventions: `"use client"` on line 1; import order Base UI → CVA → icons → cn → local; deep-path aliased imports (`@base-ui/react/dialog` as DialogPrimitive), never barrel imports; Base UI's `render=` prop instead of Radix `asChild` (with `nativeButton={false}` when Button renders another element); boolean data attributes (`data-open:`) instead of `data-state`; no forwardRef, no default exports, single export block; props destructured className → variants → size → positioning → state → children → ...props, defaults set in destructuring; `cn()` merge order variants → conditional → user className last; `data-slot` naming = family name on root, `{family}-{sub}` on parts. Process: file at registry/ui/{name}.tsx → entry in registry/registry.ts (categories Actions/Forms/Overlays/Navigation/Feedback with their dependency rules) → examples at registry/example/{name}/{name}-demo.tsx (default-exported, one concept each) → `pnpm registry:build` emits shadcn-compatible JSON → MDX page with install commands; dev verified at localhost:3333. An 18-row common-mistakes table polices the whole thing (Radix imports, transition-all, bare hover:/active:, raw shadows, dark: classes, missing motion-reduce:).
- **Reference / source:** github.com/PrototyperAI/prototyper-ui (apps/docs/skill/create-component/SKILL.md); primitives documented at base-ui.com/react/components/{name}; components installable via prototyper-ui.com/r/{name}.json.
- **Best for:** Production workflow rather than a page section: producing consistent buttons, popovers, dialogs, form controls and menus to one standard — the discipline a trade site's CTA buttons, quote-form fields and nav menus should be built under. Pairs with ⟦S0478⟧ for its motion and ⟦S0481⟧ for usage.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0480⟧

## ⟦S0481⟧ PrototyperAI/prototyper-ui — Part 13 — UI Skills, rest of the ui-skills.com catalog (Prototyper UI library)
- **What it is:** The master guide to the Prototyper UI library itself — a copy-paste React component library on @base-ui/react + Tailwind CSS v4 with an OKLCH colour system, CVA variants and compound components (the MUI team's Base UI, Radix's successor — explicitly NOT Radix and NOT stock shadcn). Covers setup, a component-selection guide, six copy-paste usage patterns, the full token system, architecture, styling/customisation, and a component reference table. The hub skill of the Prototyper set (⟦S0478⟧ animation, ⟦S0479⟧ build-primitive, ⟦S0480⟧ create-component hang off it).
- **How it looks:** Calm, token-driven product UI. Surfaces step in tiers — page background, raised card surface, secondary/tertiary nested surfaces, a distinct overlay tone for popovers/dialogs/menus, and a dedicated field background for inputs — each with its own foreground colour. Primary colour is a single strong OKLCH hue (the documented example is a blue at 55% lightness, 0.24 chroma, hue 264) with light/middle/dark ramp steps; hover states are the same colour mixed 10% toward its foreground, soft tints are 15% of the colour over transparent. Cards and inputs cast the light surface/field shadows; overlays get the deep overlay shadow; in dark mode the surface and field shadows disappear entirely (depth comes from tonal contrast) and overlays gain a subtle light border ring. Buttons read as solid primary, destructive, outline, secondary, ghost or link, from compact icon squares to large.
- **Frame by frame:** This guide summarises the library's motion rather than defining it (the exact strings live in ⟦S0478⟧): interactive elements recolour over 150ms ease-smooth; press feedback squashes to scale 0.97 (buttons), 0.98 (menu items), 0.95 (small controls) behind `motion-safe:`; overlays enter/exit with animate-in/animate-out combining fade, zoom-95 and directional slides, signature easing ease-out-fluid cubic-bezier(0.32, 0.72, 0, 1); split timing — colours 100–150ms, transforms 250ms, enters longer than exits (300ms in / 200ms out). Its own visible sequences: a Dialog with `side="right"` slides in as a sheet instead of centring (there is no separate Sheet component); a Slider's indicator fills the track to the thumb, with one thumb per value in a range; a Checkbox shows its animated draw-on tick. Everything animated carries a `motion-reduce:` off-switch.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Setup: `pnpm add @base-ui/react class-variance-authority clsx tailwind-merge lucide-react`; `cn()` = twMerge(clsx()); prototyper-tokens.css imported after tailwindcss in globals.css; next-themes `.dark` class for dark mode. Tokens store raw OKLCH channels (`--primary: 55% 0.24 264`) registered via @theme — used as `bg-primary`, or `oklch(var(--primary))` in raw CSS; never hsl() wrapping or arbitrary hex. Derived colours via color-mix in oklab: hover = 90% colour + 10% its foreground; soft = 15% colour + transparent. Token families: base (background, foreground, border ±light/dark, input, ring, radius), primary ramp, semantic (secondary, muted, accent, destructive), status (success, warning, info), surfaces (surface ×3 tiers, card, popover, overlay), fields (field-background, field-border, -hover, -invalid), derived hovers and softs. Utilities: focus-ring (2px ring, 2px offset), focus-field-ring (2px, −1px offset), invalid-field-ring, status-disabled (opacity 0.5 + pointer-events none), status-pending, no-highlight. Custom variants motion-reduce / motion-safe / hover-only (@media (hover: hover)). Component census with export counts: Button (6 variants, 9 sizes incl. icon sizes, isPending + render=), Toggle 2, Toolbar 6 exports, TextField 4, NumberField 9 (with drag ScrubArea), Checkbox 3, Switch 5 (3 sizes), RadioGroup 2, Slider 6, Select 11, Combobox 24, Menu 15, Dialog 10 (side ×4 = dialog + sheet unified), Popover 6, Tooltip 4, Tabs 5, Field 10 (universal label/description/error wrapper — every input goes inside it), Meter 7 and Progress 7 (4 colour variants each). Docs access: scripts list.mjs / docs.mjs / source.mjs / theme.mjs; URLs prototyper-ui.com/llms.txt, /llms/{component}, /llms-full.txt, /prototyper-tokens.css; MCP server `npx -y @prototyperco/mcp@latest` (list_components, get_component_docs, get_component_source, get_theme, search_docs). Standing rule: always fetch a component's docs before implementing — APIs differ from Radix/shadcn expectations.
- **Reference / source:** github.com/PrototyperAI/prototyper-ui (apps/docs/skill/SKILL.md); prototyper-ui.com for docs/tokens; Base UI (base-ui.com) as the primitive layer.
- **Best for:** Choosing and using ready-made components for the functional layer of a site — quote/contact forms (Field + TextField/Select/Combobox), call CTA buttons, navigation menus and tabs, progress/status displays. For a trade homepage this is the forms-and-controls reference; the visual sections (hero, gallery) come from elsewhere in the bank.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0481⟧

## ⟦S0482⟧ rams-design/rams — Part 13 — UI Skills, rest of the ui-skills.com catalog (rams-design)
- **What it is:** A design-review skill: it audits a UI file (or a scanned project's components) for accessibility and visual-design defects and returns a severity-banded report with a 0–100 score and a concrete fix per issue. If the Rams MCP tools (quick_review, review_files, verify_fixes) are connected it delegates to that hosted engine; otherwise it runs its built-in WCAG 2.2 + visual checklist itself.
- **How it looks:** No page design — the output is a text report in a fixed frame: a "RAMS DESIGN REVIEW: [filename]" banner, then CRITICAL / SERIOUS / MODERATE bands, each issue shown as a category tag ([A11Y]), a line number, the offending code snippet, a one-line fix, and its WCAG reference (e.g. an icon-only `<button><CloseIcon /></button>` → 'Add aria-label="Close"', WCAG 4.1.2), closing with "SUMMARY: X critical, X serious, X moderate / Score: XX/100" and a fixed footer pointing at the full engine.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. It is an audit workflow: read the file(s) first → (with MCP) quick_review on just-edited files during work (~10 seconds, top issues with severity/category/file:line), review_files before commit for the scored pass with applyable patches, verify_fixes after fixing → (without MCP) run the checklist manually in critical-first order → emit the report in the fixed format, footer exactly once.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Critical checks (must fix): images without alt (WCAG 1.1.1), icon-only buttons without accessible name (4.1.2), form inputs without label/aria-label (1.3.1), non-semantic click handlers — div/span onClick without role/tabIndex/key handler (2.1.1), links without href (2.1.1). Serious: focus outline removed without a visible replacement (2.4.7), click handlers without keyboard handlers (2.1.1), colour-only status/error signalling (1.4.1), touch targets under 24×24px minimum — 44×44px recommended (2.5.8). Moderate: skipped heading levels (1.3.1), positive tabIndex (2.4.3), role="button" without tabIndex="0" (4.1.2). Visual pass: inconsistent spacing values, overflow/alignment, z-index conflicts; mixed font families/weights/sizes, line-height problems, missing font fallbacks; contrast below 4.5:1, missing hover/focus states, dark-mode inconsistencies; missing button states (disabled, loading, hover, active, focus) and form-field states (error, success, disabled), inconsistent borders/shadows/icon sizes. The hosted engine behind the MCP tools scores 356 rules and offers one-click fixes on PRs; the local skill is its heuristic approximation.
- **Reference / source:** github.com/rams-design/rams-plugin (skills/rams/SKILL.md); full engine at rams.ai (the report footer carries its utm-tagged URL). WCAG 2.2 is the standards base.
- **Best for:** A QA gate, not a design source: run it over a finished homepage build (or any section) before delivery to catch accessibility failures and visual inconsistencies — alt text on gallery photos, labelled icon buttons in the header, form labels on the quote form, target sizes on tap-to-call buttons, contrast on hero text. Trade fit: universal end-of-build check.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0482⟧

## ⟦S0483⟧ redongreen/create-anatomy — Part 13 — UI Skills, rest of the ui-skills.com catalog (redongreen uSpec)
- **What it is:** A Figma documentation generator: from a component's Markdown spec (produced by the sibling create-component-md skill) it renders a visual anatomy annotation into Figma — the component drawn large with numbered markers on every structural element, beside a 4-column attribute table — plus one follow-up section per sub-component showing that child's internal elements, hidden ones included. The .md is a read-only source of truth; the only artifact produced is the Figma annotation.
- **How it looks:** A spec frame placed on the component's own Figma page, 200px to its right. At its centre sits a live instance of the component (richest variant, hidden children made visible) on a transparent artwork area at least 1400×290px. Every element wears a pink dashed outline (colour RGB 0.922, 0, 0.431 — a hot magenta; 1px stroke, dash 4/4). Numbered circular markers, 33px across, sit 40px outside the component's nearest edge with a thin 1px line connecting each marker to its element; elements nested inside another annotated element instead get an inline marker with a short 16px stub. Beside the artwork, the table's four columns are: number, a type icon (diamond for INSTANCE, "T" for TEXT, a slot glyph for SLOT, frame icon for FRAME), the element name (suffixed "(hidden)" for hidden elements, "(xN)" for deduplicated repeats), and a notes column with a short functional description. A header carries the component name and a one-sentence brief description (max ~15 words).
- **Frame by frame:** A render sequence, not page motion. Step 0: parse the .md's `render-meta` block (component set id, variant axes + defaults, boolean defs, slot contents, sub-components, fileKey, sourceHash) — fail fast with one exact diagnostic line if no .md resolves. Step 1–2: verify the Figma MCP connection (adapter chosen from uspecs.config.json: figma-console vs figma-mcp, same JS either way) and read the Anatomy template key + font family (default Inter). Step 3': one bounded live walk classifies only the chosen variant's direct children (instance / instance-unwrapped / text / slot / container / structural), picks the richest variant if the default is thin, reads slot default children and wrapper visuals — the old full extraction is explicitly deleted and forbidden. Step 4: reasoning pass — bind boolean defs to elements by layer name, set property-aware unhide strategies, mark inline markers, resolve slot preferred components from the seed, deduplicate repeated siblings, write semantic notes, insert synthetic elements for skipped visual layers. Step 6: import the "Anatomy & Properties v2" template by key, create + detach an instance 200px right of the component. Step 7: fill header, clone the `#anatomy-section` as "Component structure", hide the original template section. Step 8: place the instance, unhide hidden children (booleans via setProperties, others directly), populate slots with preferred components (ghost overlay at 0.6 opacity if insertion fails), recompute all bounding boxes after auto-layout reflow, draw outlines, place markers with the nearest-edge + collision-avoidance algorithm (sides scored by distance, 8px minimum gap, perpendicular offsets stepped by 41px), clone one table row per element. Step 8b: repeat the whole artwork+table build per eligible sub-component (skipping utility children like spacers/dividers and any child whose grouped element count is ≤1), then cross-reference "See <child> anatomy section" in the composition table. Step 10: screenshot validation (up to 3 fix iterations). Step 11: print the Figma URL plus a provenance footer carrying the .md's sourceHash.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Marker geometry constants, shared with ⟦S0484⟧: MARKER_SIZE 33, MARKER_OFFSET 40, PADDING 80, COLLISION_GAP 8, INLINE_STUB 16, LINE_WIDTH 1, outline dashPattern [4, 4] at strokeWeight 1, MARKER_COLOR {r 0.922, g 0, b 0.431}; artwork minimum 1400×290 with side room = 33 + 40 + 80 + ceil(perimeter markers ÷ 4) × 41 per side; template gap GAP 200. Classification enum is closed: instance, instance-unwrapped, text, slot, container, structural (RECTANGLE/VECTOR/ELLIPSE/LINE/POLYGON/STAR/BOOLEAN_OPERATION are structural). Text elements quote their content in notes only when ≤30 characters. Child-section leaf resolution walks to depth 4. The figma-mcp variant needs fileKey on every call and a page-activation block after getNodeByIdAsync (use_figma resets currentPage each call); figma-console inherits desktop page context. Execution contract: never edit the input .md, never pause to ask, only two legal stops (missing .md, dead MCP connection).
- **Reference / source:** github.com/redongreen/uSpec (skills/create-anatomy/SKILL.md). Consumes specs from the sibling create-component-md skill; template is the uSpec "Anatomy & Properties v2" Figma template configured via uspecs.config.json. Sibling ⟦S0484⟧ create-voice shares the same MCP adapter table, execution contract and marker system but produces a screen-reader spec — a different artifact, not a duplicate.
- **Best for:** Design-system documentation and hand-off — speccing a component library so developers can build from it. Trade fit: indirect only; it designs no homepage section. Its place in a trade build is downstream, if a reusable component kit (service cards, quote form, review blocks) needs formal anatomy documentation.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0483⟧

## ⟦S0484⟧ redongreen/create-voice — Part 13 — UI Skills, rest of the ui-skills.com catalog (redongreen uSpec)
- **What it is:** The sibling of ⟦S0483⟧ in the uSpec family: it renders a component's already-authored screen-reader specification from its Markdown spec into a Figma "Screen reader" frame — focus order, per-state announcement tables for VoiceOver (iOS), TalkBack (Android) and ARIA (Web), and artwork showing the numbered focus path. It authors nothing: announcements, merge analysis and property rows were produced upstream by extract-voice/create-component-md and are copied verbatim; this skill only renders.
- **How it looks:** A spec frame placed 200px to the right of the component, titled "<Component> Screen reader", with the spec's guidelines text under the header. Inside, one stacked section per entry: a "Focus order" section first (when the component has more than one stop), then one per state (e.g. "Button enabled", "Button disabled"). Each state section holds three platform tables — VoiceOver (iOS), TalkBack (Android), ARIA (Web) — whose header row shows the focus-order number in a 280px column and the part name plus its exact announcement text in a 1120px column (e.g. Button "Submit, button"), with property/value/notes rows beneath. Beside the tables, the Preview area shows the live component instance centred in a transparent wrapper, each focus stop ringed by a pink dashed outline (same magenta as ⟦S0483⟧: RGB 0.922, 0, 0.431, dash 4/4) with a numbered 33px marker 40px off its nearest edge joined by a 1px line — the numbers read in traversal order, so the picture literally shows the path a screen-reader user travels. A state removed from the focus order (e.g. disabled) renders the preview with no markers at all.
- **Frame by frame:** A render sequence. Step 0: parse the .md — Voice body (guidelines blockquote, focus-order table, per-state platform tables, slot insertions) + `render-meta` (compSetNodeId, booleanDefs reshaped to {key: default}, variantAxes/defaults, slotContents, fileKey) + the hidden `voice-render-meta` carry that maps each focus stop to its live Figma layerName and slotIndex; fail fast if no .md. Steps 1–3: platform reference files are read only for slot-scenario reasoning; MCP connection verified; Screen Reader template key + font family (default Inter) read from uspecs.config.json.
