Steps 4–5: assemble render inputs with no Figma reads — per-entry variant props are re-derived by matching state names to variantAxes options (unmatched/behavioural states fall back to variantAxesDefaults); the focus-order entry takes the variant whose state shows the most focus stops. Step 7: audit the assembled inputs against the .md (exactly 3 platform sections per state, every stop name = a carry layerName, null-layerName stops excluded). Step 8–9: import + detach the template 200px right of the component; fill name (with "Screen reader" suffix) and guidelines. Steps 10–11, one figma_execute per entry: clone the state template → clone platform sections, tables, property rows from their templates and fill them → place the component instance in the Preview placeholder, apply variant props via setProperties, force-enable all booleans (focus-order entry only) and apply slot insertions (reset slot, clear children, insert preferred component with nested/text overrides before appendChild) → resolve each focus stop's live bbox by exact layer-name match on the instance (ancestor-aware visibility for the focus-order entry) → if stops remain unresolved there, run the richest-variant fallback: test every variant with booleans + insertions applied, keep the one resolving the most stops, resize and re-centre → draw dashed outlines, then place markers with the same nearest-edge + collision-avoidance algorithm as ⟦S0483⟧ → hide the marker example and state template at the end. Step 12: screenshot validation plus a mandatory resolution check — every documented stop must have produced a marker and outline, or the inputs are fixed and re-rendered (never shipped silently). Step 13: print the Figma URL built from fileKey + frameId.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Marker/artwork constants identical to ⟦S0483⟧ (same system): MARKER_SIZE 33, MARKER_OFFSET 40, PADDING 80, COLLISION_GAP 8, LINE_WIDTH 1, dashPattern [4, 4], MARKER_COLOR {r 0.922, g 0, b 0.431}; GAP 200 for frame placement. Preview wrapper: width read from the template's Preview placeholder (so it cannot blow out the frame width), height = component height + 2 × side room with a 200px floor, where side room = 33 + 40 + 80 + ceil(stop count ÷ 4) × 41. Tables are built by four-level cloning: #state-template → #section → #state-table → #prop-row-template. Table columns: #focus-order 280px, #announcement 1120px. Name-matching law: FOCUS_STOPS names must be the carry's layerName (findStopNode matches node.name === stop.name; a human part name fails silently), with slotIndex for identically-named slot siblings. Instances are never detached during artwork rendering; bboxes are read live after every setProperties/font-load cycle. Execution contract mirrors ⟦S0483⟧: the .md is read-only, no questions, no re-extraction — the legacy tree-walk code is deleted and reintroducing it is forbidden.
- **Reference / source:** github.com/redongreen/uSpec (skills/create-voice/SKILL.md). Upstream producers named in the skill: extract-voice and create-component-md; its own reference files (agent-screenreader-instruction.md, voiceover.md, talkback.md, aria.md under the screen-reader ref set) are consulted only for slot scenarios. Shares its MCP adapter, execution contract and marker geometry with sibling ⟦S0483⟧ create-anatomy — same uSpec system, different artifact (accessibility spec vs structural anatomy), not a duplicate.
- **Best for:** Accessibility documentation and hand-off QA — proving a component's focus order and announcements across iOS, Android and web before it ships. Trade fit: indirect; it designs no homepage section, but its discipline maps onto auditing a trade site's quote form and navigation for screen-reader order (call button, form fields, submit) when an accessibility spec is needed.

# Skills chunk S0485–S0498 — Part 13 — UI Skills — rest of the ui-skills.com catalog

All fourteen entries sit in Part 13 of the catalog. Two family notes, stated plainly:
the three React Router skills (S0485–S0487) are three distinct routing modes of one
library, not duplicates; the five daisyUI skills (S0491–S0495) are one library split
into a hub skill plus four sub-skills (colors, config, install, usage) — related, but
each carries different content. No two skills in this range are the same underlying
skill under different names.

## ⟦S0485⟧ remix-run/react-router-data-mode — Part 13 — UI Skills — rest of the ui-skills.com catalog
- **What it is:** A coding-patterns skill for React Router's "data mode": routing defined as JavaScript route objects with `createBrowserRouter` + `RouterProvider`, adding loaders, actions and pending/optimistic UI to an existing React app without the framework's Vite plugin.
- **How it looks:** Nothing visually distinctive — the visitor sees an ordinary React app whose pages swap instantly on link clicks, search forms that update the URL query instead of reloading, and buttons that react before the server answers (the worked example is a favourite star that flips ★/☆ immediately on click). Layout, type and colour are entirely the builder's own; this skill supplies behaviour, not a look.
- **Frame by frame:** Click a fetcher form button → the UI reads the pending submission (`fetcher.formData`) and renders the expected result at once (star fills) → the action completes in the background → server state replaces the optimistic state with no visible change if it matched. Navigation clicks trigger `useNavigation`-driven pending states the app styles itself. No durations or easings are prescribed anywhere in the skill.
- **Mechanism & key values:** `createBrowserRouter([...])` route-object trees with `path` / `Component` / `children` / `{ index: true }`; `loader` and `action` properties per route; search forms must be `<Form method="get">` (never `onSubmit` + `setSearchParams`); inline mutations must use `useFetcher` + `<fetcher.Form method="post" action={...}>` (never `<Form>`, which navigates); optimistic UI = `fetcher.formData ? fetcher.formData.get("favorite") === "true" : isFavorite`. Detail lives in seven bundled references (routing, route-object, data-loading, actions, navigation, pending-ui, ssr).
- **Reference / source:** remix-run/agent-skills on GitHub (skills/react-router-data-mode/SKILL.md); docs at reactrouter.com/docs.
- **Best for:** Engineering reference only — React app builds with client-side routing and form mutations. No fit for single-file HTML trade homepages; relevant only if a trade site were built as a React SPA.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0485⟧

## ⟦S0486⟧ remix-run/react-router-declarative-mode — Part 13 — UI Skills — rest of the ui-skills.com catalog
- **What it is:** The simplest of the three React Router mode skills: declarative JSX routing with `<BrowserRouter>`, `<Routes>` and `<Route>` — no loaders, no actions, no data features.
- **How it looks:** A standard multi-view React app: a nav bar whose current-page link carries an "active" class (styled by the builder), pages that swap in place on click, headings/content driven by URL segments (the worked example renders "User {userId}" from the path) and a search box whose text mirrors the `?q=` query string as you type.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. The skill prescribes no animation, transition or timing of any kind; page changes are instant React re-renders.
- **Mechanism & key values:** `<BrowserRouter><Routes><Route path element>` JSX trees, nested routes with `<Route index>` children, dynamic segments (`users/:userId`) read with `useParams()`, query strings via `useSearchParams()` (`searchParams.get("q")`, `setSearchParams({ q })`), active nav styling via `NavLink`'s `className={({ isActive }) => ...}` callback with the `end` prop for exact matching, location via `useLocation()`. Three bundled references: routing, navigation, url-values.
- **Reference / source:** remix-run/agent-skills on GitHub (skills/react-router-declarative-mode/SKILL.md); docs at reactrouter.com/docs.
- **Best for:** Engineering reference only — the routing layer of a plain client-side React app. Navigation active-state pattern is the one transferable idea; no fit for the single-file HTML trade builds.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0486⟧

## ⟦S0487⟧ remix-run/react-router-framework-mode — Part 13 — UI Skills — rest of the ui-skills.com catalog
- **What it is:** React Router's full-stack "framework mode" skill: file-based routing, server/client loaders and actions, type-safe route modules, and SSR / SPA / pre-rendering strategies configured through `react-router.config.ts`. Sibling of S0485/S0486 — same library, the maximal mode, not a duplicate.
- **How it looks:** A full website or app: global nav and footer rendered once from `root.tsx` around an `<Outlet />` where each page's content lands, section-specific layouts from nested routes, pending/loading states during navigation, and error-boundary screens when a route fails. Whether pages arrive server-rendered, pre-rendered or client-rendered is invisible to the visitor except in speed.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion prescribed. The visitor-visible behaviours are instant optimistic updates (same fetcher pattern as S0485: the favourite star flips from `fetcher.formData` before the action resolves) and app-defined pending UI while loaders run; the skill names no durations, easings or transitions.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Routes configured in `app/routes.ts`; route modules export `loader` / `clientLoader`, `action` / `clientAction`, and `meta` — which must read `loaderData` (`meta({ loaderData }: Route.MetaArgs)`), the old `data` arg is deprecated. Global UI belongs in `root.tsx`, never separate layout files. Search forms `<Form method="get">`; inline mutations via `useFetcher`. Version gates: core framework features need React Router 7.0.0+; middleware needs 7.9.0+ plus the `v8_middleware` flag — verify with `npm list react-router` before implementing. Twelve bundled references (routing, route-modules, special-files, data-loading, actions, navigation, pending-ui, error-handling, rendering-strategies, middleware, sessions, type-safety).
- **Reference / source:** remix-run/agent-skills on GitHub (skills/react-router-framework-mode/SKILL.md); docs at reactrouter.com/docs.
- **Best for:** Engineering reference only — full-stack React sites/apps, auth via cookie sessions, rendering-strategy choices. No fit for single-file HTML trade homepages.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0487⟧

## ⟦S0488⟧ rolldown/tsdown — Part 13 — UI Skills — rest of the ui-skills.com catalog
- **What it is:** A build-tooling skill for tsdown, a TypeScript/JavaScript library bundler powered by Rolldown and Oxc — bundling libraries for npm with type declarations, multiple output formats and tree shaking. It produces files on disk, not screens.
- **How it looks:** Nothing on screen at all — there is no visitor-facing output. What it produces is a `dist/` folder: ESM/CJS/IIFE/UMD bundles, `.d.ts` declaration files, optional source maps, an auto-generated `package.json` exports field, or a standalone executable.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. (Watch mode rebuilds on file save; nothing visual is prescribed.)
- **Mechanism & key values:** Requires Node.js 22.18.0+ to run (build-time only; output can target `node18`/`node20`/older via `target`). Core config: `defineConfig({ entry, format: ['esm','cjs'], dts: true, clean: true })`. Dependency control via `deps: { neverBundle / alwaysBundle / onlyBundle / onlyImport }`; enhancements: `shims: true` (ESM/CJS compat), `minify: true` or `'dce-only'`, `sourcemap: true | 'inline' | 'hidden'`, `unbundle: true` (preserve directory structure), `exports: true`, experimental `css` pipeline (@tsdown/css) and `exe: true` standalone executables (@tsdown/exe), package validation via `publint` / `attw` (use `'ci-only'` in CI). CLI: `tsdown`, `--watch`, `--format esm,cjs`, `-d lib`, workspace mode `-W -F <pkg>` / `--filter /^pkg-/` / `--concurrency 4`, migration via `npx tsdown-migrate`. Framework recipes exist for React, Vue, Solid, Svelte and WASM (`rolldown-plugin-wasm`).
- **Reference / source:** rolldown/tsdown on GitHub (skills/tsdown/SKILL.md); docs tsdown.dev; Rolldown at rolldown.rs.
- **Best for:** Library/tooling work only — packaging a JS/TS library or component library for npm. No role in page design or in the single-file HTML trade builds.

## ⟦S0489⟧ rossark0/rossark-motion-skill — Part 13 — UI Skills — rest of the ui-skills.com catalog
- **What it is:** A complete method for making drawn things — characters, mascots, plants, fire, water, icons, logos, charts, whole scenes — feel alive with calm, believable motion, built on a small clock/track engine with templates for React Native and SwiftUI, and explicitly portable to the web (same math on requestAnimationFrame, SVG attributes or CSS transforms on groups). Born from a production app's onboarding/paywall art under the brief "it has to feel ALIVE" and "NO TELEPORTING".
- **How it looks:** A static illustration that quietly lives: a character whose pupils glide to glance at things, eyelids blinking shut and open, chest rising with breath, head tilting a few degrees on its neck pivot; a plant swaying from its base with leaf tips travelling further than the stem; a candle flame leaning and stretching; rain and snow falling out of sync; a chart drawing itself on once, then resting. Nothing bounces, nothing snaps, the page layout itself never moves — all motion happens inside the drawing.
- **Frame by frame:** Idle loop (6–9 s cycle for a face): gaze rests → pupils glide to a glance target in ~500 ms → hold at least 1 s → glide back; a blink fires every 3–4 s — lids close in ~110 ms, hold 30–50 ms, reopen more slowly in ~190 ms while the lower lid rises ~15% to meet the upper; breathing lifts the body layer 1–2 units over a 3–5 s ease-in-out wave throughout; the loop's last keyframe equals its first so it never jumps. One-shot scene: beats defined as millisecond windows (e.g. ring [0,900], reach [900,1500], stop [1500,1700]) overlap slightly, play once when the scene appears, then hold on the final frame with only the idle loops still running. Landing: hover → fall with gravity stretch 5–10% → contact squash 15–20% with width kept by volume rule → one small overshoot → settle.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Engine: one clock per character/group/scene — loop clocks for idle life, one-shot clocks for story beats; `track(t, keys)` keyframes `[ms, value, 'out'?]` for single moves (it stops at every key), `flow(t, keys)` for acting (passes through poses without stopping — using `track` for acting reads as a robot); helpers `wave` (−1..1), `loop` (0..1), `bell` (fade in/out over a loop), `seg` (one beat window), `seeded(i)` (stable per-item variety — never `Math.random()` per frame). Curves: travel ease-in-out cubic-bezier(0.77, 0, 0.175, 1); open/arrive ease-out cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1); ease-in only for leaving/falling; endless loops linear. Amplitudes: head tilt 3–6°, plant sway 1.5–4° over 3–6 s, flame lean 2–4° + stretch 3–6% on two waves (e.g. 700 ms and 1100 ms), smoke wisps rise 8–14 units, clouds drift over 20–60 s with parallax layers, glow grows 2–5% over 2–4 s, waiting-to-be-tapped jiggle = 1.5–3% squash-and-widen on a 200–350 ms beat, press feedback = scale 0.97, chart bars stagger 40–80 ms. Follow-through by delay, not springs: child parts read the parent 60–150 ms earlier at 0.3–0.6 strength (head counter-motion −0.45 × lean(t − 110 ms)). Volume rule: width scales by 1/sy^0.6 when height scales by sy. Interface durations: press feedback 100–160 ms, popovers/tooltips 125–200 ms, menus 150–250 ms, sheets/modals 200–500 ms, keep UI moves under 300 ms; elements enter from scale 0.9–0.97, never 0. Reduced motion: loops freeze at frame 0, one-shots show their final frame — both frames must read as good drawings on their own. Ships with a `MOTION.md` project-notes file (Part 1 = the method, Part 2 = per-project rules that override everything) and video-analysis tools (ffmpeg contact sheets, `track_edges.py`, `sample_colors.py`). Interface rules credit Emil Kowalski's design-engineering rules and Benji Taylor's "Family values".
- **Reference / source:** rossark0/rossark-motion-skill on GitHub; bundled reference MOTION.md; the skill's interface section follows Emil Kowalski and Benji Taylor ("Family values").
- **Best for:** Any section carrying illustration, a mascot, an icon or a logo that should feel alive — hero artwork, empty states, process diagrams, chart draw-ons; the amplitude/curve numbers are also a discipline reference for all page motion (calm, small, no teleporting). Directly relevant to trade homepages with drawn/SVG scenes: use the recipes for plants, weather, water, machines and vehicles at small amplitudes.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0489⟧

## ⟦S0490⟧ s0xDk/refactoring-ui — Part 13 — UI Skills — rest of the ui-skills.com catalog
- **What it is:** The rule system from the book *Refactoring UI* by Adam Wathan and Steve Schoger, packaged as a skill: design from constrained scales decided once (spacing, type, colour, shadow), build hierarchy with weight and colour rather than size, and fake depth by emulating light from above.
- **How it looks:** A clean, deliberate interface that is mostly grey — 8–10 grey shades carry text, panels and borders — with one primary colour used sparingly, generous white space that groups related items tightly and separates groups widely, headlines only slightly larger than body text but darker and heavier, soft layered shadows that grow with how "high" an element floats, and one consistent corner radius everywhere. Nothing is an arbitrary size or a one-off colour.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. The skill prescribes no animation; its only state guidance is spatial — a button's shadow shrinks on `:active` so it feels pressed, and a dragged list item's shadow grows so it reads as lifted above its siblings.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Spacing scale (base 16, factors/multiples): 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 96, 128, 192, 256, 384, 512, 640, 768 — no two adjacent values closer than ~25%; fixed opacity steps (.05, .1, .2, .4, .6, .8). Type scale: 12, 14, 16, 18, 20, 24, 30, 36, 48, 60, 72 — hand-picked, not ratio-derived; units px/rem only, never em for the type scale. Weights: 400/500 body, 600/700 emphasis, nothing below 400. Colour: 8–10 greys, 5–10 shades per primary/accent, named 100 (lightest) → 900 (darkest), base 500 picked first; write colours as HSL, never generate shades with lighten()/darken() at runtime. Five shadow elevations at hsla(0,0%,0%,.2): `0 1px 3px` (buttons), `0 4px 6px` (dropdowns), `0 5px 15px`, `0 10px 24px`, `0 15px 35px` (modals). Line-height inversely proportional to size (small text 1.5–2, large headlines ~1); line length 45–75 characters (`max-width: 20em–35em`). Three text colours max (dark / grey / lighter grey), all clearing 4.5:1; WCAG large text = 24px regular or 18.66px bold; non-text control borders need 3:1. Hard rules include: never grey text on a coloured background, more space around a group than within it, never scale elements proportionally across breakpoints, sidebars fixed width while main flexes. Ships `assets/tokens.css` (contrast-verified token set with semantic role layer + dark-mode block) plus references systems.md, diagnose.md (symptom → fix, load first when improving existing UI) and techniques.md (two-part refined shadows, depth/light).
- **Reference / source:** s0xDk/refactoring-ui-skill on GitHub; the book *Refactoring UI* by Adam Wathan & Steve Schoger.
- **Best for:** Whole-page visual discipline on any section — setting the spacing/type/colour/shadow tokens before building heroes, proof, work galleries, forms and footers; also the first call when an existing design "looks off / amateur / cluttered". Strong trade fit: its constrained scales are exactly what keeps a trades homepage looking solid rather than templated.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0490⟧

## ⟦S0492⟧ saadeghi/daisyui-colors — Part 13 — UI Skills — rest of the ui-skills.com catalog
- **What it is:** The colour and theming rulebook for daisyUI 5: a fixed set of semantic colour names whose values are variables, so every component recolours automatically when the theme changes. Sub-skill of the daisyUI family (hub = S0491).
- **How it looks:** A page built almost entirely from base tones — `base-100` blank background, `base-200`/`base-300` progressively darker raised surfaces — with content inked in `base-content`, one `primary` colour reserved for the single most important element on the page, and info/success/warning/error colours (each with a high-contrast `-content` partner) for messages. Swap `data-theme` and the entire palette changes at once; themes can nest per-section with no depth limit.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. Theme switching is an instant variable swap; the skill prescribes no transition.
- **Mechanism & key values:** 22 semantic names: primary, secondary, accent, neutral, base-100/200/300, info, success, warning, error — each brand/state colour paired with a `-content` foreground, plus base-content. Rules: use daisyUI names as Tailwind utilities (`bg-primary`); never use `dark:` with daisyUI colour names; avoid raw Tailwind colour names for text (e.g. `text-gray-800` on `bg-base-100` breaks in dark themes — a fixed colour like `red-500` stays the same in every theme, only acceptable when content must not change). Themes enabled in the plugin block (`themes: light --default, dark --prefersdark, cupcake;`, or `all` / `false`); applied via `data-theme="…"` on `<html>` or any nested element. A custom theme is a `@plugin "daisyui/theme"` block defining every variable: colours in OKLCH (worked example: base-100 `oklch(98% 0.02 240)`, primary `oklch(55% 0.3 240)`), radius tokens `--radius-selector: 1rem`, `--radius-field: 0.25rem`, `--radius-box: 0.5rem` (preferred values 0 / 0.25 / 0.5 / 1 / 2rem), `--size-selector` / `--size-field: 0.25rem`, `--border: 1px`, `--depth: 0|1` (shadow/3D effect), `--noise: 0|1` (grain). Built-in themes can be overridden by name with only the changed values. A `dark:` variant can be bound to chosen themes via `@custom-variant dark (&:where([data-theme=night], [data-theme=night] *))`. Visual theme tool: daisyui.com/theme-generator.
- **Reference / source:** saadeghi/daisyui on GitHub (skills/daisyui/colors/SKILL.md); daisyui.com/docs and theme generator.
- **Best for:** Colour system for any daisyUI/Tailwind build; the base-100/200/300 elevation-by-shade idea and one-primary-per-page rule transfer to hand-built pages too.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0492⟧

## ⟦S0493⟧ saadeghi/daisyui-config — Part 13 — UI Skills — rest of the ui-skills.com catalog
- **What it is:** The configuration reference for daisyUI 5 — a single CSS plugin block that sets which themes load, the root selector, class prefix, included/excluded modules and logging. The smallest skill in this range (~1 KB). Sub-skill of the daisyUI family (hub = S0491).
- **How it looks:** No direct visual output of its own; indirectly it decides which of the 30+ named built-in themes (light, dark, cupcake, bumblebee, emerald, corporate, synthwave, retro, cyberpunk, valentine, halloween, garden, forest, aqua, lofi, pastel, fantasy, wireframe, black, luxury, dracula, cmyk, autumn, business, acid, lemonade, night, coffee, winter, dim, nord, sunset, caramellatte, abyss, silk) a page can switch between, and whether classes carry a prefix.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Defaults: `@plugin "daisyui" { themes: light --default, dark --prefersdark; root: ":root"; include: ; exclude: ; prefix: ; logs: true; }`. `--default` marks the default theme, `--prefersdark` the theme used for `prefers-color-scheme: dark`. The worked example enables the full theme list with bumblebee as default and synthwave as prefersdark, excludes `rootscrollgutter` and `checkbox`, sets `prefix: daisy-` (all classes become `daisy-btn` etc.) and `logs: false`. A theme is applied in markup with `data-theme="THEME_NAME"` on `<html>`. Full docs: daisyui.com/docs/config.
- **Reference / source:** saadeghi/daisyui on GitHub (skills/daisyui/config/SKILL.md); daisyui.com/docs/config.
- **Best for:** Setup step for daisyUI projects only — theme roster, prefixing to avoid class collisions. No design content; no trade-homepage fit beyond that.

## ⟦S0494⟧ saadeghi/daisyui-install — Part 13 — UI Skills — rest of the ui-skills.com catalog
- **What it is:** Installation instructions for daisyUI 5: npm package, CDN links, standalone Tailwind executable, and per-framework guides. Pure setup documentation. Sub-skill of the daisyUI family (hub = S0491).
- **How it looks:** Nothing on screen — installation only. The end state is a project whose CSS entry reads `@import "tailwindcss"; @plugin "daisyui";` (or a page loading the two CDN tags), after which daisyUI classes render.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Hard requirements: daisyUI 5 needs Tailwind CSS 4; `tailwind.config.js` is deprecated in Tailwind v4 and must not be used. NPM route: `npm i -D daisyui@latest`, then add `@plugin "daisyui";` to the CSS file. CDN route (no install): `<link href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/daisyui@5" rel="stylesheet" type="text/css" />` plus `<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@tailwindcss/browser@4"></script>`; `daisyui@5/themes.css` loads all built-in themes, and separate CSS modules can be combined — but CDN files omit the `is-drawer-open:` / `is-drawer-close:` variants. Installation as a dependency is preferred over CDN. Framework-specific guides exist for ~45 stacks (11ty, Angular, Astro, Django, Laravel, Next.js, Nuxt, Phoenix, Rails, React, SvelteKit, Vite, Vue, WordPress…) at daisyui.com/docs/install.
- **Reference / source:** saadeghi/daisyui on GitHub (skills/daisyui/install/SKILL.md); daisyui.com/docs/install.
- **Best for:** Setup step for daisyUI projects only. Of marginal note for single-file pages: the two-tag CDN route is the one way daisyUI could enter a standalone HTML file.

## ⟦S0495⟧ saadeghi/daisyui-usage — Part 13 — UI Skills — rest of the ui-skills.com catalog
- **What it is:** The usage rules for writing daisyUI 5 markup correctly: how component/part/modifier classes compose, when to fall back to Tailwind utilities, and the defaults to respect. Sub-skill of the daisyUI family (hub = S0491).
- **How it looks:** Clean default-variant components composed with Tailwind layout utilities — e.g. a plain `btn` (not `btn btn-primary`) when no variant was asked for, responsive flex/grid layouts with breakpoint prefixes, placeholder photos from picsum.photos, and no custom fonts or body colour classes added unless needed.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. The only behaviour-bearing variables named are cosmetic hooks on specific components (Countdown's `--value`/`--digits`, radial-progress's `--size`/`--thickness`), with no motion values prescribed.
- **Mechanism & key values:** 12 rules, key ones: style by adding the component class plus its part and modifier classes; if classes can't achieve a change use Tailwind utilities (`btn px-10`); only if specificity blocks it, append `!` (`btn bg-red-500!`) — sparingly; build missing components from Tailwind utilities; always add responsive prefixes to flex/grid layouts; write no custom CSS unless necessary; placeholder images `https://picsum.photos/200/300` at the needed dimensions; don't add `bg-base-100 text-base-content` to body unless necessary; design decisions follow the Refactoring UI book; unrequested variants/colours stay default (`btn`, not `btn btn-primary`). Class taxonomy (for reference only, never used in code): component, part, style, behavior, color, size, placement, direction, modifier, variant. Global component overrides via `@utility btn { @apply rounded-full; }`. Semantic colours work with opacity modifiers (`text-base-content/60`); `rounded-box` / `rounded-field` / `rounded-selector` follow the active theme's radius tokens; `glass` applies the glass effect. Base modules (properties, rootcolor, scrollbar, rootscrolllock, rootscrollgutter, svg) can be dropped via `exclude:` in the plugin config.
- **Reference / source:** saadeghi/daisyui on GitHub (skills/daisyui/usage/SKILL.md); design decisions defer to the book *Refactoring UI* (see also ⟦S0490⟧).
- **Best for:** Correctness reference while writing daisyUI markup — forms, buttons, cards in Tailwind projects. Little direct use for hand-built single-file trade pages beyond its defaults discipline.

## ⟦S0496⟧ samyost1/3dicon — Part 13 — UI Skills — rest of the ui-skills.com catalog
- **What it is:** A production pipeline that turns a text prompt or a still image into a seamlessly looping animated icon with true soft transparency: AI image generation for the still, an image-to-video model for the motion, exact mathematical matting for the alpha channel, and an animated WebP as the final asset.
- **How it looks:** A small rich 3D-style icon — the worked examples are a sage-green-and-cream matte-plastic stopwatch whose hand sweeps while the body rocks gently, and a flame icon — rendered as a transparent animated WebP (example output: 857 KB, 122 frames at 24 fps) that plays natively in Chrome, Safari and expo-image with no Lottie conversion and no new native dependency. The deliverable shown to the user at each gate is the still image itself, then a contact sheet of the animation.
- **Frame by frame:** The loop, by strategy: `native` (things that move by themselves — flows, burns, breathes, ticks) = continuous motion from the object's own physics; `event` (inert objects) = the object performs its function once — opens, splits, fills, throws something off — then returns to its exact opening state; `part` = the body stays anchored while one loose/hinged/light piece moves; `surface` = the form stays fixed while light or material travels across it. Energy sets how much the body itself moves: `still` rigid; `calm` leans/settles/breathes; `lively` squashes, tilts, recoils, shakes, springs back; `playful` anticipates, overshoots, wobbles, hops in place (defaults: native/event → lively, part → calm, surface → still). Objects with repeated elements move them out of step, never in unison; anything that extends or is thrown off must retract, settle, be reabsorbed or fade so frame last = frame first and the loop closes seamlessly.
- **Mechanism & key values:** CLI stages (`python -m iconloop --out out …`): `still` → (mandatory human approval gate) → `animate` → `matte` → `encode` → `verify`. Still backends: GPT Image / Nano Banana (~13 cents); full run ~48 cents and ~4 minutes — the approval gate exists because every later stage inherits the still. Motion via OpenRouter on Seedance 2.0 by default (Seedance 2.5, Veo 3.1, Hailuo 3, Wan 2.7 also accept first+last frame; Kling 3.0 rejected — 2,500-character prompt cap; `--via replicate` falls back to Kling 2.5). Matting: the still is flattened onto a known mid-grey, so alpha is solved exactly (`C = (F − (1−a)·BG)/a`) — measured edge colour error 26.9 → 15.9 vs estimating; never chroma-key green/magenta (spills onto glossy edges); never temporally smooth alpha (smears a ghost ring). Encoding: keep the source frame rate (Kling returns 24 fps; dropping to 8 fps for size causes judder) — `--sweep` prints per-rate costs; resolution is the quality lever, not WebP quality (quality 50→90 only cut colour error 2.96→1.84 of 255 while adding 500 KB); defaults are a 512px master and 384px output, raise `--size` before `--quality`. Hard prohibitions at every energy level: whole-object rotation and drifting. `verify` measures real motion inside the object and exits non-zero if the render is near-static (a known failure: 1 moving frame of 121) — trust it over the contact sheet. Needs `ffmpeg` on PATH and API keys in `.env`.
- **Reference / source:** samyost1/3dicon on GitHub (skills/3dicon/SKILL.md); backends named in the skill: GPT Image, Nano Banana, Seedance, Veo, Hailuo, Wan, Kling via OpenRouter/Replicate.
- **Best for:** Animated app icons, logo moments, small looping product/feature icons and mascot loops anywhere a transparent animated asset is wanted — including a trade homepage's service icons or a logo mark, provided the still is approved first. Not a section-layout skill.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0496⟧

## ⟦S0497⟧ shadcn-ui/migrate-radix-to-base — Part 13 — UI Skills — rest of the ui-skills.com catalog
- **What it is:** A precision migration playbook for moving React projects and shadcn wrappers from Radix UI primitives to Base UI (`@base-ui/react`), component by component or whole-project, keeping the project buildable at every step and reporting honestly. It is a code-transformation skill — the migrated UI is meant to look and behave like the original, with named behaviour deltas flagged rather than silently patched.
- **How it looks:** Visually unchanged by design — same components, same classes wherever possible. The one visitor-visible shift is in how overlays animate: Radix's keyframe utilities (`animate-in fade-in-0` on open, `animate-out fade-out-0` on close) are replaced by CSS transitions driven from `data-starting-style` / `data-ending-style` (e.g. `transition-[opacity,transform] data-starting-style:opacity-0 data-ending-style:opacity-0`). A few feels change and must be flagged: navigation-menu hover delay drops from 200 ms to 50 ms, tabs activate manually by default instead of on focus, menu checkbox/radio items no longer close the menu on click by default.
- **Frame by frame:** No new motion is designed; enter/exit animation is re-expressed, not re-choreographed. Radix pattern: element mounts with `data-[state=open]` → keyframe animate-in/fade/zoom/slide classes run → `data-[state=closed]` runs animate-out on unmount. Base UI pattern: popup mounts in its `data-starting-style` state (opacity 0, translated/scaled per side) → transitions to its natural styles → on close it takes `data-ending-style` and the primitive holds it mounted until the transition ends (`onOpenChangeComplete` fires) → unmount. Accordion/collapsible panels animate height through the renamed variables (`--accordion-panel-height`, `--collapsible-panel-height`) with `data-starting-style:h-0 data-ending-style:h-0` on the panel's inner div.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Strategy order: (1) golden pair via the shadcn CLI — classify each wrapper by diffing against its stock origin at `https://ui.shadcn.com/r/styles/<style>/<component>.json` (style name verbatim from components.json), replay customisations onto the base variant with a three-way `git merge-file user.tsx radix-golden.tsx base-golden.tsx`, then a mandatory `grep -n "radix-ui\|@radix-ui\|IconPlaceholder"` leftover sweep on every file (a clean merge is not proof of a clean file); legacy styles (new-york, new-york-v4, default) have no base counterpart — classification only, transform the user's own file, flag that future `shadcn add` still delivers radix. (2) Transformation engine from nine bundled reference files (universal-patterns, class-mapping, consumer-props, disclosure, display-misc, form-controls, menus, overlays, wrapper-shapes), all verified against `@base-ui/react@1.6.0` type definitions and a mechanical diff of 61 registry component pairs; when a mapping is not in the references, check `node_modules/@base-ui/react/**/*.d.ts` — never guess. Universal transforms: `asChild` → `render` prop (button.tsx goes to the real `@base-ui/react/button`, never a hand-rolled useRender wrapper); Radix `Portal > Content` → Base `Portal > Positioner > Popup` with side/sideOffset/align/alignOffset forwarded to the Positioner explicitly (`Pick<...Positioner.Props>` means destructure-and-forward, or props silently land on the Popup); `Overlay` → `Backdrop`, disclosure `Content` → `Panel`, tabs `Trigger` → `Tab`, slider `Range` → `Indicator` plus a new `Control` part, select `Viewport` → `List` and `position="popper"` → `alignItemWithTrigger={false}`; `forceMount` → `keepMounted`; dismiss callbacks (`onEscapeKeyDown`, `onPointerDownOutside`…) → `onOpenChange(open, eventDetails)` branching on `eventDetails.reason` + `eventDetails.cancel()`. Class layer: `data-[state=open]:` → `data-open:` (likewise closed/checked/unchecked/active), toggle `data-[state=on]:` → `data-pressed:`, submenu trigger → `data-popup-open:`; CSS vars `--radix-*-content-transform-origin` → `--transform-origin`, trigger width/height → `--anchor-width`/`--anchor-height`, available size → `--available-width`/`--available-height`; parts whose element changes from form control to `<span>` (checkbox/switch/radio roots) lose working `disabled:` variants — replace with `data-disabled:`, and some triggers need `aria-disabled:` instead. Hard rules: never touch cmdk (command), vaul (drawer), sonner, input-otp, react-day-picker (calendar) or recharts (chart); no-counterpart primitives get plain replacements (AspectRatio → CSS aspect-ratio div, Label → native `<label>`, VisuallyHidden → `sr-only`, Direction → Direction Provider `direction` prop). Modes: progressive (default — write `<component>-base.tsx`, repoint consumers one at a time with typechecks, commit per component, flip components.json style and remove radix deps only after the last wrapper) and whole-project (dependency order, leaves first). Reports: one `.migration/<component>.md` per component in a fixed Changed / Left alone / Behavior changes / Verify by hand structure, plus `.migration/project.md` for whole-project runs; migration status is derived by scanning the ui directory for remaining radix imports, never maintained by hand.
- **Reference / source:** shadcn-ui/ui on GitHub (skills/migrate-radix-to-base/SKILL.md + its nine reference files); sources cited inside: radix-ui.com primitive docs, base-ui.com component docs, the shadcn registry's 61 radix/base component pairs, `radix-ui@1.4.3` exports.
- **Best for:** One job only: Radix → Base UI migrations in React/shadcn codebases (overlays, menus, forms, navigation). No use for page design or for the single-file HTML trade builds.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0497⟧

## ⟦S0498⟧ shadcn-ui/shadcn — Part 13 — UI Skills — rest of the ui-skills.com catalog
- **What it is:** The operating manual for shadcn/ui projects: how to find, add, style, compose, update and debug components that are copied into the project as source via the CLI, how presets work, and how to turn a DESIGN.md brand spec into a themed shadcn app with a design-system showcase page. Companion to S0497 (which handles the Radix→Base migration inside such projects); this skill is the general one.
- **How it looks:** A coherent component-driven interface built from semantic tokens: surfaces in `bg-background` / `bg-card`, text in `text-foreground` / `text-muted-foreground`, one `bg-primary` for actions, full Card composition (Header/Title/Description/Content/Footer), forms laid out as FieldGroup + Field rows — never raw divs with space-y — status shown as Badge variants rather than coloured spans, chat screens built from MessageScroller / Message / Bubble primitives with streaming follow and a jump-to-latest button. Colours are OKLCH CSS variables (`--primary: oklch(0.205 0 0)` = lightness, chroma, hue) defined in `:root` and `.dark`, so the whole UI re-themes by changing variables.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. The skill prescribes no animation, duration or easing anywhere; loading is expressed with the `Skeleton` and `Spinner` components and button pending states are composed (Spinner + `data-icon` + `disabled`), but no timing values are given.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Always run CLI via the project's own runner (`npx shadcn@latest`, `pnpm dlx …`, `bunx --bun …`) and only with documented flags. Project truth comes from `npx shadcn@latest info --json` (fields: aliases, isRSC, tailwindVersion — v4 = `@theme inline`, v3 = tailwind.config.js — tailwindCssFile, style, base (radix|base — decides `asChild` vs `render`), iconLibrary, resolvedPaths, framework, packageManager, preset). Workflow: check installed components first → `search` registries before writing custom UI → `docs <component>` and fetch the URLs before touching a component → `add` (updates via `--dry-run` / `--diff <file>` smart merge, `--overwrite` only with explicit user approval) → read every added file and fix composition/import/icon-library mismatches → never guess a registry when the user didn't name one. Critical styling rules: className for layout not styling; `gap-*` never `space-x/y-*`; `size-*` for equal dimensions; `truncate` shorthand; no manual `dark:` colour overrides; `cn()` for conditional classes; no manual z-index on overlays; icons in buttons carry `data-icon="inline-start|inline-end"` with no sizing classes; option sets of 2–7 choices use ToggleGroup; items always inside their Group; Dialog/Sheet/Drawer always need a Title (sr-only if hidden); Avatar always needs AvatarFallback; callouts = Alert, empty states = Empty, separators = Separator, loading = Skeleton. Presets: named styles nova, vega, maia, lyra, mira, luma (+ rhea, sera in the design-system reference) and opaque version-prefixed base62 codes (e.g. `a2r6bw`, `b0`) — never decode a code by hand; use `preset decode/url/open/resolve` and `apply <code>` / `apply --only theme,font` / `init --preset <code>`; switching presets asks first: overwrite, partial, merge or skip. DESIGN.md route: scaffold (`init --preset/--base --template vite|next --no-monorepo`), `add --all`, map brand tokens onto the CSS variables in tailwindCssFile (hex stays hex), pin each radius step in `@theme inline` (example ladder: sm 4px, md 6px, lg 8px buttons/inputs, xl 12px cards/dialogs, 2xl 16px, 4xl 9999px pill), turn type tokens into `type-*` @utility classes with clamped display sizes and em tracking, change control heights together (the 32px `h-8` default lives across button/input/input-group/select/native-select/combobox/toggle/input-otp/tabs/menubar/command), restyle cva variants per recipe, then build the showcase page (foundations as contrast-checked colour pairs — flag anything under 4.5:1 — type specimens, pinned state matrices via `data-preview`, edge cases, do/don't pairs, recipes, one example screen) and verify in a browser (typecheck, no console errors, loads at scrollY 0, no horizontal overflow at 375px and 1280px). Also includes an MCP server (`shadcn mcp`, tools for registry search/view/install), registry authoring rules (source `registry.json` → `shadcn build` → `public/r`; address schemes: bare name = official, `@ns/item` = namespace, `owner/repo/item[#ref]` = public GitHub), and theming via `name`/`name-foreground` variable pairs in OKLCH with class-based `.dark` mode (next-themes in Next.js).
- **Reference / source:** shadcn-ui/ui on GitHub (skills/shadcn/SKILL.md + reference files cli.md, customization.md, design-system.md, design-system-page.md, mcp.md, registry.md and rules/*.md); ui.shadcn.com; the design-system-page reference distils Primer, Carbon, Atlassian, GitLab Pajamas, Cloudscape, Twilio Paste, Salesforce Lightning, Material 3, Evergreen, Orbit and EightShapes guidance.
- **Best for:** Building and maintaining React/shadcn apps and design systems — dashboards, settings pages, chat UI, component libraries, brand-to-theme conversions. The token/theming and showcase discipline is instructive, but it is a React+CLI workflow: no direct role in the single-file HTML trade homepages.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0498⟧

## ⟦S0500⟧ slidevjs/slidev — Part 13 — UI Skills — rest of the ui-skills.com catalog
- **What it is:** A skill for building web-based slide decks with Slidev (Vite + Vue + Markdown): developer presentations with syntax-highlighted code, click-stepped animations, diagrams, maths, a presenter mode with notes and timer, and export to PDF, PPTX or PNG, or hosting as a static SPA.
- **How it looks:** A full-screen browser deck. Slides are one Markdown file split by `---`; the first frontmatter block is the deck config (theme, title). Built-in layouts give the looks: `cover` (title slide), `center`, `default`, `two-cols` / `two-cols-header` (via `::right::` slots), `image` / `image-left` / `image-right`, `iframe` variants, `quote`, `section` dividers, `fact` / `statement`, `intro` / `end`. Code blocks show line numbers and highlighted lines; diagrams render from Mermaid or PlantUML code; maths from LaTeX; presenter notes live in HTML comments and show only in presenter view.
- **Frame by frame:** Advance (click / arrow key) → the next `v-click` / `v-clicks` element appears on the same slide, or the code highlight steps to the next click range (e.g. `{1|2-3|all}` highlights line 1, then lines 2–3, then all); `magic-move` code blocks morph-animate between code states instead of cutting. Rough-annotation markers (`v-mark.underline`, `v-mark.circle`) draw onto elements on their click step. Press `C` → drawing mode opens over the slide; press `G` → camera recording starts. Slide changes use the deck's transition; per-element direction styles like `forward:delay-300` stagger entrances. (Exact transition names/timings live in the skill's linked core-animations reference, not reproduced in the catalog text.)
- **Mechanism & key values:** Toolchain: `pnpm create slidev`, `pnpm run dev` (serves at http://localhost:3030), `pnpm run build`, `pnpm run export` — export requires `playwright-chromium` installed as a dev dependency or it fails with a browser error. Authoring values: code fences annotated `{2,3}` (highlight lines), `{lines:true}` or headmatter `lineNumbers: true` (numbers), `{maxHeight:'100px'}` (scrollable code), `{monaco}` (in-slide editor), `{monaco-run}` (runnable code), `<<< @/snippets/file.js` (import code), ` ```ts twoslash ` (type hovers). Per-slide frontmatter: `zoom: 0.8`, `layout:`, `src: ./other.md` (import slides); `<Transform :scale="0.5">` scales elements; `v-drag` makes elements draggable; `global-top.vue` / `global-bottom.vue` are layers on every slide; scoped `<style>` per slide. Presenter: `duration: 30min`, `timer: countdown`, `--remote` flag for remote control, `[click]` markers in notes sync note highlighting to clicks. API: `$nav` / `useNav()`, `onSlideEnter()` / `onSlideLeave()` hooks; an MCP server for AI agents at `http://localhost:<port>/__mcp`.
- **Reference / source:** github.com/slidevjs/slidev (official Slidev repo); documentation https://sli.dev, theme gallery and showcases linked from sli.dev. Its ~40 per-feature reference files (core-syntax, core-animations, code-*, layout-*, etc.) are linked by name; their contents are not reproduced in the catalog text.
- **Best for:** Decks and presentations only — conference talks, code walkthroughs, teaching material, or a client proposal/pitch deck. No homepage-section use: it builds slide decks, not site sections, and plays no part in a trades homepage build itself.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0500⟧

## ⟦S0501⟧ stephenturner/deslop — Part 13 — UI Skills — rest of the ui-skills.com catalog
- **What it is:** A prose-editing skill: strip predictable AI writing patterns out of any text (articles, blog posts, newsletters, memos, reports, scientific writing) so it reads as if a specific human wrote it. Triggered by requests to "deslop", "de-AI", "make it sound human", "remove AI patterns", and applied whenever prose is drafted or revised.
- **How it looks:** On the page: direct prose with named human actors doing things ("The team fixed it", never "The complaint becomes a fix"), specific claims instead of vague declaratives ("The implications are significant" is cut or named), varied sentence rhythm, two-item lists where a model would write three, and paragraphs that end in different ways. Absent: em dashes, bold-first bullets, unicode arrows, signposted conclusions ("In conclusion…"), throat-clearing openers ("Here's the thing:"), emphasis crutches ("Let that sink in.").
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. It governs text, not visuals.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Ten core rules: (1) cut filler phrases; (2) break formulaic structures — binary contrasts ("Not X. Y."), negative listings ("Not a X. Not a Y. A Z."), dramatic fragmentation ("Speed. That's it."), self-posed rhetorical questions ("The result? Devastating."), anaphora/tricolon abuse; (3) eliminate AI tropes — "delve" and cousins, "quietly" and other magic adverbs, the "serves as" dodge, false ranges ("from X to Y" where the range is meaningless), superficial participle analyses ("highlighting its importance"), invented concept labels, grandiose stakes inflation, patronizing analogies, false vulnerability; (4) active voice with human subjects ("we" in scientific prose, "you" in blog posts); (5) be specific — no vague attributions ("Experts argue…"; if you cannot name the expert, you do not have a source), no lazy extremes doing vague work; domain terminology is fine, business buzzwords ("leverage", "landscape", "ecosystem") and AI vocabulary tells are not; (6) match register — reader in the room for blogs, cited formality for science; (7) vary rhythm — two items beat three, no em dashes, no stacked punchy fragments, no listicles disguised as prose; (8) trust readers — no softening, hand-holding, pedagogical voice or fractal summaries; (9) watch formatting tells (bold-first bullets, unicode arrows, "Despite these challenges…" formulas); (10) do not dilute — one point per section, no metaphor beaten to death. Pre-delivery quick checks mirror the rules (adverb load, passives, inanimate subjects doing human verbs, three same-length sentences in a row, punchy-one-liner paragraph endings, tricolons…). Scoring when reviewing: Directness, Rhythm, Trust, Authenticity, Density, each 1–10; below 35/50, revise.
- **Reference / source:** github.com/stephenturner/skills (deslop). Its four reference files — phrases.md (filler/jargon catalog), structures.md (patterns and fixes), tropes.md (full trope catalog), examples.md (before/after transformations) — are linked; their contents are not reproduced in the catalog text. Same job family as this catalog's other anti-slop writing skills (stop-slop ⟦S0390⟧, anti-ai-slop-writing ⟦S0415⟧) but a different author and a different rule set — not the same skill.
- **Best for:** All copy on a trades homepage and around it — hero lines, proof/review framing, process text, CTA labels, plus emails and proposals — anywhere the words must not read as AI-generated. A text skill, not a layout or section-design skill.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0501⟧

## ⟦S0502⟧ Superfuture/design-review — Part 13 — UI Skills — rest of the ui-skills.com catalog
- **What it is:** A senior-level design critique skill: give it a URL, a screenshot/image, or a component/code file and it returns a sharp, prioritized review of the UI across ten dimensions — visual hierarchy, typography, spacing, colour & contrast, motion, component states, responsiveness, accessibility, content & copy, brand consistency — with findings ranked from blocking to polish, each carrying a specific fix. With `--apply` (or on request) it also makes the clear, safe code fixes itself.
- **How it looks:** No visual output of its own. The deliverable is a scannable markdown report: findings grouped by severity, most important first — 🔴 Blocking (broken, inaccessible, fails WCAG AA, unusable on a target device), 🟠 Important (hurts hierarchy, readability, usability, consistency), 🟡 Polish (craft refinement) — each finding stated as What (the specific issue, quoted element or `file:line`) / Why (one-line craft or usability reason) / Fix (a concrete change with an exact value, never "increase spacing"). It ends with "Strengths" (2–4 things done well) and, if useful, the single highest-leverage change to make first.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. It judges the motion of the artifact under review (see the rubric values below) rather than producing any.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Process: (0) on review start the skill sends one anonymous usage ping (event name only, no artifact or findings) to the vendor's metrics endpoint; (1) acquire the artifact — a screenshot is best for visual judgement, a code file enables `file:line` findings and `--apply`; a URL is fetched as text, not a render, so for visual judgement it asks the user for a screenshot plus viewport; with neither screenshot nor code it asks before guessing; (2) evaluate against the bundled checklist.md rubric, checking actual numbers over impressions; (3) report ranked as above; (4) `--apply` edits only clear, safe findings (contrast, spacing values, focus states, reduced-motion, semantic tags, alt text) and re-verifies values after editing; subjective/restructuring changes stay recommendations unless confirmed. Rubric numbers from checklist.md: type scale ≈5–7 steps, each step ≥ ~1.2 ratio from the next; line-height 1.0–1.2 for display, ~1.4–1.6 for body; measure ~45–75 characters; ≤2 typefaces; spacing on a consistent 4/8px-step scale, no arbitrary 13px/27px gaps; WCAG AA contrast — body text ≥ 4.5:1, large text (≥24px / 19px bold) and UI/icons ≥ 3:1 (AAA 7:1 if claimed); never colour alone to convey meaning; motion purposeful, UI transitions ~150–250ms, larger/entrance ~300–500ms, ease-out for enters and ease-in for exits, linear only for continuous motion, `prefers-reduced-motion` honoured with a reduced/instant variant, no layout shift or interaction-blocking animation; every interactive element has hover, focus-visible, active and disabled states plus designed loading/empty/error states; visible focus ring; tap targets ≥ 44×44px (iOS) / 48dp (Android); semantic HTML with headings in order, labelled form inputs, errors announced and linked, full keyboard operability; no horizontal scroll or clipping across 320–1440+px; CTA labels describe the action ("Start free trial", not "Submit"); design tokens reused — consistent radii, shadow elevation, icon style. Pro mode (license-gated, key at ~/.design-review/license): the artifact and notes are sent to a remote report service which returns the review with extra mobile/SwiftUI and brand-token sections; a 402 response falls back to the free review; Pro findings are never fabricated locally.
- **Reference / source:** github.com/Superfuture/design-review; its checklist.md rubric is bundled and reproduced in full in the catalog text. Pro review sold at crit.officialjp.com (named in the skill).
- **Best for:** The QA/critique pass on any section or whole page before shipping — a hero gets motion/type scrutiny, a form gets states/accessibility scrutiny. Directly trade-fit as the audit step for trades homepages: it is a judgement skill, not a design source, so it pairs with (never replaces) a bank reference.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0502⟧

## ⟦S0503⟧ sveltejs/svelte-code-writer — Part 13 — UI Skills — rest of the ui-skills.com catalog
- **What it is:** A tooling skill for Svelte 5 development: documentation lookup and code analysis through the official `@sveltejs/mcp` command-line tools. The skill states it MUST be used whenever creating, editing or analysing any Svelte component (`.svelte`) or Svelte module (`.svelte.ts` / `.svelte.js`), and works best executed inside a `svelte-file-editor` subagent.
- **How it looks:** No visual output — it shapes code. What a reviewer sees is Svelte code written against the current Svelte 5 documentation and passed through the autofixer before it is finalized, instead of syntax recalled from memory.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. A command-line workflow, not a page behaviour.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Three `npx` commands: `npx @sveltejs/mcp list-sections` (lists all Svelte 5 and SvelteKit documentation sections with titles and paths); `npx @sveltejs/mcp get-documentation "<section1>,<section2>,..."` (full docs for the named sections, e.g. `"$state,$derived,$effect"`); `npx @sveltejs/mcp svelte-autofixer "<code_or_path>" [options]` (analyses inline code or a file and suggests fixes). Autofixer options: `--async` (async Svelte mode, default false) and `--svelte-version` (target version — ideally the full version from package.json, e.g. `5.16.0`, so version-specific suggestions apply; the major must be 4 or 5, default 5). Terminal rule: escape `$` as `\$` when passing code containing runes (`$state`, `$derived`, …) so the shell doesn't substitute them. Workflow: uncertain about syntax → list-sections, then get-documentation; reviewing/debugging → run the autofixer; always run the autofixer before finalizing any Svelte component.
- **Reference / source:** github.com/sveltejs/ai-tools (the official Svelte organisation's AI-tools repo, svelte-code-writer skill).
- **Best for:** No homepage-section use in single-file HTML trades builds. Relevant only if a project is built in Svelte/SvelteKit; included for completeness of the catalog.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0503⟧

## ⟦S0504⟧ Teddarific/anatomy-asset — Part 13 — UI Skills — rest of the ui-skills.com catalog
- **What it is:** A skill for drawing crafted, highly detailed isometric SVG illustrations as page assets — a hero object, a set of spot illustrations, a feature-tile scene, a banner, an OG card, a deck-slide visual — where the picture is a real, well-made physical object built from many small, precise, solid parts, and the object itself carries the product's message (a synth for a music app, a bank-vault door for "never loses data", a letter-sorting cabinet for an inbox tool). It is a fork of the same author's Anatomy skill: the drawing discipline (solids, four-tone shading, true painter's order, every line ending on something) is unchanged, but the job flips from explaining a mechanism to looking right on a page — carrying the brand, holding a composition, leaving room for the headline. Craft rules are fixed; subject, mood, colour and composition are the user's calls, and user style requests override Anatomy prohibitions (two accents, a word on a sign, a floating part) with the same craft applied. Ships a standalone `.svg` (works as `<img>`, inline, or in design tools) plus a preview page; WebGL shader layers and a 3D "turning parts" mode exist as escalations. Thirteen examples ship with the fork and eight Anatomy examples are kept as craft references.
- **How it looks:** A calm, expensive-looking isometric drawing of one dense real object — the reference example is a compact synthesiser as a 1200 × 640 landing-page hero: art in the right 56% of the canvas, empty headline space on the left, about 95 solid parts and ~880 paths, two knobs in the brand colour, black keys in a dark neutral ramp, one knob cap lifted off its shaft as the single "moment" the eye lands on. Everything is mostly monochrome grey grounded in the exact page colour, with one accent family on the subject; parts are filled solids shaded in four tones with lighter tops, thin lines (0.5–1px by canvas size) that all end on a face, another line or a dot, screws as small ringed dots, knurls, seams, label plates, a soft halo under the base. Other shipped looks: an oak writing desk with brass and leather material ramps (~157 solids), a red espresso machine with a jointed-arm robot barista in a 640 × 480 tile (~113 solids), three matching 320 × 320 spots (stopwatch, safe-deposit box, battery lantern, each under 70 KB), a 1600 × 560 bottling-line banner at azimuth 62° (~190 solids), and two full brand sets (dark electric-aviation, light clean-energy) each carrying one brand across hero, banner, tile and spots. Detail is the point: at 1× it reads as one striking object; at 4× every region still has something true to find.
- **Frame by frame:** Every asset moves, CSS only, so the motion runs even inside an `<img>`: → the signature motion is the object working — a rotor/propeller/fan spins in its own plane (`amRotor`: blades with thickness, a soft blur disc that doesn't turn, ghost blades trailing; `amSpin` for flat in-plane turning), a conveyor or belt slides one pitch at constant speed and jumps back (`amLoop`), a gauge needle or pendulum sways about its pivot (`amSwing`), keys/buttons press and release then rest (`amPress`, staggerable across a row), ink or a signal draws itself along a line, holds and fades (`amDraw`) → plus one or two small echoes out of phase with it: a part floats above its socket while its halo stays on the floor (`amFloat`), a fader or drawer slides and returns (`amSlide`), a glow breathes (`amPulse`), LEDs blink with staggered delays (`amBlink`), a flipbook swaps drawn poses for motion that isn't flat (`amFlip`) → end state: the loop continues calmly; two or three moving things at most, nothing changes painter's order. Under `prefers-reduced-motion` every motion stops and holds the rest pose — which must be designed as the hero frame. Speeds: slow motions run 2.5–8s periods; propellers/fans spin 0.45–0.8s per turn with `amRotor`, a wind turbine 5–7s with no blur. Interactive motion (pointer, scroll, keyboard) is added only when the user asks, following the bundled motion reference: time-based loop with dt clamped to 1/30s, parts ease toward targets (exponential follow τ = 0.1–0.3s, or real springs sub-stepped ~240/s, snap under 5e-4 error), an idle tour starts after ~1.4s idle and resumes ~3.6s after the last interaction, hover previews and press commits, the loop stops offscreen and when settled. The optional 3D mode re-projects and re-shades turning/hinging/free part groups every frame and re-solves painter's order from separating planes. Pass `motion: false` to `assetSvg` for a still drop.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Built with a Node kit (`kit/iso-kit.mjs` camera/solids/parts, `kit/asset.mjs` asset layer, `kit/lathe.mjs` round parts, `kit/tube.mjs` pipes/cables, `kit/audit.mjs`, plus `kit/gl.mjs` and `kit/turn*.mjs` for WebGL/3D). Sizing first, before any geometry: Spot = one small object, 25–50 parts, square (build without asking); Asset = one hero object, 50–120 parts with composition and optional ambient motion (build without asking); Scene = diorama, matching set, or anything with WebGL/3D, 120+ parts (give an estimate, propose an Asset version, build the Scene only when the user chooses it); a working preview page within the first hour. Workflow: brief → 3–5 one-line concepts (literal / metaphor / scene) with a pick and reason → parts list grouped base/structure/mechanism/controls/subject (≥25 Spot, ≥50 Asset) → compose with `fitInto(points, region, { pad, azimuth })` → build geometry once (`slabOf`, `cylinder`, `extrude`, `planOutline`, `topTicks`, `knurl`, `coil`, `radialTicks`) → paint back to front, bottom to top, sorted by `depthOf`, wrapping parts split → colour via tokens → ambient motion → ship via `assetSvg` / `previewHtml` → verify like a critic. Canvases (viewBox ≈ 1 unit per CSS px at shown size): hero art-right 1200 × 640 (art region x500 y36 w668 h568; safe zone x0 y0 w470 h640), hero art-centre 1200 × 720 (art y200 h500; safe zone top 180), art-only 800 × 600 (pad 24), feature tile 640 × 480 (pad 32), spot 320 × 320 (pad 20), wide banner 1600 × 400, social/OG 1200 × 630 (art right 55%), deck slide 1920 × 1080 (art right 60%). Composition: the object fills 80–90% of its region's width (45–60% of a hero canvas), the moment sits about a third in from the region's edges, ≥24 units of air to any edge it doesn't bleed off, halos count as art and never enter the safe zone (the preview console-errors if art enters it; open with `?safe` to see the zone). Camera: azimuth 45° shows two faces equally, 55–65° shows the long front (the synth uses 60°), 25–35° the short end; elevation 30° default, 40–50° to look into trays/dioramas, never below 25°; one camera and one world scale (±10%) per set. Line weight: 0.8–1 at 1200px+ wide, 0.6–0.7 at 600–900px, 0.5 at 160–320px spots. Craft numbers: bevels 0.4–1.6, grooves inset 3–5 from an edge, screw dots 0.4–0.55 with a ring; tone hierarchy base/feet `lo`, structure `mid`, subject `hi`, exactly one `lit` part; shade steps about 3% apart in luminance; halo about 30% strength in light theme. Pipes: bend radius about 2.6 × pipe radius, centreline clearance about 1.5 radii from anything but its own connection; sizes kept few and distinct — main ducts r 5–8, feed lines r 2–4, sense lines r 0.9–1.5, cables r 0.5–0.65. Colour: `paper` must equal the exact page colour; `groundTokens(paper)` shifts the whole neutral ramp by the paper difference (full lightness shift, colour by `tint` 0.6 default; OKLab lightness above 0.6 = light theme); accents via `assetSvg({ accents: { brand: "#ff5a1f" } })` and `<g class="ac-brand">` — `body` mode colours the whole part as its own ramp, `ink` mode colours only lines/dots/lit edge; one accent family by default (the synth has 3 accent parts in ~95), accent lightness clamped to 0.3–0.86 in light theme and 0.72 × clamped 0.14–0.6 in dark; materials are named accent ramps too (ebony `#3a3a3f` light / `#08080a` dark, brass `#b08d57`, copper/walnut low-chroma warm hexes). Export: standalone SVG with CSS inlined and scoped to its id, `role="img"` + one-sentence aria-label, art in `<g data-art="">`; PNG at 2× via `capture.mjs --scale 2`; ship both themes as separate files swapped by `<picture>`/`prefers-color-scheme` when the site has both; size budget — hero under ~400 KB raw (synth ~240 KB), spot under ~80 KB; cut cost with fewer facet steps on small cylinders (16–20) and fewer grid dots. Verification (all mandatory): `xmllint --noout` silent (an invalid SVG renders blank in `<img>`); `capture.mjs` at each shipped theme and at 390px wide, console clean; `lines.mjs` must print `line ends: 0` (every open line end within 1 viewBox px of another stroke/dot/outline or under a later fill); with pipes/cables/round parts `node build.mjs --audit` must end `audit passed` (clearance, terminals, loose ends, screen folds — a route turning over 140° on screen while under 110° in 3D fails — support, depth order, mid-flight pass-throughs, stand-in shapes whose recorded shape covers under 60% of the drawing); 4× close-ups of every junction and accent part in each theme; motion shots at several `--times` and one `--reduced`; the finished PNG is judged side-by-side against the synth example. WebGL (only for what lines can't draw — fire, water, lamp light, glow, steam; never solids or decoration): layered stack back-SVG → canvas → front-SVG in one stage sharing the camera contract (`GLSL_ISO`: project/onFloor/onWall/rayOf identical to the kit's `iso()`), world-space effects only, every term windowed to zero before any bound or canvas edge (outer rows/columns read alpha 0), tonemap never clamp, output dither ±1 LSB, DPR capped at 1.5, draw only while active and visible. Light theme is the shipping theme and is designed for paper: a glow is a saturated body + pale near-white core + coloured rim, ink solved from the colour the paper should show (`inkFor()` inverts normal compositing over white), hot bodies run dull red → orange → yellow → near-white with no salmon stage (forge steel stops: 560°C (.45,.09,.05) → 680 → 780 → 950 → 1150 → 1260°C (1,.93,.78)), the finished ink is faded once (never per-term), cavities get darker token sets as the physical ground (e.g. paper `#4a453f`), no halos in empty air, and an SVG fallback shows the same inks and hands over to the shader without a dip (fallback opacity `(1 − u)/(1 − u·α)`). 3D turning-groups mode (beta, proved on the turning-dial example and one test desk fan): group kinds turn/slide/hinge/free with world-at-rest authoring; binding rules — convex parts only, contacts flush/tangent/rim-on-flat (balls get flats for rims), joint links ≥0.2 apart bridged by a coaxial knuckle disc, no live line spans two moving groups, live tube bends need R ≥ 8r on a flat plane (take 10r; 11r at 5° tilt, 14r at 8°, 17r at 10°, 21r at 12°, 30r at 15°, 66r at 20° — past ~15° turn inside a fitting instead), tube tangents stay out of 15°–45° elevation; materials (gold, chrome, steel, gunmetal, rubber, brass, copper) remap the tone ramp per part; part costs in prism units (fixed 0.5, prism 1, round 2.5–4, tube chunk 2–3, ball with flats 8–10, lathe ~25) with budgets — small figure (weight ≤ 50): ≤2ms Node CPU/frame, ≤6ms browser task at 1440, ≤16ms at 390px with 4× throttle; dense (≤230): ≤7ms / ≤13ms / ≤33ms; `data.turn` JSON ≤250 KB; the orbit audit is slow (28-part fan: ~85s `--quick`, ~17 min full; only a full run ending `turn audit passed` counts).
- **Reference / source:** github.com/Teddarific/skills (anatomy-asset), a fork of the same author's Anatomy skill (the explainer sibling — for interactive figures that explain a technical concept with a live readout, the skill itself says to use Anatomy instead). Bundled reference files reproduced in the catalog text: 3d.md, brand.md, composition.md, concepts.md, craft.md, export.md, motion.md, react.md, verify.md, webgl.md; kit.md and walkthrough.md are referenced by name. Shipped examples named: synth-hero, writing-desk, espresso-tile, feature-spots, bottling-line, aero-* and energy-* brand sets, plus Anatomy's dial-indicator, test-rig, desk-computer, arcade-cabinet, raptor-engine, spot-plate, ripple-tank, turning-dial for craft.
- **Best for:** Hero objects, spot illustrations, feature tiles, wide banners, OG/social cards and deck slides — a crafted physical-object visual in place of stock photography, abstract floating shapes, or a screenshot in a frame. Trade fit: strong where a trades homepage needs one memorable object visual (the trade's machine, tool or unit drawn as a beautiful real thing, e.g. a boiler, a window unit, a nail gun on a workbench) in the firm's brand colour on its page colour, with headline space composed in. Cost note: this is slow, high-craft work — parts are counted in dozens to hundreds, verification is multi-pass (audits, line checks, 4× close-ups in both themes), and the WebGL/3D escalations move it into "Scene" scope that needs an estimate and an explicit go-ahead.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0504⟧
# Chunk: skills S0505–S0510 — the tjcages/linear pack (one pack, six skills)

**Duplicate finding (read first):** S0505–S0510 are not six independent skills. They are the six members of ONE pack — `tjcages/linear` (github.com/tjcages/linear) — six small role files (discipline / finish-install / methodology / monitor / setup / sync) that all sit on top of the SAME bundled reference set. Hash-verified against the full text in WEB-SKILLS.md: ALWAYS_ON.md, AUTH.md, AUTOMATION.md, EXAMPLES.md, METHODOLOGY.md and RESPONSE.md are byte-identical in every skill that ships them. S0505, S0507, S0508, S0509 and S0510 each bundle all six files (~68–69 KB each); S0506 bundles only four (ALWAYS_ON, AUTH, AUTOMATION, RESPONSE — 9 KB, no EXAMPLES/METHODOLOGY). Per the duplicate rule, the shared bundle is indexed in full once, under S0505; the other five entries give their own unique role in full and point back here for the bundle. None of the six is a design skill: they produce no page, no layout and no animation — they govern how an AI agent runs project tracking in Linear. "How it looks" below therefore describes what the user actually sees (Linear board state and chat replies), honestly, rather than inventing visuals.

## ⟦S0505⟧ tjcages/linear-discipline — Part 13 — UI Skills — rest of the ui-skills.com catalog (tjcages/linear pack)
- **What it is:** The always-on member of the tjcages/linear pack: in every agent session it makes Linear the default source of truth for project work — enforcing a repo's Linear tracking protocol if one exists, and offering setup exactly once if none does. This entry also carries the pack's full shared reference bundle (detailed here once; S0506–S0510 point back to it).
- **How it looks:** Nothing on a web page. What a visitor/user sees is a Linear board that stays current — issues moving Backlog → In Progress → Done with short comments — plus chat replies in the pack's fixed format (next action first, numbered steps, lists capped at 5, no preamble). On an untracked repo the only visible extra is a single one-line question: "This repo isn't tracked in Linear. Set it up now? (~10–20 min)". A skipped repo shows nothing at all (a `.linear-tracking-skip` file at repo root silences it).
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. (State changes happen in Linear and in chat text, not in pixels or animation.)
- **Mechanism & key values:** Detection: a repo is "tracked" if CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md or .cursor/rules/* contains a "Linear tracking" section naming team + project; "skipped" if `.linear-tracking-skip` exists. Tracked protocol: (1) search before create, (2) non-trivial work gets filed/updated in the named project + milestone, (3) Backlog → In Progress at start → Done only when shipped, (4) close the loop (state and/or comment) before session end, (5) prefer Linear's generated branch names. Soft nudge fires once only, never from Automation/monitor runs, never auto-creates anything; "No" writes the skip file. Step 0 before ANY Linear call: probe auth with a cheap tool (`list_teams` or `get_user`); on failure stop and give per-harness OAuth steps (Cursor Settings → MCP, Claude Code `/mcp`, Codex MCP settings) — never invent GraphQL/curl/API wrappers. SHARED BUNDLE (identical in S0505/S0507/S0508/S0509/S0510; S0506 ships the first three + RESPONSE only): ALWAYS_ON.md — the ~10-line always-loaded block stating the protocol above. AUTH.md — the Step 0 probe + per-harness steps above. AUTOMATION.md — optional Cursor weekly health digest: schedule Monday 7:00 AM in the user's LOCAL timezone; Cursor cron is UTC, so convert (America/Denver `0 14 * * 1` winter / `0 13 * * 1` summer; New York `0 12`/`0 11`; Los Angeles `0 15`/`0 14`; UTC `0 7 * * 1`); write policy read + comment only, status updates only on real health changes. EXAMPLES.md — six before/after transformations tied to methodology sections, plus a full worked example (fictional "widget-cli": 40 issues, 9 orphans, 11 milestones → audit 8/20 FAIL → fixes → re-score 17/20 PASS). METHODOLOGY.md v1.0.2, §0–§26 — the pack's core document: thesis = anchor all tracking structure to a North Star doc so milestones/issues derive from something true (§0); §1a already-tracked gate (enumerate first, summary before plan, explicit per-category yes/no before any write, adapt to existing structure by default); §1b six anchoring questions when no North Star exists (question 5 — the user's own goal for tracking — shapes the whole scheme); §2 four project types (Product / Tool / Drop / Marketing) predicting label and track structure; §3 milestones = roadmap phases 1:1, up to three separate tracks (engineering / launch readiness / rollout), target dates only with a real date signal, Milestones not Cycles (API can't create Cycles); §4 issue rules — granularity asked explicitly (feature-level default), 8-step backfill algorithm (Done only with evidence; cross-check that Done + backlog reconstructs the roadmap; scan docs/ for unmirrored tracks; a doc's "done" claim is evidence, not proof — corroborate), ticket style hard rules (titles plain words ≤8 words; descriptions ≤3 sentences or ≤5 bullets; comments ≤3 lines; no marketing voice), every issue gets a milestone, 3–5 area labels, project module labels namespaced in a label group (`isGroup` + `parent`), real `blockedBy`/`blocks` dependencies; §5 lifecycle Backlog → In Progress → Done-only-when-shipped (merged, checks pass, verified running if visible), and bootstrap isn't done until the protocol is written into the repo's always-loaded agent instructions; §6 drift audits at phase closes; §7 launch-readiness track (assets, infrastructure, exit plan) triggered by the launch goal, not project size; §8 campaigns as dated milestone-per-beat with creative attached; §9 status updates only at milestone/health moments, dates must survive an estimate + dependency sanity check; §10 image attachments fully automatable (`prepare_attachment_upload` → PUT raw bytes to signed URL → `create_attachment_from_upload`; signed URL expires in 60 seconds — one file at a time, exact byte size needed upfront; validated on a real 317 KB PNG, issue OFF-79); §11 manual-only list (Cycles, Project Labels, Initiatives, custom project icons, GitHub integration, the OAuth grant itself) vs everything else automatable via MCP; §12 Initiatives as cross-project rollup (attach by name, sequencing still lives in relations); §13 one team for many projects, decide Project Labels once per workspace; §17 six project shapes decision tree; §18 readiness rubric — 10 dimensions scored 0/1/2, PASS = ≥16/20 with no dimension at 0 (dimensions 1–6 load-bearing), 12–15 = SOFT, <12 = not set up; §19 eight anti-patterns (fake-precision dates, milestone spam, status theater, issue soup, duplicated roadmap layers, backlog hoarding, orphan issues, perpetual in-progress); §20 update triggers (milestone closes, health changes onTrack↔atRisk↔offTrack, approaching dates not trending Done); §21 maintenance modes (bugs-only / slow-burn / parked / revived / archive); §22 rescue playbooks (messy / half-tracked / backfill-late); §23 milestones 3–6 per track, named for outcomes not activities ("Phase 2 — Accounts & login", not "Work on auth"), description ≤3 sentences; §24 five issue categories as a lens, milestone answers "when", label answers "what part of the code"; §25 compatibility matrix (solo / team / library); §26 seven-step self-audit procedure with a fixed report template. RESPONSE.md — chat format rules (see S0506, which is built around it): lead with the next action, number multi-step tasks, end with ONE concrete next action doable in under two minutes, restate state every turn, concrete time estimates, cap lists at 5, no preamble/recap/closers ("Great question", "Hope this helps" are forbidden).
