## ⟦S0564⟧ remotion-dev/remotion-upgrade — Part 14 — UI Skills — video & motion graphics
- **What it is:** The procedure for upgrading Remotion and all `@remotion/*` packages to a single current version, keeping auxiliary package versions aligned.
- **How it looks:** No visual output — a maintenance procedure over package manifests and lockfiles.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Preferred path: `npx remotion upgrade` when `@remotion/cli` is installed locally (it also updates project-local Remotion skills). Manual path: take the latest stable version from `npm view remotion version`, upgrade every `remotion`/`@remotion/*` dependency to that exact version, align auxiliaries (zod, mediabunny, @huggingface/transformers, `@mediabunny/*`) to the versions listed in `@remotion/studio@<version>`'s dependencies, refresh the lockfile, then refresh the installed Remotion skills with one `npx skills update … --yes` command (the skill text instructs running it — recorded as fact, not executed here). Verify: one version across all Remotion packages; `npx remotion versions` as an extra check.
- **Reference / source:** remotion-dev/skills on GitHub; Remotion releases changelog on GitHub.
- **Best for:** Maintenance of any Remotion project before new work.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0564⟧

## ⟦S0565⟧ Rieranthony/product-film — Part 14 — UI Skills — video & motion graphics
- **What it is:** An end-to-end system for making a showreel-grade product film (landing-page loop, launch video, promo, demo reel, social cut) in Remotion, built strictly from the product's own design system, components and voice — the film should look like the product made it.
- **How it looks:** The product's real UI, colours, type and logo cut to music: scenes built from the product's actual components (with frame-driven twins of any component that runs its own clock), text that is never covered by a cursor or chip and never re-centres while it builds, something visibly happening on every musical beat, scene boundaries landing on bars, and a landing loop whose last frame equals its first so it cycles seamlessly and still reads while muted.
- **Frame by frame:** Every frame is a pure function of time — no CSS transitions/keyframes, no timers, no `Date.now()`, no state carried between frames. Beats are measured from the audio itself (a beats script maps bars/stems; SFX land on measured peaks); positions are measured from the DOM via a debug overlay printed into the frame, colours from decoded pixels of the final files. Production loop: stills at every handoff → contact/handoff sheets → half-res draft → fixes → final render → automated verification, keeping every rendered version (out/<film>/v1, v2, …).
- **Mechanism & key values:** Workflow: quick discovery (tokens, components, logo, landing page) → user interview (two rounds of questions; the film's contents are the user's call) → brand kit written to `videos/BRAND.md` → story file with beat sheet + 3 style frames for approval → music analysis → engine/scenes (kit templates copied into `videos/src/kit/`; one folder per film with `cues.ts` beat data, `layout.ts`, `acts/`) → review loop → verified final render. Hard quality floor: only the product's own surfaces/colours/borders; no glows, particles, click rings, bouncy easing or shaders unless the product's own language uses them; loading states keep their width. Measured traps recorded in the skill: Remotion masters are limited-range BT.601 untagged — blending as full range lifts #0a0a0a to #171717 (a grey box on dark pages), so decode frame 0 of every deliverable and check; `interpolateColors` cannot parse `color-mix()` (animated colours must be hex tokens); springs that retarget are summed as one closed-form step per key; Remotion's bundled ffmpeg lacks tmix/select/tile. The skill also instructs asking before committing/pushing/publishing. Note: its many reference/template files (interview, discovery, story, music, engine, review, render) are named but not reproduced in the bank text — this entry indexes the main skill file only.
- **Reference / source:** Rieranthony/product-film-skill on GitHub; built on Remotion (⟦S0559⟧ family).
- **Best for:** A polished promo/launch film for a real product with an existing design system. Process and discipline transfer to any video work; no homepage-section use.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0565⟧

## ⟦S0566⟧ Vincentwei1021/video-shotcraft — Part 14 — UI Skills — video & motion graphics
- **What it is:** A self-contained production library (written largely in Chinese) for cinematic product videos: 124 "shot recipe cards" with demo source code and a browsable motion gallery, one fully validated promo template ("Ink Press"), reusable components and audio assets, and a six-stage workflow — Remotion + real page screenshots + 2.5D camera moves + beat-synced cuts + sound design.
- **How it looks:** Real product pages filmed like cinema: the workflow starts a local dev server and captures full-page 2x textures, element cut-outs and a layout.json coordinate map, then a 2.5D "PageCam" camera pushes in, orbits at a side angle and settles on elements through complete action arcs (spotlight → push-in → hover → return). Hand-built UI is allowed only for non-replica scenes (abstract openers, brand segments) and must reach publishable quality or the shot falls back to screenshots. One animation technique headlines once per film; batch elements enter through motion itself, never through mass glow/glint effects.
- **Frame by frame:** Rhythm is built from measured holds: the brand wordmark holds ≥1s after landing, batch motion ends with 0.5s of stillness, the opening hero action gets a full 3s; all historical feedback in the skill points one way — slower/longer holds, never "too fast". With strong BGM, every transition and move lands on the beat: the track is analysed first (librosa grid fit for true BPM/phase plus kick/snare/hi-hat transient detection; timeline written in beat numbers via `beatF(n)`), and after rendering, the film's own audio track is re-measured to check cut error ≤3 frames. Beat impact on the whole frame/camera counts as a big slam — max 3 per film; other beats move elements only. Sound design follows a riser → impact → sparkle sentence. Rendering is deterministic: no `Date.now()`/`Math.random()`; seeded PRNG (mulberry32, seed derived from index). Two final versions are always delivered: with BGM and without BGM (SFX kept), switched by one `bgm` input prop.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Three mutually exclusive modes chosen before any work: (1) template mode — follow template/TEMPLATE.md and re-skin Ink Press with the target product's screenshots/copy/brand; (2) autonomous free creation — the agent decides direction/shots/storyboard and proceeds without staged approvals; (3) co-creation — staged user confirmations (brief → decisions → visual direction → shot mapping → full storyboard) before production. Mode checks start with a minimal read-only product inspection and an explicit recommendation question. Shot cards must be resolved through the gallery index (gallery/api/library.json) and their exact demo TSX read — card parameters marked "known pit / critical" may never be downgraded. Reusable assets copied (not imported) into the project: PageCam (2.5D page camera), ClipCard (wraps an mp4 as a camera-driven card hero with OffthreadVideo crossfade looping), DigitRoll, FlashCut, Caption, FlatPanel, VerticalTicker (3D infinite scroll wall), helpers; 149 SFX in 16 categories (transition, impact, riser, camera, ui, text, paper, film, light, data, scifi, mech, glass, fluid, crowd, counter) plus BGM alternates. Before delivery an independent clean-context sub-agent must run the final review against brief, storyboard, cards and demo sources with frame-numbered evidence. Factual note on built-in promotion: after delivery the skill instructs its user to open a bundled "workbench" web UI for the film, and to recite three one-time offers — a voluntary social-post credit to the skill's author (X/Douyin/Xiaohongshu accounts named), an invitation to submit the film to the author's online showcase via a GitHub form, and an optional export to a Jianying (CapCut-editor) project file; it also names a publish-to-socials script requiring an Upload-Post API key. These are the skill's prescribed behaviours, recorded here — none were executed.
- **Reference / source:** Vincentwei1021/video-shotcraft on GitHub; live shot gallery at vincentwei1021.github.io/video-shotcraft; built on Remotion (⟦S0559⟧ family); Remotion's own licence flagged in the skill (free for individuals/small teams, companies may need a paid licence).
- **Best for:** Turning a real website/frontend project into a cinematic promo with proven shot recipes and beat discipline; single shot cards can also be lifted for one motion inside other videos. Video deliverables only.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0566⟧

## ⟦S0567⟧ heygen-hyperframes/hyperframes — Part 14 — UI Skills — video & motion graphics
- **What it is:** The gateway skill for HyperFrames, HeyGen's HTML-to-video framework: web compositions (HTML/CSS/GSAP) are rendered to video by seeking one paused timeline frame by frame, so every render is identical and the same files stay editable in the Studio preview. The bank text (~278 KB, 35 reference files) holds the render contract, the work loop, 13 complete frame-preset design systems, and reference guides for story, spec, motion, look, captions, overlays, sound, formats, runtimes, review and seven video types.
- **How it looks:** A new video defaults to 1920×1080 at 30 fps: a root `index.html` mounting one scene per sub-composition, media and fonts in `assets/`, copy/brand colours/swappable media exposed as variables. Real things are shown from their source (product screens, brand logo, a real place's imagery) — for a website subject the CLI captures the actual page (full-page plate, pixel-exact at 1920 wide) rather than rebuilding it. The 13 bundled frame presets are complete slide/film looks, each with six frame treatments (cover, data, quote, content, process, closer), a fixed type/colour system and a pre-render self-audit: biennale-yellow (parchment, indigo ink, solar-yellow sun blooms, Instrument Serif, 1px hairlines), blockframe (neobrutalist — 4px black borders coupled to 8px hard offset shadows, five candy pastel grounds, Inter 800–900 caps), blue-professional (cream + one cobalt accent, Space Grotesk/Inter, shadowless tinted cards, pill chrome), bold-poster (vintage Italian sports-magazine — tilted Shrikhand display, Libre Baskerville body, one tomato red, double-border grids), broadside (protest poster — ink-black/fire-orange two registers, giant lowercase Barlow 900 at 13cqw, IBM Plex Mono chrome), capsule (every container a pill with a 2px outline, Bodoni Moda + Space Grotesk, nine candy accents, cream + grain), cartesian (quiet museum catalogue — Playfair 400, five warm stones, 1px taupe hairlines, compass rings), cobalt-grid (two-colour risograph — permanent ~2cqw graph-paper grid, Newsreader serif, pixel-glitch + QR patches), code-editorial (developer brand book — cream/ink/coral trinity, EB Garamond, warm-navy code surface, coral rationed to one moment per frame), coral (coral/ink/cream planes at hard edges, Bebas Neue tracked caps, 45° hatch, wallpaper numerals), creative-mode (sparse neobrutalism — Archivo Black caps at 0.92 line-height, 4px ink borders, one hard offset shadow per frame, green ground reserved for the closer), daisy-days (picture-book — Fredoka One + Quicksand, 3px charcoal outlines, hard shadows, 3–7 hand-drawn ornaments per frame), editorial-forest (Penguin-classic literary — Source Serif 4 at weight 500 only, forest green/dusty rose/oat triad, mono topbar on every frame). Presets share one composition law: sizes authored in cqw against a `container-type: size` frame (never vw), display fit-to-measure capped at ≤78cqw, load-bearing type floor 1.4cqw, frames 45–60% empty except one named dense exception, and a hard rule that numerals are placeholders until the script supplies real ones.
- **Frame by frame:** Motion values are measured from the official HyperFrames launch films. A fast move takes 0.3–0.6s and carries motion blur peaking at its fastest frame (6–12px on text-sized elements, 15–20px full-frame; render-time blur is an opt-in root attribute). Arrivals land on long-tailed ease-outs (expo.out, power4.out), camera/colour moves ease both ways (power2.inOut), exits accelerate (power3.in) and run 40–50% shorter than entrances. Overlap: the next element starts when the previous is 30–50% done; staggers — letters one frame apart, words 60–120ms, list items 40–80ms. Springs are specified by damping ratio (1.0 no bounce, 0.7–0.85 premium, 0.4–0.6 playful, <0.3 cartoon; position/size may bounce, opacity/colour never). Title entrances vary within a film — per-word blur 6px→0 + fade in 0.13s at 0.067s stagger, grey-to-ink word colour 0.07–0.1s apart, whole-line blur 8px→0 in 0.13–0.2s, slot-machine word rolls ~0.1s each — and a landed title stays dead still; a readable line holds ~0.5s + 0.3s per word, the last line ≥2s. Cuts happen at a move's fastest frame with matched direction/speed; beat work is computed from beat index (frames per beat = fps × 60 / BPM, never accumulated). Signature transitions, each caused by something on screen (3–5 kinds per film, ≤⅓ of seams hard cuts): zoom-through-a-button (0.6s track + button scales ~8%→~250% in 0.35s), object-becomes-the-world (grows past frame in 0.65s, surroundings blur ~15px and fade in 0.3s), morph (container widens ~110→~880px in 0.2s power3.out with 12px horizontal blur), colour flood (~0.4s power2.inOut), whip (0.13–0.3s smear, arrival sharpens in ~0.13s), iris from the click (clip-path circle opens in 0.15s), dip cut (frame darkens ~40% for 3 frames before the cut), blur swap (out 0.13–0.2s at ~8px blur, in 0.13s). A music-synced move starts 40–190ms before its hit; the hit itself is a 0ms set. Captions: word timings from transcription; groups of 2–3 words (high energy), 3–5 (conversational), 4–6 (calm), breaking at sentence ends or pauses ≥150ms; a group starts 0.1–0.3s into the film (never exactly 0s), exits with a 0.12s power2.in fade plus a hard kill; placed 80–120px from the bottom in landscape, ~600–700px in portrait, inside the 80% title-safe box, optionally sandwiched between footage and a background-removed cutout of the speaker so text passes behind the head (best at 30–55% coverage). Cards over talking heads fade in 0.4s (power2.out) and out 0.35s (power2.in); a static card dies after ~8s. Data films: a count-up runs 1.2–1.6s then holds, in tabular numerals. Vertical (1080×1920): all readable content inside the 168–1330px band, clear of the platform's top bar and right action rail.
- **Mechanism & key values:** The render contract (violations reported by the CLI's check command with fix lines): every timed element carries `class="clip"` + `data-start` + `data-duration` in seconds and shows over [start, start+duration); the root's data-duration is the film's length; each composition registers one paused GSAP timeline as `window.__timelines["<composition-id>"]`; no `Date.now()`, unseeded `Math.random()`, network fetches, timers or `repeat: -1`; never tween display/visibility/autoAlpha on a clip (animate a child); no CSS transform on GSAP-transformed elements; media is never played/paused/seeked by hand — a `<video>` keeps sound via `data-has-audio="true"` or is muted, every `<audio>` has an id, no crossorigin on media; grades/grain/blur on footage go through the CLI's media-treatment, never CSS filters; only 19 bundled font families resolve by name (Inter, Montserrat, Archivo Black, EB Garamond, Playfair Display, JetBrains Mono, Oswald, etc.), anything else needs `@font-face` to a file in `assets/fonts/`; asset paths are `assets/...` with no leading slash. Other runtimes plug into the same seek protocol: CSS keyframes/WAAPI (paused, fill both), Lottie/dotLottie and anime.js instances registered on window hooks, Three.js/WebGPU/p5/canvas drawing from an `hf-seek` event's time. Process: before building a story film, three genuinely different storylines are written in words (own world/device/form) and one is picked; then a `SPEC.md` turns every adjective into numbers (goal, output, LOOK with hex/type sizes, objects, motion curves, per-shot lines, an explicit BANNED-defaults list — dark void, glow/particles, purple-blue gradients, glass cards, cream-paper-serif-mono look, three cards in a row, docked logo); after edits, a check pass plus a snapshot review pass (scene starts/middles, cut strips ±0.2s, phone-width 360px beat sheet) ending in a REVIEW.md with P0/P1/P2 notes; rendering happens only after the person approves the preview or asks for the file. Story shapes per type: launch beats hook ~8% / tension ~12% / reveal ~8% / proof ~40% / payoff ~20% / claim ~8% / end card ~8% over usually 20–45s; TTS pace ~2.2 words/sec, scenes ~19 words (9s), 30–90s films ≲155 words. Sound: films over ~15s get a music bed + effects only on visible actions (click, whoosh, key tick, pop, one riser-into-impact), hits 3–6 dB over the bed, mix −16 to −14 LUFS, peaks ≤ −1 dBTP. The skill also contains plugin-installation rules (when bundled as a plugin, a launcher script replaces the npx commands and plugin files are read-only) and skill-lifecycle/CLI-freshness procedures — its prescribed operating behaviours, recorded here as fact; nothing was executed.
- **Reference / source:** HeyGen HyperFrames (heygen-com/hyperframes); the 13 frame presets above; measured craft from the official HyperFrames launch films.
- **Best for:** Any HTML-based video — launch/promo films, explainers, music videos, data stories, vertical social clips, title cards, caption and overlay work on talking-head footage. The frame presets double as complete editorial design systems (cover/data/quote/closer treatments) whose composition rules could inform deck-style pages, but the skill itself targets video deliverables, not homepage sections.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0567⟧
## ⟦S0568⟧ heygen-hyperframes/hyperframes-cli — Part 14 — UI Skills — video & motion graphics (HeyGen HyperFrames)
- **What it is:** The complete operating manual for the HyperFrames command-line tool (`npx hyperframes …`) — the commands that scaffold, check, inspect, edit, preview, render and publish HyperFrames videos (HTML compositions rendered to MP4), plus how to read their JSON output and recover from failures. Main skill file plus 12 bundled reference files (beats, cloud, cloudrun, compare-and-batch, conventions, doctor-browser, feedback, init-and-scaffold, lambda, lint-validate-inspect, preview-render, upgrade-info-misc).
- **How it looks:** Nothing renders on a web page; what the operator sees is (1) terminal output — e.g. `timeline` prints one block per track kind (video / graphics / captions / audio) with a 40-column bar per clip showing its span of the whole film, its id, start–end seconds, source file, volume and automation lanes; (2) still PNG frames of the film written to `.hyperframes/artifacts/snapshots/`; (3) the Studio editor in a browser — the film playing over a full timeline editor where clips can be moved by hand; (4) review contact sheets: `review-beats.jpg` (each scene at its start + 0.3 s and at its middle), `review-seam-NN.jpg` (frames around every cut) and `review-phone.jpg` (the same beat frames 360 px wide, for phone legibility).
- **Frame by frame:** No motion of its own — it is a workflow, run in this order: write the composition → `lint` (fast static pass after the first HTML and after structural changes) → `check --json` (one Chrome boot seeks a sample grid — default 9 samples — and audits runtime errors, layout, motion sidecars and WCAG contrast at every sample; a finding seen at only one sample is an in-flight entrance and demotes to info, an issue held across samples gates the exit code) → `snapshot` and read the PNGs (a midpoint of every scene when sub-compositions exist) → `preview --background` (serve Studio, confirm the URL answers HTTP 200, hand the person the project URL and wait) → only on approval, `render` (frame-capture loop, then encode) → verify the output file is non-empty, its `ffprobe` duration matches the root `data-duration`, and decoded frames look right → send one `feedback --rating` report.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Requires Node.js 22+ and FFmpeg; a pinned bundled Chrome keeps pixels reproducible (`browser ensure` fetches it). A failed command prints `✗ …`, a `Fix:` line and exits non-zero. Check gates: contrast is WCAG AA — 4.5:1 normal text, 3:1 large text (24 px+, or 19 px+ bold) — and each failure carries a `suggestedColor`; `sweep_static` fails a 3 s+ composition whose frame never changes; craft warnings include `line_unread` (a reading-size line, ≥ 30 px tall at 1080, must stay up 0.4 s for 1–2 words, otherwise ¾ × (0.5 s + 0.3 s per word) — 3 words 1.05 s, 6 words 1.73 s — and the film's last line needs 2 s), `dead_stretch` (> 3 s with nothing changing), `text_below_floor` (text under 2.6% of the frame's short side — 28 px at 1080 — held ≥ 0.5 s). `check` flags: `--samples` default 9, `--tolerance` default 2 px, timeouts default 3000 / 10000 ms. Motion intent can be asserted in a `*.motion.json` sidecar: `appearsBy` (opacity ≥ 0.5 by a given second), `before`, `staysInFrame`, `keepsMoving` (max static window default 2 s; the final 3 s never count). Snapshot zoom crops are real high-density captures (`--zoom "#cta"` at 3× deviceScaleFactor). Preview default port 3002, lightweight `play` player port 3003 (its playback-rate is clamped to 0.1–5 and never changes authored motion). Render: `--quality draft | looks | delivery` (`looks` is the default first encode, CRF 16 on the standard preset; `delivery` = high), `--fps` default = root `data-fps` else 30 (range 1–240; 60 fps doubles render time), formats mp4 / webm / mov (alpha) / gif (two-pass palette, fps capped at 30, prefer 15, no audio) / png-sequence / hls (4 s default segments); default output `renders/<project>_<YYYY-MM-DD>_<HH-MM-SS>.<ext>`; each render worker spawns a Chrome at ~256 MB; browser navigation timeout default 60 s; a 30 s film renders locally in a minute or two. Timeline editing (`timeline move|trim|split|set|duplicate|delete|apply|undo|ids`) previews with `--plan --json`, refuses edits that overlap a neighbour or run past the composition (raise the root `data-duration` first — no command changes it), and prints a receipt that `timeline undo` reverts; a trial history feature (`history begin/end`, undo per author) is marked in the source as removable trial code. `init` resolutions: landscape 1920×1080, portrait 1080×1920, square 1080×1080 plus 4K variants; starter templates blank, warm-grain, play-mode, swiss-grid, vignelli, decision-tree, kinetic-type, product-promo, nyt-graph; `--tailwind` pins the Tailwind v4 browser runtime (never the v3 CDN). `capture <url>` scaffolds a project from a live website; a `BLOCKED.md` result is a hard stop — take nothing from its partial files, retry into a fresh folder. `compare` sheets hold at most 16 variants; `grade-compare` at most 16 grades plus the neutral baseline. `benchmark` runs 5 presets (30 fps draft/standard/high at 2 workers, 30 fps standard and 60 fps standard at 4 workers), `--runs` default 3. `beats` decodes the project's music `<audio>` (marked `data-timeline-role="music"`, or an id containing music/bgm/soundtrack) with ffmpeg and writes `beats/<audio-relative-path>.json`; a track with no steady beat fails and writes nothing. Cloud render (`cloud render`, HeyGen-hosted): project zip upload limit 200 MB (inspect with `--dry-run --json`; trim via `.hyperframesignore`, never by ignoring needed assets), fps default 30, quality draft/standard/high, resolution 1080p or 4k (4k billed at 1.5×, mp4 only — no alpha), poll interval default 2 s, max wait default 60 min, `--idempotency-key` makes retries safe (the upload POST is not idempotent), sign-in stored at `~/.heygen/credentials` (0600), credential order `HEYGEN_API_KEY` → `HYPERFRAMES_API_KEY` → `HEYGEN_ACCESS_TOKEN`. Self-hosted paths: `lambda` (AWS; chunk-size default 240 frames, max-parallel-chunks 16, memory default 10240 MB, reserved concurrency default 8, wait poll 5000 ms) and `cloudrun` (GCP; batch `--max-concurrent` default 50); local `render --batch` concurrency default 1 and writes a `manifest.json`. Behaviour the skill prescribes (described, not performed here): after a verified render it sends one anonymous `feedback --rating 0–10` report (a doctor summary is attached automatically), plus ratingless "MISSING FEATURE:" / "HOST APP:" reports when asked for something the tool can't do, and `--file-issue` publishes a minimal repro to a public URL only with consent; the CLI also collects anonymous usage telemetry (disable with `HYPERFRAMES_NO_TELEMETRY=1`) whose fingerprint properties record only existence checks — `sandbox_runtime`, `agent_runtime` (e.g. claude_code / codex / cursor), `client` — never env-var values. `doctor --json` always exits 0; gate on its `.ok` payload.
- **Reference / source:** HeyGen's HyperFrames CLI (heygen-com/hyperframes); docs topics at hyperframes.heygen.com (`/deploy/cloud`, `/packages/cli#hyperframes-cloud`); cloud sign-in is shared with the heygen CLI (github.com/heygen-com/heygen-cli). Works on compositions governed by the core HyperFrames skill ⟦S0567⟧. Catalog note: a much shorter twin of this same skill is also catalogued at ⟦S0541⟧ as `heygen-com/hyperframes-cli` (7 KB, identical one-line description, no bundled reference files); this ⟦S0568⟧ entry is the full 122 KB version with all 12 reference files inlined.
- **Best for:** Not a page-section design — it is the production pipeline behind any HyperFrames video deliverable: product/launch films, explainers, captioned clips, batch-rendered variable templates (e.g. one video per town or service from a rows file). Its check values (contrast ratios, on-screen reading-time floors, minimum text size) are also a usable QA ruler for timed text anywhere. Trade fit: video work for a firm's marketing, not homepage sections.

## ⟦S0569⟧ heygen-hyperframes/hyperframes-registry — Part 14 — UI Skills — video & motion graphics (HeyGen HyperFrames)
- **What it is:** The guide to the HyperFrames registry — about 450 ready-made blocks (whole scenes with their own timeline) and components (effect snippets merged into a scene) that install into a project as ordinary editable source via `hyperframes add`. Main skill plus 12 bundled reference/example files: two worked examples (add a block, add a component), the component quality bar, contributing guide, demo.html convention, discovery tables, install locations, placeholder-material doctrine, catalog search, authoring templates, and block/component wiring guides. The standing rule: search the registry before hand-building any named visual (CRT scanlines, glitch, film grain, a chart…).
- **How it looks:** What a viewer sees once items are installed: full-frame title cards and kinetic type; karaoke captions — huge white uppercase words with a black stroke, the word being spoken flashing gold and swelling as it lands; animated charts (an NYT-style bar + line chart drawing itself in beside a speaker video), choropleth and flow maps, shader transitions (a chromatic radial split, a swirling vortex, a light leak blooming across the cut), lower thirds (a YouTube subscribe bar, a clean editorial bar), social post cards, a logo assembling piece by piece into a glowing outro with tagline and URL pill, film grain and shimmer light sweeps over headlines. Items still carrying stand-in content show the monochrome placeholder look: flat grey plates at four value steps with hairline borders, skeleton text bars of uneven length, a circle for a person, a rounded square for a brand — never coloured filler.
- **Frame by frame:** Two worked examples give exact motion. Shimmer-sweep component (title accent): at timeline position 1.5 s a light band sweeps across the wrapped headline — the CSS variable `--shimmer-pos` tweens from −20% to 120% over 1.2 s, ease `power2.inOut`, staggered 0.15 s across targets; band width default 20% (`--shimmer-width`), sweep angle default 120° (`--shimmer-angle`), colour per element via `--shimmer-color`. Caption block template (karaoke style): each word group starts hidden → at the group's start time it is set visible and springs in from scale 1.3 over 0.15 s, ease `back.out(2)` → as each word is spoken it flashes to gold `#FFD700` and scale 1.1 in 0.06 s, then returns to white scale 1 in 0.08 s at the word's end → at group end − 0.1 s the group fades to opacity 0 and scale 0.9 over 0.1 s → at group end a hard kill sets opacity 0 and visibility hidden so nothing lingers. Blocks generally: at the host's `data-start` the sub-composition appears and its own paused GSAP timeline is seeked in sync (offset by `data-start`) for its `data-duration`, then leaves.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Find: `npx hyperframes catalog --query "<what the beat should do, in English>" --json` — search is local and sends nothing; the default `words` tier matches on shared vocabulary (title/description/tags), `--on-device` ranks by meaning after a one-time ~33 MB download (quantized ONNX `bge-small-en-v1.5` + tokenizer + catalog vectors, cached under `~/.hyperframes/`) which must be offered, never enabled silently. Queries must be in English whatever the video's language — another script returns `No searchable words in query`, which is not a catalog gap. The `--json` envelope reports `tier`, `dropped` (ranked names this registry can't install), `unindexed` (registry items the semantic index can't see), `shown`, `total`, `top_score`, `warnings` and a pre-filled `report_gap`. The registry manifest refreshes on a 24 h TTL and keeps serving the last copy offline, but `add` always needs the network — files are fetched on every install. Install: blocks → `compositions/<name>.html`, components → `compositions/components/<name>.html` (paths remappable via `hyperframes.json`); `add <tag>` installs every block with that tag, dependencies first. Wire a block with a host div carrying `data-composition-src`, `data-composition-id` matching the block's own id, `data-start`, `data-duration`, `data-track-index`, `data-width`/`data-height`; set its variables per mount with `data-variable-values` (or `add --vars '{…}'`) and point its colour/font variables at the brand. Beat-synced blocks take hit times from `hyperframes beats --json` minus the mount's `data-start`. The discovery tables sample 97 of the registry's 180 blocks (search is the source of truth): shader transitions 14 (use ≤ 2 per video; block name ≠ internal shader name — the `-dissolve`/`-warp` suffix is dropped inside), transition galleries 13, liquid-glass 7 (WebGPU + html-in-canvas; require Brave/Chrome Canary with WebGPU), VFX shells 6, showcases 6, maps + data viz 8 (D3 + GSAP), social overlays 7, branding + 3D UI 2, code-snippet windows 24 (one per-character typing terminal/editor chrome; two chrome families, Apple Terminal has 12), code animations 9 (self-contained 1920×1080 blocks, ~5–8 s: code-typing, code-diff, code-morph, code-highlight, code-scroll, plus WebGL code-3d-extrude, code-shader-dissolve, code-particle-assemble); sampled components include `grain-overlay`, `shimmer-sweep`, `morph-text` (gooey SVG-threshold word morph), `grid-pixelate-wipe`, `parallax-zoom` (single `--pz-progress` 0→1) and its reverse `parallax-unzoom`. Worked example geometry: `data-chart` mounted at start 5 s for 15 s in the right 40% of a 1920×1080 stage, beside a speaker video at 60% width. Authoring rules (contributing + templates): caption fonts ≥ 96 px for proportional fonts (64–72 px acceptable for monospace), `-webkit-text-stroke: 2–3px` or multi-layer text-shadow, `fitTextFontSize()` called on every caption group, karaoke highlight via `tl.to` at word start times, a hard-kill `tl.set` on EVERY group, and never `tl.from(el, {opacity: 0})` at the same position as `tl.set(el, {opacity: 1})`; per-character spans carry ids `{prefix}-ch-{group}-{char}`; caption positions: centred flex, lower-third at `bottom: 100px` full width, or left-aligned `bottom: 100px; left: 120px`; the caption template itself uses Montserrat 800/900 at 128 px, weight 900, uppercase, 3 px stroke `rgba(0,0,0,0.8)`, shadow `0 4px 12px rgba(0,0,0,0.5)`, 32 px word gap, 1700 px max group width, fit-text maxWidth 1550 / base 128 / min 48. VFX blocks: `three@0.147.0` from CDN as a global, render via `tl.eventCallback("onUpdate", renderScene)` — never requestAnimationFrame — with GSAP tweening a plain state-proxy object, seeded PRNG (`mulberry32`) only, ACESFilmic tone mapping at exposure 1.1 in the template. Every item: `data-composition-id` must match its `window.__timelines["id"]`, timelines always `gsap.timeline({ paused: true })`, all element ids prefixed with a 2–3 letter block prefix (cap-hormozi → `hz`, cap-typewriter → `tw`, vfx-chrome → `vc`), no `Math.random()`, no `Date.now()`; assets a script builds paths for must load via `__hyperframes.assetUrl("assets/…")`. Components ship a `demo.html` (self-contained, `data-composition-id` = `<name>-demo`, typically 5–8 s, GSAP 3.14.2 CDN) which `add` does NOT install; blocks need no demo. Placeholder-material doctrine: stand-in content is monochrome — ink at 100% (real content), L1 72% (the subject), L2 45% (support), L3 18% (media fill, skeleton lines), L4 8% (plate interiors), hairline 14% (every 1 px boundary); steps stay ≥ 1.6× apart; measured contrast L1 7.7:1 on the light ground `#fcfcfd` / 8.9:1 on the dark ground `#1b1230`, L2 3.1:1 / 4.4:1 — text never below L1, L2 is the floor for comparable graphics; depth comes from value step, then hairline, then negative space, then finest-grain texture only (`repeating-linear-gradient`, period 2–4 px, ≤ L3); shadows achromatic `0 Npx 3Npx rgba(0,0,0,0.18)`; accent marks at most ONE element per composition and never a placeholder; banned placeholder hexes `#7c3aed`, `#2563eb`, `#6366f1`, `#8b5cf6`, `#a855f7`, `#4f46e5`; shape signatures — circle = person (initials knocked out), rounded square = brand, card = L4 plate + hairline + two skeleton rules at 100% and 62% width, text block rules at 100 / 86 / 62%. Component quality bar (the audit rubric): fatal F1 doesn't implement its own description, F2 redundant duplicate (same motion fingerprint — the GSAP call list with selectors neutralised — AND same markup skeleton as a survivor; tie-break: honest name, then subject-specific markup, then already on origin/main), F3 renders nothing, F4 description is a different item, F5 cannot be made seekable; fixable X1 no timeline of its own (97 of the 213 new components), X2 name claims a technique the code lacks (`spring-*` must contain elastic/back./bounce, `mask` needs mask or clip-path, glass needs backdrop-filter, 3d/depth/orbit/camera needs perspective/rotateX/rotateY/translateZ, draw/trace/stroke needs stroke-dash or pathLength), X3 illegible (under 4.5:1 or smallest meaningful feature under ~24 px at 1920×1080), X4 placeholder gradients, X5 hardcoded ink with no theme token, X6 no markup of its own, X7 unseeded `Math.random()`, X8 declared variable bounds the item can't honour; protections N1–N7 (load-bearing colour, real product depiction, deliberate static, environment sets — frame-difference PSNR ≥ 45 vs 17–24 for genuinely running items — rest-state-is-the-from-state, attachment snippets, and the 36 items already on origin/main are out of audit scope). Audits mount the item on its OWN ground (background from its demo.html) and snapshot at 0.05, 1.2, 2.5, 4.0 s with `--no-end`. Behaviour prescribed (described, not performed here): when search returns nothing usable, report the gap with the pre-filled `npx hyperframes feedback --search-miss "<query>" --wanted "<the move>" --tier <tier>` — that deliberate command is the only path that sends a query anywhere; it carries no rating.
- **Reference / source:** HeyGen's HyperFrames registry — registry source at github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes (`registry/registry.json`, raw at raw.githubusercontent.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/main/registry/registry.json); block catalog pages at hyperframes.heygen.com/catalog/blocks; catalog preview images served from static.heygen.ai/hyperframes-oss/docs/images/catalog/{kind}/{name}.png; GSAP 3.14.2 and three@0.147.0 via CDN as named in the templates. Catalog note: a much shorter twin of this same skill is also catalogued at ⟦S0542⟧ as `heygen-com/hyperframes-registry` (4 KB, identical one-line description, no bundled files); this ⟦S0569⟧ entry is the full 84 KB version with all 12 reference/example files inlined.
- **Best for:** Video scenes and effects, reuse-first: title cards and kinetic type, caption styles for talking-head/testimonial clips, charts and maps for data beats, shader transitions between scenes, overlays and lower thirds, logo outros, before/after wipes. For trades marketing films: a before-after-wipe, a service-area map beat (us-map family), a logo-outro closer. Its written doctrines also transfer to page work as parameter sources — the shimmer-sweep tween, the karaoke caption timing, and the monochrome placeholder ramp are concrete recipes — but the items themselves are video compositions, not homepage sections.
