## ⟦S0570⟧ heygen-hyperframes/remotion-to-hyperframes — Part 14 — UI Skills — video & motion graphics (HeyGen HyperFrames)
- **What it is:** The importer that brings existing video work into HyperFrames — Remotion first, also Motion Canvas, Lottie, Three.js, p5.js, canvas or plain HTML/CSS animation, plus rendered output from Manim, After Effects or Blender — and verifies the result frame by frame against the original. Main skill plus 11 bundled references: the Remotion→HyperFrames API map, escape hatch, eval harness, fonts, limitations, Lottie, media, parameters, sequencing, timing and transitions.
- **How it looks:** The end state is the same film the original tool produced — same scenes, same timing, same colours — except it is now plain HTML in HyperFrames Studio where every element can be selected and edited. The verification surface is a side-by-side frame strip PNG (original frame next to translated frame at 6–10 timestamps) and an SSIM summary (mean / min / p05 / p95 against a threshold); a good port is visually indistinguishable from the Remotion render, with any lossy spots written down in a `TRANSLATION_NOTES.md` beside the output.
- **Frame by frame:** The port runs: (1) lint the source with `scripts/lint_source.py` — any blocker (React state driving animation, async metadata, a React UI kit) stops translation outright and routes to the runtime-interop pattern instead; (2) translate scene by scene — each Remotion `Sequence` becomes one sub-composition host on the root timeline, frames converted to seconds (`frame / fps`), props becoming composition variables; (3) render both sides; (4) compare — `snapshot --at <t,…> --against <original.mp4>` lays the original's frame beside the translation's at every scene midpoint and on both sides of every cut, hunting for one late or recoloured element; `render_diff.sh` scores SSIM per frame; (5) any frame cluster that diverges is diagnosed from the strip (bad frames mid-scene = animation problem, at boundaries = sequencing problem) and re-translated. The motion itself is preserved by mapping: a Remotion spring entrance becomes a GSAP `back.out` pop with matched overshoot, a linear `interpolate` becomes an `ease: "none"` tween of identical duration, a count-up becomes a counter object tweened with the same easing curve.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Three import levels — **Native** (code that can become HTML + GSAP: most Remotion, HTML/CSS/GSAP, simple Motion Canvas; afterwards every element is Studio-editable and variables/catalog/presets apply), **Hosted** (code that can draw any requested frame in a browser — canvas, p5.js, Three.js, Lottie, WebGL: the code stays, HyperFrames owns the clock via its seek protocol and built-in adapters for Lottie, Three.js, anime.js, WAAPI and CSS animations; only timing, position and exposed parameters are editable; no requestAnimationFrame or timer as the time source, seeded randomness only), **Media** (anything that outputs video/frames — Manim, After Effects, Blender, PIL, moviepy — used as a clip; editable only as cut/place/layer). Code depending on wall-clock time, live physics or the network can only come in as media. Blockers (refuse + interop): `useState`, `useReducer`, `useEffect`/`useLayoutEffect` with non-empty deps, async `calculateMetadata`, imports from MUI, Chakra, Mantine, antd, shadcn, Radix, NextUI. The interop fallback bundles the Remotion code with React + `@remotion/player` via esbuild, mounts a paused `<Player>` inside the composition and registers `window.__hfRemotion` with `seekTo(frame)` / `pause()` / `durationInFrames` / `fps` so HyperFrames drives it frame by frame. Warnings (drop and note): `@remotion/lambda` / `@remotion/cloudrun` config (HyperFrames renders single-machine), `delayRender`, `useMemo` / `useCallback` wrappers, pure custom hooks (inline the body), `staticFile`, `interpolateColors`. Translation contract: one sub-composition per scene; asset paths root-relative; Remotion's render-page rule `* { box-sizing: border-box; }` pasted once into the root `index.html` — without it every bordered/padded element grows (the worked example: a 200×100 box with 20 px padding and 10 px border renders 260×160). Props: scalar `defaultProps` → `data-*` attributes on `#stage` (kebab-case; read via `dataset`, convert numbers with `Number()`); nested arrays materialize as repeated markup with per-instance `data-*` and CSS custom properties — never JSON in an attribute; scene-level values pass via `data-variable-values` on the host and `window.__hyperframes.getVariables()`; Zod schemas are validated at translation time only. Sequencing: `Sequence from={F} durationInFrames={D}` → host div with `data-composition-src`, `data-start = F/fps`, `data-duration = D/fps`, `data-track-index` per layer (background 0, overlays 1, audio 2); nested Sequences sum their offsets (frames [60+30, +60] = 90–150 → start 3 s, duration 2 s at 30 fps); `Series` → siblings with accumulating starts; inside a scene file, time is local (starts at 0) and asset paths are `../assets/…`; `Loop` → a bounded GSAP repeat whose count is derived from the available duration (`repeat: -1` only when the root declares a finite `data-duration`; stateful loop children bow out); `Freeze` → drop the wrapper (don't tween the element). Scene crossfades are driven from the ROOT timeline (a scene's own timeline sees only its own file): e.g. 0.5 s crossfade = `tl.to(scene1, {opacity: 0, duration: 0.5}, 1.5)` + `tl.to(scene2, {opacity: 1, duration: 0.5}, 1.5)`. Timing map: linear `interpolate(frame, [a,b], [x,y])` → `gsap.fromTo(…, {duration: (b−a)/fps, ease: "none"})` at offset `a/fps` (GSAP holds end values, matching Remotion's `clamp`; `extend` must be pre-extended manually); multi-segment interpolate → one tween per segment; `Easing.bezier(a,b,c,d)` → `CustomEase.create("c", "M0,0 C${a},${b} ${c},${d} 1,1")`; `Easing.poly(N)` → `power<N−1>` for integer N = 1–5 (power1 quad, power2 cubic, power3 quart, power4 quint), other exponents via a function; `Easing.elastic(b)` → `elastic.out(b, 0.3)`; Remotion's back ease default s = 1.70158 is passed explicitly. Spring → `back.out`: {damping 12, stiffness 100, mass 1} → `back.out(1.4)` over ~0.7 s (validated T2/T3); {damping 14, stiffness 90} → `back.out(1.2)` ~0.7 s (T3); {damping 8, stiffness 200} → `back.out(2.0)` or `elastic.out(1, 0.5)` ~0.6 s (not validated, budget ~0.05 SSIM); `overshootClamping: true` → `power3.out` ~0.6 s; rule of thumb overshoot ≈ (stiffness / damping²) × 1.4. Count-ups: tween a `{v: 0}` object and write `textContent` on update — `power2.out` is exactly 1−(1−t)³ (midpoint 0.875; `power3.out` gives 0.9375 and is wrong for a cubic source). Stagger props convert as frames/fps (12 frames = 0.4 s at 30 fps; the validated T3 cards land at 0 / 0.4 / 0.8 s). Transitions: `TransitionSeries` scenes overlap by the transition duration (a 15-frame transition at 30 fps: scene B starts at frame 60−15 → 1.5 s); `fade()` → manual opacity crossfade; `slide()` → incoming translateX 100%→0 with outgoing 0→−100%; `wipe()` → clip-path `inset(0 100% 0 0)` → `inset(0 0 0 0)`; `clockWipe()` / `iris()` → the `sdf-iris` shader-transition block (`hyperframes add sdf-iris`); `flip()` → rotateY 180° split across scenes; `linearTiming` → `ease: "none"`, `springTiming` → `back.out` per the spring table; custom presentations translate only if they are pure functions of progress. Media: `staticFile("x.png")` → `assets/x.png` at root, `../assets/x.png` inside scene files (copy the file across); `<Video>` gets `data-has-audio="true"` ONLY when ffprobe shows an audio stream and the source isn't muted/volume 0 — otherwise `muted` (a silent clip flagged with audio aborts the render with `ASSET_MEDIA_TYPE_MISMATCH`); `playsinline` always; `<OffthreadVideo>` → plain `<video>`; `<IFrame>` → `<iframe>` (renderer falls back to screenshot mode); function-valued `volume` → a `data-automation` volume lane or an ffmpeg `afade` bake (flag it — SSIM can't hear it); `startFrom`/`endAt` frames → `data-trim-start`/`data-trim-end` seconds; Buffer/dataURL assets are materialized to files, or embedded as data URLs only under 100 KB. Lottie: `@remotion/lottie` → lottie-web 5.12.2 (cdnjs bodymovin) with `autoplay: false`, animation JSON copied into `assets/`, the instance pushed onto `window.__hfLottie`; the adapter seeks via `goToAndStop` passing time × 1000 ms; dotLottie uses the `@lottiefiles/dotlottie-web` 0.81.0 ESM build + WASM copied locally with `setWasmUrl`; multiple animations all push onto the same array and seek in sync. Fonts: `@remotion/google-fonts` → a Google Fonts `<link>` (the compiler inlines the CSS; enumerate every weight the CSS actually uses); local `Font.loadFont` → an `@font-face` rule with the file copied into `assets/`; system-font fallback divergence between the two Chromiums costs ~0.025 mean SSIM (weight-800 strokes render heavier in HF) — use Inter to minimise drift. Verification numbers: SSIM pass = mean ≥ threshold (`R2HF_SSIM_THRESHOLD` default 0.85); validated tiers T1 single-element fade mean 0.974 vs threshold 0.95, T2 multi-scene + spring + audio + image 0.985 vs 0.95, T3 data-driven count-up 0.953 vs 0.90; set a threshold ~0.02 below the measured p05 (real regressions drop the mean 0.05+; run-to-run drift is ~0.01); encoder parity is mandatory — render the Remotion side with `Config.setVideoImageFormat("png")` and `Config.setColorSpace("bt709")`, because Remotion's default full-range `yuvj420p` vs HF's limited `yuv420p` alone costs ~0.05 SSIM; the font noise floor is ~0.025 mean SSIM. Never translated by design: HDR from Remotion, variable frame rate, multi-`<Composition>` lists (port one at a time), and the Remotion Studio props panel.
- **Reference / source:** HeyGen HyperFrames (github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes) — runtime interop pattern from PR #214, the Lottie adapter in `packages/core/src/runtime/adapters/lottie.ts`, and the docs guide `hyperframes-vs-remotion.mdx`; shader transitions from the HyperFrames catalog (hyperframes.heygen.com/catalog/blocks); Lottie format limits per airbnb/lottie after-effects.md; dotLottie-web 0.81.0 files via unpkg as named in the source. Works into compositions governed by the core skill ⟦S0567⟧ and uses the CLI of ⟦S0568⟧. Catalog note: a much shorter twin of this same skill is also catalogued at ⟦S0547⟧ as `heygen-com/remotion-to-hyperframes` (5 KB, identical one-line description, no bundled files); this ⟦S0570⟧ entry is the full 73 KB version with all 11 reference files inlined.
- **Best for:** Migration and reuse, not new design: porting an existing Remotion promo/explainer into an editable HyperFrames project, hosting Lottie/Three.js/canvas pieces inside a HyperFrames film, or cutting rendered Manim/AE/Blender output in as clips. Its SSIM frame-comparison method is also the verification discipline for any ported video asset. No homepage-section use.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0570⟧

## ⟦S0571⟧ heygen-hyperframes/slideshow — Part 14 — UI Skills — video & motion graphics (HeyGen HyperFrames)
- **What it is:** How to build a HyperFrames slideshow — a live-presented deck, not a rendered video: full-screen slides with fragment (step-by-step) reveals, clickable hotspots that branch to detail slides, and a presenter mode with speaker notes, served by `hyperframes present`. Also covers turning an existing web page into a deck. Main skill plus 1 bundled reference: the standalone-harness workaround doc for decks opened without `present`.
- **How it looks:** A browser tab showing one 1920×1080 slide at a time, full-bleed. A nav capsule floats over the deck with a Present button, prev/next arrows, a slide counter and (when the deck has sound) a speaker mute toggle. The presenter sees a second view with editable speaker notes per slide; the audience tab shows only the slide. Clickable regions on a slide (a labelled percentage-box hotspot, or the whole slide) jump sideways into a branch sequence — e.g. a "Where does $40B come from?" hotspot opening the market-sizing detail slides — and Back returns to the slide that held the hotspot. In standalone decks an ambient Three.js particle canvas can sit behind transparent slides, with the text floating on a soft radial scrim so the 3D shows in the margins.
- **Frame by frame:** Navigation seeks, it never plays: pressing Next (or P for Present, arrows, swipe) jumps the timeline straight to the next slide's rest frame, and every hold state must look correct when seeked to directly. A slide with fragments steps instead: each press advances to the next fragment's absolute hold time and that item appears (in the standalone harness the reveal animates: from opacity 0 and x −24 px to rest over 0.35 s, ease `power2.out`). On slide activation, entrance elements animate in (harness recipe: `gsap.from` from opacity 0, y +28 px, 0.4 s, stagger 0.07 s, `power2.out`, overwriting any in-flight animation). In standalone decks with a camera world, a manual slide change glides the camera between focal points over 760 ms (`cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1)`) instead of snapping. A slide marked `"autoplay": true` starts its first video on landing but still holds — the presenter advances manually. Leaving a slide stops its media automatically (the player pauses iframe video/audio and WebAudio). End state: the deck sits on the current slide's rest frame indefinitely; there is no rendered file.
- **Mechanism & key values:** A deck is a normal HyperFrames composition plus ONE JSON island written in the HTML near the top of `<body>` (never generated by script — `present` reads the file statically): `<script type="application/hyperframes-slideshow+json">` with `slides` and `slideSequences`. Each slide is a TOP-LEVEL scene (`data-composition-id`, `data-start`, `data-duration`, `data-label`, `data-width`, `data-height`) — there is no master root composition wrapping them. Island entries: `sceneId` (matching a scene's `data-composition-id`, or explicit `startTime`/`endTime`), `notes` (presenter-only), `fragments` (ABSOLUTE timeline times inside the slide's [start, end] — the same clock as `data-start`, not per-slide offsets; a slide without fragments enters at a rest frame inside it), `hotspots` (`id`, `label`, `target` = a slideSequence id, `region` = percentage box {x, y, w, h} — omit for a full-slide button). Branch slides are ordinary scenes listed ONLY in `slideSequences`, never in the main `slides` array. `ttsScript` / `ttsAudioUrl` / `ttsDurationMs` are reserved and not wired yet. Audience-readable text must be at least 40 px at 1920×1080. Never render a deck to MP4 — `render` keeps only the first scene and truncates silently; take stills with `snapshot --at` per slide. `hyperframes check --json` validates the deck: every `sceneId` resolves, every hotspot `target` exists, fragments sit inside their slide, main-line slides don't overlap. Serve with `npx hyperframes present <project-dir>` and hand over its URL ("Click Present, or press P, to open the audience tab"); the project root `index.html` should itself open as a working deck — `<hyperframes-slideshow>` wrapped around `<hyperframes-player src="…">`, the raw composition in a subfolder if needed. The component owns Present (P), Prev/Next, the counter, global mute, fullscreen, swipe, hotspots, editable per-deck presenter notes, and stopping media on slide exit — build none of these yourself. Screen-sharing: in Google Meet share the audience TAB (keeps rendering in the background); in Zoom drag the audience tab into its own window (a fully covered window freezes). Porting an existing page: keep its look, motion, interactions, widgets and media behaviour (port players/visualizers, don't approximate them); scroll/wheel/camera movement becomes a camera move from focal point to focal point on navigation — never a visibly scrolling page, and no reversals the source doesn't make; evidence images (screenshots, posts, charts, code, anything with readable text) keep their aspect with `object-fit: contain` and all four edges checked for crops; every copied `<video>`/`<audio>` needs `data-start` and `data-duration` (`data-has-audio="true"` when its sound plays) and no `preload="none"`; custom media chrome reads the native element's events and `currentTime`, never its own timer; hidden stacked slides need `opacity: 0` + `visibility: hidden` + `pointer-events: none` together or an invisible layer swallows clicks. Standalone harness (interim, until an engine-hosted present mode ships): the island must be DUPLICATED into the wrapper element's own innerHTML (the component reads its own innerHTML, not the loaded composition); the wrapper is the root `index.html` with the composition under e.g. `composition/index.html`; `<hyperframes-slideshow>` needs `tabindex="0"` or arrow keys are dead; the player needs the `interactive` attribute or iframe clicks become play/pause toggles. The composition exposes a seekable `window.__timelines.root` (a single `tl.to({}, { duration: <total> })` — 108 s in the worked example) whose `onUpdate` drives a visibility controller (`window.__hfSetTime`): scenes are 1920×1080 `.scene-frame`s hidden at rest, only the active scene visible, `updateVisibility(0)` called synchronously on load so the deck is never blank; scene backgrounds stay `transparent` when a Three.js canvas sits behind. Fragment hold-times are bunched within the first 300–500 ms of a scene so successive arrow presses feel snappy; fragment state resets on scene re-entry. The composition posts its scene manifest to the parent ~300 ms after load — `{source: "hf-preview", type: "timeline", durationInFrames: totalSeconds × FPS (30 in the example), scenes: [{id, start, duration}]}` — and EVERY scene including branch scenes must be listed or hotspots land on blank slides. Navigation camera transitions are standalone-only (never relied on for rendered output): the `#world` transform transition is 760 ms `cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1)` plus opacity 0.3 s ease, disabled via an `hf-camera-static` class for measurement, initial load, resize and validation seeks; a jump is detected when the slide index changes and |Δt| > 1.2 s; enabled by setting `iframe.contentWindow.__hfCameraTransitionsEnabled = true`. Audio: wrapper owns SFX (the user's gesture lands on the parent, so its AudioContext is the reliable one); the composition posts `{type: "hf-sfx", name}` cues unconditionally (advance / back / branch-enter / fragment) and the parent gates on mute; clips are primed on first gesture (play muted, pause, reset); worked volumes advance 0.45, fragment/branch-enter/back 0.4; SFX are resolved locally (`media-use resolve --type sfx`, Openverse CC0/CC BY with a CREDITS.md) and committed — no runtime fetches. The built-in mute is the `sound` attribute on `<hyperframes-slideshow>`: a speaker button rendered as the leftmost nav-capsule item, state reflected in `data-hf-muted`, toggles dispatch `CustomEvent("hf-sound", {detail: {muted}})`; without `sound`, no mute control shows. Presenter media bridge (standalone, interactive media): native media events are mirrored over `BroadcastChannel("hf-slideshow:" + location.pathname)`; timeupdate broadcasts throttle to 450 ms; remote time sync applies only when drift exceeds 0.35 s; only the presenter publishes; the audience tries muted playback first, and if `play()` still rejects it shows an "Enable audience media" unlock button (fixed pill, bottom 96 px) and stops chasing timeupdates until a gesture unlocks it. Media-driven visualizers read the native element (requestVideoFrameCallback preferred — composition lint rejects wall-clock loops; crossed-event firing guarded to forward jumps under 1.5 s) and use separate wiring markers (`data-media-sync-wired`, never one flag for two jobs). Editable-notes storage contract for custom wrappers: key prefix `hf-slideshow:presenter-notes:v1:` + JSON of [deck key, sequenceId, slideIndex, sceneId]; deck key from a `notes-storage-key` attribute or origin+pathname | title | player src; clearing a note saves an empty string, never removes the key. Optional Three.js ambience: three@0.160.0 module from CDN, ONE persistent canvas fixed at z-index 0 with `pointer-events: none`, scenes at z-index 1 with transparent backgrounds, renderer 1920×1080 at pixelRatio 1, PerspectiveCamera(60, 16/9, 0.1, 1000) at z = 5, its OWN requestAnimationFrame loop (never the seek timeline), frame delta clamped to 0.05 s, renderer creation guarded (console.error silenced during construction; on failure the canvas hides and `window.__threeApplyMood(sceneKey)` becomes a no-op stub that switches particle colours/visibility/clear colour per scene); light text scrim: `radial-gradient(ellipse 75% 80% at 50% 50%, rgba(255,255,255,0.88) 30%, rgba(255,255,255,0.6) 65%, rgba(255,255,255,0) 100%)` on the text container, not the scene frame. Foot-guns recorded: keep the bottom-right ~360×140 px clear of bright content (the nav capsule zone); `font-family: var(--…)` values fail lint — use concrete stacks (`system-ui, sans-serif`, `ui-monospace, monospace`) or local `@font-face`; parent code must test iframe media via `el.ownerDocument.defaultView.HTMLMediaElement`, not the parent realm's class.
- **Reference / source:** HeyGen HyperFrames — the `<hyperframes-slideshow>` / `<hyperframes-player>` components (player bundles under `packages/player/dist`), served by `hyperframes present` from the CLI of ⟦S0568⟧; compositions follow the core skill ⟦S0567⟧; named visuals come from the registry of ⟦S0569⟧. Catalog note: a much shorter twin of this same skill is also catalogued at ⟦S0549⟧ as `heygen-com/slideshow` (4 KB, identical one-line description, no bundled files); this ⟦S0571⟧ entry is the full 48 KB version with the standalone-harness reference inlined.
- **Best for:** Live presentation deliverables: pitch decks and sales decks presented over Meet/Zoom with presenter notes, decks with branching Q&A/detail slides behind hotspots, and converting an existing page or demo into a presentable deck. Not a rendered video (use the core/CLI skills) and not a homepage section; relevant when a build's deliverable is a deck someone presents live.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0571⟧
## ⟦S0572⟧ heygen-hyperframes/figma — Part 14 — UI Skills — video & motion graphics (HeyGen HyperFrames)
- **What it is:** A build-time importer that brings Figma material into a HyperFrames video project — rendered assets, brand tokens, frames as editable HTML components — frozen as local files, plus a path for turning Figma motion and storyboard frames into real animated motion instead of slide stills.
- **How it looks:** It renders nothing by itself; what the viewer ultimately sees is the brand's own Figma artwork — logos, frames, product UI — inside the video, with successive storyboard frames played as one element moving between states rather than as stills.
- **Frame by frame:** Storyboard rule: two frames holding the same element describe that element's states through time → the element tweens its geometry between the states; elements whose pixels changed crossfade in place; unmatched children enter or exit at their scene's beat; a product UI in successive states is rebuilt as live DOM and performed as interactions (cursor moves, clicks, screen responds). Motion imports are verified against Figma's own exported video: the check fails under 15 dB (faithful ≈ 20+, diverging ≈ 5).
- **Mechanism & key values:** REST import with a `FIGMA_TOKEN` (read-only File content + File metadata scopes, plus Library content for `tokens` on non-Enterprise plans); every import freezes a local file under `.media/` with its source recorded, so renders never call Figma. Commands: `npx hyperframes figma asset|tokens|component`. SVG for vectors and logos, PNG at 2× for raster; token-bound fills come out as `var(--slug, #literal)` so one variable re-brands every import. Motion path: recursive motion-context fetch → `motionContextToDocs` (drops loop-wrap tail keyframes, keeps bezier eases, reads the motion.dev snippets) → `motionToGsap` → `emitTimelineScript` (paused, finite, literal `window.__timelines` key); eases outside the mapped set fall back to linear. Storyboards: scenes are every frame-sized node ordered by `absoluteBoundingBox.x`, children matched by name then size/position, exports batched ~4 frames per call (past ~12 ids the images endpoint times out). Shaders flatten to their base colour in Figma's export path — a native PNG/MP4 export is placed as asset/clip instead. Embedded behaviour, described not executed: the skill prescribes `npx hyperframes events --skill=figma-motion` usage beacons at the start/end of its motion, shader and storyboard phases.
- **Reference / source:** HeyGen HyperFrames skill collection (heygen-hyperframes/figma); names the Figma REST API, motion.dev snippets and `@hyperframes/core/figma`.
- **Best for:** Video builds that must use a brand's real Figma design — logo/asset opens, product-UI scenes, storyboarded launch films. No direct homepage-section use (video pipeline skill); relevant to a trades build only when a firm already has Figma brand files for a promo film.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0572⟧

## ⟦S0573⟧ heygen-hyperframes/media-use — Part 14 — UI Skills — video & motion graphics (HeyGen HyperFrames)
- **What it is:** The media supply and treatment engine for HyperFrames videos: one `resolve` verb finds or makes any media — music, sound effects, images, icons, logos, voiceover, avatar or generated video, transcripts, cutouts, colour grades and LUTs — via HeyGen or free local tools, freezes it into the project ledger, and also treats placed footage (grades, looks, reveals, privacy) and mixes placed audio.
- **How it looks:** The viewer sees and hears the finished video's media layer: a music bed sitting under narration, whooshes and clicks landing on beats, real brand logos (never redrawn), a presenter or avatar speaking, word-synced captions, and footage that can be polished (a warm-daylight grade) or fully restyled — VHS tape damage, 8mm home-movie grain, four-angle CMYK halftone print, two-ink vermilion/teal print, engraved line art, ASCII glyph fields, Bayer-dither palettes, CRT curvature — plus text-behind-presenter cutout composites and held freeze-frame cutouts.
- **Frame by frame:** No single animation of its own; its motion-bearing outputs carry prescribed timing. Captions: groups enter per tone — hype scale-pop `back.out(1.7)` 0.1–0.2s at 72–96px, corporate fade+slide `power3.out` 0.3s, tutorial typewriter/fade 0.4–0.5s, storytelling slow fade `power2.out` 0.5–0.6s, social bounce `elastic.out` word-by-word — karaoke highlight throughout, exit fade 0.12s `power2.in` to scale 0.95 then a hard `tl.set` kill at group end; music content must be audio-reactive (bass scale +≤6%, treble glow ≤12px). Editorial flash overlay: rise 0.035–0.055s, recovery 0.24–0.38s, never more than one flash per second. Film Memory: exposure flicker ±0.03 in 0.45–0.8s `sine.inOut` segments, gate weave within 0.15% of the shorter edge, rotation within 0.03°.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Resolve cascade — exact-normalized cache floor (project `.media/manifest.jsonl` → unregistered `assets/` scan → global `~/.media/` cache) → provider fetch → file frozen under `.media/<type>/`, ledgered, auto-promoted to the global cache; fuzzy reuse is never automatic. Providers: HeyGen catalogs (10k+ music tracks, 75k+ assets/icons), logos via theSVG → GitHub org avatar → domain favicon; SFX from Openverse (CC0/CC BY only) then a bundled 21-file Pixabay-licensed library, volume ≈0.35, timed from the manifest (e.g. riser 10.03s). TTS order HeyGen Starfish (word timestamps in-response) → ElevenLabs → local Kokoro-82M (54 voices, prefix picks language); the docs-site narrator is pinned "River" (ElevenLabs `SAz9YHcvj6GT2YYXdXww`, 145–155 wpm, music ≈ −31 LUFS). BGM: HeyGen retrieval or Lyria → MusicGen local generation, default volume 0.12 under voice / 0.9 for a silent film; mood inference bases run 92–115 BPM by industry. Local generation ladders by RAM: FLUX.1 schnell int4 ~8GB, FLUX.2 Klein 4B ~32GB, Qwen-Image ~64GB; LTX 2.3 as local video fallback behind HeyGen avatar video. Transcription: Parakeet default (avg WER ~6.05% vs whisper.cpp 7.44%), whisper fallback with model sizes 75MB–3.1GB — `.en` models translate non-English, so `--model` is always explicit. Background removal: `u2net_human_seg`, VP9-alpha WebM (~1MB/4s at 1080p) or ProRes 4444, CRF presets fast 30 / balanced 18 / best 12, plus an inverse-alpha plate for text-between-layers. Grading persists as `data-color-grading` payloads (core presets, parametric `buildCube` LUTs, frozen `.cube` files) with seek-safe animated CSS vars (exposure −2..2, bloom 0..3, blur/kuwahara/pixelate/ascii/dither 0..1). Mixing lives in element attributes: `data-volume`, `data-fade-in/out`, `data-automation` lanes (≤512 points; duck a bed to ~0.3–0.4 under voice), `data-fx-chain` (16 node types), group buses; loudnorm targets −14 LUFS socials / −16 LUFS podcast. Behaviour note, described not executed: `resolve` and the edit tools send anonymous PostHog usage events (media type, source, provider only, `$ip: null`; opt out with `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` or `HYPERFRAMES_NO_TELEMETRY=1`; identity links to the HeyGen account when signed in), and paid HeyGen calls the agent initiates require confirmation first.
- **Reference / source:** HeyGen HyperFrames (heygen-hyperframes/media-use) with 23 bundled reference files; names the HeyGen CLI/API, Openverse/Freesound, Pixabay, ElevenLabs, Google Lyria/Gemini TTS, MusicGen, Kokoro, Parakeet/whisper.cpp, u2net.
- **Best for:** The media layer of any HyperFrames video — launch, explainer and social films; its caption style table, grade/treatment recipes and mixing rules are the reusable design content. Not a homepage-section skill; for trades work it is how a firm's promo or testimonial video gets its music, voice, captions and look.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0573⟧

## ⟦S0574⟧ heygen-hyperframes/oversized-cursor — Part 14 — UI Skills — video & motion graphics (HeyGen HyperFrames)
- **What it is:** The house cursor technique for HyperFrames launch videos: a deliberately oversized macOS-style pointer that travels the frame as a visible protagonist — it carries the viewer's eye to the next point of interest, clicks to cause the next beat, and hands itself across scene cuts.
- **How it looks:** One big clean SVG arrow — white body with black stroke, or black body `#1c1c1c` with a 1.4px white stroke, soft drop shadow — gliding across a UI scene many times larger than a real pointer; or, the power play, the subject brand's own cursor at the same scale (a Figma-style coloured multiplayer arrow with name tag travelling as one rigid unit, a creative suite's crosshair). It parks its tip on buttons and inputs, taps with a quick squash while the target reacts in parallel, and drifts aside while typing or narration runs.
- **Frame by frame:** Trigger: scene start or any pointer-led beat → the cursor enters from off-screen (canonical resting pose below the frame, `top: 115–120%`) on one continuous vector — default straight up the y-axis — in a decelerating glide of 0.4–0.92s `power3.out` (never an opacity fade or mask reveal) → the arrow TIP lands on the target's centre → click tap: scale to 0.84 in 0.1s `power2.in`, back to 1 in 0.22s `power2.out`, pivoting on the tip, while the target's own reaction tween runs at the same instant (button scale 0.94 + press colour/shadow; cursor-only taps such as focusing an input get no target reaction) → the click ignites the next beat on the same frame (menu cascade, typing kickoff, composer morph, logo flight, play-state flip) → during beats it doesn't own it drifts aside over 0.5–0.9s `power2.out`, never frozen on the action, never idle-wobbling → exit is physical: accelerate off the nearest edge in 0.5–0.7s `power2.in`, or a cut-the-curve handoff — it starts accelerating toward the next scene's first click point in the final ~0.3s before the cut and the next composition continues the same journey at matched velocity.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Size `7cqw` full-frame (≈134px at 1920 wide), 4.6–5.5cqw inside small mock frames, never smaller; one SVG arrow geometry everywhere; press pivot `transformOrigin: '21% 14%'` (the tip, for the house arrow in a 24-unit viewBox); `filter: drop-shadow(0 4px 6px rgba(0,0,0,.3))`, `pointer-events: none`, z-index above all scene content, `will-change: transform`; transform-only GSAP tweens.
- **Reference / source:** HeyGen HyperFrames house style (heygen-hyperframes/oversized-cursor), production-proven across their launch films; pairs with `cursor-click-ripple` / `press-release-spring` blocks for the target side, and the handoff with cut-the-curve ⟦S0576⟧.
- **Best for:** Video — UI scenes, product demos, morph/typing kickoffs, and rescuing a static scene with one cheap high-yield motion source; the eye-carrier idea also transfers to a web hero's demo loop. Trade fit: the pointer-led walkthrough segment of a firm's booking-form or quote-tool video.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0574⟧

## ⟦S0575⟧ heygen-hyperframes/changelog-video — Part 14 — UI Skills — video & motion graphics (HeyGen HyperFrames)
- **What it is:** A self-contained pipeline that turns a weekly changelog markdown file into a finished branded HyperFrames video — square 1080×1080, ~45–60s, a pinned HeyGen voiceover, an animated brand background, every theme shown as an animated mock of the actual UI, and a low-key caption rail. Its prime directive: visualize, don't list — text checklists are the last resort for genuinely non-visual items.
- **How it looks:** A dark film (background `#0a0c0b`) over a slowly moving encoded pattern background under a static scrim; cream ink `#f5f6f4` set in TT Norms Pro with ABC Solar Display headlines and TT Norms Mono labels; glass cards (dark translucent fill, 1px green-tinted border `rgba(190,255,205,.32)`, radius 22, deep shadow, no backdrop-filter); a mono kicker chip top-left and progress dots top-right; one rationed green `#5ef17c` moment per scene; a quiet 32px caption line riding at `top: 990`.
- **Frame by frame:** Title ≤2s — mono date kicker, ~104px display headline, green rule sweep → 4 theme scenes of ~9–12s each: the section chip and ~54px headline fly in with the scene wrapper (every ordinary seam is a cut-the-curve LEFT stamped from the vector ledger), internal reveals start ≥0.4s after the cut and every beat lands on a real VO word timestamp — the mock performs its choreography (timeline clips drop and stack into lanes, a binding pill flies into a property slot, terminal characters type at 0.02s stagger with the result line landing after a 0.3–0.5s beat, a render bar runs `power2.in` with its frame counter, checklist ticks land `back.out(1.5)` in 0.3s) → outro ≤3.5s ("See what shipped." ~96px, green rule, mono URL chip) with everything fading ~0.5s before the end. Caption words fade in over 0.12s on their timestamps, phrase by phrase.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Bootstrap is non-negotiable: copy the skill's own fonts, house BGM and `examples/master-skeleton.html` scaffold first — starting from a prior video's file is the named off-brand failure. Script is two-layer tokens (`script-tokens.json`): captions render the `display` spelling, the VO reads `spoken` phonetics from `references/lexicon.json` (initialisms spaced — "C L I"; acronyms respelled — JSON → "jay-sawn"; unknown term = stop and ask). VO is the pinned HeyGen voice `330290724a1b470fb63153f34d4c0183` ("Annie — lifelike, do not substitute") via `heygen-tts.mjs --words`; the words JSON is the timing ground truth, with a local whisper `base.en` forced-alignment fallback; `align-captions.mjs` joins spoken timings back to display tokens. Background encode: loop the bundled pattern to the exact total duration at 1080×1080, 30fps, saturation 0.72, black@0.5 drawbox crush, crf 20. BGM house track (159s) mounted at `data-volume="0.14"`. Seams: `ledger.json` → `seam-stamp.mjs` writes all wrapper entries/exits (animating a clip element instead of its wrapper is a lint error; title entry must pass `immediateRender: false`). Gates before presenting: `hyperframes check` with the caption zone (dim text ≥ .66 alpha for 4.5:1 contrast, content stays above the rail), seam-gate verify at 0 fail, and a caption-presence check sampling frames across the spoken window; render only when asked. Delivery behaviour recorded in the skill: after an S3 replace it prescribes a CloudFront invalidation on the project's distribution so the CDN does not serve the old file.
- **Reference / source:** HeyGen HyperFrames (heygen-hyperframes/changelog-video) with bundled `references/build-spec.md`, `references/script-voice.md`, `references/visualization-registry.md` and assets; it loads motion-doctrine ⟦S0578⟧ first, plus cut-the-curve ⟦S0576⟧, oversized-cursor ⟦S0574⟧, seam-craft ⟦S0577⟧ and captions-overlay ⟦S0579⟧.
- **Best for:** A recurring branded "what shipped this week" video series; its visualization registry (Studio editor, inspector panel, canvas, variant cards, storyboard, terminal, render panel, plus caching/batching/concurrency analogs) is reusable mock-UI choreography for any product-update video. Not homepage material.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0575⟧

## ⟦S0576⟧ heygen-hyperframes/cut-the-curve — Part 14 — UI Skills — video & motion graphics (HeyGen HyperFrames)
- **What it is:** The technique catalog beneath motion-doctrine: five velocity-matched seam techniques plus two in-scene techniques, all on one principle — cut at peak velocity and match direction and speed on both sides of the cut. This skill is the parameters and mechanics; the law lives in ⟦S0578⟧.
- **How it looks:** Scene changes feel like one continuous camera move: a headline swells toward the viewer and swaps mid-blur into the next line; whole scenes slide about an eighth of the frame width and hand off mid-flight; a big text line peels away word by word while the next line cascades in on the same wave; title cards whip up from below in an accelerating cascade; a composed group of cards glides aside slow-fast-slow to make room for new content.
- **Frame by frame:** ① Zoom-Through (within-scene text swap, ≈0.4s total): outgoing text scales 1→1.2 with blur 0→10px over 0.2s `power3.in`, opacity on a separate linear tween down to 0.15 → hard `tl.set` swap at peak blur (incoming preset at scale 0.75, blur 10px, opacity 0.15 — never both texts visible) → entry grows 0.75→1, blur→0, opacity→1 over 0.5s `expo.out`. ② Inverse Zoom-Through (arrival/payoff beat, ≈0.7s, 30% exit / 70% entry): exit shrinks 1→0.8; the incoming element arrives oversized at 1.25 and retracts to 1, `expo.out` ~0.5s. ③ Cut the Curve (the default scene boundary, ≈0.6s): the hero accelerates ±230px (~12% of a 1920 frame) `power4.in` over 0.2–0.4s with its fade completing at ~25–30% of travel → cut mid-motion → the incoming hero starts ∓230px at opacity 0.35 and decelerates `power4.out` for at least the exit's duration; optional blur 8–10px. ④ Waterfall Cut (text-to-text seam): words exit over 0.34s `power4.in` with a 0.18s fade and +0.022s reading-order stagger; words enter over 0.3s `power4.out` from x +230 igniting at opacity 0.35, entry gaps starting 0.05s and decaying ×0.84. ⑤ Rack-Focus Blur-Cut (the one cut meant to be seen): the outgoing surface stays fully opaque while blur spikes (cut at peak blur ≥6px, peak 8–12px, max ~16–18px) with a subtle ~1.06 lens-breathing scale, `power2.in`/`power2.out` — at most once per ~8s, only at a narrative beat. ⑥ Waterfall Entry (in-scene arrival, no seam): binary 0→1 reveal via `tl.set`, elements whip up from below — anchors offset 60–80px over 0.16–0.20s, normal words 40–50px over 0.13–0.16s, light punctuation 30–48px over 0.10–0.13s, `power4.out`, overlapping by ±1–2 frames with shrinking gaps; the final word may split into fragments that travel further. ⑦ Nudge Curve (in-scene group slide): three chained tweens — ~10% of distance in ~20% of time `power3.in`, ~65% in ~18% linear, ~25% in ~62% `power4.out` (270px reference: −30px/0.12s, −210px/0.10s, −270px/0.35s; the tail is ≥3× the ramp-in in time).
- **Mechanism & key values:** GSAP tweens on wrappers — blur the wrapper, never children. Z sign rule: the sign of d(scale)/dt must match across the cut (push = growing on both sides, pull = shrinking on both sides); a receding exit answered by a grow-from-small entry is the banned mirror. Blur is sized to the subject: 10px for text-scale, 18–20px for full-frame surfaces, the same peak on both sides at the swap frame. Mirrored `power4.in`/`power4.out` are the two halves of one `power4.inOut`, so velocity matches exactly at the cut; `.inOut` eases on either side of a cut are banned, as are full off-screen exits (partial travel + early fade instead). An opaque `#root` stage ground is required or the mid-window opacity dip flashes white (see ⟦S0577⟧). Full worker + registry GSAP templates live in the bundled `examples/gsap-implementation.md`.
- **Reference / source:** HeyGen HyperFrames (heygen-hyperframes/cut-the-curve); seam law in motion-doctrine ⟦S0578⟧, render prerequisites in seam-craft ⟦S0577⟧.
- **Best for:** Video scene seams and text-beat handoffs in launch films and explainers; the waterfall entry and nudge curve transfer directly to web work — hero headline cascades, section openers, list intros and group repositioning on a page. Trade fit: title cards and section openers in any trades brand film.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0576⟧

## ⟦S0577⟧ heygen-hyperframes/seam-craft — Part 14 — UI Skills — video & motion graphics (HeyGen HyperFrames)
- **What it is:** The render-correctness doctrine for scene-to-scene seams in HyperFrames videos — the prerequisites and master-timeline mechanics that make any transition composite correctly, independent of which transition is chosen. It contains no per-transition catalog; that lives in the transition registry / cut-the-curve.
- **How it looks:** It has no visual of its own; its visible effect is the absence of a defect. Without it, seams whose two scene wrappers dip below summed opacity 1 (the cut-the-curve mid-window cut, zoom-through's 0.15 floor, a crossfade's power-curve dip) show whatever is behind the wrappers — an unpainted renderer default of white — as a white flash at every cut, glaring on dark films.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion of its own. At each boundary the injector: extends the outgoing wrapper's `data-duration` by the transition length so it holds its final frame → pulls the incoming wrapper's `data-start` earlier by the same length, creating the overlap window → reassigns all clip `data-track-index` values as a 0/1 ping-pong so the overlapping wrappers never share a track (the higher track composites on top) → stamps the transition's `gsap_template` into `window.__timelines["main"]` at T = overlap-start.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Stage-ground prerequisite: `#root { background: var(--canvas-deep, var(--canvas, #000)) }` must be opaque — `assemble-index.mjs` emits it, and any other consumer of the templates owns the same guarantee. Governed transitions are Tier-B-ready: pure transform/opacity/filter on the two scene clip wrappers (`#el-<sid>`), no injected overlay DOM and no per-scene cooperation; overlay families (blinds, light leak, grid dissolve, page burn) and shader transitions are deferred. Template tokens the injector substitutes: `__OLD__`, `__NEW__`, `__T__` (overlap-start, seconds), `__DUR__`, `__DX__` (−1920 LEFT / 1920 RIGHT), `__DY__` (−1080 UP / 1080 DOWN), `__ORIGIN_OUT__`/`__ORIGIN_IN__` for squeeze. Verified by prototype render 2026-05-31: the master-timeline wrapper tween is seeked and rendered independently of each sub-composition's own paused timeline, with no double-seek.
- **Reference / source:** HeyGen HyperFrames (heygen-hyperframes/seam-craft); per-transition parameters in cut-the-curve ⟦S0576⟧, seam law in motion-doctrine ⟦S0578⟧.
- **Best for:** Assembling any multi-scene HyperFrames master timeline, and diagnosing white flashes at cuts or crossfades on dark films; prerequisite knowledge underneath the changelog pipeline ⟦S0575⟧ and every stamped seam.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0577⟧

## ⟦S0578⟧ heygen-hyperframes/motion-doctrine — Part 14 — UI Skills — video & motion graphics (HeyGen HyperFrames)
- **What it is:** The gateway motion law for all HyperFrames animation — load it first, before composing any video. It decides what happens at every seam and how every scene performs, so a multi-scene video feels like one continuous camera move instead of a stack of independently animated slides; the technique skills (cut-the-curve, oversized-cursor, seam-craft) implement it, and its rules supersede generic upstream motion guidance.
- **How it looks:** Nothing renders from this skill directly; its visible result across a film is that scenes hand their momentum across every cut in one dominant direction (the "current", house default LEFT), entrances arrive already mid-flight rather than starting from rest, reserved vectors appear only when they mean something (up = elevation, Z-forward = deeper into a thought, Z-backward = arrival, scale-burst = leaving a world), and no scene ever idles — at any paused second something meaningful is mid-flight.
- **Frame by frame:** At each seam: the outgoing element is still moving at the cut → hard cut with zero overlap (one side visible per frame, never a dissolve) → the incoming element enters already ≥50% through its notional path at matched velocity (mirrored `power4.in`/`power4.out`; on Z seams the sign of the scale change matches on both sides, and the incoming scene's own opening entrances are held composed or sign-matched) → inside the scene, one named sustained-motion route performs (staged reveals paid off on narration beats / a mapped camera scale+pan path / sequenced UI life / an animated sequence / cursor-led action) → a 0.3–0.75s stillness lands before the climax → exit runs at ≈75% of the entry duration (cut-the-curve inverts this: entry ≈127% of exit).
- **Mechanism & key values:** The Vector Law has four parts — axis (x stays x, y stays y, Z stays Z), direction (never mirrored; on Z, direction is the sign of scale change), speed (entry initial velocity ≈ exit final velocity), phase (the cut lands mid-motion on both sides). Workflow: write the vector ledger as `ledger.json` at the project root before authoring → `seam-stamp.mjs --ledger ledger.json --write index.html` generates the master seams → `seam-gate.mjs verify` enforces them numerically (ledger-row consistency, exit still moving, entry mid-flight, measured direction = ledger direction, zero overlap, Z-sign scan, carrier rect continuity within 12px centre / 5% size tolerance, ancestor scale included; exit 0 or the seam is not done). Carriers: a concrete object (cursor mid-path, a docking container, a flying mark, a word group) hands the eye across the cut at matched position and velocity — a crossfade is banned because it has no carrier. Causal motion: reactions start on the causing frame, scaled by implied mass. Timing intents: single entry ≤ ~800ms, total stagger ≤ 500ms, `bounce.out`/`elastic.out` forbidden, entry overshoot `back.out(1.4–1.7)` allowed, similar elements share one ease+duration intent. Only 2–3 inter-scene transitions per film, repeated; idle wobble (breathe/float/drift/glow-pulse loops) is banned as sustained motion. Any edit to a scene's first/last ~1s, or a VO regen, re-opens that seam's audit.
- **Reference / source:** HeyGen HyperFrames (heygen-hyperframes/motion-doctrine) with bundled `references/seam-gate.md`. Duplicate note: the catalog also lists this same gateway skill as ⟦S0544⟧ heygen-com/motion-doctrine — same skill name and description under the earlier heygen-com collection; treat the two listings as one underlying skill and read one.
- **Best for:** The first read before composing any HyperFrames video; its ledger + gate workflow governs the changelog pipeline ⟦S0575⟧ and all block-based films. Its thinking also transfers to multi-section web pages: one dominant scroll direction, entrances that continue momentum, no dead beats between sections.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0578⟧

## ⟦S0579⟧ heygen-hyperframes/captions-overlay — Part 14 — UI Skills — video & motion graphics (HeyGen HyperFrames)
- **What it is:** Caption doctrine for HyperFrames videos, in two combined ideas: a model that classifies every spoken phrase as drop, rail or embed, and the overlay law — captions are composited on top of the film as an overlay, never a reserved bottom band that the layout shifts content up to avoid.
- **How it looks:** A small, minimal word-by-word caption line, bottom-centred in roughly the bottom 5–8% of the canvas, riding over full-bleed footage while the composition stays centred on the true frame centre. Ordinary speech reads as a clean lower-third rail in front of the subject, a punch word optionally taking an inline emphasis highlight; at a genuine peak, one big word appears behind the subject (matte occlusion) with a designed entrance and exit.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion prescribed of its own (rail-word and embed animation lives in the upstream captions reference and caption blocks; this skill governs classification and placement). The sequence it imposes: a phrase is spoken → filler (um/uh, stutters, self-corrections) is dropped, not shown → ordinary content rides the verbatim rail in front → a peak phrase is promoted to a single embed behind the subject, at most one per sentence/beat, never two adjacent or co-visible, spaced at least a beat apart, with at most one apex climax in a beat chain.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Centre compositions on the true vertical centre, y = H/2 (landscape 540, portrait 960); centring at 0.42 × H with a dead lower band is named the bug, not the fix. Content may extend to the canvas bottom — full-bleed subjects, rails and backgrounds are all welcome under the caption skin. One soft courtesy rule: keep critical small readable text (a URL line, a legal line, a sub-caption) out of the bottom ~80px centre span where the caption line sits. There is no machine keep-out gate (the old `captions.mjs` keepout check is retired); caption-over-content legibility is judged visually in snapshot review. A pure-cinematic treatment may drop the rail and make everything embed-style — never for explainer/voiceover work where the words must read.
- **Reference / source:** HeyGen HyperFrames (heygen-hyperframes/captions-overlay); it supplements the upstream `/hyperframes` skill's `references/captions.md` and is applied concretely by the changelog caption rail in ⟦S0575⟧ and the caption system in media-use ⟦S0573⟧.
- **Best for:** Talking-head, launch and explainer videos — caption placement, laying out a composition that will carry captions, and deciding which words earn an embed moment. No homepage-section use.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0579⟧

## ⟦S0580⟧ heygen-hyperframes/wireframe-portal-title — Part 14 — UI Skills — video & motion graphics (HeyGen HyperFrames)
- **What it is:** A ready-made HyperFrames title block (1920×1080, 8s at 30fps, 9 variables): extruded wireframe letterforms burst open through a portal, the title comes through, and then its letters swap into a second phrase.
- **How it looks:** 3D wireframe letters — built from the bundled Geist typeface with a TTF loader and polygon offsetting — burst open in a portal explosion with depth fog, over a subtitle line ("HYPERFRAMES PORTAL TITLE" by default) and a gold accent (`#F5C518` by default). The default title is "BREAKTHROUGH" (max 18 chars); on the second beat the letterforms re-form into the replacement phrase ("Lets do this sir!" by default) with whole-word wrapping and automatic type size, landing with a slight settle glitch.
- **Frame by frame:** The portal bursts open (chaos variable, default 1, range 0–2) → the wireframe title comes through the burst → hold → the letters transition into the replacement phrase over `phraseDuration` 1.85s (range 0.65–2.9s) with `phraseEasing` default 8 (1 gentle – 8 snap) → letters settle with glitch strength 0.2 (range 0–4); depth fog is on throughout (early fade always on). Exact per-second keyframes are internal to the block's closed-form timeline — the skill exposes the phase order and the variables, not a frame table.
- **Mechanism & key values:** three.js 0.181.2 + GSAP 3.14.2 + Canvas 2D + GLSL shaders + post-processing + seeded PRNG + Clipper polygon offsetting; local Geist Regular/SemiBold/Bold TTFs. One paused GSAP timeline registered as `window.__timelines["wireframe-portal-title"]`, re-syncing on the `hf-seek` event — every frame a closed-form function of time (no rAF loops, no Date.now). Budget roughly 350 MB per live instance; run one at a time. The 9 variables: `title`, `replacementPhrase`, `phraseDuration`, `phraseEasing`, `settleGlitch`, `depthFog`, `subtitle`, `accent`, `burstChaos`. Block file 63 KB; install with `npx hyperframes add wireframe-portal-title`, mount via `data-composition-src`, render with `--variables`.
- **Reference / source:** HeyGen HyperFrames block library (heygen-hyperframes/wireframe-portal-title); Geist fonts under the OFL.
- **Best for:** Video title cards and section titles in launch films — a technical wireframe opener whose second phrase carries the payoff line. A video block, not a web hero, though the wireframe-letterform + phrase-swap idea could inspire a WebGL headline.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0580⟧

## ⟦S0582⟧ heygen-hyperframes/frost-sequence-camera-orbit — Part 14 — UI Skills — video & motion graphics (HeyGen HyperFrames)
- **What it is:** A complete ready-made HyperFrames sequence block (1920×1080, 22.5s at 30fps, composition id `frost-sequence-rig`, 216 variables): an orbiting camera follows an ice logo as it breaks apart into a shard-and-particle field, reforms into two successive text moments, and fades — the full material, fracture, flight, return, lighting and post pipeline is exposed as variables.
- **How it looks:** A glassy ice logo — a transmission material with IOR 1.675, pale-blue attenuation `#d5f4ff`, surface frost, cracks, crystals and internal inclusions — floats on a near-black backdrop (`#050505`) under a cool studio lighting rig (key `#f0f7ff`, rim `#d9f1ff`, plus orange and blue accent lights) with dust motes drifting around it. The camera orbits the fixed objects with slower front-facing passes so text can be read. The mark shatters into tumbling ice shards and powder, then the same field streams home and re-freezes into the first headline ("Hard to|break."), breaks and reforms again into the second ("Easy to|remember."), and fades out.
- **Frame by frame:** The camera orbits the assembled ice logo (slower front passes for reading) → a first diagonal slice (radius 0.6, strength 21.5) and follow-up shatters (radius 0.45, strength 32.5) break the volume → shards eject (speed 0.91, spread 0.48, turbulence 4, final-break eject boost ×2.5, speed cap 26.3, gravity 0 — shards never fall) and tumble (rate 1.05) amid 100k powder particles (visible shard fraction 0.44, 24 stray dust motes) → flight settles after 2.2s into a slow organic drift → return: regional stagger 1.35s plus per-shard jitter up to 2.8s, shards spring home (stiffness 29.9, damping 1.34, ramp-in 0.45s, return speed cap 60), align to the surface and refrost over 10.6s, forming headline 1 → a second breakup/reform cycle forms headline 2 → fade. Assembly grows over 3.2s from origin (−0.65, 0.55) at a −35° seam angle. Beat timings are editable in the source; the skill documents the phase order and the full parameter set rather than fixed cut times.
- **Mechanism & key values:** WebGPU renderer + GSAP 3.14.2 + matcap shading; the `frost.js` engine is 1.5 MB. Voxel shape resolution 256, erosion field 96 per axis, particle count 100k (options up to 1M). Material defaults: base roughness 0.31, backlight 0.27, thickness scale 2.04, frost threshold 0.62 / softness 0.24 / roughness 0.73, crack width 0.0025, smudge amount 0.78. Post: ACES tonemap (default), bloom threshold 3 / intensity 0.04, vignette strength 0.14, monochrome 0.04; upscaler FSR1 at renderScale 1. One paused GSAP timeline, `hf-seek` resync, seeded PRNG only; no external runtime dependencies — all assets ship locally (the shards atlas and ice-inclusions textures are fetched from the CDN at install time). Text is extruded Geist (depth 0.16 of font size, bevel 0.04, headline block width 6.5 against the 2.6-wide mark).
- **Reference / source:** HeyGen HyperFrames block library (heygen-hyperframes/frost-sequence-camera-orbit); vendored ClipperLib (Boost Software License) for polygon offsetting, with Three.js, ThreeMeshBVH and Opentype.js licences bundled; Geist fonts under the OFL.
- **Best for:** Premium brand-film logo stings and title sequences — one block carries a whole 22.5s logo → claim → claim arc; the shatter-and-reform particle mechanism is also a reference for WebGL logo/hero moments. Heavy (one instance at a time) and a video block, not a homepage section.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0582⟧

## ⟦S0584⟧ heygen-hyperframes/glass-shard-title — Part 14 — UI Skills — video & motion graphics (HeyGen HyperFrames, Remotion, ...)
- **What it is:** A HyperFrames video block (1920×1080, 12.16 s): a headline built from Voronoi-cut glass panes that fly in through fog, tile themselves into the letterforms, then fly out past the camera.
- **How it looks:** Dozens of irregular glass shards — each a jittered blob clipped to its Voronoi cell, bevelled, with matcap reflections and per-fragment fog — stream in from deep in the frame, rotating, and land edge-to-edge (tiny 0.03 gap) so together they form the solid silhouette of the headline (default "Designed in glass", Geist; Cormorant Garamond also bundled). After the hold they burst back out toward and past the viewer.
- **Frame by frame:** Trigger: composition play (12.16 s at 30 fps). → Fly-in (default 2.3 s, stagger 0.27): shards travel from z = −42 through fog, rotating (fly-in rotation 5), the z-flight decoupled from the position ease (ease power 10) so they visibly traverse depth. → They settle into the tiled headline silhouette. → Hold: assembled glass headline. → Fly-out (default 2.4 s, rotation 6): shards fly to z = +14, past the camera. → End state: empty frame.
- **Mechanism & key values:** three.js 0.181.2 + GSAP 3.14.2 + Canvas 2D + GLSL shaders, HDR environment (ferndale_studio_01_1k.hdr, 1.6 MB), matcap, shadow maps, d3-delaunay Voronoi; each shard is a Sutherland–Hodgman clip of a jittered blob against its cell so coverage is exact; tile count 1 = a single pane. 19 variables, key defaults: `tileCount` 8 (1–400), `roundness` 0.4, `bevel` 0.35, `meshSmooth` 0.6, `flyInTime` 2.3 s, `flyOutTime` 2.4 s, `chaos` 0.25, `sizeVariance` 0.35, `gap` 0.03, `easePow` 10, `sideDist` 3, `fog` 36 (0 = off). Runtime budget roughly 350 MB per live instance — run one at a time. Headline max 40 chars.
- **Reference / source:** HeyGen HyperFrames block library (`npx hyperframes add glass-shard-title`).
- **Best for:** Mechanism reference for a hero headline reveal — fragments assembling into type — and for rendered title videos. Heavy WebGL; on a homepage the transferable idea is the shard-assembly reveal for one big headline moment, recreated in lighter tech.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0584⟧

- **Mechanism & key values:** WebGL (three.js) + GSAP, PMREM environment, shadow maps (default map size 2048, softness radius 44.5); spacing is derived from cuboid dimensions and the largest reachable X half-extent so cuboids can never overlap. Cards from a built-in list or a `cardsJson` variable. Runtime budget roughly 350 MB per live instance. Font: Inter (Google Fonts).

## ⟦S0586⟧ heygen-hyperframes/code-slice-hero — Part 14 — UI Skills — video & motion graphics (HeyGen HyperFrames, Remotion, ...)
- **What it is:** A HyperFrames video block (1920×1080, 8 s): a wall of square tiles carries one headline; a sweeping invisible cursor lifts and tilts nearby tiles, and the tiles inside the letterforms flip over to reveal a second headline on their backs.
- **How it looks:** A full-frame grid of square cells (default 112 px) printed with one seamless bold headline (default "MAKE IT", Geist Bold, up to 310 px). A wave of depth rolls across the surface — tiles near the sweep lift toward the viewer and tilt — and as it passes, the cells that intersect either headline's silhouette turn over, so the rear headline (default "MATTER.") appears in flipped tiles against the dark behind-surface (`#212121`), with soft cast shadows under lifted tiles.

- **Mechanism & key values:** The whole grid is one instanced WebGL 2 draw with a shared front/rear texture pair, plus a batched projected-shadow pass; copy, text size and square cell size are independent so tiles never stretch. 18 variables, defaults: `direction` left-to-right, `sweepDuration` 4.2 s (2.6–4.5), `sweepEaseStrength` 3 (0–3), `flipDuration` 0.75 s (0.65–1.65), `cursorRadius` 210 (160–480), `cursorDepth` 80 (−320–320), `tiltStrength` 55, `flipBounce` 0.15 (0–0.8), `cellSize` 112 (24–120), `fontSize` 310 (160–480), `behindColor` `#212121`, `shadowStrength` 0.19, `shadowSoftness` 4. Headlines max 32 chars each. Runtime: GSAP + Canvas 2D + seeded PRNG per the block's contract; local Geist Bold font.
- **Reference / source:** HeyGen HyperFrames block library (`npx hyperframes add code-slice-hero`).
- **Best for:** Mechanism reference for a hero headline swap — one message flipping to a second message tile by tile — and for rendered hero videos. The transferable pattern: a cursor/sweep-driven tile flip that exchanges headline A for headline B in a hero.

## ⟦S0588⟧ Ant Design — Part 16 — Design.md brand skills (ui-skills.com)
- **What it is:** The DESIGN.md for Ant Design v6 (Ant Group's open-source enterprise React design system, est. 2015): seed-token colour derivation, typography, three-layer surfaces, elevation, shapes, component archetypes and theming via ConfigProvider, for dense data-rich consoles and admin tools.
- **How it looks:** Calm, flat, dense product UI: light-grey page (`#F5F5F5`) holding white cards and tables, one blue (`#1677FF`) reserved for the single primary action, links, focus rings and the selected menu row (pale blue `#E6F4FF` wash). Small 14 px system-font text, only two weights (400/600), tight 6 px-radius controls, hierarchy carried by borders and tonal steps rather than shadows.
- **Frame by frame:** No narrative animation; motion is component state change on three tokenised durations — trigger: hover/focus/press → 0.1 s (`motionDurationFast`); trigger: component-internal change (collapse, fade) → 0.2 s (`motionDurationMid`); trigger: surface change (modal enter, drawer slide) → 0.3 s (`motionDurationSlow`), all on named token easings (`motionEaseInOut`, `motionEaseOut`, `motionEaseOutBack`, `motionEaseOutCirc`, …), never hand-picked cubic-beziers.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Primary `#1677FF`, hover `#4096FF`, active `#0958D9`; semantic seeds success/warning/error/info expand via `@ant-design/colors`. Neutral text as rgba(0,0,0,α): 0.88 / 0.65 / 0.45 / 0.25 (composited `#1F1F1F` / `#595959` / `#BFBFBF`). Surfaces: bg-layout `#F5F5F5`, bg-container `#FFFFFF`, bg-elevated `#FFFFFF` (distinguished by shadow only). Type: base 14 px; stack −apple-system / Segoe UI / Roboto / Helvetica Neue / Arial / Noto Sans; weights 400 + 600 only. Spacing 4 px grid, scale 4/4/8/16/24/32. Radius: controls 6 px, surfaces 8 px, tags/tooltips 4 px, full pill only for avatars/badges/dots. Shadows: tertiary `0 1px 2px rgba(0,0,0,.05), 0 1px 6px −1px rgba(0,0,0,.03), 0 2px 4px rgba(0,0,0,.03)`; popup `0 6px 16px rgba(0,0,0,.08), 0 3px 6px −4px rgba(0,0,0,.12), 0 9px 28px 8px rgba(0,0,0,.05)`. Button/input 32 px tall; card padding 24 px; modal on `rgba(0,0,0,0.45)` mask, body padding 20×24 px; tabs: 2 px primary underline, no fill; tooltip `rgba(0,0,0,0.85)` inverse. Theming: seed overrides, default/dark/compact algorithms (composable), per-component token overrides, `theme.useToken()` / CSS variables / zero-runtime extraction. Note recorded in the file: white on `#1677FF` sits below WCAG AA 4.5:1 for small text.
- **Reference / source:** Ant Design (Ant Group), ant.design; file points to ant.design/docs/react/customize-theme.md and the project CHANGELOG.
- **Best for:** Forms and data-dense sections — quote forms, comparison tables, admin-style proof blocks — where certainty of state matters: explicit hover/focus/loading/error states, one-primary-action discipline, and a 0.1/0.2/0.3 s motion ladder. Enterprise-console register; not a marketing-hero style.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0588⟧

## ⟦S0589⟧ Atlassian — Part 16 — Design.md brand skills (ui-skills.com)
- **What it is:** Atlassian's portable, token-first DESIGN.md manifest (Jira/Confluence maker): the full ADS token vocabulary — colours, type, 8 px spacing, four-plane elevation, t-shirt radius scale, component behaviour rules, motion, voice and accessibility — in RFC 2119 rule language (MUST/SHOULD/MAY).
- **How it looks:** Neutral-dominant product UI: white page canvas, bordered white cards, sunken `#F8F8F8` wells inside the page (never a grey page background), restrained colour that always means something — blue links (`#1868DB`), semantic role fills for status, decorative accent ramps only on tags/avatars. Atlassian Sans throughout product; sentence case everywhere, including buttons and badges (no Title Case, no ALL-CAPS eyebrows — Atlassian does not use the eyebrow pattern).
- **Frame by frame:** Motion is a clarifying layer only, in two bands — trigger: interaction (hover, press, list-item state) → 50–150 ms; trigger: element entering/exiting/repositioning (modal, panel, flag, popup) → 150–400 ms, exits faster than entrances. Easings: `ease-out` for entrances, `ease-in` for exits, `ease-in-out` two-way; "practical" curves for everyday fades, "bold" curves reserved for prominent moves like a modal entering. One focal point per moment; no bounce/elastic in product UI; `prefers-reduced-motion` disables non-essential motion outright. Toggle thumb travel and the spinner's rotate/load-in are animated as state transitions from stored motion tokens.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Surfaces: `surface` `#FFFFFF`, `surface-sunken` `#F8F8F8`, `surface-raised` `#FFFFFF` + `shadow-raised`, `surface-overlay` `#FFFFFF` + `shadow-overlay` (four planes; raised = at most one region per screen). Text: `text` `#292A2E`, `text-subtle` `#505258`, `text-subtlest` `#6B6E76`; borders: hairline alpha `#0B120E24`, `border-bold` `#7D818A`, `border-input` `#8C8F97`, `border-focused` `#4688EC`; link `#1868DB` / pressed `#1558BC`. Colour kinds: neutrals, six semantic roles (brand/danger/warning/success/information/discovery, each with text-/icon-/border-/background-…-bold anchors), accent ramps (10 hues × subtlest→bolder), chart categorical 1–8 in order. Fonts: Atlassian Sans (Inter-based), Atlassian Mono (JetBrains Mono-based); Charlie Display/Text for marketing surfaces only; third-party fonts banned. Spacing: 8 px base, `space-0`–`space-1000`; 12-column grid, `space-300` gutters, `space-400` page padding. Radius t-shirt scale: xsmall 2 px (badges/checkboxes), small 4 px, medium 6 px (buttons/inputs), large 8 px (cards), xlarge 12 px (modals), xxlarge 16 px (video only), full (avatars/pills), tile 25%. Border widths 1 px default / 2 px selected / 2 px focused. Focus ring: 2 px, offset 2 px, ring radius = component radius + 2 px. Modal width tiers 400/600/800/968 px; tooltip 240 px (truncate 420 px); toggle tracks 32×16 and 40×20; checkbox/radio 16 px with 24 px hit target. Sentence case mandatory; strings translatable (+30% length headroom); tap targets ≥ `space-400` (32 px); test widths 320/768/1280 px; WCAG 2.2 AA floor.
- **Reference / source:** Atlassian Design System — atlassian.design; companion `atlassian-design-system` skill, ADS MCP server and `@atlaskit/icon` named as implementation sources.
- **Best for:** Rigour reference for forms, navigation and proof sections: state-certainty rules (selected = background + 2 px border + text triad together), the two-band motion ladder, and anti-drift checklists (no gradient text, no glass cards, no "hero metric" template, no repeated identical tiles). A product-UI system — its discipline transfers to quote forms and dashboards, not its brand look.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0589⟧

- **How it looks:** Precise developer-SaaS polish: near-neutral greys (page tint `#fafafb`, borders `#d9d9de`) with one purple anchor (`#6c47ff`) on primary CTAs, the logomark and eyebrow labels; purple→sky glow gradients under UI demos. Tight-tracked SemiBold headings (Suisse Intl), monospace uppercase eyebrow tags, white bento cards floating on four-layer soft shadows, 16 px card corners against 6 px button corners.
- **Frame by frame:** Small, tokenised moves — trigger: hover on nav/ghost buttons → 100 ms in, 150 ms out; icon transforms and form feedback → 200 ms; button shimmer and the support popover → 300 ms; theme colour change → 450 ms. Easings: `ease-out-cubic` `cubic-bezier(0.33,1,0.68,1)` for UI transitions, `cubic-bezier(0.4,0.36,0,1)` for the button-shimmer overlay, `cubic-bezier(0.175,0.885,0.32,1.275)` bounce for the hover arrow reveal on cards (the primary button's arrow slides in via translate-x on hover). Springs (motion/react): button content swap stiffness 200 / damping 20 / mass 0.8; drawer 300/30/0.5; nav indicator 400/50. Named: `fade-in` (default 0.3 s linear, configurable), `letter-reveal` 0.3 s ease-out (opacity + blur 2 px → 0), `blink` 1 s step-end. All gated on `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Purple ramp: 50 `#f4f2ff` → 500 `#6c47ff` (primary) → 950 `#230b6a`; hover 400 `#9785ff`, pressed 600 `#6430f7`. Grays: 25 `#fafafb` → 950 `#131316` (200 `#d9d9de` default border, 500 `#747686` secondary text). Accents: sky `#00aee3`, blue `#3b82f6`, green `#22c543`, red `#ef4444`, orange `#f36b16`, yellow `#efd420`. Brand gradient `from-purple-500 to-sky-300` (`#6c47ff` → `#3ad4fd`) for glows, never button fills; section shine radial `74.05% 100% at 50% 0%`, white → transparent. Type: Suisse Intl + Geist (tabular numbers only), Söhne Mono; custom Book weight 450. Heading scale: h1 4 rem/700/−0.035 em, h2 3.5 rem/600, h3 3 rem, h4 2 rem/−0.015 em, h5 1.25 rem, h6 1.125 rem; body/label 1–5 (1.125 rem → 0.625 rem); `tag-1` eyebrow: mono, uppercase, 0.1 em tracking, 0.6875 rem/500. Spacing 4 px base; container caps 40/48/64/80 rem at sm/md/lg/xl (640/768/1024/1280 px). Radius: 6 px buttons/inputs, 8 px popovers/cards, 12 px dropdowns/modals, 16 px bento/code/drawers, full for avatars/pills. Shadows are multi-layer only — bento card: `0 1px 1px rgba(0,0,0,.05), 0 4px 6px rgba(34,42,53,.04), 0 24px 68px rgba(47,48,55,.05), 0 2px 3px rgba(0,0,0,.04)`; auth shell adds a `0 0 0 1px rgb(0 0 0/.06)` ring + three more layers; dark mode replaces outer shadows with inset 1 px white/2.5% borders. Buttons: primary heights 1.875/1.625/1.5 rem. Section anatomy: eyebrow (tag-1) → sentence-case H2 → body-2 grey copy (max-w-2xl) → optional CTA, sections split by a 0.5 px top border `gray-950/12`. Touch targets 44×44 px. Auth `appearance` variables (defaults: `colorPrimary` `#2f3037` light / `#ffffff` dark — near-black, not purple; `borderRadius` 0.375 rem; `fontSize` 0.8125 rem); prebuilt themes dark / neobrutalism / shadcn / shadesOfPurple. Logomark: three-arc form, purple-300 upper arc + purple-500 dot/lower arc, min 18 px.
- **Reference / source:** Clerk, Inc. — clerk.com; sources named in the file: clerk.com/brand-assets, clerk.com/docs (customization/appearance), `@clerk/themes`.
- **Best for:** The closest register in this range to a premium trades homepage: tight-tracked headings, mono eyebrow tags, layered soft shadows, spring values for content swaps and drawers, and a concrete-numbers copy voice ("50,000 MRU", "$20/mo") that maps well onto review counts and price bands. ## ⟦S0591⟧ Kaizen Design System — Part 16 — Design.md brand skills (ui-skills.com)
- **What it is:** Culture Amp's Kaizen design system as a full DESIGN.md: token architecture (purple brand, semantic colours, type, base-8 spacing, radius, z-index) plus complete per-component specs — base styles, variants, interaction-state tables and props — for ~45 React Aria components.
- **How it looks:** Friendly, accessible enterprise UI: white surfaces with chunky 2 px borders (`#e1e2ea`) and 7 px default corners, purple primary buttons, Inter for UI with a serif (Tiempos Headline) reserved for display moments. Big calm display type (72 px hero) over a strict token scale; every state (hover, pressed, focus-visible, invalid, disabled) visibly and consistently rendered.
- **Frame by frame:** Mostly micro-transitions at 150 ms ease-in-out (buttons, fields, cards, tabs, links). The sequenced moves: Modal — trigger: open → overlay (rgba(0,0,0,0.5), blur 2 px) fades in while the panel goes opacity 0 → 1 and scale 0.95 → 1 over 200 ms; close reverses at 150 ms. Notification — trigger: appears → slides in from the right (translateX 100% → 0 + fade) over 300 ms; dismisses back out over 200 ms; auto-dismiss default 5000 ms for success/info only. Popover — opens opacity 0 → 1, scale 0.95 → 1 in 150 ms, closes in 100 ms. Collapsible — height 0 → auto over 200 ms. Toggle — thumb slides translateX 2 px → 22 px over 200 ms. Loading spinner — continuous rotate, 1 s linear infinite.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Stack: React 18+, TypeScript 5+, React Aria, CSS-variable tokens, WCAG 2.1 AA (text 4.5:1, large text/UI 3:1). Brand purple 100–800 with `primary` = purple-500; semantic blue/green/yellow/red/orange; `border-default` `#e1e2ea`, focus border = blue-500; data-viz pair `#7dd5bd` / `#e68d97` (colourblind-safe). Type (modular scale 1.25): display-0 72/84 w800, heading-1 34/42 w500, h2 28/36, h3 22/30, h4 18/24, h5 16/24, h6 14/24 (all w600), body-large 20/30, body 16/24, body-small 14/18, body-xs 12/18; button-primary 18/24 w500, label 14/24 w600. Spacing base-8 tokens 0/4/8/12/16/24/32/48/64/96 px (+ xs 6, sm 12, md 24, lg 36, xl 48). Breakpoints: mobile <48 em, tablet 48–64 em, desktop >64 em; 12-column grid, mobile-first. Z-index: 0 / 1 / 10 / 100 / 1000 / 10000. Shadows: 4 qualitative levels (0 none → 3 modals). Radius: none 0, sm 4, md 7 (default), lg 10, xl 16, full 9999. Components: Button padding 12×24 (medium), focus outline 2 px + 2 px offset, disabled primary → gray-300; TextField 2 px border, padding 12×16; Card 2 px border, padding 24; Table header on secondary surface, selected row purple-100; Modal widths — generic 600 px, confirmation 480 px, input 720 px, padding 32/24, z 1000; Tooltip dark gray-600, max-width 250 px, delay 300 ms, z 10000; Checkbox/Radio 20 px; Toggle track 44×24, thumb 18 px; Slider track 4 px, thumb 20 px (scale 1.1 while dragging); Avatar 24/40/64 px, groups overlap 8 px, maxVisible default 3; Text max-widths 975/780/680/600 px by size; Container 640/1024/1280/100%; Calendar cells 40×40; touch targets ≥44×44 px. Tag component is deprecated in favour of Badge (count badge hides at 0, "max+" default 99).
- **Reference / source:** Culture Amp — github.com/cultureamp/kaizen-design-system (named at the foot of the file).
- **Best for:** The range's deepest form-component state tables — quote forms, multi-step (Workflow) indicators, Likert/rating inputs, date pickers — with every state spelled out, plus an accessibility checklist that transfers to any build. Enterprise-app register; borrow the state discipline and component values, not the brand skin.
