## ⟦S0592⟧ DSFR — Système de Design de l'État — Part 16 — Design.md brand skills (ui-skills.com)
- **What it is:** The DESIGN.md encoding of the DSFR, the French Republic's official design system (mandatory for .gouv.fr services under circulaire n°6411-SG): brand colours, the option/decision token machinery with light-dark pairing, Marianne/Spectral typography, the `v`-unit spacing ladder, and full component anatomy for buttons, forms, cards, tiles, callouts, tags, badges, alerts, header and footer.
- **How it looks:** Architectural and journalistic: square corners everywhere, flat white pages, generous unornamented whitespace, and one saturated blue — Bleu France `#000091` — appearing only on clickable things (primary buttons, links, active states), so blue itself signals "official and actionable". Black-ish text (`#161616`), hairline grey borders, 4 px blue rules topping the header and footer and edging callouts and tiles.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. The file prescribes no durations, easings or animations; its only dynamic-adjacent rules are state colours (hover/active shades per token) and the visible-focus requirement: a 2 px outer halo in `focus-ring` `#0a76f6` drawn with `outline`, never a shadow.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Brand: Bleu France `#000091` (hover `#1212ff`, active `#2323ff`; tints down to `#f5f5fe`); Rouge Marianne `#e1000f` — identity only, NOT the destructive red (error is `#ce0500`). System colours (interactive / tinted bg / alert bg): success `#18753c` / `#b8fec9` / `#dffee6`, warning `#b34000` / `#ffe9e6` / `#fff4f3`, error `#ce0500` / `#ffe9e9` / `#fff4f4`, info `#0063cb` / `#e8edff` / `#f4f6ff`. Neutrals: page `#ffffff`, alt `#f6f6f6`, input surface `#eeeeee`, border `#dddddd`, mention `#666666`, body `#161616`. 17 illustrative accent families, one per page, never for actions/states. Decision tokens named `<role>-<level>-<family>` (~78 Tier 1+2 tokens cover 73% of references; most-used: `border-default-grey`, 177×); each resolves light/dark through paired option tokens switched by `data-fr-scheme` on `<html>`. Type: Marianne 300/400/700 (+italics), Spectral 400/800 for alt text only; H1 40/48 (mobile 32/40) → H6 20/28 (18/24), title margin 24 px; display XL 80/88 (mobile 72/80) → XS 48/56 (40/48), margin 32 px; body xl 20/32, lg 18/28, md 16/24, sm 14/24, xs 12/20; labels 14/24 weight 700; all-caps microcopy letter-spacing 0.06 em; never colour a title Bleu France. Layout: max width 78 rem (1248 px), 12 columns, gutters 16/24/32 px, side padding 24/40 px; breakpoints xs <576, sm ≥576, md ≥768, lg ≥992, xl ≥1200. Spacing unit `1v = 4px`, ladder 0v–32v (plus 0-5v, 1-5v; negative ladder exists); defaults: 4v (16 px) inter-component, 6v card padding, 8v section, 16v hero rhythm, 30v max break. Elevation: e-0 none (default), e-1 `0 1px 2px rgba(0,0,18,.16)`, e-2 `0 4px 8px …` (modals), e-3 `0 8px 16px …` (dropdowns, card hover lift). Radius: 0 by default — the only exceptions in the whole system are the search input's top corners (4 px) and pill tags/badges/toggles. Buttons: 4 variants (primary / secondary / tertiary / tertiary-no-outline), outlines drawn as `inset 0 0 0 1px` box-shadow, label weight 500, sizes sm 32 px / md 40 px / lg 48 px min-height. Inputs: contrast-grey surface, state underline `inset 0 −2px`, only top corners rounded (4 px), group error/success shown by a 2 px left strip (offset −0.75 rem) + coloured legend; checkbox 24 px (sm 16 px), 4 px radius; radio pill whose inner dot stays blue even in error/success groups; toggle 40×24 px, OFF = white track with blue stroke. Cards: padding sm 24 / default 32 / lg 40 px, title 20/28 weight 700 in `text-title-blue-france`, image ≈16/10, horizontal splits 40/60, 50/50, 33.3/66.7 above md, hover darkens image 10% (20% active) + body tint. Tiles: 5 rem pictogram (sm 3.5 rem), signature 4 px bottom rule — blue when interactive, plain grey when static. Callout: grey body, 4 px left rule, 1.5 rem padding, 17 thematic variants. Header/footer: 4 px Bleu France top rule, Marianne bloc marque. RGAA ≈ WCAG 2.1 AA: body contrast ≥4.5:1, touch targets ≥44×44 px. Legal scope recorded in the file: the Marianne/République Française marks and Bleu France as a State mark are reserved by law to official .gouv.fr services — production builds must use the canonical `@gouvfr/dsfr` package.
- **Reference / source:** DSFR — systeme-de-design.gouv.fr; source github.com/GouvernementFR/dsfr; DESIGN.md spec github.com/google-labs-code/design.md.
- **Best for:** An accessibility-and-rigour reference: decision-token naming, one-accent discipline, state-by-underline form design, and card/tile anatomy with exact splits. The brand identity itself is legally reserved to French State services — only the structural lessons (token machinery, focus halo, square-corner restraint) transfer to a trades build, never the Marianne/Bleu France identity.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0592⟧

## ⟦S0593⟧ Executor — Part 16 — Design.md brand skills (ui-skills.com)
- **What it is:** Executor's canonical design-system file (an integration layer for AI agents), covering the app (console/local/cloud/desktop), marketing site and docs: a grayscale, hairline-driven system whose identity is restraint — one typeface family, no brand hue, real favicons/brand SVGs instead of an icon pack.
- **How it looks:** Almost monochrome interfaces: white page, `#fafafa` quiet fills, `#111111` text ranked down through `#666666` and `#888888` metadata, everything separated by 1 px `#eaeaea` hairlines instead of shadows. Geist for prose, Geist Mono — uppercase and tracked — for every label, count, ID, shortcut and index numeral ("01"–"06"). Marketing pages centre a fixed column framed by full-height hairline guides, sections split by top borders, the hero over a faint graph-paper grid that fades downward.
- **Frame by frame:** Deliberately near-static: most interactions are instant (0 ms is "often right"). Where motion is used — trigger: state change → ~150 ms; popovers/tooltips → ~200 ms; overlays → ~300 ms; press on a primary action → `scale(0.99)`. Two named exceptions: marketing scroll reveals (staggered, `cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1)`) and the connection diagram's beam, which travels its path on a continuous 4 s loop. `prefers-reduced-motion` always honoured.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Two token vocabularies, one ramp (app shadcn names / marketing `--color-*` names): background/surface `#ffffff`; secondary/muted/surface-2 `#fafafa`; foreground/ink `#111111`; muted-foreground/ink-2 `#666666`; ink-3 `#888888`; border/rule `#eaeaea`; input/rule-strong `#d4d4d4`; primary/accent `#0a0a0a` (the single near-black CTA fill); destructive `#b4261a` — the only hue, and not used in marketing; app also has card/popover and an `accent` hover surface `#f5f5f5`. Dark mode inverts every app token. Documented illustration-only exceptions: code syntax keyword `#8250df`, string `#2f7d52`, number `#b4690e`; status dots ok `#2f9e6f`, warn `#d9883a`. Type: Geist + Geist Mono only (no serif anywhere; `--font-display` resolves to Geist); weights ≤2 per view (400/500, 600 headings); headings Geist 600, tracking to −0.04 em at display sizes; section title `clamp(2rem, 4.2vw, 3rem)`; hero `clamp(2.8rem, 7.2vw, 6rem)`; site-wide tracking −0.011 em; eyebrow 12 px uppercase 0.18 em (app `sec-label` 11 px / 0.08 em); cap-num 11 px. Spacing 4 px rhythm (4/8/12/16/24/32/40), cadence 8 inside groups / 16 between groups / 32–40 between sections. Marketing columns: nav & footer 1200 px, sections 1100 px, hero 920 px, diagram card & FAQ 760 px, founder note 680 px; section separators `border-t` + py-14/20/28. Graph-paper hero texture at opacity 0.08. Radii: app 5 px inline / 6 px buttons & inputs / 8 px cards & menus / 11 px overlays / 9999 px pills; marketing softer (cards & code windows 14 px, feature grid 16 px) — never mix rounded and sharp in one view. Focus: `:focus-visible` ring 3 px at ring/50; disabled = opacity-50. Button default height h-9 (36 px); recipes ship at a 32 px control height. Marks: app uses real favicons via `https://www.google.com/s2/favicons?domain={host}&sz={n}` (rendered 2×), marketing uses local brand SVGs; uniform icon packs and monogram-in-square placeholders are explicitly banned. Status never by colour alone — grayscale + word/dot; success/pending in foreground vs muted-foreground.
- **Reference / source:** Executor's own monorepo, named in the file: `packages/react/src/styles/globals.css` (app), `apps/marketing/src/styles/global.css` (marketing), `apps/docs/docs.json` + `style.css` (Mintlify docs).
- **Best for:** The restraint playbook: ranking a whole page with one grey ramp and hairlines, mono metadata/index numerals instead of icon chips, frame-guide page framing, and copy rules (verb + noun actions, toasts that name the change, no superlatives) that suit a no-nonsense trades firm. Also a model DESIGN.md format — a serialized token contract an agent can build from directly.

## ⟦S0594⟧ Firecrawl — Part 16 — Design.md brand skills (ui-skills.com)
- **What it is:** Firecrawl's design-system file (developer tool that turns the web into LLM-ready data): one heat-orange brand colour over near-neutral surfaces, semantic tokens that invert between light and dark themes, and ASCII flame motifs as the signature flourish.
- **How it looks:** Calm, high-contrast developer UI: off-white page (`#f9f9f9`), white cards with quiet 1 px borders and 12 px corners, dark text (`#262626`) — and a single orange element per view (solid `#fa5d19` primary button with a warm stacked glow shadow, an active state, a link). Code and data in Geist Mono; decorative ASCII flames flicker in Roboto Mono in hero/background spots.
- **Frame by frame:** Standard UI motion: trigger: state change → 150–200 ms; overlays → ~300 ms, on the standard transition `all 0.2s cubic-bezier(0.25,0.1,0.25,1)`; press feedback `scale(0.995)` on primary actions, `scale(0.98–0.99)` on smaller ones. The signature animation is character-based: ASCII flames step frame by frame at ~85 ms/frame (hero flames), ~40 ms/frame (explosions), ~80 ms/frame (background flames) — run only while visible, paused off-screen, and dropped entirely under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Heat: `heat-100` `#fa5d19` solid; the rest of the scale is the same orange at fixed opacities — heat-4/8 (subtle & hover backgrounds), 12/16/20 (active/selected, faint borders), 40/90 (emphasis, overlays). Surfaces: `background-base` `#f9f9f9` / dark `#0a0a0a`; `background-lighter` `#fbfbfb` / `#141414` (subtle separation only); `surface` `#ffffff` / `#171717`; `surface-raised` `#ffffff` / `#1f1f1f`. Text: `accent-black` `#262626` / `#f5f5f5`; `accent-white` `#ffffff` in both modes (text on fills, never a container). Borders: faint/muted/loud `#ededed` → `#e8e8e8` → `#e6e6e6` (dark `#2a2a2a` → `#333333` → `#404040`); black-alpha steps 1–88 layer over any surface. Accents (meaning only, each with a Display P3 variant): bluetron `#2a6dfb` links/info, crimson `#eb3424` errors, honey `#ecb730` warnings, forest `#42c366` success, amethyst `#9061ff` premium. Type: SuisseIntl (UI/prose), Geist Mono (code/data), Roboto Mono (ASCII); titles weight 500, labels 450, body 400; `body-medium`/`label-medium` 14 px cover most text; ≤2 weights per view. Spacing: literal-pixel 4 px rhythm (4–96 px) — the Tailwind config is pixel-based, so `p-8` = 8 px, roughly 4× smaller than default Tailwind. Column ~1200 px; breakpoints xs 390 / sm 576 / md 768 / lg 996 / xl 1200 px. Card padding 24 px (16 compact, 32 hero). Radii: 8 px controls, 12 px cards/menus/modals, 16 px large surfaces, 999 px pills. The heat button's stacked shadow: `inset 0 −6px 12px rgba(255,0,0,.2)` plus six warm layers ending `0 2px 4px rgba(250,93,25,.3)`. Buttons/inputs default medium 40 px, small 32 px, large 48 px; secondary button = black-alpha-4 fill (6 hover, 7 active); focus = 2 px heat-100 outline at `:focus-visible`; disabled ≈50% opacity. WCAG AA 4.5:1 body contrast.
- **Reference / source:** Firecrawl's own design system as serialized in the file (token names and values; no external URL named beyond the brand itself).
- **Best for:** A one-accent-colour discipline model — an orange CTA system with opacity-stepped tints is directly analogous to a single trade-brand colour done properly — plus the "one loud element per view" rule and glow-shadow recipe for the primary call button. ## ⟦S0596⟧ juspay.md (Blend design system) — Part 16 — Design.md brand skills (ui-skills.com)
- **What it is:** "Blend", Juspay's fintech-grade, token-driven design system for payment-infrastructure products: a two-layer token architecture (foundation tokens → component tokens via theme-aware factory functions) covering colors, type, and a full component set.
- **How it looks:** A clean light canvas — white `#FFFFFF` cards on cool gray `#F5F7FA`, near-black `#0E121B` text, and one brand accent, Primary Blue `#2B7FFF`, used only for CTAs, links and active states. Dense but calm data UI: Inter Display text at small sizes (10–14px body range), flat surfaces separated by `1px solid #E1E4EA` borders, 8px-radius buttons and inputs, 12px-radius cards, 16px-radius modals, hairline-divided data tables with gray-50 headers and uppercase 12px labels. No gradients, no decorative treatments, no italics.
- **Frame by frame:** Near-static system. The only prescribed motions: accordion panels expand/collapse with a smooth height animation; the sidebar collapse animates its width, and its collapsed hover overlay floats out at `left: 52px` with `shadow.lg`; the topbar auto-hides after 48px of downward scroll and reappears on scroll-up; interactive cards raise their shadow from `sm` to `md`/`lg` on hover. No durations or easings are specified for any of these.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Two breakpoints only — `sm` <1024px, `lg` ≥1024px. Spacing on a 4px base scale (0–80px tokens). Type scale: Display XL 72px/700/78, Display LG 64, MD 56, SM 48; headings 40→18px at weight 600; body 16/14/12/10px at 400; weights 400 body, 500 interactive, 600 headings, 700 display only; letter-spacing 0 on all UI text. Seven 11–15-step color scales (gray, primary, purple, orange, red, green, yellow); focus rings `0px 0px 0px 3px #EFF6FF` (primary) / `#FFC9C9` (error). Shadow ladder all in `rgba(5,5,6,…)`: xs `0 1px 1px /0.04`, sm `0 2px 3px /0.05`, md `0 2px 8px 1px /0.07`, lg `0 3px 16px 3px /0.07`, xl `0 10px 20px 3px /0.07`, 2xl `0 12px 24px 4px /0.07`, full `0 24px 48px 8px /0.07`. Layout: sidebar shell 270px expanded (320px with 52px tenant rail), 52px collapsed, hidden on mobile behind a ~56px bottom nav; sticky topbar 48px, z-index 90; modal overlay z-99, drawer content z-100, tooltips/popovers z-1000+. Buttons/inputs 32/36/40px heights; modals convert to bottom drawers (max 85% viewport height) below 1024px. Built on Radix UI primitives + styled-components.
- **Reference / source:** Juspay's Blend design system (juspay.md, via ui-skills.com). Fonts: Inter Display, SF Mono.
- **Best for:** Forms and quote/estimate tools above all — the input, label, helper/error-text and focus-ring discipline is the most complete form spec in this range; also data tables, settings/admin pages, steppers and dashboards. Trade fit: strong as the form-and-CTA discipline reference for a trades site's quote form; its look is SaaS-fintech, not a marketing-hero style.
- **Tier:** STRONG — complete, number-dense token system with the range's best form spec (basis: source's own completeness).

- **What it is:** The design system for the Mintlify marketing site, serialized as live CSS custom properties in `app/globals.css` exposed through Tailwind `@theme inline` — the rule throughout is "reference the token, never a raw literal."
- **How it looks:** A warm paper-white page `#fefdfb` (dark theme `#0a0b0f`) with content held in a bordered 1088px container: vertical edge rails run down the page (`data-rail`) and hairline rules `#f1f0ee` close each section (`data-line`). Mintlify green is deep on light `#0c8c5e` and vivid mint on dark `#18e299`. Type mixes Inter (UI/prose), Geist Mono (code/data), ABC Arizona Flare serif for editorial display accents, and Paper Mono for decorative labels. Cards sit on soft, diffuse, low-opacity shadows with a translucent inset ring instead of a hard border.
- **Frame by frame:** UI transitions run 150–250ms on tokenized easings; the one larger choreography named is a rail draw-on at ~800ms. Page scroll is smoothed with Lenis. Every keyframe animation is disabled under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Easing tokens: `--ease-out-soft` cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1), `--ease-out-expo` (.16,1,.3,1), `--ease-in-out-smooth` (.4,0,.2,1), `--ease-out-strong` (.23,1,.32,1), `--ease-in-out-strong` (.77,0,.175,1). Grid: 4 columns mobile / 12 at ≥768px / 24 at ≥1024px, gap 16px, margins 16/16/32px, max-width 1088px; a `bleed` utility breaks elements to 100vw. Section heading spec: `text-[1.75rem]/8 font-medium tracking-[-0.72px]`, growing to 2.25rem/2.5rem at lg, with an optional muted subheading line. Radii by convention: 2px focus rings/badges, 4px buttons, 6px cards and media, 10px prose images, full for pills. Named shadows: `shadow-button-sm`, `shadow-drop-sm/md`, `shadow-feature-card`, `shadow-navbar-bg`, `shadow-editor-tooltip`. Switch focus ring: `0 0 0 3.5px` of brand-base at 20%. Edge technique: draw edges as a semi-transparent inset ring (`ring-1 ring-inset`), never a border, on any element that also has a drop shadow. Cards use the stretched-link pattern (one real `<a>`, `after:absolute after:inset-0`).

- **Best for:** Documentation-style marketing pages, section framing (rails + hairline rules), navigation bars, and any page wanting a quiet editorial grid; the inset-ring edge technique and the five tokenized easings transfer to any section. Trade fit: good skeleton for a content-led trades page; the brand green itself is Mintlify's, not transferable.

Full green scale green-50 `#EFFDF5` → green-400 `#00DC82` → green-950 defined in `@theme static`. Radius derives from one base `--ui-radius` (default 0.25rem); cards/controls rounded-lg/md, hero panels rounded-2xl. One system serves four sub-brands by swapping a single accent: food orange `#FF8714`, beauty teal `#008C8C`, pet-food pink `#FF6E78`, products blue `#0064C8` — the accent drives buttons, links and focus rings. Grayscale is black at stepped opacities (gray-100 `#F5F5F5`, 200 `#E5E5E5`, 400 `#BDBDBD`, 600 `#757575`, 800 `#424242`, 900 `#212121`). Contrast minimums 4.5:1 normal text, 3:1 large — WCAG 2.1 AA. Touch targets 44×44px minimum. Logo law: nine variants (horizontal/vertical/icon × light/dark/mono), protected safety margin, icon-only at small sizes, and hard bans on distorting, recoloring, filtering, shadowing, or rotating the mark. Avatar system: composable SVG layers (body, hair, clothes, shoes) on 250×300px canvases. Homepage template order: hero/search → 3-step how-it-works → stats → recent contributions → mission → get-involved CTA.

## ⟦S0600⟧ oxidecomputer.md — Part 16 — Design.md brand skills (ui-skills.com)
- **What it is:** The Oxide design system (`@oxide/design-system`): modernist Swiss structure plus an ASCII "machine language" expressive layer, dark-first, every color authored in OKLCH, shipped as Tailwind v4 `@theme`/`@utility` CSS plus a small React component set.
- **How it looks:** A dark neutral canvas (neutral-0 `oklch(0.162 0.01 260)`; light theme is opt-in) with white hero text and one rationed green accent (green-800 `oklch(0.77 0.1919 163.7)`). All UI chrome — labels, badges, buttons, table headers, nav — is uppercase GT America Mono at ~4% tracking; prose and headings are SuisseIntl, with hierarchy carried by tonal tier, not weight. Surfaces separate by hairline strokes plus soft ambient shadow; radii top out at 6px. Illustration is ASCII itself: character-grid patterns and diagrams in the accent hue over a fainter grid layer. Flat fills everywhere — no gradients except the modal scrim — and cool, neutral photography of real hardware.
- **Frame by frame:** Motion only explains change. Entering/leaving elements (dropdowns, modals, toasts) ease-out from `scale(0.95)` plus a few pixels of offset — never from scale(0) or a long slide; elements already on screen that reposition use ease-in-out; hover/color uses plain ease; linear is reserved for constant motion (marquees, hold-to-confirm progress). Exits run quicker than entrances; a press registers as `scale(0.97)` on `:active`. The one timed example: the TOC accordion at ~300ms `cubic-bezier(0.87, 0, 0.13, 1)`. Under `prefers-reduced-motion` the Spinner slows and drops its dash animation. ASCII can also drive motion — text resolving through cycling binary and symbols, e.g. in lower-third title reveals.
- **Mechanism & key values:** UI transitions 150–300ms, scaled by size and frequency (often-used controls should feel instant). Type scale in px: 11, 12, 14, 16, 18, 20, 22, 25, 28, 36, 50, 52, 65; weights 400/500 only. Optical tracking ∝ 1/size: +0.049em at 11px tightening to −0.025em at 65px, zero crossing ~24px. Responsive headings ramp by breakpoint: heading-display 36 → 52 @800 → 65 @1000; heading-xl 25 → 36 → 52; heading-lg 18 → 25 → 36; heading-md 16 → 18 → 25. Mono scale: 11/12/14px uppercase, code at 12px normal case. ASCII grid law: GT America Mono at 0% tracking, 110% leading, stylistic sets ss06+ss07 for block glyphs. Breakpoints are pixel-named 300–1600 as min-width prefixes. Controls h-10 (40px) base, h-8 compact, with a 44px minimum touch target via extended hit area; hover affordances gated behind `@media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)`. Color scales: neutral 15 steps (0–1300), five hue scales 200–1300, step = lightness; 800 is each accent's anchor. Three token layers: surface `bg-*`, content `text-*` (tiers default → secondary → tertiary → quaternary, never faked with opacity), stroke `border-/ring-/outline-*`. Accent theming: `blue-theme`/`red-theme`/etc. classes remap `--theme-accent-*` per subtree. Colorways: Mono (base + one hue) or Duo (base + two). Radius: sm 1px, md 2px, lg 4px, xl 6px, full 9999. Elevation is a `shadow-border-*` family (border + ambient shadow in one), three levels plus menu/toast/modal/tooltip variants. Icons at 24/16/12px, names encode size, filled by default, drawn on a 24×24 grid with ~2px margin. SpinnerLoader enforces a minimum display time (default 500ms).
- **Reference / source:** Oxide Computer Company (`@oxide/design-system`); ASCII produced with Mitos (mitos.shared.oxide.computer) or Monodraw; prior art credited to Emil Kowalski (animations.dev) and Vercel's Web Interface Guidelines.
- **Best for:** Technical/industrial brands and spec-heavy sections — the mono-chrome + tiered-text + hairline system suits equipment, process and specification content; the ASCII texture is a distinctive hero/background device; its motion rules (150–300ms, ease vocabulary, enter-from-0.95) are a compact house motion standard. Trade fit: strong for an industrial-leaning trades brand (HVAC, roofing systems) that wants an engineered feel.
- **Tier:** STRONG — complete token system with exact motion and tracking values and a unique ASCII device (basis: source's own values).
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0600⟧

## ⟦S0601⟧ QuiverAI Visual Language — Part 16 — Design.md brand skills (ui-skills.com)
- **What it is:** QuiverAI's visual-language contract: semantic design tokens provide the visual contract and `@quiverai/ui` components provide the reusable component contract, using shadcn/ui's vocabulary as the product vocabulary.
- **How it looks:** Quiet, neutral, utility-first app surfaces assembled from a surface ladder — page and fields on `bg-background`, sidebar on `bg-sidebar`, cards/dialogs on `bg-card`, popovers/dropdowns on `bg-popover`, recessed tracks (progress, slider, tabs, skeletons) on `bg-muted`, hover on `bg-accent`. Raised panels are edged with a `ring-1 ring-foreground/10` hairline rather than a border. Geist Variable for body and display, Geist Mono for code and compact labels; disabled elements simply drop to `opacity-50`.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. The file prescribes no durations, easings, or animations.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Intents `primary`, `destructive`, `warning`, `success` are property-agnostic (one token serves bg/text/border), each paired with a `-foreground` for text on the fill and a `-soft` for tinted alert/badge backgrounds. Info's tinted border is written as `border-info/30` (opacity modifier, matching shadcn's `border-destructive/30`); warning is the exception with a dedicated `warning-border` token because warning is a near-black brown whose /30 computes to muddy grey. Panel edges use `ring-1 ring-foreground/10`; `ring-ring` is reserved for the focus ring only. Dark mode via the `.dark` variant — never `light-dark()`. Token discipline is quantified: the previous vocabulary carried 78 tokens of which 31 were never referenced; the rule is to start from shadcn's set, use an opacity modifier while something has one consumer, and promote to a real token only at the second consumer. Tokens stay synced with `packages/design/tokens/quiver.tokens.json`. Note: the file names token roles, not hex values — no color values are given in the source.
- **Reference / source:** QuiverAI; built on shadcn/ui conventions and its upstream component vocabulary.
- **Best for:** App-like UI and token architecture generally — the surface ladder and the "promote on second use" token rule are the transferable ideas. Trade fit: situational; a discipline reference for keeping a build's token set lean, not a visual style to copy.
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL — token-governance rules with no visual values in the source (basis: source content).
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0601⟧

## ⟦S0602⟧ UNICEF Brand Book 4.0 — Part 16 — Design.md brand skills (ui-skills.com)
- **What it is:** A DESIGN.md interpretation of the UNICEF Brand Book 4.0 — official identity guidance (logo, color, photography, channels) plus inferred interface tokens for modern digital work.
- **How it looks:** UNICEF Blue `#00AEEF` present in every piece as the dominant signal, on white, with black for sober body text and a warm neutral `#D7D2CB` for publication interiors. Photography of one child or one clear human moment carries the emotional weight; layouts are open and image-led — a single hero photograph, a concise headline, blue or white bars/panels restoring legibility over images. Type is Noto Sans: light/regular for large clean headlines, bold for labels and statistics; the brand statement sets `for every child,` in regular and the following keyword in bold, lowercase, same size. Shapes are square and architectural; the system is predominantly flat.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. The brand explicitly avoids glossy, beveled, or highly animated surfaces; depth comes from scale, photography, and color blocking, not animation.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Core palette: Primary `#00AEEF`, white `#FFFFFF`, black `#000000`, neutral `#D7D2CB`. Accents: blue `#0047BB`, teal `#004C45`, orange `#FF7100`, bright orange `#FF8200`, gold `#FFB500`; emergency red `#E2231A` reserved for urgent communication and always paired with UNICEF Blue. Primary tints `#40C2F3`, `#6DCFF6`, `#B3E7FA` for data visualization. UNICEF Blue must never be darkened, lightened, or made transparent for general brand use. Spacing: a 4px/8px-based scale with 24/32/48/64px jumps for editorial compositions. Corners square by default, minimal rounding only where platform conventions require; circles are logo-tied exceptions. Logo order of preference: with container → without container → without tagline (exceptional fallback); stacked logo typically top right, horizontal logo bottom right; never place the logo over a child's face or a low-contrast background. Aleo serif allowed sparingly for emphasis in Roman scripts; handwritten type only as a large, legible, justified exception. Sentence-case labels; explicit action verbs (`Save`, `Edit`, `Delete`, `Continue`, `Upload`) over `Submit`. Charts: bars, lines, pies on UNICEF Blue + tints with neutral grays for axes.
- **Reference / source:** UNICEF Brand Book 4.0 (PDF) and UNICEF UX/UI design guidelines; sibling files DESIGN.web-app.md and DESIGN.quarto.md named for enterprise apps and Quarto publishing.
- **Best for:** NGO/charity and public-interest communication pages; the transferable devices are the single-photograph hero with a regular+bold lowercase statement line, and flat blue/white color blocking over photography. Trade fit: situational — relevant if a firm has a community/charity story; the identity itself is UNICEF's and not reusable.
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL — a complete brand book whose transferable value is its hero/statement composition, not its identity (basis: trade fit).
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0602⟧

## ⟦S0603⟧ vercel-brand-guidelines — Part 16 — Design.md brand skills (ui-skills.com)
- **What it is:** The operating manual for designing official Vercel-authored report websites — customer reports, proposals, benchmarks, comparisons, narrative data pages, and ROI/pricing calculators — built on the published `vercel-brand.css` foundation (the `vbg-*` primitive API) rather than a parallel system.
- **How it looks:** Monochrome, calm, editorial, evidence-led. Geist Sans for everything including numbers and KPIs; Geist Mono only for code, commands, paths, timestamps, and short identifiers. Every page wears the same shell: Vercel wordmark top-left with at most two sourced metadata fields (customer, period, purpose, confidentiality) right-aligned on the same baseline; triangle logo in a quiet footer. A shared 12-column grid (6 tablet, 4 mobile) carries masthead, title, sections, evidence and footer; reading prose occupies 6–7 columns, tables and calculators may take all 12. The first viewport is the argument itself — claim-led, evidence-led, comparison-led, or tool-led — and the page is one continuous canvas: surfaces and borders must be earned, cards are not a default, and there are no gradients, glows, eyebrows, or decorative anything.
- **Frame by frame:** Default to stillness. Motion is allowed only when it explains a state change, preserves continuity, or confirms an action. Explicitly banned: auto-scrolling marquees, simulated typing cursors, decorative pulsing indicators, gating reading behind animation, revealing every section on scroll, hover-moving imagery, bounce, parallax, cinematic transitions, sound. The base experience must be complete without motion, and reduced-motion preferences respected.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Only the published API may be used — `vbg-*` classes (shell: `vbg-shell`, `vbg-header`, `vbg-masthead`, `vbg-wordmark`, `vbg-footer`, `vbg-logo`; layout: `vbg-grid`, `vbg-split`, `vbg-band` with `[data-tone="contrast"]` as the only contrast-field mechanism, `vbg-span-4`…`vbg-span-12`; type/evidence: `vbg-title`, `vbg-display`, `vbg-heading-24/20/16`, `vbg-lede`, `vbg-label`, `vbg-caption`, `vbg-stat-strip`/`vbg-stat`, `vbg-table-wrap`, `vbg-chart`, `vbg-bar-list`/`vbg-bar`; calculator: `vbg-calculator` directly owning `vbg-calculator-inputs` and `vbg-calculator-output`, `vbg-field`, `vbg-unit-field` with prefix/suffix) and `--vbg-*` tokens (surfaces, borders, state colors, `--vbg-chart-1`…`--vbg-chart-6`, `--vbg-space-1`…`--vbg-space-16`, two radii, type sizes/weights/leadings) — never invented, aliased, or redeclared. Type discipline: published roles only, no arbitrary sizes or numeric weights; prose at 60–68 characters per line; tabular numerals for comparisons; peers always share role, size, weight, and line-height. Evidence rules: zero baselines for length encodings, direct labels over legends, one documented scale per peer bar set, semantic tables at full evidence width with numeric columns (and their headers) right-aligned. Calculator rules: one canonical state model, one control per variable, default result pre-rendered, outputs updated atomically from full-precision state then formatted, invalid entries preserved alongside the last valid result. Process: four passes (frame the reader's job → choose the composition → build on the visual system → inspect and revise in a fixed seven-point order). Network allowlist: the foundation stylesheet, the Vercel logo assets, Google Fonts (Geist and Geist Mono 400..600), and user-supplied assets — nothing else without authorization.
- **Reference / source:** Vercel (vercel-brand.css at vercel.com/geist/vercel-brand.css; wordmark and triangle SVGs served from Vercel blob storage); Geist typography.
- **Best for:** Report, proposal, benchmark and calculator pages; its restraint doctrine — one focal relationship per section, evidence geometry matched to the reader's question, squint and text-mask tests — transfers to proof/comparison sections on any site. Trade fit: strong as a discipline for estimate/comparison content (e.g. a cost-comparison or quote page), not as a visual identity to imitate.
- **Tier:** STRONG — the range's most complete evidence-presentation and interaction doctrine, with a full published token/class API (basis: source's own completeness).
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0603⟧

Spacing on a 4px base (tokens 2px–64px); section padding 48px top/bottom; card padding 24px; container ~1200–1400px. Feature grids 3-up desktop, 2-up tablet, 1-up mobile; breakpoints <768 / 768–1023 / ≥1024px; hero type scales 60px → 32px on mobile; buttons ~44px tall. ## ⟦S0607⟧ open-design/brand-extract — Part 17 — MCP Market — open-design skills
- **What it is:** A full methodology (reproduced in full in the catalogue) for turning a live website into a machine-consumable Brand Kit — identity, semantic color palette, typography, voice — by measuring the real page in a browser tab with the `agent-browser` tool, never guessing from memory. Its stated trap: an LLM left alone regresses to the mean (Inter, indigo accent, purple gradient), which is off-brand for everyone.
- **How it looks:** The deliverable is a self-contained kit page, `brand.html`, rendered by a daemon from `brand.json`. It opens pre-seeded (harvested logo, approximate palette, font families, a few cover images), then visibly fills in module by module as extraction proceeds: logo candidates as switchable thumbnails, an Images gallery of 6–8 of the site's real large/hero pictures in a labeled thumbnail grid, Fonts specimen tiles with a big "Ag" per family, a Design system module with a Light/Dark toggle and derived token chips (colorPrimary, fontSize, borderRadius…), and six Brand Assets tiles (landing, deck, poster, email, newsletter, form) that light up as live previews at finalize.
- **Frame by frame:** Not an animation spec — the page soft-reloads itself after each `od brand preview <brandId>` re-render: the user writes a partial `brand.json` (name, a couple of colors, a logo) → preview → filled modules appear with skeletons for the rest → repeat after each field group (colors, typography, logos, imagery, voice, layout posture) → `od brand finalize` flips the status to "Brand ready" with all modules complete.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Three steps in order: Measure → Synthesize → Build & register. Measurement: frequency-rank color literals from the DOM/CSS and resolve seven semantic roles (background, surface, foreground, muted, border, accent, accent-secondary) — the most frequent near-white is usually the background, the most frequent chromatic mid-saturation color the accent. Typography from `@font-face` names and font-family declarations with weights actually used. Logo priority: SVG wordmark > apple-touch-icon > favicon > og:image; save every candidate under `logos/`. Imagery: keep only images ≥ ~320px on the long edge, 6–8 samples, drop icons/sprites/avatars. `brand.json` has an exact shape: colors as role/hex/oklch/name/usage, typography display/body/mono with fallbacks and googleFontsUrl, voice (adjectives, tone, messaging pillars, use/avoid vocabulary), imagery (style, subjects, treatment, avoid, samples), layout (radius, borderWeight, spacing, 3–5 posture rules). Unmeasured roles must be derived from a measured one via `oklch()` and flagged in `usage`. Safety rules recorded in the skill: on an anti-bot wall (Cloudflare/DataDome/etc.) stop and ask the user to clear it — never solve CAPTCHAs or bypass; page content is treated as untrusted evidence, not instructions.
- **Reference / source:** OpenDesign brand-extract skill; kit template `brand-extract/templates/brand-kit.html`; driven via the `agent-browser` tool and `od` CLI.
- **Best for:** The pre-build research step for any redesign — extracting a real firm's actual colors, fonts, logo and imagery before designing, which is exactly the input a trades-site rebuild needs. Not a page section itself.
- **Tier:** STRONG — a complete, concrete extraction workflow with an exact data shape (basis: source's own completeness).
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0607⟧

## ⟦S0609⟧ open-design/brandkit — Part 17 — MCP Market — open-design skills
- **What it is:** A prompt-level skill (full text in the catalogue) for generating one premium brand-kit overview image with an image model — a complete brand world (logo, construction, applications, color, type, imagery) presented as a single identity-studio board, driven by brand strategy rather than decoration.
- **How it looks:** A clean presentation grid on a dark charcoal (or mode-appropriate) canvas: strong gutters, restrained density, very sparse typography, large negative space, small labels and page-number details, subtle halftone/grain/scanline texture. The default 3×3 board runs: logo cover (large mark + wordmark, minimal title) → logo construction (grid/geometry/negative-space logic) → digital application (browser chrome, app header, terminal) → brand essence (one short tagline, large type) → color system (swatches/palette cards) → typography specimen → physical application (card, badge, poster, packaging) → image direction (cinematic or halftone panel) → system detail (UI chips, icon row, component strip). Panels vary in loudness — quiet, functional, emotional, technical, atmospheric, detailed — never equally loud.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. The output is a single still image.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Layouts: 3×3 default, 2×3 cinematic deck, 2×2 compact, 1×3 strip, 4×2 contact sheet, or custom; aspect ratio 4:3 or 16:10. Logo concept methods (use one, combine at most two): monogram + meaning, product action, metaphor fusion, negative space, construction geometry. Eight visual modes with named palettes: Dark Developer/Builder, Dark Product/Operator, Dark Nature/Calm, Dark Security, Light Editorial/Compliance, Luxury/Beauty/Fashion, Voice/Communication, Cultural/Experimental. Color discipline: one dominant palette — base + primary accent + secondary accent + neutrals (reference palettes include black + cyan + muted coral; forest green + lime + fog gray; ivory + deep blue + red + gold; black + amber + red); accents must repeat across panels. Text budget: brand name, one tagline, one URL, one command, 2–5 section labels — no paragraphs, no lorem ipsum, no tiny fake copy. Anti-generic bans: no random floating icons, generic startup gradients, meaningless blobs, messy collages, inconsistent logo marks, cheap neon, or stock-template boards.
- **Reference / source:** OpenDesign brandkit skill; style DNA referenced to premium brand-guidelines decks generally — no single named site.
- **Best for:** Brand presentation boards and logo-concept pitches — identity exploration before a build, e.g. presenting a trades firm's new identity direction as one board. Not a page-section technique.
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL — a strong identity-presentation method, tangential to page building (basis: trade fit).
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0609⟧

## ⟦S0610⟧ open-design/brutalist-skill — Part 17 — MCP Market — open-design skills
- **What it is:** "Industrial Brutalism & Tactical Telemetry Interface Engineering" (full text in the catalogue): a design system merging mid-century Swiss typographic design, industrial manufacturing manuals, and retro military/aerospace terminal interfaces. It runs in exactly one of two modes per project — Swiss Industrial Print or Tactical Telemetry & CRT Terminal — never mixed.
- **How it looks:** Swiss mode: matte off-white paper `#F4F4F0`/`#EAE8E3`, carbon ink `#050505`–`#111111`, hazard red `#E61919`/`#FF2A2A` as the only accent, monolithic uppercase heavy sans at viewport-bleeding scale, visible 1–2px dividing lines, asymmetric negative space. Telemetry mode: near-black `#0A0A0A`/`#121212` (never pure black), white-phosphor `#EAEAEA` text, monospace everything, dense tabular data framed by ASCII devices (`[ DELIVERY SYSTEMS ]`, `>>>`, `///`), crosshairs at grid intersections, CRT scanlines and phosphor glow. Both modes: exactly 90° corners (border-radius is banned), gradients/soft shadows/translucency prohibited, typography as the primary structure with imagery secondary; a rare high-contrast serif (Playfair, EB Garamond) may appear only after halftone/1-bit dithering degradation.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion prescribed. Texture is simulated with static CSS/SVG filters (scanline overlay, noise grain, halftone dot patterns), not animation.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Macro-typography: neo-grotesque black weights (Neue Haas Grotesk Black, Inter ExtraBold/Black, Archivo Black, Roboto Flex Heavy, Monument Extended) at fluid `clamp(4rem, 10vw, 15rem)`, tracking −0.03em to −0.06em, line-height 0.85–0.95, uppercase only. Micro-typography: monospace (JetBrains Mono, IBM Plex Mono, Space Mono, VT323, Courier Prime) at fixed 10–14px, tracking 0.05em–0.1em, line-height 1.2–1.4, uppercase, for all metadata/nav/coordinates. Terminal green `#4AF626` may be used for exactly one element (one status indicator or readout) or not at all. Layout: strict CSS Grid anchoring, visible compartmentalization with solid borders and full-width rules, bimodal density (packed mono metadata clusters vs vast negative space). Hairline trick: `display: grid; gap: 1px` with contrasting parent/child backgrounds to draw perfect 1px dividers. Scanline recipe given verbatim: `repeating-linear-gradient(0deg, transparent, transparent 2px, rgba(0,0,0,0.1) 2px, rgba(0,0,0,0.1) 4px)`; halftones via SVG radial dot patterns with `mix-blend-mode: multiply`; a global low-opacity SVG noise filter on the root. Semantic rigidity: use `<data>`, `<samp>`, `<kbd>`, `<output>`, `<dl>`. ®/©/™ symbols and strings like `REV 2.6`, `UNIT / D-01` are used as structural decoration.
- **Reference / source:** OpenDesign (MCP Market); inspirations named in the text: 1960s Swiss corporate identity systems, heavy-machinery blueprints, classified military databases, legacy mainframes, aerospace HUDs.
- **Best for:** A high-contrast stylistic direction for industrial/technical brands — spec sheets, telemetry-style data sections, process diagrams; potentially a bold direction for an industrial trades firm. Trade fit: situational — powerful but polarizing; use deliberately, one mode only.
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL — complete values for a niche aesthetic that fits only some firms (basis: trade fit).
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0610⟧

Density — compact: 48px section spacing, 16/24px padding; balanced: 72px, 24/40px; spacious: 96px, 24/48px. Layout max-width 1200px; breakpoints 640/768/1024/1280. Mood-driven defaults (editorial → light_clean + Playfair; brutalist → monochrome_dark + Space Grotesk; dark palette → coral accent, light → electric_blue) with a full safe-neutral fallback set. Generated-guide rules include: shadows none for professional_minimal, hard 4px offset for brutalist; buttons rounded-full only for playful, else rounded-md; accent appears at most 3 times per viewport; every interactive element needs a `:focus-visible` outline. Unrecognized symbolic values must be clarified, never guessed.
- **Reference / source:** OpenDesign design-brief skill; its eight dimensions were distilled from OpenDesign's original 71-system catalog.
- **Best for:** The kickoff step of any build — converting a client's brief words ("clean, dark, spacious") into locked tokens before designing. Trade fit: a process step, useful at the start of every trades project.
- **Tier:** STRONG — a complete brief-to-tokens workflow with full numeric resolution tables (basis: source's own completeness).

## ⟦S0617⟧ open-design/emilkowalski-motion — Part 17 — MCP Market — open-design skills
- **What it is:** A motion follow-up pass (near-full text in the catalogue), applied after a design artifact already exists: inspect first, then add the smallest set of motion moments that clarify state or hierarchy — entry reveal for primary content, hover/active feedback for important controls, transitions between UI states, scroll reveal only when it helps the story.
- **How it looks:** The existing page unchanged in copy, data, and layout — with a restrained motion layer: primary content reveals on entry, important controls respond on hover/active, state changes transition instead of snapping, and occasional scroll reveals. One motion language across the whole artifact; no mixed easings, durations, or physics.
- **Frame by frame:** Per moment: a trigger (load, hover, click/state change, or scroll into view) → a transform/opacity-only animation (layout properties — top, left, width, height — are never animated) → the settled end state. Automatic or scroll-linked motion always ships with a `prefers-reduced-motion` fallback.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Default UI transitions 140–220ms for most controls; larger page reveals may be slower but must never block reading. Animate only `transform` and `opacity`. Stagger only small groups — long staggered lists feel slow. No endless decorative loops unless they communicate status or progress; no custom cursors, no noisy particle effects, no motion that competes with content. Implementation: CSS keyframes + small JS observers for plain HTML; the repo's local stack for frameworks; pair with GSAP skills (gsap-core, gsap-timeline, gsap-scrolltrigger) when sequencing is needed; always clean up observers, timers, and animation instances.
- **Reference / source:** OpenDesign; the skill carries Emil Kowalski's motion principles (Kowalski of animations.dev).
- **Best for:** The final motion-polish pass on any section or page; also serves as a compact house motion standard (140–220ms, transform/opacity only). Trade fit: strong — applies to every trades homepage without changing its design.
- **Tier:** STRONG — concrete, broadly applicable motion discipline with real duration values (basis: source's own values).
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0617⟧

## ⟦S0618⟧ open-design/faq-page — Part 17 — MCP Market — open-design skills
- **What it is:** A page skill (full text in the catalogue) that produces a single FAQ page — collapsible accordion, live search, category filtering — as one self-contained HTML document styled by the active project's DESIGN.md tokens.
- **How it looks:** In order: a header ("Frequently Asked Questions" or "Help Center" plus a one-sentence subtitle); a prominent search bar with icon and placeholder; 3–4 pill-style category filters ("All" selected by default); the accordion — question rows with a chevron or plus/minus icon, answers hidden until expanded; and a footer CTA, "Still have questions?", with a contact link or support email.
- **Frame by frame:** Click a question header → its answer expands with a smooth transition (max-height or grid-template-rows), optionally closing the previously open item. Type in the search box → the list filters in real time, case-insensitively, matching text in questions or answers. Click a category pill → only questions with that `data-category` remain visible. Keyboard: Tab through questions, Enter expands.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Content spec: 12–18 real FAQs across 3–4 categories; answers concise at 2–4 sentences, with answers over 100 words broken into paragraphs or bullets. Edge cases: fewer than 8 FAQs → ask for more or generate realistic domain questions; 1–5 FAQs → drop categories and search, show a simple list. Build rules: semantic `<details>`/`<summary>` for progressive enhancement, or custom JS with proper ARIA; search matches question + answer text; `data-od-id` attributes on header, search, categories, accordion container, and footer; output emitted inside `<artifact>` tags as one HTML file with inline CSS/JS. Example categories shipped in the skill: Billing, Account, Technical, General (four sample questions each).
- **Reference / source:** OpenDesign FAQ Page Skill; styling defers to the active DESIGN.md of the project it runs in.
- **Best for:** FAQ sections and standalone FAQ pages — for a trades site, the natural home of financing, warranty, process, and service-area questions, with search/filter keeping long lists usable. Trade fit: strong; nearly every trades homepage needs this section.
- **Tier:** STRONG — a complete, concrete section pattern with content counts and interaction rules (basis: source's own completeness).
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0618⟧

## ⟦S0624⟧ open-design/gpt-tasteskill — Part 17 — MCP Market — open-design skills
- **What it is:** An anti-default design doctrine (full text in the catalogue) for award-level frontend pages: it attacks standard LLM layout habits — six-line wrapped headings, gappy bento grids, cheap meta-labels, invisible button text, repeated left/right layouts — by forcing a simulated Python randomization of design choices before any code, then verifying the result in a mandatory `<design_plan>` pre-flight.
- **How it looks:** A cinematic page in AIDA order: a creative nav (floating glass pill or minimal split nav); a wide, breathing hero — H1 in an ultra-wide container (`max-w-5xl`/`max-w-6xl`) flowing in 2–3 lines at `clamp(3rem, 5vw, 5.5rem)`, either centered over a full-bleed image with a dark radial wash with exactly two high-contrast CTAs below, artistically asymmetric with a floating image overlapping from bottom-right, or an editorial split with massive negative space; a gapless bento grid of 3–5 intentional cards mixing large imagery, dense typography, and CSS effects; GSAP desire sections; and a massive high-contrast CTA footer. Sections are separated by huge padding (`py-32 md:py-48`) so each reads as a distinct cinematic chapter. Imagery is seeded picsum photos treated with grayscale / mix-blend-luminosity / contrast-125 filters; backgrounds use radial blurs, grainy mesh gradients, or shifting dark overlays — never flat color.
- **Frame by frame:** Hover on any card or image → it scales to `group-hover:scale-105` over 700ms ease-out inside an `overflow-hidden` container. Scroll → images start at scale 0.8, grow to 1.0 as they enter view, then darken and fade to opacity 0.2 as they leave. A section title pins on the left (ScrollTrigger `pin: true`) while a gallery scrolls up on the right. A central paragraph's words scrub from opacity 0.1 to 1.0 sequentially with scroll. Cards stack and overlap from the bottom as the user scrolls. Horizontal accordion slices expand on hover to reveal content and imagery; a partner marquee scrolls continuously.
- **Mechanism & key values:** GSAP with ScrollTrigger (`@gsap/react`). Randomization protocol: from a deterministic seed (prompt character count), simulate `random.choice()` to lock 1 hero architecture (3 options), 1 typography stack (Satoshi, Cabinet Grotesk, Outfit, or Geist — Inter is banned), 3 component architectures, and 2 GSAP paradigms before coding. The 2-line iron rule: H1 never exceeds 2–3 lines — shrink the type and widen the container, never wrap to 4–6 lines. Bento law: `grid-flow-dense` (`grid-auto-flow: dense`) on every bento grid, with col-span/row-span values mathematically verified to interlock with zero empty cells. Component arsenal includes inline pill-shaped images embedded inside massive headings (a `w-24 h-10 rounded-full` inline-block span with a cover background), horizontal accordions, infinite marquees, and overlapping-portrait testimonial carousels. Hard bans: meta-labels ("SECTION 01", "QUESTION 05", "ABOUT US"), hero stamp/badge icons, pill-tags under the hero, raw stats in the hero, emojis in code or output. Images from `https://picsum.photos/seed/{keyword}/1920/1080` with the keyword matched to the vibe. The whole page is wrapped in `<main className="overflow-x-hidden w-full max-w-full">` to prevent horizontal scrollbars. The `<design_plan>` pre-flight must show the RNG output, the AIDA check, the hero math, the bento density proof, and the label/button-contrast sweep before code is written.
- **Reference / source:** OpenDesign gpt-tasteskill; image source picsum.photos; marquee icons from `@phosphor-icons/react`.
- **Best for:** Hero architecture (the 2-line iron rule and the three hero layouts), gapless bento feature grids, and GSAP scroll paradigms for the desire section of any homepage. Trade fit: strong as an anti-generic doctrine for trades heroes and feature grids; its picsum stock imagery should be swapped for the firm's real work photos.
- **Tier:** STRONG — concrete hero, grid, and GSAP rules with real values that directly target generic-looking output (basis: source's own values).
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0624⟧
## ⟦S0625⟧ open-design/huashu-art-motion — Part 17 — MCP Market — open-design skills

- **What it is:** The Open Design host adaptation of Huashu's "art motion" pack: a complete method-and-toolbox for planning and hand-coding art animation and explainer shots inside an existing task. It bundles 35 numbered art-style recipe cards (cave painting 40,000 BC through 2016 Shinkai, each a full pure-Canvas-2D production recipe), 9 explainer-grammar cards (3Blue1Brown, keynote/UI, finance charts, Kurzgesagt, Vox collage, whiteboard, storytime, kinetic type, presenter), 11 craft documents (reference-film breakdown, storyboard template, palettes, character-fidelity rules), and the full source of 8 generic Canvas helper modules (U, PAINT, KIT, brush/render/post extensions of PAINT, MO, CAM). It is an adapter, not a film: the upstream renderer, demo scenes, character rigs/frames, fonts, voice cloning and export pipeline are explicitly NOT included — selecting this skill does not make an MP4 exportable; assets and export use whatever the host actually provides.
- **How it looks:** Two output families. (1) Art pieces: a full-frame 1920×1080 living painting in one art-historical style — ochre cave wall with charcoal animals alternating two poses and firelight flicker; Egyptian tomb wall with 24 hand-coded hieroglyph functions and a scarab pushing the sun disc; a Roman mosaic of ~17,871 tesserae whose colours flow stone to stone; Van Gogh flow-field brushstrokes with regional palettes; Seurat pointillism (~24,000 equal dots in a 21-colour palette, optical mixing); Hopper hard-edged light patches sliding across a room; a gold-leaf Klimt robe of 150 rotating/blinking pattern motifs; a vaporwave frame run through VHS RGB-split and tracking noise. Composition stays fixed (window, table, figures in the same places) while the style and its 2–4 signature motifs move. (2) Explainer pieces: one of nine measured looks — pure-black 3b1b field with saturated thin lines (BLUE_C #58C4DD, RED_C #FC6255, pure yellow), Economist-style charts (white or FT salmon #FFF1E5, 8px red top rule, one hero colour, the rest grey), Vox's black/paper-white/one-red desk of halftone photos and torn clippings, RSA whiteboard (white #FBFBFB, black line ~6.5px, single orange accent #EF7226 ≈22% of ink), Kurzgesagt flat shapes with radial glows, kinetic type with one giant word per screen (340px hero word vs 96px sub-line vs 40px label).
- **Frame by frame:** Everything is a deterministic function of time t driven by the host timeline (seek/replay safe; same t renders pixel-identically). Art/speedrun form: t=0 opens mid-action, never on a blank or static frame (ink painting starts with strokes already landing; mosaic layout precomputed once, only colour moves) → inside each era's dwell (0.25–1.4s) one continuous hero action runs on GLOBAL time across cuts — the shared choreography: cup rises over 0.9s (cosine), holds 0.7s, lowers 0.8s (2.4s cycle), head sips, cat tail swings sin(5.2t)·0.35 + sin(11t)·0.08, blink fires when t mod 2.3 > 2.18, breathing sin(4t)·0.012 — while 2–4 era motifs loop (two-pose animal alternation every 7 frames, scarab at 10.7px/frame, meander bands scrolling, gold highlight sweeping only across a computed "goldness" mask) → at each beat-grid boundary the NEXT era's signature form sweeps in as the transition (mosaic flip, wave, vortex, pixelation) with a 1.03× punch-zoom settling over ~20 frames, and the year counter rolls in the new era's own lettering → the final era stretches (9+ beats) for a character gag played with anticipation, squash-and-stretch and follow-through (cat bats the cup off the table across ~4s) and a hand-written signature reveal → end state holds on the gag. Hand-drawn line styles quantise time (stepTime: 12fps rubber-hose, 10fps shadow puppet, 8fps Haring hard cuts, 8–12fps boiling-line seed swaps); continuous styles move every frame. Explainer form: the shot sits completely still → on the narration's noun or number, exactly one pulse event fires — punch-in 0.28s (+18–32% zoom), same-scale pan 0.30s, or slam 0.17s (scale 1.55 → 0.94 → 1.0) — → settles and stays still until the next narration beat; only environment layers (stars twinkling 1–3.5 rad/s, drifting particles, far clouds) may keep moving underneath.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Canvas 2D only, no 3D engine. Determinism: mulberry32 seeded RNG (U.rng) and integer hash everywhere; load order U first, then only the modules used; stage default 1920×1080, U.setStage for portrait 1080×1920 (the 35 style scenes are landscape-only). PAINT style renderers re-draw a flat underpainting by sampling its pixels: strokes (cell 12, len 22, width 7, outline 0.35, regional swatch palettes mixBase 0.3–0.45), dabs (cell 10, size 9), mosaic (tile 14), halftone (cell 14, or createPattern Ben-Day tiles — 10× faster), pixelate (8px blocks, palette quantise), facets (22×13 jittered triangle grid, shiftAmt 26), pointillism (hex grid pitch 10, dot r 4.5, pair-mixing clamped w 0.2–0.8 with a 0.004·|Pi−Pj|² penalty, 8% complementary dots, 7% flicker at 6fps), plus brush (fly-white bristle breaks by noise threshold, tones: burnt 0.9 / dense 0.8 / heavy 0.6 / light 0.35 / clear 0.15), inkWash (multiply, halo blur grows 0→1), flowLines (200–300px strokes, region params e.g. sky [32 steps, 7px, w10, α0.78]), watercolor (midpoint-displacement deform, layers at α 0.045–0.5 with 1.6px "water-edge" rims), cel shading (shape minus its own translate via evenodd clip; shadow offset 22–30px large parts, 10px faces), light maps (ambient ≈ rgb(30,21,13) ≈ 0.13, lighter-blended light pools, one multiply), cast shadows (shear affine, silhouettes composited once at α 0.55 so overlaps never double-darken), post stack (VHS split offset 3 + 1.5·sin(7t) px, 70px tracking band rolling at 520px/s, 4px scanline tile; film grain/flicker at 24fps; bloom = frame shrunk 4×, blur 6px, screen α 0.28). MO timing library: smooth = 6t⁵−15t⁴+10t³ (explainer default), appleOut cubic-bezier(0.25, 0.1, 0.25, 1), emphasized (0.2, 0, 0, 1), Kurzgesagt k75 (0.75, 0, 0.25, 1) and easyEase (0.333, 0, 0.667, 1), Vox longTail (0.33, 0, 0.2, 1); SwiftUI-style springs (stiffness (2π/d)², damping ratio ζ = 1 − bounce; smooth bounce 0 / snappy 0.15 / bouncy 0.3 at d = 0.5s); springHz overshoot ≈37% at 3Hz/decay 6, ≈16% at 2.5/9, ≈8% at 2.2/10; LaggedStart lag_ratio default 0.05; PULSE constants punch 0.28s / pan 0.30s / slam 0.17s / k 0.25 (write 0.18–0.32). CAM world camera {x, y, z, r}: zoom by logarithmic interpolation (zlerp — equal ratio per frame), a circular reveal needs zoom ≥ ~1100/opening-radius to cover the screen, parallax layers displace ∝ depth d and scale z^d, motion blur along camera velocity (below 1.5px/frame it degenerates to a single draw). Beat system: 128 BPM grid, eighth note 0.234s; era dwells shrink 6 → 4×5 → 3×4 → 2×3 → 1×3 eighths, finale 9+; transitions shrink 0.4s → 0.13s (complex signature transitions get 0.48–0.5s); a transition's segment start is back-computed so its reveal point lands on the bar line. Performance budget: ≤150ms/frame in QA; measured per style at 1920×1080 — Bauhaus ~5ms, Haring ~4ms, cave ~21ms max, Monet/Seurat ~100–105ms, Van Gogh ~110ms, shadow puppet ~121ms (heaviest). Colour law: blue-purple gradients/starfields/neon are banned as AI-default — a frame with >30% pixels at hue 225–300° and saturation ≥0.30 is a "blue-purple frame", >30% of the film fails delivery; eight stock 6-key palettes are supplied (paper #F3EDE2/#C8402F, poster #FFD23F/#FF5A36, ink #121417/#F2B33D, navy flat #0D1B2A, bauhaus #EFE9DD/#D62828/#1D4E89, snow, wood #EDE3D1/#C4552D, chalk #23302B/#F4D35E). Character law: no code-drawn people in finished pieces (AI-generated frame libraries, or hands/back-view/silhouette only), enforced by an 8-point fidelity checklist (recognisable silhouette, skeleton proportions, real hands, ≥2 light levels, ≥3 material details, specific performance, same rendering language as background, consistency). Motion is QA'd by frame-differencing two stills inside a dwell (avoiding the first 0.35s of punch-zoom) rather than by eye.
- **Reference / source:** Upstream https://github.com/alchaincyf/huashu-art-motion/tree/d861767d180008d27675819932070a670a3ae43f (commit d861767d180008d27675819932070a670a3ae43f), MIT licence (licence file kept with the package; its body is not reproduced in the bundled text). Named first-hand sources inside the cards: 3Blue1Brown's own manim configs and video sources (github.com/3b1b), Apple WWDC spring guidance + HIG, Linear/Stripe site CSS values, The Economist 2017 chart style guide and FT o-colors, Heer & Robertson 2007 animated-transitions paper, Hausner 2001 mosaic simulation with Felzenszwalb–Huttenlocher distance transform, Kurzgesagt's official Skillshare class transcripts, Vox art-direction interviews, RSA Animate / Minute Physics measured videos, TheOdd1sOut and Jaiden Animations measured videos, Saul Bass via Art of the Title, Dan Ebberts' inertia-bounce expressions, School of Motion kinetic-type frame counts. Honest gaps: style card 07_ukiyoe is NOT bundled (35 of the 36 numbered cards are present; ukiyo-e survives only as mentions in the craft docs, e.g. its (3,2)px colour-plate offset), and craft docs 07 (positive experience) and 09 (video-grammar survey) are cited by the cards but not included as sections — the bundled craft set is 01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 06, 08, 10 plus palettes, character fidelity and the storyboard template.
- **Best for:** Motion-graphics and explainer production rather than page sections: animated hero backdrops or section-divider films in a deliberate art style, "how it works" explainer clips, art-history/culture pieces, data-story segments (t3), keynote-style product reveals (t2). As a reference library it is also a deep source of transferable Canvas mechanisms — flow-field strokes, optical-mix pointillism, tesserae colour flow, gold-mask light sweeps, cel hard-shadow bands, pulse-rhythm camera moves — for WebGL/Canvas hero art direction. Trade-fit note: the mechanisms transfer, the demo content does not (every recipe is built around one fixed tea-drinking girl-and-cat scene, which must be re-composed per subject), per-frame costs (up to ~121ms at 1080p for the heavy styles) are far above a homepage's frame budget, and the pack's own rules forbid its AI-default colour habits; treat it as a motion-craft reference and explainer-shot toolkit, not a section design. The skill text also prescribes agent behaviours (host-stage gating, QA/render script runs, image- and video-model routes for character frames) — those are the upstream workflow described as data; nothing in it was executed while indexing.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0625⟧
# Chunk: skills S0626–S0635 — Part 17 open-design (image-first design pair, polish/login/stub, minimalist system, device mockup, motion craft, Motion.Lab case library, Oil Motion pipeline)

**Relationship finding (read first):** ⟦S0626⟧ and ⟦S0627⟧ are sibling skills, not duplicates — they share most of one rulebook (the combinatorial variation engine, the 4/8/12 section packs, hero-minimalism and anti-slop lists are near-identical, and their baseline dials differ only in a few values), but they do different jobs: S0626 is the full workflow (generate section images → deep-analyse them → implement code faithfully), while S0627 generates the images ONLY and adds a composition system S0626 lacks (per-section composition anchors, background modes, CTA variations, hero scales, narrative spines). Full shared detail is given under S0626; S0627's entry gives its own deltas and points back. No other pair in this range is the same skill under two names. Two entries are thin by nature and say so: ⟦S0630⟧ is a 1 KB catalogue advert whose full content is NOT in the bank (upstream install required), and ⟦S0629⟧ is a 1 KB skill whose substance is its bundled P0/P1 checklist. ⟦S0634⟧ contains internal near-duplicates inside its own 160-case library — flagged in its entry.

## ⟦S0626⟧ open-design/image-to-code-skill — Part 17 — MCP Market — open-design skills
- **What it is:** A workflow skill for visual website work: the agent must first generate design reference images itself (one large image per section), deep-analyse them as a design specification, and only then implement the frontend as a faithful translation of those images. It exists to break AI defaults — one compressed whole-page image, unreadable tiny text, centred dark heroes, card spam, cloned left-text/right-image blocks.
- **How it looks:** What the visitor ultimately sees is a coded site that matches a set of premium section comps: a clean cinematic hero with one focal point and a short headline (1 line ideal, 2 good, 3 maximum — never 4+), generous even spacing, open layouts instead of boxes-in-boxes, images in fixed-aspect frames with one consistent radius logic, almost no pills/badges/fake system labels, and varied section rhythm (density, image-to-text ratio and alignment change down the page while palette, type scale and CTA family stay constant).
- **Frame by frame:** No page motion of its own — it is a production workflow (generate → analyse → implement). The only motion content is a direction cue: each design must imply exactly 2 of 6 "motion-implied" energies in its imagery — scrubbing text reveal, pinned narrative section, staggered float-up, parallax image drift, smooth accordion expansion, cinematic fade-through. These are visual-direction cues for the comp, explicitly "not coding instructions".
- **Mechanism & key values:** Baseline dials (1–10): DESIGN_VARIANCE 8, VISUAL_DENSITY 3, ART_DIRECTION 8, IMPLEMENTATION_CLARITY 9, IMAGE_USAGE_PRIORITY 9, SPACING_GENEROSITY 9, ANALYSIS_PRECISION 10, IMAGE_GENERATION_EAGERNESS 10, UI_SIMPLICITY_DISCIPLINE 9. Hard rules: in Codex, N sections requested → N separate section images (1→1 … 10→10), never one multi-section collage; never crop a section/detail out of an older larger image — regenerate it fresh in the same design language; extra detail/extraction images whenever text, buttons, cards or colours are too small to read. Variation engine (pick and commit): 1 of 4 theme paradigms (Pristine Light / Deep Dark / Bold Studio Solid / Quiet Premium Neutral), 1 of 4 background characters (technical grid-dotted field / solid + ambient gradient / full-bleed cinematic imagery / tactile textured surface), 1 of 6 typography characters (clean grotesk / refined grotesk / expressive display / compressed statement / editorial serif+sans / Swiss rational), 1 of 6 hero architectures (cinematic centred minimalist / asymmetric split / floating polaroid scatter / inline typography behemoth / editorial offset / massive image-first), 1 of 6 section systems (bento rhythm / alternating editorial / poster stacked / gallery-led / Swiss grid / asymmetric premium flow), exactly 4 signature components from a list of 11 (diagonal staggered square masonry, 3D cascading card deck, hover-accordion slices, gapless bento, infinite brand marquee, turning polaroid arc, vertical rhythm lines, off-grid editorial, product UI panel stack, split testimonial quote wall, layered image crop frames), exactly 2 motion cues. Default section packs: 4 = hero/features/social proof/CTA; 8 = hero/trust bar/features/showcase/benefits/testimonials/pricing/CTA; 12 adds feature grid, product preview, problem-solution, workflow, metrics, FAQ, CTA+footer. Analysis must extract, per image: exact readable text, type scale/line-count/wrap behaviour, spacing relationships, button shape/padding/hierarchy, card dimensions and radius logic, palette and image treatment, grid and rhythm. Anti-slop lists ban (among others) purple/blue AI gradients, glassmorphism stacking, gradient headline tricks, filler words (unleash, elevate, revolutionize, next-gen, seamless, transformative platform) and fake brands (Acme, Nexus, Flowbit, Quantumly, NovaCore). A 21-point clarity check closes the skill (hero clean, text extracted, no cropping, first screen readable on a small laptop, micro-UI reduced…).
- **Reference / source:** Open Design catalogue skill (Part 17, MCP Market). The skill text names no upstream URL, site or author.
- **Best for:** Process, not a section design: use before building any hero/landing/marketing page when an image-led reference is wanted before code. For trades work it disciplines the comp stage, but the generated comps are invented imagery — a real firm's photos, reviews and facts still have to replace them in implementation. Pairs with ⟦S0627⟧ (the image-generation half, with a richer composition system).
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0626⟧

## ⟦S0627⟧ open-design/imagegen-frontend-web — Part 17 — MCP Market — open-design skills
- **What it is:** The image-generation-only sibling of ⟦S0626⟧: it art-directs and outputs one separate horizontal reference image per website section — never a single tall whole-page image, never a collage — and stops there (no analysis or implementation phase). Same variation engine, section packs and anti-slop lists as S0626 (see that entry); this entry records what is different.
- **How it looks:** A set of horizontal section comps (16:9, 16:10 or 21:9; hero usually 16:9 or 21:9) that read as one brand world — same palette (1 primary + 1 secondary + 1 sparing accent + neutral scale), same type family/scale, same CTA family — while composition deliberately varies: the hero is biased AWAY from the default left-text/right-image (alternatives named: centred over background image, bottom-left or bottom-right over image, top-left lead, stacked centre, image-as-canvas, off-grid editorial, mini minimalist, inverted classic), and section sizes mix — some large and content-rich, some mini minimalist, some medium editorial.
- **Frame by frame:** Static images — no motion. Like S0626 it picks exactly 2 of the same 6 motion-implied energies (scrubbing text reveal, pinned narrative, staggered float-up, parallax drift, accordion expansion, cinematic fade-through) as direction cues the stills should imply.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Deltas from S0626: baseline dials VISUAL_DENSITY 4 and SPACING_GENEROSITY 8 (S0626: 3 and 9), plus two dials S0626 lacks — LAYOUT_VARIATION 8, CONVERSION_DISCIPLINE 8. Hard output rule with defaults when the count is unstated: "landing page" → 6 sections/images, "full website template"/"full website"/"marketing site" → 8, "product page"/"portfolio" → 6, "hero" → 1; images are announced one by one ("Section 1 of 8: Hero"…). Per-section systems S0626 does not have: 10 composition anchors (centred statement; top-left lead/support bottom-right; bottom-left text over image; bottom-right CTA cluster; left-third caption + right-two-thirds visual — "classic, use sparingly, never twice in a row"; inverted classic; centred low — text in lower 40% over hero image; off-grid editorial offset; stacked centre; image-as-canvas) with ≥3 different anchors required across a site; 12 background modes per section (solid + inline asset, subtle texture/paper/grid, full-bleed image + tonal overlay, editorial side-image 50/50·60/40·40/60, image-as-canvas, flat colour block + detail crop, cinematic tonal gradient, atmospheric graded photo, duotone, soft radial vignette + product crop, micro-noise gradient, colour-blocked diptych) — never all the same mode; 6 CTA variations (primary pill, outline/ghost, underlined link + arrow, full-width banner CTA, oversized headline + tiny CTA hint, CTA as caption); 3 hero scales per page (Giant Statement / Mid Editorial / Mini Minimalist); 6 narrative spines (artifact-collectible, journey-pilgrimage, tool-precision instrument, living system-garden, stage-spotlight, archive-dossier); exactly 1 "second-read moment" per page (e.g. one oversized punctuation/numeral, one material switch, a narrow vertical side-rail note). Brief-to-direction mapping table: minimalist/clean/Swiss → Mini hero, solid surfaces, gradients skipped; editorial/magazine → Mid or Giant hero, duotone/graded side images; cinematic/luxury/bold → Giant hero, full-bleed + overlay + vignette; SaaS/product/fintech → Mid Editorial, solid + inline asset; agency/portfolio → Giant or Mini decisively; e-commerce → Mid with strong product focus. Gradient discipline: low-chroma palette-matched tonal gradients, single-hue photo grades, soft vignettes and noise-textured gradients are allowed and encouraged; rainbow/mesh, purple-to-blue AI defaults, pink-to-orange, neon glow halos and gradient text are banned. Composition-variety rejection rules: same anchor >2 sections in a row or same background mode >3 in a row fails the set; non-minimalist briefs must include ≥1 full-bleed/duotone/atmospheric background and ≥1 mini minimalist section. Headline guidance: 5–10 strong words. 21-point clarity check (includes: image count == section count, hero not the reflexive left-text/right-image). Creativity rule: actively raise at least 3 of composition, typography distinctiveness, scale contrast, hero concept, image treatment, section rhythm, framing, visual tension, layout surprise.

## ⟦S0628⟧ open-design/impeccable-design-polish — Part 17 — MCP Market — open-design skills
- **What it is:** A short post-generation pass for an EXISTING design artifact: inspect what is actually there, then sharpen it — it must not restart the project or change its content, brand or scenario unless asked.
- **How it looks:** The same page, tightened: consistent spacing and type scale, hierarchy and interaction states fixed, mobile overflow/clipping and contrast problems repaired, generic AI tells removed (purple-blue glow gradients with no product reason, generic 3-card feature rows, oversized rounded cards everywhere, empty marketing adjectives, decorative effects that don't aid comprehension). Ends in a better runnable state, not a critique list.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion of its own. Its "Animate" mode adds restrained, useful motion only where it improves feedback or storytelling, with reduced-motion fallbacks preserved.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Six follow-up modes: Audit (highest-impact issues across hierarchy, spacing, colour, type, interaction states, responsiveness, accessibility), Critique (what feels generic/overdesigned/underdesigned/inconsistent), Polish (edit the top issues directly), Animate, Harden (mobile overflow, text clipping, contrast, missing states, broken links, fragile layout), Live (final visual QA + next actions for presentation/sharing). Operating rules: inspect the current HTML/page before editing — never guess from the prompt; a few decisive fixes over broad cosmetic churn; preserve accessibility (focus states, contrast, semantic controls, readable text, reduced-motion fallbacks).
- **Reference / source:** Open Design catalogue skill (Part 17). Pairings it names: `design-taste-frontend` or `gpt-taste` for anti-slop redesigns, `emilkowalski-motion` or GSAP skills for motion polish, image/video skills when real assets are needed instead of CSS decoration.
- **Best for:** The QA/polish stage of any build — a final pass over a finished hero or full homepage before delivery. Trade fit: general; it is a checklist discipline, not a design.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0628⟧

## ⟦S0629⟧ open-design/login-flow — Part 17 — MCP Market — open-design skills
- **What it is:** A small skill for generating mobile-first login/authentication screens — phone + SMS verification, password login, or social SSO — as a single standalone HTML prototype with default, loading and error states, gated by a bundled acceptance checklist before output.
- **How it looks:** A 375 px-wide phone screen: labels sitting above their inputs (never placeholder-only), a password field with a show/hide toggle, social sign-in buttons with real SVG icons, red error text under the offending field, a loading spinner inside the primary CTA while submitting, "Forgot password" and "Don't have an account" links, a country picker when phone auth is used, brand-coloured input focus states. No horizontal scroll; safe-area insets respected on notched devices.

- **Mechanism & key values:** Workflow: read references/checklist.md first → clarify auth method → pass the P0 checklist gate → build → wrap output in an `<artifact>` tag. Hard numbers: viewport 375 px (iPhone standard); touch targets minimum 44 px; keyboard types `tel` for phone, `password` for password fields. P0 (7 must-pass): labels above inputs; password show/hide toggle; SVG social icons, not emoji; ≥44 px targets; red error text below the field; CTA hover/active states; no unmarked placeholder text like "example@email.com". P1 (5 should-pass): spinner in button during submission; forgot-password link; sign-up link; country picker for phone auth; brand-colour focus state.
- **Reference / source:** Open Design catalogue skill (Part 17); its bundled reference `login-flow/references/checklist.md` is inlined in the bank text.
