## ⟦S0631⟧ open-design/minimalist-skill — Part 17 — MCP Market — open-design skills
- **What it is:** A complete design system for "Premium Utilitarian Minimalism & Editorial UI" — document-style interfaces like top-tier workspace platforms (Notion-like): warm monochrome, flat components, editorial serif display type, macro-whitespace, bento grids and scarce muted-pastel accents. It actively rejects generic SaaS styling.
- **How it looks:** White or warm bone (#FFFFFF / #F7F6F3 / #FBFBFA) pages divided by hairlines (1px solid #EAEAEA), off-black text (#111111 or #2F3437, never pure black; secondary text #787774), crisp 8–12 px-radius cards with generous 24–40 px padding, big serif headlines with tight tracking next to clean geometric sans body text, tiny uppercase pastel tags, borderless FAQ rows separated only by a bottom hairline with + / − toggles, <kbd> key-cap chips, and desaturated warm photography under a whisper of grain. Almost no shadow anywhere; colour appears only as washed-out pastel tags/chips.
- **Frame by frame:** Motion is deliberately near-invisible. On scroll, blocks enter via IntersectionObserver: from translateY(12px) + opacity 0 to rest over 600ms, cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); lists/grids cascade with animation-delay calc(var(--index) × 80ms). On hover, cards gain a barely-there shadow (0 2px 8px rgba(0,0,0,0.04), 200ms); buttons press to scale(0.98) on :active. Optional ambient layer: one very slow radial-gradient blob (20s+ duration, opacity 0.02–0.04) drifting behind the hero on a fixed, pointer-events:none layer. Transform and opacity only — never layout properties.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Banned outright: Inter, Roboto, Open Sans; Lucide/Feather/Heroicons icon sets (use Phosphor Bold/Fill or Radix, one consistent stroke width); Tailwind's shadow-md/lg/xl (shadows must be ultra-diffuse, opacity < 0.05); primary-coloured section backgrounds; gradients, neon, 3D glassmorphism (beyond subtle navbar blur); rounded-full on large containers/cards/primary buttons; emojis anywhere; placeholder names (John Doe, Acme Corp, Lorem Ipsum); AI copy clichés (Elevate, Seamless, Unleash, Next-Gen, Game-changer, Delve). Type: body/UI sans 'SF Pro Display', 'Geist Sans', 'Helvetica Neue', 'Switzer'; hero/quote serif 'Lyon Text', 'Newsreader', 'Playfair Display', 'Instrument Serif' at letter-spacing −0.02em to −0.04em, line-height 1.1; mono 'Geist Mono', 'SF Mono', 'JetBrains Mono'; body line-height 1.6. Pastel accents (bg/text): Pale Red #FDEBEC/#9F2F2D, Pale Blue #E1F3FE/#1F6C9F, Pale Green #EDF3EC/#346538, Pale Yellow #FBF3DB/#956400. Components: bento cards border 1px solid #EAEAEA, radius 8px or 12px max, padding 24–40px; primary CTA solid #111111 bg, white text, radius 4–6px, no shadow, hover #333333 or scale(0.98); tags pill radius 9999px, text-xs, uppercase, letter-spacing 0.05em, pastel bg; accordion = border-bottom 1px #EAEAEA only; kbd chips border 1px #EAEAEA, radius 4px, bg #F7F6F3; faux-OS window chrome = white top bar + three small light-grey circles. Imagery: monochrome rough continuous-line ink illustrations + one offset pastel-filled geometric shape; photos desaturated/warm with overlay opacity 0.04 warm grain; placeholder pattern https://picsum.photos/seed/{context}/1200/800; section depth from low-opacity full-width imagery or radial light spots (radial-gradient, warm, opacity 0.03) or fine geometric line patterns. Execution: macro-whitespace first (section padding py-24 or py-32), content width max-w-4xl / max-w-5xl, will-change only on actively animating elements, scroll animation via IntersectionObserver never scroll listeners.
- **Reference / source:** Open Design catalogue skill (Part 17, MCP Market). No upstream URL named in the text; its stated visual analogy is top-tier workspace platforms.
- **Best for:** A whole-page design language for quiet, document-like pages: process explainers, towns/areas listings, FAQ, text-led proof pages — anywhere restraint reads as premium. For trades it fits a calm, established firm (not an image-led hero): the hero would be type-led with at most a desaturated photo, so it is one strong "version" direction against photo-heavy alternatives. NOT for colourful or high-drama sections.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0631⟧

## ⟦S0632⟧ open-design/mockup-device-3d — Part 17 — MCP Market — open-design skills
- **What it is:** A template for a static product showcase scene: an iPhone 15 Pro (and optionally a MacBook Pro 14") built entirely from CSS 3D transforms — no mockup images — with the user's REAL HTML content rendered live inside the device screens, glass-lens highlights and a mirrored floor.
- **How it looks:** A 1920×1080 stage on a warm dark-grey radial gradient (#1a1a1f centre → #0a0a0f edges) with a reflective floor. Left/centre, the iPhone stands tilted (titanium-silver #a8a8ad frame, 4px solid, 56px screen radius) showing a real 375×812 mobile UI at true mobile type sizes; right and slightly smaller, the MacBook shows a 1440×900 desktop UI scaled into its lid, its base/keyboard suggested by CSS shadow lines only. Two or three soft elliptical white highlights (radial-gradient, rgba(255,255,255,0.4) → transparent 60%) fake glass/lens refraction across the devices; below them, a flipped, fading reflection. Optional furniture: a small caption line top (codename/date/version, opacity 0.6) and a product slug block bottom-right (big logo + tagline + hairline sub-caption). Four background palettes: charcoal / pearl / midnight blue / mocha — never rainbow gradients.
- **Frame by frame:** Static by default. Optional: an 8s CSS turntable — @keyframes turntable swings rotateY between −12° and +12°, ease-in-out, infinite alternate — which must be disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** iPhone transform: rotateY(−12deg) rotateX(4deg) translateZ(40px); MacBook: rotateY(8deg). Floor reflection: transform scaleY(−1) with mask-image linear-gradient(to bottom, rgba(0,0,0,0.4), transparent 70%). Screen content rules: if the user gives text/data, auto-render a mock app UI (status bar + title + body + bottom tab bar or home indicator); if they give HTML, embed it as-is in a `<div class="screen">` (never iframe srcdoc) with a scale transform to fit; screen UI in Tailwind at real mobile sizes (text-sm/text-base, never text-9xl). Hard bans: no external mockup image URLs (no Unsplash/Dribbble links) — devices are CSS/SVG only; screen content must be the user's real data — no lorem ipsum, no "Your text here". Single self-contained HTML file. Outside-device type: Inter Tight / SF Pro style.

Its bundled example (inlined in the bank) shows an "HTML Anything" app: iPhone running a template-picker/task page (top: 选择模板 → 杂志风网页 PPT； middle: input + ⌘+Enter; bottom tab bar 任务/模板/设置）, MacBook running a three-column editor （任务列表 / 编辑器 / 实时预览）, captioned "2026 SPRING · CODENAME ATLAS · v0.4".

## ⟦S0633⟧ open-design/motion-design — Part 17 — MCP Market — open-design skills
- **What it is:** A motion-craft helper for timed pieces (brand/product films, promos, explainers, kinetic type): it refines the brief into a beat map, art-directs one strong representative frame first, then choreographs attention with primary/secondary/ambient motion layers, and gives the exact Open Design video-composition contract. It is not a renderer or template — the host task owns artifact creation, format and export; for interactive briefs it delivers runnable HTML instead of video.
- **How it looks:** A short film built around one recurring motif that transforms beat to beat (the worked example: scattered words orbit → one word attracts the others → the orbit becomes a timer → the timer completes and becomes the wordmark), typeset as a graphic object with deliberate scale/line-breaks/negative space, a small intentional palette, one material/world logic carried through (editorial ink, precision instrument, folded paper, tactile collage, vector geometry, painterly field), and an intentional close that resolves the motif and holds the final message. No default neon gradients, glass cards, glowing orbs or beige backgrounds.
- **Frame by frame:** Per beat the map records `time → viewer takeaway → focal object → transformation → copy/audio → exit`, with entrances, reading holds and exits inside the time budget. Choreography: the lead action carries the idea; a secondary action answers it (trailing label, settling shadow, elastic edge); ambient motion only when the scene needs life — quiet holds may be genuinely still. Motion moves on arcs for physical subjects, straight paths for precision/mechanical intent; transitions are match-cuts on shared shapes, tracked hand-offs or meaningful masks, preserving velocity and direction; loops must match start/end state AND velocity with no duplicated pause. Timing starting ranges: small accent/punctuation 120–220ms (decisive snap, then settle); main element arrival 350–650ms (quick travel, controlled landing); meaningful shape transformation 600–1200ms; large reveal/camera move 900–1800ms. Ease-out for arrivals, ease-in for motivated exits; constant speed only for conveyors/clocks/scans; playful material may overshoot, precision instruments must not bounce by default.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Defaults for an unconstrained short film: 12–18s, 16:9, 1920×1080, 30fps, no invented voiceover; portrait social = 9:16. Visual grammars by type: product/brand film (real benefit + concrete action, actual screens, motif carried into the closing frame), kinetic typography (words act out meaning via weight/tracking/direction; stable reading window; animate a phrase as a unit — reveal timing is not reading time), explainer/data (show the object before transforming it; reveal axes before values; beats aligned to real audio timing), art/procedural (seed texture once and move it coherently — regenerating marks per frame flickers), 3D/pro-tool (keep the user's AE/Blender/Remotion project, edit the smallest scene). Authoring contract (Open Design): timeline-driven HTML + GSAP (SVG for type/diagrams, Canvas for dense/procedural worlds); composition root `<div id="main" data-composition-id="main" data-start="0" data-duration data-width data-height data-poster-time>`; master timeline `gsap.timeline({ paused: true })` registered at `window.__timelines.main`, with a full-length clock tween `tl.to(clock, {t: duration, duration, ease: 'none'}, 0)` — timeScale(1), no repeat/start delay, actual duration() must equal data-duration (tl.duration(x) changes speed, it does NOT add a hold); deterministic under seeking — state must be a function of clock.t drawn in a per-frame rAF loop, never Date.now, unseeded randomness or onUpdate/onComplete-dependent visuals (export seeks with callbacks suppressed); SVG pop helper sets the same svgOrigin in both states (example popShape: scale 0→1, 0.45s, back.out(2)); scaffold pins GSAP 3.14.2 at ./gsap.min.js; poster-time must satisfy 0 ≤ t < data-duration and show a representative frame (no separate invented cover). Sound policy: `<meta name="od-motion-audio" content="required|silent">`; tracks declared as `<audio src data-start data-duration data-volume>` (example volume 0.3), local pre-trimmed files, music below speech, no loop/playback-rate/media-start attributes; "no voiceover" ≠ no music. Video delivery is dual: editable HTML source + rendered MP4 via the host HyperFrames renderer (`media scaffold --project … --composition-dir "motion-source/film"`, author index.html with `<meta name="od-motion-output" content="video">` and `<link rel="alternate" type="video/mp4" href="../../film.mp4">`, then `media generate --surface video --model hyperframes-html`, `media wait <id>` if queued); at most one targeted repair + re-render after review. Defect table included (slideshow feel → carry one object through a transformation; no weight → adjust travel time/acceleration/anticipation/settle; painterly flicker → seed and cache marks…).
- **Reference / source:** An original Open Design skill; SOURCES.md (inlined) credits https://github.com/alchaincyf/huashu-art-motion (representative-frame-first, deterministic procedural drawing), https://github.com/LottieFiles/motion-design-skill (timing vs spacing, easing, primary/secondary/ambient) and https://github.com/LobzyJay/motion-design-with-claude-and-codex (restraint, preserving the user's tool). No engine or assets vendored.
- **Best for:** Planning and authoring motion graphics — a trades firm's promo/explainer film, an animated logo/hero film, kinetic-type social clips. Its timing table and three-layer choreography also serve as the motion brief behind a homepage hero film; it is not a library of page-section effects (that is ⟦S0634⟧).
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0633⟧

## ⟦S0634⟧ open-design/motion-lab — Part 17 — MCP Market — open-design skills
- **What it is:** Motion.Lab — a searchable library of 160 ready-made motion cases, each with a bilingual (Chinese/English) name, a difficulty rating (1–3 of 3), a parameter definition (range/select controls with min/max/step/default/unit) and complete copy-paste HTML/CSS/JS. Structure: SKILL.md (workflow) + references/index.md (all 160 IDs with category + tags) + four category files — basic.md 42 cases, text.md 40, interaction.md 40, advanced.md 38. Cases are integration starting points, explicitly not finished product: scope the selectors, wire the parameters for real, clean up listeners/rAF, add reduced-motion fallbacks.
- **How it looks:** A catalogue of small, vivid demo scenes, mostly staged with one shared demo accent palette (hsl(280 90% 60%) purple ↔ hsl(200 90% 60%) blue gradients — a demo skin to re-colour, not a brand). Representative sights: a headline whose letters ride a sine wave; a stat counting 0 → 1,234; cards that stack and stick as you scroll (sticky-stack); a button that leans toward your cursor (magnetic, strength factor 0.4); a dot-grid whose points are pulled toward the pointer within a 100px radius; blurred colour balls merging like lava when they overlap (metaball, blur default 28px); a purple word "SCROLL" sliding 200px in lockstep with scroll (GSAP ScrollTrigger scrub); snow, fireworks, a spiral galaxy of 3,000 points, matrix rain in green katakana.
- **Frame by frame:** Each case is its own loop/trigger; the mechanisms group into families. Entrances (basic): trigger on load — fade/slide/scale/flip/skew/blur from an offset state to rest, typically 0.6–0.9s ease-out, several with overshoot cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1) (zoom-bounce, scale-in/out, text-zoom-in, char-fall); bounce-in lands through scale keyframes 0.3 → 1.1 → 0.9 → 1.05 → 1 over 1s. Loops (basic): marquee duplicates content and translates −50% over 12s linear; pulse scales to 1 + intensity (0.15) mid-cycle; heartbeat double-thumps at 14%/42% of a 1.2s cycle; jello/tada/wobble run fixed squash-and-stretch keyframe sets at ~0.9–1s. Text (text): typewriter adds one char per 80ms with a blinking caret (0.8s step-end); scramble resolves random glyphs into the target over 1.5s (new char locks every 3 frames at 50ms ticks); count-up runs 1500ms with cubic ease-out 1−(1−t)³ in the code; mask-reveal opens a clip-path inset (100% → 0) over 1.2s cubic-bezier(0.65, 0, 0.35, 1); per-char wave/bounce/fall use animation-delay calc(0.1s × n). Interaction: hover states transition 0.25–0.6s (lift −8px + deeper shadow; image zoom to scale 1.3 over 0.5s; flip-card rotateY 180° over 0.6s with preserve-3d); magnetic elements follow the pointer at 0.3–0.4× offset with a 0.3s cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.8, 0.2, 1) settle and snap back on leave; click ripples spawn a circle at the click point scaling ×4 (ripple-click) or ×10 (click-ripple-material) fading out over 0.6s; scroll-reveal fires once via IntersectionObserver (threshold 0.2 in code) from translateY(40px)/opacity 0 to rest over 0.6s; scroll-parallax shifts layers at data-speed × 0.3 of section offset; sticky-stack cards pin at top: 80px and overlap as the next scrolls up. Advanced: GSAP stagger lifts items y:40 → 0, 0.6s each, 0.15s stagger; GSAP timeline chains three 1s moves at '<0.2' offsets; physics-spring integrates velocity with stiffness 0.12 / damping 0.88 toward centre after a drag; cloth/gravity run Verlet/gravity sims per frame; canvas/WebGL cases (particles, shaders, flow fields, metaballs) run continuous rAF loops; svg-draw-path draws a 400-unit dash over 3s ease-in-out infinite alternate; lottie-checkmark draws circle (dash 276) then tick (dash 60), each 0.8s ease-out, tick delayed by the first duration.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Parameter style is uniform: CSS cases read var(--duration, <default>) etc.; JS cases read a `params` object. Honest ranges from the sources: durations cluster at 0.6–0.8s defaults for entrances, 0.8–1.5s for attention loops, 12s marquee / 15s vertical marquee, 2–3s gradient/colour cycles; distances 20–40px default (slide-up 40px, fade-in-up 20px, scroll-reveal 40px); blur-in starts at 14px blur + scale 1.05; tilt cases — three-d-tilt parameter max 15° (its sample code rotates ×30 total) and tilt-card-strong max 25° with glare, code rotating params.max × 2; grid-magnetic radius 100px, pull factor 0.3, dot grid 6×12 at 24px spacing with 0.2s transform transitions; particle counts — three-particles 100–5000 (default 1500, size 0.05), particle-galaxy default 3000, flow-field default 600, canvas-starfield 300 with z-speed 4/frame; fluid-distort uses SVG feTurbulence baseFrequency 0.02 animated 0.02→0.04→0.02 over 6s + feDisplacementMap scale default 24; morph-svg swaps path `d` on a 1.5s interval (the sample snaps rather than interpolating — a starting point, as the skill itself warns). Workflow rules the skill prescribes: find cases via references/index.md by ID/name/category/tags; check whether GSAP/Three.js already exist in the project (NOT bundled with the skill — never add several animation frameworks); size Canvas/WebGL to container × DPR; throttle scroll via frame scheduling; support keyboard/touch/focus as well as pointer; respect prefers-reduced-motion with a static/simplified state; never ship the sample's hardcoded sizes, placeholder text or asset paths unmodified. Quick picks named in the SKILL.md: button ripple → `click-ripple-material`; headline typing → `text-typewriter`, multi-line → `text-typewriter-multi`; card flip → `hover-flip-card`; scroll entrance → `scroll-reveal`; particle backgrounds → choose among `particle-fountain`, `canvas-starfield`, `flow-field`, `particle-galaxy` by purpose. Full case inventory — BASIC (42): fade-in, fade-in-up, fade-in-down, fade-in-left, fade-in-right, fade-out, slide-in-left, slide-in-right, slide-up, slide-down, slide-fade-corner, zoom-bounce, bounce-in, bounce-down, elastic-in, scale-in, scale-out, scale-pulse, flip-x, flip-y, flip-in-3d, rotate-in, rotate-360, pulse, shake, heartbeat, swing, jello, wobble, tada, flash, marquee, spinner, blur-in, blur-out, grayscale-in, color-cycle, gradient-shift, border-draw, shadow-grow, skew-in, typewriter-cursor. TEXT (40): typewriter, text-typewriter-multi, text-delete-retype, wave-text, text-wave-3d, mask-reveal, split-char, text-split-reveal, text-char-fall, text-word-fly, text-rotate-in, stagger-fade, count-up, number-marquee, scramble, gradient-text, rainbow-text, text-rainbow-shift, glitch-text, text-glitch-rgb, text-shadow-shift, text-shadow-long, text-3d, letter-spacing-wave, underline-draw, highlight-sweep, text-blink-cursor, text-neon, text-fire, text-ice, text-metallic, text-outline, text-stroke-animate, vertical-marquee, text-fade-up, text-slide-left, text-zoom-in, text-blur-reveal, text-bounce, text-flip-3d. ## ⟦S0635⟧ open-design/oil-motion — Part 17 — MCP Market — open-design skills
- **What it is:** A full production pipeline that turns AI-generated video / frame sequences into interactive web motion driven by scroll, pointer, drag, touch, orientation, audio, data or state. Its split of labour: the generation model handles semantic change (limbs, structure, material, occlusion); code handles input mapping, playback control, media processing and performance. The package ships local Python media scripts and TypeScript runtime controllers — pure local processing, no API key (generation itself uses host tools). Four single sources of truth, each fact living in exactly one file: `source/concept-contract.yaml` (intent), `source/motion-brief.yaml` (derived plan), `build/timeline.json` (compiled frames/boundaries/curves), `build/motion-budget.json` (format + controller decision).
- **How it looks:** What the visitor experiences: a hero or section subject that responds to them — scroll and a product disassembles into an exploded view and reassembles on the way back, every stopped frame a clean, readable still (motion blur is banned in scrub material); move the pointer and a character's gaze follows it around a full circle without ever showing the back of its head; drag and a product rotates on a turntable through front, side and back views; tap and a short clip plays forward to a held end-state — and plays backwards from the current frame when the input reverses, never hard-cutting to a different source. Depending on the locked contract the background is either baked into the video (full scene, lighting, contact shadows) or the subject floats transparently over the page's own background (alpha atlas or WebGL-keyed video).
- **Frame by frame:** Three runtime behaviours. frame-scrub (time_control: scrub): the input value maps continuously to a frame — progress = clamp((value − start)/(end − start), 0, 1); targetFrame = progress × (frameCount − 1) — the picture moves only while the input moves and freezes exactly where the input stops; fast reverse and jumps land on the correct integer frame (video seeks submit only the latest target; all-keyframe encoding for random access); circular inputs travel the shortest arc distance. segment-playback (segment-play): an input event immediately starts the clip playing in real time from the current frame toward the target state's hold frame — playback stops only ON `hold` (invariant: start ≤ hold < endExclusive; stopping on endExclusive or overshooting-then-jumping-back are named defects); reverse input cancels the current play and rewinds along the same timeline/curve (never negative playbackRate); a wheel/trackpad inertia stream counts as ONE gesture = one step; rapid repeated inputs keep only the newest target. autonomous-playback (autonomous): time drives the piece (idle/loop pieces); loops allowed only for material that passed closed-loop seam QA. Page navigation only selects state IDs — it never swaps the media `src` between states; desktop/mobile variants are chosen once at init.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Nine-step flow: lock intent (Concept Contract: driver, input_semantics continuous|step|event, time_control scrub|segment-play|autonomous, navigation, clip_continuity chain|independent, background_owner video|page, aspect_ratio taken from the real destination container — 16:9 hero, 9:16 portrait fullscreen, 1:1 card; never default 1:1 unconfirmed) → derive Motion Brief (parameter_space linear|circular|2d|discrete — never crush 2D/discrete states into one linear video; frame_policy native|interpolate; target_fps; gesture_policy with boundary clamp|loop and programmatic_navigation ignore|observe) → run `motion_budget.py --strict` (explicit --background-owner and --time-control; --scroll-pages only for scroll+scrub) → keyframes K0…Kn (one main semantic change per clip; chain mode: clip 2+ starts from the previous clip's ACTUAL accepted tail frame; transparent keyframes must be generated as real alpha PNGs — never colour-back-then-key-out; keyframe pixels must cover max CSS size × target DPR) → Pilot hard gate (first keyframe set + first clip mounted in the real page; approval recorded by production_gate.py with SHA-256 hashes — any later change invalidates it) → generate + per-clip QA (two chain gates: verify-chain on generation inputs, verify-output-chain on decoded output seams) → frame prep + compile → runtime from assets → final QA (target CSS size, DPR, cold cache, fast reverse, mobile, resource failure). Fixed delivery decision order: background_owner=video → baked-video; parameter_space=2d → alpha-atlas; discrete → budget each state separately; random access within budget → alpha-atlas; 1D sequential past the video frame threshold → chroma-video; 1D atlas over texture/decode budget → chroma-video; other small transparent → alpha-atlas. Texture maths: single texture ≤ 4096 per side and the runtime takes ONE atlas — columns = floor(4096/cell_width), rows = floor(4096/cell_height); e.g. 640×640 cells fit 6×6 = 36 frames, so 48 frames force cells ≤ ~585px (576px only if display × DPR ≤ 576); clarity may never be sacrificed to fit an atlas. Atlas packing example: `motion_pipeline.py atlas --cell-width 360 --cell-height 360 --quality 88` → motion.webp + motion.json. Chroma route: key colour default #00FF00 (#FF00FF when the subject contains green), composited deterministically from accepted alpha keyframes via composite_alpha_keyframe.py; the compiler re-simulates keying on encoded frames with the runtime's dominance-v2 parameters and rejects visible key blocks/spill/eaten interiors — widening thresholds to mask a bad master is forbidden. Baked route: compile_scroll_video.py emits desktop + mobile all-keyframe MP4s (compile.json must show allFramesAreKeyframes: true), poster.png, timeline.json; multi-segment via repeated `--segment DEST=START:HOLD:END_EXCLUSIVE`. Stabilisation when needed: normalize --anchor bottom --max-scale-change 0.08 (banned for free/camera/perspective motion). Explainer pages (create_explainer.py): budget default demands ≥24 frames per scroll page for scroll pieces; autoplay modes loop|pingpong|once (example 18fps); drivers pointer-angle (atan2 mapping), pointer-x, drag, scroll, autoplay. Prompt library (references/prompting.md): verbatim blocks for identity lock, locked camera, baked scene, chroma background, and per-motion clauses — circular gaze (face always to camera, gaze through 12/3/6/9 o'clock, constant rate, loop-exact end frame), 2D gaze (minimum 3×3 grid of sampled poses + bilinear selection; never one video traversed for random access), horizontal head yaw (−60° → +60°, linear, no loop), turntable (generate 0°/90°/180°/270° keyframes from real product references, then four 90° clips K0→K1→K2→K3→K0 — a single front photo must not be spun 360° or the back is invented), one-take seams (six paradigms: scale penetration, occlusion wipe, shape match, time lapse, reflection dive, cutaway dissolve — each clip one level of change, the hinge frame is both clips' boundary), exploded view (both end states generated as stills and human-approved first; labels/numbers added by code afterwards, never by the video model), scrub timeline staging guidance (e.g. 0–35% first stage, 35–80% main relation, 80–100% final state — no front-loading then near-duplicate holds), segment transitions, discrete states, and one-issue-at-a-time repair prompts. Requirements: Python 3.10+, FFmpeg/ffprobe with `-fps_mode` support (verified on FFmpeg 9.0.1), Pillow, NumPy, PyYAML; scripts in-package: motion_pipeline.py, compile_scroll_video.py, motion_budget.py, optimize_motion.py, loop_cleanup.py, chroma_key.py, media_edges.py, composite_alpha_keyframe.py, compose_travel_frames.py, create_explainer.py, production_gate.py; runtime assets: interactive-motion.ts (createFrameAnimator / createSegmentPlayer), step-gesture.ts (createStepGestureAdapter), chroma-video-renderer.ts. Pattern library (references/motion-patterns.md): 14 reference cards (material-chapter product, surface-to-interior dive, small-window expansion, multi-image convergence, scatter-to-order, perspective straighten, sticker stage, hover preview/spotlight, relationship star map, squeeze carousel, voice-state orb, content-space, usage-trace ageing, icon morph) each tagged with its evidence class (hands-on tested / preview observed / page description) and split into semantic-media vs container-choreography vs UI-state layers — only the semantic layer enters this pipeline.
- **Reference / source:** Upstream https://github.com/oil-oil/oil-motion at commit 07e31f2265f80caa8f2c1df825d85ac24a46307c, MIT licensed (license kept in-package). Open Design adaptation keeps all local scripts/controllers/references, replaces provider-specific generation and credential setup with host tools, and ships no demo media. Pattern-card references named inside: motionsites.ai (Cordex, Alethia, Orbit Stickers), 21st.dev component pages (scroll expansion hero, scroll choreography, scroll morph hero, container scroll animation, hover preview, spotlight card, radial orbital timeline, squeeze carousel, voice powered orb), cosmos.so, recent.design (aging button, 3-in-1 icon morph).
- **Best for:** Heavy, high-craft interactive hero pieces: a scroll-scrubbed product story (process section — e.g. a tear-off/rebuild sequence or a window cross-section build-up), a pointer-follow mascot/character, a drag turntable of a real product, state-driven before/after transitions. Trade fit: this is the most powerful — and most expensive — route in the range; it needs generated or shot video masters, a pilot gate and per-device compiled assets, so it suits ONE flagship hero, not routine sections. Its contract discipline (scrub vs segment-play, hold frames, reverse behaviour, texture/DPR budgets) is also the reference for judging any scroll-driven video idea. NOT for simple reveals — those are ⟦S0634⟧ cases at a fraction of the cost.

Banned in prose: "for brevity", "the rest follows the same pattern", "Let me know if you want me to continue", and similar. Method: Scope (count the distinct deliverables requested and lock the number) → Build (generate all of them completely) → Cross-check (re-read the request, compare counts). If a response nears the token limit, the skill prescribes stopping at a clean breakpoint (end of a function/file/section) and ending with a literal marker of the form `[PAUSED — X of Y complete. Send "continue" to resume from: next section name]`, resuming with no recap on "continue". (Recorded here as the skill's stated behaviour; it is an instruction set aimed at whatever agent runs it.)
- **Reference / source:** Open Design collection (`open-design/output-skill`); no upstream author or site named in the text.

## ⟦S0641⟧ open-design/redesign-skill — Part 17 — MCP Market — open-design skills
- **What it is:** A redesign playbook for existing projects: scan the codebase, diagnose against a long audit checklist (typography, colour/surfaces, layout, interactivity/states, content, components, iconography, code quality, strategic omissions), then apply targeted fixes in a fixed priority order — never a from-scratch rewrite.
- **How it looks:** The finished page it aims at: a characterful font instead of Inter/browser defaults (it names Geist, Outfit, Cabinet Grotesk, Satoshi; serif display + sans body for editorial), heavy tight headlines, body copy capped near 65 characters wide, off-black backgrounds (`#0a0a0a`, `#121212`) instead of pure `#000000`, one accent colour only (saturation below 80%), one grey family (all warm or all cool), shadows tinted to the background hue, subtle noise/grain or mesh/radial gradients instead of flat fills and even linear gradients, a max-width container around 1200–1440px, asymmetric layouts instead of everything centred, variable card heights, varied border radii (tighter inside, softer on containers), overlapping elements via negative margins, no sudden dark section inside a light page (or commit to full dark), background imagery behind hero/feature/CTA blocks (placeholder source it names: `https://picsum.photos/seed/{name}/1920/1080`). Component tells it removes: 3 equal card columns, accordion FAQs, 3-card testimonial carousels with dots, pill "New/Beta" badges, avatar circles only, 4-column footer link farms, Lucide/Feather-only icons (use Phosphor or Heroicons), rocket-for-launch/shield-for-security clichés.
- **Frame by frame:** Interaction motion it prescribes: hover → background shift, slight scale or translate on buttons/cards; press (`:active`) → `scale(0.98)` or `translateY(1px)`; all interactive transitions 200–300ms (no zero-duration jumps); anchor scrolling → smooth (`scroll-behavior: smooth`); animations run on `transform`/`opacity` only, never `top`/`left`/`width`/`height`. Upgrade techniques add: variable-font weight/width interpolation on scroll or hover; outlined text filling with colour on scroll entry; large type as a mask/window over video or animated imagery; parallax card stacks that stick and stack over each other on scroll; split-screen halves sliding in opposite directions; staggered entry cascades (Y-translate + fade, never everything at once); spring easing instead of linear; scroll-driven reveals via expanding masks, wipes, or draw-on SVG paths; true glassmorphism (backdrop blur + 1px inner border + inner shadow); spotlight borders that light up under the cursor.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Audit-and-fix workflow (Scan → Diagnose → Fix) on the existing stack. Key numbers: body width ~65ch; container 1200–1440px; accent saturation < 80%; one accent colour; weights 500/600 added between 400/700; tabular numbers (`font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`) for data; full-screen sections use `min-height: 100dvh`, never `height: 100vh`; transitions 200–300ms; press feedback `scale(0.98)`/`translateY(1px)`; skeleton loaders shaped like the layout instead of round spinners. Fix priority order: 1 font swap, 2 colour palette cleanup, 3 hover/active states, 4 layout and spacing, 5 replace generic components, 6 loading/empty/error states, 7 typography scale and spacing polish. Copy bans: "Elevate", "Seamless", "Unleash", "Next-Gen", "Game-changer", "Delve", "Tapestry", "In the world of…"; sentence case headers; organic numbers (e.g. `47.2%`, `$99.00`) instead of `99.99%`/`$100.00`. Also requires the usually-forgotten pieces: legal links, back navigation, custom 404, form validation, skip-to-content link, cookie consent where required.
- **Reference / source:** Open Design collection (`open-design/redesign-skill`); no upstream author named. Placeholder image source named in the text: picsum.photos.
- **Best for:** Whole-page redesign passes — the audit half of any homepage rebuild (directly relevant to redesign-style portfolio builds). Its upgrade techniques map to hero (text-mask reveals, outlined-to-fill type), work/gallery (parallax card stacks), and general polish (spotlight borders, grain, tinted shadows).
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0641⟧

## ⟦S0642⟧ open-design/reference-design-contract — Part 17 — MCP Market — open-design skills
- **What it is:** A pre-build process skill: when a client gives taste signals or a rough "like this" reference, it turns them into three written files — a reusable `DESIGN.md`, a `design-contract.md` decision record, and a short `implementation-handoff.md` — before any page is generated. Documents, not a page design.
- **How it looks:** No on-screen output of its own. Optionally it produces a small hand-built `example.html` contract preview, explicitly not the main deliverable. The `DESIGN.md` it writes uses exactly nine headings: 1. Visual Theme & Atmosphere, 2. Color, 3. Typography, 4. Spacing & Grid, 5. Layout & Composition, 6. Components, 7. Motion & Interaction, 8. Voice & Brand, 9. Anti-patterns.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. (Motion attitude is one of the things the contract records under "Keep" — density, composition, material, typography rhythm, colour temperature, motion attitude.)
- **Mechanism & key values:** 8-step workflow: lock the job (ask at most two questions, only when a missing answer would change direction; otherwise pick a labelled inferred default) → read evidence (screenshots, URLs, existing DESIGN.md, brand docs; say so if evidence is missing, never invent brand facts) → split every reference into Keep / Change / Do-not-copy → freeze ONE coherent visual stance (not five moodboards; if directions compete, name them, pick the recommended one, continue) → write the three files → validate against a P0 checklist (nine headings present; every reference split Keep/Change/Do-not-copy; inferences labelled; handoff short enough to paste into the next run; anti-patterns are exact things, not vague phrases). The contract file carries an evidence table with confidence labels `observed` / `provided` / `inferred`.
- **Reference / source:** Open Design collection (`open-design/reference-design-contract`); bundled reference file `reference-design-contract/references/checklist.md`. No external site named.
- **Best for:** The planning stage before any homepage build that starts from a reference site or client taste signals — it is the paperwork form of "copy the mechanism, then adapt it": references are decomposed into keep/change/do-not-copy before building.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0642⟧

## ⟦S0647⟧ open-design/soft-skill — Part 17 — MCP Market — open-design skills
- **What it is:** A complete premium-UI generation system ("Principal UI/UX Architect & Motion Choreographer"): before coding, it rolls a "Creative Variance Engine" — one vibe/texture archetype × one layout archetype — then builds with nested "double-bezel" components, pill buttons with nested icon discs, a floating glass nav, and spring-style cubic-bezier motion throughout.
- **How it looks:** One of three texture worlds: (1) Ethereal Glass — near-black `#050505` background, subtle glowing purple/emerald radial mesh orbs, vantablack cards with heavy `backdrop-blur-2xl` and white/10 hairlines, wide grotesk type; (2) Editorial Luxury — warm cream `#FDFBF7`, muted sage or deep espresso, high-contrast variable serif display type, a film-grain overlay at `opacity-[0.03]`; (3) Soft Structuralism — silver-grey or white ground, massive bold grotesk, airy floating components with very soft diffused shadows. Layouts: Asymmetrical Bento (mixed grid spans, e.g. `col-span-8 row-span-2` beside stacked `col-span-4` cards), Z-Axis Cascade (cards overlapping like physical cards, some rotated `-2deg`/`3deg`), or Editorial Split (massive type on the left half, scrollable horizontal image pills / staggered cards on the right). Every major card is a "double-bezel": an outer shell (faint `bg-black/5` or `bg-white/5`, hairline ring, `p-1.5`–`p-2` padding, `rounded-[2rem]`) holding an inner core with its own background, an inset top highlight `shadow-[inset_0_1px_1px_rgba(255,255,255,0.15)]`, and a smaller concentric radius `rounded-[calc(2rem-0.375rem)]`. Primary buttons are full pills (`rounded-full px-6 py-3`); an arrow never sits loose — it lives inside its own `w-8 h-8 rounded-full` disc flush at the button's right edge. Section heads are preceded by a micro eyebrow pill (`text-[10px] uppercase tracking-[0.2em]`, `px-3 py-1`). Sections breathe: `py-24` to `py-40`. Banned outright: Inter/Roboto/Arial/Open Sans/Helvetica (use Geist, Clash Display, PP Editorial New, Plus Jakarta Sans), thick Lucide/FontAwesome/Material icons (ultra-light lines only — Phosphor Light, Remix Line), generic 1px grey borders, harsh dark shadows, edge-to-edge sticky navbars, symmetrical 3-column grids.
- **Frame by frame:** All transitions use custom cubic-beziers — the house curve is `cubic-bezier(0.32,0.72,0,1)` at `duration-700`; `linear` and `ease-in-out` are banned. Nav: at rest the navbar is a floating glass pill detached from the top (`mt-6`, `mx-auto`, `w-max`, `rounded-full`). Click the hamburger → its 2–3 lines rotate/translate into an X (`rotate-45` / `-rotate-45`) → a full-screen glass overlay opens (`backdrop-blur-3xl`, `bg-black/80` or `bg-white/80`) → nav links cascade in from `translate-y-12 opacity-0` to rest with staggered delays (`delay-100`, `delay-150`, `delay-200`…). Button hover: the button itself presses to `active:scale-[0.98]`; the nested icon disc slides diagonally (`translate-x-1`, `-translate-y-[1px]`) and scales to `scale-105`. Scroll entry: elements start at `translate-y-16 blur-md opacity-0` and resolve to `translate-y-0 blur-0 opacity-100` over 800ms+ via IntersectionObserver / Framer Motion `whileInView` (scroll listeners are banned). Only `transform` and `opacity` animate; `backdrop-blur` only on fixed/sticky elements; grain only on a fixed `pointer-events-none` overlay.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Tailwind utility system. Mobile law: any asymmetric layout collapses below 768px to single column (`w-full`, `px-4`, `py-8`); Z-axis rotations and overlaps are removed below 768px; full-height sections use `min-h-[100dvh]`, never `h-screen`. Execution sequence: roll variance → scaffold (texture, whitespace, type scale) → architect (double-bezel everywhere) → choreograph (beziers, staggered nav, button physics) → output. A pre-output checklist re-verifies every ban and value above.
- **Reference / source:** Open Design collection (`open-design/soft-skill`); no external upstream named. Fonts/tools it assumes: Geist, Clash Display, PP Editorial New, Plus Jakarta Sans; Phosphor Light / Remix Line icons; Framer Motion.
- **Best for:** Whole-homepage art direction with a premium consumer/agency feel — hero, navigation (floating pill + full-screen menu), cards/feature grids (double-bezel + bento), CTA buttons (button-in-button). The Editorial Luxury archetype is the closest fit for a high-end trades homepage; the mobile-collapse rules are explicit, which suits phone-first trade traffic.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0647⟧

## ⟦S0649⟧ open-design/stitch-skill — Part 17 — MCP Market — open-design skills
- **What it is:** A generator of `DESIGN.md` files for Google Stitch: it translates the anti-slop taste-skill rule set (same family as ⟦S0650⟧/⟦S0651⟧) into Stitch's semantic, natural-language design format — descriptive colour/type/component rules with exact values — so Stitch generates screens in one consistent premium system. The bank bundles a complete worked example, the "Taste Standard" DESIGN.md.
- **How it looks:** The system it encodes (from the bundled example): a restrained, gallery-airy page — Canvas White `#F9FAFB` ground, Pure Surface `#FFFFFF` cards, Charcoal Ink `#18181B` text (never pure black), Steel Secondary `#71717A` body text, Muted Slate `#94A3B8` tertiary, Whisper Borders `rgba(226,232,240,0.5)`, diffused shadows `rgba(0,0,0,0.05)` (40px blur, -15px offset; card form `0 20px 40px -15px rgba(0,0,0,0.05)`). Exactly ONE accent per project, saturation under 80% — the example offers Emerald Signal `#10B981`, Electric Blue `#3B82F6`, Deep Rose `#E11D48`, or Amber Warmth `#F59E0B`. Type: Geist/Satoshi/Cabinet Grotesk/Outfit display, track-tight `-0.025em`, leading 1.1, weight 700–900, display size `clamp(2.25rem, 5vw, 3.75rem)`; body 1rem–1.125rem at leading 1.65, max 65ch; mono (Geist Mono/JetBrains Mono) 0.8125rem for metadata — and ALL numbers switch to mono when density exceeds 7. Inter is banned; generic serifs (Times, Georgia, Garamond, Palatino) banned — modern serifs only (Fraunces, Gambarino, Editorial New, Instrument Serif) and never in dashboards. Cards: `2.5rem` radius, 2rem–2.5rem internal padding, used only when elevation means hierarchy (high-density layouts swap cards for border-top dividers). Hero signature: small photos embedded inline between words of the headline at type height, rounded, as visual punctuation; no overlapping elements anywhere; no centred hero at high variance (split screen / left-aligned / asymmetric whitespace instead); max one primary CTA; no "Scroll to explore" filler. Layout: CSS Grid only (no flexbox percentage math), max-width 1400px, padding 1rem/2rem/4rem by breakpoint, bento feature grids (Row 1: 3 columns, Row 2: 2 columns 70/30), the 3-equal-cards row banned.
- **Frame by frame:** Stitch itself generates static screens; the DESIGN.md records intended motion for the later coding agent. Intended behaviour: spring physics on interactive elements (`stiffness: 100, damping: 20`, no linear easing); lists/grids mount with cascaded stagger (`animation-delay: calc(var(--index) * 100ms)`); every active component carries a perpetual micro-loop (Pulse on status dots, Typewriter on search bars, Float on feature icons, Shimmer on loaders — skeletal shimmer matched to layout, never round spinners); layout changes reorder smoothly via shared element IDs; buttons give tactile feedback (`-1px translateY` or `scale(0.98)` on `:active`). Only `transform`/`opacity` animate; grain/noise only on fixed pointer-events-none pseudo-elements.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Four configuration dials set per project — Creativity, Density, Variance, Motion Intent, each 1–10; bundled defaults: Creativity 8, Density 4, Variance 8, Motion 6 (the skill body defaults Variance 8 / Motion 6 / Density 4). Responsive law: below 768px everything collapses to one column (`width: 100%`, `padding: 1rem`, `gap: 1.5rem`), no horizontal scroll ever, touch targets minimum 44px, buttons full-width on mobile, inline headline images stack below the headline, section gaps scale as `clamp(3rem, 8vw, 6rem)`; verify at 375px, 390px, 768px, 1024px, 1440px. Full-height sections `min-height: 100dvh`, never `h-screen`. Output document structure: 9 sections (Visual Theme & Atmosphere; Color Palette & Roles; Typography Rules; Component Stylings; Layout Principles; Motion & Interaction; Anti-Patterns; plus hero and responsive rules folded through). Prerequisite: access to Google Stitch (labs.google.com/stitch); optional Stitch MCP server.
- **Reference / source:** Open Design collection (`open-design/stitch-skill`), upstream https://labs.google.com/stitch; bundled reference file `stitch-skill/DESIGN.md` (the full "Taste Standard" example). Rule lineage: the taste-skill family — see ⟦S0650⟧ (current) and ⟦S0651⟧ (v1).
- **Best for:** Producing the design-system document that drives a whole build — the front-of-project artifact for any homepage (all sections inherit it). The bundled example values (palette, type scale, card geometry, hero rule) are directly reusable as a starting system for a trade homepage even without Stitch.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0649⟧

## ⟦S0650⟧ open-design/taste-skill — Part 17 — MCP Market — open-design skills
- **What it is:** The current (v2) "tasteskill" anti-slop frontend system for landing pages, portfolios, and redesigns (explicitly NOT dashboards, data tables, or multi-step product UI). It starts by reading the brief and stating a one-line "Design Read", sets three dials (DESIGN_VARIANCE / MOTION_INTENSITY / VISUAL_DENSITY), then enforces a large rulebook of layout, type, colour, content, and motion law plus a mechanical pre-flight checklist. ⟦S0651⟧ is its earlier version — same underlying skill.
- **How it looks:** Output is gated by the dials (baseline VARIANCE 8 / MOTION 6 / DENSITY 4; inference table maps briefs to values — minimalist/clean 5-6/3-4/2-3, premium consumer 7-8/5-7/3-4, playful/Awwwards 9-10/8-10/3-4, trust-first/public-sector 3-4/2-3/4-5). The page it produces: asymmetric hero that FITS the first viewport — headline max 2 lines, subtext max 20 words and 3–4 lines, CTA visible without scrolling, top padding capped at `pt-24`, max 4 hero text elements total (eyebrow OR brand strip, headline, subtext, CTAs — no tagline under the CTAs, no trust strip, no avatar row inside the hero; the logo wall goes in its own section directly below, as real SVG logos only, no category labels under them). Type defaults `text-4xl md:text-6xl tracking-tighter leading-none` for display, body `text-base leading-relaxed max-w-[65ch]`; heroes with 3–5-word headlines may go `text-6xl md:text-7xl`, a 4-line headline is always a font-size error. Sans-first discipline: Inter discouraged (Geist, Outfit, Cabinet Grotesk, Satoshi preferred); serif is heavily discouraged as a default and Fraunces + Instrument Serif are banned as defaults — emphasis inside a headline is italic/bold of the SAME font, never an injected serif word; italic words with descenders (y g j p q) need `leading-[1.1]` minimum plus `pb-1` reserve. Colour: max 1 accent locked across the WHOLE page, saturation < 80%, neutral Zinc/Slate/Stone bases; the "AI purple/blue glow" is banned as a default; and for premium-consumer briefs the beige+brass palette family is banned by hex (backgrounds `#f5f1ea`, `#f7f5f1`, `#fbf8f1`, `#efeae0`, `#ece6db`, `#faf7f1`, `#e8dfcb`; accents `#b08947`, `#b6553a`, `#9a2436`, `#9c6e2a`, `#bc7c3a`, `#7d5621`; text `#1a1714` family) with named rotation alternatives (Cold Luxury, Forest, Black and Tan, Cobalt + Cream, Terracotta + Slate, Olive + Brick + Paper, monochrome + one saturated pop). One theme per page (no section flips light/dark mid-page), one corner-radius system per page. Layout law: nav on ONE line at desktop, height max 80px (default 64–72px); eyebrows rationed to max 1 per 3 sections (hero counts as 1; mechanically count `uppercase tracking` labels ≤ ceil(sections/3)); the "left headline + right small paragraph" split-header is banned (stack vertically instead); max 2 consecutive image+text zigzag sections; a layout family may appear at most once per page (≥4 different families across 8 sections); bento grids have exactly as many cells as content items, with 2–3 cells carrying real visual variation (image/gradient/pattern), never all white-on-white text. Content law: section shape = headline ≤ 8 words + sub-paragraph ≤ 25 words + one visual or one CTA; lists over 5 items must change component (card grid, tabs, scroll-snap pills, carousel, marquee), spec tables with a hairline under every row are banned (use 2-col spec cards, grouped chunks, or featured-vs-rest); quotes max 3 lines with name + role attribution and real typographic quotes; fake-precise invented numbers banned; images are mandatory — image-generation tool first, then real photos (`picsum.photos/seed/{descriptive-seed}/{w}/{h}`), real brand logos via Simple Icons (`https://cdn.simpleicons.org/{slug}/ffffff`) — never div-based fake screenshots or hand-rolled decorative SVGs. The single most emphasised ban: the em-dash character `—` (and en-dash as separator) is COMPLETELY banned everywhere visible — headlines, eyebrows, pills, buttons, captions, quotes, alt text; hyphens only. Also banned: version labels in heroes (V0.6, BETA), section-number eyebrows (`001 · Capabilities`), scroll cues, decorative status dots, locale/weather strips, pills overlaid on images, decorative photo credits, version footers, decoration text strips at hero bottom (`BRAND. MOTION. SPATIAL.`), filled-track progress bars as comparisons.
- **Frame by frame:** Motion must be motivated (hierarchy / storytelling / feedback / state transition) and dial-matched: if MOTION_INTENSITY > 4 the page must actually move; marquees max ONE per page. Canonical patterns with code: (a) GSAP Sticky-Stack — each card (except the last) pins at `start: "top top"` with `pin: true, pinSpacing: false`, and as the next card arrives the pinned card scales to `scale: 0.92` and fades to `opacity: 0.55`, scrubbed by the next card's trigger (`start: "top bottom"`, `end: "top top"`). (b) GSAP Horizontal-Pan — wrapper pins at `start: "top top"`, inner track translates `x` by -(track width − viewport width), `end: "+=${distance}"`, `scrub: 1`, `invalidateOnRefresh: true`. (c) Scroll-reveal stagger (Motion `whileInView`, the lighter default): items rise `y: 24 → 0` and fade in over 0.6s with `delay: i * 0.06`, ease `[0.16, 1, 0.3, 1]`, `viewport: { once: true, amount: 0.3 }`. Springs default `stiffness: 100, damping: 20`. Magnetic buttons and perpetual micro-interactions only when MOTION_INTENSITY > 5, built on Motion `useMotionValue`/`useTransform` — never `useState` for continuous values, never `window.addEventListener("scroll")` (hard ban), never mixed GSAP/Three.js + Motion in one component tree. Liquid Glass, when the read calls for it: `backdrop-filter` + 1px inner border `border-white/10` + inner shadow `shadow-[inset_0_1px_0_rgba(255,255,255,0.1)]`, with a solid fallback under `prefers-reduced-transparency` (an appendix supplies a full labelled web-approximation CSS skeleton: blur(24px) saturate(180%) contrast(1.05), inset highlights, dark-mode variant). Anything above MOTION_INTENSITY 3 must collapse under `prefers-reduced-motion`. Performance targets: LCP < 2.5s, INP < 200ms, CLS < 0.1; grain/noise only on fixed pointer-events-none pseudo-elements.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Stack defaults: React/Next.js RSC with interactive parts isolated as `'use client'` leaves; Tailwind v4 (`@tailwindcss/postcss`, not the old postcss plugin); animation via Motion (`motion/react` import; `framer-motion` is the legacy alias); fonts via `next/font` or self-hosted `@font-face` with `font-display: swap`. Breakpoints sm 640 / md 768 / lg 1024 / xl 1280 / 2xl 1536; container `max-w-[1400px] mx-auto`; `min-h-[100dvh]` never `h-screen`; CSS Grid never flex percentage math. Icons: Phosphor, HugeIcons, Radix, Tabler (priority order); Lucide discouraged; one family per project, one global strokeWidth (1.5 or 2.0); never hand-drawn SVG icons. Design-system honesty table: real briefs map to official packages (Fluent UI, @material/web, Carbon, Polaris, Atlaskit, Primer, govuk-frontend, uswds, Bootstrap 5.3, Radix Themes, shadcn/ui) — install the official package, one system per project; aesthetic directions (glassmorphism, bento, brutalism, editorial, dark tech, aurora, kinetic type) are built natively and labelled as inspiration, not official systems. Dial definitions: VARIANCE 1-3 symmetrical 12-col, 4-7 offsets (`margin-top: -2rem` overlaps, mixed aspect ratios), 8-10 masonry/fractional grids (`2fr 1fr 1fr`) and massive empty zones (`padding-left: 20vw`), with mandatory single-column collapse < 768px; MOTION 4-7 = `transition: all 0.3s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)` + delay cascades, 8-10 = GSAP ScrollTrigger / CSS scroll-driven animation; DENSITY 1-3 = `py-32`–`py-48` gaps, 4-7 = `py-16`–`py-24`, 8-10 = tight, mono for all numbers, cards banned above density 7. Buttons/forms a11y: CTA text WCAG AA (4.5:1 body, 3:1 large), CTA labels never wrap at desktop (max ~3 words), one label per CTA intent across the whole page; labels above inputs, errors below, `gap-2`. Redesign protocol: detect greenfield vs preserve vs overhaul; audit brand tokens/IA/content/SEO first; never silently change URL slugs, nav labels, form field names/order, logo, or legal copy; modernisation levers in order (typography → spacing → colour → motion layer → hero recomposition → block replacement). A Section-10 pattern vocabulary names the reusable moves (Asymmetric Split / Editorial Manifesto / Video-Mask / Kinetic-Type / Curtain-Reveal / Scroll-Pinned heroes; Dock Magnification, Gooey Menu, Dynamic Island, Mega Menu; Bento, Chroma Grid, Split-Screen Scroll, Sticky-Stack; Parallax Tilt, Spotlight Border, Holographic Foil, Tinder Swipe, Morphing Modal; Horizontal Hijack, Locomotive Sequence, Zoom Parallax, Scroll Progress Path; Dome Gallery, Coverflow, Drag-to-Pan, Accordion Slider, Hover Image Trail; Kinetic Marquee, Text Mask, Scramble, Circular Text, Gradient Stroke; Particle Button, Skeleton Shimmer, Directional Hover, Ripple, SVG Line Drawing, Mesh Gradient, Lens Blur). Ships with install-command and canonical-docs appendices per design system. Ends in a ~60-item mechanical Pre-Flight Check — any unticked box means not done.
- **Reference / source:** Open Design collection (`open-design/taste-skill`, "tasteskill"). Appendices cite the official docs/repos of Material Web, Fluent UI, Carbon, Polaris, Atlassian, Primer, GOV.UK, USWDS, Bootstrap, Tailwind, Radix, shadcn/ui, MDN/W3C scroll-animations drafts, and Apple HIG Liquid Glass docs. Earlier version: ⟦S0651⟧.
- **Best for:** The governing design law for an entire homepage build — hero discipline, section-layout variety, proof/logo walls, work galleries, forms, CTA consistency, and the final QA checklist. Its GSAP skeletons serve process (sticky-stack) and work/gallery (horizontal pan) sections; its vocabulary names most section mechanisms a builder would shortlist. For trade homepages: note its audience is landing/portfolio work, and its palette/serif bans are defaults with stated brand-brief overrides.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0650⟧

## ⟦S0651⟧ open-design/taste-skill-v1 — Part 17 — MCP Market — open-design skills
- **What it is:** SAME underlying skill as ⟦S0650⟧ taste-skill — this is its earlier version (v1, "High-Agency Frontend Skill"). Same three dials at the same baseline (DESIGN_VARIANCE 8, MOTION_INTENSITY 6, VISUAL_DENSITY 4), same architecture conventions, same bias-correction rules, same AI-tells bans in earlier, shorter form. Full detail lives in the ⟦S0650⟧ entry; read that one. This entry records only what v1 states differently or uniquely.
- **How it looks:** As ⟦S0650⟧, with these v1-specifics: icons restricted to exactly `@phosphor-icons/react` or `@radix-ui/react-icons` import paths; fluid-CSS motion band defined as `transition: all 0.3s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)` (kept in v2); dial bands defined identically (variance 8-10 = masonry, `2fr 1fr 1fr` grids, `padding-left: 20vw` empty zones; density 8-10 = mono for all numbers, cards banned).
- **Frame by frame:** As ⟦S0650⟧ (springs `stiffness: 100, damping: 20`; stagger via `staggerChildren` or `animation-delay: calc(var(--index) * 100ms)`; magnetic hover only via Framer Motion motion values; no `window.addEventListener('scroll')` at MOTION 8-10). V1's unique motion content is the "Motion-Engine Bento" below.
- **Mechanism & key values:** UNIQUE TO V1 — Section 9, the "Motion-Engine Bento Paradigm" (Bento 2.0) for SaaS/feature grids: background `#f9fafb`; cards pure white `#ffffff` with 1px `border-slate-200/50`; `rounded-[2.5rem]` containers; diffusion shadow `shadow-[0_20px_40px_-15px_rgba(0,0,0,0.05)]`; card titles/descriptions placed OUTSIDE and BELOW the cards (gallery style); `p-8`–`p-10` card padding; grid shape Row 1: 3 columns, Row 2: 2 columns split 70/30. Every card must contain a perpetual micro-interaction, isolated in its own memoized Client Component (60fps, `AnimatePresence` on dynamic lists), from 5 named archetypes: (1) The Intelligent List — items endlessly auto-sort/reorder via `layoutId`, simulating live prioritisation; (2) The Command Input — typewriter cycling through prompts with blinking cursor and a shimmering "processing" state; (3) The Live Status — breathing status dots plus a notification badge that pops in with an overshoot spring, stays 3 seconds, vanishes; (4) The Wide Data Stream — seamless infinite carousel of metric cards looping `x: ["0%", "-100%"]`; (5) The Contextual UI (Focus Mode) — a document view where a text block highlights in stagger, then a floating micro-icon toolbar floats in. V1's pre-flight check is a short 7-item list (v2 expands it to ~60).
- **Reference / source:** Open Design collection (`open-design/taste-skill-v1`). Superseded by ⟦S0650⟧.

## ⟦S0652⟧ open-design/ui-animation — Part 17 — MCP Market — open-design skills
- **What it is:** A complete UI-motion engineering skill — the largest in this range (main text + 18 bundled reference files + 3 measurement scripts). It designs, implements, reviews, and debugs interface animation (easing, springs, gestures, drag, scroll motion, SVG), sweeps an interface for moments that deserve motion, reverse-engineers motion from a screen recording (frame extraction → tracking → curve fitting → code + handoff spec), names described effects from a glossary, and gates sparse interface sound. It is a motion-craft reference, not a visual-direction system.
- **How it looks:** Applied well, the visitor sees: controls that press instantly and subtly (button dips to `scale(0.97)` the moment it is touched, no delay); menus, popovers and tooltips that grow out of the exact element that opened them (never from screen centre, never from `scale(0)` — they start at `scale(0.9–0.96)` with a fade); a button whose label becomes "Copied" in place instead of a toast popping up in a far corner; drawers that slide in on a steep iOS-like curve; tabs and wizard steps that slide in the direction of travel (forward = leftward, back = rightward); lists whose items cascade in 30–50ms apart; numbers that pop in digit by digit or roll like an odometer in the direction the value moved; a hold-to-delete button that fills with colour over 2 seconds while held and snaps back on release; before/after style comparison images wiped by a draggable clip edge; SVG strokes that draw themselves; success moments where a check path draws itself while the badge rotates in from 80° with a springy bob. Motion the skill forbids the visitor from ever seeing: scroll-reveals on every section, animations on keyboard/high-frequency actions, marquees of motion with no purpose, scroll hijacking.
- **Frame by frame:** Core choreography rules: enter slightly slower, exit faster and simpler (exit ≈20% faster, same direction as entry); high-frequency ephemeral UI inverts — enter at 0ms, exit with a 100–150ms fade; paired elements (modal + overlay, tooltip + arrow) share easing and duration exactly; staggers run 30–50ms per item, total under 300ms, most important element leading (page-level entrances use 80ms per word / 100ms per section: each word/block rises 8px, un-blurs from 5px, fades in over 800ms on `cubic-bezier(0.25, 0.46, 0.45, 0.94)`). Press: `:active` fires at 0ms with `scale(0.96–0.98)` (recipe: 160ms `cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1)` transition, duration forced to 0s while pressed) and `touch-action: manipulation`. Toast: rises `translate3d(0, 6px, 0)` + fade over 220ms, enter/exit same direction. Crossfade swap: outgoing/incoming overlap with an 8px rise and 4px blur over 150ms ease-out (a 2px blur masks rough crossfades generally). Icon swap (copy→check etc.): both icons animate opacity + scale 0.8↔1 + blur 4px↔0 together, spring `duration: 0.2, bounce: 0`, exit completes before enter (`mode="wait"`). List removal: exiting item leaves flow immediately (`AnimatePresence mode="popLayout"`) and fades/scales to 0.8 over 0.15s while siblings reflow in parallel. Step forms: panels travel x ±100 with fade over 0.2s. Card flip: `rotateY(180deg)` over 400ms with `preserve-3d`, parent `perspective: 1000px`. Peripheral de-emphasis: hovering one chip blurs/fades its SIBLINGS to `opacity: 0.5, blur(2px)` while the hovered chip scales to 1.04 (blur kept at 2–3px, never past ~4px). Subtle exits use a fixed −12px offset regardless of element height (spring `duration: 0.45, bounce: 0`); full-height exits are reserved for presence-building entries. Clip-path family: inset reveal wipes over 300ms; tab colour overlay slides its clip over 200ms; scroll image reveal un-clips bottom-to-top over 800ms `cubic-bezier(0.77, 0, 0.175, 1)` when 10% visible (rootMargin −100px); comparison slider = top image clipped by `inset(0 var(--split) 0 0)` following the drag handle. Scroll-triggered reveals (marketing only, 2–4 moments per page, never product UI, never above the fold): element rises `translateY(10–16px)` + fades over 400–600ms with strong ease-out, triggered when ~10–20% into the viewport (`rootMargin: "0px 0px -10% 0px"`), siblings staggered 80–120ms like a wave (heading leads, distance varies by importance), plays ONCE, never re-fires on scroll-up. Scrubbed/scroll-driven motion has NO duration and NO easing (`linear` only — scroll position is the clock): CSS `animation-timeline: view()`/`scroll()` first (inside an `@supports` guard), Motion `useScroll` second, raw scroll listeners never. Parallax differential ≤ ~15% of scroll distance, transform-only, decorative layers only, skipped on mobile. Sticky scrollytelling pins ≤ ~2–3 viewport heights, progress maps monotonically, always scroll-past-able. Drag/gesture: element locked 1:1 to the pointer with NO easing during the drag (grab offset preserved — the point grabbed stays under the finger; pointer capture set on down; axis committed only after ~10px of travel and held until release; extra touch points ignored); on release the animation inherits the finger's exact velocity. Dismissal is velocity-led: flick speed > 0.11 px/ms dismisses on its own (sign checked — a flick back toward open cancels even past the distance threshold), slow releases fall back to a distance threshold (~20px minimum to avoid accidents); the target is chosen by momentum projection `project(v) = (v/1000) · 0.998/(1−0.998)` (≈ ×499 of v in px/s terms), not by the release point. Past a boundary, movement damps instead of stopping: `max · (1 − exp(−offset/max))`, Apple's rubber-band `(overshoot · dimension · 0.55) / (dimension + 0.55 · |overshoot|)`, or flat 0.3× friction at the boundary. Detents (ruler/tick pickers): value follows the pointer continuously during drag, snaps only on release to the detent nearest the projected landing (`value + velocity · 0.15`), spring `stiffness: 500, damping: 40`, with the passing tick scaling/darkening as feedback. Rotary knobs track angle from centre with ±180° wrap normalisation; accumulated turns are clamped, never the per-frame angle. Carousels: CSS scrollers take `touch-action: pan-x` + `overscroll-behavior-x: contain`; JS libraries (Embla/Swiper) keep `pan-y` — do not override. SVG: line drawing animates `stroke-dashoffset` to 0 over 0.6s on the enter curve, path normalised with `pathLength="100"`, dash 1px / gap 1.1px so round caps don't peek, `animation-fill-mode: forwards`; rotations/scales apply to a `<g>` with `transform-box: fill-box; transform-origin: center` (SVG's default origin is the viewBox corner); path morphs need identical point structure (else the `flubber` library); ambient idle life uses non-syncing loops (float 1.5px over 3s, rotate 2° over 4s, ~2s initial delay, paused off-screen).
- **Mechanism & key values:** Easing defaults table — button press 100–160ms; tooltips/small popovers 125–200ms; dropdowns/selects 150–250ms; modals/drawers 200–350ms; on-screen moves 200–300ms; page transitions 250–400ms; hover colour/opacity 200ms `ease`; hover transform 100–150ms; illustrative/marketing up to 1000ms; routine UI stays under 300ms and duration scales with distance. Named curves — Enter `cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1)`; Move `cubic-bezier(0.25, 1, 0.5, 1)`; Drawer (iOS-like) `cubic-bezier(0.32, 0.72, 0, 1)` (so steep its 500ms feels fast — most distance covered in the first 200ms); Expo out `cubic-bezier(0.19, 1, 0.22, 1)`; Press `cubic-bezier(0.25, 0.46, 0.45, 0.94)`; On-screen move `cubic-bezier(0.645, 0.045, 0.355, 1)`. `ease-in` is banned for UI (starts slow = feels sluggish). Implementation priority: CSS transitions > WAAPI > CSS keyframes > JS/rAF (transitions retarget on interruption; keyframes restart from zero — keyframes only for predetermined sequences). Springs: parameters stiffness 100–500, damping 15–40, mass 0.5–2; presets Snappy 500/40, Bouncy 300/20, Gentle 200/30, Stiff 700/50; Apple framing — damping ratio 1.0 = critically damped default, ~0.8 only when the gesture carried momentum; Apple's shipped values: Move/PiP damping 1.0 response 0.4, Rotation 0.8/0.4, Drawer/sheet 0.8/0.3; Motion's `{ type: "spring", bounce, duration }` maps to damping/response; SwiftUI `response = 2π·√(m/k)`, `dampingFraction = c/(2·√(k·m))`. Asymmetry measured on a real container morph at 60fps: open reaches 121% of travel at 284ms, container overshoots to 9.8% wider than rest, settles by 584ms — fitted spring `stiffness: 155, damping: 11` (ζ 0.44); close undershoots ~2% at 185ms, at rest by 300ms — `stiffness: 620, damping: 36` (ζ ~0.75), for which `cubic-bezier(0.32, 0.72, 0, 1)` substitutes cleanly. Bounce belongs to the open only; the close stays near-critically damped. The 14 transition recipes share one `:root` token block; key tokens — container morph: open 580ms with the overshoot transcribed as `linear(0, 0.45, 0.78, 1, 1.17, 1.21, 1.18, 1.12, 1.05, 1.02, 1)`, close 300ms on the drawer curve, content cross-blur 140ms at 3px, incoming content delayed 140ms; card resize 300ms; panel reveal open 400ms / close 350ms, 12px rise, 4px blur (drawer variant 240ms on the move curve, `translateY(100%)`); dropdown open 250ms / close 150ms from `scale(0.96)` (never below `scale(0.92)`), tooltip 125ms from `scale(0.97)` with first-show delay 300–500ms then instant for siblings; modal open 250ms / close 150ms from `scale(0.96)`, origin centre, `@starting-style` entry (Baseline since Aug 2024); notification badge slide 260ms from offset (−8px, +12px) with 2px blur, dot pop 500ms delayed by half the slide; text swap 150ms, 4px, 2px blur, three-phase JS with forced reflow; page slide 200ms, 8px, 3px blur, 60ms stagger; number pop-in 500ms, 12px travel, 70ms per-digit stagger, 6px blur; odometer roll 260ms, changed digits only, `tabular-nums` mandatory; icon swap 200ms from `scale(0.25)` with 2px blur; avatar group hover lift −4px over 320ms, hovered scale 1.05, neighbour falloff ×0.45 per step of distance, bouncy return ease `cubic-bezier(0.34, 3.85, 0.64, 1)`; success celebration 550ms across opacity/rotate/bob/blur (rotate from 80deg, bob 40px, blur from 10px, bob ease `cubic-bezier(0.34, 3.85, 0.64, 1)`), check path draws over 550ms after an 80ms delay, path length measured with `getTotalLength()` — never hardcoded; error shake segments 80/80/60ms at distance 4px / overshoot 2px on `cubic-bezier(0.36, 0.07, 0.19, 0.97)`, border reverts over 200ms, error state holds 1200ms, `.is-error` and `.is-shaking` kept as separate classes. Decision framework: frequency decides first — 100+ uses/day = no animation ever; tens/day = remove or drastically reduce; occasional = standard; rare/first-time = delight allowed; novelty budget ≈90% expected / 10% novel, one-shots gated so reloads are instant; purpose must be feedback, orientation, continuity, or deliberate delight. Discovery sweep: six seam classes (feedback gap, teleporting state, missing spatial story, group entrance, gesture seam, flat delight moment) grepped with file:line evidence; report = 5–7 survivors with exact values PLUS 2–5 deliberate rejections naming the question that killed each. Performance law: animate `transform`/`opacity` only (paint-tier swaps — `scale()` for width/height, `translate()` for margins, `drop-shadow` filter for box-shadow, clip-path inset-round for border-radius); never `transition: all`; blur ≤ 20px; CSS variables on a parent must never drive child transforms (recalc storm — set `transform` on the element); `will-change` toggled only during motion; looping animations paused off-screen via IntersectionObserver; long tasks (>50ms) sharing the tick are the usual cause of intermittent jank — defer work to `transitionend` or chunk it under a ~5ms-per-frame budget with `scheduler.yield()`. Accessibility: hover gated behind `@media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)`; reduced motion must be handled in JS too (`<MotionConfig reducedMotion="user">` / `useReducedMotion()`), replacing spatial travel with fades — a global `transition: none !important` is also wrong (it strips kept feedback); looping decorations pause via `animation-play-state: paused`, not `display: none`; theme switches disable transitions during the flip. Review mode: ten non-negotiable standards with flag-on-sight triggers, a mandatory Before/After/Why table, a remedial hierarchy (delete → reduce → fix easing → fix origin → make interruptible → move to GPU → asymmetric timing → polish → accessibility), and a Block/Approve verdict citing file:line. Debugging: symptom tables (sluggish / robotic / cheap / janky / jumps / flickers) with ordered causes — tune easing before duration. Reverse-engineering pipeline: `scripts/extract_frames.py` (ffmpeg) → contact sheet → vision pass → `scripts/track_motion.py` (OpenCV; metrics.json per-frame x/y/width/height/cx/cy/opacity/blur/radius proxies) → `scripts/fit_curves.py` (scipy; spring + bezier fits per property) → choreography table (first-change and settle frame per property; lead/lag gaps carry the feel) → code emitted for CSS (springs sampled into `linear()`), Motion, SwiftUI, Reanimated, UIKit (`CASpringAnimation` settlingDuration) plus a written handoff spec per direction. Fit error < 0.03 tight, 0.03–0.08 decent, > 0.08 suspect (usually multi-phase — split and fit segments); `fit_curves.py` defaults to 30fps and MUST be passed the extraction fps or durations double and stiffness quarters; never sample above the source rate. Interface SFX rules: gesture-unlocked AudioContext only, gain ~0.1–0.2, clips of tens of milliseconds, additive to visual feedback, silent for high-frequency actions, skipped under reduced-motion, all routed through one `play(id)` helper. Vocabulary reference: ~70-term reverse-lookup glossary (entrances, sequencing, transforms, transitions, scroll, feedback, easing, springs, loops, polish, performance, principles).
- **Reference / source:** Open Design collection (`open-design/ui-animation`). Upstream: https://github.com/mblode/agent-skills/tree/5a781a88ed60c1033767b6b6a966887cd93dd912/skills/ui-animation (commit `5a781a88`, MIT licence, per its bundled SOURCES.md). External anchors named inside: easing.dev and easings.co (curve catalogues), Apple's "Designing Fluid Interfaces" sample code (rubber-band + momentum projection), Sonner (flick constant 0.11), Vaul (drawer curve and 500ms), Embla/Swiper (carousel touch-action), Base UI / Radix (trigger-origin CSS variables), `flubber` (path morphing), Craft / Raphael Salaja (interface SFX sources).
- **Best for:** The motion layer of EVERY section — this is the parameter source for hero entrances (word/section stagger), call/CTA and forms (press feedback, in-place confirmation, error shake, hold-to-confirm), navigation (origin-aware dropdowns, icon swaps), proof/reviews (number pop-in and odometer count-ups), work/gallery (clip-path reveals, comparison sliders, avatar-group hover), process (page side-by-side step slides, step-form direction rules), and any drag/swipe surface. Its scroll chapter is the restraint check on scroll reveals and scrollytelling, and its review format is the motion QA gate. Applies to interactive/product-style motion most directly; its marketing-page rules (400–600ms reveals, 2–4 moments) are the ones that transfer to trade homepages.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0652⟧

## ⟦S0654⟧ open-design/vfx-text-cursor — MCP Market — open-design skills
- **What it is:** A video-intro / hero-frame effect: a cursor "types" a quote onto a dark canvas character by character, trailing chromatic-aberration ghosts and directional light flares, inspired by HyperFrames' vfx-text-cursor.
- **How it looks:** A 1920×1080 near-black frame (`#06070a`, or `#0a0d12` with a warm-blue cast) with a subtle vignette. One quote sits centred at 6–8vw, weight 700, in Inter Tight / Source Sans 3 / Noto Sans SC — never serif. Revealed text is white `#f5f5f7`. A small uppercase caption sits top ("FRAME 01 · OPENING", 11px, letter-spacing 0.18em, opacity 0.5), a 24–28px source/chapter sub-line under the quote at opacity 0.6, and a mono timecode (`00:03:21`) bottom-right. One accent only, picked from hot pink `#ff3b6f`, cyan `#00d4ff`, or amber `#ffb547`.
- **Frame by frame:** Trigger = frame start. (1) The cursor (a 16px-wide block `▍`, blinking on a 1.0s keyframe cycle, dragging a 60–120px radial-gradient motion-blur trail) advances; characters appear one at a time at 80ms intervals. (2) At the instant each character lands it carries a chromatic ghost — `text-shadow: 2px 0 #ff3b6f, -2px 0 #00d4ff` — which converges back to clean white within 200ms. (3) 3–5 directional light-leak flares (thin `linear-gradient(45deg, transparent, accent, transparent)` rectangles, `mix-blend-mode: screen`, irregular angles) flash near the typing position. (4) When the quote completes, a 0.5s shimmer sweep crosses the whole line. End state: the full quote static in white with caption, sub-line and timecode. Under `prefers-reduced-motion` all characters show at once, no typing.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Single self-contained HTML file; `@keyframes` + JS `setTimeout` per-character timer. Per-char interval 80ms; chromatic convergence 200ms; cursor blink period 1.0s; trail 60–120px; flares 3–5; shimmer 0.5s. Hard rule: binary chromatic only (one pink + cyan pair), never full R/G/B rainbow; the quote must be user-supplied, never invented.
- **Reference / source:** Inspired by HyperFrames vfx-text-cursor; bundled example uses the quote "Markdown 是给作者的中间过程, HTML 才是给读者的最终形态。" with chapter mark "FRAME 01 · OPENING" and timecode 00:03:21.
- **Best for:** Hero — a video-opening or quote-reveal frame; text-in-motion reference for a typed headline treatment. Video-first: built as a 1920×1080 frame, so web use means adapting the timing values.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0654⟧
