## ⟦S0657⟧ accessibility-baseline — MCP Market — open-design craft rules + all templates
- **What it is:** The accessibility compliance floor plus craft commitments every artifact must clear before shipping: contrast, touch targets, focus visibility, form labelling, keyboard operability, ARIA discipline, and native-mobile parity. The active DESIGN.md decides brand appearance; this file decides the legal/craft floor.
- **How it looks:** What a visitor (and an assistive-tech user) actually gets: every text readable against its background, a clearly visible focus ring when tabbing, form fields with real text labels (never placeholder-only), error text wired under the field it belongs to, buttons that are real `<button>`s, one `<h1>` with unskipped heading levels, and landmark regions (`header`/`nav`/`main`/`footer`) instead of a wall of divs.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion of its own. It constrains motion made elsewhere: flashing content may not exceed three flashes in any one-second period (WCAG 2.3.1, Level A) unless below the flash thresholds, and transform motion must honour `prefers-reduced-motion` (full rule set in ⟦S0658⟧).
- **Mechanism & key values:** Working target WCAG 2.2 AA (clears the legal floors: EU EAA = WCAG 2.1 AA via EN 301 549 v3.2.1; US ADA Title II = WCAG 2.1 AA, deadlines 2027-04-26 for jurisdictions ≥50,000 population and 2028-04-26 below; Section 508 still references WCAG 2.0 AA). Contrast minimums, thresholds inclusive, no rounding: normal text 4.5:1; large text 3:1 (large = ≥18pt regular ≈24px, or ≥14pt bold ≈18.5px — 18px regular is NOT large); non-text UI and focus indicator 3:1. APCA as design-review only: body copy Lc ≥60 reasonable, thin small text needs Lc ≥75+. Touch targets: AA floor 24×24 CSS px (SC 2.5.8, with Spacing/Equivalent/Inline/User-agent/Essential exceptions); AAA craft 44×44 (2.5.5); iOS HIG 44×44pt; Material 3 48×48dp. Focus: never remove the outline without replacement (triple failure 1.4.11/2.4.7/2.4.13); AAA indicator ≥2 CSS px perimeter at ≥3:1. Default error wiring: `<label for>` + `aria-describedby` pointing at hint AND error + `aria-invalid="true"` + error span with `role="alert"` (`aria-errormessage` is progressive enhancement only). ARIA decision order: native element → native element restyled → APG pattern verbatim → closest APG pattern + documented deviation; never invent ARIA (WebAIM Million 2026: ARIA pages average 59.1 errors vs 42 without; 51% of top-1M home pages have a missing form-input label). WCAG 3.3.7 Redundant Entry is Level A — never re-ask for data already entered in the same process.
- **Reference / source:** Grounded in WCAG 2.2 Understanding pages, ISO/IEC 40500:2025, ADA Title II 2024 + 2026 IFR, EN 301 549 v3.2.1, WAI-ARIA 1.3 + AccName 1.2 + Core AAM 1.2, WebAIM Million 2026, A11yn (arXiv 2510.13914), APCA W3C silver branch; prior art fecarrico/A11Y.md and Community-Access/accessibility-agents named.
- **Best for:** Every section, as a shipping gate — most load-bearing on forms (quote/contact), navigation, and any tappable card grid on mobile.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0657⟧

## ⟦S0658⟧ animation-discipline — MCP Market — open-design craft rules + all templates
- **What it is:** The rulebook for whether motion should run at all, and at what duration, easing and accessibility floor. Animate only when the user is moving through space, time or state (navigation, container expansion, progress feedback, gesture follow-through) — never to teach, decorate, signal "premium", or fill silence.
- **How it looks:** Motion that confirms a state change that has already happened (optimistic UI first, motion second): buttons and toggles respond almost instantly, panels and dropdowns arrive quickly, cross-screen changes take longer, and nothing decorative loops forever. Under reduced-motion settings the page swaps slides and parallax for plain opacity/colour crossfades.
- **Frame by frame:** No single animation — this file constrains all of them. A conforming interaction runs: trigger (press/hover/scroll) → motion inside the duration band for its class (below) → settle at the new state, always paired with a static affordance (colour, position, label) so the change reads without the motion. Looping/ambient motion: carousels cap at 3–5 cycles then pause; any motion running over 5 seconds needs a pause control (WCAG 2.2.2, Level A); ambient motion cancels on route change; reward bursts are one-shot; spinners stop and escalate by 60s.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Duration ladder — 50–100ms instant feedback (press, toggle, hover); 150ms default for state confirmation (the cross-system convergence: Material 3 `short3`, IBM Carbon `moderate-01`, Shopify Polaris `150`, Tailwind default, SLDS `duration-fast`); 200–300ms entering UI (modals, sheets, dropdowns); 300–500ms cross-screen transitions and container morphs; >500ms reserved for cross-screen/staged/platform-native only. Frequent animations (seen ~50×/session) ≤200ms; mobile runs 20–30% shorter than desktop. Curve vs spring: curves for opacity/colour between two known values; springs for position, scale, rotation, gesture. Material 3 standard easing `cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)` (front-loaded); M2's `cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1)` is legacy, not M3; M3 `emphasized` is a two-segment Bézier path reproducible in CSS only via `linear()` (Chrome 113+). Apple SwiftUI default spring `(response: 0.5, dampingFraction: 0.825)` — the cited ".snappy 0.25s / .smooth 0.35s" numbers are wrong, all presets share the 0.5s base and differ in bounce (0 / 0.15 / 0.3). Spring defaults disagree: motion.dev physics default ζ ≈ 0.5 (bouncy) vs React Spring `default` ζ = 0.997 (critically damped; its `wobbly` ≈ motion.dev's default). View Transitions API default 0.25s and does NOT auto-apply `prefers-reduced-motion` — the author must override. Folklore busts: Doherty's 1982 paper contains no "400ms" (lowest measured threshold 300ms); Heer & Robertson tested 1.25s and 2s and recommend ~1s per stage; the "skeletons feel 11% faster" claim misreads a ribbed-progress-bar study.
- **Reference / source:** Tversky/Morrison/Bétrancourt 2002 (IJHCS), Heer & Robertson TVCG 2007, Harrison/Yeo/Hudson CHI 2010, Doherty & Thadani IBM Systems Journal 1982, Chang & Ungar UIST 1993, Material 3 motion tokens, IBM @carbon/motion, Apple SwiftUI Animation API, W3C View Transitions, WCAG 2.2.2 + 2.3.3, WebKit 2017 reduced-motion rationale.
- **Best for:** The motion budget for every section — hero choreography restraint (explicitly banned in productivity contexts), hover/press micro-feedback, scroll and page transitions, and the reduced-motion fallback design.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0658⟧

## ⟦S0659⟧ anti-ai-slop — MCP Market — open-design craft rules + all templates
- **What it is:** Concrete, checkable rules separating "designed by a human who shipped product" from default LLM output. Several rules are auto-enforced by OpenDesign's `lint-artifact` linter at P0 (must-fix); the rest are flagged guidance.
- **How it looks:** A page that passes looks deliberately art-directed: a flat hero surface with intentional type instead of a purple-blue gradient, monoline SVG icons instead of emoji, display headings in the bound display font, real metrics or honestly labelled placeholders, and accent colour appearing at most twice on a screen. What it bans is equally visible: the rounded card with a coloured left border, blob/wave SVG backgrounds, and the stock Hero → Features → Pricing → FAQ → CTA skeleton with no variation.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Seven P0 cardinal sins: (1) default Tailwind indigo as accent — exactly `#6366f1`, `#4f46e5`, `#4338ca`, `#3730a3`, `#8b5cf6`, `#7c3aed`, `#a855f7` (use the DESIGN.md `--accent`); (2) two-stop "trust" gradient on the hero (purple→blue, blue→cyan, indigo→pink); (3) emoji as feature icons (✨🚀🎯⚡🔥💡) inside headings/buttons/list items — use 1.6–1.8px-stroke monoline SVG with `currentColor`; (4) sans-serif on display text when the seed binds a serif (h1/h2 must use `var(--font-display)`); (5) rounded card with coloured left-border accent; (6) invented metrics ("10× faster", "99.9% uptime"); (7) filler copy (lorem ipsum, "feature one / two / three"). P1 soft tells: the standard section skeleton with no unconventional section; external placeholder image CDNs (unsplash.com, placehold.co, placekitten.com, picsum.photos) — use the shipped `.ph-img` class; more than ~12 raw hex values outside `:root`; `var(--accent)` used 6+ times in the body (cap 2 visible uses per screen). P2: sections missing `data-od-id`; decorative blob/wave SVG; perfectly symmetric layout with no tension (alternate one tight section, one breathing section). Soul formula: ~80% proven patterns + ~20% distinctive choice living in one bold visual move, voice/microcopy, one memorable micro-interaction, one insider detail.
- **Reference / source:** Adapted from refero_skill (https://github.com/referodesign/refero_skill, MIT), tightened to OpenDesign's lint surface (`AI_DEFAULT_INDIGO` in `apps/daemon/src/lint-artifact.ts`).
- **Best for:** A QA gate over every section of every build — the fastest tell-check before a version is shown. Especially hero and proof/reviews, where invented metrics and trust gradients breed.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0659⟧

## ⟦S0660⟧ color — MCP Market — open-design craft rules + all templates
- **What it is:** Universal colour-use rules layered on top of the active DESIGN.md palette: how much of the screen each colour layer may occupy, how often the accent may appear, and which defaults are banned. The design system supplies the tokens; this file enforces their use.
- **How it looks:** A calm page that is 70–90% neutrals, with a single accent colour showing up at most twice per screen (typically one eyebrow/chip plus the primary CTA), semantic colours almost invisible until needed, and gradients under 1% of pixels. Dark themes sit on soft near-black `#0f0f0f` (never pure `#000`) with `#f0f0f0` text and hairline borders of 1px `rgba(255,255,255,0.08)`; light themes on `#fafafa` with `#111111` text (never pure white/black).
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Four palette layers by pixel share — Neutrals 70–90% (`--bg`, `--surface`, `--fg`, `--muted`, `--border`); one Accent 5–10% (`--accent` only, never invent a second); Semantic 0–5% (`--success`, `--warn`, `--danger`); Effect <1% (gradients, glows, rarely justified). Accent discipline: at most 2 visible uses per screen; links count as accent (demote to `--fg` underline if a CTA is also present); hover/focus rings count as accent. Contrast gates (run as gates, not goals): body text ≤16px 4.5:1; large text (>18px or 14px bold) 3:1; UI components against adjacent surfaces 3:1. When the brand colour is too light for text, darken the accent to a 600-level shade for text and reserve the bright variant for fills. Tokens are named by purpose (`--accent`, `--success`), never by hue (`--blue-500`). Anti-defaults: indigo `#6366f1` is the top AI tell; the two-stop trust gradient on a hero is second; decorative gradients with no hierarchy job are banned.
- **Reference / source:** Adapted from refero_skill (https://github.com/referodesign/refero_skill, MIT); examples use OpenDesign's standard tokens.
- **Best for:** Palette discipline on every section — the accent-rationing rule is the direct control for hero, call/CTA and proof sections competing for the same colour.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0660⟧

## ⟦S0661⟧ form-validation — MCP Market — open-design craft rules + all templates
- **What it is:** The full form-validation lifecycle: an input state machine that decides when a field may show an error, the WHATWG Constraint Validation API as the platform floor, WCAG 3.3.x announcement/recovery wiring beyond the accessibility baseline, and a schema-as-contract layer so one validation definition runs on server and client.
- **How it looks:** A form that never shouts early: fields sit unmarked while you type, an error appears under a field only after you leave it with bad input, and it clears the moment the input becomes valid — no second blur needed. On submit with errors, focus moves to a heading-led summary at the top ("2 problems") with anchor links to each bad field; the field keeps everything you typed. Error text names the exact subrule that failed ("Phone number is too short"), not a generic "invalid input".
- **Frame by frame:** Static layout — the motion is state change. The input state machine: `pristine` (untouched, no chrome) → `dirty` (typing, still no error chrome) → `touched` (first blur runs the field constraint) → `invalid-after-touched` (error shows, linked via `aria-describedby`) → `recovering` (editing an invalid field re-validates on `input`, error clears on becoming valid) → `submitting` (submit disabled, polite live-region status) → `server-error` (server's message text, treated as invalid-after-submit). CSS `:user-invalid` matches exactly the two invalid-after states.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Timing rules — first blur after edit runs the constraint (never on focus or first keystroke); async background preflight (uniqueness, address lookup) debounces 250–500ms, announces via polite live region, never gates typing; submit awaits authoritative server validation. Baymard anchors: 31% of sites have no inline validation and most of the rest fire too early; 98% use generic catch-all errors — ship 4–7 distinct messages per high-traffic complex field (email, phone, card, postal code); 34% of checkouts wipe the card field on an unrelated error — preserve user input. Platform floor: declare `required`, `type`, `pattern`, `min`/`max`, `minlength`/`maxlength`, `step`; `setCustomValidity("")` clears (empty string only); use `form.requestSubmit()`, never `form.submit()`; numeric-entry fields use `type="text" inputmode="numeric" pattern="[0-9]*"` (never `type="number"` for ZIP/OTP/card). Error summary: heading-led container with `tabindex="-1"`, focused on submit, and NO `role="alert"` on it (double announcement); `role="alert"` is reserved for inline per-field errors. Schema layer: Standard Schema (`~standard` interface) consumed by Zod 4 / Valibot / ArkType; server is the truth, return `{ errors }` from the action instead of throwing; `novalidate` pattern A (set `form.noValidate = true` after hydration) or B (server-validated no-JS path) — never a bare server-rendered `novalidate` with no fallback. WCAG beyond the baseline: 3.3.3 suggest the determinable fix; 3.3.4 legal/financial/data submissions need reversibility, a check step, or a confirm screen; 3.3.8 no cognitive-function-test auth without an alternative — never block paste on password/code fields.
- **Reference / source:** WHATWG HTML Living Standard (Constraint Validation), CSS Selectors L4 (`:user-invalid`, Baseline 2023: Chrome 119 / Firefox 88 / Safari 16.5), WCAG 2.2 SC 3.3.x, ARIA APG forms patterns, Standard Schema spec (@standard-schema/spec), Baymard 2023/2024 inline-validation research, WebAIM Million 2026.
- **Best for:** Forms — the quote-request and contact forms are the money sections of a trades homepage; also any multi-step estimator. Pairs with ⟦S0657⟧ (label/error wiring) and ⟦S0664⟧ (form states).
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0661⟧

## ⟦S0662⟧ laws-of-ux — MCP Market — open-design craft rules + all templates
- **What it is:** Named cognitive/perceptual/behavioural laws translated into concrete composition directives — how many options fit on a decision screen, where the primary action anchors in scanning order, how grouping is signalled. Guidance for agents and reviewers; not auto-checked by the linter (sibling craft files own the auto-checked rules).
- **How it looks:** Pages composed so the eye groups before the brain reads: tight 8–12px spacing inside a group against 32–48px between groups, equivalent items sharing identical treatment with exactly one deliberate standout (the recommended tier, the active nav item), enclosure used sparingly (≥16px padding inside a region, ≥1px hairline) so a card actually means something, and the most important nav items parked at the far left and far right of the menu where recall is strongest.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. (Its Peak-End entry defers to ⟦S0658⟧: the emotional peak belongs at the end of a flow as confirmation, not as mid-flow motion.)
- **Mechanism & key values:** Perception — Proximity (Wertheimer 1923): 8–12px within group / 32–48px between groups, the cheapest grouping signal; Similarity: identical class sets for equivalent affordances, deviation reserved for the one standout; Common Region (Palmer 1992): padding ≥16px, distinct surface; Uniform Connectedness (Palmer & Rock 1994) is the strongest grouping signal — connected lines/brackets for wizard steps and comparison sets; Von Restorff (1933): the different item is remembered — pair contrast with a non-colour signal. Decision — Hick's Law: decision time ~log(n+1); cap a single decision screen at 3–5 visible primary options, rest behind progressive disclosure; Choice Overload (Iyengar & Lepper 2000): pricing 3–4 tiers with exactly one recommended, product grids 6–9 hero cards above the fold, settings ≤5 named groups; Anchoring (Tversky & Kahneman 1974): first number re-weights the rest — place the recommended tier to anchor, show savings as dollar deltas, pre-select the safer radio default; Pareto: emphasise the 2–3 actions driving the dominant journey; Tesler: complexity is conserved — surface guidance at the exact step it surfaces. Memory — Miller/Cowan: working memory ~4 reliable items (7±2 chunks); chunk with section headings; Serial Position (Ebbinghaus 1885): primacy + recency — key items at menu extremes, utilities in the middle; Peak-End (Kahneman et al. 1993): stage a high-effort celebratory success state, keep middles calm; Zeigarnik (1927): visible progress ("3 of 5 steps") pulls completion — beneficial flows only, streak/nag use is a dark pattern. Interaction — Fitts (1954) paired with the 24×24 CSS px AA target floor; Doherty Threshold: the implementable ladder lives in ⟦S0664⟧ (no indicator under 300ms … stop past 60s); Goal-Gradient (Hull 1932): show real endowed progress only, never fabricated; Postel (RFC 760): accept phone/date input in any natural shape, normalise internally, emit one format. Expectation — Jakob's Law (Nielsen 2000): reuse category conventions (nav placement, cart icon, CTA upper-right) so novelty must earn its keep.
- **Reference / source:** Primary sources cited per law: Hick 1952 / Hyman 1953, Miller 1956, Cowan 2001, Fitts 1954, Wertheimer 1923, Palmer 1992, Palmer & Rock 1994, Kahneman/Fredrickson/Schreiber/Redelmeier 1993, Zeigarnik 1927, Csíkszentmihályi 1975, Hull 1932, von Restorff 1933, Broadbent 1958, Sweller 1988, Postel RFC 760 (1980), Carroll & Rosson 1987, Tversky & Kahneman 1974, Kurosu & Kashimura 1995, Iyengar & Lepper 2000, Pareto/Juran, Ebbinghaus 1885, Tesler (Apple, 1980s), Nielsen 2000, Norman 1988, Parkinson 1955.
- **Best for:** Composition decisions on every section — navigation layout, pricing/tier counts, proof-wall density, form grouping, CTA placement and the recommended-option standout in towns/areas and call/CTA blocks.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0662⟧

## ⟦S0663⟧ rtl-and-bidi — MCP Market — open-design craft rules + all templates
- **What it is:** The rules for right-to-left layout and bidirectional text: base direction, CSS logical properties, bidi isolation, what mirrors and what must not, and the typography couplings that break layouts in Arabic/Hebrew/Persian/Urdu.
- **How it looks:** An RTL page that reads as a true mirror where mirroring is correct — back arrow flipped, navigation rail and checkbox label swapped sides, slider fill growing from the right — while clocks, media controls and scrubbers, charts, photos and logos stay unflipped. Phone numbers and IBANs inside Arabic text sit in a forced-LTR island so the digits don't scramble; Arabic body type runs larger and looser (14–18px at line-height 1.5–1.75) with no letter-spacing, so the cursive joins stay intact.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion; these are layout-resolution rules applied at render.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Base: full-page RTL needs `<html dir="rtl" lang="ar">` (dir alone misses font-stack/hyphenation/speech; inside an opposite-direction ancestor set both `lang` and `dir` on the subtree); unknown-direction UGC uses `dir="auto"`. Logical properties first: `margin-inline-start`, `padding-inline-start`, `inset-inline-start`, `border-inline-start`, `border-start-start-radius`, `text-align: start/end`, `inline-size`/`block-size` (Baseline Widely Available: Chrome 87, Safari 14.1, Firefox 66). Tailwind v4.0 folded inline-axis utilities into core (`ms-*`, `me-*`, `ps-*`, `pe-*`, `start-*`, `end-*`); v4.2 added block-axis (`mbs-*`, `mbe-*`, `pbs-*`, `pbe-*`) and renamed insets to `inset-s-*` / `inset-e-*`; the `tailwindcss-rtl` plugin is obsolete. Bidi: prefer isolate controls U+2066 LRI / U+2067 RLI / U+2068 FSI, all closed by U+2069 PDI, over legacy embeddings (U+202A–U+202E + U+202C PDF); in HTML use `<bdi>`, and `<bdi dir="ltr">` for weak-character values (phone, IBAN, card numbers) where first-strong detection fails. Must mirror: directional arrows, nav rail position, tab order, calendar weekday order, slider and non-media progress fill, checkbox-label position. Must NOT mirror: clock faces, circular refresh icons, media playback controls AND the media scrubber, chart x-axes, photographs, brand logos, physical-object icons. Numerals follow locale, not direction (Arabic-Indic digits are bidi class AN). Known platform conflict: the search icon — Apple flips its SF Symbol, Material 3 says don't; decide per platform. Typography: never apply CSS `letter-spacing` to Arabic runs (breaks cursive joining); no italics on Arabic/Hebrew; never prototype RTL with Lorem Ipsum. Forms: `<input dir="auto">` for uncertain-direction fields; force `dir="ltr"` on email/URL/phone/IBAN/card inputs even inside RTL paragraphs.
- **Reference / source:** Unicode UAX #9 rev 51 (Sept 2025) + Unicode 17.0, CSS Logical Properties Level 1, HTML Living Standard, Tailwind v4.0/v4.2 changelogs, W3C alreq, Material 3 RTL guidance, Apple HIG internationalization.
- **Best for:** Any section that may render in an RTL locale — navigation, forms, sliders/galleries (fill direction), and mixed-script proof/reviews content.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0663⟧

## ⟦S0664⟧ state-coverage — MCP Market — open-design craft rules + all templates
- **What it is:** The rule that every interactive surface must render five states — loading, empty, error, populated, edge — plus three extra form states, with exact content requirements and loading-indicator thresholds. It names the single most reliable AI-design failure: shipping only the populated state.
- **How it looks:** A gallery that shows a layout-matched skeleton while photos load, an empty state with a headline, a plain explanation and a primary CTA (never a blank or bare "No data"), and an error panel that says what happened, why, and what to do next — with the user's form input still intact. Long names, 10,000-row tables and RTL content stretch the layout without breaking it.
- **Frame by frame:** States replace each other rather than animate: request fires → (under 300ms: nothing shown) → skeleton or labelled spinner matched to the expected layout → content lands (focus moves to it if the action was user-initiated) → or the error state with retry. Retry discipline: first retry immediate on click, second/third at 2s / 4s / 8s exponential backoff, after 3 failures "Retry" is replaced by "Contact support" plus a copyable error ID, with "Last attempted: Xs ago" shown. No spinner runs indefinitely: a "taking longer than expected" notice appears at 15s and animation stops at 60s into an error with retry/cancel/continue.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Loading ladder by expected duration — 0–300ms: no indicator; 300ms–2s: subtle spinner or skeleton; 2–10s: layout-matched skeleton or labelled spinner ("Loading payments…"); 10–30s: determinate progress bar with cancel; 30–60s: progress bar with explicit cancel; 60s+: stop animation, show error. Form states on top of the five: untouched (default styling, no messages), dirty-valid (helper text persists, no success-colouring), submitted-pending (submit button loading, fields locked); validation fires on blur, live fields only after first blur, and errors clear the instant input becomes valid. Empty-state types: first-use (illustration + headline + value sentence + CTA — the onboarding moment), no-results (echo the query, suggest alternatives; prefer server-supplied suggestions), cleared (celebratory + optional next action), error-as-empty (never — error is its own state). Error severity tiers: field-level (border + inline message + focus), form-level (summary banner + per-field markers), section-level (inline panel with retry, rest of page functional), page-level (full state + recovery CTA), app-level (persistent banner/modal). ARIA/focus map: inline error on submit → `role="alert"` + focus to first error field; toast → `role="status"`, no focus move; critical/destructive → `role="alertdialog"` + focus to dialog; loading begins → `role="status"` announcement, no focus move. Live-region containers must exist in the DOM before content is injected. Edge test matrix included (10,000+ rows sorted/filtered; 200-char title with missing avatar; all-required-fields-at-max-length form; single-character and special-char queries; detail view missing all optional metadata).
- **Reference / source:** Distilled from WCAG 2.2, NN/g, Material Design 3, Apple HIG, and Baymard Institute checkout research.
- **Best for:** Forms, work/gallery grids, review walls, search and any data-fed section — the completeness checklist a version must pass, and the loading thresholds every spinner/skeleton on the page obeys (cross-referenced by ⟦S0662⟧'s Doherty entry).
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0664⟧

## ⟦S0665⟧ typography-hierarchy-editorial — MCP Market — open-design craft rules + all templates
- **What it is:** The editorial extension of the typography stack (layers on ⟦S0667⟧ + ⟦S0666⟧) for long-form articles, magazine layouts, digital guides and editorial landing pages: hierarchy paced like a print spread — entry point, tension, rest, disruption, resolution — instead of SaaS's additive stacking. Opt in via `od.craft.requires: [typography, typography-hierarchy, typography-hierarchy-editorial]`.
- **How it looks:** A headline that is a visual event — 56–96px, usually light or regular weight, never bold — floating in at least 2× its line-height of space above and below, then a hard drop to an 18–24px deck. Body runs 16–18px at a tight 60–70ch measure. A pull quote at 28–40px breaks clean out of the column (full width or offset), set plain with no box, border or background. Bold appears at most twice per 400 words; section pacing alternates dense and spacious instead of uniform padding.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Scale table — Display/lede 56–96px (may exceed ⟦S0667⟧'s default display range), leading 1.0–1.1, tracking −0.02em to −0.05em (Latin; 0 for Arabic/Persian/Urdu joining scripts); Deck/standfirst 18–24px, leading 1.4–1.5; Byline/dateline 12–14px, tracking 0.02–0.04em; Body 16–18px, leading 1.6–1.7 (serif), measure 60–70ch, `text-align: start`, never justified; Pull quote 28–40px, regular/light, tracking −0.01em (Latin only), leading 1.2–1.3, spacing above/below ≥ a section break, may be the page's only `var(--accent)` use; Caption 12–13px, tracking 0.01em; Section label 11–12px medium, tracking 0.06–0.1em if caps. Scale-event rule: display/deck ratio ≥1.5× or absolute delta ≥24px. Pull quotes: one per long-form article is usually right, two maximum, never at regular intervals. Whitespace carries hierarchy — space is the default section-break signal; rules/dingbats only when they reinforce publication identity. Anti-patterns: bold display headline (reads as billboard), uniform section padding, pull quote styled as a callout box, deck set at body size, a heading forced at every content shift, positive tracking on display, UI chrome inside the reading column.
- **Reference / source:** OpenDesign craft file extending `typography.md` + `typography-hierarchy.md`; RTL separator handling defers to ⟦S0663⟧, accent rationing to ⟦S0660⟧.
- **Best for:** Editorial hero and long-form sections — a magazine-register landing page, guide/article pages, and any "story" section where pacing, not stacking, should carry the hierarchy.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0665⟧

## ⟦S0666⟧ typography-hierarchy — MCP Market — open-design craft rules + all templates
- **What it is:** The hierarchy-behaviour contract layered on ⟦S0667⟧: not sizes or tracking values, but how hierarchy behaves — one dominant entry point, intentional contrast between levels, and information flow a reader can still reconstruct when the hierarchy is deliberately violated. Applies per surface; long surfaces may re-establish a new primary at intentional pacing resets.
- **How it looks:** A page where the eye lands in exactly one place first. The dominant element wins on at least two vectors at once — say scale plus the space around it — while everything else is visibly demoted. No wall of equal-weight text (flat hierarchy), no crowd of bold accented elements fighting (noise hierarchy), and no staircase of regular → medium → semibold → bold each one step heavier.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Three core contracts: (1) one dominant entry point per visual region; (2) rhythm = contrast between levels, not a list of sizes; (3) recoverable information flow. Five hierarchy vectors — Scale (large→small = primary→secondary), Weight (heavier = primary), Spacing (more space = more importance), Tracking (tighter = faster, wider = ceremonial), Alignment (breaking the grid signals importance); at least two vectors must work in the same direction on the dominant element. Three-level working model: Primary (entry point; scale, spacing or alignment break), Secondary (structure; weight, scale step or tracking shift), Tertiary (labels/captions/metadata; scale reduction, weight reduction or positive tracking). More than three visible levels above the fold is a composition problem. Lint values: adjacent levels ≥1.25× apart in scale OR compensated by a weight/spacing jump; no two adjacent levels share the same scale AND weight AND spacing; at least one gap ≥1.5× the others. Semantic role ≠ visual role is explicitly allowed (an `<h1>` may render quieter than a nearby `<p>`; body copy may sit at display scale) when DOM order still matches meaning, proximity groups the inverted element with its context, and only one primary exists in the region. Anti-patterns: graduated weight ladder, uniform section spacing, heading as the only hierarchy vector, symmetrical co-primary emphasis, size-only hierarchy.
- **Reference / source:** OpenDesign craft file; aesthetic-specific variants (e.g. ⟦S0665⟧ editorial) extend it. Opt in via `od.craft.requires: [typography, typography-hierarchy]`.
- **Best for:** Judging and fixing the type composition of any section — the "what does the eye hit first" check for hero, proof and call/CTA blocks before any size values are touched.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0666⟧

## ⟦S0667⟧ typography — MCP Market — open-design craft rules + all templates
- **What it is:** The base typography rules applied on top of any DESIGN.md: the design system picks the fonts, this file decides how they behave at every size — scale, leading, letter-spacing, line length and weight discipline. Called out in its own text as the source of "the single most-skipped rule in AI-generated design" (letter-spacing).
- **How it looks:** Type with the two reliable craft tells done right: ALL-CAPS labels visibly letterspaced instead of cramped, and big display headings tightened instead of loose. At most 6–8 sizes on the page, at most 3 visible above the fold, body copy in a 50–75-character column, and only three weights doing all the work — read, emphasise, announce — with 700+ almost never appearing.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Type scale (multiplicative 1.2 or 1.25, cap 6–8 sizes): Display 48–72px, H1 32–48px, H2 24–32px, H3 20–24px, Body 15–18px, Small 13–14px, Caption 11–12px. Leading: Display/H1 (≥32px) 1.0–1.2; Body 1.5–1.6; Small 1.5. CJK overrides (not optional — CJK glyphs fill the em box): display leading 1.3–1.4 at EVERY size including multi-line cover/hero titles split with `<br>` (the single most common violation), body 1.7–1.8, tracking 0 (negative tracking is Latin-only); in mixed artifacts set Latin values on the Latin element only. Letter-spacing table: body (14–18px) 0; small (11–13px) 0.01–0.02em; UI labels/buttons 0.02em; ALL CAPS 0.06–0.1em (required — Bringhurst's 5–10% of em); headings 32px+ −0.01 to −0.02em; display 48px+ −0.02 to −0.03em. Line length 50–75ch, `max-width: 65ch` default. Max 2 typefaces per artifact, always with a system fallback chain; never `font-family: system-ui` alone on a heading. Three-weight system: Read 400/450, Emphasize 510/550, Announce 590/600. Never `text-align: justify` on the web.
- **Reference / source:** Adapted from refero_skill (https://github.com/referodesign/refero_skill, MIT), re-tuned for OpenDesign tokens; caps-tracking floor cites Bringhurst, *Elements of Typographic Style* §3.2.7.
- **Best for:** The type foundation under every section of every build — hero display settings, caps eyebrows/labels, body measure in content and form sections.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0667⟧

## ⟦S0669⟧ template/audio-jingle — MCP Market — open-design craft rules + all templates
- **What it is:** An audio-generation dispatch workflow, not a page design: it plans and produces one music, speech or sound-effect file per run through OpenDesign's unified media dispatcher. The project's `audioKind` metadata selects the sub-mode.
- **How it looks:** Nothing on screen except the resulting audio file in the project, which the FileViewer renders with transport controls the moment it lands. Planning shows in chat as a 2–3 sentence plan summary plus the returned filename.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. Workflow sequence: read project metadata (`audioKind`, `audioModel`, `audioDuration`, `voice`) → write the plan → assemble the model-format prompt → dispatch → hand off filename plus one variation suggestion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Three sub-modes — `music` routes to Suno V5 (default) / Udio / Lyria 2, planned as genre + 1–2 reference artists, tempo BPM + key, 3–5 instruments max, vocal choice, mood arc; `speech` routes to MiniMax TTS (default) / Fish / ElevenLabs V3, planned as the final verbatim script + voice + pacing + pronunciation hints; `sfx` routes to ElevenLabs SFX (default) / AudioCraft, planned as texture + duration + envelope + layering. Dispatch command: `media generate --project … --surface audio --audio-kind <music|speech|sfx> --model … --duration <seconds> [--voice <provider voice id>] --output "<slug>-<duration>s.mp3"` — duration binds to the API parameter, never to prose. Hard rules: TTS runs the script literally (proof it first — one stray comma changes cadence); MiniMax `--voice` must be a real `voice_id` (e.g. `male-qn-qingse`), never prose — omit the flag for the daemon default; music structure by length: under 30s single section, 30–90s intro + body, 90s+ full arc; SFX prefers one specific texture description over a paragraph of hype.
- **Reference / source:** Provider models named in the skill: Suno V5, Udio, Lyria 2, MiniMax TTS, Fish, ElevenLabs V3 / ElevenLabs SFX, AudioCraft. Ships `example.html` as its only asset besides the skill file.
- **Best for:** Producing audio assets (jingle, narration, SFX) for video or hero media — no homepage-section use. Indexed so the audio route is discoverable alongside the video templates.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0669⟧

## ⟦S0671⟧ template/clinical-case-report — MCP Market — open-design craft rules + all templates
- **What it is:** A generator for a structured medical case presentation (clinical rounds, conferences, documentation) as a single-page HTML report, in SOAP/Conference or Brief Rounds format chosen from reference files before writing.
- **How it looks:** A professional medical document: Georgia or system serif on white with dark text, print-clean on A4/Letter. Vital signs and lab results sit in HTML tables with reference ranges and flags; critical findings (ST elevation, raised troponin, low BP) are pulled into a visually distinct callout box with a red left border. Sections are tagged `data-od-id` (`hpi`, `vitals`, `pmh`, `examination`, `investigations`, `assessment`, `plan`), and a disclaimer footer states the case is educational/simulated.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** SOAP/Conference structure: patient ID, chronological HPI with timeline markers, PMH/medications/allergies, review of systems, systematic examination, vitals table, investigations, assessment (primary diagnosis first line + one-sentence reasoning + differential of exactly 3–5 items each with supporting/refuting evidence + a validated risk score — TIMI/GRACE/Killip + Shock Index for ACS, CURB-65 pneumonia, qSOFA sepsis, Wells PE), then a management plan organised by problem with specific drug names, doses, routes and frequencies ("Piperacillin-Tazobactam 4.5g IV q8h for 5 days", never "start antibiotics"; "[drug] — dose per local formulary/protocol" when uncertain). Generated values must be physiologically consistent with the diagnosis and never overwrite or contradict user-provided data. Brief Rounds format drops HPI/examination for an ID line, interval events, active problems and plan-by-problem. `@media print` rules required; all P0 items in `references/checklist.md` must pass.
- **Reference / source:** Internal references `references/case-formats.md` and `references/checklist.md`; standard hospital case-presentation conventions.
- **Best for:** NOT-FOR-TRADES for homepage building — a clinical document template. Indexed for completeness; its only transferable devices are the flagged-callout and print-stylesheet patterns.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0671⟧

## ⟦S0672⟧ template/contact-widget — MCP Market — open-design craft rules + all templates
- **What it is:** A self-contained floating chat/contact widget in a single HTML file with zero dependencies: bubble, welcome home screen, social links, an optional meeting card, a message input, and an offline fallback form. Pure front-end — no tracking, no phone-home, works offline once loaded.
- **How it looks:** A circular button fixed bottom-right; the open panel is a clean minimal SaaS card (16px radius, shadow `0 8px 32px rgba(0,0,0,0.12)`) headed by the agent's avatar, name, online status dot and greeting, with a row of circular social icons and a calendar-icon "Book a meeting" card below. Visitor clicks the bubble → panel toggles open/closed; hover darkens buttons ~5%; pressing the bubble scales it to 0.95 while active. If `is_available=false`, the home screen is replaced by the offline message plus a name/email/message form. Leave a message and we'll get back to you!", optional `social_telegram` / `social_whatsapp` / `social_instagram` / `meeting_url` (omitted when empty). Geometry: 16px internal padding, 12px gaps, cards 16px radius, bubble and avatars full-round, bubble shadow `0 4px 12px`. All values inlined as literals — no template placeholders in the output, and no third-party SDK scripts unless the user explicitly asks for backend wiring (escalation tiers: mailto fallback → own `/api/contact` POST → a real chat SDK such as Knocket, Crisp, Tawk.to, Chatwoot or Intercom, never auto-injected).

## ⟦S0673⟧ template/critique — MCP Market — open-design craft rules + all templates
- **What it is:** A design-review report generator: it scores any artifact across five dimensions with cited evidence and produces a single-file HTML review report with a radar chart and aggregated Keep / Fix / Quick-wins action lists. Inspired by the huashu-design expert-critique flow.
- **How it looks:** A report page (active DESIGN.md tokens, or a neutral light theme — off-white background, near-black text, one accent for the radar fill): header naming the artifact, date, reviewer ("OD · Critique skill") and a one-line verdict; a big inline-SVG radar chart of the five scores; five dimension cards in a one- or two-column grid, each showing the 0–10 score with its band, an evidence paragraph and one Keep/Fix/Quick-win bullet; three checkbox action lists at the bottom.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Five independent dimensions: Philosophy consistency, Visual hierarchy, Detail execution, Functionality, Innovation. Bands: 0–4 Broken, 5–6 Functional, 7–8 Strong, 9–10 Exceptional. Scoring discipline: every score needs a 30–80 word evidence paragraph naming specific elements (classes, pages, line numbers); the score is the worst sustained band, never averaged up; an overall mean above 8 is suspicious; a low Innovation score (5) is acceptable for production work. Action lists: Keep 3–5 bullets, Fix 3–6 ordered by visual cost saved per minute, Quick wins 3–5 (5–15 minutes each). Hard rules: all 5 scores every time, single-file HTML with everything inline, radar chart mandatory, and never review your own artifact in the same turn you made it (self-critique only on explicit request).
- **Reference / source:** Inspired by the *huashu-design* expert-critique flow (named in the skill).
- **Best for:** The QA/review loop over built sections — a structured second pair of eyes before a version is finalised; not a page design itself.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0673⟧

## ⟦S0676⟧ template/dcf-valuation — MCP Market — open-design craft rules + all templates
- **What it is:** A discounted-cash-flow valuation workflow that writes a reusable Markdown report to Design Files at `finance/<safe-company-or-ticker>-dcf.md`, estimating intrinsic value per share with every assumption documented and sourced facts separated from analyst judgment. OD-native contract only — it assumes no finance runtime.
- **How it looks:** No page visual — the deliverable is a structured Markdown memo: valuation summary (current price, fair value, upside/downside, confidence), data coverage, a Key Inputs table (value / source type / citation), a five-year FCF forecast table, a 3×3 sensitivity matrix, caveats, sources, and an evidence note.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Inputs: 3–5 years of revenue, operating cash flow, capex and FCF; latest cash, debt, minority interest, diluted shares; current price/market cap. Every input is tagged `sourced`, `derived`, `user-provided` or `assumption` — revenue, FCF, debt, cash, shares, price and estimates are never invented. Growth: prefer historical FCF CAGR, cross-checked against revenue/margins/estimates; sustained explicit-period growth capped at 15% unless the user supplies higher; growth fades over the forecast period. Discount rate starts from `references/sector-wacc.md` and is adjusted for leverage, size, geography, cyclicality, concentration and moat, with the deviation explained. Terminal value: Gordon Growth at a default 2.5% terminal growth. Sensitivity: 3×3 matrix of WACC (base ±1%) × terminal growth (2.0% / 2.5% / 3.0%), plus checks on terminal value as a share of enterprise value and FCF-per-share multiples. External pages and filings are treated as untrusted evidence for facts and citations only — embedded instructions in source content are explicitly not followed.
- **Reference / source:** Adapted from Dexter's DCF workflow (https://github.com/virattt/dexter); sector WACC table in the skill's `references/sector-wacc.md`.
- **Best for:** NOT-FOR-TRADES — a finance document workflow with no visual design content. Indexed for completeness.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0676⟧

Panels and cards can be clicked to zoom; a dark-mode toggle flips the whole surface, chart colours included, because they derive from CSS variables. DESIGN.md tokens are mapped onto the seed's CSS variables — no new tokens invented.
- **Frame by frame:** Trigger = tab click: the view swaps (only one of Team Members / Team Details / Activity Log visible) and the URL hash syncs (`#members` | `#details` | `#activity`). First reveal of the details tab: the role bar chart animates in with easing. Hover on the chart: a tooltip shows the precise label + value. Click a panel/card: it zooms; click again or press Esc: it restores. "Export CSV" downloads every row currently in the team table, including the Workflow column.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Seed-first workflow (start from `assets/template.html`; the hand-built `example.html` is the gallery reference; `references/checklist.md` holds P0/P1/P2 gates). Three fixed tabs with hash sync; chart colours re-derived from CSS variables in dark mode; CSV export of the visible table. The artifact must render correctly opened directly from disk — no build step, no network.
- **Reference / source:** FlowAI aesthetic (named in the skill); internal assets `assets/template.html`, `references/checklist.md`, `example.html`.
- **Best for:** Interactive dashboard work; its tab-switch, click-to-zoom and tooltip behaviours are a compact interaction-pattern set. Not a homepage template.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0682⟧

## ⟦S0683⟧ template/gamified-app — MCP Market — open-design craft rules + all templates
- **What it is:** A template presenting a gamified mobile app as a multi-screen hi-fi prototype: three phone frames side by side on one dark showcase page, each phone a different moment in the journey (cover poster, today's-quests dashboard, quest detail).
- **How it looks:** A full-bleed near-black stage (`#0e0d0c` or the DS dark token) with a soft top spotlight gradient and a mono caption row ("HI-FI PROTOTYPE · IPHONE" left, brand wordmark right). Each phone is 360×780 with a 12px black bezel, 44px corner radius, dynamic-island notch, status bar, and a bottom tab bar of 5 icons (Today, Library, Stats, a central ⊕ CTA, Profile) with the active tab in accent. Phone 1 is a cover poster: big display headline with one accent word, a muted 1–2 sentence body, and a teaser sliver of the next screen at its bottom edge. Phone 2 is the hero screen: greeting ("Good morning, Sam"), a glassmorphic level ribbon ("LV 14 · Level 14 · 1648 / 2480 XP") with a progress bar inside, and a 3×2 grid of quest tiles — each a different pastel against the same neutral surface, with a glyph chip top-left, title, mini-meta and a "+NN XP" pill bottom-right. Phone 3 is quest detail: a hero block in the quest's accent colour, big serif quest title, a "REWARD +90 XP" stamp, a 3–4 step checklist (one done, two pending) and a big accent "Start quest" pill. Everything is CSS — linear-gradients and inline SVG glyphs, no images.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — the showcase page does not animate; the three frames are presented as fixed screens (the row wraps to a vertical stack on narrow viewports).
- **Mechanism & key values:** Phone geometry: 360×780 frames, 12px bezel, 44px radius. Quest content is generated as real, specific quests (e.g. "Body — 20-min strength: pushups & planks", "Read — Four Thousand Weeks"), never placeholders. Bold display type and a brighter, broader palette than typical product UI, kept adult — playful, not childish; each tile a different pastel so no colour overpowers. `data-od-id` on the stage, each phone and each frame's regions.
- **Reference / source:** Quest examples in the skill reference real products/content (Huberman Lab, *Four Thousand Weeks*, The Bear S3 E4) as sample copy; design tokens from the active DESIGN.md.
- **Best for:** App-showcase presentation pages; the phone-frame trio is a transferable device for showing a product's screens in a hero or work section.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0683⟧

## ⟦S0684⟧ template/github-dashboard — MCP Market — open-design craft rules + all templates
- **What it is:** A template for a single-screen GitHub repository analytics dashboard (growth, project health, stars/forks/contributors, issue and PR activity) in a custom "Soft Paper Workspace" style — explicitly not a GitHub UI clone. It also defines the data collection and provenance discipline behind the numbers, and can emit a refreshable live-artifact source set instead of a static file.
- **How it looks:** Light mode only: a warm off-white canvas `#F2F2F0` holding two white rounded panels — a 256px sidebar and the main panel — each with 16px radius and a 1px `#ECECEA` hairline border, ink `#0A0A0A`, Geist/Inter type. A 48px topbar (repo context left, refresh/export/actions right), a repo header, then a KPI strip of 5 compact cards (stars, forks, contributors, issues, PRs) in tabular lining numerals. The main grid splits 2fr/1fr: growth chart or activity table left, top contributors (circular 28–32px avatars) and health cards right. Tables run 13px body text with 11px uppercase column labels and 1px row dividers; status chips are pastel pills; card shadow is barely-there (`0 1px 2px rgba(10,10,10,.04), 0 1px 1px rgba(10,10,10,.02)`); a small muted provenance/last-updated note closes the page.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion in the static artifact.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Data via GitHub CLI/REST: repo totals from `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}`; contributors paginated `per_page=100`, sorted by contributions descending, top 5–8 shown; issues/PRs counted via Search API (`repo:{owner}/{repo} is:issue` / `is:pr`) or paginated lists filtering out `pull_request` items; recent activity normalised into display-ready rows capped at 5–10, with type/label classes precomputed (no template conditionals). GitHub exposes no complete historical deltas, so growth figures come from GraphQL/event snapshots or are explicitly marked estimated/synthetic in `provenance.json`. Colour stays small and semantic: green healthy, amber warning, blue feature/PR, red only defects/risk; at most one solid black primary action per area. Live-artifact mode writes `template.html` + `data.json` + `artifact.json` + `provenance.json` (index.html is daemon-derived); regions tagged `data-od-id` (`sidebar`, `topbar`, `repo-header`, `kpi-strip`, `growth-chart`, `contributors`, `activity`, `provenance`). No tokens, cookies or private metadata are ever persisted. Scope: one repository per dashboard.
- **Reference / source:** GitHub REST/GraphQL/Search APIs; internal references `references/template.html`, `references/example-data.json`, `references/artifact-example.json`, `references/provenance-example.json`, plus `example.html`.
- **Best for:** Data-report pages and dashboards; the provenance-labelling discipline (every metric sourced or flagged estimated) is the transferable lesson for proof/stat sections. Not a homepage template.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0684⟧

## ⟦S0685⟧ template/guizang-ppt — MCP Market — open-design craft rules + all templates
- **What it is:** A single-file HTML horizontal-swipe deck in an electronic-magazine + e-ink register ("Magazine Web PPT"): WebGL shader backgrounds on hero pages, serif-led type, mono metadata, and 10 paste-ready layout skeletons — Monocle after code was stitched onto it, explicitly not corporate PPT.
- **How it looks:** Magazine pages in one of five tuned theme presets (Ink Classic, Indigo Porcelain, Forest Ink, Kraft Paper, Dune) — ink on paper with hairline structure, no shadows, no floating cards: hierarchy is carried by large type plus typeface contrast plus grid whitespace. Headlines in Noto Serif SC + Playfair Display, body in Noto Sans SC + Inter, metadata in IBM Plex Mono, Lucide line icons (no emoji). Hero pages let a WebGL fluid/contour/dispersion background show through; ordinary pages keep it barely visible. Images are first-class: cropped only at the bottom, in standard ratios.
- **Frame by frame:** Trigger = ←/→ key, scroll wheel, touch swipe or bottom dot: the deck pages horizontally to the next slide. When the incoming slide is a hero page, the theme colours and the WebGL shader transition softly (interpolated) rather than cutting; on body pages the shader recedes. ESC opens the index/overview.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Five magazine directions, inferred from the brief (never switched mid-deck): Monocle Editorial (default), WIRED Tech, Kinfolk Slow, Domus Architectural, Lab/Reference. Theme colour: pick ONE of the 5 presets — user hex values are refused — swapped as a whole `:root` block (`--ink`, `--ink-rgb`, `--paper`, `--paper-rgb`, `--paper-tint`, `--ink-tint`); everything else flows through the variables. Theme rhythm law: every slide carries `light`, `dark`, `hero light` or `hero dark`; no 3+ consecutive slides on one theme; decks of 8+ pages need ≥1 hero dark and ≥1 hero light; a hero page lands every 3–4 pages. Layouts (paste-ready `<section>` skeletons): cover, act divider, big numbers, lead image + text, image grid, two-column pipeline, suspenseful close/question, big quote, before/after, image + text mix — classes must be pre-checked against the template's `<style>` (`h-hero`, `h-xl`, `stat-card`, `pipeline`, `grid-2-7-5`, `frame-img`, `callout`, `chrome`, `foot`…), since a missing class collapses the design to browser defaults. Image rules: lead image 16:10 or 4:3 with `max-height: 56vh`; image grids use fixed `height: 26vh`, never `aspect-ratio`; full-screen hero 16:9 with `max-height: 64vh`; small insets 1:1, 3:2 or 3:4; never `align-self: end` on images (grid + `align-items: start` instead); source images ≥1600px wide, deck total under 10MB; Chinese big titles ≤5 characters with `nowrap`. Narrative arc for outline-less briefs: Hook 1 page → Context 1–2 → Core 3–5 → Shift 1 → Takeaway 1–2; page counts scale with talk length (15 min ≈ 10 pages, 30 min ≈ 20, 45 min ≈ 25–30).
- **Reference / source:** Style anchors named in the skill: Guizang's "One-Person Company: Organizations Folded by AI" talk deck (2026-04-22, 27 pages), the layout of *Monocle* magazine, and Garry Tan's "Thin Harness, Fat Skills" demo. Internal references: `references/styles.md`, `components.md`, `layouts.md`, `themes.md`, `checklist.md`; seed `assets/template.html` + `assets/example-slides.html`.
- **Best for:** Talk/deck deliverables. For homepages, the transferable systems are the hero-page rhythm law (a visual event every 3–4 sections) and the magazine type-role discipline.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0685⟧

## ⟦S0687⟧ template/html-ppt — MCP Market — open-design craft rules + all templates
- **What it is:** "HTML PPT Studio" — the master deck-authoring skill behind the whole html-ppt family: a token-based static HTML presentation system where one theme file = one look, one layout file = one page type, one animation class = one entry effect. This is the full-detail entry for the family; the thirteen focused entry-point cards ⟦S0688⟧–⟦S0695⟧ and ⟦S0698⟧–⟦S0702⟧ all route here.
- **How it looks:** Decks of full-screen slides sharing chrome slots (`.deck-header`, `.deck-footer`, `.slide-number`, progress bar) from `assets/base.css`; only the `.slide.is-active` slide is visible. Looks range across 36 themes — minimal-white, editorial-serif, soft-pastel, sharp-mono, arctic-cool, sunset-warm, catppuccin-latte/mocha, dracula, tokyo-night, nord, solarized-light, gruvbox-dark, rose-pine, neo-brutalism, glassmorphism, bauhaus, swiss-grid, terminal-green, xiaohongshu-white, rainbow-gradient, aurora, blueprint, memphis-pop, cyberpunk-neon, y2k-chrome, retro-tv, japanese-minimal, vaporwave, midcentury, corporate-clean, academic-paper, news-broadcast, pitch-deck-vc, magazine-bold, engineering-whiteprint — plus 15 full-deck templates with scoped `.tpl-<name>` CSS and 31 single-page layouts.
- **Frame by frame:** Trigger = keyboard: ←/→/Space/PgUp/PgDn/Home/End navigate (the active class moves, the incoming slide's `data-anim` entry effects and any `data-fx` canvas effects initialise on slide enter and clean up on leave); T cycles themes live; A cycles the demo animation on the current slide; F fullscreen; O opens the slide overview grid; N opens the notes drawer; S opens the presenter window — a popup with four draggable, resizable magnetic cards (CURRENT and NEXT pixel-perfect iframe previews loaded via `?preview=N`, a large-font SPEAKER SCRIPT card, and a TIMER card with slide counter) kept in sync with the audience window by `postMessage` + `BroadcastChannel` with no reload or flicker, card geometry persisted to `localStorage`; R resets the timer (in presenter); Esc closes overlays; `#/N` deep-links to slide N.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Pure static HTML/CSS/JS, CDN webfonts only. Inventory: 36 themes (`assets/themes/*.css` token overrides), 15 full-deck templates (8 extracted from real decks, 7 scenario scaffolds), 31 layouts, 27 CSS animations via `data-anim` (or `anim-stagger-list` for sequenced reveals), 20 canvas FX via `data-fx` — particle-burst, confetti-cannon, firework, starfield, matrix-rain, knowledge-graph (force-directed), neural-net, constellation, orbit-ring, galaxy-swirl, word-cascade, letter-explode, chain-react, magnetic-field, data-stream, gradient-blob, sparkle-trail, shockwave, typewriter-multi, counter-explosion. Authoring rules: always start from a template, never author from scratch; colours/radii/shadows only from CSS variables in `assets/base.css` as overridden by the theme (no literal `color: #111`); one `.slide` per logical page; speaker notes in `<div class="notes">` (display:none — presenter-only text NEVER appears as visible slide content); always include `assets/runtime.js`. Presenter scripts: 150–300 words per slide. PNG export via `scripts/render.sh` using Playwright's managed Chromium only (never the user's installed Chrome). Install: `npx skills add https://github.com/lewislulu/html-ppt-skill`.
- **Reference / source:** Upstream `lewislulu/html-ppt-skill` (https://github.com/lewislulu/html-ppt-skill), MIT, © 2026 lewis. Internal catalogs: `references/themes.md`, `layouts.md`, `animations.md`, `full-decks.md`, `presenter-mode.md`, `authoring-guide.md`.
- **Best for:** Any HTML slide deck. For homepage work, its 27 CSS entry animations + 20 canvas FX are a named motion-effects catalogue worth mining (constellation, counter-explosion, word-cascade, gradient-blob).
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0687⟧

- **What it is:** A complete standalone 16:9 deck system in "Tactical Telemetry / CRT Terminal" taste — deactivated-CRT charcoal slides, white-phosphor monospace, one hazard-red accent, scanline overlay and ASCII syntax, for debriefs, security reviews and incident write-ups that report rather than sell. One substrate only: never mixed with a light mode in the same artifact.
- **How it looks:** Slides like a declassified mission packet: charcoal `#0A0A0A` / `#121212` (never pure black), phosphor text `#EAEAEA` with `#9A9A98` secondary, hazard red `#E61919` reserved for alerts, classifications and the one data point that breaks the trend. Every corner is square (`border-radius: 0`); structure comes from 1px hairlines `#2A2A28` and `display: grid; gap: 1px` cell fields laid over a hairline-coloured background. A fixed scanline layer (`repeating-linear-gradient`, 2px/4px cycle, opacity ≤0.08) and optional SVG phosphor grain (≤0.06) sit over everything. Titles are heavy condensed grotesque at `clamp(56px, 7vw, 96px)`, uppercase, tracking −0.04em, leading 0.9; body and meta are monospace (JetBrains Mono / IBM Plex Mono) with tabular numerals. Every slide carries a top register strip (classification, slide ID, timestamp, coordinates) and a bottom bar (serial number + page). Set pieces include a diagonal hazard-stripe alert block (`repeating-linear-gradient(135deg, …)`), a specimen slide with one mono character at viewport-bleeding scale, and a telemetry grid whose trend-breaking cell turns red.
- **Frame by frame:** Mechanical and instant: slide changes are hard cuts — no fades (optionally a 60ms flicker, opacity 0.85 → 1). The only living elements are a blinking caret (`▌`) on the cover and a single pulse on the live status dot. Nothing else moves.
- **Mechanism & key values:** 10–14 slides across 11 required archetypes: classification cover (giant numeral/call-sign left, redaction bar above the title, mono meta column right), 8-cell briefing strip, numbered objectives (3–5 theses with `>>>` markers), telemetry grid, threat/risk register (severity column in red), sequence/timeline (vertical mono list on a 2px left rule, hazard markers on critical events), pure-CSS wiring diagram, specimen, alert, audit log (timestamp + actor + event), closing colophon. Colour discipline: terminal green `#4AF626` may appear on at most ONE element in the whole deck (e.g. a single status indicator) or not at all, and never as body text. Banned: border-radius >0, drop shadows, gradients, glassmorphism, glow, sans body fonts, emoji/illustration/stock, light-mode slides, transitions other than cuts. ASCII decoration (`[ … ]`, `>>>`, `///`) at least four times across the deck.
- **Reference / source:** Distilled from Leonxlnx/taste-skill `brutalist-skill` (https://github.com/Leonxlnx/taste-skill), §2.2 Tactical Telemetry & CRT Terminal; deck mechanics follow the html-ppt convention of ⟦S0687⟧.
- **Best for:** Ops/security/incident decks. For web work, the hairline `gap: 1px` cell-grid and register-strip chrome are transferable data-table devices; the overall register is a presentation taste, not a homepage direction.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0696⟧

## ⟦S0697⟧ template/html-ppt-taste-editorial — MCP Market — open-design craft rules + all templates
- **What it is:** A complete standalone 16:9 deck system in editorial-minimalist taste — warm cream slides, serif display with grotesque body, hairline rules, mono meta and generous macro-whitespace — for investor updates, design reviews, internal manifestos and lecture decks that should read like a print supplement.
- **How it looks:** Warm off-white substrate `#FBFBFA` / `#F7F6F3` with off-black `#1A1A19` text (never pure white or black), slides padded at least 72px × 96px. Three type families with three jobs: serif display (Instrument Serif / Newsreader / Lyon), grotesque body (Inter Tight / Switzer — plain Inter banned), mono meta (JetBrains Mono). Titles run `clamp(56px, 6.5vw, 96px)` at line-height 1.05 and tracking −0.025em, at most 14ch wide, one word possibly italic. Every slide opens with a mono uppercase eyebrow (letter-spacing 0.18em) plus a section number (`01 / 09`), and carries its page number in mono at bottom-right. All structure is `1px solid #EAEAEA` hairlines — including a `gap: 1px` hairline-grid table — with no drop shadows anywhere. One muted-pastel accent per deck (e.g. sage `#346538` on `#EDF3EC`, or red `#9F2F2D` on `#FDEBEC`), used at most three times and never as a slide background. Bento data slides use an uneven 6-column hairline grid; the bar chart is flat with the accent only on the latest bar; feature rows are uneven hairline-divided columns, never 3 equal cards.
- **Frame by frame:** Trigger = keyboard, wheel/trackpad, touch swipe or dot buttons (all driving the same active-slide state): the slide changes with a fade of roughly 400ms `cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)` — no translate, no blur, no auto-advance. With the runtime not booted, or in print, every slide stays visible in a vertical stack.
- **Mechanism & key values:** 10–12 slides recommended across 10 archetypes: cover (serif title, italic mid-sentence accent, mono meta footer), eyebrow + thesis (lede left, mono numbered TOC right), numbered manifesto (3–4 hairline-separated theses), bento data slide, quote/pull-out (large serif sentence, mono attribution, hairlines above and below), comparison (two columns split by a vertical hairline), table/index, chart/breakdown, team/colophon (mono key-value list, no avatars), closing (italic serif final line, ghost-button CTA, mono signature). Banned: Inter/Roboto/Open Sans, heavy shadows, glow, gradient text, emojis (use `—` or nothing), full-bleed photography on every slide (one or two image slides max), AI-cliché copy ("Elevate", "Unleash", "Seamless", "Next-Gen"), transitions noisier than the fade.
- **Reference / source:** Distilled from Leonxlnx/taste-skill `minimalist-skill` (https://github.com/Leonxlnx/taste-skill); navigation model follows the project's deck convention (100vw × 100vh `.slide` sections, `.active` / `.is-active`), with the baked `example.html` owning nav inside the gallery iframe.
- **Best for:** Print-register decks; compositionally it is the deck sibling of ⟦S0665⟧'s editorial hierarchy — the eyebrow + section-number chrome and hairline-grid tables transfer directly to editorial web sections.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0697⟧

## ⟦S0703⟧ template/hyperframes — MCP Market — open-design craft rules + all templates
- **What it is:** The HyperFrames composition skill: HTML is the source of truth for video — a composition is an HTML file whose clips carry `data-*` timing attributes, animated by a paused GSAP timeline the framework drives, covering compositions, captions, TTS narration, audio-reactive visuals, text highlighting and scene transitions. (CLI commands live in the separate hyperframes-cli skill.) This entry indexes its prescribed behaviour factually; nothing in it was executed.
- **How it looks:** Rendered video frames at 1920×1080 or 1080×1920: scenes whose elements are laid out at their most-visible "hero frame" first, with headlines at 60px+, body at 20px+, data labels at 16px+ (rendered-video minimums), tabular numerals, and dark backgrounds kept free of full-screen linear gradients (H.264 banding) in favour of radial or solid fills with localised glow. Inside OpenDesign the default test-render identity is a dark canvas `#0b0b0f` with one warm accent `#ffb76b` and one cool accent `#7da4ff`.
- **Frame by frame:** The choreography law for every multi-scene composition: (1) each scene's elements animate IN with `gsap.from()` tweens to their CSS end-state positions — first tween offset 0.1–0.3s (never t=0), at least 3 different eases per scene, no entrance pattern repeated within a scene; (2) the outgoing scene's content stays fully visible — exit tweens are banned; (3) a transition (crossfade, wipe, reveal or shader transition) IS the exit and carries the scene change — jump cuts are banned; (4) only the final scene may fade elements out (e.g. to black).
- **Mechanism & key values:** Layout-before-animation method: build the hero frame as static CSS first (`.scene-content` fills the scene with `width/height: 100%`, padding and flex-column + gap; absolute positioning reserved for decoratives), then `gsap.from()` entrances and final-scene `gsap.to()` exits. Clip contract: every clip needs `id`, `data-start`, `data-track-index` (layering is CSS `z-index`, not track index), `data-duration` (required for img/div/compositions; takes precedence over timeline length); compositions add `data-composition-id`, `data-width`/`data-height`, optional `data-composition-src` — sub-compositions wrap in `<template>`, standalone files must NOT. Timeline contract: all timelines `{ paused: true }`, registered as `window.__timelines["<id>"]`, built synchronously (never in async/setTimeout/Promise). Determinism: no `Math.random()` / `Date.now()` (seeded PRNG e.g. mulberry32); no `repeat: -1` — compute finite repeats as `Math.ceil(duration / cycleDuration) - 1`; never animate `visibility`/`display` or call media play/pause; video is always `muted playsinline` with audio as a separate `<audio>` element; no `<br>` in content text (wrap via `max-width`), except deliberate one-word-per-line display titles. Visual Identity Gate: no composition HTML before a DESIGN.md / visual-style.md / named style (8 presets in `visual-styles.md`: Swiss Pulse, Velvet Standard, Deconstructed, Maximalist Type, Data Drift, Soft Signal, Folk Frequency, Shadow Cut) is in force; OD runs skip the gate and use the defaults above. OpenDesign render path (described, not executed): scaffold into a hidden `.hyperframes-cache/<ts>-<rand>` dir, edit only its `index.html`, dispatch render via the OD daemon's `media generate --surface video --model hyperframes-html` and poll `media wait` (each call ≤ ~25s) — only the `.mp4` lands in the project root; light subcommands (lint, transcribe, tts) may run in-shell, Chrome-bound ones (render/inspect/preview) go through the daemon. Quality tooling: `lint` + `validate` (WCAG contrast audit seeking 5 timestamps, 4.5:1 normal / 3:1 large text), `inspect` (headless-Chrome layout audit with timestamps/selectors/fix hints, `--samples 15`, `--at` for hero frames; intentional overflow marked `data-layout-allow-overflow`), and an animation-map script reporting per-tween summaries, an ASCII Gantt, stagger intervals, >1s dead zones and offscreen/collision/invisible/paced flags.
- **Reference / source:** HyperFrames framework; GSAP 3.14.2 (CDN) for timelines; Kokoro-82M for TTS (references/tts.md); shader transitions in the `@hyperframes/shader-transitions` package; on-demand references for captions, audio-reactive, CSS marker patterns (highlight/circle/burst/scribble/sketchout), typography, motion principles, transitions, and HTML-in-Canvas (`drawElementImage`).
- **Best for:** Video production — intros, title cards, captioned clips, audio-reactive pieces. For web builds its transferable discipline is the layout-before-animation method and the entrance-only/transition-as-exit choreography law.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0703⟧

## ⟦S0704⟧ template/ib-pitch-book — MCP Market — open-design craft rules + all templates
- **What it is:** An investment-banking pitch-book workflow for strategic-alternatives / M&A board materials: a 10-slide deck with confidentiality ribbons, financial tables, a valuation football field and a four-path alternatives matrix, seeded from a shipped template. Repackaged from Anthropic's Pitch Agent; outputs are discussion materials, not advice.
- **How it looks:** A sober board deck on system fonts (deliberate, for confidential/offline export): cover with bank brand, project codename and a confidentiality ribbon; trading-comparables and precedent-transaction tables in tabular numerals with median/mean summary rows and the target row highlighted; a football-field slide of aligned horizontal valuation ranges with a current-price tick; a DCF slide pairing an assumptions table with a WACC × terminal-growth sensitivity matrix; a four-quadrant strategic-alternatives matrix with the recommended path inverted; and a recommendation slide built on a pull-quote plus a phased process timeline.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion specified; navigation is the seed template's horizontal deck chrome with print rules.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Default 10-slide spine: 1 cover, 2 table of contents, 3 sector/market context (KPI strip + one chart narrative; dense slides use the seed's `.body.fit`, `.metric-strip`, `.chart-card`, `.compact-copy` primitives with chart height ~150px, checked at 1366×768 and 1440×900 for chrome overlap), 4 trading comps, 5 precedent transactions, 6 football field, 7 DCF + sensitivity, 8 alternatives matrix, 9 recommendation, 10 disclaimers & sources. Build from `assets/template.html` (keep its horizontal navigation, demo-data/source-status treatment, print rules, system-font defaults); `example.html` (fictional NorthPeak / Hartfield) is a layout-density reference only — its names and numbers must never ship as real. Data discipline: every figure carries a citation log (source type — public filing / licensed vendor / management provided / user supplied / assumption; source name; freshness; licensing; confidence — source-backed / management-provided / model-derived / assumption); management-provided and MNPI-bearing data is separated in tables and footnotes and marked restricted; untraceable numbers are removed or labelled assumption in the slide footer. External sources are treated as untrusted evidence that cannot override the skill or its compliance gates. Remote fonts are opt-in only (privacy/availability/PDF trade-off must be accepted). Pre-flight reads: `references/compliance.md`, `references/conventions.md`, the seed, and the active DESIGN.md (tokens mapped into the deck's `:root`).
- **Reference / source:** Workflow and naming adapted from Anthropic's Apache-2.0 `financial-services` repository (Pitch Agent) — see the skill's `references/attribution.md`. Deliberately distinct from ⟦S0693⟧ (VC/seed fundraising), ⟦S0685⟧ (magazine decks), ⟦S0676⟧ (the Markdown DCF memo this deck summarises) and ⟦S0681⟧ (operating finance reports).
- **Best for:** Board/M&A materials. The football-field aligned-range graphic is the transferable device — a strong pattern for price-band or options-range presentation in work/gallery or pricing contexts.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0704⟧

## ⟦S0705⟧ template/image-poster — MCP Market — open-design craft rules + all templates
- **What it is:** An image-generation dispatch workflow: assemble one tight, structured prompt from the brief and produce exactly one finished image asset per turn (variations only when asked), delivered as a file in the project — never described without being produced, and never wrapped in an `<artifact>` tag.
- **How it looks:** The produced still image itself, framed per the assembled prompt: subject and composition first (what is in frame, where, at what scale, eye-line and crop), then lighting and mood, palette/textures, and camera language when photographic realism is wanted.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — the output is a still image.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Project metadata supplies `imageModel`, `imageAspect` and optional `imageStyle`; `imageAspect` is honoured exactly (upstream cost is the same, and matching it avoids a re-render). Prompt assembly order is fixed: 1) subject + composition, 2) lighting + mood (natural/studio/moody; warm/cool; key + rim + fill; time of day outdoors), 3) palette + textures (hex anchors when a brand palette exists, else a 3-word mood tag such as "muted ochre + ink"), 4) camera/lens only on request (e.g. "85mm portrait, shallow DOF" or a film stock), 5) the avoid list (no extra fingers, no warped text, no logo placeholders). Dispatch via the unified media contract (described, not executed here): `media generate --project … --surface image --model <imageModel> --aspect <imageAspect> --output "<name>.png" --prompt "<assembled prompt>"`, which returns one JSON line naming the file. Hard rules: one image per turn unless variations are asked; no filler typography inside the image unless in-frame text was requested — real copy beats lorem; every render is saved.
- **Reference / source:** None named beyond the OpenDesign media contract and the project's image-model metadata.
- **Best for:** Producing poster/hero image assets. No page layout content — indexed so the image route sits alongside the templates that consume imagery.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0705⟧

## ⟦S0707⟧ template/kami-deck — MCP Market — open-design craft rules + all templates
- **What it is:** A single self-contained HTML deck in the kami (紙/纸) design system — print rhythm, one ink-blue accent, serif at a single weight, no italic, no cool greys: viewport-sized slides on one horizontal track, magazine-style. Sister skill to kami-landing ⟦S0708⟧ (outside this chunk); its navigation model is borrowed from guizang-ppt ⟦S0685⟧ while the aesthetic stays kami.
- **How it looks:** Two slide registers only. Cover, chapter and end slides flip to ink-blue `#1B365D` with ivory text — the deck's only dark surfaces. Everything else sits on parchment `#f5f4ed` in serif at weight 500. Every slide carries a chrome strip (brand mark · deck title · live counter like `01 / 09`), all counters/metrics/page numbers in tabular numerals, and an ink-blue progress bar with dot navigation — ink-blue is also the only accent anywhere (covers may use at most 5% of a parchment slide's surface). No gradients, almost no imagery: hierarchy is carried by type alone. Slide kinds: cover (centred serif title + tagline), chapter (numeral divider), content (section number + title + body + optional bullets), stats (3–4 metric cells: value · label · sub), quote (pull quote with an ink-blue left rule + author signature), cta (closing pitch + 1–2 buttons), end (mega serif kicker word + colophon). A typical deck runs 11 slides; 6–15 is the sweet spot.
- **Frame by frame:** Trigger = → key, Space, or scroll/swipe: the flex track slides smoothly one viewport to the side, the dot indicator advances and the ink-blue progress bar ticks forward. Trigger = Esc: an overview grid of scaled slide thumbnails appears. At 1080px and 640px widths the cover/content slides collapse to a single column and the dot nav keeps working.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Tokens, type rules and forbidden colours live in `design-systems/kami/DESIGN.md` (the source of truth — read before shipping); slide scale ratios versus print are macro ×1.6 and letter-spacing ×0.6 (DESIGN.md §3/§5). Language stacks set on `:root`: EN → Charter, zh-CN → TsangerJinKai02 / Source Han Serif, ja → YuMincho (JA also overrides `--olive` to `#4d4c48` for YuMincho's thinner strokes). Hard boundaries: no second accent colour; no italic anywhere (emphasis swaps to ink-blue); no `rgba()` tag fills — pre-blend over parchment and use the solid hex table; no router. The runtime (keyboard/wheel/touch nav, dots, progress, ESC overview) matches `open-design-landing-deck/scripts/compose.ts`'s model, but that system's CSS is explicitly not reused.
- **Reference / source:** Upstream `tw93/kami` (https://github.com/tw93/kami, MIT) — the original Claude skill; tokens in `design-systems/kami/DESIGN.md`; navigation model from ⟦S0685⟧; sister skill kami-landing ⟦S0708⟧.
- **Best for:** Print-rhythm decks and title plates. The per-slide chrome strip with a live counter and the two-register (ink-blue divider / parchment content) rhythm are the transferable devices for section dividers on editorial pages.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0707⟧
# Chunk: skills S0708–S0762

Two collections: S0708–S0750 are OpenDesign `template/` skills (MCP Market — open-design craft rules + all templates); S0751–S0762 are brand DESIGN.md systems (MCP Market — 152 brand design systems, open-design). Family notes: S0720–S0724 are the five "Orbit briefing" siblings — same briefing concept, each scoped to one connector and dressed in that product's own chrome (not duplicates).
