- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL — hero type treatment and scale-hover transfer; the lime fintech identity is distinctive and not a trades default (basis: trade fit).
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0898⟧

## ⟦S0899⟧ x-ai — Part 17 — MCP Market — brand design systems (open-design)
- **What it is:** xAI's website design system: dark-first monospace brutalism — an almost-black canvas, white-only palette, monospace display type at extreme scale, and depth built purely from border opacity. Zero shadows, zero gradients, zero colour.
- **How it looks:** `#1f2228` (warm blue-tinted near-black) everywhere; `#ffffff` text with secondary levels at 70/50/30% white. The hero is a single GeistMono headline up to 320px at weight 300, centred in a full-viewport field of empty dark space. Body and section headings switch to universalSans (30px headings, 16px/1.5 body). Buttons are GeistMono uppercase at 1.4px tracking with sharp 0px corners: white-filled primary, ghost secondary with a `rgba(255,255,255,0.2)` border. Cards are transparent with 0.1-opacity white borders.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. The signature interaction is inverted: links and interactive elements dim on hover to `rgba(255,255,255,0.5)` instead of brightening; card borders brighten 0.1 → 0.2 opacity on hover. No durations are prescribed.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Elevation by opacity only: flat → 3% white surface → 0.1 border → 0.2 border (active) → blue focus ring `rgb(59,130,246)/0.5` (the single non-white value, Tailwind's default ring). Sparse 8px-grid spacing scale (4/8/24/48px); section padding 48–96px; container ~1200px. Radius 0px default, 4px rare. Breakpoints 640/768/1000/1024/1280/1536/2000px (Tailwind). Built with Tailwind arbitrary values; icons from Heroicons.
- **Reference / source:** xAI (x.ai); GeistMono (Vercel's Geist Mono) and universalSans typefaces.
- **Best for:** The extreme-scale monospace hero as a single dramatic device, and the dim-on-hover / border-opacity discipline for a stark technical section. As a whole identity it signals an AI research lab, not a trade firm.
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL — the mono-display hero device transfers; the monochrome lab identity does not (basis: trade fit).
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0899⟧

## ⟦S0900⟧ xiaohongshu — Part 17 — MCP Market — brand design systems (open-design)
- **What it is:** Xiaohongshu's (小红书 / RED) design system, sampled from the live site's production CSS: a lifestyle UGC platform whose UI deliberately disappears behind user photos — white surfaces, one brand red, translucent-overlay neutrals, pill everything, and a variable-height masonry waterfall feed.
- **How it looks:** White `#FFFFFF` cards on a `#F5F5F5` canvas, soft-black text (`rgba(0,0,0,0.80)` titles, 0.62 paragraphs — never pure black), PingFang SC at 400/500/600 with a compact scale (H1 only 32px/600; body 14–16px) and a dedicated `RED Number` face for counts. Brand red `#FF2442` (component layer `#FF2E4D`) appears only on primary pill CTAs, the 2px tab underline, hearts and badges; bookmark-active is the lone yellow `#FDBC5F`. Feed cards round at 12–16px with no shadow, image flush to the top edge; card heights vary with image aspect — the misalignment is the look.
- **Frame by frame:** Nearly static. PC feed-card hover → translateY(−2px) plus a faint shadow `0 4px 12px rgba(0,0,0,0.08)` (dropped entirely in dark mode). Mobile secondary actions slide up as a bottom sheet over a `rgba(0,0,0,0.5)` scrim (top-only 16px radius, drag handle), dismissed by drag-down or scrim tap. Tab switches move the 2px red underline to the active label. No durations are recorded in the document.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Translucent neutrals instead of grey steps: fills `rgba(48,48,52,0.05/0.10/0.20)` for hover/disabled/pressed; separators `rgba(0,0,0,0.08/0.20)`. Dark mode sampled too (surface `#19191E`, canvas `#0E0E11`, red shifts to `#FF2E4D`). Waterfall: JS-positioned masonry (translate3d + ResizeObserver), 5 columns ≥960px → 4 → 3 → 2 below 500px, gap fixed 10px; mobile two-column at ~48.2% width. Follow button is a three-state component (red "+ Follow" → grey "Following" → grey "Mutual"). Buttons pill 9999px, 8px 20px / 12px 32px padding; min tap target 44px. Brand-red rule (explicit in source): emit `#FF2442` by default; `#FF2E4D` only when pixel-replicating the live button/active-bar; never mix both on one component. The wordmark itself must not be fabricated — labelled grey placeholder instead.
- **Reference / source:** Xiaohongshu (xiaohongshu.com/explore) — values sampled from production CSS `:root` / `.force-light` / `:root[dark]` blocks, as recorded in the document.
- **Best for:** The waterfall masonry is a direct model for a work/gallery section of real project photos at mixed aspect ratios; the three-state follow button maps to any subscribe/save toggle; translucent-fill state system and bottom-sheet pattern transfer to mobile-first pages. The lifestyle-UGC brand voice itself does not transfer.
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL — the masonry gallery and state-fill mechanisms genuinely fit trades work galleries; the brand system around them does not (basis: trade fit).
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0900⟧
# Chunk: skills S0901–S0953

One brand design system (S0901, tail of Part 19) followed by 52 Front-End Checklist rule-skills (Part 20). The rule-skills are audit rules, not design systems: each prescribes one checkable requirement plus a check/fix pattern, a priority · difficulty · time rating, and a rule page on frontendchecklist.io. Relationships worth knowing before shortlisting: S0952 (breadcrumb schema) and S0953 (breadcrumb markup) are complementary halves of one feature, not duplicates; S0906 (notifications) and S0927 (live regions) share the aria-live mechanism at different scopes; S0908 is the full tooltip pattern and S0936 only its naming check; S0931/S0932 are an inverse pair (required children vs required parent); S0943/S0944/S0945 are the visible-byline / credentials-bio / structured-markup trio for author E-E-A-T; S0919, S0921, S0930, S0933, S0938, S0939 are six distinct ARIA-validity rules.

## ⟦S0901⟧ zapier — Part 19 — MCP Market — 152 brand design systems (open-design)
- **What it is:** A full brand design system reverse-engineered from Zapier's website: warm cream canvas, one vivid orange accent, three-font type system, border-defined structure instead of shadows. Category given in the source: Productivity & SaaS.
- **How it looks:** Pages sit on warm cream `#fffefb` (never pure white) with warm near-black text `#201515`. Hero headlines in wide geometric Degular Display at 56–80px, weight 500, line-height 0.90 — vertically compressed stacked blocks. Cards and inputs are flat cream boxes outlined with 1px sand borders `#c5c0b1` and 5px radius; no drop shadows anywhere. The single orange `#ff4f00` appears only on primary CTA buttons and as a 4px inset-shadow underline under the active tab. Sections are separated by full-width sand divider lines, not background colour changes; the footer flips to a full dark `#201515` block with cream text and sand links. Integration cards show two app icons joined by an arrow/connector inside a sand border.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion system is prescribed. The only state changes: tab hover swaps the inset underline from orange (active) to sand; dark and ghost buttons shift background to sand `#c5c0b1` on hover; links remove their underline on hover; input focus turns the border orange.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Colours — Zapier Black `#201515`, Cream White `#fffefb`, Off-White `#fffdf9`, Zapier Orange `#ff4f00`, Dark Charcoal `#36342e`, Warm Gray `#939084`, Sand `#c5c0b1`, Light Sand `#eceae3`, Mid Warm `#b5b2aa`. Tab indicator: `box-shadow: rgb(255,79,0) 0px -4px 0px 0px inset` (active), sand version on hover. Type — Degular Display hero 80/56/40px w500 lh 0.90; Inter section heading 48px w500 lh 1.04, sub-headings 36/32/28px, card title 24px w600 tracking −0.48px, body 16px w400–500 lh 1.20–1.25 tracking −0.16px, caption 14px, micro 12px w600 uppercase +0.5px tracking; GT Alpina editorial 48px w250 tracking −1.92px / 40px w300 tracking −1.6px. Buttons — orange CTA padding 8px 16px radius 4px; large dark/ghost buttons padding 20px 24px radius 8px; pill radius 20px padding 0 16px; overlay button `rgba(45,45,46,0.5)` radius 20px. Spacing base 8px, scale 1–72px; section padding 64–80px vertical; max content width ~1200px. Radius scale 3/4/5/8/14/20px. Breakpoints: <450, 450–600, 600–640, 640–680, 680–768, 768–991, 991–1024, 1024–1280, >1280px; nav collapses to hamburger, hero Degular scales 80px → 40–56px, section padding drops to 40–48px on mobile.
- **Reference / source:** open-design brand design systems collection (Part 19); models zapier.com. Fonts named: Degular Display, Inter, GT Alpina.
- **Best for:** A warm, paper-like SaaS/trades rebrand direction — hero, navigation, forms, footer, proof/stat sections. Trade-fit note: the border-not-shadow structure and single-accent discipline transfer well to a local firm's site; the fonts are commercial, so a build would substitute metric-similar faces.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0901⟧

## ⟦S0902⟧ 404-page — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** Audit rule: the site must serve a custom, branded 404 page with recovery paths, returned with a real HTTP 404 status. Priority: medium · Difficulty: beginner · Time: 20 min.
- **How it looks:** A centred error page in the site's own branding: large "404" / "Page Not Found" heading, a short apology line, a prominent search box, and a "Try these instead" link list (Home, Products, Blog, Contact). Nothing moves.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. On load the page can fire a 404 tracking event (path + referrer) to analytics.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Server/framework must return status 404 (a branded page served with 200 is a soft 404 — an indexing bug); page carries `<meta name="robots" content="noindex">`; reference CSS centres content in a max-width 500px column, h1 at 3rem, search input max-width 300px padding 0.75rem 1rem. Nginx `error_page 404 /404.html;`, Apache `ErrorDocument 404 /404.html`, Next.js `app/not-found.tsx`.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist (thedaviddias/front-end-checklist); rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/html/404-page
- **Best for:** Error/utility pages on any build; a QA checklist item before launch. Trade fit: any trades homepage package should ship a branded 404 with phone number and service links as recovery paths.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0902⟧

## ⟦S0903⟧ about-page — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** Audit rule: the site must have a dedicated About page naming the people/organisation behind the content, as an E-E-A-T trust signal. Priority: medium · Difficulty: intermediate · Time: 10 min.
- **How it looks:** A normal content page at /about — purpose, history, mission, the key people, expertise evidence and contact information — linked from main navigation or footer.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Route /about, discoverable via nav/footer link; judged against Google Search Central Search Essentials. No numeric parameters prescribed.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist; rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/seo/about-page
- **Best for:** Towns/areas and trust content planning; a pre-launch SEO checklist gate. Trade fit: directly relevant — a local firm's About page (owner, years trading, accreditations) is a primary trust page.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0903⟧

## ⟦S0904⟧ accessibility-testing — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** Audit rule: automated accessibility testing (axe-core based) must be wired into component tests, E2E tests and CI. Priority: high · Difficulty: intermediate · Time: 30 min.
- **How it looks:** Nothing on screen — this is a test-suite/CI rule. Its visible effect is indirect: shipped pages free of the violations axe catches (missing alt text, missing form labels, invalid ARIA, many contrast failures).
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** jest-axe for component tests (`axe(container)` + `toHaveNoViolations()`), @axe-core/playwright (`AxeBuilder`, e.g. `.withTags(['wcag2a','wcag2aa'])`, including a 375×667 mobile-viewport scan) or cypress-axe for E2E, pa11y for CI. Lighthouse CI assertion example: `categories:accessibility: ["error", {minScore: 0.9}]`. Automated testing catches an estimated 30–50% of WCAG violations; target ≤ 0 unexpected axe violations on covered states; manual keyboard/screen-reader checks still required.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist; rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/testing/accessibility-testing
- **Best for:** Build QA process for every section version; pairs with all the ARIA rule-skills in this part. Trade fit: process rule, applies to all builds.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0904⟧

## ⟦S0905⟧ accessible-authentication — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** Audit rule: sign-in, MFA, CAPTCHA and recovery flows must not depend on memorisation or transcription when an assisted path exists (WCAG 2.2 SC 3.3.8). Priority: high · Difficulty: advanced · Time: 25 min.
- **How it looks:** A login form that accepts pasted passwords and password-manager autofill, an OTP field the browser can autofill, and alternative buttons such as "Continue with a passkey" or "Email me a sign-in link" next to the password path.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Field semantics: email `autocomplete="username webauthn"`, password `autocomplete="current-password"`, OTP `autocomplete="one-time-code"` with `inputmode="numeric"`; never block paste; do not split the OTP into a custom widget that breaks autofill; CAPTCHA in auth needs a non-cognitive alternative path.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist; rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/accessibility/accessible-authentication (the rule text cites WCAG 2.2 SC 3.3.8 Accessible Authentication (Minimum)).
- **Best for:** Forms — any login, account or client-portal flow. Trade fit: low for a trades marketing homepage (no auth), essential if a build adds a customer portal.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0905⟧

## ⟦S0906⟧ accessible-notifications — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** Audit rule: toast/alert notifications must be announced to screen readers via ARIA live regions with the right urgency and enough reading time. Priority: high · Difficulty: intermediate · Time: 25 min. Shares its mechanism with ⟦S0927⟧, scoped to notifications.
- **How it looks:** Toast cards stack in a fixed bottom-right container (1rem from edges, 0.5rem gaps), each with a coloured 4px left border and icon — green `#28a745` on `#d4edda` for success, red `#dc3545` on `#f8d7da` for errors, amber `#ffc107` on `#fff3cd` for warnings, blue `#17a2b8` on `#d1ecf1` for info — plus a dismiss × button.
- **Frame by frame:** Trigger: a toast is added → it slides in from the right over 0.3s ease-out (translateX(100%) + opacity 0 → rest position, fully opaque) → it stays for its type's duration → auto-dismisses or is closed with the × button. Screen-reader path in parallel: role="status" (polite) for success/info, role="alert" (assertive) for errors/warnings. Under prefers-reduced-motion the slide-in animation is removed.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Durations: success 3–5s (map value 3000ms), info 5s (5000ms), warning 8s (8000ms), error 0 = never auto-dismiss. Toast styling: padding 1rem, radius 0.5rem, shadow `0 4px 12px rgba(0,0,0,0.15)`, container z-index 1000. `aria-atomic="true"` on live regions; assertive reserved for truly urgent messages only.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist; rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/html/accessible-notifications
- **Best for:** Forms (submission success/error feedback), call/CTA confirmation states. Trade fit: quote-form feedback on a trades site should follow exactly this pattern.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0906⟧

## ⟦S0907⟧ accessible-tables — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** Audit rule: data tables must use semantic markup — `<th>` with scope, caption, id/headers for complex tables — and never be used for layout. Priority: medium · Difficulty: intermediate · Time: 20 min.
- **How it looks:** An ordinary data table visually; the difference is heard, not seen: a screen reader announces each cell with its row and column headers ("Row 3, Column 2: $99" with context) instead of a bare value. On mobile, wide tables sit in a horizontally scrollable wrapper region.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** `scope="col" | "row" | "colgroup" | "rowgroup"`; `<caption>` or aria-labelledby for purpose; merged-cell tables use `id` on headers and `headers="…"` lists on cells. Mobile wrapper: `tabindex="0" role="region" aria-label="…"` with `overflow-x: auto` and a `2px solid #005fcc` focus outline. Finding priority per the rule: missing header relationships outrank a missing caption on simple tables.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist; rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/accessibility/accessible-tables
- **Best for:** Pricing/comparison tables (e.g. service price bands) in work/gallery or call/CTA sections. Trade fit: relevant wherever a build shows a price or coverage table.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0907⟧

## ⟦S0908⟧ accessible-tooltips — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** Audit rule: tooltips must work for keyboard and screen-reader users — focusable trigger, aria-describedby association, hover + focus display, Escape dismissal. Priority: medium · Difficulty: intermediate · Time: 20 min. The naming-only sub-check is ⟦S0936⟧.
- **How it looks:** A small dark bubble (`#1a1a1a` background, white text, 0.875rem, padding 0.5rem 0.75rem, radius 4px) with a 6px arrow, offset 8px from its trigger on the top/bottom/left/right; white on `#1a1a1a` is a 16.1:1 contrast ratio, above the 4.5:1 WCAG requirement.
- **Frame by frame:** Trigger: hover or keyboard focus on the trigger (after a 300ms default delay in the reference React component) → tooltip fades in over 0.15s ease-out, rising 4px into place → stays visible while hovered or focused → Escape key, mouse-leave or blur hides it. Under prefers-reduced-motion it appears instantly at full opacity. Essential information must never live only in a tooltip.
- **Mechanism & key values:** `role="tooltip"` + trigger `aria-describedby="<tooltip-id>"`; Floating UI variant uses offset(8), flip(), shift({padding: 8}) middleware. Native `title` attribute is recorded as limited — custom tooltip preferred.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist; rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/html/accessible-tooltips
- **Best for:** Forms (field help), navigation, icon buttons anywhere. Trade fit: minor on a trades homepage; relevant for form hints and icon-only controls.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0908⟧

## ⟦S0909⟧ accesskeys — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** Audit rule: every `accesskey` attribute value on a page must be unique, so keyboard shortcuts never collide. Priority: medium · Difficulty: intermediate · Time: 10 min.
- **How it looks:** Invisible — accesskeys are keyboard shortcuts on links/controls (e.g. `accesskey="h"` on Home, `accesskey="c"` on Contact). A duplicate means only the first matching element is reachable and behaviour varies by browser.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** One value per element, unique document-wide; fix is to reassign or remove redundant accesskeys. Standards named: WCAG Overview (W3C WAI), MDN Accessibility.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist; rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/accessibility/accesskeys
- **Best for:** Navigation QA on keyboard-heavy pages. Trade fit: rarely used on trades sites; a checklist sweep item only.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0909⟧

## ⟦S0910⟧ accordion-accessibility — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** Audit rule: accordions must use button triggers with aria-expanded/aria-controls inside headings, with full keyboard support. Priority: medium · Difficulty: intermediate · Time: 25 min.
- **How it looks:** A bordered stack (1px `#e0e0e0` border, 8px radius) of full-width header rows — bold 1rem trigger text left, chevron icon right, 1rem × 1.5rem padding — with content panels opening beneath each header.
- **Frame by frame:** Trigger: Enter/Space (or click) on a header button → panel unhides and plays a 0.2s ease-out slide-down (opacity 0 + translateY(−8px) → opaque at rest) while the chevron rotates 180° over 0.2s and aria-expanded flips to true → panel content sits open until toggled again. Focus moves between headers with Arrow Up/Down, Home (first) and End (last). Under prefers-reduced-motion, panel animation and icon transition are both disabled. Focus ring: `2px solid #0066cc` outline, offset −2px.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Trigger = `<button>` inside a heading (h2/h3 per document outline, no skipped levels), `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls="<panel-id>"`; panel `role="region"` + `aria-labelledby="<trigger-id>"` + `hidden` when closed. Native `<details>/<summary>` is the recorded low-styling alternative.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist; rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/html/accordion-accessibility
- **Best for:** FAQ sections, process detail, service explanations. Trade fit: high — FAQ and "how it works" accordions are standard trades-homepage sections; this is the pattern to copy.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0910⟧

## ⟦S0911⟧ affiliate-disclosure — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** Audit rule: pages with affiliate or sponsored links must carry a clear disclosure before the links appear (FTC requirement). Priority: medium · Difficulty: intermediate · Time: 10 min.
- **How it looks:** A small shaded notice box near the top of the article (reference example: `#f9f9f9` background, 10px padding, 4px radius, small italic text) stating the financial relationship in plain language, before any affiliate link.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Disclosure placed at the beginning of content or adjacent to the links; unambiguous wording ("we may receive a small commission at no extra cost to you"). No numeric parameters beyond placement.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist; rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/seo/affiliate-disclosure (rule text names FTC guidelines)
- **Best for:** Blog/review content with commercial links. Trade fit: low for a trades homepage; relevant only if a build includes review/roundup articles.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0911⟧

## ⟦S0912⟧ ai-content — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** Audit rule: AI-generated content must be human-reviewed and refined — accuracy checked, original insight added — before it can rank. Priority: medium · Difficulty: intermediate · Time: 10 min.
- **How it looks:** Nothing visual; the on-page trace is an article header carrying a named human author and a "Fact-checked on <date>" line, and body copy with first-hand experience rather than generic rewrite text.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Judged against Google's Search Essentials and "helpful, reliable, people-first content" guidance; AI-assisted drafting alone is not a failure — unsupported claims, missing editorial review and low originality are. No numeric parameters.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist; rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/seo/ai-content
- **Best for:** Content QA for any copy written with AI assistance. Trade fit: applies to trades-site copy production generally.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0912⟧

## ⟦S0913⟧ all-noindex-pages — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** Audit rule: inventory every page carrying a `noindex` directive and confirm only pages that should stay out of search (admin, utility, thin, staging) are blocked. Priority: medium · Difficulty: intermediate · Time: 10 min.
- **How it looks:** Invisible on screen — the directive lives in `<meta name="robots" content="noindex, follow">` (or `noindex, nofollow`) or the X-Robots-Tag header; the failure mode is a money page silently missing from search results.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** `noindex, follow` = hide page, still crawl its links; `noindex, nofollow` = ignore entirely; contrasted with robots.txt `disallow`, which blocks crawling rather than indexing. Verify via rendered HTML/headers and Search Console; fix conflicting canonical/robots signals at the strongest final signal first.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist; rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/seo/all-noindex-pages
- **Best for:** Pre-launch and post-migration SEO audits. Trade fit: launch checklist for every trades site.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0913⟧

## ⟦S0914⟧ alt-text — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** Audit rule: every `<img>` must have an alt attribute — descriptive for informative images, empty for decorative — per WCAG 2.1 SC 1.1.1 (Level A). Priority: critical · Difficulty: beginner · Time: 15 min.
- **How it looks:** Invisible visually; a screen reader reads the alt aloud in place of the image. Informative alt describes purpose/meaning ("Bar chart showing Q3 2024 revenue increased 40% year-over-year, reaching $2.4M"), linked-image alt names the destination ("Follow us on Twitter"), image-of-text alt repeats the text verbatim, decorative images get `alt=""` so they are skipped entirely.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Missing alt = error; alt equal to filename or generic ("image", "photo") = failure. Complex images (charts, org charts) get a short alt plus a longer description via aria-describedby/figcaption. CAPTCHA alt describes purpose, not characters. Verified with axe/WAVE and the Lighthouse "Images do not have alternate text" audit. Source cites ~2.2 billion people worldwide with vision impairment.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist; rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/images/alt-text (rule text names the W3C alt decision tree and WCAG 2.1 SC 1.1.1)
- **Best for:** Every image on every section — hero, work/gallery before-and-after photos, team photos. Trade fit: critical; gallery-heavy trades pages live or die on this in QA.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0914⟧

## ⟦S0915⟧ anchor-smooth-scroll — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** Audit rule: smooth scrolling on anchor links must be disabled (instant jump) for users with prefers-reduced-motion, and anchor jumps must move keyboard focus to the target. Priority: low · Difficulty: beginner · Time: 10 min.
- **How it looks:** Clicking a same-page nav link either glides the page to the section (motion allowed) or cuts straight to it (reduced motion). The target section receives focus, so a keyboard user's next Tab continues from there.
- **Frame by frame:** Trigger: anchor click → if `(prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)` matches, the page smooth-scrolls to the target; if reduced motion is set, the page jumps instantly → focus is set on the target element (`tabindex="-1"` added if needed, `focus({preventScroll: true})`) → end state: target at the top of the viewport, focus ring suppressed for programmatic focus but shown (`:focus-visible`, 2px outline) for keyboard focus.
- **Mechanism & key values:** CSS form: `scroll-behavior: smooth` only inside `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)`. JS form: `scrollIntoView({behavior: prefersReduced ? 'instant' : 'smooth', block: 'start'})` driven by a matchMedia listener. Rationale: animated scroll can trigger vertigo/nausea in vestibular disorders.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist; rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/accessibility/anchor-smooth-scroll
- **Best for:** Navigation — single-page trades homepages with in-page section links. Trade fit: direct; one-page builds use anchor nav heavily.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0915⟧

## ⟦S0916⟧ anchor-text — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** Audit rule: link text must describe the destination — no "click here" / "read more" generics, and no keyword stuffing. Priority: medium · Difficulty: beginner · Time: 5 min.
- **How it looks:** Links read as meaningful phrases inside sentences ("read our complete guide to SEO best practices") instead of bare "click here"; a screen reader's link list reads as a meaningful index of destinations.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** No numeric parameters; judged on descriptiveness and context. Verification via rendered HTML inspection and Search Console.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist; rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/seo/anchor-text
- **Best for:** All copy — service links, towns/areas links, article links. Trade fit: applies to every internal link on a trades site (e.g. town pages should be linked with the town + service as the anchor).
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0916⟧

## ⟦S0917⟧ animated-content — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** Audit rule: animated GIFs should be converted to MP4/WebM video — GIFs are uncompressed and typically 80%+ larger for the same clip. Priority: medium · Difficulty: intermediate · Time: 10 min.
- **How it looks:** A short looping animation on the page that behaves like a GIF (autoplays silently, loops) but is delivered as a `<video>` with a poster frame shown while it loads; below-fold clips lazy-load.
- **Frame by frame:** Trigger: page load / scroll into view → poster frame displays → video autoplays muted and loops continuously (the GIF behaviour being mimicked) → end state: seamless loop, no controls shown. Motion content itself is whatever the clip shows; the rule governs the delivery format, not the choreography.
- **Mechanism & key values:** `<video autoplay loop muted playsinline poster="…">` with WebM source first, MP4 fallback. Avoid GIF for animations larger than a few hundred pixels or longer than a second. Tools named: FFmpeg, Cloudinary/Imgix, Lighthouse.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist; rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/performance/animated-content (rule text points at web.dev performance guidance)
- **Best for:** Work/gallery demos, before/after clips, process animations. Trade fit: relevant if a build embeds demo loops of work in progress.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0917⟧

## ⟦S0918⟧ animation-performance — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** Audit rule: animations must animate only `transform` and `opacity` (GPU compositor properties) — never layout properties like width, top or margin — to hold 60fps. Priority: high · Difficulty: intermediate · Time: 20 min.
- **How it looks:** Motion that stays smooth even while the page is busy: elements fade, slide and scale without jank or reflow of surrounding content.
- **Frame by frame:** The rule's reference patterns: fade-in — opacity 0 → 1 over 300ms ease; slide-up fade — opacity 0 + translateY(16px) → rest over 400ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); slide-in from off-canvas — translateX(−100%) → 0 over 300ms ease-out (replacing a left: −100% → 0 keyframe); expand — scale(0) → scale(1) over 300ms (replacing width/height keyframes); button press — scale(0.97) while active. All animations are removed under prefers-reduced-motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Rendering pipeline: animating layout properties restarts Style → Layout → Paint → Composite every frame on the main thread; transform/opacity only trigger Composite. Position changes convert to translate(), size changes to scale(). `will-change: transform` used sparingly (each promoted layer costs GPU memory; add just before animating, remove after). CSS transitions/animations preferred over JS libraries for simple effects.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist; rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/css/animation-performance
- **Best for:** Every animated section — hero entrances, scroll reveals, hover states, switchers. Trade fit: this is the performance gate for all motion design on the portfolio builds.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0918⟧

## ⟦S0919⟧ aria-allowed-attr — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** Audit rule: an element may only carry the ARIA attributes its role supports (e.g. `aria-checked` belongs on checkbox, not on a heading). Priority: medium · Difficulty: intermediate · Time: 10 min. One of six ARIA-validity rules in this part (with ⟦S0921⟧, ⟦S0930⟧, ⟦S0933⟧, ⟦S0938⟧, ⟦S0939⟧).
- **How it looks:** Invisible — unsupported attributes are ignored or misread by screen readers, so the failure is a control whose state is never announced.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Validate each role/attribute pair against WAI-ARIA 1.2; fix by removing or correcting the attribute — or, per the rule's standing guidance, by replacing the custom widget with a native element. Verify in the accessibility tree / axe / Lighthouse.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist; rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/accessibility/aria-allowed-attr
- **Best for:** QA of any custom widget (toggles, tabs, version switchers). Trade fit: applies to the custom 1·2·3 section switchers and interactive widgets on portfolio builds.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0919⟧

## ⟦S0920⟧ aria-command-name — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** Audit rule: elements with command roles (button, link, menuitem) must have an accessible name, from text content, aria-label or aria-labelledby. Priority: medium · Difficulty: intermediate · Time: 10 min. Overlaps ⟦S0926⟧ (names for all interactive elements) at command-role scope.
- **How it looks:** Invisible visually; a screen reader announces "Close dialog, button" instead of a bare "button". The classic failure is an icon-only button (e.g. a trash icon) with no label at all.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Name sources in the examples: visible text, `aria-label` for icon buttons, `aria-labelledby`. No numeric parameters.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist; rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/accessibility/aria-command-name
- **Best for:** Navigation, call/CTA buttons, icon buttons everywhere. Trade fit: the phone/call buttons and icon controls on a trades homepage must pass this.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0920⟧

## ⟦S0921⟧ aria-deprecated-role — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** Audit rule: deprecated or abstract ARIA roles (example given: `directory`) must be replaced with modern roles or native elements. Priority: medium · Difficulty: intermediate · Time: 10 min.
- **How it looks:** Invisible — deprecated roles risk being dropped inconsistently by browsers/AT, so the element's meaning may silently vanish for screen-reader users.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Search the codebase for deprecated role values; replace with the modern equivalent or a native element (`<nav>` instead of `role="navigation"` is the recorded preference). Judged against WAI-ARIA 1.2.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist; rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/accessibility/aria-deprecated-role
- **Best for:** Legacy-markup QA sweeps. Trade fit: minor; a grep-level checklist item on inherited code.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0921⟧

## ⟦S0922⟧ aria-dialog-name — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** Audit rule: every `role="dialog"` / `role="alertdialog"` element must have an accessible name, via aria-labelledby pointing at its heading or an aria-label. Priority: medium · Difficulty: intermediate · Time: 10 min.
- **How it looks:** Invisible visually; when a modal opens, the screen reader immediately announces its title ("Edit Profile", "Session Timeout") so the user knows why focus moved before interacting.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. The sequence it governs: dialog opens → focus shifts into it → its name is announced first, then its contents.
- **Mechanism & key values:** `aria-labelledby="<heading-id>"` preferred, `aria-label` for simple alerts; examples pair the name with `aria-modal="true"`. No numeric parameters.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist; rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/accessibility/aria-dialog-name
- **Best for:** Forms — quote modals, callback dialogs, cookie/consent dialogs. Trade fit: relevant if a build puts the quote form in a modal.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0922⟧

## ⟦S0923⟧ aria-hidden-body — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** Audit rule: `aria-hidden="true"` must never be applied to `<body>` — it removes the entire page from the accessibility tree. Priority: critical · Difficulty: intermediate · Time: 10 min.
- **How it looks:** The page looks completely normal on screen while being entirely non-existent to a screen reader — no headings, links or text are reachable at all. Usually caused by modal code that hides the background by targeting the wrong element.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Correct pattern: aria-hidden goes on the background app container only, with the modal rendered in a sibling portal that stays exposed. Check the body at every lifecycle point (modal open/close), not just initial markup.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist; rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/accessibility/aria-hidden-body
- **Best for:** Modal/dialog implementations anywhere (forms, galleries). Trade fit: a must-check wherever a build uses modals or lightboxes.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0923⟧

## ⟦S0924⟧ aria-hidden-focus — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** Audit rule: `aria-hidden="true"` containers must not contain focusable elements — aria-hidden leaves the tab order untouched, creating silent "ghost focus". Priority: medium · Difficulty: intermediate · Time: 10 min.
- **How it looks:** Invisible until a keyboard user tabs into a hidden region: focus lands on a control the screen reader never announces, so focus appears to have vanished.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. The failure sequence: Tab press → focus enters the aria-hidden subtree → screen reader stays silent → user cannot tell where they are.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Fixes: add `tabindex="-1"` to focusable children inside the hidden container, or apply the `inert` attribute to the container (cleanest modern fix; older browser targets may need the manual tab-order fallback). Companion concern named in the source: focus management generally.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist; rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/accessibility/aria-hidden-focus (rule text cites WAI-ARIA 1.2)
- **Best for:** Off-canvas navigation, hidden panels, carousels, modal backgrounds. Trade fit: mobile menus and gallery carousels on trades builds must be checked for this.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0924⟧

## ⟦S0925⟧ aria-input-field-name — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** Audit rule: every input, textarea and select (and custom textbox/combobox/spinbutton/searchbox/listbox widgets) must have an accessible name; a placeholder is not one. Priority: critical · Difficulty: beginner · Time: 10 min. Maps to WCAG 2.1 SC 1.3.1 and SC 4.1.2.
- **How it looks:** Visually, a form whose fields carry real labels — a visible `<label>` tied to each field, or an aria-label on a standalone search box. Without it, a screen reader announces only "text field" / "edit" with no idea what to type, and voice-control users cannot say "click Email Address" to reach the field.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Accessible-name computation order: 1) `aria-labelledby`, 2) `aria-label`, 3) associated `<label>` (for/id or wrapping), 4) `title` (last resort); placeholder is explicitly not a reliable name. Preferred fix: `<label for>` + matching `id`. Applies to all `<input>` except type=hidden.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist; rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/accessibility/aria-input-field-name
- **Best for:** Forms — the quote/contact form above all. Trade fit: critical; an unlabelled quote form fails the exact users it exists for.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0925⟧

## ⟦S0926⟧ aria-labels — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** Audit rule: all interactive elements (buttons, links, widgets) must have a concise, descriptive accessible name — no unnamed controls, no generic "Click Here" / "More". Priority: high · Difficulty: intermediate · Time: 10 min. The broader sibling of ⟦S0920⟧.
- **How it looks:** Invisible visually; in a screen reader's elements list every control reads as its action or destination ("Download PDF report") instead of mystery-meat entries, and voice-control users can activate controls by speaking their names.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Name via descriptive text content or `aria-label` (icon-button pattern: `<button aria-label="Download PDF report">` around a decorative icon). No numeric parameters.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist; rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/accessibility/aria-labels
- **Best for:** Navigation, call/CTA, footer social icons — every control on the page. Trade fit: universal QA sweep for trades builds.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0926⟧

## ⟦S0927⟧ aria-live-regions — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** Audit rule: dynamic content changes (form errors, cart counts, loading states, results) must be announced through ARIA live regions at the correct politeness level. Priority: high · Difficulty: intermediate · Time: 20 min. The general mechanism behind ⟦S0906⟧.
- **How it looks:** Invisible visually; a screen reader speaks updates without focus moving — "3 items added to cart", "5 results found", or an error the moment it appears.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. The required sequence: an empty live region exists in the DOM first → content is injected into it later → the screen reader announces the change (polite: after current speech finishes; assertive: interrupts immediately). A region created with its content already inside never announces — the recorded anti-pattern.
- **Mechanism & key values:** `aria-live="polite"` for non-urgent updates (cart count, search results), `aria-live="assertive"` only for critical alerts (errors, session expiry), `aria-live="off"` for frequently updating content; `role="status"` implies polite, `role="alert"` implies assertive.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist; rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/accessibility/aria-live-regions
- **Best for:** Forms (validation errors, submit confirmation), search/filter results, any dynamic widget. Trade fit: quote-form feedback and review/filter interactions on trades sites.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0927⟧

## ⟦S0928⟧ aria-meter-name — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** Audit rule: `<meter>` elements and `role="meter"` widgets must have an accessible name saying what is being measured. Priority: medium · Difficulty: intermediate · Time: 10 min.
- **How it looks:** A gauge/bar showing a value (e.g. 45%); with the rule applied, a screen reader announces "CPU Usage, 45%" instead of a context-free "50%".
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Name via `aria-labelledby` pointing at a visible label, or `aria-label` (example: `<meter value="0.6" aria-label="Cloud storage space used">`). Native meter carries min/max/value as usual.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist; rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/accessibility/aria-meter-name
- **Best for:** Stat/proof displays (capacity, ratings, coverage meters). Trade fit: occasional — any gauge-style stat widget in a proof section.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0928⟧

## ⟦S0929⟧ aria-progressbar-name — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** Audit rule: progress bars (`role="progressbar"` / `<progress>`) must have an accessible name describing the process, plus value attributes when the value is known. Priority: medium · Difficulty: intermediate · Time: 10 min.
- **How it looks:** A loading/upload bar; a screen reader hears "Uploading files…, 70%" rather than a bare "progress bar". The label should not redundantly include the word "progress".
- **Frame by frame:** The bar itself fills as the task advances (the widget's own behaviour); the rule governs naming, not the fill animation: name via aria-label/aria-labelledby, with `aria-valuenow` / `aria-valuemin` / `aria-valuemax` supplied when known. Visual progress meters that communicate status should use real progress semantics, not decorative divs.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Example pattern: `role="progressbar" aria-valuenow="70" aria-valuemin="0" aria-valuemax="100" aria-label="Uploading files..."`. No durations prescribed.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist; rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/accessibility/aria-progressbar-name
- **Best for:** Multi-step quote forms (step progress), upload flows, loading states. Trade fit: relevant to a stepped quote form's progress indicator.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0929⟧

## ⟦S0930⟧ aria-required-attr — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** Audit rule: roles that mandate state/property attributes must carry them (a slider without `aria-valuenow` is incomplete). Priority: medium · Difficulty: intermediate · Time: 10 min.
- **How it looks:** Invisible — without the required attributes a screen reader cannot announce the control's current value or bounds, so a slider is focusable but meaningless.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Recorded correct patterns: slider = `role="slider"` + aria-valuenow/valuemin/valuemax + aria-label; scrollbar = `role="scrollbar"` + aria-controls + aria-orientation + aria-valuenow/valuemin/valuemax. Validate the full role set against WAI-ARIA 1.2.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist; rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/accessibility/aria-required-attr
- **Best for:** Custom sliders and widgets — before/after image sliders above all. Trade fit: direct; before/after sliders are a signature trades-homepage component.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0930⟧

## ⟦S0931⟧ aria-required-children — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** Audit rule: composite container roles must own their required child roles, or screen readers cannot enumerate the widget's items. Priority: high · Difficulty: intermediate · Time: 15 min. Inverse of ⟦S0932⟧.
- **How it looks:** Invisible structurally: a tab strip, menu, tree or listbox that a screen reader can actually count and step through ("tab 1 of 3") instead of an opaque div soup where no tabs exist at all.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Required pairs (WAI-ARIA 1.2 required owned elements): tablist→tab; list→listitem; listbox→group/option; menu/menubar→menuitem/menuitemcheckbox/menuitemradio; radiogroup→radio; tree→treeitem; treegrid→row; grid→row/rowgroup; row→cell/gridcell/columnheader/rowheader. Layout wrappers between container and children get `role="none"`/`role="presentation"`. Prefer native `<ul>/<li>`, `<select>/<option>` where possible. Also maps to WCAG 2.1 SC 4.1.2.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist; rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/accessibility/aria-required-children
- **Best for:** Tabs, menus, listboxes in navigation and version switchers. Trade fit: the 1·2·3 section switchers and tabbed service content must pass this if built with ARIA roles.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0931⟧

## ⟦S0932⟧ aria-required-parent — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** Audit rule: child roles that require a specific parent role must actually be contained by one (a `listitem` outside a `list`, a `tab` outside a `tablist`, a `menuitem` outside a `menu`). Priority: medium · Difficulty: intermediate · Time: 10 min. Inverse of ⟦S0931⟧.
- **How it looks:** Invisible — an orphaned child role loses its group announcement, so a screen reader never says "Item 1 of 3" and group navigation breaks down.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Fix = wrap the child in the required container role (or switch to the native element pair). No numeric parameters; judged against WAI-ARIA 1.2.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist; rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/accessibility/aria-required-parent
- **Best for:** QA of tabs, menus, lists built from divs. Trade fit: same surface as ⟦S0931⟧ — custom navigation and switchers.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0932⟧

## ⟦S0933⟧ aria-roles — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** Audit rule: role attribute values must be valid standard ARIA roles — typos like `role="btn"`, `role="check-box"` or invented roles like `role="tooltip-item"` are silently ignored. Priority: medium · Difficulty: intermediate · Time: 10 min.
- **How it looks:** Invisible — an invalid role means the element is exposed to assistive tech with no (or the wrong) meaning; the recorded better fix is often a native element (`<button type="button">`) instead of a corrected custom role.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Validate every role value against the WAI-ARIA 1.2 role list; prefer native HTML controls over custom ARIA widgets whenever possible. No numeric parameters.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist; rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/accessibility/aria-roles
- **Best for:** Whole-codebase QA sweep. Trade fit: grep-level check on any hand-built widgets.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0933⟧

## ⟦S0934⟧ aria-text — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** Audit rule: elements with `role="text"` must not contain focusable descendants — the role flattens its whole subtree into one text string, hiding links/buttons inside it from screen readers. Priority: medium · Difficulty: intermediate · Time: 10 min.
- **How it looks:** A line like "Price: $10.00" reads as a single string (the legitimate use). The failure looks identical on screen: a sentence containing a real link or button that a screen-reader user cannot find or activate, while a keyboard user may still tab to it and hear nothing sensible.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Fix = remove role="text" from any container with interactive children, or move the interactive elements outside it. role="text" is noted as mainly a VoiceOver-specific edge case.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist; rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/accessibility/aria-text
- **Best for:** Copy blocks with inline links/CTAs. Trade fit: minor; check any price/callout line that mixes text spans with a link.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0934⟧

## ⟦S0935⟧ aria-toggle-field-name — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** Audit rule: toggle fields (checkboxes, radio buttons, switches) must have an accessible name describing what they control. Priority: medium · Difficulty: intermediate · Time: 10 min.
- **How it looks:** A checkbox or switch sitting next to its label text; a screen reader announces name + state together ("Subscribe to newsletter, checkbox, checked"; "Enable dark mode" on a `role="switch"` button with aria-checked).
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Name via `<label for>`, `aria-labelledby` (visible label element) or `aria-label`. Switch pattern recorded: `<button role="switch" aria-checked="false" aria-labelledby="switch-label">`. No numeric parameters.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist; rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/accessibility/aria-toggle-field-name
- **Best for:** Forms — consent checkboxes, option toggles in a quote form. Trade fit: the quote form's consent/service toggles must pass.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0935⟧

## ⟦S0936⟧ aria-tooltip-name — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** Audit rule: `role="tooltip"` elements must have an accessible name of their own or be referenced from their trigger via aria-describedby. Priority: medium · Difficulty: intermediate · Time: 10 min. The naming-only slice of the full tooltip pattern in ⟦S0908⟧.
- **How it looks:** Invisible — correct association means the hint text ("Saves your current changes to the cloud") is announced when the trigger is focused; without it the tooltip's information never reaches screen-reader users.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Two valid patterns recorded: trigger carries `aria-describedby="<tooltip-id>"`, or the tooltip carries its own `aria-label`. No numeric parameters.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist; rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/accessibility/aria-tooltip-name
- **Best for:** Any tooltip usage; pairs with ⟦S0908⟧. Trade fit: minor, same surface as S0908.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0936⟧

## ⟦S0937⟧ aria-treeitem-name — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** Audit rule: every `role="treeitem"` in a tree widget must have a non-empty, descriptive accessible name; expandable items must also carry aria-expanded. Priority: medium · Difficulty: intermediate · Time: 10 min.
- **How it looks:** A file-explorer style hierarchy (folders/files, nested nav); as a screen-reader user arrows through it, each stop announces name + state + position — "src, collapsed, level 1, 1 of 3" — instead of a nameless "treeitem, level 2".
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. Navigation it governs: arrow keys move focus item to item, each focus change announcing name, level, set size/position and expanded state.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Name from text content by default; `aria-label` to override/supplement (e.g. "app.css — CSS stylesheet"), `aria-labelledby` to compose from parts. Companion attributes table: aria-expanded (required when the item has children), aria-level, aria-setsize, aria-posinset, aria-selected. Judged against WAI-ARIA 1.2 treeitem role, the APG Tree View pattern and WCAG 2.1 SC 4.1.2.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist; rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/accessibility/aria-treeitem-name
- **Best for:** Tree widgets — file explorers, nested nav, org charts. Trade fit: low for a trades homepage; relevant only to deeply nested service/town navigation.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0937⟧

## ⟦S0938⟧ aria-valid-attr — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** Audit rule: every `aria-*` attribute used must actually exist in the WAI-ARIA specification — misspellings (the classic: `aria-labeledby` for `aria-labelledby`) and invented attributes (`aria-required-type`) are ignored by browsers. Priority: high · Difficulty: beginner · Time: 5 min.
- **How it looks:** Invisible — the markup looks plausible in source while assistive tech receives nothing, e.g. a button whose aria-expanded is spelled wrong never reports its state.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Spell-check attribute names against WAI-ARIA 1.2; also confirm the attribute is valid for the element's role (that half is ⟦S0919⟧) and its value is valid (⟦S0939⟧). Tools named in the source: Axe DevTools, WAVE.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist; rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/accessibility/aria-valid-attr
- **Best for:** Whole-codebase QA sweep; fast win (5-minute rule). Trade fit: grep-level check on all hand-written ARIA.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0938⟧

## ⟦S0939⟧ aria-valid-attr-value — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** Audit rule: ARIA attribute values must match the type the spec expects — `aria-expanded="true"` not "yes", numeric `aria-valuenow` not "half", and ID references (aria-labelledby, aria-owns) must point at elements that exist. Priority: medium · Difficulty: intermediate · Time: 10 min.
- **How it looks:** Invisible — an invalid value is ignored or misread, so a menu reports no state and a label reference silently resolves to nothing.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Value types per attribute: boolean tokens true/false, integers, ID lists. Broken ID reference is an explicit failure case in the examples. No numeric parameters beyond type conformance.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist; rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/accessibility/aria-valid-attr-value
- **Best for:** QA of any stateful widget (menus, sliders, accordions). Trade fit: pairs with ⟦S0910⟧/⟦S0930⟧ on interactive sections.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0939⟧

## ⟦S0940⟧ article — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** Audit rule: article pages must carry valid Article structured data (Schema.org Article / NewsArticle / BlogPosting) in JSON-LD with headline, image, datePublished and author. Priority: high · Difficulty: intermediate · Time: 15 min.
- **How it looks:** Nothing on the page itself changes; the payoff is in search results — the article becomes eligible for rich results, Top Stories treatment and Google Discover, with headline, image and author shown in the snippet.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** JSON-LD block: `"@type": "BlogPosting"` with headline, image array, ISO-8601 datePublished/dateModified, author as Person objects with name + profile url. Schema must truthfully match visible content — irrelevant schema is worse than none.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist; rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/seo/article (judged against Google Search Central documentation)
- **Best for:** Blog/news content pages. Trade fit: applies if a trades build ships advice articles; not a homepage rule.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0940⟧

## ⟦S0941⟧ article-links — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** Audit rule: articles must contain a healthy density of links — internal links to related content plus external links to authoritative sources. Priority: medium · Difficulty: intermediate · Time: 10 min.
- **How it looks:** Body copy with inline links woven through it: citations out to authority sources and links across to the site's own related guides.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** The prescribed fix quantity: add 2–3 internal links to related content and 1–2 external links to authoritative sources, scaled to article length. External example uses `rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"`.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist; rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/seo/article-links
- **Best for:** Blog/article content; internal-linking structure between service and town pages. Trade fit: the internal-link half transfers directly to service ↔ town page linking.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0941⟧

## ⟦S0942⟧ audio-descriptions — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** Audit rule: videos whose visuals carry information (actions, scene changes, on-screen text, expressions) must offer an audio-description track narrating that visual content for blind users. Priority: medium · Difficulty: intermediate · Time: 30 min.
- **How it looks:** A standard video player whose track menu offers an "English Audio Description" option alongside captions; with descriptions on, a voice narrates the visual beats in the gaps between dialogue ("A woman in business attire enters a modern office lobby"). An alternative build offers a version picker: Standard version / Version with audio descriptions.
- **Frame by frame:** Trigger: playback with the descriptions track enabled → at each cue window (WebVTT timestamps, e.g. 00:00:03.000 → 00:00:06.000) the description line is spoken over the visual it matches → dialogue resumes; cues must fit dialogue gaps and never overlap important audio. Talking-head and audio-only content need no descriptions.
- **Mechanism & key values:** `<track kind="descriptions" src="descriptions-en.vtt" srclang="en" label="English Audio Description">` alongside the captions track; extended-description version (with pauses) when gaps are too short; or bake descriptions into the main narration. Description writing rule from the examples: name the subject and action specifically ("Marcus slams his fist on the table in frustration"), never vague ("He reacts").
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist; rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/accessibility/audio-descriptions
- **Best for:** Hero/demo videos, work footage, testimonials on video. Trade fit: relevant if a build embeds project or testimonial video with visual-only information.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0942⟧

## ⟦S0943⟧ author-byline — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** Audit rule: every article must show a clear, visible author byline — name, role/credentials, and a link to the author's bio page. Priority: medium · Difficulty: beginner · Time: 5 min. Visible half of the author E-E-A-T trio with ⟦S0944⟧ and ⟦S0945⟧.
- **How it looks:** In the article header: a 40×40px round author photo, "By Jane Doe" as a link (rel="author") to /authors/jane-doe, and a small second line with role and date ("Lead Performance Engineer • Nov 15, 2023"), laid out as a flex row with 10px gap.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Example markup values copied above (40×40 avatar, border-radius 50%). Judged as an E-E-A-T Expertise/Authoritativeness signal under Google's Quality Rater Guidelines.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist; rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/seo/author-byline
- **Best for:** Blog/article headers. Trade fit: minor for a homepage; useful pattern for an "owner's note" byline in a proof section.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0943⟧

## ⟦S0944⟧ author-expertise — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** Audit rule: each author must have a bio/profile stating their relevant qualifications — experience, certifications, prior work — with links to professional profiles. Priority: medium · Difficulty: intermediate · Time: 10 min.
- **How it looks:** An "About <name>" block (a section with an aria-labelledby heading) holding a short credentialled bio paragraph — years of experience, certifications (example: 15 years, CISSP) — and a small nav of social/professional links (LinkedIn, Twitter).
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** No numeric parameters; emphasis on YMYL topics where credentials matter most. Judged against Google Search Central guidance.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist; rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/seo/author-expertise
- **Best for:** Team/about content and article author pages. Trade fit: the pattern transfers to trades proof — owner credentials, accreditations and years trading presented the same way.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0944⟧

## ⟦S0945⟧ author-info — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** Audit rule: author identity must also exist as structured data — a Person/Organization JSON-LD block linked from the Article/WebPage schema's author property. Priority: medium · Difficulty: intermediate · Time: 15 min. Machine-readable third of the trio with ⟦S0943⟧/⟦S0944⟧.
- **How it looks:** Invisible on the page; search engines use it to connect the author to their other profiles and build entity/Knowledge Graph recognition.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** JSON-LD Person with `name`, `jobTitle`, `url`, `sameAs` array (LinkedIn/Twitter profile URLs) and `worksFor` Organization. The sameAs links are the mechanism that transfers cross-site authority.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist; rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/seo/author-info
- **Best for:** Article/blog builds alongside ⟦S0940⟧. Trade fit: low for a homepage; relevant to any content-led build.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0945⟧

## ⟦S0946⟧ autofocus-avoidance — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** Audit rule: form fields must not use the `autofocus` attribute on pages with content before the form — it teleports screen-reader users mid-page without context. Priority: low · Difficulty: beginner · Time: 10 min.
- **How it looks:** The failure: page loads and focus (and on mobile, the on-screen keyboard) jumps straight to a mid-page email field, skipping the heading and intro the user never heard. Correct state: focus starts at the top of the page.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. Permitted sequence instead: user clicks to open/reveal a form → only then does JS set focus into it (`setTimeout(() => ref.focus(), 0)` after the interaction). On SPA route changes, focus moves to the new page's h1 (`tabIndex={-1}`) so the title is announced.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Exceptions recorded: search-only pages and bare login pages (nothing before the form) may autofocus. Detection snippet: `document.querySelectorAll('[autofocus]')`.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist; rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/accessibility/autofocus-avoidance
- **Best for:** Forms — quote/contact forms mid-page. Trade fit: direct; a trades homepage form sits below a hero, so autofocus must stay off.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0946⟧

## ⟦S0947⟧ autoplay-media — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** Audit rule: media must not autoplay with sound; any autoplaying video must be muted with immediately accessible pause/stop controls. Priority: high · Difficulty: beginner · Time: 10 min. Maps to WCAG 1.4.2 (audio control) and 2.2.2 (pause, stop, hide).
- **How it looks:** A hero background video may loop silently (`autoplay muted loop playsinline`) with a prominent, labelled pause button ("Pause background video") reachable in the first few tab stops; a content video sits still behind its own play control until the user starts it.
- **Frame by frame:** Trigger: page load → muted video (if used) starts playing and loops → user can pause it at once via the keyboard-reachable control → end state under user control. Audio rule: audio playing automatically for more than 3 seconds must have pause/stop/volume controls; moving content generally needs a pause/stop/hide mechanism, and the rule text adds autoplay should stop after 5 seconds or provide a stop mechanism.
- **Mechanism & key values:** WCAG thresholds copied: 1.4.2 — automatic audio > 3 seconds requires controls; custom player pattern keeps play/pause + mute toggles with aria-labels reflecting state ("Pause video" / "Play video").
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist; rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/accessibility/autoplay-media
- **Best for:** Hero background video and any embedded media. Trade fit: direct — hero work-footage loops are common on trades builds and must ship muted with a pause control.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0947⟧

## ⟦S0948⟧ avif-format — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** Audit rule: images should be served in AVIF (with WebP and JPEG fallbacks) for best compression — ~50% smaller than JPEG, ~20% smaller than WebP. Priority: medium · Difficulty: intermediate · Time: 20 min.
- **How it looks:** Identical pictures on screen; the difference is bytes — photo content arrives at roughly half the JPEG weight, so hero and gallery images land faster, especially on mobile connections.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** `<picture>` with AVIF source first, WebP second, JPEG `<img>` fallback; example srcset widths 400/800/1200w, sizes `(max-width: 600px) 100vw, 50vw`. Support table in source: AVIF 93%+ browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Safari 16+, Edge), WebP 97%+, JPEG/PNG 100%. Quality guide: heroes AVIF 50–60 (≈ JPEG 80–85), product photos 60–70, thumbnails 40–50; icons/logos stay SVG/PNG. Sharp settings: avif quality 60, effort 4; Next.js `images.formats: ['image/avif', 'image/webp']`. AVIF encoding is slow — pre-generate at build time. CDN auto-format (Cloudinary f_auto, Imgix auto=format, Cloudflare Polish) is the alternative route.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist; rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/images/avif-format
- **Best for:** Hero imagery and work/gallery photography — the heaviest assets on a page. Trade fit: high; photo-heavy before/after galleries gain the most.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0948⟧

## ⟦S0949⟧ avoid-eval — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** Audit rule: never use `eval()`, `new Function()`, or string-form setTimeout/setInterval — dynamic code execution is a critical XSS vector. Priority: critical · Difficulty: beginner · Time: 10 min. (Indexed as data: this entry records the rule; nothing in it was executed.)
- **How it looks:** Nothing on screen — the failure is invisible until exploited: any user-controlled string reaching eval() executes as code in the visitor's browser (session theft, requests as the user, redirects).
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Safe replacements prescribed: JSON.parse() for data, URLSearchParams for query strings, bracket notation + an allowlist for dynamic property access, an explicit dispatch table for dynamic calls, function references for timers. Enforcement: ESLint `no-eval`, `no-new-func`, `no-implied-eval` all set to error; backstop CSP `script-src 'self'; object-src 'none'` (without 'unsafe-eval', eval and new Function are browser-blocked; CSP alone does not catch every Function-constructor path per the rule text).
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist; rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/javascript/avoid-eval (rule text links MDN eval/Function references and ESLint rules)
- **Best for:** JavaScript security QA on any interactive build. Trade fit: checklist gate for hand-written JS in widgets and forms.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0949⟧

## ⟦S0950⟧ back-forward-cache — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** Audit rule: pages must stay eligible for the browser back/forward cache (bfcache) and restore state correctly when resumed from memory. Priority: high · Difficulty: advanced · Time: 25 min.
- **How it looks:** Pressing Back returns to the previous page instantly, exactly as it was left — no reload flash, no re-render — with only time-sensitive bits (unread counts, session warnings) refreshed.
- **Frame by frame:** Trigger: Back/Forward navigation → if the page is bfcache-eligible, the browser resumes the frozen page from memory → `pageshow` fires with `event.persisted === true` → the page refreshes only stale state and closes transient overlays (drawers, popovers, stale toasts) → end state: page live again without a full reload. An `unload` listener is the most common eligibility blocker.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Use `pagehide` instead of `unload` for teardown (e.g. sendBeacon analytics); `beforeunload` only while the page is dirty, removed as soon as it is clean. Pass conditions from the source: no unconditional unload listeners, restore happens in the target browser, time-sensitive state refreshes on `pageshow.persisted` without forcing reload. Verify with the browser's bfcache diagnostics and Lighthouse unload warnings.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist; rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/performance/back-forward-cache
- **Best for:** Navigation performance on multi-page builds (service/town page sets). Trade fit: matters once a trades site grows beyond one page.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0950⟧

## ⟦S0951⟧ blocked-links — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** Audit rule: links and resources pointing at adblocker-filter-listed tracking domains can be blocked outright — clicks and loads silently fail for users with blockers. Priority: low · Difficulty: intermediate · Time: 15 min.
- **How it looks:** For a visitor with uBlock Origin (20–40% of desktop users, per the source), a link routed through a tracking redirect domain simply does nothing when clicked, and analytics/tag scripts from blocked domains never load, skewing measurement.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Blocked-domain table from the source: googletagmanager.com, google-analytics.com, analytics.google.com, hotjar.com, doubleclick.net, facebook.net / connect.facebook.net, heap.io, fullstory.com — blocked by EasyList/EasyPrivacy-style filters (`||domain^` rules). Fixes: use direct destination URLs with UTM parameters instead of tracking redirects; self-host or proxy critical scripts (recorded Nginx pattern: `/gtm/` proxied to googletagmanager.com); or move analytics server-side / to privacy tools (Plausible, Fathom, Umami). The rule's limit: work around blocking only for first-party analytics, not advertising pixels.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist; rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/security/blocked-links (rule text links EasyList and uBlock Origin filter syntax)
- **Best for:** Analytics/tag setup and outbound-link hygiene. Trade fit: minor but real — tracking on preview/landing pages should use direct links.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0951⟧

## ⟦S0952⟧ breadcrumb — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** Audit rule: pages with a visible breadcrumb trail must carry matching BreadcrumbList structured data (JSON-LD). Priority: medium · Difficulty: intermediate · Time: 10 min. The structured-data half of breadcrumbs; the visible-markup half is ⟦S0953⟧.
- **How it looks:** Nothing changes on the page; in search results the raw URL under the title is replaced by the readable path (Blog › SEO Tips), improving click-through.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** JSON-LD BreadcrumbList with itemListElement of ListItem entries (position, name, item URL) mirroring the visible trail exactly. Guardrails from the source: never emit a one-item BreadcrumbList on flat/landing/hub pages; "Home" goes in the schema only if it also appears in the visible trail.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist; rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/seo/breadcrumb
- **Best for:** Inner pages of multi-page builds (service and town pages). Trade fit: applies to town/service sub-pages, not the homepage.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0952⟧

## ⟦S0953⟧ breadcrumb-navigation — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** Audit rule: breadcrumb navigation must use accessible semantic markup — `<nav aria-label="Breadcrumb">`, an ordered list, and `aria-current="page"` on the current page, which is plain text, not a link. Priority: medium · Difficulty: beginner · Time: 15 min. Complement of ⟦S0952⟧ (which covers the schema for the same trail).
- **How it looks:** A small horizontal trail near the top of the page — linked ancestors separated by "/" (0.875rem text, links `#0066cc`, current page in muted `#666` at weight 500, separators in `#999` rendered by CSS so screen readers skip them). Focus ring on links: `2px solid #0066cc`, offset 2px. On small screens (≤640px) the middle items collapse away, leaving first, an ellipsis, and last.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. Screen-reader sequence: the nav is announced as "Breadcrumb navigation", the list reads in order, and the final item is announced as the current page.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Separators via CSS `::before` content or aria-hidden spans — never announced. Any BreadcrumbList JSON-LD must match the visible items in order and labels (see ⟦S0952⟧); no one-item schema on hub pages. Verify with screen reader, keyboard focus pass and the Rich Results Test.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist; rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/html/breadcrumb-navigation
- **Best for:** Navigation on inner pages (service, town, article). Trade fit: town/service sub-page navigation pattern.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0953⟧
# Skills S0954–S0996 — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills

All 43 entries in this chunk are single checkable rules from the Front-End Checklist
(thedaviddias/front-end-checklist), each shipped as a short audit skill: a "when to use"
trigger, a Check / Fix / Explain / Code Review prompt set, and a bundled `rule.md`
reference with the rule's priority, difficulty, time estimate, code examples and
verification steps. None of them is a design or motion reference — they produce no
layout, artwork or animation of their own; they are a final-QA sweep for finished
pages. "How it looks" below therefore describes what the visitor experiences when the
rule is satisfied, and "Frame by frame" is "Static — no motion" except where the rule
itself governs moving content (carousel, @property). No two skills in this range are
the same underlying skill; the close clusters (canonical S0961/S0962/S0963, broken
links S0954/S0957, consent S0974/S0984, cleanup S0969/S0976, CSS delivery
S0992/S0994/S0996) are distinct rules and cross-reference each other in their entries.

## ⟦S0954⟧ broken-external-links — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** An SEO audit rule: find outbound (external) links that return 4xx/5xx errors and update them to the live URL or remove them.
- **How it looks:** Nothing on the page itself changes visually. A visitor who clicks a reference or resource link in the copy lands on a working page instead of a "Page Not Found" error — and never on an expired domain that a third party has since bought and repurposed.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Regularly scan rendered pages for external links returning 4xx/5xx; fix to the correct URL or delete the link. Rule metadata: Priority medium · Difficulty intermediate · Time 10 min. Judged on the rendered HTML and HTTP responses, not source files; check against Google Search Central (Search Essentials).
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist (thedaviddias/front-end-checklist); rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/seo/broken-external-links
- **Best for:** Final QA sweep on any section carrying outbound links (proof/reviews citations, manufacturer links in work/gallery copy). Applies to every trade homepage.
- **Tier:** STRONG — the checklist's own maintenance rule for link integrity; priority medium in the source.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0954⟧
