## ⟦S0955⟧ broken-html — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** An SEO/markup audit rule: fix malformed HTML — unclosed tags, wrong nesting, stray or unescaped characters — so the document is well-formed HTML5.
- **How it looks:** The page renders the same in every browser instead of each browser's error-recovery guessing differently; headings, paragraphs and spans nest the way the layout intends, and screen readers and crawlers read the intended hierarchy.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Validate the document structure: all tags properly closed and nested per the HTML5 specification, logical head/body hierarchy. Priority medium · Difficulty intermediate · Time 10 min. Verify in rendered HTML/HTTP response and re-crawl after fixing.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist (thedaviddias/front-end-checklist); rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/seo/broken-html
- **Best for:** Final QA sweep on the whole built page — a precondition for every section behaving the same in Chrome, Safari and Firefox. Every trade.
- **Tier:** STRONG — foundational validity rule; priority medium in the source.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0955⟧

## ⟦S0956⟧ broken-images — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** An images audit rule: no image on the page may 404 or show the browser's broken-image icon — validate paths at build time and give runtime images a fallback.
- **How it looks:** Every photo slot shows a real photo or a deliberate placeholder image — never the torn-picture icon, an empty collapsed box, or a hero area with a hole in it. CSS background heroes sit on a fallback background colour while/if the image loads.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. (On an image error, the `onerror` handler swaps the `src` to the fallback image once, instantly.)
- **Mechanism & key values:** Build-time CI script checks every local `<img src>` against the output folder and fails the build on a miss; runtime fallback `onerror="this.src='/images/fallback.png'; this.onerror=null;"` — setting `this.onerror=null` is mandatory to prevent an infinite error loop if the fallback also fails. Detect broken images in-page via `img.complete === false || img.naturalWidth === 0`. Priority high · Difficulty beginner · Time 15 min. A broken Largest Contentful Paint image also directly harms LCP.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist (thedaviddias/front-end-checklist); rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/images/broken-images
- **Best for:** Hero, work/gallery and before/after sections — anywhere real job photography carries the page. Critical for trade homepages, which are photo-led.
- **Tier:** STRONG — priority high in the source; a visible defect class, not a nicety.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0956⟧

## ⟦S0957⟧ broken-links — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** An SEO audit rule: resolve internal broken links — links within the site that return 404 or 5xx. The internal counterpart of ⟦S0954⟧ (external links).
- **How it looks:** Every nav item, inline link and button on the page leads to a live page on the same site; no visitor or crawler ever hits a dead end from the site's own menus.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Audit after any content move/deletion; update the link to the correct URL or remove it. Broken internal links waste crawl budget and leak link equity. Priority high · Difficulty beginner · Time 10 min.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist (thedaviddias/front-end-checklist); rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/seo/broken-links
- **Best for:** Navigation, footer and towns/areas link blocks — any section whose job is moving the visitor. Every trade.
- **Tier:** STRONG — priority high in the source.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0957⟧

## ⟦S0958⟧ browser-caching — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** A performance rule: configure Cache-Control and ETag headers per resource type so repeat visits load assets from the browser cache instead of the network.
- **How it looks:** The page looks identical — but on a second visit it appears almost instantly, because the CSS, JS, fonts and images come from disk/memory cache (DevTools shows "(disk cache)") instead of being re-downloaded.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Hashed CSS/JS and fonts: `public, max-age=31536000, immutable` (1 year). Images: `public, max-age=2592000` (30 days) with `stale-while-revalidate=86400`. HTML: `public, max-age=0, must-revalidate`. API responses: `private, max-age=0, no-store`. ETags answer revalidation with a body-less 304. Priority high · Difficulty intermediate · Time 20 min.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist (thedaviddias/front-end-checklist); rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/performance/browser-caching ; standards: web.dev Learn Performance, Chrome Lighthouse docs.
- **Best for:** Whole-page delivery layer under every section; matters most on image-heavy trade homepages revisited from an email link. Pairs with ⟦S0966⟧ (CDN) and ⟦S0973⟧ (compression).
- **Tier:** STRONG — priority high in the source.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0958⟧

## ⟦S0959⟧ browser-required — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** A performance-process rule: performance audits must run in a real browser engine (Lighthouse, Puppeteer/Playwright, WebPageTest), not by static code analysis alone.
- **How it looks:** No visitor-facing output — it governs how the builder measures the page. Its product is lab numbers (LCP, CLS, INP) and filmstrip screenshots of the page loading under throttling.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Only a rendering engine can execute JS, run layout and calculate Core Web Vitals. Example throttling profile in the source: Fast 3G — 100 ms latency, 750 Kbps down / 250 Kbps up via CDP `Network.emulateNetworkConditions`. Automate in CI on every pull request; audit mobile-first and from multiple regions. Priority medium · Difficulty intermediate · Time 10 min.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist (thedaviddias/front-end-checklist); rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/performance/browser-required ; tools named: Lighthouse, WebPageTest, PageSpeed Insights, Playwright.
- **Best for:** The QA stage of any build — the measurement discipline behind the performance rules in this chunk. Not a page ingredient.
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL — a workflow rule, valuable when auditing, invisible in the deliverable.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0959⟧

## ⟦S0960⟧ button-name — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** An accessibility rule: every `<button>` must have a discernible, descriptive accessible name — visible text, `aria-label`, or `aria-labelledby` — and buttons must do actions while links do navigation.
- **How it looks:** Visually the buttons are unchanged (icon-only buttons still show just the icon); a screen-reader user focusing one hears "Close modal" or "Subscribe to Newsletter" instead of a bare "button".
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Name via text content first, then `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`; never leave an icon-only button unlabelled; don't put the word "Button" in the label (the role is already announced). `<button>` for submit/open/close/save/delete/toggle; `<a href>` when moving to another URL. Priority critical · Difficulty beginner · Time 5 min. Verify in the accessibility tree / with axe, WAVE, keyboard-only pass.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist (thedaviddias/front-end-checklist); rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/accessibility/button-name ; standards: W3C WAI WCAG, MDN Accessibility.
- **Best for:** Call/CTA buttons, carousel and gallery controls, form submits — every interactive element on a trade homepage.
- **Tier:** STRONG — the source's only critical-priority rule in this range; applies everywhere.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0960⟧

## ⟦S0961⟧ canonical-chain — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** An SEO rule: the URL inside a `rel="canonical"` tag must itself return 200 OK — never point a canonical at a URL that then redirects. One of the three canonical rules (see also ⟦S0962⟧, ⟦S0963⟧).
- **How it looks:** No visitor-facing change; search engines index exactly the intended final version of the page and consolidate its ranking signals there.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Canonical target = the final, non-redirecting destination URL (the source's example: canonical to page-a which 301s to page-b is wrong; canonical directly to page-b is right). Priority medium · Difficulty intermediate · Time 10 min.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist (thedaviddias/front-end-checklist); rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/seo/canonical-chain
- **Best for:** Head/metadata QA on multi-page sites (towns/areas and service pages with moved URLs). Minor on a single homepage.
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL — matters when URLs have moved or multiplied; priority medium in the source.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0961⟧

## ⟦S0962⟧ canonical-header — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** An SEO rule: if a canonical is declared both in the HTML `<link rel="canonical">` and in the HTTP `Link` response header, the two must name the exact same URL.
- **How it looks:** No visitor-facing change; crawlers receive one consistent canonical signal instead of two conflicting ones they may ignore entirely.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Compare the HTML tag against the header (`Link: <https://example.com/target-page>; rel="canonical"`) and align them character-for-character. Priority medium · Difficulty intermediate · Time 10 min.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist (thedaviddias/front-end-checklist); rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/seo/canonical-header
- **Best for:** Head/metadata QA where a server or CDN also emits Link headers (PDFs and non-HTML assets especially). Companion to ⟦S0963⟧.
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL — only bites when both declaration methods are in play.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0962⟧

## ⟦S0963⟧ canonical-url — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** An SEO rule: every page carries a canonical URL tag naming the preferred version, consolidating duplicates created by parameters, www/non-www, protocol and pagination.
- **How it looks:** No visitor-facing change; the indexed, ranking version of each page is the clean preferred URL rather than a parameterised twin.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Absolute URL with protocol and domain, HTTPS, no tracking parameters; self-referencing canonicals on every page are best practice; for paginated content include `?page=N` for N > 1 and strip other query params. Use a canonical when the same content must stay reachable at several URLs; use a 301 instead for permanent moves, domain migrations and HTTP→HTTPS. Priority high · Difficulty beginner · Time 10 min.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist (thedaviddias/front-end-checklist); rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/seo/canonical-url ; Google canonicalization guidance.
- **Best for:** Head/metadata QA on every page of a multi-page trade site (service and town pages with filter/sort parameters). Companion to ⟦S0961⟧ and ⟦S0962⟧.
- **Tier:** STRONG — priority high in the source; standard on any indexable page set.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0963⟧

## ⟦S0964⟧ carousel-accessibility — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** An accessibility rule for carousels/sliders: auto-rotating content must have pause/stop controls, full keyboard navigation, screen-reader slide announcements, and must respect prefers-reduced-motion (WCAG 2.2.2).
- **How it looks:** A slideshow with visible previous/next buttons, a pause button, and dot indicators; one slide visible at a time, inactive slides hidden. A keyboard user can tab to the controls and step through slides; a screen reader hears "slide, 1 of 3".
- **Frame by frame:** Trigger: autoplay timer (the source's React example uses a 5000 ms interval) → the active slide swaps to the next and the indicators update. Hover or focus anywhere on the carousel → auto-advance pauses. Pause button (aria-pressed) → rotation stops and the aria-live region switches on to announce changes. Arrow keys step slides; Home/End jump to first/last. If the OS requests reduced motion → autoplay never starts.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Markup contract: `aria-roledescription="carousel"` + aria-label on the region; each slide `role="group"`, `aria-roledescription="slide"`, `aria-label="N of M"`; live region `aria-live="polite"` while paused, `"off"` while playing; indicators as a tablist with aria-selected. Focus-visible outline in the source CSS: 2px solid #0066cc, 2px offset; indicator dots 12px. Priority medium · Difficulty advanced · Time 30 min. The source itself warns autoplay carousels have low engagement — question using one at all.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist (thedaviddias/front-end-checklist); rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/html/carousel-accessibility ; WCAG 2.2.2.
- **Best for:** Any gallery/testimonial slider on a trade homepage (work/gallery, proof/reviews) — the compliance contract for the one moving component most likely to ship.
- **Tier:** STRONG — mandatory whenever a carousel is used; the rule also argues for restraint.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0964⟧

## ⟦S0965⟧ cascade-layers — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** A CSS architecture rule: declare an explicit `@layer` stack so cascade order is decided by layer order, not selector specificity — ending !important wars.
- **How it looks:** No direct visitor-facing output; it is the ordering system underneath the page's styles, so component and utility styles combine predictably instead of overriding each other by accident.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Declare the stack first: `@layer reset, base, components, utilities;` — later layers beat earlier ones regardless of specificity; unlayered styles sit above all layers (useful for gradual migration). Import third-party CSS into a low `vendor` layer so site styles always win. Layers can nest (components.forms, components.cards). Browser support: Chrome 99+, Firefox 97+, Safari 15.4+; Tailwind v3.3+ maps its base/components/utilities onto layers. Priority low · Difficulty intermediate · Time 30 min.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist (thedaviddias/front-end-checklist); rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/css/cascade-layers ; MDN @layer, web.dev cascade-layers guide.
- **Best for:** The stylesheet architecture of a single-file trade homepage — keeps hero-to-footer styles from fighting as sections are assembled from different references.
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL — pays off on large hand-assembled stylesheets; the source rates it low priority.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0965⟧

## ⟦S0966⟧ cdn — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** A performance rule: serve static assets through a content delivery network so users download from an edge server near them.
- **How it looks:** The same page, arriving measurably sooner for visitors far from the origin — the source puts the latency cut at 50–70% for distant users; response headers show CDN markers (cf-ray on Cloudflare, x-amz-cf-id on CloudFront).
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** CDN in front of the origin with per-type cache headers (hashed assets `max-age=31536000, immutable`; an example Cloudflare page rule sets Edge TTL 1 month on /static/*). Providers named: Cloudflare, Vercel, AWS CloudFront, Fastly, Akamai. Side benefits: traffic-spike absorption, DDoS protection, TLS offloading. Priority high · Difficulty intermediate · Time 30 min.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist (thedaviddias/front-end-checklist); rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/performance/cdn
- **Best for:** Delivery layer for the whole page, especially photo-heavy heroes and galleries served to a national audience. Pairs with ⟦S0958⟧ (caching) and ⟦S0973⟧ (compression).
- **Tier:** STRONG — priority high in the source; near-free speed for static preview/portfolio pages.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0966⟧

## ⟦S0967⟧ charset — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** An HTML rule: declare `<meta charset="UTF-8">` as the first element in `<head>` so every character renders as intended.
- **How it looks:** Text renders cleanly in every language and symbol — Café, 北京, العربية, £ and ★ appear as themselves instead of mojibake (garbled character sequences).
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** The declaration must appear within the first 1024 bytes of the document; UTF-8 covers all Unicode. Use the short `<meta charset="UTF-8">` form, not the old http-equiv Content-Type form. Next.js emits UTF-8 automatically — verify the rendered HTML rather than duplicating the tag. Priority critical · Difficulty beginner · Time 5 min.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist (thedaviddias/front-end-checklist); rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/html/charset ; MDN HTML, WHATWG HTML Living Standard, W3C Markup Validator.
- **Best for:** Every page, unconditionally — a one-line precondition in the head of any trade homepage (review stars, £/$ symbols and accented names all depend on it).
- **Tier:** STRONG — priority critical in the source; zero-cost, always applies.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0967⟧

## ⟦S0968⟧ citations — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** An SEO/trust rule: back factual claims in the copy with links to authoritative external sources (.gov, .edu, official bodies, industry leaders) using descriptive anchor text.
- **How it looks:** Statements about statistics, regulations or research in the copy carry links on the telling words (e.g. "World Health Organization" linking to who.int), so a reader can verify the claim in one click.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Cite claims where they are made, keep citations highly relevant, and let the link "neighbourhood" signal the page's topic. Feeds the Trustworthiness pillar of Google's E-E-A-T. Priority medium · Difficulty beginner · Time 10 min.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist (thedaviddias/front-end-checklist); rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/seo/citations
- **Best for:** Proof/reviews and process copy that quotes figures (failure rates, warranty terms, safety standards) on trade homepages.
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL — valuable where copy makes checkable claims; priority medium in the source.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0968⟧

## ⟦S0969⟧ clean-up-comments — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** A production-hygiene rule: strip development comments, debug markup, console calls and dead code from shipped HTML/JS/CSS — while keeping accessibility and legal comments.
- **How it looks:** The shipped page is byte-for-byte the same visually; view-source shows no TODO/FIXME/DEBUG notes, no debug panels or red test boxes, no commented-out old layouts, and no leaked endpoints or credentials in comments.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Automate in the build: Terser `drop_console: true`, `drop_debugger: true`, `output.comments: false`; Vite terserOptions the same; PostCSS postcss-discard-comments + cssnano. Pre-deploy scripts delete *.debug.js/test files and dev env files. Overlaps ⟦S0976⟧ on console statements — this rule is the wider one (comments, markup, endpoints, secrets). Priority medium · Difficulty beginner · Time 10 min.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist (thedaviddias/front-end-checklist); rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/html/clean-up-comments ; MDN HTML, WHATWG HTML Living Standard.
- **Best for:** Final pre-ship sweep of the single-file homepage before it goes to the client. Every trade.
- **Tier:** STRONG — cheap insurance against leaking internals; priority medium in the source.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0969⟧

## ⟦S0970⟧ code-splitting — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** A JavaScript performance rule: split large bundles with dynamic `import()` and route boundaries so the browser only downloads and parses the code the current view needs.
- **How it looks:** The first screen becomes interactive quickly instead of sitting painted-but-frozen; heavy features (PDF export, chart panels, rich editors, maps) appear after a brief loading state only when the visitor actually triggers them.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. (Deferred chunks load on route change, interaction, or hover-prefetch, behind a Suspense/loading fallback.)
- **Mechanism & key values:** The source's anchor number: a 500 KB JS bundle blocks interactivity for 3–5 seconds on a mid-range mobile even after download, because parse/compile follows transfer. Route-based splitting via React.lazy/`import()`; hover-triggered `webpackPrefetch` for likely next pages; conditional loading (analytics production-only, polyfills feature-detected). Suggested budget in the source: initial route bundle ≤ 150 KB gzipped; verify with Webpack Bundle Analyzer / vite-bundle-visualizer / Bundlephobia. Priority high · Difficulty intermediate · Time 25 min.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist (thedaviddias/front-end-checklist); rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/javascript/code-splitting ; web.dev dynamic-imports guide.
- **Best for:** Multi-page builds and any homepage carrying heavy interactive sections (configurators, 3D, maps). Less relevant to a lean single-file page, where the same thinking becomes "don't ship the library until the section needs it".
- **Tier:** STRONG — priority high in the source; the main lever on Time to Interactive.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0970⟧

## ⟦S0971⟧ color-contrast — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** An accessibility rule (WCAG 2.1 SC 1.4.3 / 1.4.11, Level AA): text and essential UI must meet minimum contrast ratios against their backgrounds, in every interactive state.
- **How it looks:** Body copy, captions, button labels, input borders, icons and focus indicators stay legible at a glance — including in bright sunlight and for low-vision or colour-blind visitors; no pale-grey-on-white placeholder-style text carrying real content.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** AA minimums: 4.5:1 for normal text (< 18pt, or < 14pt bold); 3:1 for large text (≥ 18pt/24px, or ≥ 14pt bold ≈ 18.67px); 3:1 for non-text UI (icons, input borders, focus indicators). AAA: 7:1 / 4.5:1. Ratio = (L1 + 0.05) / (L2 + 0.05) from relative luminance; range 1:1 to 21:1. Source benchmarks: #595959 on white passes 4.5:1; #767676 on white is 3:1 (large text only); #cccccc on white ≈ 1.6:1 fails. Never fake it with opacity — check the blended colour. Check default, hover, focus, active, visited and disabled states. Priority high · Difficulty intermediate · Time 15 min. Tools named: WebAIM Contrast Checker, TPGi Colour Contrast Analyser, WhoCanUse.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist (thedaviddias/front-end-checklist); rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/accessibility/color-contrast ; WCAG 2.1 SC 1.4.3 and 1.4.11.
- **Best for:** Every text-bearing section — hero headline over photography is the classic failure on trade homepages; also call/CTA buttons and form fields.
- **Tier:** STRONG — priority high in the source and a legal-baseline requirement (ADA / EN 301 549).
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0971⟧

## ⟦S0972⟧ color-oklch — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** A CSS colour-system rule: define palette tokens in `oklch()`/`oklab()` instead of hsl/hex, so equal numeric lightness steps look equally bright across every hue.
- **How it looks:** Colour ramps where step 300, 500 and 700 sit at the same perceived brightness whether the hue is blue, green or orange — no yellow step glowing brighter than its blue neighbour; hover and active states step down evenly; dark mode is the same palette with only the lightness axis moved.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** `oklch(L C H)`: L 0–1, C 0–0.4+, H 0–360°. The source's worked 11-step ramp uses lightness 0.97, 0.93, 0.86, 0.76, 0.65, 0.55 (base 500), 0.46, 0.38, 0.30, 0.22, 0.15. Wide gamut: serve richer chroma (e.g. C 0.20 → 0.28) inside `@media (color-gamut: p3)`; out-of-gamut values clamp gracefully on sRGB. Support: Chrome 111+, Firefox 113+, Safari 15.4+ (hsl fallback or postcss-oklab-function for older). Tailwind v4's default palette is oklch. Note: oklch L is not WCAG luminance — still verify ratios per ⟦S0971⟧. Priority low · Difficulty intermediate · Time 20 min.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist (thedaviddias/front-end-checklist); rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/css/color-oklch ; MDN oklch(), oklch.com picker; colour model by Björn Ottosson.
- **Best for:** The token layer of any trade brand system — even shade steps for buttons, badges, proof bands and dark sections.
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL — a quality upgrade for palette construction; the source rates it low priority.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0972⟧

## ⟦S0973⟧ compression — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** A performance rule: serve all text resources (HTML, CSS, JS, SVG, JSON, XML) with Gzip or Brotli compression.
- **How it looks:** The identical page, delivered in a fraction of the bytes — the source cites ~70%+ typical reduction on text assets, and Brotli files 15–20% smaller than Gzip — so first paint lands sooner, especially on mobile networks.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Nginx: `gzip on` with `gzip_min_length 1000`; Brotli via module. Don't compress files under ~1 KB (overhead wins) and never re-compress binary formats (JPG/PNG/video). Pre-compress static assets at build time instead of paying CPU/TTFB on the fly. Compression cuts transfer only — parse/execute cost remains, so pair with ⟦S0970⟧. Priority high · Difficulty beginner · Time 10 min.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist (thedaviddias/front-end-checklist); rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/performance/compression ; web.dev Learn Performance.
- **Best for:** Server/CDN configuration under every page; non-negotiable for single-file homepages whose whole weight travels in one HTML response.
- **Tier:** STRONG — priority high in the source; near-free, universal.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0973⟧

## ⟦S0974⟧ consent-mode — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** A privacy/analytics rule: implement Google Consent Mode v2 so Google tags adjust their behaviour to the visitor's consent state, with conversion modelling filling the gaps for non-consenting users. Companion to ⟦S0984⟧ (the consent banner itself). Note: the checklist files it under its performance category and its "when to use" wrapper carries performance boilerplate — the substance, indexed here from the rule body, is privacy/measurement.
- **How it looks:** No visual element of its own — the visitor sees the consent banner (see ⟦S0984⟧); behind it, analytics and ads pings carry consent parameters (`gcd`, `gcs`) and fire or hold according to the choice made.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Set defaults before any GTM/gtag script, high in `<head>`: `gtag('consent','default',{ad_storage:'denied', ad_user_data:'denied', ad_personalization:'denied', analytics_storage:'denied', wait_for_update:500})` — `ad_user_data` and `ad_personalization` are the v2 additions. On acceptance, send a matching `consent update` immediately. Never hardcode 'granted' in regulated regions; use a Google-certified CMP; verify with Tag Assistant. Required for EEA advertising under the Digital Markets Act. Priority high · Difficulty intermediate · Time 10 min.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist (thedaviddias/front-end-checklist); rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/performance/consent-mode ; Google Tag Assistant.
- **Best for:** Any tracked trade page running GA/Ads tags for a UK/EU audience — i.e. the measurement layer under the whole homepage.
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL — essential when Google tags run in the EEA; irrelevant on an untracked static preview.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0974⟧

## ⟦S0975⟧ consistent-help — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** An accessibility rule (WCAG 2.2 SC 3.2.6 Consistent Help): when the same help mechanisms repeat across pages in a flow, they must appear in the same relative order and location on each page.
- **How it looks:** The Help link, chat trigger, phone number and contact link sit in the same spot — e.g. the header utility area — on step 1, step 2 and step 3 of a journey, so a stuck visitor finds them where they learned to look.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Audit the mechanism set as a group (chat, phone, FAQ/help centre, contact form) and compare DOM order and placement across pages at the same breakpoint and zoom. A page with no help mechanism does not fail; responsive rearrangement is fine if relative order survives within the breakpoint. Priority medium · Difficulty beginner · Time 15 min.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist (thedaviddias/front-end-checklist); rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/accessibility/consistent-help ; WCAG 2.2 SC 3.2.6.
- **Best for:** Multi-step quote/estimate forms and multi-page trade sites where the call/CTA and help links repeat in the header or footer of every page.
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL — only applies where help repeats across a flow; priority medium in the source.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0975⟧

## ⟦S0976⟧ console-cleanup — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** A JavaScript hygiene rule: remove console statements (log, debug, info, table, time, trace, group) from production code, or route them through an environment-aware logger. The JS-focused half of ⟦S0969⟧.
- **How it looks:** Nothing visual — the visitor's browser console stays clean instead of printing debug dumps of user data, API responses and feature flags.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** `console.error` (error tracking) and sparing `console.warn` may stay; everything else goes. Enforce with ESLint `'no-console': 'error'` in production (Biome: noConsoleLog), strip automatically with Terser `drop_console: true` (webpack) or Vite terserOptions `drop_console` + `drop_debugger`. Priority medium · Difficulty beginner · Time 10 min.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist (thedaviddias/front-end-checklist); rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/javascript/console-cleanup ; MDN JavaScript Guide, web.dev Learn JavaScript.
- **Best for:** Pre-ship sweep of the homepage's inline scripts (slider, cursor, form logic) before delivery. Every trade.
- **Tier:** STRONG — trivial cost, prevents leaking data into every visitor's console.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0976⟧

## ⟦S0977⟧ const-let — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** A JavaScript correctness rule: never declare with `var` — use `const` by default and `let` only when the binding is reassigned.
- **How it looks:** No visitor-facing output; it prevents a class of silent behaviour bugs (loop variables, hoisted names) that would otherwise surface as wrong values in interactive sections.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** The source's canonical bug: `for (var i…)` with setTimeout logs 3, 3, 3 (one shared function-scoped binding); `let` logs 0, 1, 2 (block scope). `var` hoists as undefined; `let`/`const` throw a ReferenceError in the temporal dead zone. `const` freezes the binding, not the value — object mutation still works; use Object.freeze for true immutability. Enforce with ESLint `no-var: error` + `prefer-const: error`. Priority high · Difficulty beginner · Time 10 min.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist (thedaviddias/front-end-checklist); rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/javascript/const-let
- **Best for:** All inline JavaScript in a single-file build (counters, sliders, switchers) — the cheapest bug-prevention rule in the set.
- **Tier:** STRONG — priority high in the source; zero trade-offs.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0977⟧

## ⟦S0978⟧ contact-page — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** An SEO/trust rule: the site needs a dedicated, easy-to-find Contact page offering several working ways to reach a real business.
- **How it looks:** A /contact page with an Email section (mailto link), an Office section with a postal address in an `<address>` block, and typically a phone number and form; a "Contact Us" link sits in the footer of every page.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Multiple contact methods (email, phone, form), physical address/map where applicable (name-address-phone consistency feeds local SEO), discoverable from any page. Feeds the Trust pillar of E-E-A-T. Priority medium · Difficulty beginner · Time 5 min.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist (thedaviddias/front-end-checklist); rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/seo/contact-page
- **Best for:** The call/CTA destination of a trade site — the page the homepage's phone buttons and quote CTAs ultimately point at; local firms gain local-search value from the address block.
- **Tier:** STRONG — a basic legitimacy signal every trade site should pass; priority medium in the source.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0978⟧

## ⟦S0979⟧ container-queries — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** A CSS responsiveness rule: make components respond to their container's width with container queries instead of the viewport width with media queries, so the same component works in a sidebar, a grid or full width.
- **How it looks:** A card that stacks image-over-text when narrow and flips to a side-by-side layout when its container widens — the same card component visibly re-flowing correctly in a narrow sidebar column and in a wide content grid on the same page.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. (Layout switches discretely at the container breakpoints as the container resizes.)
- **Mechanism & key values:** Parent opts in: `container-type: inline-size` (or shorthand `container: card / inline-size`). Children query it: `@container (min-width: 400px)`; the source's worked card goes side-by-side at 480px (200px image column, square image) and richer at 720px (320px column). Named containers (`@container sidebar (max-width: 300px)`) target a specific ancestor. Size-relative units: cqi/cqb (1% of container inline/block size). Baseline support in the source: Chrome 115, Edge 115, Firefox 116, Safari 16.4.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist (thedaviddias/front-end-checklist); rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/css/container-queries
- **Best for:** Work/gallery cards, review cards and town tiles on trade homepages — components reused across hero, grid and sidebar contexts.
- **Tier:** STRONG — the modern default for component responsiveness; priority medium in the source.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0979⟧

## ⟦S0980⟧ content-dates — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** An SEO rule: article/blog pages show a visible published date and carry machine-readable published/updated dates in structured data and meta tags.
- **How it looks:** A byline under the headline reading "Published March 15, 2024 · Updated November 20, 2024", and that same date appearing next to the result in Google search snippets.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Three layers: visible `<time datetime="2024-03-15">`; Article/BlogPosting JSON-LD with `datePublished` and `dateModified` in ISO 8601 (`2024-03-15T10:00:00Z`); Open Graph `article:published_time` / `article:modified_time`. Update `dateModified` only on substantive edits, never on trivial changes or every deploy. Priority medium · Difficulty intermediate · Time 10 min. Validate with Google's Rich Results Test.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist (thedaviddias/front-end-checklist); rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/seo/content-dates ; Google Article structured-data guidance, schema.org dateModified.
- **Best for:** News/advice articles and case-study pages attached to a trade site — anywhere freshness is a ranking and trust factor.
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL — homepages rarely carry dates; essential on article templates.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0980⟧

## ⟦S0981⟧ content-security-policy — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** A security rule: send a strict Content-Security-Policy header controlling which origins may load scripts, styles, images and frames — the primary defence-in-depth against XSS, clickjacking and data injection — and sanitize untrusted HTML before it reaches the DOM.
- **How it looks:** Nothing visible on a healthy page; the protection shows only in what cannot happen — injected third-party scripts and framed copies of the page are refused by the browser.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Roll out Report-Only first and monitor reports at least a week before enforcing. Strict target header (source example): `default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'nonce-{random}' 'strict-dynamic'; style-src 'self' 'nonce-{random}'; img-src 'self' data: https:; font-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'`. Never `unsafe-inline`/`unsafe-eval` for scripts — use per-request nonces or sha256 hashes. Sanitize rich HTML with DOMPurify before `innerHTML`/`dangerouslySetInnerHTML`; large apps add Trusted Types (`require-trusted-types-for 'script'`). Companion headers in the source set: X-Content-Type-Options nosniff, X-Frame-Options DENY, Referrer-Policy strict-origin-when-cross-origin, HSTS max-age=31536000. Priority high · Difficulty advanced · Time 45 min. Tools: Google CSP Evaluator, securityheaders.com, Mozilla Observatory.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist (thedaviddias/front-end-checklist); rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/security/content-security-policy ; OWASP HTTP Headers Cheat Sheet, MDN Web Security.
- **Best for:** The hosting/response layer of any live trade site with forms (quote forms collect personal data); less relevant to a static preview file.
- **Tier:** STRONG — priority high in the source; the baseline security header for production.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0981⟧

## ⟦S0982⟧ content-without-css — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** An accessibility/resilience rule (WCAG 1.3.1 / 1.3.2): content, instructions and the main task must remain understandable and operable with author CSS disabled or replaced by user styles — meaning lives in semantic HTML and DOM order, never in CSS alone.
- **How it looks:** With styles stripped, the page reads as a clean single column in the right order: real headings, lists, field labels, required markers and error messages all still present as text — a checkout still reads Shipping → Payment → Review, in that order.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** DOM order must equal reading/task order (no flex/grid `order` tricks carrying the sequence); labels in `<label>`, groups in `<fieldset>`/`<legend>`, required markers and instructions as DOM text linked with `aria-describedby` — never only in `::before`/`::after` content, background images or placeholders. Pass test from the source: disable author styles (Firefox View → Page Style → No Style), read top to bottom, tab the main task, trigger a validation error — everything must still work. Priority high · Difficulty intermediate · Time 20 min.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist (thedaviddias/front-end-checklist); rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/accessibility/content-without-css ; WCAG 1.3.1 Info and Relationships, 1.3.2 Meaningful Sequence; MDN semantic HTML.
- **Best for:** Forms (quote/estimate) and process sections — the parts of a trade homepage a visitor must complete, not just admire.
- **Tier:** STRONG — priority high in the source; also a free robustness check on hand-built markup.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0982⟧

## ⟦S0983⟧ contract-testing — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** A testing rule: use consumer-driven contract tests (Pact) at the frontend↔backend API boundary, so each side tests independently against a published contract instead of brittle end-to-end setups.
- **How it looks:** No visitor-facing output — its product is a verified contract file in a Pact Broker and a CI gate that blocks a deploy whose API shape no longer matches what the frontend consumes.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Flow: consumer writes Pact tests against a mock server → pact JSON published to the broker with a version tag → provider replays each interaction against the real API and reports results → `pact-broker can-i-deploy` gates release. Matchers: `like`, `string`, `integer`, `decimal`, `eachLike`, `regex`, `iso8601DateTime`, `nullValue` — shape/type checks, not business-value checks. Priority medium · Difficulty advanced · Time 120 min.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist (thedaviddias/front-end-checklist); rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/testing/contract-testing ; Pact documentation, Martin Fowler on consumer-driven contracts.
- **Best for:** App-like builds with a real API (booking/quote backends). No application to a static trade homepage.
- **Tier:** NOT-FOR-TRADES — a backend-integration discipline; nothing on a trade homepage consumes it.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0983⟧

## ⟦S0984⟧ cookie-consent — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** A privacy rule: obtain valid consent before setting any non-essential cookie or loading any tracker, via a consent banner/CMP that genuinely blocks scripts until the visitor chooses. Companion to ⟦S0974⟧ (Google's signalling layer).
- **How it looks:** On first visit, a dialog banner ("We use cookies") with Reject non-essential, Manage preferences and Accept all buttons; expanding preferences shows unticked Analytics and Advertising toggles beside a locked-on "Strictly necessary" row. A "Cookie settings" entry point stays available (e.g. in the footer) after the banner is gone.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion specified. (Visitor clicks a choice → banner dismisses → only the granted categories' scripts initialise; revoking later stops them on the next load.)
- **Mechanism & key values:** Valid consent (GDPR Art. 4(11)) must be freely given, specific, informed and unambiguous — pre-ticked boxes are invalid, declining must be as easy as accepting, no cookie walls. Categories: strictly necessary (session/CSRF/login — no consent), functional (depends), analytics, advertising, social embeds (consent required). Exposure named in the source: fines up to €20 million or 4% of global annual turnover. CMPs named: Cookiebot, OneTrust, CookieYes, Osano. Pair with Consent Mode v2 defaults (`wait_for_update: 500`). Priority high · Difficulty intermediate · Time 30 min.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist (thedaviddias/front-end-checklist); rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/privacy/cookie-consent ; GDPR Article 6, Recital 32.
- **Best for:** Any live trade site with analytics or ad pixels and a UK/EU audience — legally load-bearing, and the banner is a real homepage component to design.
- **Tier:** STRONG — priority high in the source; mandatory where trackers run in regulated regions.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0984⟧

## ⟦S0985⟧ critical-images — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** An images/performance rule: identify the critical (hero/above-the-fold) images and load them at high priority — `fetchpriority="high"` plus a `<link rel="preload">` — because the hero image is usually the LCP element.
- **How it looks:** The hero photograph is simply there when the page first paints, instead of popping in after the text; below-fold gallery images still lazy-load as the visitor scrolls to them.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. (Load sequence: HTML head preload starts the hero download immediately → hero renders with the first paint → lower sections' images fetch later on approach.)
- **Mechanism & key values:** Source figure: prioritising the LCP image can improve LCP by 20–40%. Priority table: hero/banner — preload + fetchpriority="high"; above the fold — fetchpriority="high", never `loading="lazy"`; below the fold — `loading="lazy"`; footer — lazy + `decoding="async"`. Responsive preloads switch at `media="(max-width: 768px)"`. Next.js: the `priority` prop. Priority high · Difficulty beginner · Time 15 min.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist (thedaviddias/front-end-checklist); rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/images/critical-images
- **Best for:** The hero of every trade homepage — the single highest-yield image rule in the set — and any full-width section opener.
- **Tier:** STRONG — priority high in the source; direct LCP lever.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0985⟧

## ⟦S0986⟧ critical-request-chains — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** A performance rule: shorten chains of dependent requests (HTML → CSS → font) that serialise the critical rendering path, by preloading deep resources and inlining small critical ones.
- **How it looks:** First paint arrives without the visible stall of a page waiting on a stylesheet waiting on a font; text appears in the real font instead of flashing a fallback late.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Targets from the source: keep critical chain depth to a maximum of 2–3; inline assets under ~2 KB directly in the HTML; preload fonts from the HTML head (`<link rel="preload" as="font" crossorigin>`); never use CSS `@import` (it adds a chain level); avoid chained redirects on critical resources. Diagnose in Lighthouse's Critical Request Chains audit and the WebPageTest waterfall. Priority high · Difficulty advanced · Time 20 min.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist (thedaviddias/front-end-checklist); rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/performance/critical-request-chains ; Lighthouse, WebPageTest.
- **Best for:** The head/loading architecture of the homepage — pairs with ⟦S0992⟧ (critical CSS) and ⟦S0985⟧ (critical images).
- **Tier:** STRONG — priority high in the source; governs how fast every section can appear.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0986⟧

## ⟦S0987⟧ cross-browser-testing — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** A testing rule: verify the site in all major browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge, desktop and mobile), automated in CI with screenshot comparison.
- **How it looks:** No visitor-facing output; its evidence is a matrix of per-browser screenshots of the same page — homepage at 375 / 768 / 1280 / 1920 px widths — that must match, plus passing layout assertions (no horizontal overflow, CLS under threshold).
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Source market table: Chrome/Blink ~65% (critical), Safari/WebKit (critical — iOS default), Firefox/Gecko (high), Edge/Blink (high), Samsung Internet (medium). Playwright projects: chromium, firefox, webkit, msedge + Pixel 5 and iPhone 12 devices. Assertions in the source suite: CLS < 0.1; visual diffs capped at maxDiffPixels 100. Known traps listed: flexbox gap in Safari < 14.1, subgrid Firefox-first, date inputs in Safari. Real iOS devices or BrowserStack required for true Safari behaviour. Priority high · Difficulty intermediate · Time 60 min.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist (thedaviddias/front-end-checklist); rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/testing/cross-browser-testing ; Playwright, BrowserStack, LambdaTest, Sauce Labs, caniuse.com.
- **Best for:** The release gate of every build — the check that a hero tuned in Chrome hasn't broken in Safari, where much of the trade audience browses.
- **Tier:** STRONG — priority high in the source; process rule, applies to every delivery.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0987⟧

## ⟦S0988⟧ cross-origin-isolation — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** A security rule: adopt cross-origin isolation (COOP + COEP + CORP) deliberately — only where an app needs the security boundary or gated features like SharedArrayBuffer — after auditing every cross-origin embed.
- **How it looks:** Nothing visible; in the console `self.crossOriginIsolated` reads `true` on isolated routes, and incompatible third-party embeds simply fail to load — which is why the audit comes first.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Document headers: `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin` + `Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp`; subresources answer with CORS or `Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: same-origin`. Pass = intended routes isolated and popup/OAuth/payment/embed flows still working; fail = the app uses isolated-only APIs while `crossOriginIsolated` is false. Priority medium · Difficulty advanced · Time 30 min.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist (thedaviddias/front-end-checklist); rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/security/cross-origin-isolation
- **Best for:** Web apps with workers, editors or sensitive data. A marketing homepage does not need it — the source says so itself.
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL — powerful but opt-in; most trade sites should leave it off.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0988⟧

## ⟦S0989⟧ cross-origin-security — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** A JavaScript security rule: handle cross-origin communication safely — validate `postMessage` origins, configure CORS narrowly, protect against CSRF, and refuse open redirects.
- **How it looks:** Nothing visible in normal use; the failures it prevents are invisible too — a malicious page silently issuing commands to an embedded widget, or a login link that bounces the visitor to a phishing site via a `?next=` parameter.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** postMessage: check `event.origin` against an explicit allowlist before parsing, always send to a named target origin, never `'*'` for sensitive data. CORS: explicit origin allowlist with credentials; `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` only on public, credential-less APIs. CSRF: SameSite cookies plus a token header (`X-CSRF-Token`). Open redirects: accept only destinations starting with `/`, else fall back to a default route — the source's test is `?next=https://attacker.example`, which must be rejected. Priority high · Difficulty intermediate · Time 20 min.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist (thedaviddias/front-end-checklist); rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/javascript/cross-origin-security ; MDN JavaScript Guide, web.dev Learn JavaScript.
- **Best for:** Any page embedding iframes/widgets or handling login/return flows; on a static trade homepage it mainly guards embedded maps, review widgets and form endpoints.
- **Tier:** STRONG — priority high in the source wherever cross-origin code runs.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0989⟧

## ⟦S0990⟧ css-at-property — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** A CSS capability rule: register custom properties with `@property` (type, initial value, inheritance) so the browser can animate them and validate token assignments — unregistered properties can only flip discretely.
- **How it looks:** A card whose background gradient slowly rotates its angle on hover instead of snapping; a hue variable sweeping a whole section from blue to warm orange while components using it shift colour mid-transition; a progress bar whose fill percentage glides.
- **Frame by frame:** Trigger: hover or a class/JS change sets the registered property → the browser interpolates the typed value step by step (the source's gradient angle runs 135deg → 225deg over a 0.6s ease transition; a hue shift runs over 0.4s; a progress fill over 0.5s) → the gradient/hue/fill settles at the end value. Without registration the same change jumps in one frame.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Registration shape: `@property --x { syntax: '<angle>'; initial-value: 135deg; inherits: false; }` — a typed syntax REQUIRES `initial-value` or the registration is silently invalid. Syntax types: `<color>`, `<length>`, `<number>`, `<integer>`, `<percentage>`, `<angle>`, `<time>`, `<length-percentage>`, list forms `+`/`#`, universal `*`. `inherits: false` scopes a token per-component. JS equivalent: `CSS.registerProperty()`. Support: Chrome/Edge 85+, Firefox 128+, Safari 16.4+. Priority low · Difficulty advanced · Time 30 min.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist (thedaviddias/front-end-checklist); rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/css/css-at-property ; MDN @property, CSS Properties & Values API spec, web.dev @property article.
- **Best for:** Animated gradient heroes, theme-shift sections and animated counters/proof bars on trade homepages — the enabling technique behind smooth token-driven motion.
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL — a specialist motion enabler; the source rates it low priority but it unlocks effects nothing else in CSS can do.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0990⟧

## ⟦S0991⟧ css-containment — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** A CSS performance rule: declare `contain` on self-contained components so changes inside them can't trigger page-wide layout/paint work, and use `content-visibility: auto` to skip rendering off-screen sections entirely.
- **How it looks:** The page looks unchanged; long pages scroll and update without the whole document re-laying-out when one card changes, and below-fold sections materialise as they approach the viewport.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** `contain` values: `layout`, `style`, `paint`, `size`, `inline-size`; shorthands `content` = layout + paint + style, `strict` = layout + paint + style + size. Fixed-size widgets (source example: a 300×250 ad unit) take `strict`; repeated list/feed items take `content`; a chat widget takes `layout paint`. Long-page pattern: `content-visibility: auto; contain-intrinsic-size: auto 800px;` — the intrinsic-size estimate prevents scrollbar jumps. Note container queries implicitly apply inline-size containment. Priority medium · Difficulty advanced · Time 20 min.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist (thedaviddias/front-end-checklist); rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/css/css-containment
- **Best for:** Long scrolling trade homepages with many repeated cards (reviews, towns, gallery items) — keeps big pages fluid.
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL — pays off as page length and component count grow; priority medium in the source.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0991⟧

## ⟦S0992⟧ css-critical — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** A CSS delivery rule: inline the minimum above-the-fold ("critical") CSS in a `<style>` block in the head and load the rest asynchronously, removing CSS from the render-blocking path.
- **How it looks:** The header and hero appear fully styled on first paint — correct fonts, colours and layout immediately — instead of an unstyled flash that snaps into place when the stylesheet arrives; footer and below-fold styling lands a moment later, unseen.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. (Load sequence: HTML arrives with critical styles inline → first paint is already styled → the full stylesheet swaps in via preload/onload without blocking.)
- **Mechanism & key values:** Inline budget in the source: ~14 KB of critical CSS. Async pattern: `<link rel="preload" as="style" onload="this.rel='stylesheet'">` with a `<noscript>` fallback. Extract automatically — tools named: critical (Addy Osmani), critters, Penthouse; extraction viewport in the source configs: 1200×800. Automate in the build; never hand-maintain. Priority high · Difficulty advanced · Time 30 min.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist (thedaviddias/front-end-checklist); rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/css/css-critical
- **Best for:** The head of every homepage — works with ⟦S0986⟧ (request chains) and ⟦S0985⟧ (critical images) to make the hero instant.
- **Tier:** STRONG — priority high in the source; direct FCP/LCP improvement.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0992⟧

## ⟦S0993⟧ css-custom-properties — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** A CSS system rule: define design values (colours, spacing, type, radii, shadows) once as `--custom-properties` on `:root` and reference them with `var()` everywhere, instead of scattering hard-coded values.
- **How it looks:** A consistently tokened page — one brand colour on every button, badge and link — where a rebrand or a dark-mode switch restyles the whole site from a handful of variable lines; components can locally override a token (a card with its own surface colour and deeper shadow) without new classes.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** The source's token set: colours (`--color-primary: #2563eb`, hover `#1d4ed8`, text `#111827`, muted `#6b7280`, border `#e5e7eb`), spacing scale `--space-1: 0.25rem` → `--space-8: 2rem`, type `--text-sm: 0.875rem` → `--text-xl: 1.25rem`, radii 0.25rem / 0.5rem / 9999px, layered shadows. Use `var(--name, fallback)` and nested fallbacks (`var(--shadow-button, var(--shadow-sm))`). Unlike preprocessor variables these are live runtime values — JS reads them with getComputedStyle and writes with setProperty; dark mode is a `prefers-color-scheme` block redefining the same tokens. Priority high · Difficulty beginner · Time 20 min. Companion: ⟦S0990⟧ registers these properties for animation/typing.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist (thedaviddias/front-end-checklist); rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/css/css-custom-properties
- **Best for:** The foundation layer of any single-file trade build — every section's colours and spacing trace back to one token block.
- **Tier:** STRONG — priority high in the source; basic craft for hand-built pages.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0993⟧

## ⟦S0994⟧ css-file-size — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** A performance rule: keep CSS files small — minify, purge unused rules, and split by route — because CSS blocks rendering until it is downloaded and parsed.
- **How it looks:** The same styled page, painting sooner; nothing visual changes except the wait for first paint shrinking, most noticeably on mobile connections.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Audit threshold in the source: flag individual CSS files over 50 KB gzipped. Levers: PurgeCSS against the actual templates, cssnano minification, route-specific stylesheets instead of one global bundle, and Chrome DevTools' Coverage tab to measure the unused percentage per page. Avoid shipping a whole framework (Bootstrap/Foundation) for a few components, and avoid deep preprocessor nesting that inflates selectors. Priority medium · Difficulty intermediate · Time 10 min.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist (thedaviddias/front-end-checklist); rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/performance/css-file-size ; PurgeCSS, CSSNano, Lighthouse.
- **Best for:** Whole-page weight control alongside ⟦S0996⟧ (minification, its sibling) and ⟦S0992⟧ (critical CSS) — the size budget for the styles a single-file homepage inlines or links.
- **Tier:** STRONG — cheap, measurable win; priority medium in the source.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0994⟧

## ⟦S0995⟧ css-grid — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** A CSS layout rule: use CSS Grid for two-dimensional layouts (rows and columns together) and keep Flexbox for one-dimensional ones, instead of forcing Flexbox/floats into 2D workarounds.
- **How it looks:** Card grids whose rows align cleanly across columns; a page skeleton drawn as named areas — header across the top, sidebar beside main, footer across the bottom — collapsing to a single stacked column on mobile; cards whose titles, text and buttons line up across the row via subgrid.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. (Grids re-flow discretely at breakpoints/container widths.)
- **Mechanism & key values:** Responsive-without-media-queries pattern: `grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(280px, 1fr)); gap: 1.5rem`. Named areas with `grid-template-areas` over `280px 1fr` columns and `auto 1fr auto` rows, `min-height: 100vh`; the source's mobile switch is a 768px media query. Track sizing with `minmax(200px, 300px)` + `1fr`; explicit spans (`grid-column: 1 / 3`); subgrid (`grid-template-rows: subgrid` with `grid-row: span 4`) aligns card internals — with a fallback note where subgrid support is missing. Priority medium · Difficulty intermediate · Time 25 min.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist (thedaviddias/front-end-checklist); rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/css/css-grid
- **Best for:** Work/gallery grids, services matrices, towns/areas tiles and the overall page skeleton of a trade homepage — the default 2D layout tool.
- **Tier:** STRONG — core layout craft used by nearly every section; priority medium in the source.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0995⟧

## ⟦S0996⟧ css-minification — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** A CSS delivery rule: minify all CSS in production builds — strip whitespace, comments and redundant syntax with cssnano/lightningcss — and combine with Gzip/Brotli.
- **How it looks:** Identical rendering; the stylesheet simply arrives smaller. The source's worked example shrinks a navigation stylesheet from ~600 bytes to ~215 bytes (~65% smaller); its general figure for minification alone is 20–40% savings.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Tooling: cssnano (default/advanced presets — discardComments, colormin, convertValues, mergeRules, minifySelectors), Vite `cssMinify: 'lightningcss'`, webpack CssMinimizerPlugin, Next.js automatic production minification. Production only, always with source maps for debugging; if minification breaks selectors, disable `minifySelectors` rather than shipping unminified. Sibling rules: ⟦S0994⟧ (file size/purging) and ⟦S0973⟧ (transfer compression). Priority high · Difficulty beginner · Time 15 min.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist (thedaviddias/front-end-checklist); rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/css/css-minification
- **Best for:** The build step of every delivered page — free bytes on every style the homepage ships.
- **Tier:** STRONG — priority high in the source; fully automatable, no downside when source maps are kept.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0996⟧
# Skills chunk — ⟦S0997⟧–⟦S1032⟧

All 36 skills in this range belong to one collection: **Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills** (thedaviddias/front-end-checklist, expressed as 391 small checkable rule-skills; rule pages at frontendchecklist.io). None of them is a design, layout or animation reference — each is a QA/audit rule with a When-to-use trigger, a Check, a Fix, an Explain, a Code Review brief and a bundled rule.md carrying priority / difficulty / time and worked code. Their place in the workflow is the final QA sweep of a finished page, so every entry is Tier **SITUATIONAL** with that basis stated; priorities quoted are the rule's own.

**Duplicate check:** no two skills in this range are the same underlying skill under different names — no entry is collapsed to a pointer. Three companion pairs cover adjacent ground and are cross-referenced inside their entries instead: ⟦S1009⟧ definition-list (what may sit *inside* a `<dl>`) vs ⟦S1014⟧ dlitem (`<dt>`/`<dd>` must sit *inside* a `<dl>`) — the two directions of one nesting law, mirroring the axe-core rules `definition-list` and `dlitem`; ⟦S1020⟧ duplicate-id-active vs ⟦S1021⟧ duplicate-id-aria — the axe pair for duplicate IDs on focusable elements vs on ARIA-referenced elements; ⟦S1000⟧ cumulative-layout-shift (visual stability overall) vs ⟦S1011⟧ dimensions (the single image-attribute fix that is CLS's biggest cause).

---

## ⟦S0997⟧ css-non-blocking — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** A QA rule requiring CSS to load without blocking first render: critical styles inline, everything else fetched asynchronously. A check/fix procedure, not a design.
- **How it looks:** Nothing decorative of its own. The visitor-visible effect is the page painting already styled — header, hero and type in place on first paint — instead of a blank white screen that suddenly snaps into style when a big stylesheet lands.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. The sequence it changes is load order: HTML parses → inlined critical CSS paints the above-the-fold layout immediately → the full stylesheet swaps in behind it with no visible flash or restyle jump.
- **Mechanism & key values:** `<link rel="preload" as="style" onload="this.onload=null;this.rel='stylesheet'">` with a `<noscript>` stylesheet fallback; Filament Group loadCSS pattern (insert link with `media="only x"`, switch media on load); split by media attribute (e.g. `media="print"`, `media="screen and (max-width: 768px)"`); resource hints (preconnect, prefetch); service-worker caching of `destination === 'style'` requests; Next.js/Vite noted as handling it automatically. Rule's own grading: Priority high · Difficulty intermediate · Time 20 min.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist (thedaviddias/front-end-checklist); rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/css/css-non-blocking ; tools named: loadCSS (Filament Group), Addy Osmani's critical, PurgeCSS.
- **Best for:** Final QA sweep on every homepage build — the delivery check that a heavy single-file page (hero CSS, section CSS) does not blank-screen on slow connections. Applies to all sections equally; no trade restriction.
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL — a QA-sweep check, not a design reference.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0997⟧

## ⟦S0998⟧ css-order — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** A QA rule requiring all CSS to be loaded before JavaScript in the document head, so styling precedence is set before scripts run and no flash of unstyled content (FOUC) occurs.
- **How it looks:** No visual system of its own. On screen it is the absence of a defect: text never appears briefly in default browser styling (wrong font, no layout) before the real design pops in.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. It governs document order only: stylesheet links → inlined critical `<style>` → deferred/async scripts.
- **Mechanism & key values:** All `<link rel="stylesheet">` before any blocking `<script>` in `<head>`; async scripts exempt (they may sit anywhere); critical CSS inlined between the two groups; FOUC guard pattern — content `visibility: hidden` until a `styles-loaded` class lands on stylesheet load, with a 3000 ms timeout fallback that reveals content anyway; build-tool enforcement via webpack splitChunks styles cacheGroup (priority 10–20) or a head-reordering plugin. Priority medium · Difficulty beginner · Time 10 min.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist; rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/css/css-order .
- **Best for:** QA sweep of the page shell/head on any build; pairs with ⟦S0997⟧ (loading) — this one is ordering, that one is blocking behaviour.
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL — a QA-sweep check, not a design reference.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0998⟧

## ⟦S0999⟧ css-print — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** A QA rule requiring a print stylesheet, so a page sent to a printer comes out as a clean black-on-white document instead of a screenshot of the screen layout.
- **How it looks:** On paper: serif body text (Times New Roman at 12pt, line-height 1.4), headings 18/16/14/12pt, black text on white, tables with 1pt ruled borders, links underlined with their full URL printed after them in 10pt grey, running header/footer on each sheet ("Page X of Y"). Navigation, sidebars, ads, share buttons, carousels, modals and all buttons are gone.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. Trigger is the print command: the `@media print` ruleset swaps the screen layout for the paper layout in one step; beforeprint/afterprint handlers optionally expand collapsed sections and stamp a print date.
- **Mechanism & key values:** `@media print` block or `<link … media="print">`; `@page { margin: 2cm; size: A4 }` with margin-box content using `counter(page)`/`counter(pages)`; `print-color-adjust: exact`; paragraphs `orphans: 3; widows: 3`; headings `break-after: avoid`; tables/images `page-break-inside: avoid`; `a[href]:after { content: " (" attr(href) ")" }`; hide list includes nav, .sidebar, .ads, .comments, .pagination, .btn and all submit/button inputs; named pages (`@page chapter`, `@page :left/:right` with 3cm binding margins). Priority medium · Difficulty intermediate · Time 30 min.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist; rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/css/css-print .
- **Best for:** QA sweep for content a homeowner might actually print — a quote/estimate page, a services or process page, a long guide. Low relevance to an animated homepage hero; relevant to inner content pages.
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL — a QA-sweep check, not a design reference.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S0999⟧

## ⟦S1000⟧ cumulative-layout-shift — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** A QA rule requiring the page to stay visually stable while it loads — Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS) score below 0.1 — so content never jumps under the reader's eye or finger.
- **How it looks:** Every block is in its final position from first paint: the hero image occupies its full box immediately (empty but correctly sized), headlines don't drop down when the webfont arrives, a banner slot is already its final height before the banner fills it. The failure it prevents: text sliding down mid-read and a tap landing on the wrong link.
- **Frame by frame:** No authored motion. The motion described is the defect sequence — parse → render without reserved space → image/font/late content loads → surrounding content shifts position → CLS accrues. With the rule applied the sequence is: space reserved up front → assets load into their boxes → nothing moves. Animations must use transform/opacity only (example: `translateX(-100px) → 0`, 0.3s ease-out) since animating margin/width itself shifts layout.
- **Mechanism & key values:** CLS thresholds — 0–0.1 good, 0.1–0.25 needs improvement, >0.25 poor; width/height attributes or `aspect-ratio` on all images/embeds (example hero 1200×600, `aspect-ratio: 16/9`); reserved containers for dynamic content (example ad box 300×250, banner wrapper `min-height: 60px`); skeleton placeholders at final dimensions; `@font-face` with `font-display: swap`, `size-adjust: 100%`, `ascent-override: 90%`, `descent-override: 20%`; never inject content above existing content; measured with web-vitals `onCLS` and a `layout-shift` PerformanceObserver (entries with `hadRecentInput` ignored). Priority high · Difficulty intermediate · Time 20 min.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist; rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/performance/cumulative-layout-shift .
- **Best for:** QA sweep on every section of a media-heavy trades homepage — hero imagery, before/after galleries, review cards, late-loading embeds — anywhere a shift would move the call button. Companion to ⟦S1011⟧, which covers the image-attribute fix specifically.
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL — a QA-sweep check, not a design reference.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1000⟧

## ⟦S1001⟧ currency-formatting — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** A QA rule requiring all numbers, prices and dates to be formatted with the browser's Intl APIs instead of hand-built strings, so every locale sees its own conventions.
- **How it looks:** The same price renders correctly per visitor: `$1,234.50` (en-US), `1.234,50 €` (de-DE), `¥1,235` (ja-JP — no minor units, rounded), `£1,234.50` (en-GB), `CHF 1'234.50` (fr-CH); percents as `74%` vs `74 %`; big counts compacted (`1.5M`, `150万`); units spelled out (`42 kilometers`); dates as `3/11/2025` vs `11.3.2025` vs `2025/3/11`; relative times as "3 days ago" / "tomorrow".
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. Formatting happens at render; nothing animates.
- **Mechanism & key values:** `Intl.NumberFormat(locale, { style: 'currency', currency })`, plus percent/unit/compact styles; `Intl.DateTimeFormat` (dateStyle/timeStyle), `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat(numeric: 'auto')`, `Intl.Collator({ sensitivity: 'base', numeric: true })` for sorting; the user's locale passed explicitly on every call — an omitted locale uses the server locale in SSR and mismatches the client (hydration bug); formatter instances cached per locale+currency key rather than constructed per render; fallback via `Intl.NumberFormat.supportedLocalesOf([...])`. Priority medium · Difficulty beginner · Time 20 min.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist; rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/i18n/currency-formatting ; standards named: MDN Intl.NumberFormat / Intl.DateTimeFormat.
- **Best for:** QA sweep wherever numbers print: price-band sections, finance examples, stats/count-ups, dates on reviews and project cards. Directly relevant to trades pages that publish price ranges.
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL — a QA-sweep check, not a design reference.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1001⟧

## ⟦S1002⟧ custom-element-accessibility — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** A QA rule requiring custom elements / Web Components to expose real semantics — ARIA reflection, keyboard operation and form participation — via ElementInternals, or be replaced by a native control.
- **How it looks:** Nothing visual of its own; the custom widget looks identical either way. The difference is what assistive technology perceives: the control is announced with its role, name and state ("checkbox, checked") instead of being skipped or read as an anonymous group.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion prescribed. The interaction sequence it specifies: Tab reaches the widget (host `tabindex="0"`) → Space toggles a checkbox → in compound widgets Arrow keys move within the group while only the active item stays tabbable → state changes are reflected to ARIA and to the enclosing form's value at each step.
- **Mechanism & key values:** `attachInternals()` in the constructor; `internals.ariaRole` / `ariaChecked` set on the internals object (ARIA inside the shadow root does not reach the accessibility tree on its own); `static formAssociated = true` with `setFormValue()` and `setValidity()` for custom inputs; roving tabindex — active item `tabindex="0"`, all others `"-1"`, ArrowUp/ArrowDown/Home/End move it; slotted light-DOM content labelled explicitly. First resort is native: a styled `<button>`, `<input>`, `<select>` or `<details>` beats a rebuilt widget. Priority medium · Difficulty advanced · Time 60 min.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist; rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/html/custom-element-accessibility .
- **Best for:** QA sweep only when a build hand-rolls a widget (custom checkbox, listbox, toolbar, menu) instead of using native elements — rarely triggered on a trades homepage, decisive when it is.
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL — a QA-sweep check, not a design reference.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1002⟧

## ⟦S1003⟧ dark-mode-css — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** A QA rule requiring dark-mode support driven by the OS preference (`prefers-color-scheme`), implemented by redefining colour tokens — plus a manual toggle pattern.
- **How it looks:** With the OS in dark mode the same page renders on deep slate surfaces with near-white text: the rule's own token set flips surface `#ffffff → #0f172a`, elevated surface `#f9fafb → #1e293b`, text `#111827 → #f1f5f9`, muted text `#6b7280 → #94a3b8`, border `#e5e7eb → #334155`, primary `#2563eb → #3b82f6`; photos sit slightly dimmed (brightness 0.85, contrast 1.05) so they don't glare.
- **Frame by frame:** One motion value is prescribed: on theme switch, `background-color`, `color` and `border-color` cross-fade over 200 ms ease — and that transition is suppressed on initial page load (a `.no-transition` guard) so the first paint doesn't animate.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Semantic CSS custom properties on `:root` (never colour-named tokens), redefined inside `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)`; components consume variables only — no dark-specific component CSS; manual override via `[data-theme="dark"]`/`[data-theme="light"]` persisted in `localStorage` under `theme-preference`; `color-scheme: light dark` (or `dark` under the attribute) so scrollbars and form controls follow; dark-mode contrast must still meet WCAG ratios. Priority medium · Difficulty intermediate · Time 25 min.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist; rule page https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/css/dark-mode-css .
- **Best for:** QA sweep if a build ships a dark theme or theme toggle — for the current trades homepages, only relevant where a dark section system or toggle exists; the token-flip pattern is also the clean way to run light/dark section alternation deliberately.
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL — a QA-sweep check, not a design reference.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1003⟧

## ⟦S1004⟧ data-minimisation — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills
- **What it is:** A QA rule requiring the site to collect only the personal data a stated feature actually consumes — GDPR Article 5(1)(c) applied to forms, storage, API payloads, analytics and logs.
- **How it looks:** Nothing visual of its own. Its on-screen trace is shorter forms: the rule's example cuts a newsletter form from email + first name + last name + phone + date of birth down to email alone, because only the email is ever read.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
