Non-negotiables: `jest.restoreAllMocks()` in `afterEach` (a leaked Date.now mock contaminating the next test is the worked example); realistic API mocking via MSW (`setupServer` + listen/resetHandlers/close lifecycle); spies restored after use; a test that mocks the very function it claims to test "tests nothing".
- **Reference / source:** https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/testing/mock-best-practices; Testing Library guiding principles; Playwright docs.
- **Best for:** Engineering QA of the codebases behind builds — no homepage-section application.
- **Tier:** NOT-FOR-TRADES — test-engineering hygiene only; banked so the checklist is complete.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1140⟧

## ⟦S1141⟧ modal-accessibility — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills (accessibility)
- **What it is:** Audit rule: modal dialogs must be fully keyboard- and screen-reader-operable — labelled dialog role, focus trapped inside, Escape to close, focus returned to the trigger on close (priority high · intermediate · 30 min).
- **How it looks:** A dialog opens over a dimmed backdrop (quote form, confirmation, gallery lightbox); the visitor's keyboard focus starts inside it, tabs only through its own controls, and the page behind does not scroll; closing drops focus back on the exact button that opened it.
- **Frame by frame:** Trigger: user activates the trigger → current focus element is stored → dialog appears, focus moves onto/into it, background scroll locks (`overflow: hidden` on body) → Tab and Shift+Tab cycle strictly within the dialog's focusable set (last→first, first→last) → Escape key or backdrop click closes → dialog unmounts, scroll unlocks, focus returns to the stored trigger → end state: page exactly as before, focus restored.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Required attributes: `role="dialog"`, `aria-modal="true"`, `aria-labelledby` → the dialog title's id, `aria-describedby` → description id; container `tabIndex={-1}` to receive initial focus; focusable selector used by the trap: `button, [href], input, select, textarea, [tabindex]:not([tabindex="-1"])`; native alternative: the `<dialog>` element with `showModal()` (browser supplies trapping/Escape); verify by opening with keyboard only, tabbing the full cycle, escaping, and checking focus return.
- **Reference / source:** https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/accessibility/modal-accessibility; W3C WAI WCAG overview; MDN Accessibility.
- **Best for:** Quote-form modals, callback request dialogs, confirmations and image lightboxes on trade homepages — the interaction component where accessibility most often breaks.
- **Tier:** STRONG — high priority; any build that ships a modal needs exactly this contract.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1141⟧

## ⟦S1142⟧ modern-array-methods — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills (javascript)
- **What it is:** Audit rule: replace manual loops with declarative ES2015+ array/object methods so data transformations state their intent (priority medium · beginner · 15 min).
- **How it looks:** Nothing on screen changes — the rendered page is identical. The difference lives in the code that produces lists, grids and filtered collections behind the page.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Method kit with semantics: `map` transform · `filter` select · `reduce` aggregate/group · `find`/`findIndex` first match · `some`/`every` boolean checks · `flatMap` map+flatten one level; object side: `Object.entries`/`fromEntries` (entries→map→fromEntries is the transform pipeline), `Object.keys`/`values`; deep copy with `structuredClone()` (handles Date, Map, Set, circular refs) instead of `JSON.parse(JSON.stringify())` which drops them; `Array.from` for NodeList/Set/arguments and range generation.
- **Reference / source:** https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/javascript/modern-array-methods; MDN JavaScript Guide; web.dev Learn JavaScript.
- **Best for:** Code quality inside a build's interaction layer (filtering galleries, computing stats) — no direct section or visual application.
- **Tier:** NOT-FOR-TRADES — a coding-style rule; recorded for checklist completeness.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1142⟧

## ⟦S1143⟧ modern-format — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills (images)
- **What it is:** Audit rule: serve photos as WebP/AVIF with JPEG/PNG fallbacks instead of legacy formats alone — images are typically 50%+ of page weight (priority high · intermediate · 20 min).
- **How it looks:** The same photographs at the same visual quality — a hero and gallery that simply arrive faster and lighter, especially on mobile data; nothing in composition or colour changes.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. Delivery flow: browser reads the `<picture>` element top-down → first supported `<source>` wins (AVIF, then WebP) → unsupported browsers fall through to the `<img>` JPEG → the chosen file is also picked by width from its srcset (400w/800w/1200w against the sizes rule).
- **Mechanism & key values:** Savings vs JPEG at equal quality: WebP ~25–35% smaller (WebP lossless ~26% smaller than PNG), AVIF ~40–50% smaller. Support: WebP 97%+ globally; AVIF Chrome 85+, Firefox 93+, Safari 16.4+. Conversion recipe (Sharp): WebP at quality 80; AVIF at quality 60, effort 6. Markup: `<picture>` with avif source, webp source, JPEG `<img>` fallback carrying width/height; CSS backgrounds via `@supports (background-image: url('test.webp'))` or a format-negotiating CDN; Next/Image serves formats automatically (`formats: ['image/avif','image/webp']`). Verify in DevTools Network — Type column must read webp/avif.
- **Reference / source:** https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/images/modern-format; web.dev "Serve images in modern formats".
- **Best for:** Hero, work/gallery and before/after imagery — the biggest single weight lever on photo-heavy trade homepages, feeding directly into S1113 (LCP).
- **Tier:** CROWN — for image-led homepages this is the standard delivery format rule.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1143⟧

## ⟦S1144⟧ mutation-testing — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills (testing)
- **What it is:** Audit rule: measure test quality with mutation testing (Stryker) — inject small plausible bugs into business logic and check the suite actually fails; line coverage alone proves only that code ran (priority medium · advanced · 120 min).
- **How it looks:** Nothing on any screen — its artefact is a report (HTML) where files glow green where all mutants were killed and red where a subtle bug survived the tests unnoticed.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. Process: mutator rewrites one operator/boundary/literal → suite runs → a failing test kills the mutant; a green suite lets it survive → score = killed ÷ total × 100 → repeat per mutant.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Mutation types: arithmetic (+→−), comparison (>→>=), logical (&&→||), boolean literal (true→false), string literal (→''), array declaration (→[]), conditional boundary (<→<=), block removal. Thresholds in the worked config: high 80 · low 60 · break (fail build) 50; focused CI config: 85/70/65; target 80%+ on critical paths (pricing, auth, validation), scope `mutate` to critical modules only, concurrency 4, incremental mode for CI; ~100% is explicitly not the goal (equivalent mutants).
- **Reference / source:** https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/testing/mutation-testing; Stryker Mutator documentation.
- **Best for:** Engineering assurance on calculation-heavy code (quote calculators, pricing) — no homepage design application.
- **Tier:** NOT-FOR-TRADES — deep QA tooling for application code, banked for completeness.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1144⟧

## ⟦S1145⟧ naming-conventions — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills (css)
- **What it is:** Audit rule: class names follow one consistent methodology (BEM by default) so a name states its component, part and variant without opening the stylesheet (priority medium · beginner · 15 min).
- **How it looks:** Nothing changes visually — the rule governs the class attributes under the design: `.card`, `.card__title`, `.card--featured` on a card component instead of ambiguous `.active`, `.blue-button`, `.container`.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** BEM grammar: Block (`.card`) · Block__Element (`.card__header`, double underscore) · Block--Modifier (`.card--dark`, double hyphen) · element modifier `.card__title--large`; kebab-case only. Namespace prefixes by class kind: `c-` components, `l-` layout, `u-` utilities, `is-` JS-applied state (`.is-active`, `.is-open`), `js-` JS hooks that are never styled. Bans: presentational names (`.blue-button`, `.big-text`) and unscoped generics; utility-first (Tailwind) counts as its own convention when used consistently.
- **Reference / source:** https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/css/naming-conventions; MDN CSS; web.dev Learn CSS.
- **Best for:** Maintainability of a build's stylesheet — most relevant when a single-file homepage's CSS grows large and sections are edited repeatedly.
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL — pays off in proportion to stylesheet size and edit frequency.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1145⟧

## ⟦S1146⟧ nap-consistency — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills (seo)
- **What it is:** Audit rule: the business Name, Address and Phone must be byte-identical in format everywhere they appear — footer, contact page, about page, LocalBusiness schema and Google Business Profile (priority medium · intermediate · 15 min).
- **How it looks:** The same line everywhere a visitor meets it: "123 Main Street, Suite 4" and "(555) 123-4567" in the footer, on the contact page and inside the schema — never "123 Main St, Ste 4" in one place and a different phone format in another; in search, Google shows the details with confidence instead of suppressing them.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Pick one canonical format per field and enforce it: phone format (one of `555-123-4567` vs `(555) 123-4567`), street abbreviation (St. vs Street), suite notation (Suite 4 vs Ste 4 vs #4), state (IL vs Illinois), exact business name. Audit process: export every phone/address instance site-wide → compare → fix all surfaces including GBP. Multi-location: one dedicated page per location's NAP, never mixed on one page. Companion rule S1128 supplies the schema the details must match.
- **Reference / source:** https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/seo/nap-consistency; Google Business Profile; Schema.org PostalAddress.
- **Best for:** Footer, contact and towns/areas pages of every local trade firm — a direct local-ranking input and a factual-accuracy guard for the details a build publishes.
- **Tier:** CROWN — for local-service sites this is foundational: the firm's own name/address/phone consistency is non-negotiable.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1146⟧

## ⟦S1147⟧ navigation-landmark — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills (html)
- **What it is:** Audit rule: every major navigation block is a `<nav>` element with a unique label, so screen-reader users can list and jump between nav regions, backed by skip links (priority high · beginner · 15 min).
- **How it looks:** The familiar furniture — top menu in the header, breadcrumb trail under it, a footer link block — each announced to assistive tech by name ("Main", "Breadcrumb", "Footer"); the first thing a keyboard user meets is a "Skip to main content" link that appears when focused.
- **Frame by frame:** Static at rest. One small motion: the skip link sits hidden above the viewport (`top: -40px`) → on keyboard focus it slides into view at the top (`top: 0`, 0.2s transition) → activating it jumps focus past the navigation to `#main-content`.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Label each region: Main / Secondary / Footer / Breadcrumb / Pagination / Table of contents; multiple unlabeled `<nav>`s and nested `<nav>`s are the flagged mistakes; `aria-label` for a short name, `aria-labelledby` when a visible heading exists; current page marked `aria-current="page"` (including the last breadcrumb item, rendered as a span, not a link); skip-link CSS: absolute, `top: -40px` hidden, `:focus { top: 0 }`, z-index 1000, 8px 16px padding. Use nav only for major blocks — minor link groups (social icons) don't qualify.
- **Reference / source:** https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/html/navigation-landmark.
- **Best for:** Navigation and footer of every build — the detailed companion to S1111's landmark rule.
- **Tier:** STRONG — high priority in the source; nav is on every page.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1147⟧

## ⟦S1148⟧ new-tab — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills (security)
- **What it is:** Audit rule ("External Link Security"): every `<a target="_blank">` must carry `rel="noopener noreferrer"`, closing the reverse-tabnapping hole where the opened page rewrites the original tab via `window.opener` (priority medium · beginner · 10 min). The instructions embedded in this skill's text (scan, fix, enforce) are its audit procedure — described here as data, not executed.
- **How it looks:** Nothing differs on screen — an external link opens its new tab as usual. What cannot happen behind the visitor's back: the destination page silently swapping the original tab for a phishing lookalike login page.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. Attack sequence the rule blocks: user clicks a `_blank` link → new tab's script runs `window.opener.location = 'https://fake-bank…'` → user returns to the original tab → it now shows the fake page. With `noopener`, `window.opener` is null and step two is impossible.
- **Mechanism & key values:** `noopener` nulls window.opener; `noreferrer` also suppresses the Referer header and implies noopener; use both for external links, `noopener` alone when a same-origin referrer is needed for analytics. Browser baseline: Chrome 88+ / Firefox 79+ imply noopener for cross-origin `_blank` only — same-origin links and older browsers still need the explicit attribute, and noreferrer is never implied. Enforcement: ESLint `react/jsx-no-target-blank` (error, enforceDynamicLinks); documented exception: intentional opener communication (OAuth popups) omits it with a code comment.
- **Reference / source:** https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/security/new-tab; OWASP reverse tabnapping testing guide; MDN rel=noopener/noreferrer.
- **Best for:** Every external link on a build — review-platform links, manufacturer/certification sites, social profiles in footers.
- **Tier:** STRONG — a one-attribute security fix on a pattern every homepage contains.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1148⟧

## ⟦S1149⟧ no-explicit-any — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills (javascript)
- **What it is:** Audit rule: TypeScript's `any` type is banned — replace it with `unknown` plus narrowing, generics, or Zod validation at data boundaries, because one `any` silently un-types every caller downstream (priority medium · intermediate · 20 min).
- **How it looks:** Nothing on any screen — a type-system discipline whose visible effect is bugs caught at compile time (a missing `settings.timeout` errors in the editor instead of crashing for a visitor).
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** `unknown` accepts anything but forbids use until narrowed (typeof / in / instanceof checks or a type guard `value is T`); generics preserve the input→output type relationship (`first<T>(arr: T[]): T | undefined`) that `any[] → any` destroys; assertions (`as Type`) acceptable only after a runtime check the compiler can't see, never to silence an error; API/fetch/localStorage data enters as `unknown` and is parsed by a Zod schema, with the TS type inferred from the schema (`z.infer`). Enforcement: ESLint `@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any` plus the no-unsafe-assignment/call/member-access/return family at "error", and `noImplicitAny` (in `strict`) with a clean `tsc --noEmit`.
- **Reference / source:** https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/javascript/no-explicit-any; TypeScript handbook (any, unknown); typescript-eslint rule docs.
- **Best for:** TypeScript codebases behind builds — no application to a hand-written single-file HTML homepage or its design.
- **Tier:** NOT-FOR-TRADES — engineering hygiene only; banked for checklist completeness.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1149⟧

## ⟦S1150⟧ no-unchecked-indexed-access — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills (javascript)
- **What it is:** Audit rule: enable TypeScript's `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` flag so index access honestly returns `T | undefined`, forcing a check instead of letting empty-array reads crash at runtime (priority medium · intermediate · 15 min).
- **How it looks:** Nothing on screen — the change is in what the compiler proves: `tags[0].toUpperCase()` on a possibly-empty array becomes a type error at build time rather than a TypeError in a visitor's browser.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** The flag is NOT part of `"strict": true` — it must be added explicitly in tsconfig `compilerOptions`. With it: `arr[i]` and `Record<string, T>` lookups type as `T | undefined`; `Array.at()` also returns `T | undefined`; iteration (for…of, forEach, map) is unaffected; destructuring (`const [first] = arr`) is NOT covered — still typed T. Handling patterns: explicit undefined check, `??` fallback, `?.` chaining; non-null assertion `!` allowed only where a bounds check is immediately visible (bounds-checked loops). Classic catch: parallel-array indexing (`grades[i]` inside `scores.map`) — the better fix is one array of objects.
- **Reference / source:** https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/javascript/no-unchecked-indexed-access; TSConfig reference; TypeScript 4.1 release notes.
- **Best for:** TypeScript application code — no application to a static trade homepage's design or content.
- **Tier:** NOT-FOR-TRADES — compiler-flag hygiene; banked for completeness.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1150⟧

## ⟦S1151⟧ nofollow-internal — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills (seo)
- **What it is:** Audit rule: never put `rel="nofollow"` on links to your own pages — it blocks PageRank flow to them and buys nothing; PageRank sculpting via internal nofollow has been dead since Google's 2019 change (priority medium · intermediate · 10 min).
- **How it looks:** Nothing on screen — links look and behave identically. The difference is in the crawl graph: internal authority flows to every service and town page instead of being deliberately dammed at the footer or nav.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Since 2019 Google treats nofollow as a hint for crawling but PageRank still does not pass through a nofollowed link, and the blocked equity is lost, not redistributed. Correct tools per goal: keep a page out of the index → `noindex` meta ON the target page; keep it uncrawled → `Disallow:` in robots.txt; sponsored links → `rel="sponsored"`; user-generated links → `rel="ugc"` (the one near-legitimate internal case is `nofollow ugc` on untrusted profile-bio links). Audit: Screaming Frog — Links report, filter Link Type: Internal and Follow: No; or a DOM query filtering same-domain anchors whose rel contains nofollow; watch for blanket `rel="nofollow"` applied template-wide.
- **Reference / source:** https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/seo/nofollow-internal; Google "Qualify your outbound links" and the 2019 evolving-nofollow announcement.
- **Best for:** Internal linking audits on multi-page builds — town/service matrices where every page needs the equity the nav and footer pass.
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL — only bites when a template or plugin has sprayed nofollow internally, but then it taxes the whole site's rankings.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1151⟧
# Skills S1152–S1190 — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills

All 39 entries in this chunk are small checkable rules from the Front-End Checklist (thedaviddias/front-end-checklist), each with a bundled rule.md reference carrying its own Priority / Difficulty / Time, a Check, a Fix and verification steps. The library's own guidance: use these as a final QA sweep or when auditing HTML/CSS/JS/SEO/security details. None of them is a design or motion system — "How it looks" below describes what the visitor (or the search result) actually shows when the rule is followed, and "Frame by frame" is "Static — no motion" except where the rule's subject is itself a rendering/motion behaviour (S1169, S1184, S1190).

Duplicate check: no two skills in this range are the same underlying skill under different names. Two close relations are stated plainly in their entries: **S1188 redirect-chain and S1189 redirect-chains are a companion pair, not duplicates** — S1188 is the server-side rule (flatten multi-hop redirect chains), S1189 is the linking rule (point internal links at final URLs); each source cross-references the other, and both carry full entries. **S1181 preconnect is the narrow single-hint companion of S1175's full resource-hints family** — different scope, full entry, pointer recorded.

## ⟦S1152⟧ noindex-in-sitemap — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills (SEO)
- **What it is:** A crawl-signal audit rule: a URL must never appear in the XML sitemap while also carrying a noindex directive (meta robots or X-Robots-Tag header) — the two signals contradict each other.
- **How it looks:** Nothing visible on the page itself; the effect shows in search coverage — the sitemap lists only canonical, indexable, 200-status URLs, so crawl budget goes to pages meant to rank.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Rule.md priority high · intermediate · 15 min. Decision tree: in sitemap + noindex + want indexed → remove noindex; don't want indexed → remove from sitemap. Sitemap exclusion list: noindexed pages, non-200s (301/404/410), duplicates, admin/login/checkout thank-you pages. Detection via Screaming Frog crawl filtered on the meta-robots column; Next.js pattern: filter `page.noindex` out of `app/sitemap.ts` output.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist rule "Noindex in Sitemap", https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/seo/noindex-in-sitemap; cites Google's sitemap guidance and robots-meta documentation.
- **Best for:** Final QA sweep on any multi-page site; crawl hygiene for towns/areas and service pages. Trade fit: STRONG as a sweep check, though a small trade site rarely hits the conflict.
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL (bites only where sitemap and noindex coexist)
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1152⟧

## ⟦S1153⟧ noscript-tag — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills (HTML)
- **What it is:** A progressive-enhancement rule: JS-dependent features must ship `<noscript>` fallback content, and important content must already exist in the initial HTML rather than appearing only after hydration.
- **How it looks:** With JavaScript disabled or failed, the visitor still sees the real content: navigation fully expanded (the toggle button hidden by a noscript style block), forms that submit normally with a plain-language note about what won't work (no live validation, no character counter), and static gallery grids with numbered pagination links instead of infinite scroll.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. (The rule's own examples gate enhanced widgets behind JS; the no-JS state is the static fallback itself.)
- **Mechanism & key values:** Rule.md priority medium · beginner · 10 min. Prescriptions: alternative content, not just an "Enable JavaScript" message; feature detection over UA sniffing (`'ontouchstart' in window`, `'IntersectionObserver' in window` with a pagination fallback); server and client must render the same critical content to avoid hydration mismatches; noscript CSS pattern `.js-only { display:none }` revealed under a `.js-enabled` class; verify with Puppeteer `setJavaScriptEnabled(false)`.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist rule "Provide noscript fallback content", https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/html/noscript-tag.
- **Best for:** Navigation, forms and work/gallery sections on any homepage — the fallback discipline behind menus, quote forms and galleries. Trade fit: STRONG — a trade homepage whose menu or quote form dies without JS loses enquiries.
- **Tier:** STRONG
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1153⟧

## ⟦S1154⟧ nosnippet — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills (SEO)
- **What it is:** A robots-meta audit rule: important pages must not carry `nosnippet` (or `max-snippet:0`), which suppresses the description shown under the title in search results.
- **How it looks:** In the search result, the page shows title + URL + a 1–2 sentence description the searcher can judge; a nosnippet page shows title and URL with a blank space where the description would be.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Rule.md priority medium · intermediate · 10 min. Directive table: `nosnippet` = no snippet; `max-snippet:0` = same; `max-snippet:N` = snippet capped at N characters; `max-snippet:-1` = unlimited (the recommended explicit allow); `noarchive` hides only the cached copy. Check both the meta robots tag and the X-Robots-Tag header. Legitimate exceptions: legally sensitive or confidential content.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist rule "Avoid nosnippet on important pages", https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/seo/nosnippet; cites Google's robots-meta directive documentation.
- **Best for:** Final QA sweep over hero/landing, service and towns pages that exist to be clicked from search. Trade fit: STRONG as a sweep check.
- **Tier:** STRONG
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1154⟧

## ⟦S1155⟧ object-alt — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills (Accessibility)
- **What it is:** An accessibility rule: every `<object>` element must contain descriptive fallback content inside the tag, serving as the functional equivalent when the embedded resource can't load or render.
- **How it looks:** If an embedded PDF, map or media object fails, the visitor sees a real alternative in its place — e.g. a paragraph with a download link for the PDF, or a fallback image with alt text — instead of an empty box.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Rule.md priority medium · intermediate · 10 min. Fallback goes between the `<object>` open/close tags (plain text or semantic elements, or an `<img>` with alt); screen readers read it when the object itself is inaccessible; crawlers can index it. Verify in the browser accessibility tree plus axe/Lighthouse.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist rule "Provide alternative text for objects", https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/accessibility/object-alt; cites the HTML standard's object element and WCAG non-text content.
- **Best for:** QA sweep wherever embeds are used (PDF brochures, embedded maps on towns/areas or contact sections). Trade fit: SITUATIONAL — only where `<object>` embeds actually appear.
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1155⟧

## ⟦S1156⟧ offline-fallback — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills (Performance)
- **What it is:** A PWA rule: a service worker must pre-cache a self-contained `/offline` page and serve it for failed navigation requests, replacing the browser's generic "No internet connection" screen.
- **How it looks:** Offline, the visitor lands on a branded, centred card — icon, "You're offline" heading, one plain sentence of guidance and a "Try again" button — instead of the browser's unbranded error page. The example page is a white card (max-width 420px, 1rem radius) on a pale background, all styles inline.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. (An optional connectivity banner slides in as a fixed pill at the bottom centre when the connection drops, and shows "Back online" for 3 seconds on reconnect — the only motion the source describes.)
- **Mechanism & key values:** Rule.md priority low · beginner · 20 min. Hard requirements: the offline page makes zero network requests (all CSS/JS/images inline or pre-cached); it is added to the precache list in the service worker `install` event; the fetch handler serves it only for `mode === 'navigate'` requests, network-first with cache fallback; Workbox equivalent: `setCatchHandler` returning the cached `/offline` for document requests. Verification: Lighthouse PWA check "Responds with a 200 when offline".
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist rule "Provide an offline fallback page", https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/performance/offline-fallback; cites web.dev's offline-fallback article and MDN's Service Worker API.
- **Best for:** QA sweep for app-like sites; marginal for a trade homepage. Trade fit: SITUATIONAL — a lead-generation homepage rarely needs offline behaviour.
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1156⟧

## ⟦S1157⟧ offscreen-lazy — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills (Images)
- **What it is:** An image-loading rule: below-the-fold images get native `loading="lazy"`; the LCP image (hero, first product image) must never be lazy-loaded and gets `fetchpriority="high"` instead; every lazy image keeps explicit width/height to prevent layout shift.
- **How it looks:** The page paints fast with the hero in place; gallery and testimonial photos further down simply appear as the visitor scrolls to them, with no content jumping because each image's box is reserved by its dimensions.
- **Frame by frame:** Trigger: scroll. The browser starts downloading each lazy image when it comes within a distance threshold of the viewport — Chromium: ~1250px on a slow connection, ~2500px on a fast one — so the image is ready as it scrolls into view; end state: image rendered in its reserved space, zero layout shift.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Rule.md priority high · beginner · 10 min. `loading="lazy"` goes on the `<img>` inside `<picture>`, never on `<source>`; pair with `decoding="async"`; next/image lazy-loads by default (use its priority prop for the LCP image); legacy IntersectionObserver fallback uses `rootMargin: '200px'`. A finding is only valid when fold position is reasonably certain — the rule itself forbids inventing lazy defects from ambiguous snippets.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist rule "Lazy load offscreen images", https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/images/offscreen-lazy; cites the HTML spec's lazy-loading thresholds.
- **Best for:** Hero discipline (never lazy) plus work/gallery, proof and towns sections (always lazy) on every homepage. Trade fit: STRONG — photo-heavy trade pages are exactly where this pays.
- **Tier:** STRONG
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1157⟧

## ⟦S1158⟧ og-image-size — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills (SEO)
- **What it is:** A social-preview rule: the og:image must be 1200×630 px (1.91:1), referenced by absolute HTTPS URL with matching og:image:width/height tags.
- **How it looks:** When the page is shared, the platform renders a full-width preview card with the image edge-to-edge; a too-small or wrong-ratio image is skipped (blank card) or centre-cropped, cutting off text and subjects.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Rule.md priority medium · beginner · 10 min. Numbers: recommended 1200×630; minimum 600×315 (smaller may not display); file size under 5 MB, under 1 MB preferred; JPEG at 80–85% quality ≈ 100–300 KB, PNG ≈ 300–600 KB; WebP has limited platform support. Platform table in the source: Facebook 1200×630 (min 600×315), LinkedIn 1200×627, Twitter/X summary_large_image 1200×628 (min 300×157, 2:1), Slack/iMessage 1200×630. Verify with the Facebook Sharing Debugger, X card docs and LinkedIn Post Inspector.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist rule "OG Image Size", https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/seo/og-image-size.
- **Best for:** Final QA sweep on every shareable page — homepage, service and towns pages. Trade fit: STRONG — trade work gets shared by link constantly (quotes, previews, recommendations).
- **Tier:** STRONG
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1158⟧

## ⟦S1159⟧ og-tags — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills (SEO)
- **What it is:** A social-metadata rule: every page carries the five core Open Graph tags — og:title, og:description, og:image, og:url, og:type — with absolute HTTPS URLs for image and URL.
- **How it looks:** Shared links render as a proper card (title, description, image) on Facebook, LinkedIn, Slack and messaging apps; without the tags the platform guesses, usually producing a bare or wrong preview.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Rule.md priority medium · intermediate · 10 min. Length caps from the source: og:title ~95 characters, og:description ~200 characters; og:image at least 1200×630; og:type defaults to `website` but should be set explicitly (`article` for posts); og:url must equal the canonical URL exactly. Platforms cache OG data aggressively — refresh via each platform's debugger after a fix.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist rule "Open Graph Tags", https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/seo/og-tags; cites the Open Graph Protocol and Facebook's Sharing Debugger.
- **Best for:** Final QA sweep on all pages. Trade fit: STRONG — pairs with ⟦S1158⟧ (image size) and ⟦S1160⟧ (URL match) as the social-card trio.
- **Tier:** STRONG
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1159⟧

## ⟦S1160⟧ og-url-match — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills (SEO)
- **What it is:** A social-attribution rule: og:url must be character-for-character identical to the `<link rel="canonical">` URL — same protocol, domain, path, query string and trailing slash.
- **How it looks:** Nothing on the page changes; in platform share counts, all shares of a page aggregate onto one URL instead of splitting (the source's example: variants with UTM parameters, bare and www URLs showing 45, 23 and 12 shares separately instead of one count of 80).
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Rule.md priority medium · beginner · 10 min. Strip UTM parameters, session IDs and tracking tokens from og:url; add a canonical tag if none exists and match og:url to it. Bulk-check by exporting both fields from a Screaming Frog crawl, or per-page in the Facebook Sharing Debugger.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist rule "OG URL Match", https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/seo/og-url-match; cites the Open Graph Protocol and Facebook sharing best practices.
- **Best for:** Final QA sweep on all shareable pages. Trade fit: STRONG as a sweep check.
- **Tier:** STRONG
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1160⟧

## ⟦S1161⟧ optimized — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills (Images)
- **What it is:** An image-pipeline rule: every image is compressed and metadata-stripped before deployment — re-encoded at the prescribed quality settings per format, EXIF/IPTC removed, SVGs run through SVGO.
- **How it looks:** Identical pictures on screen; the change is in the bytes — the source's headline example: an 8 MB DSLR JPEG with EXIF becomes under 200 KB with no visible quality difference, and EXIF alone can add 30–60 KB per image.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. (Progressive encoding, prescribed here for JPEG, changes the paint sequence — see ⟦S1184⟧.)
- **Mechanism & key values:** Rule.md priority high · intermediate · 20 min. Settings copied from the source: JPEG mozjpeg quality 80, progressive true; PNG pngquant quality 65–80 (40–80% reduction) or lossless oxipng (10–20%); WebP quality 80; AVIF quality 60, effort 6; SVG via SVGO (remove comments/metadata/editor namespaces; keep viewBox for responsive SVGs). Lighthouse's "Efficiently encode images" audit flags anything reducible by 4 KB+; the source's CI pattern fails builds when an image could shrink by more than 10 KB or still carries metadata.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist rule "Optimise images for faster loading", https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/images/optimized.
- **Best for:** Build-pipeline QA for hero, work/gallery and proof imagery on every homepage. Trade fit: STRONG — trade sites run on phone photos, the worst offenders.
- **Tier:** STRONG
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1161⟧

## ⟦S1162⟧ organization — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills (SEO)
- **What it is:** A structured-data rule: the homepage (and only the homepage) carries an Organization JSON-LD block — name, url, logo as an ImageObject, sameAs social profiles, contactPoint — so Google can populate the brand Knowledge Panel.
- **How it looks:** Nothing on the page itself; in branded search results the Knowledge Panel shows the firm's actual logo, social links and contact details instead of Google's guesses.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Rule.md priority medium · intermediate · 15 min. Required: name, url, logo; logo.url must be an absolute HTTPS URL to a persistent logo file (with width/height in the ImageObject); sameAs should contain at least 2 verified social profiles (Wikipedia/Wikidata where they exist); the block must NOT be duplicated on interior pages. Validate with Google's Rich Results Test.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist rule "Add Organization schema markup", https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/seo/organization.
- **Best for:** Homepage QA sweep; pairs with ⟦S1177⟧ (visible address + LocalBusiness) for local firms. Trade fit: SITUATIONAL — worth adding on a trade homepage, but LocalBusiness schema usually matters more for a local firm than Organization alone.
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1162⟧

## ⟦S1163⟧ orientation — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills (Accessibility)
- **What it is:** A WCAG 1.3.4 rule: all content and controls must work in both portrait and landscape; no orientation locks and no blocking "rotate your device" overlays, unless the activity itself is orientation-essential.
- **How it looks:** The visitor rotates the phone or tablet and the layout reflows — columns stack or wrap, navigation, forms and submit buttons all stay reachable; nothing disappears and no rotate-device wall covers the page.
- **Frame by frame:** Trigger: device rotation. The responsive layout re-wraps into the new aspect (the source's example: a checkout grid goes single-column, widening to a 2fr/1fr split at 768px, panels using min-width:0 so they wrap instead of vanishing) → end state: every core task still completable.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Rule.md priority high · intermediate · 20 min. Banned: `screen.orientation.lock()` without a task-specific reason, JS that replaces the body with a rotate message, fixed heights/widths that collapse after rotation. Accepted essential exceptions in the source: a piano-keyboard app, a check-deposit camera flow, fixed-orientation hardware. Non-blocking orientation hints are fine. Verify on phone and tablet viewports in both orientations, including with zoom/large text.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist rule "Support both portrait and landscape orientation", https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/accessibility/orientation; cites WCAG 1.3.4 Orientation and its Understanding document.
- **Best for:** Mobile QA sweep for every section — heroes, forms, dashboards. Trade fit: STRONG — trade customers browse on phones in every posture, including mounted devices.
- **Tier:** STRONG
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1163⟧

## ⟦S1164⟧ orphan-pages — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills (SEO)
- **What it is:** A site-architecture rule: every important page needs inbound internal links; a page reachable only via the sitemap is an orphan that receives no PageRank and is rarely recrawled.
- **How it looks:** Nothing changes visually on the orphan page itself; it becomes reachable through ordinary reading — a contextual link inside a related article's body copy, a related-articles section, or its category listing.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Rule.md priority medium · intermediate · 20 min. Fix pattern: for each orphan, add contextual links from 2–5 relevant existing pages with descriptive anchor text matching the target's primary keyword (the quick reference floor is at least one link). Detection: Screaming Frog Reports → Orphan Pages, log-file analysis, or Search Console "Discovered – currently not indexed". Prevention workflow: on publishing, link from 3 existing related pages and add to the category/archive listing. Triage: fix important content; ignore thank-you/campaign pages; noindex intentional utilities.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist rule "Add internal links to orphan pages", https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/seo/orphan-pages; cites Google's crawlable-links guidance.
- **Best for:** QA sweep on larger sites — service pages and towns/areas pages are the classic orphans. Trade fit: SITUATIONAL — a 5-page trade site has none; a 24-town build can grow them fast.
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1164⟧

## ⟦S1165⟧ page-load-time — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills (Performance)
- **What it is:** A performance rule: the page must fully load in under 3 seconds on a standard connection, audited against the source's metric thresholds.
- **How it looks:** The visitor sees content almost immediately and can interact without waiting; the source's impact table is the cost of failing: bounce ~9% at 1–2s, ~13% at 2–3s, ~25% at 3–5s, ~38% at 5–10s, ~50%+ beyond 10s; 53% of mobile users abandon a site slower than 3 seconds.
- **Frame by frame:** The load sequence the rule budgets, with the source's Good thresholds: DNS/TCP setup → Time to First Byte < 200ms → First Contentful Paint < 1.8s → Largest Contentful Paint < 2.5s → Time to Interactive < 3.8s → full load < 3s. ("Needs work" ceilings: TTFB < 500ms, FCP < 3s, LCP < 4s, TTI < 7.3s, load < 5s.)
- **Mechanism & key values:** Rule.md priority high · intermediate · 30 min. Levers named: preconnect/preload critical assets, inline critical CSS, defer/async scripts, image optimisation, compression plus immutable static caching (`maxAge: '1y'`), code splitting and memoisation in React. Measure with Lighthouse on throttled 3G, WebPageTest, PageSpeed Insights field data, and RUM.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist rule "Keep page load time under 3 seconds", https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/performance/page-load-time.
- **Best for:** Whole-homepage QA gate — every section's weight and motion budget answers to this. Trade fit: STRONG.
- **Tier:** STRONG
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1165⟧

## ⟦S1166⟧ page-weight — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills (Performance)
- **What it is:** A weight-budget rule: total page weight under 1500 KB maximum, under 500 KB as the working target, with per-resource budgets by type.
- **How it looks:** Nothing directly visible; the felt effect is load speed on mobile — the source notes a 1.5 MB page takes 3–5 seconds on 4G.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Rule.md priority high · beginner · 20 min. Budget table copied from the source (Target / Acceptable / Poor): total < 500 / < 1500 / > 1500 KB; HTML < 50 / < 100 / > 100 KB; CSS < 50 / < 100 / > 100 KB; JavaScript < 200 / < 400 / > 400 KB; images < 200 / < 500 / > 500 KB; fonts < 100 / < 200 / > 200 KB. Typical breakdown: images 50–70% of weight, JS 15–25%, CSS 5–10%, fonts 5–10%, HTML 2–5%. Lighthouse budget.json pattern in the source: total 500, script 200, image 200, stylesheet 50, font 100 (KB). Enforcement: budgets in CI plus RUM monitoring.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist rule "Keep page weight under 1500KB", https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/performance/page-weight.
- **Best for:** Whole-page QA gate, set before choosing hero media and gallery density. Trade fit: STRONG — the single-file immersive builds this bank produces need an explicit weight ceiling.
- **Tier:** STRONG
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1166⟧

## ⟦S1167⟧ pagination — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills (SEO)
- **What it is:** A canonicalisation rule for paginated series: each paginated page self-canonicalizes; canonicalizing pages 2+ to page 1 tells Google they are duplicates and stops them being indexed.
- **How it looks:** Nothing visible on the page; in search, products or posts that exist only on page 3 of a listing become findable instead of unreachable.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Rule.md priority medium · intermediate · 15 min. Rules copied from the source: one URL pattern only (`?page=2` or `/page/2`, never both); Google dropped rel=prev/next in March 2019 — do not rely on it; infinite scroll / load-more UIs must still expose crawlable paginated URLs or fallback links; indexing strategy — page 1 always index, pages 2–5 index if unique, pages 6+ consider noindex, filtered variants usually noindex + canonical to base. Trap flagged: some CMS themes auto-noindex all paginated pages.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist rule "Use canonicals on paginated pages", https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/seo/pagination; cites Google's pagination and duplicate-consolidation guidance.
- **Best for:** QA sweep on listing-heavy sites (work galleries, blog archives). Trade fit: SITUATIONAL — most trade homepages don't paginate; matters when a work/gallery archive does.
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1167⟧

## ⟦S1168⟧ pagination-accessibility — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills (HTML)
- **What it is:** An accessibility rule for pagination controls: a `<nav aria-label="Pagination">` landmark, `aria-current="page"` on the current page, descriptive labels on every control, and live-region announcements when content changes without a reload.
- **How it looks:** A row of numbered buttons with Previous/Next at the ends; the current page is filled in the accent colour and announced to screen readers as "Page 2, current page"; in the source's CSS the buttons are 2.5rem squares with a visible focus outline, and at ≤640px the numbers hide, leaving Previous/Next.
- **Frame by frame:** Trigger: activating a page control. Content swaps → an aria-live="polite" region announces "Page N of M" (and "Showing X to Y of Z results" where a size selector exists) → end state: the new page's control carries aria-current and the current-page styling.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Rule.md priority medium · beginner · 20 min. Requirements table from the source: container = nav + aria-label; current page = aria-current="page"; every link labelled ("Go to page 3", "Page 2, current page"); ellipses marked aria-hidden; all controls keyboard-focusable with disabled state on first/last page; page-size options in the example component: 10/25/50/100. Companion to ⟦S1167⟧ (the SEO half of pagination).
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist rule "Make pagination accessible", https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/html/pagination-accessibility.
- **Best for:** Work/gallery or archive pagination wherever it exists. Trade fit: SITUATIONAL — only where pagination exists, but mandatory there.
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1168⟧

## ⟦S1169⟧ parallax-effects — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills (Accessibility)
- **What it is:** A motion-safety rule for parallax: background/foreground differential movement must be disabled when the visitor prefers reduced motion, must have a static fallback conveying the same content, and should have a site-wide user toggle.
- **How it looks:** With motion allowed, the hero background drifts slower than the foreground content as the visitor scrolls (the classic fixed-attachment or translateZ depth effect). With reduced motion set, the same hero is simply static — background scrolls normally with the page, all content readable, layout unchanged.
- **Frame by frame:** Trigger: scroll, with prefers-reduced-motion unset → layers move at different speeds, creating the depth mismatch the rule exists to govern. With `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` → no differential movement at any scroll position; end state identical content, zero parallax.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Rule.md priority medium · intermediate · 20 min. Prescribed pattern: default `background-attachment: scroll`; parallax only inside `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)`; JS implementations must check `matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)')` and listen for changes; the source's React component default parallax speed is 0.5; the user-toggle kill switch sets animation/transition durations to 0.01ms and removes transforms. Rationale: the eye/inner-ear depth mismatch triggers dizziness, nausea and vertigo in vestibular disorders. Companion to ⟦S1190⟧ (the general reduced-motion rule).
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist rule "Provide alternatives to parallax effects", https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/accessibility/parallax-effects.
- **Best for:** Hero and layered-background sections — a hard gate on any parallax design taken from this bank. Trade fit: STRONG as a constraint on hero builds (the bank's parallax heroes must ship this fallback), SITUATIONAL as a standalone pick.
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1169⟧

## ⟦S1170⟧ parameters — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills (SEO)
- **What it is:** A URL-hygiene rule: parameterized URLs must carry canonical tags that consolidate variants, so filters, sorts and tracking parameters don't mint thousands of duplicate URLs that waste crawl budget and split PageRank.
- **How it looks:** Nothing visible on the page; in the crawl, one canonical listing page instead of a swarm of `?color=red&size=large&sort=price&utm_source=…` variants.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Rule.md priority medium · intermediate · 15 min. Category table from the source: tracking (utm_*, fbclid, gclid, ref) and session (sessionid, sid, PHPSESSID) — always strip from canonicals; filtering and sorting — canonicalize to the base URL (or self-canonicalize if genuinely indexable); pagination — self-canonicalize; search results — usually `noindex, follow`. Audit trigger: URLs with 3+ parameters get reviewed for crawl waste. Note in the source: Google's URL Parameters tool was removed — canonical tags are now the mechanism.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist rule "Limit unnecessary URL parameters", https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/seo/parameters; cites Google's URL-parameter and duplicate-consolidation guidance.
- **Best for:** QA sweep on filtered/sorted listings. Trade fit: SITUATIONAL — a trade homepage has few parameters; matters for galleries with filters and any tracked campaign URLs.
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1170⟧

## ⟦S1171⟧ password-field-security — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills (Security)
- **What it is:** A form-security rule: password fields use `type="password"` with the correct autocomplete token, an accessible show/hide toggle, and a strength indicator with stated requirements — and work with password managers rather than against them.
- **How it looks:** A labelled password box with an eye toggle button at its right edge (aria-pressed, announced as "Show password"/"Hide password"); under it, a thin strength bar that fills and changes colour (red → orange → yellow → light green → green across scores 0–4) with a checklist of requirements ticking off as they are met.
- **Frame by frame:** Trigger: typing. The strength meter recomputes live (bar width steps in 20% increments per score point, 0.3s width/colour transition) and the requirements list flips items from unmet to met; trigger: toggle click → the field switches between masked and plain text. End state: a submittable form whose errors are tied to fields via aria-describedby and role="alert".
- **Mechanism & key values:** Rule.md priority high · intermediate · 30 min. Values from the source: `autocomplete="current-password"` for login, `"new-password"` for registration; example minlength 8 (login) and 12 (registration) with the best-practice table setting minimum length at 12 characters with uppercase, lowercase and numbers; strength requirements = ≥12 chars, lower, upper, digit, special; hashing with bcrypt/Argon2/scrypt; breach screening via the Have I Been Pwned range API (k-anonymity: only the first 5 hex characters of the SHA-1 are sent). Test in 1Password, LastPass and Bitwarden.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist rule "Secure password input fields", https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/security/password-field-security.
- **Best for:** Login/registration forms only. Trade fit: NOT-FOR-TRADES — a trade lead-generation homepage has no passwords; relevant only if a client portal is ever built.
- **Tier:** NOT-FOR-TRADES
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1171⟧

## ⟦S1172⟧ paste-inputs — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills (Accessibility)
- **What it is:** A forms rule: never block pasting into any input — remove `onpaste="return false"` and any paste-event preventDefault, especially on password, card and long-string fields.
- **How it looks:** Nothing distinctive on screen; the visitor (or their password manager) pastes an email, IBAN, tracking number or generated password straight into the field instead of typing it character by character.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Rule.md priority medium · intermediate · 10 min. Audit = search the codebase for paste handlers and onpaste attributes; fix = delete them (default browser behaviour is the correct behaviour). Grounded in WCAG 2.2's accessible-authentication requirement: blocking paste blocks password managers and motor-impaired users who rely on copy-paste.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist rule "Allow pasting into form inputs", https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/accessibility/paste-inputs; cites WCAG accessible authentication and MDN's paste event.
- **Best for:** Forms QA sweep — quote and contact forms. Trade fit: SITUATIONAL — quote forms rarely block paste, but the check costs nothing and a blocked paste on a form field is a conversion leak.
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1172⟧

## ⟦S1173⟧ pdf-size — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills (SEO)
- **What it is:** A document-delivery rule (titled "Keep linked PDFs under 60 MB"): linked PDFs must stay small enough for Googlebot to download and fully index, with an HTML companion page for important content.
- **How it looks:** Nothing on the page changes; the effect is that a linked brochure/report's full text can appear in search instead of being silently truncated or skipped.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Rule.md priority medium · intermediate · 15 min. Thresholds copied from the source: under 5 MB ideal; 5–15 MB acceptable, consider compressing; 15–60 MB at risk of partial indexing; over 60 MB likely skipped. Audit flags: HEAD-request Content-Length over 10,485,760 bytes (10 MB) → compress; over 15,728,640 bytes (15 MB) → at risk of truncation (the rule's Check section works to the 10/15 MB flags even though the headline limit is 60 MB). Compression: Ghostscript `PDFSETTINGS` presets /screen 72dpi, /ebook 150dpi, /printer 300dpi, /prepress 300dpi+; strip embedded fonts/images/metadata; PDFs must not be password-protected or un-OCR'd scans.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist rule "Keep linked PDFs under 60 MB", https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/seo/pdf-size.
- **Best for:** QA sweep wherever PDFs are linked (brochures, guarantees, spec sheets). Trade fit: SITUATIONAL — relevant when a trade site links warranty or product PDFs meant to be found.
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1173⟧

## ⟦S1174⟧ performance-budget — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills (Testing)
- **What it is:** A process rule: explicit performance budgets (bundle sizes, Lighthouse scores, Web Vitals) are defined in version control and enforced in CI so a pull request that blows the budget fails the build.
- **How it looks:** Nothing visitor-facing; the visible artefact is a red CI check on the offending PR — "this PR added 200 KB to the bundle" caught in review instead of after user complaints.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Rule.md priority medium · intermediate · 25 min. Worked values from the source: size-limit example — main bundle 200 kB, CSS 30 kB, vendor chunk 150 kB (all gzip); Lighthouse CI assertions — performance ≥ 0.8 (error), accessibility ≥ 0.9 (error), FCP ≤ 2000ms (warn), LCP ≤ 2500ms (error), TBT ≤ 300ms (error), CLS ≤ 0.1 (error); Lighthouse budget.json — script 250, image 500, total 1600 (KB); Vite chunkSizeWarningLimit 500 KB. Starting-threshold table: main JS (gzip) good < 150 KB, needs work > 300 KB; total JS good < 400 KB, > 800 KB; TBT good < 200ms, > 600ms; CLS good < 0.1, > 0.25. RUM alerting completes the loop: LCP p75 above 2.5s for 3 consecutive deploy windows, INP p75 above 200ms, CLS p75 above 0.1. Method: start loose, tighten progressively, review quarterly.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist rule "Enforce performance budgets in CI", https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/testing/performance-budget.
- **Best for:** Build-process QA behind ⟦S1165⟧/⟦S1166⟧ (the budgets those rules set, enforced automatically). Trade fit: SITUATIONAL — a one-file build has no CI, but the thresholds transfer directly as manual release checks.
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1174⟧

## ⟦S1175⟧ performance-resource-hints — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills (Performance)
- **What it is:** A loading rule covering the four resource hints — preload (current-route critical assets), prefetch (likely next navigation), preconnect (origins needed immediately), dns-prefetch (lower-confidence origins) — each used only within its stated limits.
- **How it looks:** Nothing visibly different in the design; the felt effect is the hero and fonts arriving sooner — the source claims 100–300ms average LCP improvement when hints are aimed correctly, and warns a wrong hint is worse than none.
- **Frame by frame:** The load sequence the hints reorder: page request → DNS/TCP/TLS for preconnected origins and downloads of preloaded assets start immediately, in parallel with HTML parsing, instead of when the parser/CSS discovers them → first paint and LCP land earlier; prefetched next-page assets sit idle in cache until a navigation uses them.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Rule.md priority high · intermediate · 20 min. Practical limits from the source's decision table: preload ≤ 3–5 per route, current route only; preconnect ≤ 2–4 origins, only ones definitely used soon (fonts, media CDN, APIs); dns-prefetch as the lightweight fallback for speculative vendors; prefetch only the next most likely navigation. Anti-patterns: preloading future-route or widget assets, prefetching the current page, forgetting `as`/`crossorigin` (causes duplicate requests). Verify in the network waterfall and on a throttled mobile profile. ⟦S1181⟧ is this family's preconnect-only companion rule.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist rule "Use resource hints for faster loading", https://frontendchecklist.io/en/rules/performance/performance-resource-hints; cites web.dev performance guidance and Patterns.dev.
- **Best for:** Hero (preload the LCP image/font) and whole-page loading QA. Trade fit: STRONG — a disciplined 3–5 preloads is exactly what an image-led trade hero needs.
- **Tier:** STRONG
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1175⟧

## ⟦S1176⟧ permissions-policy — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills (Security)
- **What it is:** A hardening rule: the server sends a Permissions-Policy header disabling every browser feature the site doesn't use (camera, microphone, geolocation, payment, USB…), shrinking what an XSS or a rogue embed can reach.
- **How it looks:** Nothing visible on the page; the effect appears only when something tries to call a denied API — the browser refuses (e.g. a compromised script cannot silently open the camera or microphone).
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Rule.md priority medium · intermediate · 15 min. Syntax: `feature=()` denies all origins, `(self)` same-origin only, quoted origins for named third parties, `*` permissive (avoid). Recommended baseline from the source: `Permissions-Policy: camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=(), payment=(), usb=(), interest-cohort=()` — the last directive opts out of the deprecated FLoC API. Iframes inherit the page policy unless the `allow` attribute grants specific features. The old Feature-Policy header/syntax is deprecated — do not use it. Verify against the live production response headers, not just config.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist rule "Set a Permissions-Policy header", https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/security/permissions-policy; cites MDN, the W3C Permissions Policy spec and OWASP's headers cheat sheet.
- **Best for:** Server/hosting QA sweep for the whole site. Trade fit: SITUATIONAL — a one-line header on the host; worth setting, invisible when right.
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1176⟧

## ⟦S1177⟧ physical-address — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills (SEO)
- **What it is:** A local-trust rule: the business's complete physical address is visibly displayed — contact page and footer — wrapped in an `<address>` element and matching the LocalBusiness schema and Google Business Profile exactly.
- **How it looks:** In the footer of every page and on the contact page: the business name in bold, then street, city, region, postcode and country on separate lines, with tappable phone and email links under it — instead of a vague "Springfield area" line in a plain div.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Rule.md priority medium · beginner · 10 min. Completeness check: street number and name, city, state/region, postal code, country. Placement table: contact page required; footer strongly recommended; About page recommended; LocalBusiness schema required. Consistency law: the on-page address must match the GBP and JSON-LD character-for-character in format — even "St." vs "Street" differences erode local ranking confidence. Legal notes: address display is required under the EU e-Commerce Directive, the UK Electronic Commerce Regulations 2002, and for regulated US industries; use the registered address, not a PO Box. The source's exception matters for trades: service-area businesses use service-area guidance instead, and an address must never be invented to satisfy the rule.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist rule "Display a physical business address", https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/seo/physical-address.
- **Best for:** Footer and contact sections — a core local-SEO and trust element for trade firms. Trade fit: STRONG — name/address/phone consistency is foundational for a local trades homepage.
- **Tier:** STRONG
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1177⟧

## ⟦S1178⟧ picture-element — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills (Images)
- **What it is:** An image-markup rule: every `<picture>` element must end with an `<img>` as its last child — the required fallback that also carries alt, width, height, loading and fetchpriority — with typed `<source>` elements before it.
- **How it looks:** The visitor's browser picks the best format it supports (AVIF first, then WebP, then the JPEG fallback) or the right crop for the viewport (the source's art-direction example: a square crop on mobile ≤480px, 4:3 on tablet ≤1024px, a wide 16:9 banner on desktop) — the picture simply always renders; a `<picture>` with no `<img>` renders nothing at all where no source matches.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. (Selection happens once at parse: sources are evaluated top-to-bottom and the first match wins.)
- **Mechanism & key values:** Rule.md priority high · beginner · 10 min. Compression figures from the source: AVIF ~40–50% smaller than JPEG, WebP ~25–35% smaller. Order law: most-preferred format first (AVIF before WebP — reversing them silently serves WebP to AVIF-capable browsers). Attributes on `<source>` are ignored — alt/loading/fetchpriority/decoding/width/height belong on the `<img>`. The `<img>` src should be a universally supported format (JPEG/PNG). A missing `<img>` child is a W3C validation error; `<picture>` works with JavaScript disabled.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist rule "Use <picture> with an <img> fallback", https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/images/picture-element; cites MDN responsive images and web.dev image performance.
- **Best for:** Hero and work/gallery imagery — the standard responsive-image pattern for photo-led trade pages. Trade fit: STRONG.
- **Tier:** STRONG
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1178⟧

## ⟦S1179⟧ plain-language — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills (Accessibility)
- **What it is:** A content rule: page copy is written in plain language — short sentences, common words, active voice, technical terms defined on first use — targeted at roughly an 8th-grade reading level for general audiences.
- **How it looks:** Short scannable paragraphs and numbered steps instead of walls of text: "Complete the form, then click Submit" instead of "The form should be completed by the user before submission can be processed"; error messages that say "Your password is incorrect. Please try again" instead of credential-verification jargon.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Rule.md priority medium · beginner · 20 min. Numbers from the source: avoid sentences of 30+ words, write 15–20-word sentences (its checker flags anything over 25); paragraphs of 2–4 sentences; spell out acronyms on first use; lists for 3+ items; action verbs first in instructions ("Click", "Enter", "Select"); most important information first. Verify with Hemingway Editor / readable.com and by reading aloud.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist rule "Write in plain language", https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/accessibility/plain-language.
- **Best for:** All homepage copy — hero lines, process steps, form labels and error text. Trade fit: STRONG — trade customers are busy, stressed (a leak, a breakdown) and often reading on a phone; pairs with ⟦S1187⟧ (the SEO reading-level twin).
- **Tier:** STRONG
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1179⟧

## ⟦S1180⟧ pluralization — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills (i18n)
- **What it is:** An internationalisation rule: count-bearing strings must select their grammatical form via Intl.PluralRules or ICU MessageFormat so every CLDR plural category of every target locale is covered — never string concatenation or a binary singular/plural branch.
- **How it looks:** Correct grammar in every locale: Russian renders "1 элемент / 3 элемента / 11 элементов / 21 элемент" from one message key; Arabic gets all six of its forms; an English-only binary branch would print the wrong form for five of Arabic's six categories.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Rule.md priority medium · intermediate · 25 min. CLDR categories: zero, one, two, few, many, other. Counts by language from the source's table: English and German 2 forms (one/other), French one covers 0 and 1, Russian one/few/many/other, Polish one/few/many/other, Arabic all six, Japanese other only. Implementation: `new Intl.PluralRules(locale).select(count)` (cache instances per locale — constructing per call is expensive), ICU syntax `{count, plural, one {…} other {…}}` in react-intl, or i18next suffixed keys (`_zero _one _two _few _many _other`); a missing key silently falls back to `other` and ships wrong grammar — validate plural-key completeness in CI. Ordinals use `type: 'ordinal'`.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist rule "Handle plural forms with Intl.PluralRules or ICU MessageFormat", https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/i18n/pluralization; cites MDN Intl.PluralRules and the Unicode CLDR plural rules.
- **Best for:** Multilingual product UIs only. Trade fit: NOT-FOR-TRADES — trade homepages in this bank are single-locale English with no count-driven strings.
- **Tier:** NOT-FOR-TRADES
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1180⟧

## ⟦S1181⟧ preconnect — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills (Performance)
- **What it is:** The preconnect-only companion to ⟦S1175⟧: add `<link rel="preconnect">` for the few third-party origins the page will definitely use immediately (fonts, hero-media CDN, APIs), and remove it everywhere else.
- **How it looks:** Nothing visible in the design; the felt effect is third-party assets (webfonts, CDN images) starting sooner because DNS lookup, TCP handshake and TLS negotiation already finished before the request was made — the source puts the saving at hundreds of milliseconds on the critical path.
- **Frame by frame:** Page request → connection setup for the preconnected origins runs in parallel with HTML delivery → when the font/CDN request is issued, it goes straight onto the warm connection instead of paying setup latency first.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Rule.md priority medium · intermediate · 10 min. Limits copied from the source: keep preconnects to roughly 2–4 high-value origins per page; include `crossorigin` for fonts and other CORS-fetched assets; use `dns-prefetch` instead for origins that are probable but not guaranteed (analytics, chat); never preconnect origins used only after interaction. Verify in Lighthouse ("preconnect-to-required-origins") and the WebPageTest waterfall.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist rule "Use preconnect for critical third-party origins", https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/performance/preconnect; cites web.dev performance guidance and Lighthouse documentation.
- **Best for:** Head-level loading QA on any homepage using external fonts or a CDN. Trade fit: STRONG — one or two preconnects (font origin, image CDN) is the standard trade-hero setup; the full hint family is ⟦S1175⟧.
- **Tier:** STRONG
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1181⟧

## ⟦S1182⟧ privacy-policy — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills (Privacy)
- **What it is:** A legal-presence rule: a "Privacy Policy" link sits in the footer of every page, leading to a real policy page that states what data is collected, why, who receives it, how long it is kept (including analytics, logs and monitoring), and how users exercise their rights.
- **How it looks:** The footer carries a clearly labelled "Privacy Policy" link (commonly beside Terms of Service and Cookie Policy) on every page — not buried in a "Legal" dropdown; the policy itself is a stable, crawlable page in plain language.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Rule.md priority high · beginner · 15 min. Required contents follow GDPR Article 13: controller identity and contact, DPO if required, data collected, purpose, legal basis, retention period, third-party sharing, international transfers, user rights, withdrawal of consent, and the supervisory-authority complaint route. Required wherever any personal data is collected — emails, names, IP addresses (even in server logs), cookies, payment data, analytics. Additional placements: signup and contact forms (before collection), the cookie banner (which links to the policy — banner and policy are different things, both required), marketing emails, login pages. Expected URL paths: /privacy, /privacy-policy or /legal/privacy — never a modal or an anchor on another page.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist rule "Link to your privacy policy in the footer", https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/privacy/privacy-policy; cites GDPR Article 13 and the CCPA.
- **Best for:** Footer — a standing element of every homepage build, next to the address (⟦S1177⟧). Trade fit: STRONG — any trade site with a quote form or analytics collects personal data and needs this.
- **Tier:** STRONG
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1182⟧

## ⟦S1183⟧ product — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills (SEO)
- **What it is:** A structured-data rule for e-commerce: every product page carries Product JSON-LD (name, image, description, offers with price, priceCurrency and availability) so Google can show price, stock and star ratings in the result.
- **How it looks:** Nothing on the page itself; in search results the listing gains a price, an In Stock line and a star rating with review count under the title instead of a plain blue link.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Rule.md priority medium · intermediate · 20 min. Required for rich results: name, image (absolute-URL array), description, offers.price (numeric), offers.priceCurrency (ISO 4217 code), offers.availability (a schema.org URL — InStock, OutOfStock, PreOrder, BackOrder, Discontinued). Recommended: aggregateRating, brand, sku, gtin/mpn, priceValidUntil. Hard laws from the source: the schema price must exactly match the visible page price, and AggregateRating may only be used with genuine reviews — mismatches risk a manual action and loss of rich-result eligibility. Validate with the Rich Results Test.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist rule "Add Product schema markup", https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/seo/product; cites Google's product structured-data guide and Schema.org Product.
- **Best for:** E-commerce product pages only. Trade fit: NOT-FOR-TRADES — trade homepages sell services, not products; the equivalent that matters here is LocalBusiness/service schema, not Product.
- **Tier:** NOT-FOR-TRADES
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1183⟧

## ⟦S1184⟧ progressive-jpeg — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills (Images)
- **What it is:** An image-encoding rule: JPEGs are saved in progressive (interlaced) format rather than baseline, so they render as a full-frame blurry preview that sharpens over successive passes.
- **How it looks:** A large photo (typically the hero) appears almost immediately as a soft, low-quality version of the whole image, then refines to full sharpness in a few passes — instead of a baseline JPEG painting in line by line from the top, leaving the lower half blank until late.
- **Frame by frame:** Trigger: image download begins → pass 1 paints the entire frame at low fidelity → each subsequent pass adds detail across the whole frame → end state: full-quality image, at a file size similar to (sometimes slightly smaller than) the baseline equivalent.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Rule.md priority low · beginner · 10 min. Detection: the progressive marker byte pair 0xFF 0xC2 in the file, or `identify -verbose` reporting "Interlace: JPEG". Conversion: ImageMagick `-interlace JPEG`; Sharp `.jpeg({ progressive: true, quality: 80, mozjpeg: true })`; CDN switches — Cloudinary `fl_progressive`, Imgix `fm=pjpg`. Guidance table from the source: large heroes and above-the-fold images — use progressive; small thumbnails — baseline is fine; where WebP/AVIF are served, progressive JPEG matters only as the fallback.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist rule "Use progressive JPEG encoding", https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/images/progressive-jpeg; cites MDN responsive images and web.dev image performance.
- **Best for:** Hero image delivery (as the JPEG fallback inside ⟦S1178⟧ picture stacks; the encoding itself is prescribed by ⟦S1161⟧). Trade fit: SITUATIONAL — a free perceived-speed win on the hero, minor elsewhere.
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1184⟧

## ⟦S1185⟧ pwa-installability — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills (HTML)
- **What it is:** A PWA checklist rule: the site meets the browser's installability criteria — HTTPS, a valid web app manifest, a registered service worker with a fetch handler, and correctly sized icons including a maskable variant.
- **How it looks:** The browser shows an install affordance (address-bar button/prompt); once installed, the app opens in its own window without browser chrome (display: standalone) with the firm's icon on the home screen, the icon clipped cleanly to Android's shape because the maskable art fills its canvas.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. (Install flow: `beforeinstallprompt` fires when criteria are met → the app defers it and shows its own install button at a chosen moment → prompt → accepted/dismissed outcome; iOS Safari has no such event — Share → "Add to Home Screen" is the manual path.)
- **Mechanism & key values:** Rule.md priority low · intermediate · 30 min. Manifest minimums from the source: name or short_name, start_url, display, and icons of at least 192×192 and 512×512 PNG, plus a 512×512 maskable; maskable safe zone = a circle of radius 40% of the icon's smallest dimension (204px radius centred on a 512 icon) — keep the logo inside it. Service worker must respond with a 200 when offline (pairs with ⟦S1156⟧). Display modes: standalone (most app-like), minimal-ui, fullscreen, browser (not "installed"). The source's engagement claim: installed users spend 3× more time in the app on average. Verify in DevTools → Application → Manifest and a Lighthouse PWA audit.
- **Reference / source:** Front-End Checklist rule "Meet PWA installability criteria", https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/html/pwa-installability.
- **Best for:** App-like web products. Trade fit: NOT-FOR-TRADES — a trade homepage's goal is a phone call or quote form, not home-screen installation.
- **Tier:** NOT-FOR-TRADES
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1185⟧

## ⟦S1186⟧ quality — Part 20 — MCP Market — Front-End Checklist rule-skills (SEO)
- **What it is:** A content-quality rule: every page that wants organic traffic must demonstrate E-E-A-T and fully satisfy its search intent — specific, evidenced, first-hand content with a named, credentialed author — because low-quality content is suppressed site-wide, not just per page.
- **How it looks:** A page that reads like it was written by someone who did the work: concrete numbers and steps (the source's "after" example names starter feeding, 12–18 hour fermentation, hydration ratios and six years of the author's own baking), visible publication/updated dates, cited sources, and a byline — instead of three generic sentences that could belong to any business.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Rule.md priority high · intermediate · 30 min. Thin-content red flags copied from the source: under 300 words for an informational page; text that could apply to any business ("We deliver quality service"); templated variable-substitution copy; content paraphrased from a single source; multiple near-identical pages on one topic. The E-E-A-T signals table: Experience = personal stories, original photos, case studies; Expertise = credentials, depth, accuracy; Authoritativeness = backlinks, mentions, reputation; Trustworthiness = cited sources, corrections policy, accurate claims. Google's five self-assessment questions are reproduced in the source (original information? substantial and complete? insightful beyond the obvious? would you stand behind creating it? made for people, not engines?). Exceptions recorded: utility/compliance pages may be brief; AI-assisted drafting is not itself a failure — unsupported claims and no editorial review are.
