## ⟦S1301⟧ ideagram — Part 22 — User's installed catalog (MengTo, Owl-Listener designer-skills, ConardLi, tastemaker, elayadesign)
- **What it is:** Turns a concept, feature description, blog post or pitch into ONE on-brand illustration by matching it to a real unDraw illustration held in a local library and recoloring it to the brand accent — never by hand-drawing SVG paths. A second, non-default path generates an original illustration with an image model under a strict style system when such a tool exists and the library has no match.
- **How it looks:** A flat, modern editorial illustration in the unDraw/Storyset register, built as a scene rather than a floating subject: a calm, low-contrast background shape or suggested environment; a midground device or object (screen, chart, control panel) carrying the single saturated brand accent; a proportioned character (roughly 7–8 heads tall, relaxed pose, simple face) in the foreground performing the core action on that object; a soft ground shadow and one or two sparse decorative details. Palette is restrained neutrals (off-white, greys, charcoal) plus natural skin tones and exactly ONE accent colour, which is the loudest thing in the frame and marks the single focal point. The subject fills about 50–65% of the frame with at least ~35% calm whitespace. The fallback primitive style is stricter still: exactly two colours (near-black base `#262631` + one accent), flat fills only, no gradients, shadows or bevels, rounded corners on human-made objects, circles/capsules for organic forms.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. The deliverable is a still SVG (or a PNG exported from it).
- **Mechanism & key values:** Local library at `~/.ideagram/undraw/` (20–30 downloaded unDraw SVGs spanning common themes covers most requests); `scripts/build_library_index.py` writes `index.md`/`index.json` for matching; matching is by scene/metaphor, not loose keyword overlap. `scripts/recolor_undraw.py --accent "#<hex>"` swaps only unDraw's `#6c63ff` accent family, leaving skin, ink and neutrals untouched; a flagged secondary accent (green `#8ed16f`, pink `#ff6584`) can be remapped with `--also "#8ed16f:#<hex>"`; recoloring always restarts from the original file because the script only remaps `#6c63ff` outward. Scene composition reuses WHOLE components only (`scripts/extract_component.py`, placed with `<g transform="translate() scale()">`, bounds measured with `getBBox()`; mirroring via `scale(-1,1)` to make figures face each other); grafting sub-limbs between figures is explicitly fragile and avoided. `scripts/validate_assets.py` checks the SVG parses; `scripts/export_png.py` (needs cairosvg + system cairo) exports raster sizes. Real unDraw palette values recorded in the anatomy reference: ink `#090814`, accent `#6c63ff`, light grey `#e6e6e6`, dark clothing/hair `#3f3d56`/`#3f3d58`/`#2f2e41`, shading done by layering black at opacity 0.05–0.2 rather than extra hexes. Fallback style contract: two colours only, base `#262631`, accent default `#6C5CE7`, primitives built on a `400 400` viewBox; multiple same-kind actors are distinguished by fill-vs-outline, never a third colour. Generation path: 7 composition structures (hero scene, before/after, character state, concept metaphor, workflow/flow, layers/stack, journey/path), a 3-step fresh-metaphor recipe (concept → physical action → low-key concrete object → character performs the action), a prompt template restating the full style DNA in every call, and an 11-point QA checklist (one idea/one focal point, character earned its place, scene not floating object, palette discipline, ≥~35% whitespace, no deformed hands/faces, ≤3 short label words, metaphor not the first cliché).
- **Reference / source:** unDraw — undraw.co/illustrations (free, no attribution; illustrator Katerina Limpitsouni named in the anatomy reference); Storyset named as the sibling style register; Streamline (streamlinehq.com/illustrations) named only as a manual escape hatch. Bundled references: `references/undraw-anatomy.md`, `references/style-contract.md`, `references/metaphor-library.md`, `references/composition-patterns.md`, `references/style-dna.md`, `references/prompt-template.md`, `references/qa-checklist.md`.
- **Best for:** Producing the illustration assets themselves — hero, feature, blog, explainer and empty-state spots on any section that needs a human figure explaining an idea. Trade fit: the register is friendly SaaS-editorial, so on trade homepages it suits small explainer/process spots rather than carrying a hero or a whole section's design.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1301⟧

## ⟦S1302⟧ kb-retriever — Part 22 — User's installed catalog (MengTo, Owl-Listener designer-skills, ConardLi, tastemaker, elayadesign)
- **What it is:** A retrieval and Q&A assistant skill (written in Chinese) for answering questions from a local, mixed-format knowledge-base directory — Markdown/text, PDF and Excel — by navigating a layered directory index and searching progressively (grep first, then small windowed reads), never loading whole files into context. It produces no page, graphic or visual output of any kind.
- **How it looks:** Nothing on screen — there is no visual artifact. Its only output is a text answer in the language the user asked in, conclusion first with brief supporting evidence, citing the files used with approximate locations (e.g. "来源：design/api_gateway.md 第 100 行附近" or "reports/2023_Q1_sales.xlsx Summary 工作表"), and explicitly flagging assumptions or missing information instead of inventing facts.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Knowledge-base root is the user-specified path, otherwise `./knowledge/`; existence must be checked with a shell test (`test -d knowledge`) — using Glob to test for the directory is expressly forbidden, and if the default root is missing the skill asks rather than guessing. Navigation follows a per-directory `data_structure.md` index tree, read in ~300-line windows and recursed only along the branches most relevant to the question. Retrieval uses 3–8 keywords per question (core nouns plus synonyms, abbreviations, broader/narrower terms), precise grep include/path scoping, and local reads around hits only (Read windows of ~200–500 lines); a unified iteration loop repeats with tightened keywords for at most 5 rounds, then reports the gap. Mandatory learn-before-processing gate: before touching any PDF, first read `references/pdf_reading.md`; before any Excel, first read `references/excel_reading.md` AND `references/excel_analysis.md` — processing a file without reading its guide is a listed prohibited behaviour. PDF route: `pdftotext input.pdf output.txt` extracted to a file (never to stdout; `-f`/`-l` for page ranges, `-layout` to preserve layout), pdfplumber for tables and coordinate-level extraction, pypdf for metadata/basic text, OCR (pytesseract via pdf2image) only for scans, and `scripts/convert_pdf_to_images.py` as the fallback for text-less scanned PDFs. Excel route: pandas — preview structure with `nrows` (first 10–50 rows), `usecols`/`dtype` for selective reads, then boolean filters, groupby aggregation, pivot tables and derived columns against identified key fields. Using web search or any outside source while answering from the knowledge base is expressly forbidden.
- **Reference / source:** Bundled files: `README.zh-CN.md`, `references/pdf_reading.md`, `references/excel_reading.md`, `references/excel_analysis.md`, `scripts/convert_pdf_to_images.py` (MIT licensed). Tools it prescribes: grep, windowed file reads, pdftotext/poppler-utils, pdfplumber, pypdf, pypdfium2, pandas.
- **Best for:** No homepage section — it is an internal research utility for interrogating a local document store (docs folders, report archives, mixed PDF/Excel collections) with sourced answers. No trade fit for page building.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1302⟧
## ⟦S1303⟧ tastemaker — Part 22 — User's installed catalog (tastemaker; ~402 KB, 34 reference files per the catalog)
- **What it is:** A complete UI-design operating system, not a single technique: it generates on-brand, non-generic UI (landing pages, dashboards, app screens, components) by grounding style in real pixels and locking it in project memory instead of inventing taste fresh each session. One default mode (**build**, the Steps 0–5 workflow below) plus three verbs — **study** (extract reusable design DNA from a screenshot/URL, never the pixels), **audit** (score existing UI against its numbered gate list, return a ranked punch list, never edits), **comps** (write structured image-generator briefs to `.tastemaker/comps-brief.md`, no code; it calls no image API itself) — plus optional **aesthetic modes** (brutalist, minimalist…), opt-in override files at `references/modes/<name>.md` that swap dials on the same engine; none ship in the base skill. Its four founding ideas: (1) extract tokens deterministically from real reference pixels with scripts, never from a text summary of a vibe; (2) remember — `.tastemaker/style-lock.md` per project, `~/.tastemaker/profile.md` across projects — so style is locked and reused, not re-derived; (3) scope design effort to the PRD/spec's actual screen list; (4) craft is many small choices compounding. It also bundles a full vendored illustration skill (`ideagram/`), a `SECURITY.md`, 20 Python scripts and 4 JS/CSS assets (inventoried under Mechanism).
- **How it looks:** A page built under it is recognisably *not* the generic template: no indigo-to-purple gradient, no hero → 3-feature-cards → testimonial → CTA → footer rhythm. The hero has one job — one promise headline (6–12 words), a one-sentence subhead, one primary CTA (plus at most one secondary) and ONE focused proof visual (real product capture, chart, photo or recolored illustration), never a cluster of badges/rails/floating chips. Every section is mostly something to look at — a mockup, chart, before/after, diagram, stat tile, real photo or illustration — with text demoted to caption (its #1 rule: show, don't tell). Colour is a locked, generated-per-project palette with neutrals tinted toward the anchor hue and the accent held to roughly ≤5% of any viewport; type is one curated mood pairing (display + body, ≤3 families on the page); spacing follows one named scale with generous, role-weighted section padding, so sections read as separate moments. Every section that needs a photo has a real fetched photo, every concept section a real illustration, every icon from one fetched icon family, and the page moves — GSAP scroll reveals and at least one scroll-storytelling beat on marketing pages. Structure itself varies between projects (named macrostructure + rotated component archetypes), so two sites in the same mood still have different page shapes.
- **Frame by frame:** The skill's motion grammar, by surface. *Page load (marketing):* a GSAP hero timeline of at most four beats — (1) navigation/context, (2) headline, (3) subhead + actions, (4) the single proof visual, animated as one composition (its internal labels are NOT staggered separately). *Scrolling:* elements marked `data-reveal` fade in with an 8–16px upward rise as they enter (starter defaults: duration 0.22s, distance 16px, ease `power3.out`, group stagger 0.06s); scrubbed reveals tie progress to scroll position (a visual assembles, a path draws, a number counts as you scroll); at most one or two pinned sections hold while their content steps through; background/foreground layers drift at slightly different rates for parallax depth. *Hero comparison variant:* when the proof is a before/after, the two real screenshots are layered and the top one is wiped by animating a `--wipe` CSS variable driving `clip-path: inset()` back and forth on a slow loop (example: to 80% over 4s, `sine.inOut`, yoyo, capped 15–85% so both states always show). *Pointer (optional hero upgrade):* an element or mascot's eyes drift toward the cursor by lerped follow — `current += (target − current) × 0.06–0.12` per frame, max travel ~10–25px, nearer layers move more than far ones; eases back to rest on mouse-leave; only under `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)`. *Micro-interactions:* press = `scale(0.97)` over 120ms ease-out on pointer-down; hovers settle in 100–150ms; popovers/menus scale in from their trigger's origin starting at `scale(0.95)` + opacity 0 (never `scale(0)`); a toast exits the same edge it entered. *App-shell screens (no scroll narrative exists):* panel/tab switches slide 8–12px directionally + fade, lists/tables stagger in on data-load, only the thing that changed animates, loading is a layout-mirroring skeleton; a dragged object follows the pointer 1:1 and releases into a spring settle. *Reduced motion, everywhere:* spatial motion collapses to a ≤150ms opacity crossfade, the wipe freezes at its 50% midpoint, a shader background renders one static frame (speed 0), and the spring settle becomes critically damped with no overshoot — state feedback itself is never removed.
- **Mechanism & key values:** *Workflow.* Step 0 memory precedence is strict: current user request > `.tastemaker/style-lock.md` > resolved `.tastemaker/decisions.log` entries > `~/.tastemaker/profile.md` (pending-review entries never count as approval). Step 1 classifies every screen (marketing narrative / app shell / transactional form / data view / editor-canvas / settings / empty-loading-success state) — classification controls density, components and motion track. Step 1.25 design read + dials (defaults: variance 7, motion 5, density 4, art direction 7; Persuade variance 7–9/motion 5–8/density 3–5, Operate 3–6/2–5/6–9, Read 4–6/1–4/3–6, Experience 8–10/6–9). Step 1.5 sourcing precedence: repo's own components → shadcn/ui base → Watermelon → KokonutUI → bklit for charts → lucide-animated then itshover for icons → MCP search → inspo reference JSX → hand-roll only when the stack can't consume registries (stack detection first: static HTML/Vue/Svelte/native port the *pattern* by hand; never emit `npx shadcn add` at a non-React stack). Step 2 style: references → `scripts/extract_palette.py` (deterministic dominant colours/contrast/lightness from real pixels); no references → `scripts/generate_palette.py --mood premium|warm|technical|playful|elegant [--mode light|dark] [--seed N]` (OKLCH, a harmony rule — analogous/complementary/triadic/split/mono — and per-role lightness solved against the contrast contract, Leonardo-style). Contrast floors enforced by `scripts/check_contrast.py --matrix`: body/muted text 4.5:1, button label on any fill 4.5:1, fill vs page 3:1, accent-as-highlight/icon 3:1, state-carrying border 3:1 (purely decorative hairlines exempt); the lock records the legal-pairings lists (text-safe ≥4.5 / UI-safe ≥3.0 / decorative <3.0), and Step 4's failure path for an illegal pairing is ordered: reuse a legal pairing → nudge the new colour's lightness within its hue family and re-run the matrix → fall back to a safe neutral (`text`/`on-primary`) → surface a genuine conflict to the user. A runtime light/dark toggle, when wanted, is generated as the SAME `--seed` in both modes and both matrices verified. Mood type pairings (all Google Fonts): premium **Unbounded + Albert Sans** (alt Inter + Inter, tight tracking), warm **Zain + Nunito** (alt Epilogue + Baskervville), technical **Archivo + IBM Plex Sans** (+ IBM Plex Mono for code/data only, never body copy), playful **Urbanist + Open Sans** (alt Fredoka + Nunito), elegant **Gloock + Inter** (alt EB Garamond + DM Mono accents). Anchor palettes (character references, NOT to ship — the generator makes the real one): premium light text `#050315` / bg `#FBFBFE` / primary `#2F27CE` / secondary `#DEDCFF` / accent `#433BFF`, dark primary lightened to `#5850E0` (the light primary only hits 2.16:1 on the dark `#0A0A12` bg, under the 3:1 visibility floor); warm primary `#B85A38` (darkened from `#C96F4A`, which cleared only 3.59:1 with white labels; `#B85A38` clears 4.61:1); technical dark-native text `#E6E6EA` / bg `#0B0D12` / primary `#047857` (from `#10B981` at 2.54:1 → 5.48:1) / accent `#34D399`; playful primary `#4361EE` / secondary `#7209B7` / accent `#F72585`; elegant text `#211F1C` / bg `#F7F4EE` / primary `#2F2A24` / accent `#B5762C`, dark primary replaced by `#9C6524`. White is the verified button-label colour on all five anchor primaries. Step 2.5 structure: a six-beat narrative arc (hook → problem/stakes → solution → how-it-works → proof → close; minimum four distinct beats, five default) is worked out BEFORE picking one of **12 named macrostructures** (1 Feature Stack, 2 Bento Showcase, 3 Editorial Index, 4 Long-Scroll Narrative, 5 Stat-Led, 6 Gallery Grid, 7 Product Demo/Workbench, 8 Split Diptych, 9 Conversational FAQ, 10 Manifesto, 11 Catalogue, 12 Poster Fold), filled with catalogued archetypes — nav **N1–N7**, hero **H1–H6**, feature **F1–F7**, proof **P1–P4**, CTA **C1–C4**, footer **Ft1–Ft6**, section-head **S1–S4** (the eyebrow-left/heading-right two-column head is banned outright; eyebrows default OFF, max 1–2 per page, stacked only) — under a mandatory rotation rule: macrostructure, nav, footer and hero must each differ from the last build (checked against the last 3–5 entries of `.tastemaker/log.json`, trimmed ~20, and cross-project `~/.tastemaker/structure-history.json`, trimmed ~40; `scripts/check_structure_history.py --current <picks.json>` flags a pick at 60%+ of the last 5 global builds; reusing an archetype requires changing ≥1 variation knob). Step 3 assets, all in the same pass: photos via `scripts/fetch_photos.py` from Openverse (800M+ images, default filter CC0 + Public Domain Mark, NO API key, anonymous limits 20/min · 200/day; optional `--source pixabay` needs `PIXABAY_API_KEY`; Unsplash deliberately unused — its API demands visible attribution); icons via `scripts/fetch_icons.py` from Iconify, set chosen by locked mood (premium → heroicons, warm → tabler, technical → lucide, playful → ph, elegant → material-symbols), pre-tinted to the accent, one set per project; brand/logo walls fetch the REAL marks (`--set simple-icons` monochrome or `--set logos` official colour — a genuine miss means drop the item, never a text chip); credits go in a code-comment `CREDITS` block only, never on the page; existing logos are preserved byte-for-byte, cold-start marks are constructed from 2–5 primitive shapes in the locked palette (never a letter in a box), then `scripts/export_favicons.py`. Step 4 build: ten non-negotiables (show-don't-tell; hero one job/one visual; motion wired this pass on the correct per-screen track; no asset-empty section; only legal colour pairings; spacing scale with internal ≤ external; the motion gate + `scripts/audit_motion.py`; core states designed — populated/loading/empty/error/disabled/focus/hover/pressed/success; interface-quality rules apply to pulled components too; copy grounded in ONE specific checkable fact per headline, three candidates from mechanism/outcome/tension angles, and a **hard ban on em dashes in all shipped copy** — scanner HIGH). Before finalizing, a two-pass pre-emit self-critique scores 11 axes 1–5 (ShowTell, Philosophy, Hierarchy, Specificity, Restraint, Variety + ColorHarm, MoodTone, Type, Spatial, Preference — the last five adapted from the TASTE study) and anything <3 is revised; after building, a mood-scoped gate list of 51+ numbered gates is swept (incl. accent ≤ ~5% of a viewport, section headlines capped at ~50–65% of hero display size, no invented metrics/testimonials/logos, no mid-render token improvisation) plus three mechanical scans — `scripts/anti_slop_scan.py`, `scripts/audit_motion.py`, `scripts/check_component_coherence.py` — HIGH findings must be fixed before handoff. The build is stamped (first CSS line: macrostructure, arc, archetype IDs + knobs, mood, palette seed, contrast result, 11 critique scores) and logged to both history files plus `~/.tastemaker/copy-history.json` (~40 entries). Step 5 closes the loop: one specific keep/reject question per pass, logged as JSONL to `.tastemaker/decisions.log` (fields ts/project/surface/status kept|rejected|pending-review/axis/decision/reason/source/promote); autonomous runs log `pending-review` and never fabricate approval; resolved structure/copy decisions patch the matching history entry's `outcome`; promotion into `~/.tastemaker/profile.md` only for resolved, reusable, cross-project preferences. *Type values:* headline 6–12 words — 6–8 words gets full display size, 9–12 words steps ~15–20% smaller, 3–5 words caps at the SAME ceiling (never bigger), and must read on 1–2 lines; subhead 16–28 words, ≤2 desktop lines; bold display line-height floor 1.0 (0.87 clips descenders); hero must fit the fold at 1280×800; ≤3 font families (display + body + ≤1 outlier in ≤2 slots); no italic headings; body copy never in mono. *Spacing:* 4px base, tokens `space-1` 4px · `space-2` 8px · `space-3` 12px · `space-4` 16px · `space-6` 24px · `space-8` 32px · `space-12` 48px · `space-16` 64px · `space-24` 96px · `space-32` 128px · `space-40` 160px · `space-48` 192px; content-card internal padding floor `space-6` (24px), compact/dense cards `space-3`–`space-4` (12–16px), showcase cards `space-8` (32px); landing section padding by weight — connective `space-12`–`space-16`, standard `space-16`–`space-24`, pivotal `space-32`–`space-48` — with adjacent-section boundary gaps ~120–250px on desktop, stepped down 1–2 tiers at ≤40rem; one separation mechanism per project (alternating tint / hairline divider / padding only); no horizontal scroll at 320–1920px (`overflow-x: clip` on html+body, image grid tracks `minmax(0,1fr)`); hit targets ≥44×44px below 40rem; no two-line clickable text at any width. *Motion values:* easing tokens `--ease-out: cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1)`, `--ease-in-out: cubic-bezier(0.77, 0, 0.175, 1)`, `--ease-drawer: cubic-bezier(0.32, 0.72, 0, 1)`; duration tokens press 120ms, popover 180ms, panel 240ms; ranges — button press 100–160ms, tooltip/popover 125–200ms, dropdown/select 150–250ms, modal/drawer 200–500ms, on-screen morph 180–300ms, UI motion budget ≤300ms, entrance fade+rise restrained at 150–250ms for premium; hover tooltips delay ~800ms, focus tooltips 0ms; focus ring ≥3:1 and appears instantly, never transitioned; animate `transform`/`opacity` only, never `transition: all`, never `ease-in` on UI, blur crossfade ≤2px (hard cap 20px). Engines: GSAP 3.12.5 + ScrollTrigger via cdnjs is the default (`assets/gsap-starter.js`, `gsap.matchMedia()` reduced-motion); anime.js is a scoped alternative ONLY for SVG motion-path/shape-morph work (measured: full bundle ~118KB min / ~41KB gzip vs GSAP core+ScrollTrigger ~117KB / ~46KB and GSAP+Draggable+MorphSVG+DrawSVG ~179KB / ~69KB; two porting gotchas recorded — ScrollObserver threshold syntax differs silently, and it needs an explicit initial `handleScroll()` or above-fold reveals never fire); Motion (motion.dev) for React springs/layout/exit and registry components that ship it, loaded build-free pinned as `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/motion@12/+esm`, spring defaults `{type:"spring", duration:0.4, bounce:0}` and `bounce:0.2` for momentum gestures; one engine per project (the named exception: lucide-animated/itshover icons bring Motion for icon micro-motion while GSAP drives the page). Paper Shaders (`@paper-design/shaders` pinned 0.0.80) is the default ambient hero background over a hand-rolled canvas loop — mood→effect pairs: premium Mesh Gradient / Static Radial Gradient, warm Waves / Neuro Noise, technical Grain Gradient / Warp, playful Metaballs / Dot Orbit, elegant Smoke Ring / God Rays — confined behind a bg-colour vignette at ~0.3–0.6 opacity, never directly behind text, speed 0 under reduced motion. *Registries named (verified commands in the source):* shadcn/ui base; Watermelon `@watermelon` → `https://registry.watermelon.sh/r/{name}.json` (260+ components + full blocks; the `/r/` path is required — without it the URL returns HTML and fails); KokonutUI `@kokonutui` → `https://kokonutui.com/r/{name}.json` (Tailwind v4 only); bklit `@bklit` → `https://ui.bklit.com/r/{name}.json` (17+ chart types — always pull, never hand-roll a chart); lucide-animated `https://lucide-animated.com/r/{name}.json` (467+ animated icons, MIT, Motion added automatically); itshover `https://itshover.com/r/{name}.json` (186+ icons, Apache 2.0, brand/tech marks); MCP servers shadcn-ui-mcp-server (60 req/hr without a GitHub token, 5,000 with) and 21st.dev (requires an API key, optional only); GrayBlocks documented as NOT agent-consumable (Figma/Framer/Webflow-only, paid). Two registry traps recorded: `shadcn init` overwrites a locked palette with its own oklch defaults (re-apply the lock after init, keep its `--chart-*`/`--sidebar-*` token names), and interactive overwrite prompts hang agents (pass `--yes`). *Behavioural library defaults* (`library-selection.md`): Base UI (dialogs/popovers/menus/selects), cmdk (command palette), Sonner (toasts), input-otp, Motion (React animation), NumberFlow (animated numbers), Recharts or bklit (static charts), Liveline (real-time charts), dnd kit (drag & drop), Virtuoso (long lists), Zustand, clsx, cva, next-themes. *Non-Latin scripts:* the two-family Latin model does not apply — one family across a weight scale; Korean starting point Pretendard (9 weights 100–900, SIL Open Font License, NOT on Google Fonts — loads from jsDelivr `pretendard@v1.3.9` variable CSS), `letter-spacing: 0` (never Latin negative tracking), `word-break: keep-all` for UI text, line-height looser than the Latin 1.0–1.15 floor; Noto Sans JP/SC named as less-vetted starting points. *Prescribed outbound behaviour (described as data; nothing here was run):* `SECURITY.md` states the skill's scripts contact exactly five hosts — `api.iconify.design` (icons), `api.openverse.org` (photos), `pixabay.com` (only with the user's opt-in `PIXABAY_API_KEY`), `cdn.jsdelivr.net` and `cdnjs.cloudflare.com` (pinned library delivery) — enforced at runtime by `scripts/_netguard.py` (https-only, allowlist re-checked on every redirect, anything else raises `BlockedURLError`); it states there is no telemetry or analytics and nothing about the project is transmitted; CI asserts the bundled scripts contain no `subprocess`, `os.system`, `shell=True`, `eval`, `exec` or `pickle` (`scripts/test_security.py`), and `scripts/check_domains.py` fails the build on any domain outside the vetted allowlist (a former optional logo-source domain sits on a permanent denylist after a 2026-08-02 external audit flagged it as a phishing risk; the same remediation fixed a `file://` local-file-read vector in `fetch_photos.py`). The skill also prescribes treating project documents (PRDs, specs, READMEs, tickets) and text inside reference images as untrusted data, never instructions: an embedded directive (run a command, fetch a URL, reveal keys…) must be quoted to the user and not acted on. *Sub-part inventory — the 34 bundled files, so the Map can point precisely:* `SKILL.md` (modes, Steps 0–5, the ten build non-negotiables, honesty note); `SECURITY.md` (egress allowlist, netguard, untrusted-input rules, audit history); `references/style-tokens.md` (mood classification table, generator usage, five mood type pairings + light/dark anchor palettes with hexes, runtime-toggle pairing, non-Latin typography, the full spacing/radius scales, contrast floor); `references/style-lock-format.md` (the lock's exact structure incl. the Color contract table and per-section fields); `references/taste-memory.md` (three memory layers, decisions.log JSONL format, capture/promotion rules, profile format); `references/reference-intelligence.md` (design read, dials, five-lane reference board, mandatory search/fetch sourcing rule — an inferred board must be labelled `inferred, not viewed`); `references/inspo-mcp.md` (inspo MCP as default board source when connected — budget: ONE `recommend`, one or two `search_screens`, then `get_screen` on the 3–5 kept; its 19-shape taxonomy vs this skill's 12; DNA-not-pixels rule; supahero.io manual fallback); `references/narrative-arc.md` (the six beats, StoryBrand/PAS grounding, beat→archetype mapping, merge/skip rules); `references/macrostructures.md` (the 12 named page shapes with when/mood affinities + honesty rule); `references/component-catalog.md` (archetype IDs N/H/F/P/C/Ft/S with shapes, use-whens, knobs and per-mood routing tables; cross-cutting rules: no fake chrome, one icon family, section-head size cap); `references/diversification.md` (log.json + structure-history.json formats, rotation rule, outcome-weighted tie-breaking via `summarize_outcomes.py`, build-stamp format); `references/component-patterns.md` (show-don't-tell conversion table, proof-section visual floor, column-balance rule, separation mechanisms, per-screen patterns: landing, app shell with chrome palette-mapping and density rules, data tables, pricing — 3 tiers default — onboarding, empty states, about pages, settings/forms); Each entry states the relationship.

## ⟦S1304⟧ web-design-engineer — Part 22 — User's installed catalog (ConardLi)

- **What it is:** A workflow skill that makes an AI agent work as a design engineer for browser-rendered artifacts — pages, dashboards, interactive prototypes, HTML slide decks, animations, UI mockups, data visualizations — built in HTML/CSS/JavaScript/React. Its core is process discipline: verify facts first, gather real design context, calibrate the brief on five dials, declare the design system before writing code, show a rough v0 early, then build, self-check, and critique on request.
- **How it looks:** There is no single look — the output wears whatever design system was declared for the task, and the skill's job is to stop that system collapsing into AI defaults. On screen the visitor sees: real brand assets doing the recognition work (the actual logo, real product photography or real UI screenshots, referenced as images — never CSS silhouettes or hand-drawn SVG stand-ins); a restrained oklch-derived palette with colour count held to roughly ≤4 roles; non-default typography with bold scale contrast (title-to-body ratio ≥2.5×, 4–6× normal on heroes); honest placeholders where material is missing (a labelled `[icon]` box, a `16:9 image` card, an initial-letter avatar) instead of fabricated stats, fake logo walls or dummy testimonials; and polished micro-interactions (button press, card hover, entry motion). Named anchor looks it can instantiate from its recipe files include: Linear-style — warm near-black `#08090A` ground, 1px hairline borders `rgba(255,255,255,0.06)`, purple `#5E6AD2` accent on under 5% of pixels, radius never above 16px, keyboard-shortcut chips; Apple HIG-style — one product photograph centred on white `#FFFFFF` / `#F5F5F7`, hairline `#D2D2D7` dividers, text-link CTA in system blue `#0071E3`, one idea per long section; MUJI-style — warm off-white `#F4F2EC`, 60–80% empty space, no accent colour at all; Aesop-style — warm chamois `#E8E4D9`, sage `#7A8470`, serif body copy, square corners, no shadow. Multi-variant work appears as a floating "Tweaks" panel in the bottom-right corner (completely hidden when closed) or a side-by-side design canvas.
- **Frame by frame:** The skill itself is a process, so motion is per-artifact and per chosen recipe; it prescribes an animation ladder and forbids reaching for heavy libraries first: (1) CSS transitions/animations for ~80% of micro-interactions, (2) React state + setTimeout/requestAnimationFrame, (3) a custom `useTime` + `Easing` + `interpolate` timeline engine for scrub-able demo scenes (always shipped with play/pause + a scrubber), (4) Popmotion only as fallback; GSAP/Framer Motion/Lottie avoided unless explicitly requested. Recipe-level motion values it carries include: Apple HIG — expo-out cubic-bezier, 350–650ms layout moves, 150–250ms hovers, slow Ken Burns drift on hero imagery; Linear — ~150ms ease-out hovers, 350–450ms layout moves on the quint curve `cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1)`; MUJI — fades only, 600–900ms, nothing translating more than a few px; Aesop — subtle fades and ~450ms ease-out drawer slide-ins, never spring-bounce; Bloomberg Terminal — uniform linear ticker scroll, instant state flips, 50–80ms blink flash on data updates, no easing; Field.io — generative type morphing on variable-font axes during scroll with long expo/quint-out curves such as `cubic-bezier(0.83, 0, 0.17, 1)` and staggered multi-element choreographed entries; slide decks — a fixed 1920×1080 stage auto-fitted by JS `transform: scale()`, ←/→/Space navigation, position persisted in localStorage. Every animation must carry hierarchy, feedback, causality or narrative, and motion beyond simple state feedback must collapse cleanly under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Seven-step workflow with three hard checkpoints (Step 0 verify facts via search before designing around any named product/brand; Step 1 ask-or-not judgement by scenario; Step 2 gather context — code over screenshots, user material over industry references; Step 2b produce a one-block "Design Read" and calibrate five dials, each 1–10 — visual variance, motion intensity, information density, asset dependence, brand fidelity — with preset rows, e.g. mainstream SaaS landing 6/5/4/6/5, data dashboard 4/3/8/3/7, existing-product extension = match existing + fidelity 10; Step 3a four positioning questions — narrative role, viewing distance (10cm phone / 1m laptop / 10m projector), visual temperature, capacity check; Step 3 declare the design system in Markdown — palette, typography, spacing, radius strategy, shadow hierarchy levels 1–5, motion style — and wait for confirmation; Step 4 viewable v0 with placeholders; Step 5 full build with all states — default/hover/active/focus/disabled/loading/empty/error; Step 6 lightweight pre-delivery checklist, executable browser acceptance ONLY when the user explicitly asks for QA/验收; Step 7 five-dimension critique, each scored 0–10 — philosophy alignment, visual hierarchy, craft quality, functionality, originality — with per-output-type weighting). Brand Asset Protocol: recognition order logo > product imagery / UI screenshots > colour tokens > typography; logo non-negotiable (stop and ask if unsourceable); all assets captured in `brand-spec.md`. Anti-cliché table with reasons and brand-spec exceptions: purple→pink→blue gradients, rounded card + coloured left border, emoji as icons, SVG-drawn imagery, CSS silhouettes for products, Inter/Roboto/Arial/Fraunces/system-ui as display, cyber-neon on `#0D1117`, fabricated stats/testimonials. Colour derived in `oklch()` only (e.g. `--primary: oklch(0.55 0.25 var(--primary-h))`, neutral ramp `oklch(0.98 0.002 250)` → `oklch(0.21 0.014 250)`); six starter colour×font pairings (modern tech `oklch(0.55 0.25 250)` + Space Grotesk; elegant editorial warm brown `oklch(0.35 0.10 30)` + Newsreader/Outfit; premium near-black + Sora; coral consumer; teal minimal-professional; caramel artisan + Caveat/Newsreader). A library of **25 anchored style recipes** in 7 schools (Editorial/Minimalist 5, Information Architecture 5, Modern Tool/Builder SaaS 4, Motion/Experimental 3, Brutalist/Raw 3, Warm Humanist 3, Specialty/Genre 2), each a single ~50-line file with concrete palette hexes, font names/weights, spacing ladder, radius/shadow/motion character, 3–5 signature moves, avoid list and an AI-prompt seed — load only the one recipe being used. A Design Direction Advisor fallback for vague briefs: propose exactly 3 directions from different schools, each with a named designer/studio anchor (Pentagram, Kenya Hara, Linear, Field.io, Are.na, Stripe Press…), never 3 from one school. Technical hard rules: React + pinned-CDN Babel (versions/integrity fixed, no `type="module"`); never a global `const styles = {...}`; cross-file components shared via `Object.assign(window, {...})`; never `scrollIntoView`; split files over 1,000 lines; variants as one file + Tweaks toggles. Scale floors: presentation text ≥24px on a 1920×1080 canvas, touch targets ≥44px, print ≥12pt, web body 16–18px; critique checks: 8pt spacing grid {8,16,24,32,48,64,96}, ≤2 font families, whitespace ≥40% of area (60%+ minimalist). Dashboards: Chart.js or D3 via CDN, ResizeObserver containers, dark/light toggle, data-ink discipline. Existing-UI work is classified Extension / Redesign·Preserve / Redesign·Overhaul with protected contracts (routes, form fields, legal copy, analytics hooks, accessibility wins) that must never change silently. The skill text also prescribes agent behaviours (web fact-checks, asking the user at checkpoints, optional browser QA runs) — recorded here as what the skill says, not actions taken by this index.
- **Reference / source:** ConardLi's `web-design-engineer` skill (Part 22 — User's installed catalog), distilled from Anthropic's Claude Design system prompt (launched April 2026, ~420 lines), MIT licensed; bundled references: advanced-patterns code templates, block library, browser-acceptance harness, design calibration, design directions (6 schools), failure-patterns catalog, redesign protocol, critique guide, and the 25 style-recipe files. Named real-world anchors throughout: Linear, Vercel, Raycast, Notion, Apple HIG, MUJI/Kenya Hara, Aesop, Dieter Rams/Braun, Monocle, Pentagram/Paula Scher, Vignelli, Bloomberg Terminal, Tufte, NYT, Field.io, Active Theory, Resn, Are.na, Bloomberg Businessweek (Turley era), Balenciaga, Mailchimp, Stripe Press, Headspace.
- **Tier:** STRONG — basis: it is the bank's most complete design-direction and build-discipline skill; its anti-slop rules, real-asset protocol and recipe library are load-bearing for any homepage build, but it is a general workflow rather than a single proven section mechanism, so it does not take a CROWN.
- **Best for:** Whole-page direction and build discipline for any homepage section — hero, proof/reviews, work/gallery, process, towns/areas, call/CTA, forms, navigation, footer — plus dashboards, prototypes and decks. Trade fit: strong for trade homepages — the asset protocol (real logo and real job photography, no CSS silhouettes, no invented reviews or stats) and the failure-patterns catalog (no repeated eyebrow-header formula, no zigzag monotony, no decorative trust theatre) map directly onto trade lead pages; recipes such as dieter-rams-braun (industrial/hardware), aesop and stripe-press (quiet premium) are plausible trade anchors, while the Motion/Experimental recipes (field-io, active-theory, resn) are heavy, moment-only treatments that fight a lead-gen page's job.

## ⟦S1305⟧ web-video-presentation — Part 22 — User's installed catalog (ConardLi)

- **What it is:** A methodology + collaboration-workflow skill that turns an article or a narration script into a click-driven 16:9 web presentation that "looks like a video" — a Vite + React + TypeScript project built on a fixed 1920×1080 stage, where each click advances one narration beat and each step owns the full screen — with optional per-step synthesized narration audio, made to be screen-recorded into a finished video for Bilibili / YouTube / 视频号. It explicitly does NOT plan animation inside the written outline: the outline fixes rhythm and information density only, and each chapter's animation is designed at build time from the content.
- **How it looks:** A video stage, not slides: the 1920×1080 stage sits centred on any screen with black letterbox around it; one focused idea fills the whole frame per step — hero type at 80px and up, generous margins (at least ~80px safe area on all sides), no header, no footer, no page numbers, no brand bar. A progress bar lives invisible along the bottom edge and only appears when the mouse hovers there, so recordings show zero chrome. Every chapter must contain real visual demonstrations built in CSS/SVG/Canvas/JS — numbers counting up, bars growing, rankings swapping, flow nodes lighting in sequence, diagrams drawing themselves, particle fields, simulated terminals or chat windows — never a chapter of plain text, and list items are revealed one at a time (the item being spoken lights up; earlier items grey back as context). 23 built-in themes give it distinct looks, e.g. `midnight-press` (warm espresso dark ground, hot-orange accent, italic serif hero numerals, slow cinematic ~1.6s reveals, 140×100 stage padding), `blueprint` (deep navy, drafting cyan, IBM Plex Mono, 60px grid + 2px dashed rules), `newsroom` (newspaper cream, Playfair Display serif, flag-red accent, 0 radius), `terminal-green` (pure black, JetBrains Mono only, CRT scanlines, phosphor glow), `bauhaus-bold` (0 radius, 4px solid borders and stage frame, offset solid shadows, weight-900 hero numerals), `dune` (charcoal-brown ink on sand, almost no accent, 140×100 padding, slowest ~1.75s reveals).
- **Frame by frame:** Playback is click-driven: the visitor/presenter clicks the stage (or presses →) → the global `(chapter, step)` counter advances → the current full-screen scene is replaced by the next step's scene — each step is a pure function of the step counter, no timers. Within a step, motion is content-driven and designed per chapter; the bundled tech-review example shows the house style: screen fades from black to the warm dark ground over 1.5s ease-out → a distant particle cloud drifts in with 1.0s stagger → the hook line types out character by character at 100ms/char → the hero score sharpens from blur(20px) over 1.2s with a 400ms offset while an SVG crown draws itself around it by mask reveal over 1.5s; comparison bars wipe left-to-right to their values (leader to 100% in 1.2s ease-out, runner-up to ~70% staggered 600ms later) and the gap figure blur-clears in between; ambient micro-motion (breathing accent glow on 5–6s cycles, slow Ken Burns push, faint drifting scanlines) is permitted only as background, never as the main event. With audio synthesized, Auto mode (`?auto=1`) runs hands-free: press Space once (browser autoplay gate) → the step's mp3 plays → 200ms after it ends the stage auto-advances → … → the final step holds its end state, ready to stop the recording; animation longer than its step's narration is cut off mid-flight — there is no wait-for-animation fallback.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Pipeline: article → in ONE pass produce `script.md` (platform-style narration script, original language kept) + `outline.md` (chapters, steps, per-chapter "information pool" of facts/quotes/numbers pulled from the article) → **Checkpoint Plan**, a hard stop aligning 5 things at once (script, outline, theme, real assets, build mode) → build chapter 1 in the main thread as a complete anchor version → mandatory user acceptance of chapter 1 (unskippable) → chapters 2–N in the chosen mode (A per-chapter acceptance / B sequential / C parallel subagents) → **Checkpoint Audio** → optional TTS → screen recording. Hard numbers: stage 1920×1080 scaled by transform, no responsive breakpoints; steps per chapter 3–8, chapters ~30–60s each, total minutes ≈ total time ÷ 30s per chapter; narration timing estimated at ~4 Chinese chars/sec (seconds ≈ chars ÷ 4); script information-retention floor — `script.md` length ≥ 60% of `article.md`, facts/figures/argument chains must survive; spoken lines ≤20 chars by default (Bilibili; Douyin ≤12 chars / 1-second hook, YouTube long-form ≤30 chars), hook must land within 3 seconds; script rhythm split by `---`, one idea per beat. The single source of truth is each chapter's `narrations.ts`: its array length must equal (max step index in the chapter's code) + 1, and it drives both step count and audio; chapter-structure edits require bumping the stepper's localStorage `STORAGE_KEY`. Themes: 23 built-in, each ~25–35 CSS tokens — colours (`--shell`, `--surface`/`-2`/`-3`, `--text`/`-2`/`-mute`/`-faint`, `--rule`, `--accent`/`-soft`/`-glow`) and font families (`--font-display-cn`/`-en`/`--font-body`/`--font-mono`) MUST come from tokens (no hardcoded hex or font names in chapter CSS), while font sizes, spacing, animation durations/easings and gaps are deliberately free per chapter; theme personality rides in via primitive classes `.hero-num`, `.rule`, `.card`, `.stage-frame`; exactly one accent colour per theme; `--text` on `--surface` ≥ 4.5:1 contrast. Audio: `extract-narrations` scans all chapters into `audio-segments.json`; synthesis writes one mp3 per step to `public/audio/<chapter-id>/<step-N>.mp3` (1-indexed), incrementally (existing files skipped); provider-agnostic — each backend is one shell file implementing `tts_synthesize` (plus optional `tts_check`/`tts_install_help`); built in: MiniMax via `mmx-cli` (default, needs the user's MiniMax API key) and OpenAI TTS via curl (needs the user's `OPENAI_API_KEY`; model `tts-1` default or `tts-1-hd`, voices alloy/echo/fable/onyx/nova/shimmer), with paste-in snippets for ElevenLabs, edge-tts, macOS `say`, Azure and Google; runtime modes Manual (click, silent) / Audio (`?audio=1` or M — plays audio, manual advance) / Auto (`?auto=1` — plays and auto-advances); a missing or empty narration falls back to estimated timing `max(1500ms, chars × 250ms)`; segments ≥15s are flagged as over-dense. A mandatory self-check protocol (independent reviewer agent → subagent → strict self-check, fix all failures before reporting) applies to the script, the outline and every finished chapter; chapter red lines include no setTimeout/setInterval-driven animation, per-chapter CSS class prefixes and folder isolation, `npx tsc --noEmit` must pass. The skill prescribes agent/user interactions and optional paid TTS calls using the user's own API keys — recorded here as what the skill says; nothing was executed for this index.
- **Reference / source:** ConardLi's `web-video-presentation` skill (Part 22 — User's installed catalog), MIT-licensed collection sibling of ⟦S1304⟧; named tools/providers: Vite + React + TypeScript scaffold (`scripts/scaffold.sh`), MiniMax `mmx-cli` (github.com/MiniMax-AI/cli), OpenAI TTS, plus optional ElevenLabs / edge-tts / Azure / Google Cloud TTS / macOS `say`; 23 named built-in themes (midnight-press, dark-botanical, chalk-garden, blueprint, terminal-green, neon-cyber, bold-signal, creative-voltage, paper-press, newsroom, monochrome-print, vintage-editorial, sunset-zine, pastel-dream, warm-keynote, electric-studio, bauhaus-bold, swiss-ikb, dune, indigo-porcelain, forest-ink, kraft-paper, split-canvas).
- **Tier:** NOT-FOR-TRADES — basis: it produces narration-driven video presentations for recording, not lead-generation pages; no homepage section is built with it (its sibling ⟦S1304⟧ explicitly routes this job here and excludes it from its own scope).
- **Best for:** Turning articles/scripts into recordable video-style presentations — tutorials, product demos, keynote-style talks, Bilibili/YouTube/视频号 content. For trade homepages it has no direct section use; the only transferable ideas are presentational discipline — one idea per screen, hidden chrome, and one-item-at-a-time reveal pacing for step-driven content.

Relationships stated plainly: S1306 (formal audit) and S1314 (build-time gate) are two distinct skills from the same anti-slop family — S1306's own text defers full-page audits to S1314's ARTICLE.md catalog, and both ship the identical REFERENCES.md link list; neither is collapsed into the other. S1321 and S1322 are sibling GSAP/Lenis systems with near-identical tokens — S1321 is the reusable data-attribute motion system, S1322 the page-level storytelling anatomy (preloader, sticky stack); both are indexed in full and cross-pointed.

## ⟦S1306⟧ audit-ai-design-slop — UI prompting & inspiration workflows
- **What it is:** A diagnostic audit workflow: inspect a website, app, screenshot, mockup, or design code and produce an evidence-backed report of AI-design clichés, generic generated defaults, and established UI defects — removal-first, with no redesign prescribed.
- **How it looks:** It produces no page or visual output. The deliverable is a compact Markdown report: a one-paragraph Verdict, a Checked scope list, a Findings table (Priority | Class | Pattern | Evidence | Harm | Remove or fix), and an Unknowns section.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. It is an inspection procedure, not a visual effect.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Every finding must cite a concrete location/component/line of copy. Findings are classed as Quality defect or Slop pattern, prioritised P0 (blocks completion, severe accessibility issue, deceptive proof) / P1 (harms comprehension, trust, navigation, interaction) / P2 (repeated slop weakening hierarchy/identity) / P3 (minor polish). Report the 5–8 highest-impact findings by default, grouping repeats into one systemic finding. The removal test: state the element's job → if removing it improves clarity without losing that role, recommend removal → otherwise the smallest correction in the existing system. Hard boundaries: no numeric slop score, no guessing whether AI made the design, no new font/palette/layout prescribed unless asked, no technique rejected in isolation (a gradient, glass, card, or animation can be intentional). Flag categories: decorative stacking (glow + gradient text + glass + borders + shadows + grids + particles doing the same job), component/template repetition, typography/copy clutter, motion theater (motion that delays access, repeats mechanically, moves targets, blocks input, ignores reduced motion), fake proof (invented metrics/testimonials/awards/logos), and established UI failures (competing primary actions, low contrast, clipping/overflow, hover-only information, missing states, unclear focus).
- **Reference / source:** Bundled REFERENCES.md link list: impeccable.style/slop, getdesign.md, github.com/Leonxlnx/taste-skill, github.com/petergyang/no-ai-slop, github.com/MengTo/Skills, two X posts (MengTo, GoogleDesign), a YouTube video, WCAG 2.2 quickref + contrast/reflow/target-size understandings, NN/g ten usability heuristics, Material 3 accessible design, Apple HIG typography, GOV.UK design system typography. Full-page audits defer to the sibling skill's catalog (no-ai-design-slop/ARTICLE.md — see ⟦S1314⟧).
- **Best for:** QA gate on any finished section or page before sign-off; not a design source. Trade fit: strong as the audit pass over trade homepages (fake proof and decorative stacking are the two failure modes it names that trade pages commit most).
- **Tier:** STRONG (as a QA/audit reference — the bank's own anti-slop standard; not a section mechanism).
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1306⟧

## ⟦S1307⟧ audit-reference-originality — UI prompting & inspiration workflows
- **What it is:** An audit workflow that compares a shipped website against its supplied reference corpus (pages, capture packs, screenshots, copy, brands, numbers, images, videos, layouts, motion, code) and reports originality risks with paired evidence — distinguishing common visual grammar from distinctive copying.
- **How it looks:** No page output. The deliverable is a report led by one verdict — Clear in checked scope / Clear with low-risk similarities / Changes recommended / Block release / Blocked by missing evidence — followed by the source registry, a severity-ordered red-flag table, category pass list, history findings, access gaps, and a prioritised fix plan.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. An evidence-comparison procedure.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Six-step method: build the source registry → inventory the current site AND its history (git log / git show / git log -S / --name-status for renamed or deleted files; a bundled helper `scripts/build_evidence_inventory.py` finds exact-file matches, basename reuse, normalized text overlap, repeated number tokens) → compare across 8 categories (Text, Brands, Numbers, Images, Assets, Videos, Structure and motion, History) → triangulate each flag (current evidence + reference evidence + what differs) → propose fixes that replace rather than disguise → report. Rubric evidence hierarchy, strongest first: 1 identical file bytes/Git blob, 2 near-identical rendered text (eight-word sequences tested), 3 matching brand names/numbers/URLs, 4 matching image crops/video frames, 5 several distinctive composition/motion elements combined, 6 generic style resemblance (levels 5–6 need judgment and caveats). Severity: Blocker (exact unlicensed media/code/identity or substantial verbatim copy shipped) / High (distinctive near-copy, source identity or numbers visible) / Medium (isolated recognizable overlap) / Low (similar grammar, original identity/content) / Clear. False-positive controls: black-and-white, one accent, large sans type, standard hero/work/pricing/FAQ/footer sequence, fade/slide/marquee/parallax, common icon libraries, ordinary stock subjects are NOT flags alone. Findings are called "originality risks", never legal plagiarism; cosmetic recoloring is explicitly not a fix for copied identity, copy, media, or composition.
- **Reference / source:** Bundled references/audit-rubric.md (reproduced in full in the skill text). No external sites named beyond the method's own tooling (git, the bundled Python helper).
- **Best for:** Release gate for reference-inspired builds — exactly the bank's copy-then-adapt workflow: run it after adapting a reference so the shipped page keeps the mechanism, not the identity. No direct section use.
- **Tier:** STRONG (process/QA reference for the adapt-a-reference workflow; not a section mechanism).
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1307⟧

## ⟦S1308⟧ aura-asset-images — UI prompting & inspiration workflows
- **What it is:** A stock-image sourcing skill: search the Aura Assets library (aura.build/assets, Unsplash-style) by tag and return 5 real direct image URLs per category, with resolution and crop guidance.
- **How it looks:** The output is photographs, not a design: backgrounds, abstract wallpapers, architecture shots, portraits, and headshots delivered as direct image URLs (Supabase storage links), ready to drop into a hero, feature section, or avatar slot at a stated aspect ratio.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. The images are stills.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Search via `https://www.aura.build/assets?q=<tag>&order=popular`; tags that work well: background, abstract, architecture, portrait, headshot. URL format `https://hoirqrkdgbmvpwutwuwj.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/assets/assets/<UUID>_800w.jpg`; swap `_800w` → `_1600w` for higher res (if the 1600w variant 404s, keep 800w and direct the user to the asset page). Curated picks are also shipped at `_3840w`. Ratios: avatars 1:1, headshots 4:5 or 3:4, website heroes/large backgrounds 16:9, mobile wallpapers/stories 9:16. Suggested exports — backgrounds 16:9 at 1920×1080 / 2400×1350, 9:16 at 1080×1920; abstract desktop wallpaper 2560×1600 or 2880×1800; architecture web hero 2400×1350, feature 1600×900; portraits 3:4 1500×2000, 4:5 1200×1500; headshots 4:5 800×1000 / 1200×1500, 1:1 avatar fallback 512×512. Cropping rules: faces keep eyes ~1/3 from the top, don't cut chin/forehead; backgrounds preserve horizon lines and keep 30–50% negative space for text. The skill ships 25 curated URLs (5 per category) verbatim in its text.
- **Reference / source:** aura.build/assets (Aura Assets library). Bundled demo prompt references a Neuform page (neuform.ai Kiwi Floral) as the demo quality bar.
- **Best for:** Asset supply for heroes and feature sections when a build needs photographic backgrounds/architecture quickly. Trade fit: usable for atmosphere imagery only — the curated sets are abstract/architectural/portrait, not trade work photography; a firm's real work must never be replaced by these as "proof" imagery.
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL (asset sourcing, not a design mechanism; generic stock — never as a firm's own work evidence).
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1308⟧

## ⟦S1309⟧ browser-video-recording — UI prompting & inspiration workflows
- **What it is:** A production workflow for making polished browser screen-recording-style demo videos: real in-app-browser screenshots are rendered by a bundled Python script into an MP4 with a natural macOS cursor, click choreography, and calm zoom-follow framing.
- **How it looks:** The output is a video, not a page: a browser-only crop (never the desktop) at 4:3, the page filling the frame, a large natural macOS pointer gliding between real click targets, pausing, dipping subtly on click, while the camera framing eases toward the clicked content.
- **Frame by frame:** Capture: set the browser viewport to 1920×1440 → navigate and perform real clicks/backs/searches/scrolls → save a browser-only screenshot after each important state (01-results-top.png, 02-after-card-click.png…) → record each click target's viewport coordinates. Render at 60 fps: the cursor travels sparse, mostly straight paths between recorded points → pauses briefly on the target → clicks with a subtle scale dip/rebound (no decorative rings) → the page transition happens after the click, not before → the zoom-follow camera reframes the clicked content, always calmer than the cursor.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Output 4K 4:3 = 3840×2880 at 60 fps; source viewport 1920×1440. Cursor scale 3.0; click animation strength 15 (subtle scale dip); cursor rotation up to 8deg, from horizontal velocity only. Renderer: bundled `scripts/render_browser_demo.py` (python3 + Pillow + ffmpeg/ffprobe; optional macOS cursor extraction via swift/screencapture, else a transparent PNG cursor_asset + cursor_hotspot). Config keys: shots, scene_starts [time, shotName, transition], cursor_keys [time, x, y], camera_keys [time, x, y, zoom], click_times, duration, fps, output_size, source_size, cursor_scale. Native-recorder path (optional MCP): frameRate 60, resolutionRawValue "4K", ratioPresetRawValue "4:3", explicit selectedRegionOnScreen. Verification is mandatory: ffprobe for codec/width/height/r_frame_rate/duration/size, plus a mid-video thumbnail (ffmpeg -ss 8, one frame) inspected for cursor visibility, framing, and browser-only crop; reset the viewport override before finishing.
- **Reference / source:** Codex in-app browser (Browser skill/MCP) as the frame source; bundled script and demo files (demo/PROMPT.md, demo/expected-output.md, demo/input.md). Expected-output example: "3840 x 2880 at 60 fps, natural macOS cursor and deliberate click pauses, zoom follows the active control, ffprobe dimensions and duration verified."
- **Best for:** Producing demo/showcase videos of a finished page (motion-study evidence, walkthroughs). No homepage section use — it is a recording pipeline, not a page mechanism.
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL (production tooling for demo videos; no page-design application).
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1309⟧

## ⟦S1310⟧ build-daily-inspiration-sites — UI prompting & inspiration workflows
- **What it is:** An orchestration workflow: turn one completed daily UI inspiration capture (a five-item manifest) into exactly five original landing-page builds, one per separate Codex task, each privately deployed via Sites.
- **How it looks:** The output is five complete single-route landing pages, each with a replacement brand identity — new name, positioning, copy, numbers, pricing, and imagery — that keeps only the reference's high-level visual grammar: hierarchy, pacing, section logic, contrast, spacing, image treatment.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion of its own. It prescribes that each build task create "restrained, maintainable interaction behavior appropriate to the new page rather than claiming to reproduce reference motion": CSS for micro-interactions, IntersectionObserver/Web Animations API for light reveals, Framer Motion/Motion One for state-driven React motion, GSAP ScrollTrigger only for justified pinned/scrubbed sequences, carousel library only when CSS scroll-snap is insufficient; reduced-motion fallbacks required. A static full-page image does not establish source motion — briefs must not infer it.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Exactly 5 manifest items, exactly 5 tasks, exactly 1 full-page reference image attached per task (rendered as a Markdown image attachment — a path-only handoff is a blocker, never a fallback). Validation first: `node <skill-dir>/scripts/validate_capture.mjs <article-dir>/manifest.json` requiring itemCount 5, content.md, one non-empty fullPageImage per item, pageUrl per live item, one builder prompt per item. Before dispatch, build an originality matrix: five distinct identities (brand name + slug, positioning, audience, conversion goal, vocabulary, proof points/metrics/plans/prices, imagery direction), cross-checked against each other for accidental similarity. Briefs follow references/thread-brief-contract.md and must contain no unresolved placeholders (NEW_BRAND, TODO). Each task: initialize Sites immediately, build the complete page (shell, header, hero, proof, features, demo, process, work, testimonials, pricing, FAQ, final CTA, footer, responsive, keyboard/focus, reduced motion), production build, narrow commit, private deployment, return URL + source location + commit. Hard rules: Codex in-app browser only, never Chrome; no model-authored SVG illustrations; never edit the five sites concurrently in the source checkout.
- **Reference / source:** Consumes the output of ⟦S1311⟧ daily-ui-inspiration-capture; brief contract in bundled references/thread-brief-contract.md; builds use the Sites plugin skills (sites:sites-building, sites:sites-hosting).
- **Best for:** Process/orchestration — the multi-build pipeline that turns a capture pack into adapted builds. Pairs with the originality audit ⟦S1307⟧ as its release gate. No direct section mechanism.
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL (workflow orchestration; the per-build design content comes from the capture pack, not this skill).
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1310⟧

## ⟦S1311⟧ daily-ui-inspiration-capture — UI prompting & inspiration workflows
- **What it is:** The capture workflow that produces the dated inspiration bundles ⟦S1310⟧ consumes: collect exactly 5 live landing-page references into an article folder with stills, videos, full-page screenshots, section crops, motion frames, and one AI-builder prompt per item.
- **How it looks:** The deliverable is an evidence pack per reference: one representative still, a short video of the real page scrolling, one tall full-page screenshot from the hero's first pixel to the footer's last pixel, contiguous section crops cut from that image (hero, every meaningful middle section, footer), and at least 4 motion-progression frames (opening hero, hover/settled state, scroll transition, lower section).
- **Frame by frame:** Capture sequence per reference: open the live page → record slow scroll with visible hover/click states, sticky nav behavior, reveal animations, parallax, marquee loops, carousels, cursor effects → after every scroll to a capture position, wait 2 seconds before capturing so reveals, lazy media, and sticky state changes settle → save the full-page scroll screenshot → cut section crops losslessly from it (no missing pixels between sections, no overlap unless a sticky element forces it) → extract ≥4 motion frames from the video. If live capture is blocked/login-gated/low quality, save the best local fallback and document the reason in the manifest (videoFallbackReason).
- **Mechanism & key values:** Exactly 5 final references (the 5-reference motion-study workflow supersedes older 20-image gallery runs). Dedupe against all previous articles/*-ui-inspiration-capture/manifest.json files — reject repeats of normalized title, source URL, or image URL; verify with `node scripts/check-ui-inspiration-duplicates.mjs` (duplicateCount must be 0). Sources: Framer Marketplace preferred, Dribbble best-effort; rotate searches (website hero, saas landing page, product website, web design hero, recent web design, recent product design). Output contract: articles/YYYY-MM-DD-ui-inspiration-capture/ with content.md + manifest.json (no README.md); article structure fixed — `### Full-Page And Section Evidence`, full-page image as a normal Markdown image, `#### Section Crops`, crops as Markdown images hero→footer; crop coordinates live in manifest.json only, never as captions. Manifest item fields include title, creator, sourceUrl, pageUrl, imageFile, videoFile/videoFallbackReason, fullPageImage, sectionImages (label, path, y-start, y-end, height), motionFrames, viewport, why, pattern, interactionNotes, animationNotes, prompt. Browser rule: Codex in-app browser only, never Chrome.
- **Reference / source:** Framer Marketplace and Dribbble as capture sources; project runbook + scripts/ui-inspiration-capture-guidelines.md govern when present. Feeds ⟦S1310⟧; its full-page evidence standard is repaired by ⟦S1316⟧ when captures come out blank.
- **Best for:** Research supply chain — building the reference packs the design method shortlists from. No homepage section use.
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL (capture/research workflow; evidence quality standard, not a design mechanism).
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1311⟧

## ⟦S1312⟧ generate-reference-inspired-brand-worlds — UI prompting & inspiration workflows
- **What it is:** An art-direction workflow for image generation: from one supplied visual reference (brand identity image, poster, campaign, moodboard), generate multiple original brand campaign worlds that feel related to it, with a controlled similarity target and protected signature elements never copied.
- **How it looks:** Each output is a 16:9 landscape brand campaign key visual: a rich staged scene with people performing a brand-specific ritual, a shared medium/texture/palette relationship with the reference, and the new brand's wordmark rendered exactly once, large, in original letterforms.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. The deliverables are still key visuals.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Similarity dial (intent, not a measured score): 30% distant inspiration (abstract principles only) / 50% recognizable influence (medium + tone shared; palette, composition, subjects, type changed) / 70% adjacent brand family (composition logic, texture, palette relationships, human presence, wordmark scale shared; new subjects, actions, arrangement, letterforms — the default for "not too different") / 85% close neighbor (most visual grammar kept, at least four signature elements changed; never an exact commercial identity). Process: label inputs (Image 1 = primary visual-language reference; Image 2 = current concept anchor when revising) → extract visual DNA as two lists (reusable visual grammar: scene density/depth layers, palette relationships, surface, lighting/emotional temperature, type scale/weight/placement logic, human presence, organic-vs-architectural rhythm; protected signature elements: exact people/poses/clothing, motif arrangement, foreground-to-background layout, brand name/slogans/logos, distinctive letterforms, pixel-for-pixel composition) → build a distinct-brand matrix holding 4–6 constants (aspect ratio, medium/texture, palette relationship, wordmark color/scale/placement, scene density, emotional tone) while varying name, meaning, environment, human ritual, signature motif per brand → one image-generation call per brand using the fixed prompt spine (style-transfer, verbatim name rendered exactly once; unusual names spelled out letter by letter, e.g. M-O-S-S-W-E-F-T). Validation checklist: exact wordmark spelling, one occurrence, no extra copy/marks, ≥4 signature elements different, brands differ from each other in meaning/ritual/environment/motif, correct aspect ratio. Revisions save as versioned siblings (brand-name-v2.png), never overwriting V1. Worked examples at 70%: MOSSWEFT, KINTRA, NIGHTJAR, TIDETURN, EMBERHOUSE sharing a saturated vintage editorial photomontage / coarse halftone / 1970s woven-tapestry spine.
- **Reference / source:** The host's image-generation tooling (built-in imagegen skill when available); worked examples in bundled references/example-prompts.md. The third-party reference behind the examples is intentionally not bundled.
- **Best for:** Generating original campaign/hero imagery families for a new brand identity. Trade fit: limited — produces campaign key visuals, not a firm's real work photography; could art-direct a portfolio concept's hero image family, never a client's proof imagery.
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL (image art-direction workflow; not a page mechanism).
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1312⟧

## ⟦S1313⟧ html-to-interaction-prompts — UI prompting & inspiration workflows
- **What it is:** An analysis workflow: read a supplied HTML page's actual source, identify its reusable interactions, capture screenshot/video evidence for each, and write portable builder prompts — packaged as an article (and, in daily-inspiration mode, a full 5-item capture article).
- **How it looks:** The deliverable is an article of named interaction prompts (e.g. "Hero Particle Field That Follows The Mouse", "Cursor Glow Hover On Cards", "Scroll Behavior And Section Reveal System"), each with its screenshot or motion frames inserted directly under the prompt heading, plus — for landing pages — a section-by-section anatomy for every section from shell to footer.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion of its own; it documents other pages' motion. Its capture protocol is motion-aware: actuate the interaction before capture (move the pointer for cursor effects, hover cards, scroll into pinned sections, wait for canvas motion), and after every scroll to a capture position wait 2 seconds before the screenshot so lazy media and reveal animations settle.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Source is truth: grep the HTML/CSS/JS for mousemove, pointermove, canvas, webgl, ScrollTrigger, requestAnimationFrame, hover, sticky, pin, parallax, magnetic, glow, shader, animation before writing anything — never infer exact effects from a screenshot alone when HTML exists. Split prompts by reusable interaction idea, not implementation lines. Prompt structure: Core idea / Technology / Implementation / Interaction / Success; landing pages add a per-section anatomy block (Purpose, Layout, Visual details, Animation — initial state, trigger, easing, duration, stagger, transform origin, opacity, blur, clip/mask, parallax depth, loop, settled state — Interaction states, Scroll interaction, Library/API). Portability rules: no hard-coded colors, sizes, thresholds, DOM ids (unless exact recreation is asked); "derive colors from the page theme", "scale density to the layout and device". Library guidance with explicit selection rules: CSS transitions/keyframes for simple states; IntersectionObserver/Web Animations API for light reveals; Framer Motion/Motion One for React state-driven motion; GSAP ScrollTrigger for pinned/scrubbed/parallax/masked reveals; Lenis only when smooth scrolling materially supports the choreography; CSS scroll-snap first, Embla/Keen/Swiper when carousel physics is needed; Rive/Lottie for authored vector timelines; Three.js/WebGL only for real 3D/shader/particles (cap pixel ratio, pause offscreen, mobile density reduction, static fallback); CSS sticky before GSAP pinning. Daily-capture mode: exactly 5 inspirations, each with still + embedded local MP4 recorded from the actual pageUrl (never a cover-image pan), full-page screenshot + contiguous section crops, manifest itemCount 5. Verification: git diff --check, every media file exists and is non-empty, ffprobe on MP4s.
- **Reference / source:** Consumes HTML files / generated-page.html / live pages; interoperates with the ⟦S1311⟧ daily capture contract and its article structure. Bundled demo files (demo/PROMPT.md, demo/expected-output.md, demo/input.md).
- **Best for:** Turning a reference page into reusable, adaptable interaction prompts — the extraction step of the bank's copy-the-mechanism workflow. No direct section use.
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL (extraction/analysis workflow feeding the build method; not itself a mechanism).
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1313⟧

## ⟦S1314⟧ no-ai-design-slop — UI prompting & inspiration workflows
- **What it is:** The build-time companion to ⟦S1306⟧: a passive design quality gate applied while creating or revising UI — catch generic AI defaults and established defects as they are introduced, preserving the chosen art direction — backed by the full pattern catalog (ARTICLE.md) that the audit skill defers to.
- **How it looks:** It changes no visual directly; applied well, the page it guards keeps one focal point per viewport, hierarchy carried by size/weight/placement rather than pills and eyebrows, grouping by proximity before containers, and decoration where every gradient/glow/glass layer has a stated job. What it removes is visible: tracked eyebrows over every heading, nested cards, purple-to-blue gradient defaults, radial spotlights behind sections, icon tiles over every feature, fake dashboards and invented metrics.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion of its own. Its motion doctrine (catalog §8): motion may explain state, causality, hierarchy, continuity, or spatial change; flag identical entrance animations on every element, perpetual animations competing with reading, marquee that hides content, bounce/elastic on ordinary state changes, scale/rotate hover defaults, layout-property animation, sticky storytelling that traps the user, content that stays invisible if JS fails; reduced motion must present a stable final state, not merely a shorter animation.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Core test — a choice is suspect when several hold: it could be pasted into an unrelated product unchanged; it repeats a familiar generated pattern; it conflicts with the local system; it communicates no information/state/action/hierarchy/brand meaning; it competes with content or weakens trust. Eight compact gates run whenever a section/component/effect/state is added: System, Hierarchy, Composition, Typography, Color and material, Product truth, Interaction, Motion and access. Same removal test as ⟦S1306⟧ (name it → state its job → delete if clarity improves → smallest correction otherwise → replacement only on real loss). The bundled ARTICLE.md catalog has 10 numbered sections (Product and Direction; Composition, Layout, and Space; Containers, Cards, and Shape; Typography and Hierarchy; Color, Lighting, and Material; Imagery, Illustration, and Icons; Components, States, and Interaction; Motion and Scroll; Copy, Proof, and Page Structure; Quality, Accessibility, and Production) plus six high-signal clusters — Generic AI SaaS (tracked eyebrow + oversized sentence headline + purple gradient + radial lights + glass cards + icon tiles + bento + vague copy), Card apocalypse, Motion theater, Fake sophistication, Reference mismatch, Polish before truth — with the rule to fix the root cause once, not every instance. It merges three sources: the Impeccable slop catalog, the DesignCode anti-slop workflow, and Meng's design-skill principles. Boundary vs ⟦S1306⟧: this skill edits during the work; a formal review-only request routes to audit-ai-design-slop and does not edit.
- **Reference / source:** References include impeccable.style/slop, getdesign.md, github.com/Leonxlnx/taste-skill, github.com/petergyang/no-ai-slop, github.com/MengTo/Skills, WCAG 2.2 (quickref, contrast, reflow, target size), NN/g heuristics, Material 3 accessibility, Apple HIG typography, GOV.UK typography — the same REFERENCES.md list as ⟦S1306⟧. Catalog sources: Impeccable slop catalog, DesignCode anti-slop workflow, MengTo design skills.
- **Best for:** Every build, as the standing quality gate — the bank's anti-slop standard during construction (its sibling ⟦S1306⟧ is the after-the-fact audit). Especially load-bearing for trade homepages: fake proof, template section sequences, and card repetition are its named targets.
- **Tier:** STRONG (governing quality doctrine for all builds; not a section mechanism).
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1314⟧

## ⟦S1315⟧ optimize-web-animations — UI prompting & inspiration workflows
- **What it is:** A performance profiling and repair workflow for animated pages: measure the real page in the browser, find animations still running offscreen and leak-prone long-lived resources, patch the smallest owning component, and re-verify — without removing visible motion.
- **How it looks:** The visitor sees no change — that is the point. Visible motion still runs and resumes correctly; what changes is invisible: offscreen marquees, skeletons, canvas/WebGL loops, and GSAP/Three/Matter effects stop consuming CPU/GPU until scrolled back into view, and long sessions stop slowing down.
- **Frame by frame:** The fix behavior: a section scrolls out of view → an IntersectionObserver marks it `is-offscreen` → its CSS animations pause (`animation-play-state: paused !important`, including ::before/::after) and its canvas/WebGL RAF loop cancels → the section scrolls back → animations and loops resume on re-entry. Under reduced motion, continuous motion is disabled per the component's existing behavior.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Baseline profiling at top, mid-page, footer, and one mobile viewport; CSS animations counted by computed animationName/animationPlayState/visibility including pseudo-elements; canvases inspected separately (CSS profiling does not prove RAF stopped). Target result after patching: `offscreenRunningCount: 0` at every sampled state. IntersectionObserver threshold ~0.01 for animation gating; observe the card shell and animated descendants for repeated cards, not the whole document; marquee tracks pause with their section. Leak hardening checklist: clear every timeout/interval, cancel RAF before unmount/restart, disconnect Intersection/Resize/Mutation observers, remove global listeners with the same handler reference, dispose Three/WebGL textures/materials/geometries/renderers and remove renderer DOM nodes, kill GSAP tweens/timelines (including shader-uniform objects), stop media streams, guard async loaders with an isDisposed flag, cap physics frame deltas after visibility pauses. Memory audit: idle sample after 10–30 seconds plus a short route-cycle sample (the bundled sampler uses 3 cycles); DOM/canvas/image/iframe counts should return to baseline; heap APIs returning null must be reported as unmeasured, not as "no leak". Bundled references/browser-profiling.md ships the full evaluator (DOM scan bounded to 10,000 elements, 15s evaluate timeouts, 500ms settle waits, mobile pass at 390×844). Avoid list: never pause visible hero motion with an over-broad ancestor selector; animation-play-state does not cover JS RAF loops or pseudo-elements unless selected; no unbounded stress loops.
- **Reference / source:** Codex Browser (in-app browser) as the profiling surface — explicitly not Chrome unless the user asks; bundled demo files and references/browser-profiling.md.
- **Best for:** Post-build performance pass on any motion-heavy homepage (the pinned/parallax/WebGL builds in this bank are exactly its target). No section-design use; it is the cost-control layer for the heavy mechanisms.
- **Tier:** STRONG (performance doctrine for motion-heavy builds; pairs with every heavy mechanism as its budget check).
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1315⟧

## ⟦S1316⟧ stitched-full-page-capture — UI prompting & inspiration workflows
- **What it is:** A screenshot-repair technique: build a trustworthy full-page image by stitching settled viewport captures, for lazy-loaded, scroll-animated, Framer, WebGL/canvas, or reveal-heavy pages where one-shot browser fullPage screenshots come out blank, gray, white, or sparse.
