- **How it looks:** The output is one tall image of the complete page — hero's first pixel to footer's last pixel, every lazy section mounted and revealed — from which section crops are cut; compared against the broken native capture, it has no blank bands, no missing sections, no narrow content strip.
- **Frame by frame:** The capture walks the page: open the real page URL → scroll top to bottom once to warm lazy media and reveal sections → return to the top → scroll downward in viewport-sized or slightly overlapping steps → wait about 2 seconds after each stop → capture the settled viewport → stitch the slices vertically into the full-page image → cut section crops from the stitched image → validate against the representative still, MP4, and motion frames.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Bundled helper: `node <skills-root>/stitched-full-page-capture/scripts/stitch_full_page_capture.mjs --manifest <article manifest.json>` (Playwright Chromium; reads items[].pageUrl, fullPageImage, sectionImages; writes fullPageCaptureMethod: "stitchedViewportScreenshots" plus viewport, step, segment count, corrected crop coordinates into the manifest). Defaults: --viewport 1440x1100, --step 950 (less than viewport height for overlap), --wait 2000 ms after each scroll stop, --quality 3 (ffmpeg JPEG quality, lower is better), --item N repairs one item (1-based). Rejection criteria for a candidate full-page image: blank/gray/white bands, very low visual content, missing lazy-loaded sections, extremely narrow content column, disagreement with the scroll video. Validation: sips pixel dimensions match expectation; crop coordinates contiguous and ending at the full-page image height; project checks (git diff --check, duplicate checker, ffprobe over videos). Native fullPage screenshots may be kept as comparison candidates but are never the source of truth unless they visually match the stitched capture.
- **Reference / source:** Built for the ⟦S1311⟧ daily-inspiration article pipeline (manifest-driven); Playwright Chromium capture; bundled demo files (demo/PROMPT.md, demo/expected-output.md, demo/input.md).
- **Best for:** Evidence capture for reference packs and QA screenshots of reveal-heavy pages — the reliable way to get section-by-section screenshots of animated builds. No page-design use.
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL (capture tooling; the standard for screenshot evidence on animated pages).
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1316⟧

## ⟦S1317⟧ unsplash-asset-images — UI prompting & inspiration workflows
- **What it is:** A stock-photo picking skill: choose real Unsplash photos for avatars, headshots, portraits, large website backgrounds, and abstract wallpapers, and deliver the canonical photo-page URLs with the exact resolutions and aspect ratios to produce.
- **How it looks:** The output is a curated set of photographs per category — clean-framed faces on simple backgrounds for avatars, shoulders-up professional-but-human headshots, editorial candid portraits, wide landscapes with clean negative space for heroes, abstract gradient/organic wallpapers — each with its target crop sizes.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. Still photography delivered as URLs plus crop instructions.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Output rule per recommendation: 1) the Unsplash page URL (canonical), 2) suggested ratios + sizes. License handling: Unsplash images are generally free to use; avoid Unsplash+ images unless the user explicitly wants them; photographer credit is good practice, not required attribution. Deliverable sizes — Avatars 1:1: 256×256, 512×512, 1024×1024. Headshots 4:5: 800×1000, 1200×1500, 1600×2000; 3:4: 900×1200, 1500×2000. Portraits 3:4 1500×2000, 4:5 1200×1500, 1:1 social crop 1080×1080. Large backgrounds 16:9: desktop hero 1920×1080, 2400×1350, 2880×1620; social banner 1500×500 (3:1, manual crop). Abstract wallpapers: desktop 2560×1600 or 2880×1800, mobile 1080×1920 (9:16). Ratio cheatsheet: avatar 1:1, headshot card 4:5 default (3:4 taller), hero background 16:9, mobile wallpaper/story 9:16. Selection rules: clean negative space, avoid busy backgrounds, keep faces centered, use `crop=faces` on production URLs so faces are not cropped awkwardly. Ships 25 curated photo-page URLs (5 per category) verbatim. Note: deliver only main photo page URLs — no source/secondary image links.
- **Reference / source:** Unsplash (unsplash.com photo pages, listed in full in the skill text). Sibling/alternative to ⟦S1308⟧ aura-asset-images (different library: Unsplash vs Aura Assets).
- **Best for:** Asset supply for avatar/headshot slots, hero backgrounds, and wallpaper-style section backgrounds. Trade fit: atmosphere and background use only — never as a firm's real team or work evidence (the bank's honesty rules require real photos for people presented as real).
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL (asset sourcing; not a design mechanism).
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1317⟧

## ⟦S1318⟧ video-to-superprompt — UI prompting & inspiration workflows
- **What it is:** An analysis workflow that turns a reference video into one super-detailed, paste-ready recreation or inspiration prompt — capturing what the video shows, how it moves, how to rebuild it, and what assets are needed.
- **How it looks:** The deliverable is a single fenced text prompt (or an article/asset pack when asked) structured as: asset map, brand and content, global design system, motion system, then one block per visible section/beat in video order (purpose, layout, visual details, animation, interaction, scroll behavior, implementation notes), closing with video/scroll implementation, WebGL notes, responsive requirements, accessibility/performance, and a success check.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion of its own; it transcribes motion. Its inspection samples the video at timeline beats rather than uniform thumbnails: ffprobe for duration/dimensions/frame rate/codec/size, frames extracted at fps=1 for a quick pass, plus start/middle/end and visible transition moments for long or scroll-heavy videos.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Six-step workflow: locate the source (ask for the exact file/URL rather than inventing details if inaccessible; inspect connected HTML/CSS/JS first for exact recreations) → inspect technically (ffprobe + ffmpeg frame extraction as above) → analyze in six layers (story, screen/layout, motion, visual design, technical rebuild, accessibility/performance) → plan assets (asset map with exact URLs/local names/placeholders; separate generation prompts for image plates, video clips, WebGL elements, posters, sprites, masks, textures; image prompts kept separate from video prompts) → write the superprompt from bundled references/superprompt-template.md → verify (asset paths exist or are marked placeholders; frames non-empty and representative). Quality bar: long enough to rebuild the interaction without seeing the video; names exact mechanisms (pinned section, scrubbed timeline, video.currentTime, parallax layer, mask, shader, particle field, carousel physics); mobile and reduced-motion behavior included every time; anti-patterns called out (generic landing sections, decorative blobs, mismatched stock, autoplay-only video where scroll-scrubbing is required, text overlap). Output modes: Prompt only / Article / Implementation brief / Asset-generation pack. Prescribed rebuild techniques inside the template: pinned/sticky section mapping scroll progress to video.currentTime; videos muted, playsInline, preload metadata/auto, object-fit cover, no controls unless user-facing; GSAP ScrollTrigger or native requestAnimationFrame for pinned timelines; Three.js/WebGL only for real particles/3D/shaders with pixel-ratio caps and static fallbacks.
- **Reference / source:** Bundled references/superprompt-template.md and demo files (demo/PROMPT.md, demo/expected-output.md with an example beat log 0–4s hero / 4–10s title split / 10–16s pinned card stack / 16–20s footer uncover, demo/input.md). ffmpeg/ffprobe are the named tools.
- **Best for:** Extracting a buildable spec from a motion reference video — the video counterpart to ⟦S1313⟧'s HTML extraction. No direct section use.
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL (analysis workflow feeding builds; not a mechanism).
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1318⟧

## ⟦S1319⟧ web-technique-to-skill — UI prompting & inspiration workflows
- **What it is:** The authoring method for turning a technique you already built and shipped into a reusable web-design skill: isolate the one mechanism, reproduce its approved reference exactly in the demo around that focus, and package both with numbers, failure-anchored rules, and browser verification.
- **How it looks:** The deliverable is a skill package — agent-skills/<category>/<skill-name>/ with SKILL.md (imperative, name+description frontmatter only), agents/openai.yaml, and demo/ (index.html, PROMPT.md with Minimal/Recreate/Remix prompts, preview.jpg, optional owned reference assets). The demo must be recognizably the source page — same first frame, palette, type treatment, composition, atmosphere, motion hierarchy — with the technique name as its visible h1/title and the verified stack line (e.g. "Vanilla JavaScript · Canvas 2D") on the first screen.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion of its own; it governs how other techniques' motion gets documented (every authored key state, plus forward, reverse, fast-skip, and reload-at-depth paths must be verified for time/scroll-spanning mechanisms).
- **Mechanism & key values:** Core moves: name the mechanism in one sentence ("the one thing that, if removed, makes the effect stop working" — it must survive changing subject, palette, and layout) → name the demo by the concrete technique and disclose the verified stack (runtime, renderer/API, technique layer — verified from imports/context creation, never guessed from the look; state absences plainly, e.g. "No WebGL, shaders, or Three.js") → split mechanism (skill) from staging (demo only) from incidental (dropped) → anchor every rule to the failure it prevents → carry numbers, not adjectives (ranges per layer/state, timing/easing, budgets, trade-off formulas) → keep the expensive gotchas symptom-first (colour space, layout timing, stacking/compositing, ordering, platform quirks) → declare the boundary against the nearest existing skill in the opening lines → state cost honestly from a profile. Lifecycle constants for web-design skills: clamp dt to about 1/30 s, cap DPR at 2, size from ResizeObserver with a zero-viewport guard, pause on document.hidden and offscreen, reset the time base on resume, reduced motion renders a designed still frame (never a hidden effect) with controls still live. Demo quality floor: deliberate type scale, one spacing rhythm, restrained palette with one meaningful accent, styled controls with visible focus, real specific copy, one self-contained file when the reference permits, 390px through 1440px, semantic HTML, clean console. Browser verification: drive the demo at 1440×900 and 390×844, exercise the primary interaction, tab order, reduced-motion path, side-by-side comparison with the source at the source viewport. Worked example values in the bundled demo handoff: beam period 11s; fog march 24 steps desktop / 12 mobile chosen by pixel count; card lift 6px over 240ms on cubic-bezier(.22,.65,.28,1); tide rates deliberately coprime.
- **Reference / source:** Extracted-from provenance is recorded per skill ("Record where the design came from" — one line naming the source project). Sibling boundary: article-prompts-to-skills handles article/prompt-pack sources; this skill handles techniques already built. The web-design skill family it governs includes ⟦S1323⟧–⟦S1328⟧-style technique skills.
- **Best for:** Meta-workflow — packaging proven build techniques into the library itself. No homepage section use.
- **Tier:** SITUATIONAL (skill-authoring method; governs how technique entries like the scroll & motion family are written).
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1319⟧

## ⟦S1320⟧ build-awwwards-quality-sites — Web design — core builds
- **What it is:** A complete build system for distinctive, motion-rich marketing/editorial/portfolio/landing sites: art direction first, an honest asset system, a composed hero, a GSAP motion system on exactly one smooth-scroll engine, optional purposeful Three.js, and a validation pass — with "Awwwards quality" as an acceptance bar, never an award claim.
- **How it looks:** A cohesive site whose visual idea, media, typography, and motion tell the same story: the first viewport is the strongest authored moment — clear message and CTA combined with original imagery, video, pointer-responsive interaction, or a justified Three.js scene — followed by a coherent section progression to a final CTA and footer, with disciplined typography/spacing and refined hover, focus, active, loading, disabled, error, touch, and reduced-motion states throughout.
- **Frame by frame:** Page load → a composed GSAP intro sequence plays in the hero while navigation, primary message, and CTA stay readable and usable before the animation completes. Scroll → headings reveal word by word with a restrained stagger, then supporting copy and media sequence after them; ScrollTrigger drives only justified scrubbed or pinned sequences. Pointer → effects are additive and respond without breaking on touch, keyboard, coarse pointers, window blur, or visibility change. Reduced motion / no JS / WebGL failure → the static first frame is complete and final states render immediately (not merely shortened animations).
- **Mechanism & key values:** Stack decisions are hard rules: GSAP is the primary animation system; evaluate Lenis and Locomotive Scroll and choose exactly ONE as the sole smooth-scroll engine — never install or initialize both; connect it to ScrollTrigger, refresh after media/font changes, destroy on cleanup. CSS handles simple hover/focus/tap; one system only controls any given property. Split-text rules: preserve an unsplit accessible name, hide decorative split words from assistive technology, never split links or meaningful inline markup, keep unsplit content visible without JS. Three.js gates: only when spatial depth, texture transition, displacement, or pointer response materially supports the direction; canvas has one clear responsibility, subordinate to content; cap device pixel ratio, pause offscreen/hidden, throttle pointer input, no per-frame allocation, static poster provided, canvas replaced entirely under reduced motion or WebGL failure, full disposal (frames, observers, listeners, render targets, textures, geometries, materials, renderer) plus context-loss handling. Asset honesty rules: no model-authored SVG/CSS/canvas illustrations (transparent PNG cutouts, generated or licensed, instead; simple brand marks, interface icons, data graphics, and a justified shader canvas excepted); photographs for every avatar — never initials, illustrated heads, silhouettes, or generated people presented as real customers/staff; Solar icons via Iconify for interface symbols, Iconify SVG Logos only for legitimate real marks in truthful contexts, Logo Ipsum only for explicitly disclosed fictional specimens, and omit the logo wall when no honest proof exists. Explicit rejects: generic gradient blobs, ornamental bento grids, glass everywhere, stock component layouts, fake testimonials, invented partnerships, logo-wall theater, motion with no narrative role. Before coding, select and name at least one compatible installed web-design skill and write a compact direction (visual thesis, hero focal asset, type hierarchy, color system, section sequence, motion narrative, chosen scroll engine, Three.js decision, asset provenance plan).
- **Reference / source:** GSAP + ScrollTrigger; Lenis or Locomotive Scroll (one only); Three.js; Iconify (Solar icons, SVG Logos); Logo Ipsum (fictional specimens only); Aura.build imagery only when the user requests it or it is relevant and available, as inspiration not an asset library.
- **Best for:** Whole-homepage builds at the portfolio quality bar — the umbrella build doctrine under which the scroll & motion family (⟦S1321⟧–⟦S1328⟧) supplies mechanisms. Applies to every section; its honesty rules (real photos, no fake proof, no invented claims) are binding on trade pages.
- **Tier:** CROWN (the bank's own top-level build system for award-tier sites — the governing whole-page reference).
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1320⟧

## ⟦S1321⟧ cinematic-gsap-lenis-motion-system — Web design — scroll & motion
- **What it is:** A complete, reusable cinematic motion system — GSAP + ScrollTrigger + Lenis behind a small data-attribute markup API — covering masked text reveals, scroll reveals, clip image reveals, parallax, pinned horizontal galleries and story scenes, magnetic hovers, a custom cursor, and mouse-reactive layers, all sharing one set of motion tokens.
- **How it looks:** A luxury-editorial page that moves as one connected language: headlines rise word by word out of masks with a soft blur resolving; images unclip top-to-bottom while settling from a slight zoom; background photographs drift slower than the content scrolling over them; a gallery pins and travels sideways; links and buttons lean toward the cursor; a difference-blend cursor dot follows with a lag and swells with a label ("Explore") over interactive elements. Nothing bounces or springs — everything is smooth, slightly delayed, intentional.
- **Frame by frame:** Scroll into a headline (trigger at top 82–84% of viewport) → each word starts 110% below its mask, invisible, blurred 8px → words rise one after another (0.055s stagger) over 0.9s on power4.out, blur clearing to 0 → line version: lines rise 100% with 0.11s stagger over 1s. A reveal group enters → items start 36px down, invisible, blurred → rise over 0.95s, 0.075s stagger. An image figure enters → clip-path inset animates from inset(0 0 100% 0) to inset(0 0 0% 0) over 1.1s while the image scales 1.08→1 and fades 0.75→1 over 1.2s. Scrolling a parallax section → the 115%-height image travels up by viewportHeight × speed (default 0.18) across the section's passage, scrubbed with 1.2s of lag. A horizontal gallery pins at top → the track slides left by (scrollWidth − viewport width) over an added scroll distance equal to scrollWidth, scrub 1. A story scene pins → panels translate up 100% × (panels − 1) and depth layers shift −16% as scroll advances (scrub 1.1). Hovering a magnetic element → it translates toward the pointer at 0.18 × offset (quickTo 0.45s power3.out) and eases back to 0 on leave. Moving the mouse → the cursor follows with 0.35s quickTo lag; entering a labelled target scales it to 1.75 and shows the label; mouse-parallax layers drift at their depth factor (default 0.04, quickTo 0.8s).
- **Mechanism & key values:** Lenis: lerp 0.08, smoothWheel true, wheelMultiplier 0.9, anchors true; Lenis RAF driven through the GSAP ticker with lagSmoothing(0); ScrollTrigger.refresh() on window load. GSAP defaults: ease power3.out, duration 0.85. Token ranges: eases power3.out / power4.out / expo.out only (bounce, elastic, springy banned); scrub 0.8–1.4; reveals 0.75–1.1s; hover 0.35–0.6s; cursor lag 0.25–0.45s; word stagger 0.035–0.07s; line stagger 0.08–0.14s; card stagger 0.06–0.1s; reveal trigger start "top 82%"; anticipatePin 1. Reveal presets: fade-up y 32→0, blur-in y 18 + blur 10px→0, scale 0.96→1, slide-left x 48→0, slide-right x −48→0 — all with autoAlpha. Parallax images: height 115%, object-fit cover. Hover recipes: magnetic scale kept under 1.03; magnetic card tilt rotateX/rotateY under 4deg; image zoom 1→1.06 over 0.7s power3.out; animated arrow x 0→6 with duplicate fade-in; directional hover movement under 16px. Cursor: position fixed, z-index 9999, mix-blend-mode difference, hidden under (prefers-reduced-motion) or (pointer: coarse). Markup API: data-motion-text="words|lines", data-reveal / data-reveal-group / data-reveal-item, data-image-reveal, data-parallax-section / data-parallax-image / data-parallax-speed, data-horizontal-gallery / data-horizontal-track, data-story-scene / data-story-panel / data-story-depth, data-magnetic / data-magnetic-strength, data-cursor / data-cursor-label, data-mouse-parallax / data-mouse-depth. Accessibility: content hidden by CSS only under html.has-motion (set by JS), split text keeps an aria-label of the full text with split spans aria-hidden; reduced motion sets everything to final state and skips Lenis entirely. Performance: transform/opacity/short clip-path only; blur only on text or small elements; will-change only on animating elements; gsap.context() + ctx.revert() in SPAs.
- **Reference / source:** GSAP + ScrollTrigger docs (gsap.com/docs/v3), Lenis (github.com/darkroomengineering/lenis) — bundled REFERENCES.md. Sibling system: ⟦S1322⟧ cinematic-scroll-storytelling shares the stack and near-identical tokens but is organized as a page anatomy (preloader, sticky stack) rather than a reusable attribute API.
- **Best for:** The motion backbone of a whole homepage — heroes (masked word/line reveals), work/gallery (clip reveals, pinned horizontal gallery), process/story sections (pinned story scenes, parallax), navigation/CTAs (magnetic, cursor). This is the general-purpose system the trade builds standardize on.
- **Tier:** CROWN (the bank's flagship reusable motion system — complete code + tokens, proven pattern family).
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1321⟧

## ⟦S1322⟧ cinematic-scroll-storytelling — Web design — scroll & motion
- **What it is:** A page-level recipe for a cinematic scroll-driven landing page on Lenis + GSAP ScrollTrigger: preloader, parallax hero, kinetic split-text intro, story sections, a sticky project card stack, scrubbed progression scenes, and a parallax footer reveal — a fixed anatomy with build order, prompt template, and QA checklist.
- **How it looks:** The page opens on a black preloader with a thin progress bar and brand/title, which slides away upward to reveal a hero whose background image drifts against masked headline words rising into place; scrolling, each story block arrives composed (fade-up with blur resolving), projects stack as full cards that layer and recede with depth, and the footer is uncovered by a slow upward parallax handoff.
- **Frame by frame:** Load → preloader bar scales X 0→1 over 1.1s (power3.out, origin left) → after a 0.15s beat the whole loader slides up (yPercent −100, 0.9s, power4.inOut) and is removed → hero headline words rise from 110% below their masks, blurred 8px, staggering 0.05s over 0.95s (power4.out) as the hero settles. Scroll into a story section (top 82%) → items rise 36px, fade in, un-blur over 1s with 0.08s stagger, once only. A pinned progression scene (scroll length +140% of viewport, scrub 1.1) → media eases scale 1.08→1 while copy blocks fade/rise 40px with 0.15 stagger, all linear to scroll. Scrolling the project stack → each sticky card (top: 12vh) is covered by the next; as the next card travels from 78% to 24% of viewport height, the covered card scales down toward 0.92 (+0.015 per index), fades to 0.72 opacity, and shifts up 24px. Parallax layers move viewportHeight × speed (default −0.16; hero example −0.18) across their section, scrub 1. Footer → rises from yPercent −12 at 0.85 opacity to rest position at full opacity by the time its top reaches 45% of the viewport.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Same core stack as ⟦S1321⟧: Lenis lerp 0.08, smoothWheel, wheelMultiplier 0.9, RAF via GSAP ticker, lagSmoothing(0), ScrollTrigger.refresh() on load. Motion tokens: enter ease power3.out/power4.out; scrubbed scenes ease "none" with scrub 0.8–1.4; text reveal 0.8–1.1s; card reveal 0.9–1.2s; word stagger 0.035–0.07s; line stagger 0.08–0.14s; card stagger 0.06–0.1s; reveal offset y 24–48; blur 4–10px → 0; sticky card scale depth 1 down to 0.92. Page anatomy in order: 1 Preloader, 2 Hero (image parallax + masked headline + scroll cue), 3 Intro (word-by-word kinetic type), 4 Story sections, 5 Recent Projects sticky stack, 6 Gallery/proof (scrubbed horizontal or progressive reveals), 7 Footer parallax reveal. Markup: data-preloader/data-preloader-bar, data-parallax-section/data-parallax-layer[data-speed], data-split-reveal (="words"), data-story-section/data-reveal-item, data-sticky-stack/data-stack-card, data-progress-scene/data-progress-media/data-progress-copy, data-footer-parallax. Build order is prescribed: static page → preloader + hero → split reveals → section reveals → sticky stack → parallax → scrubbed pins → reduced-motion/touch fallbacks → browser QA. Reduced motion: preloader removed instantly, all reveals set to final state, no smooth-scroll layer. Avoid list: bounce/elastic/springy, aggressive scale jumps, gaming effects, too many simultaneous scroll effects, scroll hijacking that harms reading.
- **Reference / source:** GSAP ScrollTrigger docs and Lenis repo (bundled REFERENCES.md). Sibling of ⟦S1321⟧ — same stack and tokens; choose this for the storytelling page anatomy (preloader + sticky stack + footer reveal), ⟦S1321⟧ for the reusable attribute-driven system.
- **Best for:** Hero-to-footer storytelling homepages and portfolio case-study pages: hero (parallax + masked reveal), work/gallery (sticky card stack is a strong "our work" mechanism — each project card covers the last), process (progression scenes), footer (parallax reveal). One idea per pinned viewport; keep pins limited on mobile per its own QA.
- **Tier:** CROWN (complete page-level storytelling system with code, tokens, and anatomy — a first-choice homepage skeleton).
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1322⟧

## ⟦S1323⟧ pointer-trail-emitter — Web design — scroll & motion
- **What it is:** A cursor-trail mechanism whose spacing stays constant at any hand speed: motes are emitted per unit of distance travelled, not on a timer, so a flick draws the same continuous ribbon as a crawl. Vanilla JavaScript + Canvas 2D (the bundled demo "Wisps"); the skill also covers anchoring the trail in a 3-D scene.
- **How it looks:** Moving the pointer lays a ribbon of small soft motes — a few pixels of core inside a faint halo — evenly spaced along the path, drifting with a slow curl and a slight buoyant rise after the hand passes, then fading out over ~1.5–2.75s. A resting hand keeps a faint aura (one mote every ~0.42s) instead of a growing column. On a neutral dark field the ribbon reads as wisps/sparks/embers depending on palette.
- **Frame by frame:** Pointer moves → the emitter damps toward the pointer (lag, not pinned) → travelled distance accumulates → each time the accumulator crosses the 0.030-unit step, a mote spawns at its exact owed position along that frame's segment (sub-segment placement, capped at 14 spawns per frame against teleports) → motes launch slightly against the direction of travel (−0.09 along, ±0.19 lateral), coast under weak damping (1 − 0.5·dt), curl (sin/cos per-mote phase), and rise (+0.022·dt) → opacity fades in over the first 12% of life and out from 22% to 100%, size softening ×(1 + 0.55u) → ring buffer recycles slots (slot taken BEFORE the index advances — advancing first makes every mote appear where the previous one started).
- **Mechanism & key values:** Tuned table (trail hanging 3.4 units from a 36° camera, plane ≈2.2 units tall — scale spatial values by your own plane extent): emission step 0.030 units; spawns-per-frame cap 14; emitter damping damp(…, 16, dt); scatter ±0.30 units (≈13% of plane height); depth jitter ±0.45 units; life 1.45–2.75s (idle motes 2.1–3.4s); coast damping 1 − 0.5·dt (halved from 1.1, which stopped motes within 0.1 unit); buoyancy +0.022·dt; curl sin(t·1.3 + φ)·0.17, cos(t·1.1 + 1.7φ)·0.14; size 0.018–0.050; count 190 desktop / 90 low tier; idle emission every 0.42s. Measured proof: over one fixed path, distance emission laid 1,885 motes slowly vs 1,738 quickly (1.08× spread); a timer laid 2,537 vs 1,545 (1.64×). Cost: per-mote update measured 0.00% of CPU samples — the real cost is additive fill, so sprite size first, count second. 3-D anchoring: parent points to the camera and work in camera space (half-height = tan(fov·π/360) × distance), depthTest/depthWrite false, own render order/layer so the trail never appears in reflection passes. Round sprites drop the per-particle angle attribute entirely. DOM-overlay port for z-index is explicitly argued against (loses bloom/post chain; every constant needs unit conversion, px_per_unit = (innerHeight/2) / (tan(fov/2) × D)). Lifecycle: gate on (hover: none) for touch; dt clamped ≈1/30s; DPR cap 2; pause on document.hidden with time-base reset; reduced motion renders a designed still frame of the laid ribbon, controls still live; keyboard path required — nothing may depend on the pointer alone.
- **Reference / source:** Authored technique skill (extracted from a shipped build per the ⟦S1319⟧ method); demo "Wisps" (Vanilla JavaScript · Canvas 2D, CSS interface only — no WebGL/shaders/Three.js). Named alternatives inside the skill: add-shader-cursor-trail and shaders-cursor-ripples for packaged WebGPU looks, reveal-hover-effect (⟦S1324⟧) when the cursor exposes an image, ambient-section-particles when motes fill a section.
- **Best for:** Hero atmosphere on dark, image-led heroes — a signature pointer moment. Use sparingly: it is a cursor effect, not a section structure. Trade fit: one hero only, subtle palette matched to the brand; never over forms, copy-dense sections, or on touch (no hover position exists).
- **Tier:** STRONG (complete mechanism with measured values; a hero-accent effect, not a page system).
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1323⟧

## ⟦S1324⟧ reveal-hover-effect — Web design — scroll & motion
- **What it is:** A cursor-following spotlight reveal: a second, perfectly aligned image is stacked over a base image and exposed through a soft feathered radial CSS mask that follows the eased pointer — hover-to-color, before/after, x-ray, material, and texture reveals.
- **How it looks:** The visitor sees the base treatment full-frame (e.g. a product in pale linework, or a roof in flat desaturated tones). Where the cursor rests, a soft circular window of the second treatment (full color, finished material) opens — fully solid through the center, feathering invisibly to nothing at the edge — and glides after the pointer with a slight trailing ease. Move away and the window shrinks closed, leaving the plain base image.
- **Frame by frame:** Pointer enters → the spotlight opens directly under the pointer (never sweeping in from the component center) → radius grows toward 260px (radius easing 0.14 per frame) while the position trails the raw pointer (easing 0.1) → moving the pointer drags the feathered circle, the reveal image visible only inside it (mask alpha 1 through 40% of radius, then 0.75 at 60%, 0.4 at 75%, 0.12 at 88%, 0 at 100%) → pointer leaves, cancels, or the window blurs → target radius returns to 0 and the mask collapses → the RAF loop stops once position and radius settle. Optional background grid (48px, opacity ~0.1) drifts at most ±16px with a slower 0.06 ease.
- **Mechanism & key values:** CSS mask-image radial-gradient on the overlay (both mask-* and -webkit-mask-* declared), driven by --reveal-x / --reveal-y / --reveal-radius custom properties from one requestAnimationFrame loop. Desktop spotlight radius 260px; compact 140–220px; computed fallback radius = min(260, max(140, component width × 0.22)), overridable via data-reveal-radius. Position ease 0.1, radius ease 0.14; under reduced motion both become 1 (direct update, no trailing) and grid parallax is disabled. Hard requirements: both images identical dimensions, composition, crop, focal point, object-fit and object-position (a one-pixel mismatch shows inside the spotlight); coordinates converted with getBoundingClientRect (page coordinates drift after scroll); first-pointermove-without-enter handled; scroll/resize recalculation via ResizeObserver; coarse pointers (hover: none) get the static base image, plus an explicit "Show alternate" toggle control when the reveal carries unique information (the demo's "Reveal material" button toggles the full overlay). Overlay image is aria-hidden/decorative when both images show the same subject; native cursor stays visible. Performance: no canvas.toDataURL per frame, will-change on the masked overlay only, loop stops at idle, cleanup returned for framework unmount. Nested variant: foreground glass/refraction cards can run the same mask with viewport pointer state minus the card's rect, updated in the same frame so the refraction never lags.
- **Reference / source:** MDN references bundled (mask-image, radial-gradient, requestAnimationFrame, pointermove, prefers-reduced-motion). Demo: "Materia" — a 1586×992 aligned pair, mineral plaster base revealing an opal-glass/chrome treatment, 48px technical grid, serif editorial hero.
- **Best for:** Work/gallery and product-detail moments — before/after is its named trade use: a worn surface revealing the finished result under the visitor's own cursor is a strong interactive proof device for roofing/siding/remodeling galleries and hero product shots. Needs a genuinely aligned image pair; misalignment kills it.
- **Tier:** STRONG (complete mechanism with exact mask stops and easing values; a single-component effect with a direct trade application).
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1324⟧

## ⟦S1325⟧ scroll-progress-timeline — Web design — scroll & motion
- **What it is:** A data-driven scroll timeline: an ordered process rendered as a semantic ordered list, connected by one line whose progress fill tracks the reader's scroll position, with steps activating as the fill head crosses them.
- **How it looks:** A quiet base line runs from the center of the first step's dot to the center of the last; on top of it, a filled progress line grows downward (vertical) or rightward (horizontal) exactly with scroll, in both directions. Steps sit beside the line — centered alternating on wide screens when both sides carry similar weight, a single left rail for long copy — each step's dot and content lighting into its active state as the fill reaches it, while inactive steps stay fully readable.
- **Frame by frame:** Scroll down → the viewport anchor advances between the first and last point centers → normalized progress = (viewportAnchor − lineStart) / (lineEnd − lineStart), clamped 0–1 → the fill scales (scaleY for vertical, scaleX for horizontal, transform-origin top/left) in one coalesced animation frame → the step whose center the progress head crosses becomes active (aria-current="step" only when meaningful, never live-announced per update) → scroll back up and the fill retreats and steps deactivate in reverse. Fonts/images loading or resize → geometry is re-measured.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Content is data-driven (array of {id, number, title, body}) rendered as a real <ol> with real headings — the line and active states enhance the structure, never replace it. Measure first and last point centers, not section edges; apply scale transforms so updates stay on the compositor; schedule DOM writes in one RAF. Layout rules: centered alternating only with sufficient width and balanced content; left rail for long copy/compact steps/mixed card heights; horizontal for short sequences with keyboard-safe overflow; pinned full-screen chapters only when each step carries a distinct visual state, pin kept finite; small screens collapse to a simple left rail without changing reading order. Active-state animation kept small: opacity, translate, scale, blur, color, or media transitions. Use IntersectionObserver for simple active-state entry; normalized scroll measurement or GSAP ScrollTrigger when the fill must be continuous or coordinate pinned media. Navigation: step links are real anchors with scroll-margin for sticky headers; focus is never moved during passive scrolling; URLs/history stay stable unless the user selects a step. Reduced motion: complete line or discrete reached states, no scrubbed interpolation, blur, pinning, or large transforms.
- **Reference / source:** Bundled REFERENCES.md: GSAP ScrollTrigger docs, MDN CSS transforms, IntersectionObserver, ResizeObserver, aria-current. Demo: "Fieldwork — From Question to Proof" — four uneven editorial steps beside a sticky chapter title, each with number, phase, heading, description, evidence tag, and media panel.
- **Best for:** Process sections — this is the direct mechanism for a trade "how it works" (survey → quote → install → guarantee) that fills as the visitor reads; also roadmaps, case-study sequences, service journeys. Vertical left-rail form is the mobile-safe default for trade pages.
- **Tier:** STRONG (complete, numbers-light but structurally exact; the canonical process-section mechanism).
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1325⟧

## ⟦S1326⟧ scroll-scrubbed-visual-sequence — Web design — scroll & motion
- **What it is:** A reversible scroll-controlled visual transformation: a sticky or pinned stage whose visual state is a pure function of normalized scroll progress, rendered by video, image sequence, canvas, SVG, or DOM — product assembly, object rotation, hero transformation, diagram walkthrough.
- **How it looks:** One full-viewport stage stays fixed while the page scrolls beneath it; the object on stage transforms continuously and exactly with the scrollbar — an exploded assembly drawing itself together, a product rotating, a photo sequence advancing frame by frame — with copy stops changing at set progress points. Scroll back and every state replays in reverse, identically; the same scroll position always shows the same frame.
- **Frame by frame:** Scroll into the tall section (height set from scrollVh) → the sticky stage locks to the viewport → progress = (viewportTop − sectionTop) / (sectionHeight − viewportHeight), clamped 0–1 → the renderer maps progress to its state (video currentTime with RAF-coalesced seeks, image-sequence frame index clamped 0…frameCount−1, canvas redraw only when progress changes, SVG/DOM transforms/opacity/clip-path/CSS variables) with no implicit easing → copy stops activate at their configured progress points (example stops 0, 0.42, 0.78) → at progress 1 the stage releases cleanly and the next section takes over. No wheel delta, elapsed time, or autoplay is ever the source of truth.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Example configuration from the skill: scrollVh 280, frameCount 96, fit "contain", posterFrame 0, reducedMotionFrame 95, copyStops [0, 0.42, 0.78]. Renderer selection rules: video for continuous/photographic sequences (frequent keyframes, preload metadata, reserve aspect ratio); image sequence for exact art-directed frames (preload current frame first, then nearby — never block first paint on the whole set); canvas for procedural drawing (DPR cap 2, redraw only on progress change); SVG/DOM for diagrams, product cards, interface states, accessible text; WebGL only when depth/lighting/a real 3D camera materially strengthens it (static poster + disposal required). GSAP form: ScrollTrigger.create with start "top top", end += innerHeight × 2.8 for the example, pin, scrub: true, invalidateOnRefresh, onUpdate render(progress); a dependency-free implementation measures on scroll/resize with one render per animation frame. Media safety: poster visible until the first real frame paints; cancel stale image requests; never queue every seek during fast scrolling; object-fit with an explicit focal point so the subject survives mobile crops; pause while offscreen or document hidden; full cleanup on route change. Smoothing is optional and added only after correctness is proven. Reduced motion: pinning and scrubbing removed, the selected static frame rendered, ordinary document flow restored; ordered information also exposed as text or a list.
- **Reference / source:** Bundled REFERENCES.md: GSAP ScrollTrigger docs, MDN video element, Canvas API, requestAnimationFrame, prefers-reduced-motion. Demo: "Aperture 04 — Matter to Memory" — an inline-SVG optical object (rings, shards, core, labels, measurement grid) going exploded → calibrated → resolved across one sticky chapter.
- **Best for:** Hero transformations and product/process walkthroughs — for trades: a roof assembly building up layer by layer, a window cross-section assembling, a before→after photo sequence scrubbed by scroll. One sequence per page is the sane budget; it is a stage mechanism, not a whole-page system.
- **Tier:** STRONG (complete renderer-agnostic mechanism with exact progress math and a worked config).
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1326⟧

## ⟦S1327⟧ scroll-scrubbed-word-reveal — Web design — scroll & motion
- **What it is:** A text reveal where a marked-up passage becomes readable word by word as scroll progress advances — words interpolate from quiet (low opacity, blurred, slightly dropped) to normal type — while inline links, emphasis, and responsive wrapping survive untouched.
- **How it looks:** A headline, quote, or manifesto paragraph sits in normal document flow, its later words ghosted back — faint, soft-focused, sunk a fraction of an em. As the reader scrolls, clarity sweeps through the text word by word in reading order, each word sharpening and settling into full-strength type; scroll back and the words ghost again in reverse. It reads as comprehension being paced, not as typing.
- **Frame by frame:** Scroll advances section progress → each word's local progress = clamp(reveal × wordCount − index) → the word's --word-progress custom property updates → opacity rises from its hidden value (0.12–0.3) to 1, blur falls from 4–10px to 0, vertical offset rises from 0.08–0.22em to 0 → neighbouring words overlap slightly (10–30% direct word overlap) so the sweep feels continuous → at full progress the passage is identical to normal typography. Reduced motion: every word shown immediately, no blur, transforms, or pinning.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Preparation is the mechanism: keep one untouched accessible text source; walk text nodes with TreeWalker (never flatten with textContent/innerHTML); skip script, style, form controls, and [data-no-split] elements; replace only non-whitespace tokens with spans, preserving whitespace nodes exactly; generated spans are aria-hidden only when an equivalent unsplit accessible copy remains. Scroll span scales with text length: 120–220% of viewport height for a paragraph — no fixed line count, no line-based splitting (wraps must stay free to change with width, language, zoom, font loading). Easing: none in the scroll mapping; ease only the visual interpolation when needed. Implementation: GSAP ScrollTrigger with scrub when precise start/end/refresh or a shared timeline is needed; dependency-free scroll measurement + RAF for a standalone section. Emphasis rules: links/strong/em/mark/accent spans keep semantics and styling; color inherited by default; accents styled on the original element, not token indexes; essential links never revealed only after being passed; re-split only when source text changes. Cleanup: kill ScrollTriggers, remove listeners, cancel frames, restore the original marked-up subtree; refresh geometry after fonts load when positions depend on text metrics. Banned by the skill: typewriter cursor, random delays, autoplay (unless explicitly requested).
- **Reference / source:** Bundled REFERENCES.md: GSAP ScrollTrigger docs, MDN TreeWalker / createTreeWalker, MDN prefers-reduced-motion, WAI page-structure tutorial. Demo: "A Field Note on Attention" — an editorial manifesto on a warm paper field with a compact progress rail.
- **Best for:** Manifesto/statement moments — a firm's promise, a guarantee statement, a founder quote, the intro paragraph of a story section (⟦S1322⟧ uses the same device for its intro beat). One passage per page; ideal for the single big claim a trade homepage makes before its proof sections.
- **Tier:** STRONG (complete mechanism with exact defaults; the canonical text-in-motion device).
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1327⟧

## ⟦S1328⟧ scroll-world-storytelling — Web design — scroll & motion
- **What it is:** A whole-page storytelling system: turn an article, case study, or brand narrative into one connected scroll-driven journey using exactly one of three renderers — scrubbed video, a real-time Three.js world, or semantic HTML/SVG data and typography — chosen before building and never mixed by default.
- **How it looks:** One visual world holds the entire page: a continuous camera flight through a place (video mode), a single 3D object/planet/system that the scroll orbits and transforms (Three.js mode), or an editorial evidence-ledger of kinetic type, charts, and metrics (HTML mode). Copy arrives in 5–7 deliberate beats over a pinned or sticky stage; there are no ordinary stacked sections, one quiet navigation, and one final CTA.
- **Frame by frame:** Scroll → one normalized scroll value drives the single renderer: video mode coalesces seeks in requestAnimationFrame so currentTime tracks scroll forward and backward exactly, the first frame serving as poster until the video paints; Three.js mode maps progress to camera position/target, object rotation, lights, and scene states while ambient motion stays subordinate; HTML mode drives CSS custom properties, chart stroke offsets, bar scales, counters, and active copy from the same value → each beat (scroll weight 0.7–1.8 viewport heights) activates its scene, eyebrow, headline, and one-sentence body at its scroll position → reverse scrolling restores the exact prior state with no jump, flash, or unintended reversal at any seam → the final beat presents the single CTA. Reduced motion: poster or ordered stills (video), static CSS/SVG poster (Three.js), or uninterpolated state changes (HTML), all in ordinary document flow.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Story map first: 5–7 beats (Hook, Old way, New rule, Mechanism, Proof, Payoff, Action) in a beat ledger — eyebrow 2–4 words, headline 3–8 words, body one sentence ideally under 24 words, evidence an exact source fact or asset, motion one verb phrase, CTA on the final beat only. Style bible: 3 precise mood adjectives, one world metaphor, 4–6 named colors (one dominant field, one accent), one display + one reading type voice, one material language, one motion grammar (forward glide, orbit, crane, lateral track, dive, staged reveal), 3 excluded clichés; for generated media the style preamble is reused byte-for-byte in every asset prompt. Video mode: one continuous 6–15s camera move, no cuts; three materially different style studies before generating; prefer 16:9, 6–10s, 720p for a first pass; multi-leg journeys start each leg from the previous leg's actual last frame; encode for scrubbing with ffmpeg: libx264, preset slow, crf 20, yuv420p, GOP 8 (-g 8 -keyint_min 8 -sc_threshold 0), +faststart, audio stripped; byte-range hosting or Blob URL before scrubbing. Three.js mode: three art-direction studies that change field/material/light/type relationship/composition (the glowing-blue-planet default is explicitly rejected unless earned); one scene/camera/renderer/world group; DPR cap 2; pause when hidden/off-screen; dispose on teardown; local pinned Three.js files, no remote CDN for the core renderer. HTML mode: semantic HTML first, one truthful chart grammar (bars, line, range, slope, comparison), labels as selectable text, values exposed in accessible text or a table, page complete with JavaScript disabled — and it must not secretly become Canvas/WebGL. House rules: preserve the source thesis, sequence, facts, and caveats; never invent proof; native reversible scrolling, never hijack the wheel; one primary CTA; never spend generation credits or publish without approval. Verification is a 10-point fresh pass (story, timing, reverse, performance, responsive at 390/768/1024/1440, mobile, accessibility, integrity, console, mode proof), repeated until no material gap remains.
- **Reference / source:** Bundled REFERENCES.md: github.com/oso95/scroll-world, Three.js docs, MDN (HTMLMediaElement.currentTime, requestAnimationFrame, prefers-reduced-motion, SVG stroke-dashoffset), ffmpeg docs, x.ai Grok video-generation docs (the video demo uses Grok Imagine). Demo set "The Contract" — a three-mode launcher with video, threejs, and html-data folders sharing six beats (Destination, Fence, Bar, Loop, Route, Proof).
- **Best for:** A full homepage-as-journey for a story-led build — case-study pages, a firm's founding-to-proof narrative, a product journey. Heaviest of the scroll family: choose ONE mode and budget accordingly (video = asset/seek tuning cost; Three.js = WebGL performance + fallback work; HTML = lightest and most accessible). For trade homepages the HTML/data mode fits proof-and-numbers stories; the video mode fits a cinematic place/craft story. Clash note: do not combine with a second pinned full-screen system (⟦S1321⟧/⟦S1322⟧ pins) on the same page.
- **Tier:** CROWN (the bank's most complete scroll-world system — story method, three production modes, encoding values, verification bar).
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1328⟧

## ⟦S1329⟧ staggered-word-reveal — Web design — scroll & motion
- **What it is:** A word-by-word text reveal for short headlines and intros: the text is split into word spans and each word fades in and rises into place, once, when the text scrolls into view. Vanilla CSS + IntersectionObserver; no SplitText or heavy library needed.
- **How it looks:** A headline sits invisible with every word dropped 20px; as it enters the viewport the words appear one after another in reading order, each gliding up and fading in over 0.8s, until the whole line rests calm and fully readable. Editorial and restrained — no bounce, rotation or blur.
- **Frame by frame:** Trigger: the element becomes ~20% visible (IntersectionObserver threshold 0.2, rootMargin "0px 0px -10% 0px"). Word 0 transitions opacity 0→1 and translateY(20px)→0 over 0.8s; each following word starts 0.07s after the previous one; when the last word lands the observer unobserves the element, so it never replays. With JavaScript disabled the text is simply visible; under reduced motion the words are shown statically with no transition.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Words wrapped in inline-block spans with `transition-delay: calc(var(--word-index) * 0.07s)`; duration 0.8s; ease cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); stagger 0.06–0.08s per word (default 0.07s); initial state opacity 0 / translate3d(0, 20px, 0); animate transform + opacity only. Splitter preserves spaces, avoids innerHTML, puts the original sentence in an aria-label and marks word spans aria-hidden. GSAP equivalent given: fromTo y 20→0, opacity 0→1, duration 0.8, ease "expo.out", stagger 0.07.
- **Reference / source:** None named. Bundled demo/PROMPT.md only (canonical demo lines "Motion should / explain the / next state", four-part timeline with a keyboard-accessible Replay control).
- **Best for:** Hero headlines, section intros, pull quotes, short marketing lines on any homepage. Do not use on long paragraphs or text containing links/buttons.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1329⟧

## ⟦S1330⟧ add-mouse-driven-orbit — Web design — WebGL / Three.js / shaders
- **What it is:** Passive pointer parallax for a Three.js hero: one damped, normalized pointer target is split across camera translation, a carried look-at, and unequal rotations of near and far object groups, so the scene pivots with depth instead of sliding like a poster. Not OrbitControls — the visitor never drags or inspects.
- **How it looks:** The visitor moves the mouse and a 3D subject (the source scene is a procedural moss root in a grey-green field, white Lexend headline and pale card pinned over it) turns gently toward the pointer: the camera arcs one way, the near form yaws a little more than the far layer, and the composition stays framed around the copy. Leave the window and everything eases back to the authored center pose.
- **Frame by frame:** Trigger: pointermove (touch pointers ignored). The handler records only normalized coordinates (−1..1). Each frame the smoothed value damps toward the target (0.055 per 60 Hz frame, frame-rate corrected as 1 − (1−0.055)^(dt·60)); camera position goes to (−smooth.x × 26, smooth.y × 16), lookAt carries 42% of the camera offset, near group rotates y 0.055 rad / x 0.026 rad, far group y 0.030 rad — all in stage-pixel world units from the source. On pointerleave the target resets to 0,0 and the scene eases home. Values are rounded to 3 decimals and only published when changed.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Three.js; ResizeObserver-cached viewport rect (never getBoundingClientRect in the pointer handler); dt clamped to 1/30 s; DPR capped at 2; pause when hidden/offscreen; CSS parallax can share the same smoothed pair with smaller coefficients for text. Reduced motion: a designed three-quarter still at approx. x=.28, y=−.12, with keyboard-operable X/Y range controls still live. Full teardown (cancel frame, disconnect observers, dispose Three resources) specified.
- **Reference / source:** Extracted from inner-green-3d.html; bundled demo "Sylva — Living Orbit" (demo/PROMPT.md).
- **Best for:** Cinematic 3D heroes, pointer-responsive hero objects, organic model parallax. For trade pages: a hero product/material visual that should feel alive without becoming a product viewer.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1330⟧

## ⟦S1331⟧ add-shader-cursor-trail — Web design — WebGL / Three.js / shaders
- **What it is:** The exact Shaders-library (WebGPU) halftone cursor trail used on the Tidal Commons hero: an invisible fluid flow field follows the cursor and drives a grid of twinkling white dots, finished with chromatic ripples and film grain, implemented as progressive enhancement over a static hero.
- **How it looks:** Over a dark diagonal gradient background, a trail of white halftone dots swells along the path the cursor has just taken and relaxes behind it, the dots twinkling; a subtle chromatic ripple distorts the field and a fine film grain sits over everything. Content and links stay above the layer and fully usable; without WebGPU the visitor just sees the original image/dark background.
- **Frame by frame:** Trigger: cursor movement inside the section. The invisible ChromaFlow node records the pointer path in its alpha channel; the DotGrid node's dotSize is mapped from that alpha (input 0..1 → output 0..1), so dots grow where the flow is fresh and shrink as it decays; the black-to-white gradient is masked through those dots; CursorRipples then adds chromatic distortion and FilmGrain finishes the frame. The layer mounts only when the section is near the viewport and unmounts when it leaves, when the tab hides, or when the window blurs.
- **Mechanism & key values:** The graph is exact and order-locked — six nodes: DotGrid id="trailDots", density 40, twinkle 0.9, visible=false, dotSize driven by inline map from source "trailFlow" alpha; ChromaFlow id="trailFlow", intensity 1.4, radius 2.9, visible=false; LinearGradient #1e1e1f→#070708 (HSL, {0,1}→{1,0}); LinearGradient #000000→#ffffff (HSL, same endpoints, maskSource="trailDots"); CursorRipples with defaults; FilmGrain strength 0.1. Blend guidance: mix-blend-mode screen at opacity ~0.72–0.82 over photographic heroes, normal blending on near-black sections. Capability gates: navigator.gpu present, (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine), no reduced-motion, no reduced-transparency, document visible + window focused, IntersectionObserver. Package `shaders`, imported from shaders/react|vue|svelte|solid; heavy module lazy-loaded behind a lightweight gate component.
- **Reference / source:** The Tidal Commons hero; Shaders docs at https://shaders.com/docs/guide; bundled references/implementation.md. Distinct from ⟦S1338⟧ shaders-cursor-ripples: same library, different effect (dot trail vs image distortion).
- **Best for:** Hero backgrounds and contact-section backgrounds where a premium interactive sheen is wanted. Heavy (WebGPU) — enhancement only, never the carrier of content.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1331⟧

## ⟦S1332⟧ background-grid-webgl — Web design — WebGL / Three.js / shaders
- **What it is:** A perspective WebGL background grid: a ground-plane grid seen from an elevated camera, its lines fading with distance, with sparse particle haze, a slow forward drift and gentle camera parallax.
- **How it looks:** Thin grid lines on a dark field recede toward a horizon and dissolve into darkness rather than ending; a light dust of floating particles gives the space depth; the grid drifts slowly forward so the background feels alive but calm, with the design's accent color used only sparingly for glow/particles — explicitly not a loud synthwave neon floor.
- **Frame by frame:** Continuous ambient loop, no discrete trigger: the grid cycles forward positionally, particles float slowly, and the camera offsets gently with the mouse through damped parallax. The source prescribes the behaviors and tuning knobs but no numeric speeds or timings.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Three.js (or equivalent real WebGL); perspective camera above the plane looking toward the origin; grid built as a large plane helper or custom grid with line opacity fading by distance; additive sparse particle field at low opacity. Tuning knobs named: grid density (plane size, division count, line spacing), fade falloff, forward drift speed, particle float speed, camera height/distance/tilt/parallax strength, accent restraint.

## ⟦S1333⟧ build-interactive-particle-trail — Web design — WebGL / Three.js / shaders
- **What it is:** A pointer/touch particle trail that emits discrete motes by distance traveled along the gesture — interpolated across the whole segment — into a fixed, recycled GPU point pool, so spacing stays consistent at any gesture speed. Optional keyboard-triggered bursts reuse the same pool.
- **How it looks:** Dragging across the source scene (pollen over a procedural moss root) lifts individual grains off the surface: a fast flick and a slow crawl leave the same evenly spaced dotted trail; the grains drift upward with a slight wobble and fade away over about a second and a half. A resting cursor does not grow a bright clump — it trickles single motes. A "Release pollen" button fires a denser burst from the same pool.
- **Frame by frame:** Trigger: pointer/pen/touch movement raycast onto one stable interaction plane. Distance from the previous hit is measured; count = min(14, floor(distance / 7)) motes are spawned interpolated along the segment; if nothing spawned and idle time passes 55 ms, one mote trickles at the current point. In the vertex shader each mote's age = uTime − birth: it travels with drag (1 − 0.34·u), rises 46 units over its life, wobbles sideways sin(phase·2π + age·2.6)·22·u, and its alpha fades in over the first 9% of life and out from 40% to 100%; at 1.6 s it is culled in-shader and its pool slot is recycled by the ring head. Leaving the surface resets the previous hit so re-entry draws no diagonal bridge.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Landed defaults: path spacing 7 units; per-frame emission cap 14; idle interval 55 ms; pool size 620 points; lifetime 1.6 s; random size 0.50–1.15; burst = 40–60 spawns at 2.5× spread. One THREE.Points draw call, prebuilt soft radial sprite, additive blending, depthWrite: false; flight integrated in the vertex shader from typed-array attributes (origin, velocity, birth, seed), uploaded only on respawn. dt clamped to 1/30 s, DPR cap 2, pause hidden/offscreen. Reduced motion: a designed still trail is seeded and the burst button swaps in a denser still.
- **Reference / source:** Extracted from inner-green-3d.html; bundled demo "Sylva — Pollen Trace" (demo/PROMPT.md). Sibling, not duplicate, of ⟦S1331⟧ (continuous shader ribbon) — this one is discrete grains.
- **Best for:** Interactive hero surfaces and gallery moments where the visitor's gesture should disturb the scene (dust off a surface, pollen, sparks). Decorative layer only; keep content in semantic HTML.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1333⟧

## ⟦S1334⟧ build-threejs-scroll-worlds — Web design — WebGL / Three.js / shaders
- **What it is:** The full production system for real-time Three.js scrollytelling: one persistent 3D world (one renderer, one scene) whose camera, lighting, fog, materials, objects, DOM story and interactions evolve through 4–8 authored chapters, conducted by native document scroll via one normalized, reversible scroll state. Includes a world-bible intake/ledger method, a realtime architecture reference, and a QA reference; the bundled Kage demo is the quality bar.
- **How it looks:** One continuous place rather than stacked sections. The Kage reference: a night Kyoto mountain sanctuary — dark blue-black field, vermilion moon, tiered temple on a centered axis, torii, approach stairs, lanterns, dark trees, mist, falling red leaves, wet ground, heavy film grain; muted sage-white uppercase type, a giant foreground KAGE word and large vertical Japanese characters; transparent foreground cut-outs (grass, branches, stones, walls) parked at the viewport edges per chapter. DOM copy stays in real HTML above the fixed canvas, with a chapter rail and progress UI.
- **Frame by frame:** Trigger: native scroll. scrollY converts to a fractional chapter value (e.g. 2.35) from measured section anchors. Exact progress drives chapter ownership, navigation state, foreground ownership and interaction gating; a damped copy (damp(current, target, 5.2, dt)) drives the camera along Catmull–Rom position and target curves with per-segment FOV interpolation (tall viewports get a pullback + FOV opening instead of a crop). Each frame the two adjacent chapters' declared world values — key light, fog density, particles, grade — are lerped and applied. When a chapter wins the viewport, its foreground stage re-parents into a fixed host, slides in fully opaque and settles; the retiring stage fades and blurs out over ~820 ms. Display headings reveal word by word (~72 ms between words in Kage; word-bible range 40–90 ms). Interactions are local only: raycast hover/focus warms light or reveals a label without moving the camera. The journey is fully reversible — the same scroll position recreates the same state forward, backward, after a fast jump and after reload.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Scene graph: worldRoot → environment / architecture (persistent landmarks) / chapterSets / interactives / atmosphere / optional nearPlane3D. Renderer: ACESFilmic tone mapping, sRGB output, PCFSoft shadows; color textures sRGB, data textures linear; KTX2/Basis + Meshopt/Draco compression. Starting budgets: DPR 1.25–1.5 mobile / 1.5–2 desktop; visible triangles 150k–300k / 500k–1.2m; draw calls 50–90 / 90–160; shadowed lights 1–2 / 2–4; blended full-screen layers 2 / 3; critical initial transfer 3–6 MB / 5–10 MB; frame time ≤16.7 ms ideal. Quality tiers (world-bible example): mobile dpr 1.35, shadows 1024, particles 0.45, post "lite"; desktop dpr 1.75, shadows 2048, particles 1, post "full"; governor downgrades after ~120 frames above 22 ms. Motion table: camera damping constant 4.5–7.0; pointer parallax 0.1–0.5° / 0.02–0.12 units; foreground retirement 650–950 ms. Kage camera table (6 chapters) is recorded in full, e.g. ch.1 position [0, 4.05, 13.6], target [0, 6.60, −18.0], fov 36. dt clamped to 1/30 s; pause on hidden; prefetch 1–2 chapters ahead. Reduced motion: snap to nearest composed chapter, stop ambient loops/stagger/blur, keep the full ordered DOM story; WebGL failure: composed poster/stills fallback.
- **Reference / source:** Bundled demo "Kage — Hidden Realms of Kyoto" (demo/index.html) plus references/world-bible.md, references/realtime-architecture.md, references/quality-and-qa.md, references/kage-anatomy.md, references/scroll-conductor.js. Structural strengths (intake, ledgers, budget gates) adapted from the public oso95/scroll-world project, https://github.com/oso95/scroll-world, reviewed at commit 71cc36d — its renderer is a pre-generated video chain; this skill keeps real geometry.
- **Best for:** Flagship immersive homepage journeys, interactive portfolios, exhibitions, product stories. Heavy: for a trade homepage this is a whole-experience commitment with a strict transfer budget, not a section effect — use only when the business story genuinely is a journey.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1334⟧

## ⟦S1335⟧ build-wireframe-scan-reveal — Web design — WebGL / Three.js / shaders
- **What it is:** A 3D model entrance driven by one expanding world-space scan: a temporary wireframe cage (LineSegments built from the same geometry as the solid mesh) rides the wavefront, the solid surface fills in behind it with a lag, then the cage burns away and is disposed.
- **How it looks:** From a low, off-center origin an irregular glowing rim sweeps across the object; at the rim the topology shows as a bright cage with a fading wire trail behind it, and behind the trail the finished solid surface; ahead of the rim there is nothing. As the sweep completes, the wire glow fades out over the last stretch and only the solid form remains — a survey pulse growing the object rather than a circular mask wiping it in.
- **Frame by frame:** Trigger: load or the Replay button. Over 3.4 s the scan radius grows with easing 1 − (1−t)^1.35 toward scene diagonal × 1.3 + 900. The cage snaps on during the first 6% of the timeline; its rim brightness is a Gaussian around the current radius (width 135 units, ×1.60) plus a trail (×0.34) extending 950 units behind the front. The solid's fragment shader discards everything beyond radius − 520 units, with a two-sine wobble (sin(y·0.011 + x·0.007)·36 + sin(z·0.021 + y·0.013)·17) keeping the front irregular. Wire opacity fades via smoothstep(0.72, 1, t); at completion the discard branch is disabled, the cage is removed and its geometry/material disposed.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Both materials share uScanOrigin and uScanRadius in world space (local space tears when groups are scaled/nested). Cage: additive blending, transparent, depthWrite false, depth test kept on, pale version of the scene accent. Duration 3.4 s; solid lag 520 units; rim width 135; trail 950; DPR cap 2; dt clamp 1/30 s; pause hidden/offscreen. Reduced motion: a designed diagnostic still at ~62% radius with cage and solid both visible; Replay recomposes the still and announces state via aria-live.
- **Reference / source:** Extracted from inner-green-3d.html; bundled demo "Sylva — Survey Pulse" (demo/PROMPT.md).
- **Best for:** Hero object entrances, model/product reveals, holographic assembly and survey/inspection-themed sections — a natural fit for an inspection or "what we check" story on a trade page.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1335⟧

## ⟦S1336⟧ globe-gl — Web design — WebGL / Three.js / shaders
- **What it is:** An implementation guide for globe.gl (Globe.GL): a WebGL/Three.js 3D globe for data visualization, with chained-configuration data layers — points, arcs, polygons, paths, heatmaps and hex bins, labels or HTML elements, 3D objects and custom layers — in plain HTML or React (react-globe.gl).
- **How it looks:** A textured earth sphere filling its container that the visitor can drag to steer, carrying glowing data points, arcs between locations, shaded polygons or floating labels. The bundled demo direction centers a luminous 360-point rotating sphere with a faint orbital ellipse inside a restrained technical interface, overlaid with a "Live" field label, a 72.4 metric and a "Drag to steer" hint.
- **Frame by frame:** The demo globe rotates continuously and responds to dragging; beyond that the skill body prescribes no fixed animation values — motion comes from the library and the layers chosen. Container is sized by CSS and the globe fills its parent.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Quick start: `new Globe(el).globeImageUrl(url).pointsData(data)` via ESM import or the CDN script (//cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/globe.gl). Performance guidance: reduce point count/size on mobile; use a darker globe texture for neon-style data overlays. No numeric animation parameters are prescribed in the source.
- **Reference / source:** The globe.gl library; bundled demo/PROMPT.md. Distinct from ⟦S1337⟧ globe-particles (custom particle shader globe, no data layers).
- **Best for:** Data-globe visualizations; on a trade homepage, at most a service-coverage visual if a real location dataset exists — otherwise too data-viz for a homeowner page.
