## ⟦S1337⟧ globe-particles — Web design — WebGL / Three.js / shaders
- **What it is:** A globe built purely from luminous shader particles: a dense spherical core plus a thinner tilted orbital ring or flattened disc, rendered as one THREE.Points cloud with a custom shader — a planetary/data-globe effect with no textures and no data layers.
- **How it looks:** A premium planet of thousands of crisp round points on a dark atmospheric background: the core reads mostly neutral or white-hot, the tilted ring and highlights carry the brand accent color; the globe rotates slowly, breathes almost imperceptibly, and drifts a few degrees toward the mouse. Silhouette stays clean and spherical — depth comes from layered particle density, not bloom.
- **Frame by frame:** Continuous loop: rotation.y advances at rotationSpeed (default 0.12 × t); overall scale breathes 1 + sin(t·0.55)·0.045; each point also breathes in the vertex shader, 1 + sin(u_time·0.65 + layer·4)·0.012; pointer movement tilts rotation.x/z by pointer × mouseStrength (default 0.08) around the base tilt (−0.42, 0.22). Under reduced motion a single still frame renders.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Recipe defaults: sphereCount 2600, ringCount 1300, radius 1.35, ringRadius 2.05, ringThickness 0.12; camera PerspectiveCamera fov 38 at distance 5.6; u_pointSize 18; maxDpr 1.6; additive blending, depthWrite false, transparent; circular soft points via gl_PointCoord smoothstep(0.5, 0.0, d) squared; shell is a square container min(100%, 760px), canvas pointer-events none. Accent defaults to the --brand-accent CSS variable (fallback #8b5cf6 in the recipe example).
- **Reference / source:** Neuform reference demo "NEUS | Enterprise Brand Architecture", https://neuform.ai/pages/neus-enterprise-brand-architecture/index.html (Neuform rank #1 for this skill when synced; 607 views · 21 favorites · 6 remixes).
- **Best for:** Hero centerpiece for planetary, orbital or infrastructure subjects; for trade pages, situational at best — reads sci-fi unless heavily adapted.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1337⟧

## ⟦S1338⟧ shaders-cursor-ripples — Web design — WebGL / Three.js / shaders
- **What it is:** Cursor-following fluid WebGPU distortion over an existing real image, using the Shaders library's ImageTexture + CursorRipples: the photo itself ripples like disturbed water under the pointer. Built to replace drifting CSS spotlight/flashlight reveals, which it instructs to delete outright.
- **How it looks:** A hero or gallery photograph sits perfectly still until the pointer sweeps across it; along the pointer's path the image warps and refracts fluidly, with optional chromatic splitting at the ripple edges, then settles back to the undistorted photo. The real <img> stays underneath the canvas the whole time as the accessible fallback and loading state.
- **Frame by frame:** Trigger: pointer movement over the media panel. Shaders tracks the cursor globally and converts coordinates using the canvas bounds (the canvas itself is pointer-events: none); CursorRipples post-processes the ImageTexture surface, displacing the image along the recent pointer path; displacement decays (decay 7.3) until the image rests. On load, the fallback image shows alone; when the shader signals onReady, a short opacity handoff fades the canvas in over it. Disabled entirely for reduced motion or missing WebGPU — the static image remains.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Required composition, order load-bearing: `<Shader toneMapping="aces"><ImageTexture url objectFit="cover" /><CursorRipples decay={7.3} radius={0.6} /></Shader>`; tune intensity/chromaticSplit/edges only from that baseline; do not substitute the library's Water component and do not add generator nodes (SolidColor, Blob, Form3D, GaborNoise, Glow) unless asked. Layering: wrapper position relative, definite size, overflow hidden, isolation isolate; fallback z-index 0, canvas z-index 1, canvas wrapper aria-hidden; mount gated on "gpu" in navigator + no reduced-motion, via lazy import (React lazy or Next.js dynamic ssr:false); exactly one shader canvas per media panel.
- **Reference / source:** Shaders framework guide https://shaders.com/docs/guide; package https://www.npmjs.com/package/shaders; interaction reference "Fragrance Hero", https://previews.shaders.com/sections/fragrance-hero. Same library as ⟦S1331⟧ but a different effect (image distortion vs halftone dot trail) — not a duplicate.
- **Best for:** Hero images and gallery/work panels on any homepage — one of the most trade-transferable WebGPU effects in this range because it decorates a real photo of real work; the static photo fallback is mandatory and built in.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1338⟧

## ⟦S1339⟧ threejs-landscape — Web design — WebGL / Three.js / shaders
- **What it is:** A complete quiet Three.js landscape backdrop: a domain-warped noise heightfield sampled on a polar grid, ground colored by slope and moisture instead of a texture, 104k GPU-instanced grass blades, scattered stones, a six-stop gradient sky dome, a camera-band star field, and a time-of-day system that cross-fades full light states instead of cutting.
- **How it looks:** Rolling grassland runs to soft landforms at the horizon; cliffs read stony, low hollows green and wet, ridges pale — all from vertex color, no tiling texture. Grass ripples in wind around the subject. The sky is a smooth six-stop gradient; at night tens of thousands of stars appear in the band the camera can actually reach. Switching morning → noon → sunset → night melts the whole scene's light, fog and sky from one state to the next.
- **Frame by frame:** Ambient continuous motion: grass bends in the vertex shader (bend driven by sin(uTime·1.7 + per-blade phase) × wind amplitude) at zero CPU cost. Time-of-day changes lerp every state value (sun position/color, hemisphere, ambient, fill, rim, fog color/range, ground and grass colors, six sky stops, shadow strength, star opacity) between two stored states; switching mid-transition freezes the current interpolated state as the new start so it never jumps. Weather (⟦S1341⟧) layers on top as multipliers, never as extra presets.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Polar grid: AN 900 angular × RN 52 radial, radius 2.0→700 spaced by pow(t, 2.4) so each ring covers similar screen pixels; winding index order (a0, b1, b0, a0, a1, b1). Height: domain warp fbm(x·0.012, z·0.012, 3)·26, then broad fbm ×34 at 0.0075 plus ridged ×9 at 0.021 (ridge amplitude must scale up with distance). Vertex color: slope = 1 − normal.y; moisture = smoothstep(−4, 6, −height); rock lerp grass by (1 − slope·3.2)·(0.35 + moist·0.65), then sand by max(0, 0.5 − moist)·0.6. Grass: one InstancedMesh, 104,000 instances of an 11-vertex 5-segment ribbon, all shaping in the vertex shader via onBeforeCompile with aParams (height, phase, tint, lean), customProgramCacheKey set; field is a camera-anchored patch snapped to cell size. Stones: icosphere scaled (1, 0.62, 1), translated +0.3 to sit sunk, rejection-sampled by slope. Sky: 8×512 canvas, stops at 0 / 0.30 / 0.52 / 0.68 / 0.84 / 1, back-side sphere, horizon stop slightly below the geometric horizon. Stars: ~39,000 points in three size classes, sizeAttenuation false, size scaled by devicePixelRatio, additive, fog false.
- **Reference / source:** Bundled demo "A Place To Stand Something In" (demo/PROMPT.md). Companions: ⟦S1341⟧ threejs-weather (weather on top), ⟦S1340⟧ threejs-towers (architecture standing in it).
- **Best for:** Hero backdrops and scroll-world environments where a building, object or figure must sit in a believable place. A full scene system, not a section garnish — heavy.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1339⟧

## ⟦S1340⟧ threejs-towers — Web design — WebGL / Three.js / shaders
- **What it is:** Procedural Three.js architecture: a small geometry vocabulary (face, box, prism, prismN, sweepPlan, lathe, ring/arc, fan, tube) that builds pagodas, castles, domes and spires from parameter tables instead of mesh files — plus a build animation in which one rising clipping plane reveals finished work below it while scaffolding stands above it.
- **How it looks:** A tower assembles itself from the ground up in about four to five seconds: below the rising line, solid finished stonework, plaster and tile; exactly at the line, a flat cap course that matches the plan being cut (square, then octagonal, then sixteen-sided); above the line, only scaffold poles and braces waiting. Stage captions name the work as it passes (READY, STONEWORK, TIMBER, PLASTER…) with a large quiet percentage in the corner. East Asian roofs sag and curl up at the corners from one profile function. A style control swaps a castle keep for a five-tier pagoda — same primitives, different parameters.
- **Frame by frame:** Trigger: the build timeline (the demo also supports scrubbing and a remix drives the plane from scroll). The single THREE.Plane (normal (0,−1,0), constant = heightAt(t)) eases between stage target heights; every structural material clips against it, so courses appear as the plane passes; the cap mesh at the plane's height rebuilds its geometry as the plan changes between height bands (recorded example caps: [0→4.74, r 2.56, 4 sides], [4.74→5.42, r 2.02, 8], [5.42→6.46, r 1.86, 16]); scaffold tiers grow in with short eased scales (verticals in Y, horizontals in X) just ahead of the line and fall away before the next stage lands; a one-shot sound fires per stage and a bell on the last.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Ten builders append into shared vertex/normal/UV/index arrays; merge by material, not by part — six buildings in 11–18 draw calls. Roof profile: six parameters (lift, tip, flare, pow, trunc, ridge); corner term pow(|u|, 2.0), flare 1 + flare·corner·pow(tc, 3.2), lift ·corner·pow(tc, 2.6), slope g = 1 − pow(1−tc, pow); t is clamped (tc = min(1, t)) before any Math.pow or overshooting tiles return NaN and the roof vanishes. Clipping: renderer.localClippingEnabled = true, each structural material gets clippingPlanes [CLIP] and clipShadows true; interiors use a capped DoubleSide dark volume. Scaffold BoxGeometry UVs are rewritten in world units so a 3 m pole and a 15 cm brace don't share one grain scale. Stages are [local caption, ENGLISH, target height] triples (example heights 0.00 / 3.36 / 6.24 / 8.80…). Non-square plans are built as a mirrored outline swept per storey, with ledges decked by flat annuli.
- **Reference / source:** Bundled demo "A Building That Builds Itself" (demo/PROMPT.md). Stands in ⟦S1339⟧ threejs-landscape; weathered by ⟦S1341⟧ threejs-weather.
- **Best for:** Process and construction sections — a building assembling itself is a direct visual metaphor for a builder's or roofer's process — plus architectural title sequences and procedural landmarks.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1340⟧

## ⟦S1341⟧ threejs-weather — Web design — WebGL / Three.js / shaders
- **What it is:** A weather system for Three.js scenes in which clear / rain / storm / snow are one control and one shared particle pool: frustum-anchored rain, a storm that is the rain intensified rather than a second system, multi-flash lightning on its own light with distance-delayed thunder, a blizzard envelope, settling snow pack, wet ground and seam-free looping ambience.
- **How it looks:** Rain actually falls through the camera's view. The storm leans the same rain harder — more drops, faster, slanting further — while sun and fog close in. Lightning strobes two to four times over about a fifth of a second from a different direction each strike, the sky brightening with it; thunder arrives later and quieter the farther away it was. Snow starts calm, periodically blows up into a whiteout, and the longer it snows the whiter the ground, stones and grass tips become. After rain the ground darkens and puddles in the hollows catch the sky, with small splash rings where drops land.
- **Frame by frame:** State change: density is applied by setDrawRange on a pre-allocated worst-case pool, so there is no realloc hitch. Rain→storm dials: drops drawn 60%→100% of pool, fall speed ×1.0→×1.42, slant grows with speed² (slant = base·v·v), sun 30%→14%, fog far ×0.52→×0.38. Lightning: a pulse train (leader amplitude s = 0.42 + near·0.58, then 1–3 return strokes at +0.05–0.19 s each, 30–95% amplitude) decays exponentially (τ 0.085) into a dedicated DirectionalLight (intensity v·3.2), sky scalar 1 + v·0.80 and a DOM flash at v·0.15 opacity placed under the typography; thunder is scheduled (0.32 + (1−near)·2.7) s later at gain 0.30 + near·0.60. Snow: blizzard envelope cycles phases of [12, 6, 15, 8] seconds (calm, build, blow, ease); snowPack chases its target at dt/24 rising and dt/13 melting; entering snow resets the phase clock to zero.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Precipitation volume 17 wide × 50 deep × 40 tall, anchored 46 units ahead of the camera and rotated to the camera azimuth, frustumCulled = false. Float32BufferAttribute copies its input — keep and mutate attr.array, with DynamicDrawUsage. Re-lighting is gated: refresh only when |blizK + snowPack − lastLook| > 0.006. Snow in shader-mixed materials needs its own uniform (tips whiten first: tip mix to (0.90, 0.94, 1.00) at uSnow, base to (0.60, 0.65, 0.72) at uSnow·0.86). Wet ground order of payoff: roughness down + slight metalness, puddle decals in hollows, instanced splash-ring sprites proportional to rain intensity. Ambience loops by folding the tail over the head with an equal-power (sin/cos) crossfade; weather runs on its own gain bus with the blizzard as a swelling second layer.
- **Reference / source:** Bundled demo "Four Weathers Over One Field" (demo/PROMPT.md). Pairs with ⟦S1339⟧ threejs-landscape and ⟦S1340⟧ threejs-towers.
- **Best for:** Atmosphere and seasonal states on 3D heroes and scroll worlds; on trade pages it is a scene layer (e.g. storm over a roofing hero), not a standalone section.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1341⟧

## ⟦S1342⟧ unicorn-studio — Web design — WebGL / Three.js / shaders
- **What it is:** An embed/customization guide for Unicorn Studio: no-code WebGL scenes (layers + effects + events) exported as an SDK embed or, plan permitting, a JSON/code export for self-hosted loading.
- **How it looks:** Designed interactive WebGL scenes layered with text, images and video — the bundled demo direction is a full-bleed procedural canvas atmosphere (eighteen slow wave bands and one narrow moving signal beam) behind precise interface framing and compact live-system metadata. Scenes react through authored events: Appear (entrance), Scroll (progress/velocity), Hover, Mousemove.
- **Frame by frame:** Motion is whatever the authored scene contains — the skill prescribes no timings of its own. With data-us-lazyload="true" a scene initializes when it approaches the viewport; the container must have explicit width/height or nothing displays.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Load the UMD SDK from jsDelivr (versioned), call UnicornStudio.init() once the DOM is ready; container attributes: data-us-project="PROJECT_ID", optional data-us-project-src for JSON, data-us-scale (render scale), data-us-dpi (resolution multiplier), data-us-fps (cap), data-us-lazyload="true", data-us-production="true". Performance-first recipe: 420px-high container with scale 0.75, dpi 1.25, fps 45. Keep under ~10 scenes per page (WebGL context ceiling ~16). Site-builder previews (Webflow/Framer/Wix/Figma Sites) typically don't render in edit mode — preview/publish to verify.
- **Reference / source:** Unicorn Studio docs: https://unicorn.studio/docs/ , embed guide https://unicorn.studio/docs/embed/ , performance https://unicorn.studio/docs/performance/ , events https://unicorn.studio/docs/events/ .
- **Best for:** Hero backgrounds and interactive scenes when the visual is authored by a designer in Unicorn Studio rather than hand-coded; external hosted dependency unless JSON export is available.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1342⟧

## ⟦S1343⟧ vantajs — Web design — WebGL / Three.js / shaders
- **What it is:** An integration guide for Vanta.js: ready-made animated WebGL background effects (WAVES, BIRDS, FOG, NET and others, mostly Three.js-based) injected as a canvas into a container element, with init/update/resize/destroy lifecycle patterns including React/Next.js cleanup.
- **How it looks:** A living animated background behind a hero — the worked recipe is slow dark waves rolling under the content (color 0x0b1220, shininess 40, waveHeight 16, zoom 0.9). Quick "wow" without building a scene; the effect fills its container, so the container must have explicit size.
- **Frame by frame:** Continuous ambient animation from the chosen effect; the skill body prescribes no timings — look and pace come from the effect's options. effect.setOptions({...}) changes options live, effect.resize() responds to container changes, effect.destroy() must be called on unmount in SPAs.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Include three.min.js (recipe uses three r134 from cdnjs) plus one effect bundle (cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/vanta/dist/vanta.<effect>.min.js), then VANTA.WAVES({ el: "#hero", ... }). Some builds require window.THREE or THREE passed in options. Keep to 1–2 effects per page; provide a fallback background color/image and consider disabling on small screens/weak GPUs.
- **Reference / source:** Vanta GitHub https://github.com/tengbao/vanta ; demo gallery/customizer https://www.vantajs.com . Note: its bundled demo prompt reuses the same canonical-example wording as ⟦S1342⟧'s (eighteen wave bands + signal beam) — a catalog boilerplate overlap; the two skills are different libraries, not duplicates.
- **Best for:** Fast decorative hero backgrounds on static or framework sites. On trade pages, only a very subtle dark waves/fog behind a hero — taste risk if it reads tech-demo.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1343⟧

## ⟦S1344⟧ webgl-3d-object — Web design — WebGL / Three.js / shaders
- **What it is:** A single real 3D WebGL hero object: geometric mesh with a physically based material, directional key + ambient/hemisphere fill + rim light, perspective camera, and subtle rotation and floating motion — real geometry and lighting instead of CSS transform tricks.
- **How it looks:** A faceted form (default an icosahedron) floats in a square stage, its flat faces catching a bright key light from the upper front-right and a cool sky-blue rim from behind-left, with a soft contact shadow on an invisible floor plane beneath it. It turns slowly and bobs gently; highlights and edges read as a real lit object.
- **Frame by frame:** Continuous loop: rotation.y = t·0.28; rotation.x = −0.16 + sin(t·0.45)·0.06; rotation.z = sin(t·0.32)·0.08; position.y = sin(t·0.8)·0.08 (prescribed float band 0.04–0.12 units). Under reduced motion one still frame is rendered and the loop stops.
- **Mechanism & key values:** IcosahedronGeometry(radius 1.35, detail 1) by default (dodecahedron/box/custom BufferGeometry/glTF allowed); MeshStandardMaterial color 0x8aa4ff, metalness 0.48, roughness 0.34, emissive 0x101833 at intensity 0.22, flatShading true; camera PerspectiveCamera fov 38 at (0, 0.15, 5.2); AmbientLight 0.38; key DirectionalLight 2.15 at (3.4, 4.2, 4.8), shadow map 1024; rim DirectionalLight 0x7dd3fc at 0.82 from (−4.2, 1.2, −2.8); ShadowMaterial plane opacity 0.18 at y −1.65; ACESFilmicToneMapping, exposure 1.05; DPR cap 1.75. Material ranges: premium metal metalness 0.45–0.7 / roughness 0.25–0.45; soft ceramic 0.0–0.15 / 0.38–0.62; emissive intensity 0.12–0.35 for glow-tinted tech.
- **Reference / source:** Neuform reference demo "PulsoApps | Tu app lista en 5 días." https://neuform.ai/pages/pulsoapps-tu-app-lista-en-5-d-as-3/index.html (Neuform rank #1 for this skill when synced; 405 views · 20 favorites · 10 remixes).
- **Best for:** Hero centerpiece objects and product-like moments. For trade homepages an abstract object rarely beats a real photo of work — situational.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1344⟧

## ⟦S1345⟧ webgl-laser — Web design — WebGL / Three.js / shaders
- **What it is:** A fixed full-screen raw-WebGL laser background: one thin vertical beam with a white-hot core, a restrained halo in the page's brand color, and soft smoky fog concentrated around the beam, rendered on a pointer-events-none canvas behind all content.
- **How it looks:** On a near-black field a hair-thin vertical line of light — white at the center, bleeding into a soft accent-colored halo; smoky clouds drift slowly upward around the beam and dissipate outward; the edges fall into a vignette. The glow breathes gently; nothing flickers or cycles color. It reads as a light blade, never a thick neon pillar.
- **Frame by frame:** Continuous: the fog layers scroll (base FBM uv drifts −t·0.035 vertically, fine layer +t·0.05, with a horizontal sway sin(p.y·3.5 + t·0.11)·0.14) while the halo pulses at 0.9 + 0.1·sin(t·1.15) — pulse affects glow only; the beam position is static (u_xOffset). Under reduced motion a single static frame renders.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Raw WebGL full-screen quad, one fragment shader: core = exp(−(d/u_coreWidth)²), glow = exp(−(d/u_glowWidth)^1.45), scatter = exp(−(d/(u_glowWidth·5.5))^1.25); 5-octave value-noise FBM fog, smoke = smoothstep(0.30, 0.86, fogBase·0.72 + fogFine·0.28) × scatter × u_smokeDensity. Defaults: coreWidth 0.0045, glowWidth 0.035, smokeDensity 0.52, xOffset 0.0, maxDpr 1.5. Color read from the --brand-accent CSS variable (fallback #ff4d8d): halo = brand mixed 16% toward white, smoke = brand mixed 28% toward mid-grey × 0.55, core color (1.0, 0.96, 0.90) × 1.35 over a (0.006, 0.007, 0.010) base; vignette smoothstep(1.25, 0.18, length(p)).
- **Reference / source:** Neuform reference demo "Squish — Turn Your Ideas Into Stunning Visuals", https://neuform.ai/pages/squish-turn-your-ideas-into-stunning-visuals/index.html (Neuform rank #1 for this skill when synced; 351 views · 14 favorites · 1 remix).
- **Best for:** Dark cinematic hero backgrounds in tech registers. Narrow fit for trade homepages — an abstract beam, not a section system.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1345⟧

## ⟦S1346⟧ corner-diagonals — Web design — CSS surface detail
- **What it is:** Diagonal-cut (chamfered) corners for buttons, cards, panels and container shells, implemented with CSS clip-path polygons and applied as one consistent system of cut sizes — engineered, sharp surfaces instead of rounded pills or plain rectangles.
- **How it looks:** Rectangles with one, two or all four corners sliced off at 45°: a primary button becomes a chamfered gradient block; a card sits inside a thin gradient shell whose line follows exactly the same clipped silhouette; repeated across a page the cuts read as a deliberate structural motif.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion of its own. The only prescribed state change is hover brightening on the primary button (filter: brightness(1.08)); the shape itself never moves.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Cut tokens: --corner-cut-sm 8px, --corner-cut-md 14px, --corner-cut-lg 24px; tuning ranges 6–10px for small controls, 12–18px for cards, 20–32px for large panels. Polygons supplied for all-four-corners, top-left+bottom-right, and top-right+bottom-left cuts. Lines: --corner-line rgba(255,255,255,0.18), strong 0.34; fill rgba(10,14,24,0.82); accent #8b5cf6 in the token example. Bordered shell = outer wrapper with 1px padding and a 135deg gradient background, same clip-path on wrapper and inner surface. Button: min-height 44px, padding 0 18px, gradient from accent to accent darkened 28% (color-mix); focus-visible outline 2px offset 3px. Border, background and hit area must all follow the same polygon.
- **Reference / source:** Neuform reference demo "Auralis - Neural Audio Engine", https://neuform.ai/pages/auralis-neural-audio-engine/index.html (Neuform rank #1 for this skill when synced; 1,953 views · 80 favorites · 39 remixes).
- **Best for:** Buttons, cards, panels, CTA shells in tech/engineered registers; on trade pages use sparingly — the sci-fi cut can read cold against homeowner content.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1346⟧

## ⟦S1347⟧ corner-lasers — Web design — CSS surface detail
- **What it is:** A corner-anchored laser composition: two or three thin beams derived from a single off-center corner emitter point, with a white-hot beam core, an accent-colored halo, concentrated bloom at the junction and atmospheric haze around it.
- **How it looks:** From a bright node near one corner of the frame, narrow beams shoot outward along different directions like the seam of a geometric room corner or portal edge; the emitter is the brightest point in the composition, and the surrounding air glows softly in the design's accent color so the corner feels lit by volumetric haze rather than lines drawn on black.
- **Frame by frame:** Motion is ambient and restrained — slow pulsing, faint energy traveling along the beams, gentle shimmer; chaotic flicker is explicitly out. The source prescribes these behaviors qualitatively and gives no numeric durations or speeds.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Prefer raw WebGL shader treatment; beams computed with signed-distance / line-distance logic from one anchor point so each stays thin, crisp and continuous; core kept near white, halo and haze tint derived from the active design accent (never hardcode blue). Tuning knobs named: corner position, beam count and angles (two or three rays), core thickness vs outer glow tuned separately, bloom radius, fog density and falloff, vignette strength. No exact parameter values are given in the source.
- **Reference / source:** Neuform reference demo "Aura | Superintelligence for Biology", https://neuform.ai/pages/aura-superintelligence-for-biology/index.html (Neuform rank #1 for this skill when synced; 278 views · 15 favorites · 7 remixes). ## ⟦S1348⟧ css-alpha-masking — Web design — CSS surface detail
- **What it is:** Edge fades with CSS alpha masking: a linear-gradient mask (mask-image plus the -webkit- prefixed twin) makes an element's content dissolve at its left/right or top/bottom edges instead of ending on a hard line.
- **How it looks:** A logo strip, marquee row, image or text block whose outer edges melt smoothly into the background — fully opaque through the middle 70% of its width, fading to transparent across the first and last 15%.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. The mask is a still gradient; it is often paired with a moving marquee underneath, but the fade itself never changes.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Horizontal: `mask-image: linear-gradient(to right, transparent, black 15%, black 85%, transparent)` with the identical -webkit-mask-image declaration (required for Safari); vertical variant swaps in `to bottom`. Knobs: direction (to right/left/bottom/top), the 15%/85% stop positions for fade depth, and replacing `transparent` with rgba(0,0,0,0.2) for a softer, partial fade. Pitfall recorded: masks only affect alpha — the element needs visible content, and overflow:hidden alone does nothing.
- **Reference / source:** None named.
- **Best for:** Logo/review marquee edges, gallery rails, hero image edges, fading sticky headers and footers — broadly useful on trade homepages wherever a strip or image should bleed out softly.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1348⟧

## ⟦S1349⟧ css-border-gradient — Web design — CSS surface detail
- **What it is:** Subtle gradient borders for premium surfaces, via the padding-box/border-box layered-background trick or a masked ::before ring — a refined edge highlight instead of a flat border or a loud glow.
- **How it looks:** A dark glass card, pricing panel or hero surface whose 1px edge catches the light: a bright neutral at the top-left, a whisper of brand accent through the middle of the edge, fading to near-invisible — noticeable at normal zoom, barely there when scanning the page.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion by default; the skill explicitly rules out animated gradients as a default.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Width 1px (2px only for large hero cards or active states); angle 135deg or 160deg; stops = neutral highlight, one brand accent, neutral fade, most stops below 0.4 opacity. Simple pattern: border 1px solid transparent; background: linear-gradient(var(--surface), var(--surface)) padding-box, linear-gradient(135deg, rgba(255,255,255,0.34), rgba(125,92,255,0.36), rgba(255,255,255,0.08)) border-box, with --surface rgba(10,14,24,0.72) and radius 20px in the example. Masked variant: ::before with padding 1px, 145deg gradient (accent stop at 45%), -webkit-mask-composite xor / mask-composite exclude. Apply to one hierarchy level at a time; check light and dark themes separately.
- **Reference / source:** Neuform reference demo "Kiwi Floral | Artisan Botanical Design", https://neuform.ai/pages/kiwi-floral-artisan-botanical-design-1/index.html (Neuform rank #1 for this skill when synced; 2,154 views · 47 favorites · 27 remixes).
- **Best for:** Cards, pricing/quote panels, nav bars, modals, buttons, hero surfaces, selected-plan highlights — highly transferable to trade pages (quote and pricing cards especially).
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1349⟧

## ⟦S1350⟧ gooey-blob-system — Web design — CSS surface detail
- **What it is:** A gooey blob system: multiple independent circles animated inside an SVG filter (Gaussian blur followed by a color-matrix alpha threshold) so that when shapes approach they fuse into one continuous fluid mass, and separate again as they drift apart.
- **How it looks:** Soft organic blobs with no hard edges wander; as two come close, a liquid neck stretches between them and they merge into a single blobby form; as they part, the neck thins and pinches off, leaving round separate blobs again. The whole system feels like one cohesive fluid rather than a set of circles.
- **Frame by frame:** Continuous smooth motion loop: shapes approach → their blurred alpha fields overlap → the thresholded filter renders the overlap as one connected surface → shapes separate → the bridge pinches off. The skill instructs tuning blur, contrast and shape spacing together so merging stays visible, and forbids fast jittery motion; it gives no numeric durations, blur radii or matrix constants in its text.
- **Mechanism & key values:** SVG filter chain: feGaussianBlur then a color matrix threshold applied to a group of animated shapes. Guardrails recorded: do not fake it with plain blurred circles that never merge; keep motion smooth and cohesive; provide a static or simplified fallback for low-motion contexts.
- **Reference / source:** Neuform reference demo "Modern Talent Platform", https://neuform.ai/pages/modern-talent-platform/index.html (Neuform rank #1 for this skill when synced; 170 views · 10 favorites · 2 remixes).
- **Best for:** Hero atmosphere, loaders, cursor fields, background accents. Playful/organic register — situational for trade pages.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1350⟧

## ⟦S1351⟧ liquid-metal-border — Web design — CSS surface detail
- **What it is:** Animated liquid-metal WebGL borders via the React `metal-fx` package: the MetalFx component wraps exactly one real host element (button, link, chip, card) and paints a flowing metallic ring around it, driven by the control's actual state, with a static CSS border kept as fallback.
- **How it looks:** Around a pill button or card edge runs a thin ring of liquid chrome — iridescent in the chromatic preset, cool steel in silver, warm in gold — with a soft wandering halo glow when enabled. An idle tab sits at faint strength (0.1–0.2); hover, focus or selection raises it to 0.75–0.9 so the active control visibly lights up in metal. In dark mode the ring can cast a soft mirrored reflection onto an explicitly named neighbouring element; reflections never render in light mode.
- **Frame by frame:** Trigger: hover / focus / selection state change. The ring's rendered opacity (strength) follows the state while the shader pattern keeps flowing at its own pace (strength changes opacity, not animation speed); on leaving the state, strength drops back or the instance is paused, freezing on its last frame with the silhouette still visible. Offscreen instances pause automatically via IntersectionObserver. Reduced motion: paused with glow disabled; the semantic state also lives in aria-pressed/aria-selected, never in the effect alone.
- **Mechanism & key values:** React 18+, SSR-safe, mounts the WebGL pipeline after hydration; one shared WebGL context, one compiled shader and one animation loop across all mounted instances. Props: variant "button" (1px ring baseline, shaderScale 1.6) or "circle" (2px, 1.3); preset "chromatic" (default) / "silver" / "gold"; theme "auto"/"dark"/"light" (SSR starts dark); strength 0..1, default 1, keep ≤0.9 for routine controls; ringCssPx overrides ring thickness; shaderScale 1.3–1.6 for large cards; borderRadius override or read from the child; normalizeHostStyles default true (strips the child's background/border/outline/shadow — set false to keep a custom focus ring); reflectionTargets = explicit refs only, dark mode only. Tuning defaults: primary pill strength 0.75 ringCssPx 1; icon button variant circle strength 0.7; quiet states disable glow before thinning the ring.
- **Reference / source:** Liquid Metal demo https://metal.jakubantalik.com/ ; repository https://github.com/Jakubantalik/metal-fx ; npm package metal-fx.
- **Best for:** Primary CTAs, selected tabs/filters, premium cards in React builds — reserved for active/selected/primary surfaces, never whole grids of idle controls. Not usable in a plain single-file HTML build (React package).
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1351⟧

## ⟦S1352⟧ number-details — Web design — CSS surface detail

They support the hierarchy; they never compete with headings or CTAs.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** No code or numeric parameters are prescribed beyond the rules: always two-digit format (01, 02, 03) for consistency; one numbering style per section, never mixed; mono or narrow uppercase typography at low contrast; consistent spacing and alignment across all numbered elements; markers are secondary structure, not primary content.

## ⟦S1353⟧ solar-duotone-bold — Web design — CSS surface detail
- **What it is:** An icon-system discipline: Iconify's Solar Duotone Bold set is the single default icon family for the whole interface, using its duotone treatment (solid main glyph plus a lower-opacity secondary fill) consistently.

- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** No sizes or numeric parameters are prescribed in the text; the rules are: keep icon sizes consistent within a component group; use duotone opacity intentionally so secondary fills support the glyph; match stroke/fill/color treatment to the surrounding surface contrast; never mix Solar Duotone Bold with unrelated outline families in the same control set; never rely on icons alone for unfamiliar actions.

## ⟦S1354⟧ agency-grid-layout-minimal — Web design — grid & layout systems
- **What it is:** A full minimal-agency design-system direction: a disciplined editorial multi-column grid, oversized tight-tracked typography, tiny uppercase utility labels, restrained architectural image blocks and subtle structural detail, applied across layout, type, imagery, service rows, labels, CTAs and motion.

Buttons are understated — thin gradient-border wrappers, neutral fills, small uppercase labels.

Background effects, if present at all, stay extremely quiet (a faint wireframe object or low-opacity abstract geometry).
- **Mechanism & key values:** Wide max-width page shell with clear column divisions; type system built on scale contrast (very large display sizes vs tiny uppercase metadata and calm paragraph copy); surfaces minimal — light neutral backgrounds, subtle tonal shifts, thin separators, quiet image frames, restrained accent. Accent is one selective color — if no brand accent exists, subdued oxblood, bronze or antique gold — concentrated in headings, active index states and callouts.

## ⟦S1356⟧ editorial-tech — Web design — grid & layout systems
- **What it is:** A design-system direction that blends editorial magazine composition with precision product-tech detailing: asymmetrical grids, cinematic media bands, mono utility labels and one restrained accent color, applied across layout, typography, surfaces, media, navigation and motion.

Palette is mostly dark neutrals or controlled light neutrals; the single accent appears only on active states, numeric highlights, current steps, progress indicators and key CTAs.

Named patterns: sparse wide-spaced top nav with a framed logo mark; step lists and chapter markers with mono counters and timeline ticks; thin-framed panels with controlled image crops. ## ⟦S1357⟧ framed-grid-layout — Web design — grid & layout systems
- **What it is:** A layout system where every section sits inside a precise framed box on one shared 12-column parent grid: 1px guide borders, L-shaped corner brackets on the frames, and a very low-opacity diagonal line texture under everything.
- **How it looks:** A pale neutral page (background #f7f7f4) divided into clean rectangular frames with translucent white surfaces; each frame's four corners carry small L-shaped bracket marks in a stronger line tone; headings, controls and media edges align frame-to-frame like a technical drawing; a faint diagonal hatch is visible only on close inspection.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion prescribed; the system is pure structure.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Tokens: --fg-bg #f7f7f4; --fg-surface rgba(255,255,255,0.62); --fg-line rgba(24,24,27,0.14); --fg-line-strong rgba(24,24,27,0.34); --fg-texture rgba(24,24,27,0.035) (must stay below 0.05 opacity); --fg-gap 16px; --fg-pad clamp(16px, 2vw, 28px); --fg-corner 18px. Parent grid: repeat(12, minmax(0, 1fr)), gap 16px, background = repeating-linear-gradient(135deg, transparent 0 11px, texture 11px 12px) over the bg color. Frames: 1px solid line border, shared padding, overflow hidden. Brackets are eight background layers (linear-gradients sized 18px×1px and 1px×18px at each corner) — no extra markup. Spans: span-12/8/6/4; at max-width 760px the grid collapses to one column and all spans go full width. One border color, one bracket color, one spacing scale across the whole page; no heavy shadows and no mixed border weights.
- **Reference / source:** Neuform reference demo "Alert Interface", https://neuform.ai/pages/alert-interface/index.html (Neuform rank #1 for this skill when synced; 1,043 views · 32 favorites · 12 remixes).
- **Best for:** Whole-page structure for clean, technical, editorial pages; process, towns/areas and spec-like sections read especially well framed. A disciplined skeleton option for a trade page with a measured, surveyed feel.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1357⟧

## ⟦S1358⟧ image-first-grid-layout — Web design — grid & layout systems
- **What it is:** An image-led design system: one dominant full-bleed photograph or media surface is the stage, and a visible-but-quiet grid — rails, guides, corner markers — plus anchored overlay content blocks give it product-grade structure.
- **How it looks:** A cinematic photo fills most or all of the viewport, darkened by layered left-to-right and bottom-up gradient washes so type stays readable without flattening the image; thin vertical guide rails with tiny square markers run through the stage; the headline and CTA group sit anchored low or along a deliberate edge in one grid column, while a secondary box — quote, proof or metric — floats lightly (translucent, thin-bordered) in an adjacent lane; the top nav is a sparse transparent shell so the image remains the main event.
- **Frame by frame:** Motion emphasizes reveal and drift — masked text entrances, slow line movement, an optional faint WebGL/canvas line field drifting over the image plane in screen or additive blend, gentle hover highlight sweeps on buttons; no numeric timings are prescribed in the source.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Full-screen or large-stage hero layer treated as the foundation, not a card; overlay darkness tuned until readability is strong; supporting cards low-fill/transparent so they sit on the image instead of severing it; type = confident sans-serif headlines, soft low-contrast body copy, restrained micro-labels; buttons use translucent dark fills and thin borders with small moving highlight sweeps. Tuning knobs named: image dominance, overlay darkness, grid visibility, technical atmosphere, content anchoring. Explicitly not a gallery layout and not plain editorial minimalism.
- **Reference / source:** Neuform reference demo "Kiwi Floral | Artisan Botanical Design", https://neuform.ai/pages/kiwi-floral-artisan-botanical-design-1/index.html (Neuform rank #1 for this skill when synced; 2,154 views · 47 favorites · 27 remixes).
- **Best for:** Heroes built on one strong real photograph — highly trade-relevant: a finished job photo as the full stage with the headline anchored low and a proof/metric box overlaid — and work/gallery openers.

## ⟦S1360⟧ nested-container-frames — Web design — grid & layout systems
- **What it is:** A container-in-container layout system: one outer centered container with visible vertical boundary lines and corner markers, holding inner containers inset from the edges, each with its own background and rounded frame.
- **How it looks:** The page reads as a framed sheet — a centered column bounded by two thin vertical rules with small corner markers; inside it, hero, feature, proof and CTA blocks sit inset from the edges, each on its own slightly different background with rounded corners, like nested trays. Frame levels separate the modules instead of heavy cards.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. (Layout system only; the skill prescribes no animation of its own.)
- **Mechanism & key values:** The outer container defines the global page width; inner containers are inset with consistent padding; each level separated by layered frame (border + background) with a consistent spacing rhythm between outer frame and inner blocks. Guardrails: do not nest cards inside cards until the layout feels boxed in; frame lines must not overpower readability.
- **Reference / source:** Neuform demo "Squish — Turn Your Ideas Into Stunning Visuals" (https://neuform.ai/pages/squish-turn-your-ideas-into-stunning-visuals/index.html), Neuform rank #1 for this skill when synced; 351 views · 14 favorites · 1 remix.

## ⟦S1361⟧ split-layout-technical — Web design — grid & layout systems
- **What it is:** A technical split-screen design system: two panels with distinct roles, fine frame lines, mono metadata rails, quiet editorial typography, and one premium inset surface.
- **How it looks:** On desktop, two equal or near-equal vertical panels — one side an immersive/media focal panel, the other carrying explanation, specs and metadata. Each panel has its own internal framing: inset vertical rules, edge offsets, corner squares, thin borders. Slim mono rails run along the top and bottom with labels, coordinates, version markers and timestamps. Palette restrained and neutral with one selective accent; panels stack vertically on small screens without losing the sense of separate zones.

## ⟦S1363⟧ ambient-section-particles — Web design — style systems & page moods
- **What it is:** A bounded particle atmosphere inside one section only — petals, leaves, snow, sparks, confetti, dots, paper or brand fragments — with configurable physics, pointer disturbance, visibility pausing and reduced-motion fallbacks.
- **How it looks:** One section whose background carries a sparse drifting field of small shapes behind the content — the demo is softly falling seed fragments over a dark botanical chapter — with a deliberately quiet, lower-density zone reserved behind long text and controls so copy stays primary. The layer is decorative, pointer-transparent, and clipped to the section's bounds.
- **Frame by frame:** Particles seed inside or just above the section → they fall and drift under gravity and wind with phase-based sway, rotation and per-particle opacity → a pointer moving through the section applies a small distance-based push to nearby particles, which then settle back naturally → at the bottom edge each particle recycles to the top, exits, or settles into a shallow capped pile depending on mode → the loop runs only while the section is visible (IntersectionObserver) and pauses when it leaves the viewport or the tab hides → under reduced motion the section shows one sparse static arrangement instead.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Renderer ladder: canvas for roughly 40+ particles, DOM/inline SVG for a few branded fragments, WebGL only for thousands. One requestAnimationFrame loop per layer; density scaled by container area and clamped for mobile/low-power. Reference config in the skill: count 54, gravity 7, wind −3, sway 16, speed [8, 18], size [4, 12], opacity [0.18, 0.62], rotation [−0.8, 0.8], mode "recycle", pointerRadius 110, maxDpr 2. End modes: recycle / exit / settle / static. Resize via ResizeObserver; never one listener per particle.
- **Reference / source:** Bundled demo "Seedfall — A Quiet Weather System"; implementation references are MDN docs (Canvas API, requestAnimationFrame, IntersectionObserver, ResizeObserver, prefers-reduced-motion). Sibling: ⟦S1377⟧ falling-leaves is the recognisable-shape specialist — the source itself routes generic motes here and leaves/petals there.
- **Best for:** A single mood section — hero backdrop or one feature/CTA section — never a page-wide screensaver.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1363⟧

## ⟦S1365⟧ beam-glow-states — Web design — style systems & page moods
- **What it is:** A React component skill: animated border-beam edge glow for loading, processing, selected, current, focus and pressed states, using the `border-beam` package (API verified against border-beam 1.3.0).
- **How it looks:** A card, button, input or tab carries a restrained light that travels around its border, runs along its bottom edge, or breathes as a contained glow / outward halo — e.g. a task card with an ocean-blue pulse inside its border while it reads "Generating layout options…", settling to a slow neutral traveling border once selected. The beam is decoration only; state stays readable from text, shape, contrast and ARIA attributes without it.
- **Frame by frame:** State activates → the beam fades in over 0.6s → the effect loops: traveling border (default cycle 1.96s), traveling bottom line (3.1s), or breathing pulse (2.3s) → state clears → the beam fades out over 0.5s (the component stays mounted so the fade-out is not skipped). Selected-state beams are deliberately slowed to 3.2–5s cycles; for large collections only the newly selected item animates, for 800–1200ms, then keeps a static selected style.
- **Mechanism & key values:** npm package `border-beam`, React/ReactDOM 18+, named import `BorderBeam`; component-scoped styles (no CSS import). Sizes: `sm` compact traveling border, `md` full traveling border, `line` bottom edge, `pulse-inner` contained breathing glow, `pulse-outside` outward halo (only one per view). Color variants: colorful (default), mono, ocean, sunset. Prescribed ranges: loading pulse-inner strength 0.55–0.75, duration 2.3–3s; selected strength 0.3–0.55; focus strength 0.35–0.6. Defaults: brightness ~1.3, saturation ~1.2 on dark themes, hueRange 30 (line capped at 13); mono always uses static colors. Discipline: skip the beam for operations of ~150ms or less; once shown keep loading visible ~400–600ms; one dominant animated beam per viewport. Pulse presets stop under prefers-reduced-motion; rotate/line presets must be disabled by the consumer. State semantics: aria-busy / aria-selected / aria-current / aria-pressed as appropriate.
- **Reference / source:** Border Beam by Jakub Antalik — live demo https://beam.jakubantalik.com/, GitHub https://github.com/Jakubantalik/border-beam, npm package `border-beam`; plus MDN references for prefers-reduced-motion and the ARIA state attributes.
- **Best for:** Component-level state feedback — quote-form processing states, selected plan/option cards, focused inputs. React-only as shipped; a single-file HTML build would need the effect re-created in CSS/JS.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1365⟧

## ⟦S1372⟧ dither-background — Web design — style systems & page moods
- **What it is:** A dark monochrome procedural background of enlarged square pixels with visible 4×4 Bayer-style ordered dithering, shaped into broad organic waves or cloud masses — with the full canvas recipe included in the skill.
- **How it looks:** A near-black screen visibly built from chunky square cells, brightness quantized into a six-step gray ramp (near-black, charcoal, soft gray, rare white), forming one main bright cloud/wave mass that sits centrally or off-axis while the edges vignette back into near-black. It reads as designed atmosphere, not TV noise: the square Bayer matrix is legible from normal viewing distance, and framed UI or hero copy sits cleanly on top.
- **Frame by frame:** The field drifts continuously and slowly: two sine waves and a 4-octave noise cloud evolve with a small time drift so the masses move without flicker; under prefers-reduced-motion the drift is zeroed and the field renders static.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Canvas 2D, fixed full-viewport, `pointer-events: none`, base #030303, content stacked above at z-index 1. Defaults: cellSize 7 (tuning range 5–10px), maxDpr 1.5. Palette: [3,3,3], [16,16,17], [34,35,37], [74,75,78], [168,169,171], [236,236,232]. Recipe as shipped: BAYER_4X4 matrix normalized as (value + 0.5) / 16; brightness threshold step = brightness + threshold × 0.18; ridge via smoothstep(0.48, 0.92) over fbm cloud + wave; vignette via smoothstep(0.18, 1.15); drift = time × 0.018.
- **Reference / source:** Neuform demo "Alert Interface" (https://neuform.ai/pages/alert-interface/index.html), Neuform rank #1 when synced; 1,043 views · 32 favorites · 12 remixes. This field is also the texture layer used inside ⟦S1373⟧.
- **Best for:** Atmospheric hero/section backgrounds behind framed UI, hero content or data overlays on dark pages.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1372⟧

## ⟦S1377⟧ falling-leaves — Web design — style systems & page moods
- **What it is:** A falling-foliage effect in which each leaf tumbles on its own axis — presenting its face, thinning to an edge, opening out on its other side — with its sideways slip driven by that same tumble. Covers a 2-D canvas build and an instanced-3-D variant; for autumn maple, sakura, blossom, ash or snowfall shapes where a generic particle field reads as confetti.
- **How it looks:** The demo scene is one dark night frame — near-black sky, low ember moon, fogged treeline — with a maple fall crossing the whole frame in three depth layers: small slow faint leaves behind the type, the mid layer as the body of the effect, and two or three large near leaves crossing in front of the headline. Watching any single leaf for a few seconds shows it present its brighter face, thin to nothing edge-on, and reopen on a duller, paler back. Colors are sampled per leaf from a small ramp (deep oxblood through vermilion to dry amber), never one flat red.
- **Frame by frame:** Per leaf, continuously: the in-plane roll drifts while the through-plane spin turns (drawn as scaleX = cos(spin), which crosses zero at the edge-on instant) → lateral slip peaks exactly when the leaf is edge-on (x += sin(spin) · slip · dt, ninety degrees out of phase with the tumble) while it falls at its own speed → on exit it respawns above the top at a new random x in 2-D, or ahead of the camera in 3-D. Every parameter — fall speed, tumble rate, roll rate, slip, phase, scale, opacity — is randomized per leaf.
- **Mechanism & key values:** 2-D: two pre-rendered sprites per color (face/back), chosen by the sign of cos(spin), one drawImage per leaf, sprite pre-rendered once at largest draw size. 3-D: InstancedMesh quads, never point sprites (they can never turn edge-on); recycle into a disc hung down the camera's sight line rather than around it (on a 36° camera, a couple of hundred leaves banded around the camera put barely a dozen in frame). Density rule: on-screen density = count ÷ band area — halving the recycle radius quadruples density at the same count; viewport scale factor k = clamp(√((W·H)/(1440·900)), 0.5, 1.3). Depth layers: far scale 0.3–0.5 / opacity 0.22–0.40, mid 0.5–0.85 / 0.46–0.78, near 1.05–1.9 / 0.50–0.82. 3-D leaves use alpha-testing for correct sorting; an emissive red must zero its green/blue channels (0x780200, not 0x8c1410) or tone mapping returns it pink. Budgets: dt clamped to ~1/30s, DPR capped at 2, pause on document.hidden and off-screen, sizes from ResizeObserver. Reduced motion renders one composed still frame rather than hiding the leaves.
- **Reference / source:** Bundled demo "Late Autumn — The Maple Fall"; the skill itself names its sibling ⟦S1363⟧ ambient-section-particles as the reach-for when the shapes are generic motes.
- **Best for:** One seasonal/mood section where the falling shape must be recognizable — maple fall, or the bundled sakura remix pattern (daylight editorial page, pale petals, single near layer crossing a serif headline).
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1377⟧

## ⟦S1385⟧ operational-enterprise-ai — Web design — style systems & page moods
- **What it is:** An enterprise AI/automation/security product-page system that builds credibility by showing what the system does, where it stops, who approves actions, and how failures recover — boundaries, approvals, auditability, exceptions and rollback as page structure.
- **How it looks:** A near-black cinematic hero with hairline grid lines, warm-white type, muted gray labels, tabular numerals and one restrained pale signal color; a boundary-led headline with qualified actions on the left and a clearly labeled sample workflow trace (intake, policy, prepared action, audit packet, human approval gate, rollback target) on the right. A white interlude chapter quantifies the problem with verified metrics. Square panels, low radii, minimal shadow throughout — no glowing orbs, particle fields or cyberpunk decoration. Expandable solution rows, a security chapter, case-study evidence, and a qualified demo/waitlist handoff close the page.
- **Frame by frame:** Controls 160–220ms; section entrances 500–760ms. Slow background media, precise metric reveals and restrained row transitions; hard black-to-white chapter handoffs instead of smooth-scroll effects; parallax below 5%; offscreen work paused; settled states rendered immediately under reduced motion.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Every solution row keeps summary, permissions, action, approval, output, audit, exception and rollback in a stable data model, expanded by semantic disclosure (Enter/Space) with text equivalents for diagrams; designed states include loading, unavailable integration, insufficient permission, stale data, denied approval, partial completion, rollback and error. Metrics may only appear with scope, source and timeframe; case studies separate verified facts from marketing interpretation.
- **Reference / source:** Intelli — live reference https://intelli.framer.website/ and Framer template listing https://www.framer.com/community/marketplace/templates/intelli/.
- **Best for:** Trust/proof structure and qualified CTA handoffs; the "show the process, approvals and guarantees before the ask" structure maps well to high-ticket work (permits, warranties, guarantee handling), though the visual register is enterprise-dark.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1385⟧

## ⟦S1388⟧ skeuomorphic-ui — Web design — style systems & page moods
- **What it is:** A CSS surface recipe for tactile skeuomorphic UI: layered gradients, stacked inner and outer shadows, reflective gradient borders, micro texture, and embossed text/icon details for pressed, carved, soft-plastic or soft-metal controls.
- **How it looks:** Light tactile surfaces — a card, button, switch or dial with a soft vertical gradient (lighter top, darker bottom), a bright 1px top edge and darker lower edge, and a glossy sheen across its top third. Raised elements sit on deep soft outer shadows with an inset top highlight; a pressed/active surface sinks 1px and reverses its depth with carved inset shadows. Labels and icons look embossed via paired light/dark text and drop shadows; an optional 1px-dot micro texture is felt rather than noticed.
- **Frame by frame:** State transitions only: raised → pressed (and hover) animate over 160–240ms — the shipped recipe uses 200ms ease on box-shadow, transform and background.
- **Mechanism & key values:** Surface recipe: rounded shape + vertical gradient, 1px gradient-border wrapper (padding-box/border-box technique), outer shadows for elevation + inset shadows for carved depth, top-edge highlight, embossed text/icons, micro-details only at supported scales. Reference surface: border-radius 22px; gradient #f8fafc → #e9eef5 at 48% → #cfd7e4; shadows 0 18px 34px rgba(31,41,55,0.18) + 0 5px 12px rgba(31,41,55,0.12) + inset highlights; pressed state translateY(1px) with inset 0 4px 10px rgba(31,41,55,0.22). Tokens --sk-edge-top rgba(255,255,255,0.82), --sk-edge-bottom rgba(79,93,122,0.34). Micro texture: two radial-gradient dot layers at 18px and 22px tile sizes. Taste rules: one physical material per component, light always from the top, no pure-black shadows, never mix glassmorphism/neumorphism/skeuomorphism in one component. Component-recipe sibling of the full dark page system ⟦S1382⟧.
- **Reference / source:** Neuform demo "Kiwi Floral | Artisan Botanical Design" (https://neuform.ai/pages/kiwi-floral-artisan-botanical-design-1/index.html — the same demo page referenced by ⟦S1361⟧), Neuform rank #1 when synced; 2,154 views · 47 favorites · 27 remixes.
- **Best for:** Tactile buttons, switches, dials, inputs and toolbars; premium hardware-like control details inside a page.

## ⟦S1390⟧ thinking-orbs — Web design — style systems & page moods
- **What it is:** A React library skill for accessible animated AI loading/agent-status indicators: monochrome dot orbs on a transparent canvas, in six semantic states, replacing generic spinners in chat, copilot, voice, search and generation interfaces.
- **How it looks:** A small cluster of monochrome dots animating in a state-specific pattern at exactly 20px (inline with text, in buttons, in status rows) or 64px (chat-avatar scale, empty states) — light ink on dark surfaces, dark ink on light, canvas transparent. The six states map to internal patterns: working → orbits, searching → globe, solving → rubik, listening → wave, composing → ribbon, shaping → morph. The presets are separate designs with different dot counts and tuning, not scale factors of each other.
- **Frame by frame:** A continuous per-state dot animation runs on one requestAnimationFrame loop per visible instance, all instances sharing the performance.now() clock so they stay in phase. It pauses when the orb scrolls offscreen (IntersectionObserver) and when the tab is hidden; the `paused` prop freezes the current frame; under prefers-reduced-motion it renders one deterministic static frame while still following live theme changes. The orb is removed on done, error, cancellation or idle — it is indeterminate feedback, never a progress signal.
- **Mechanism & key values:** npm package `thinking-orbs`; React and ReactDOM 18+ peer dependencies; plain Canvas 2D arcs (no WebGL or SVG filters), device pixel ratio capped at 2. Sizes are exactly 20 or 64 — arbitrary sizes are a type error; size the wrapper for extra space instead of transforming the canvas. `speed` multiplies the baked per-state speed (start at 1; ~0.75–1.25 for product tuning; never simulate pause with speed 0). Theme: "auto" (ancestor data-theme/dark/light class first, else prefers-color-scheme), "dark" = light dots for dark backgrounds, "light" = dark dots. Accessibility: defaults to role="img" with a per-state label (override with a task-specific aria-label); when adjacent role="status" text announces the same state, set aria-hidden on the orb to avoid duplicate announcements. Raw API for custom canvas owners: resolvePreset + MODE_DRAWS frame painters, STATE_TO_MODE mapping. Next.js: must sit behind a client boundary ("use client"). The public API is monochrome only — no custom colors or determinate progress.
- **Reference / source:** Thinking Orbs by Jakub Antalik — live demo https://orbs.jakubantalik.com/, GitHub https://github.com/Jakubantalik/thinking-orbs.
- **Best for:** App-interface loading states (chat, copilot, search, tool-running); no direct homeowner-page use — a product-UI component, indexed for component completeness.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1390⟧

## ⟦S1391⟧ affinity-diagram — UX research & discovery
- **What it is:** A qualitative synthesis method skill: cluster many qualitative data points (observations, quotes, notes) from multiple sessions or sources into themed clusters and insight statements. For one transcript use ⟦S1401⟧; for one segment's inner state use ⟦S1395⟧.
- **How it looks:** The output is a structured text hierarchy, not a screen design: named clusters grouped under typically 3–5 top-level themes, each theme carrying a clear insight statement ("the so what"), supporting evidence quotes, and notes on frequency, intensity and connections between themes, with insights ranked by impact on design decisions.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. (Research document output.)
- **Mechanism & key values:** Workflow: extract data points → bottom-up clustering (never start from predefined categories) → name each cluster → build the theme hierarchy → write insight statements → identify patterns → prioritize. Cross-interview sampling principle: process each transcript fully before clustering; tag every observation with its participant ID (P1, P2, P3…); after clustering, verify every participant appears at least once in the output; patterns appearing in only one interview are flagged single-source, not discarded.
- **Reference / source:** None named (method skill; sibling skills ⟦S1401⟧ summarize-interview and ⟦S1395⟧ empathy-map named inside the source).
- **Best for:** The research-synthesis step behind personas, journey maps and copy/proof decisions; no direct page-section use.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1391⟧

## ⟦S1392⟧ behavioural-analytics — UX research & discovery
- **What it is:** A method skill for reading funnels, retention curves and event data as a designer: separating a genuine design problem from a tracking artefact, and producing ranked hypotheses about where the design is failing. It does not define metrics or run experiments.
- **How it looks:** The output is a short written analysis, not a screen design: a ranked list of hypotheses, each stating the segment it applies to, the observation that would kill it, and whether the answer needs existing data, a session recording or a conversation — ranked by how cheaply each can be killed. Confidence is stated alongside each finding.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. (Research document output.)
- **Mechanism & key values:** Before trusting any number, rule out five artefacts: the event does not fire on what its name says; the denominator moved (acquisition change, not design); the funnel "step" is not enforced (users can skip, return, arrive mid-flow); a release, holiday or campaign lands on the same date; the platform split hides opposite effects. Then read shape over value: a cliff at one step = something blocking; a slope across many steps = the flow is simply too long (removing one step moves it only slightly); retention that falls then flattens = a real core with a bad first run; retention that keeps falling = no core yet, a value-proposition problem; bimodal time-on-task = two populations — segment before designing. The skill ships an EVALS.md with three scored test cases (tracking artefact, slope-vs-cliff, bimodal average); a case passes only when every must-contain line is met.
- **Reference / source:** None named (method skill; sibling skills metrics-definition, a-b-test-design and ⟦S1399⟧ qual-quant-triangulation named inside the source).
- **Best for:** Diagnosing drop-off in live funnels (e.g. quote/contact form steps) before commissioning a redesign.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1392⟧

## ⟦S1393⟧ card-sort-analysis — UX research & discovery
- **What it is:** A method skill for analyzing open or closed card sort results into a proposed grouping and label set for information architecture. Used after a sort study has been run.
- **How it looks:** The output is a written analysis: common category patterns and the naming conventions participants used, a similarity matrix showing how frequently items were grouped together, a recommended navigation structure based on user mental models, and a flagged list of cards that were inconsistently categorized, with next steps (tree testing, further research or design iterations).
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. (Research document output.)
- **Mechanism & key values:** Workflow: confirm the study (open vs closed, participant count, card set) → analyze groupings → build the similarity matrix → recommend IA structure → flag ambiguous items → suggest next steps. The source points to an information-architecture skill (ux-strategy) for turning the evidence into a full structure.
- **Reference / source:** None named (method skill; sibling information-architecture skill named inside the source).
- **Best for:** Navigation and services-taxonomy decisions — e.g. how homeowners group a multi-service trades offering.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1393⟧

## ⟦S1394⟧ diary-study-plan — UX research & discovery
- **What it is:** A method skill for designing a diary study — prompts, cadence, duration, participant criteria and analysis frame — for behavior that unfolds over days or weeks. For a single-session study, the source points to a usability-test plan instead.
- **How it looks:** The output is a ready-to-execute research plan document: research goals, study design (duration, participants, entry prompts, capture methods, check-in schedule, onboarding), an analysis framework for coding and theming entries across participants, and an attrition plan.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. (Research document output.)
- **Mechanism & key values:** Prescribed defaults: duration typically 1–4 weeks; 8–15 participants with screening criteria and a compensation plan; entry prompts daily or event-triggered, mixing structured and open-ended; capture via photo, video, text or voice; mid-study interviews or pulse surveys as check-ins; onboarding includes a participant briefing, practice entries and tool setup.
- **Reference / source:** None named (method skill).
- **Best for:** Longitudinal behavior questions (e.g. how homeowners live through a multi-week renovation) where a single session cannot reach the evidence.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1394⟧

## ⟦S1395⟧ empathy-map — UX research & discovery
- **What it is:** A method skill for building a Says / Thinks / Does / Feels empathy map for one user or segment — a fast shared-understanding artifact. For a composite archetype use ⟦S1404⟧; for cross-session themes use ⟦S1391⟧.
- **How it looks:** The output is a four-quadrant map: Says holds direct quotes from research, Thinks holds inferred beliefs and concerns, Does holds observed actions and workarounds, Feels holds emotional states and anxieties — plus the user's goals, pain points, extracted design insights and a note of what is still unknown.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. (Research document output.)
- **Mechanism & key values:** Method: Dave Gray / XPLANE empathy mapping. Discipline: quadrants are built from actual research data, not assumptions — Says uses real quotes where available, Thinks is explicitly inference from behavior and context; the build sequence is clarify the user → map each quadrant → identify goals → identify pain points → extract insights → note gaps.
- **Reference / source:** Gamestorming (Dave Gray) and Lean UX (Jeff Gothelf and Josh Seiden), named in the source's further reading.
- **Best for:** Quickly aligning a team on one segment's inner state — e.g. a homeowner dealing with active water damage — before copy and proof decisions.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1395⟧

## ⟦S1396⟧ interview-script — UX research & discovery
- **What it is:** A method skill for writing a structured user interview guide — warm-up, core exploration, scenarios and wrap-up — with non-leading question guardrails. Used before running interviews; for analyzing results, the source points to ⟦S1401⟧.
- **How it looks:** The output is a ready-to-use script document: timed sections with questions organized by research theme, follow-up probes, and facilitator notes on staying neutral, handling tangents and managing time.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. (Research document output.)
- **Mechanism & key values:** Funnel approach (broad context before specific features) with JTBD-style probing ("When did you last…? What were you trying to accomplish? What happened next?"). Section timings: introduction 2–3 min (welcome, purpose, consent), warm-up 3–5 min, core exploration 20–30 min, specific scenarios 10–15 min, wrap-up 3–5 min. Question quality rule: a question that contains its own implied answer is rewritten as an open invitation; a yes/no question is extended ("…and why?"). The source includes a leading → non-leading rewrite table (e.g. "Was that frustrating?" → "How did you feel about that?").
- **Reference / source:** Interviewing Users (Steve Portigal) and Just Enough Research (Erika Hall), named in the source's further reading.
- **Best for:** Preparing customer interviews whose answers will feed personas, JTBD maps and page copy.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1396⟧

## ⟦S1397⟧ jobs-to-be-done — UX research & discovery
- **What it is:** A method skill for mapping the job a user is hiring a product or service to do: job statements, the job's dimensions, its stages, and the forces of progress that drive switching (push, pull, anxiety, habit).
- **How it looks:** The output is a JTBD map structured by situation, motivation and outcome, with the job broken down across its stages and a competitor set that includes workarounds and do-nothing — plus design opportunities per stage.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. (Research document output.)
- **Mechanism & key values:** Job statement format: "When [situation], I want to [motivation], so I can [outcome]." Three job dimensions: functional, emotional and social. Eight job stages: define, locate, prepare, confirm, execute, monitor, modify, conclude. Differentiation rule: functional jobs are easy to copy; emotional outcomes and the anxieties around switching (fear of regret or failure) are where real differentiation lives, and every benefit claim should map to one named dimension rather than mixing all three.
- **Reference / source:** Clayton Christensen and Tony Ulwick's Outcome-Driven Innovation, named in the source's further reading.
- **Best for:** Framing a trades offer around the homeowner's real job (e.g. "stop the leak and the worry") and finding the stage where the page should concentrate.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1397⟧

## ⟦S1398⟧ journey-map — UX research & discovery
- **What it is:** A method skill for building an end-to-end user journey map for a defined persona across the stages of a complete experience — used after interviews or usage data have been gathered.
- **How it looks:** The output is a stage-by-stage (usually 5–7 stages, awareness to post-use/advocacy) map with, per stage: goals, actions, touchpoints, thoughts, emotional state forming a curve, pain points and opportunities — plus identified moments of truth and 3–5 prioritized improvement opportunities.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. (Research document output.)
- **Mechanism & key values:** Each map row runs the full structure per stage; opportunities are prioritized by impact and feasibility; quality rules: represent emotion honestly (not every stage is negative), base quotes on research rather than assumptions, and identify moments of truth — the points where users decide to continue or leave.
- **Reference / source:** Mapping Experiences (Jim Kalbach) and The Elements of User Experience (Jesse James Garrett), named in the source's further reading.
- **Best for:** Mapping the homeowner journey from first search through booking to post-job advocacy, so sections answer the right stage.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1398⟧

## ⟦S1399⟧ qual-quant-triangulation — UX research & discovery
- **What it is:** A method skill for the situation where interviews and numbers disagree: it names the mechanisms by which one evidence type misleads, routes each question to the evidence that can actually answer it, and designs a resolving study. It does not average findings or invent percentages.
- **How it looks:** The output is a reconciliation document: for each side, what it actually measured versus what it claims to measure, a ranked competing-account table, a resolving study with a pre-registered drop rule, and later a verdict stating which account survived and what the losing side's data was measuring instead.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. (Research document output.)
- **Mechanism & key values:** Disagreement-shape table with five entries: research says broken, data says fine (four mechanisms, incl. the proxy trap — behavior caused by something else); data says broken, research says fine (three); both say fine but conversion is low (three); people say they'd use it, nobody does (two: stated preference is not a prediction of behavior); both agree and both are wrong (three: selection effects, shared proxies). Question routing: what/how often/where → data; why/intent → research; is this worth building at all → neither (needs an actual commitment test). Rules: weight revealed over stated behavior; never resolve by averaging positions into a compromise nobody measured. Ships an EVALS.md with three scored test cases.
- **Reference / source:** None named (method skill; sibling skills ⟦S1392⟧ behavioural-analytics and ⟦S1401⟧ summarize-interview named inside the source).
- **Best for:** Adjudicating conflicting evidence about a page or funnel before acting on either side.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1399⟧

## ⟦S1400⟧ research-repository — UX research & discovery
- **What it is:** A method skill for designing a research repository: insight architecture, tagging taxonomy, insight templates and governance — so findings stay findable instead of dying in decks and drive folders.
- **How it looks:** The output is a repository design document: a three-layer model (insights, studies, raw data), an insight record template, a tagging scheme with controlled-vocabulary rules, search and discovery guidance, and governance (ownership, cadence, staleness handling).
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. (Research document output.)
- **Mechanism & key values:** Insights are the primary unit, not studies; each insight record carries statement, confidence (High / Medium / Low), method, date, participant sample, tags, source links and related insights. Tagging rules: controlled vocabulary first, plural lowercase, 5–8 tags per insight, no personal names in tags, quarterly reconciliation. Insights are added within a week of the study completing. Tool comparison table included in the source: Notion, Airtable, Dovetail, Confluence, EnjoyHQ.
- **Reference / source:** None named (method skill).
- **Best for:** Organizing accumulated customer/prospect research so future builds can retrieve it; a process skill, not a page pattern.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1400⟧

## ⟦S1401⟧ summarize-interview — UX research & discovery
- **What it is:** A method skill for turning one interview recording, transcript or notes into a structured summary — themes with verbatim evidence, jobs, pains, workarounds and confidence levels. Cross-session synthesis belongs to ⟦S1391⟧.
- **How it looks:** The output summary follows a fixed anatomy: participant profile; 3–5 key themes, each with supporting verbatim quotes; jobs to be done (situation / motivation / outcome); pain points with perceived severity; workarounds found; delighters; 5–8 verbatim quotes in the participant's own words; surprises (anything that contradicts prior assumptions); and concrete next steps or follow-ups.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. (Research document output.)
- **Mechanism & key values:** Rules: summarize only what is in the transcript — never invent quotes or fill gaps with assumptions; distinguish stated from inferred insights; attach a per-insight confidence (high = stated directly by the participant; medium = inferred from behavior described; low = single mention, needs corroboration); flag anything thinly evidenced as "[unclear from transcript]"; keep quotes verbatim, including false starts.
- **Reference / source:** None named (method skill).
- **Best for:** The per-session step that feeds personas, JTBD and journey maps with quotable, confidence-rated evidence.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1401⟧

## ⟦S1402⟧ survey-design — UX research & discovery
- **What it is:** A method skill for designing surveys that measure attitudes and self-reported behavior — screening, Likert scales, NPS and SUS included — with wording and order guardrails.
- **How it looks:** The output is a ready-to-field survey: clear objective, defined audience and sample-size rationale, an ordered question flow (screeners → behavioral → attitudinal → demographics last, open-ended questions last), validated scales where they fit, and a pilot plan.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. (Research document output.)
- **Mechanism & key values:** Prescribed numbers: Likert scales 5- or 7-point with a labeled midpoint and clearly labeled endpoints; NPS on the standard 0–10 scale (promoters 9–10, passives 7–8, detractors 0–6); SUS administered as the verbatim 10-item scale, scored 0–100, where 68 is average and above 80 is good; sample guideline ~385 responses for ±5% margin of error at 95% confidence; keep the survey under 5 minutes, with quality dropping past 10–15 questions; pilot with 3–5 people from the target audience. Guardrails: one concept per question, no leading phrasing, behavioral questions before attitudinal, "Prefer not to say" offered on demographics.
- **Reference / source:** None named (method skill).
- **Best for:** Post-job satisfaction and market surveys whose numbers will actually hold up.
- **Deep read:** WEB-SKILLS.md ⟦S1402⟧

## ⟦S1403⟧ usability-test-plan — UX research & discovery
- **What it is:** A method skill for writing a usability test plan — research questions, tasks with success criteria, participant criteria and a metrics scheme — for evaluating a design or prototype.
- **How it looks:** The output is a complete plan: 3–5 focused research questions, a session structure with script elements, tasks each carrying success criteria and expected completion time, a metrics table, and pilot-session and analysis checklists.
- **Frame by frame:** Static — no motion. (Research document output.)
